Traditional pharmacoeconomic models often rely on static, cohort-based approaches that inadequately capture real-world heterogeneity in patient populations, dynamic treatment pathways, and evolving healthcare market conditions. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-resolution, agent-based simulation framework integrating large-scale electronic health records (EHRs), claims data, and pharmaceutical market dynamics. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to construct microsimulation models representing millions of individualized patient agents with attributes derived from multi-source healthcare datasets. These agents will interact within simulated health systems to evaluate long-term clinical and economic outcomes of interventions under varying policy scenarios. Computational workflows will employ parallelized Monte Carlo methods for uncertainty analysis, Bayesian hierarchical models to address data sparsity in subgroup analyses, and machine learning techniques to predict treatment adherence and non-linear outcome trajectories. The scalability of HPC infrastructure is essential for iterative scenario testing, including sensitivity analyses of drug pricing policies, formulary decisions, and disparities in access across demographic groups. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible computational toolkit for dynamic cost-effectiveness analysis, validated against real-world outcomes data from partner health systems. Results will directly inform policymakers and healthcare payers by quantifying trade-offs between pharmaceutical innovation, affordability, and population health impacts. The project’s computational advances will enable more granular evaluation of value-based pricing models and tailored reimbursement strategies, addressing urgent challenges in sustainable healthcare financing. By harnessing HPC capabilities, this work aims to establish new standards for evidence generation in pharmaceutical policy, bridging methodological gaps between clinical efficacy data and real-world economic decision-making.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of economics and policy analysis to the study of the relationship of pharmacy services and pharmaceutical processes and products to the health care system and their impact on health care organizations. Includes instruction in health economics, pharmacoeconomics, health care systems, health care organization and management, statistics and biostatistics, outcomes research, health care policy, pharmacy services, and pharmaceutical industry operations.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the growing complexity of systemic risk propagation in global financial networks, driven by the rapid evolution of decentralized finance (DeFi) ecosystems and escalating geopolitical volatility. Traditional models of international financial stability struggle to capture the nonlinear interactions between centralized banking systems, cross-border payment infrastructures, and algorithmically driven DeFi markets, particularly under stress scenarios involving sanctions, supply chain disruptions, or currency weaponization. The core computational challenge lies in modeling multi-layered financial networks with real-time adaptive agents, where high-frequency cross-border payment data, smart contract interactions, and geopolitical event feeds must be processed simultaneously. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a hybrid simulation framework combining dynamic network analysis, multi-agent reinforcement learning, and event-driven computational storytelling. The high-performance computing (HPC) component will enable parallelized scenario testing across distributed ledger architectures, foreign exchange (FX) liquidity pools, and central bank digital currency (CBDC) prototypes at scale. Key computational requirements include GPU-accelerated agent training environments, in-memory processing of petabyte-scale transaction graphs, and stochastic optimization of crisis response pathways. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for identifying critical contagion thresholds in international payment systems, stress-testing frameworks for hybrid (traditional/DeFi) financial architectures, and policy simulations for multilateral currency swap line activation. By creating the first integrated computational model of geopolitical-DeFi-tradfi interdependencies, this research aims to provide central banks and international financial institutions with actionable insights for maintaining global financial stability in an era of fragmented monetary ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage international financial operations and related currency transactions. Includes instruction in international banking, international monetary and financial policy, money and capital markets, foreign exchange, risk analysis, and international cash flow operations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of cultural and literary representations of LGBTQ+ identities across digital archives, with a focus on 20th- and 21st-century anglophone media. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how queer narratives have been systematically marginalized or transformed in mainstream cultural artifacts, despite their centrality to community formation and resistance. By applying computational methods to large-scale textual and visual datasets—including digitized periodicals, novels, film subtitles, and activist ephemera—the project aims to map patterns in linguistic expression, thematic shifts, and representational biases that have shaped perceptions of gay and lesbian identities. Key computational approaches include natural language processing (NLP) techniques for sentiment analysis and topic modeling, neural network-based image recognition to study visual tropes in film and art, and network analysis to trace collaborative or antagonistic relationships among authors, publishers, and advocacy groups. The scale of data (spanning 10+ terabytes of heterogeneous sources) necessitates distributed computing for efficient preprocessing, feature extraction, and iterative model training. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible corpus of annotated LGBTQ+-themed materials, quantitative frameworks for assessing representational equity in cultural production, and visualizations of temporal-spatial trends in queer visibility. This work will advance interdisciplinary scholarship by bridging digital humanities methodologies with queer theory, offering new tools to contextualize the sociocultural impacts of LGBTQ+ movements beyond traditional archival limitations. The requested HPC resources are essential to process complex multimodal data while maintaining reproducibility, enabling analyses that would otherwise be computationally infeasible on local infrastructure.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies

cip_definition: A program that focuses on homosexuality in history, society, politics, and cultural life; usually with an emphasis on the modern emergence of gays and lesbians as a sociocultural minority movement, the identification of social, literary, and artistic themes and the definition of, and public policy and legal issues surrounding, the gay and lesbian community.

abstract: Phlebotomy procedures, while routine, present significant variability in patient outcomes due to anatomical differences, technique precision, and equipment interactions. Complications such as hemolysis, hematoma, or failed venipuncture attempts remain prevalent, disproportionately affecting populations with challenging venous access (e.g., pediatric, geriatric, or chronically ill patients). This project seeks to develop a biomechanical simulation framework to model needle-tissue interactions during blood collection, optimizing procedural protocols and device design. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will create multiscale models integrating real-world data on vascular anatomy, blood rheology, and material properties of skin, adipose, and venous tissues. Patient-specific variables—including dehydration status, BMI, and venous elasticity—will be parameterized using clinical datasets from partner laboratories. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will simulate blood flow dynamics under varying needle insertion angles and vacuum tube pressures, while finite element analysis (FEA) will quantify tissue stress distributions. Machine learning components will identify predictive markers for procedural success from simulated and empirical training datasets. The resulting platform will enable virtual testing of novel phlebotomy devices, personalized insertion strategy recommendations, and AI-driven training modules for technicians. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source simulation toolkit, optimized needle geometries for high-risk populations, and evidence-based guidelines for minimizing hemolysis in low-pressure venous systems. By bridging clinical phlebotomy practice with computational engineering, this work addresses a critical gap in precision specimen collection, with direct implications for diagnostic accuracy, patient comfort, and healthcare costs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians and other health care professionals, to draw blood samples from patients using a variety of intrusive procedures. Includes instruction in basic vascular anatomy and physiology, blood physiology, skin puncture techniques, venipuncture, venous specimen collection and handling, safety and sanitation procedures, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize casino floor operations through real-time modeling of dynamic variables, including game popularity, player traffic patterns, and staffing efficiency. While casino operations management intersects with hospitality and business disciplines, existing computational tools inadequately address the unique interdependencies of gaming environments, which require balancing regulatory compliance, revenue optimization, and customer experience. The research problem centers on the lack of adaptive models capable of simulating hyper-dynamic scenarios, such as sudden shifts in player demand during events or the impact of new gaming technologies on operational workflows. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement large-scale agent-based simulations that model individual player behavior, dealer interactions, and facility logistics at granular temporal resolutions. Monte Carlo methods will quantify uncertainties in player decision-making, while graph neural networks will analyze spatial traffic flows to recommend optimal table game placements and staffing allocations. The computational workflow will integrate real-world data from partner casinos, anonymized player telemetry, and regulatory constraints into a unified optimization engine. Expected outcomes include predictive models for demand forecasting, a framework for evaluating the operational impact of emerging technologies (e.g., cashless gaming interfaces), and scenario-testing tools to mitigate revenue loss during disruptions. By enabling millisecond-scale simulations of entire casino ecosystems, this project aims to advance decision-support systems in a specialized industry where traditional operations research methods struggle with volatility and scale. The results will provide actionable insights for resource allocation, floor design, and adaptive staffing strategies, while maintaining computational reproducibility for regulatory audit purposes. This work fills a critical niche in non-STEM domains by applying advanced computational techniques to an understudied sector with distinct operational challenges.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in casino operations and services not listed above.

abstract: The increasing adoption of alternative fuel vehicles (AFVs) necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize their complex energy systems, improve component durability, and streamline conversion processes from conventional vehicles. Current empirical models and small-scale simulations inadequately address the interdependencies between electrical, thermal, and mechanical systems in AFVs, leading to suboptimal performance and reliability. This project proposes a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach to model and simulate multi-physics interactions in AFV technologies, including hybrid powertrains, compressed natural gas (CNG) storage systems, and battery thermal management. The research will focus on developing scalable computational frameworks to analyze transient behaviors during energy conversion, predict component degradation under cyclic loads, and optimize control algorithms for hybrid energy systems. High-fidelity simulations will integrate finite element analysis (FEA) for structural integrity, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for thermal and fluid interactions, and machine learning to refine predictive maintenance protocols. By leveraging parallelized computing resources, the project aims to resolve time-resolved datasets spanning milliseconds to operational lifespans, enabling the identification of failure thresholds and efficiency bottlenecks. Expected outcomes include validated models for AFV energy management, predictive tools for retrofitting conventional vehicles, and open-access datasets to support technician training programs. These results will directly inform curriculum development in AFV diagnostics and conversion techniques while advancing industry standards for sustainable transportation. The requested HPC allocation will enable the resolution of multi-scale, multi-domain challenges that are computationally intractable on local clusters, accelerating the transition to low-emission mobility solutions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the maintenance of alternative fuel vehicles and the conversion of standard vehicles to AFV status. Includes instruction in electrical vehicles, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) vehicles, compressed natural gas (CNG) vehicles, hybrid fuel technology, electrical and electronic systems, engine performance, diagnosis and repair, and conversion/installation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale analysis of socio-cultural transformations in 19th- and early 20th-century Canada through computational historiography. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how regional identities and institutional networks evolved during periods of rapid industrialization and urbanization, particularly in understudied Francophone and Indigenous contexts. Traditional methodologies struggle to systematically process the vast, fragmented corpora of primary sources—including census records, parish registries, newspaper archives, and government correspondence—that are essential to tracing these dynamics. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques to extract entities, relationships, and thematic trends from digitized texts (totaling ~10 million pages), alongside geospatial analysis to map migration patterns and resource flows using historical GIS datasets. Network analysis tools will then model interactions between key institutions (e.g., religious organizations, trade unions) and demographic groups. Computational demands include training custom transformer models for French- and Indigenous-language documents, parallel processing of high-resolution spatial data, and simulating demographic scenarios under varying socio-economic conditions. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated historical materials, visualizations of regional identity formation, and quantitative frameworks for assessing institutional influence on cultural change. By integrating computational methods with archival research, this work aims to redefine scholarly debates on Canadian nation-building, particularly regarding marginalized communities, while establishing scalable protocols for digital humanities research in resource-intensive historical linguistics and geostatistics. The requested HPC allocation is vital to handling memory-intensive workloads and achieving reproducibility across iterative model training and dataset validation phases.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the society, culture, and institutions of Canada from its origins to the present. Includes instruction in Canadian historiography, sources and materials, historical research methods, and applications to the study of specific themes, issues, periods, and institutions.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design of healthcare environments by integrating spatial analytics, behavioral dynamics, and environmental health data. Current architectural practices for healthcare settings often rely on static guidelines that inadequately address the complex interplay between spatial configurations, occupant behavior, and health outcomes. To address this gap, we propose a data-driven approach combining generative design algorithms, agent-based modeling (ABM), and high-fidelity simulations of environmental variables (e.g., airflow, acoustics, light exposure) to predict how design choices influence infection transmission rates, patient recovery times, and caregiver efficiency. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to run large-scale parametric simulations, iterating over thousands of spatial layouts while incorporating real-world datasets from hospital motion-tracking systems, microbial sampling, and patient health records. Machine learning models will be trained to identify design features that correlate with improved health metrics, enabling the generation of adaptive, context-specific design recommendations. Key computational challenges include scaling ABM to simulate occupant interactions in multi-story facilities, coupling computational fluid dynamics with epidemiological models, and optimizing generative adversarial networks (GANs) for 3D spatial synthesis. Outcomes will include an open-source simulation toolkit for evidence-based healthcare design, predictive models linking spatial parameters to health risks, and a framework for dynamically updating architectural guidelines in response to emerging public health threats. This work aims to advance interdisciplinary collaboration between computational sciences, architecture, and public health by establishing a methodological bridge between data-driven design and clinical outcomes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the impact of design and architecture on the health of individuals and larger populations, and how to create settings that promote health, healing, and well-being. Includes instruction in architecture, interior design, human health services, communication studies, medical and clinical innovations, behavioral and engineering sciences, hospitals and health systems, and environmental conditions that influence health.

abstract: This project seeks to integrate high-performance computing (HPC) resources into the creation and optimization of metal art fabrication processes, addressing the challenges of material efficiency, structural integrity, and aesthetic innovation in contemporary metalworking. Traditional metal arts practices rely heavily on iterative physical prototyping, which is time-intensive, resource-consuming, and limited in its capacity to predict complex material behaviors under varied conditions. To overcome these constraints, this research proposes a computational framework combining physics-based simulations, parametric design algorithms, and machine learning (ML) to model and optimize metal-forming techniques such as casting, welding, and electroforming. Finite element analysis (FEA) will simulate stress distribution in sculptural forms under load, while computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models will analyze molten metal flow in intricate molds. Machine learning algorithms, trained on empirical data from past studio projects, will predict outcomes of material interactions (e.g., oxidation patterns, enamel adhesion) and recommend parameter adjustments for desired visual and structural results. These computational tools will interface with 3D modeling software to provide real-time feedback during the design phase, enabling artists to explore geometries and material combinations that exceed manual feasibility. The requested HPC resources are critical for running multi-physics simulations at scale, processing high-resolution volumetric datasets, and training ML models with minimal latency. Expected outcomes include reduced material waste, enhanced precision in large-scale installations, and novel aesthetic possibilities through data-driven design. By bridging computational modeling with studio practice, this project aims to establish a replicable framework for integrating advanced computing into metal arts education and production, fostering interdisciplinary innovation at the intersection of art, materials science, and digital technology.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of individual artistic expression and technical skills necessary for fabricating refined metal works. Includes instruction in aesthetics, anodizing, art history, casting, design, electroforming, enameling, metalsmithing, sculpture, two and three-dimensional design, wax carving, and welding.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and validate computational models to optimize personalized learning strategies for adolescents with disabilities in secondary special education programs. The research problem centers on the challenge of efficiently tailoring instructional content, scaffolding techniques, and transition readiness activities for students with diverse learning needs. Current approaches to individual education plan (IEP) development rely heavily on manual assessment and trial-and-error modifications, creating delays in addressing students' evolving requirements. We propose leveraging high-performance computing resources to analyze multi-modal educational datasets—including academic performance metrics, behavioral interaction logs, and longitudinal IEP outcomes—through machine learning frameworks. The computational approach will combine natural language processing of curriculum materials, agent-based modeling of classroom dynamics, and predictive analytics to simulate intervention impacts across neurodiverse learner profiles. By processing historical data from 15,000+ anonymized student records and generating synthetic cohorts through probabilistic sampling, the models will identify patterns in skill acquisition trajectories and predict optimal instructional adaptations. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for educators that recommends research-backed modifications to lesson plans, behavioral supports, and transition-planning strategies based on student characteristics. The project's significance lies in its potential to reduce the resource-intensive nature of special education personalization while improving postsecondary readiness outcomes. Access to scalable computing resources is critical for training neural networks on complex, heterogeneous educational data and running computationally intensive simulations of classroom scenarios under varied intervention conditions. Results will contribute to evidence-based practices in secondary special education while maintaining human-in-the-loop decision-making frameworks essential for ethical implementation.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals in Secondary Special Education Programs
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to children with special learning needs or disabilities who are in the secondary grades. Includes instruction in diagnosing learning disabilities; developing individual education plans; curriculum development, instructional strategies, and classroom management for secondary grades special education; content, methods, and modifications in specific subject areas; issues in vocational education; and promoting successful transitions to postsecondary settings.

abstract: Atmospheric chemistry and climate systems are interconnected through complex feedback mechanisms that remain inadequately quantified in current models, particularly under evolving anthropogenic and natural forcings. This project seeks to advance understanding of how multiphase atmospheric chemistry—spanning gas-phase reactions, aerosol formation, and aqueous-phase processes—modulates regional and global climate dynamics. A critical gap exists in modeling the coupled impacts of reactive trace gases (e.g., ozone, methane) and aerosols on radiative forcing, cloud microphysics, and extreme weather events, especially in understudied regions such as the upper troposphere and polar atmospheres. To address this, we propose the development and deployment of a high-resolution, chemistry-climate coupled model integrating the Community Earth System Model (CESM) with the Advanced Chemistry Module (ACM), enhanced to include halogen-driven oxidation pathways and ice-nucleating particle interactions. The simulations will resolve processes at spatial scales ≤50 km and temporal scales ≤1 hour to capture nonlinear feedbacks between atmospheric composition and meteorological variables. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the computational demands of these simulations, which involve ~10^7 core-hours for parameterization testing, multi-decadal climate runs, and ensemble-based uncertainty quantification. Machine learning tools will be applied post hoc to identify emergent patterns in the petabyte-scale output, focusing on teleconnections between chemistry-driven perturbations and shifts in atmospheric circulation. Expected outcomes include (1) improved parameterizations of aerosol-cloud-climate interactions for the Sixth International Coupled Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP6), (2) quantification of hydroxyl radical variability as a function of stratosphere-troposphere exchange under climate change, and (3) actionable projections of how chemistry-mediated feedbacks may amplify or dampen Arctic warming. These results will directly inform international climate assessments and air quality mitigation strategies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of atmospheric constituents, reactions, measurement techniques, and processes in predictive, current, and historical contexts. Includes instruction in climate modeling, gases and aerosols, trace gases, aqueous phase chemistry, sinks, transport mechanisms, computer measurement, climate variability, paleoclimatology, climate diagnosis, numerical modeling and data analysis, ionization, recombination, photoemission, and plasma chemistry.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for simulating and optimizing architectural designs that integrate adaptive cultural heritage preservation with contemporary urban resilience strategies. The research addresses a critical gap in architectural practice: the lack of scalable, data-driven tools to model how historic structures and culturally significant sites can be dynamically preserved while adapting to modern environmental pressures, such as climate change and urbanization. Current approaches often treat preservation and innovation as separate processes, leading to fragmented solutions that fail to balance cultural value with functional sustainability. To address this, the project proposes a novel computational method combining generative design algorithms, agent-based modeling, and multi-objective optimization. These tools will process heterogeneous datasets—including 3D LiDAR scans of historic sites, climate projections, material degradation models, and socio-cultural usage patterns—to generate design alternatives that maximize preservation integrity, energy efficiency, and community utility. HPC resources are essential for managing the computational complexity of real-time simulations that account for nonlinear interactions between structural, environmental, and human factors across multiple temporal scales (decadal weathering, seasonal use patterns, and emergency scenarios). Expected outcomes include an open-source computational platform enabling architects to test hybrid preservation-adaptation strategies, validated through case studies on UNESCO World Heritage sites facing acute climate threats. The project’s significance lies in advancing architecture’s capacity to serve as an interdisciplinary mediator between cultural memory and futurity, offering scalable methodologies applicable to global heritage challenges. By situating computational power at the intersection of archival precision and speculative design, this work redefines architectural problem-solving in contexts where tradition and transformation must coexist.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of architecture and to conduct research in various aspects of the field. Includes instruction in architectural design, history, and theory; building structures and environmental systems; project and site planning; construction; professional responsibilities and standards; and related cultural, social, economic, and environmental issues.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop an AI-driven framework for optimizing hyper-personalized marketing strategies in decentralized finance (DeFi) platforms, a rapidly evolving subset of financial services. The proliferation of blockchain-based lending, insurance, and asset management tools has created complex, dynamic customer interaction patterns that traditional marketing analytics cannot sufficiently model. Current approaches fail to integrate real-time on-chain transaction data, cross-platform social sentiment, and regulatory constraints into cohesive customer journey predictions. To address this gap, we propose a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) system trained on heterogeneous datasets, including Ethereum transaction logs, Discord/Twitter communications, and simulated regulatory scenarios. The computational challenge lies in processing high-frequency, high-dimensional data streams while maintaining interpretability for compliance-sensitive financial marketing decisions. High-performance computing resources are critical for three components: (1) Parallelized graph neural networks to map evolving customer-asset networks across 10M+ wallet addresses, (2) Quantum-inspired optimization algorithms to balance customer lifetime value predictions with regional advertising restrictions, and (3) Federated learning architectures preserving privacy across competing DeFi platforms. Expected outcomes include a real-time recommendation engine that adapts promotional campaigns at sub-15-minute intervals while maintaining audit trails for financial compliance. This work bridges distributed systems research with behavioral economics in an understudied domain, offering novel metrics for customer trust quantification in trustless environments. Successful implementation could reduce customer acquisition costs by 18-22% for partner platforms while providing regulators with transparent AI explainability frameworks. The computational infrastructure will enable unprecedented scale in financial marketing simulations, processing an estimated 4.3 TB of mixed structured/unstructured data daily across 15 specialized GPU nodes.
cip_title: Business and Personal/ Financial Services Marketing Operations
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform marketing and operational tasks associated with the provision of personal and financial services. Includes instruction in banking, marketing research, advertising, promotional campaign organization, insurance, media relations, and applicable technical and administrative skills.

abstract: Emergency departments (EDs) face escalating challenges due to increasing patient volumes, resource constraints, and the critical need for rapid, data-driven decision-making. A key unmet need is the ability to predict patient outcomes and optimize care pathways in real time, particularly for high-acuity conditions such as sepsis, traumatic injury, and acute cardiovascular events. Existing predictive models often lack the granularity, scalability, or computational efficiency required for dynamic ED environments. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing and validating machine learning (ML) models to predict clinical deterioration, prioritize resource allocation, and personalize treatment strategies using multimodal data from electronic health records (EHRs), real-time vital sign streams, and imaging studies. The computational complexity of integrating heterogeneous data sources—spanning structured EHR entries, free-text clinical notes, and high-resolution physiological waveforms—necessitates high-performance computing (HPC) resources. We propose a hybrid deep learning framework combining transformer-based natural language processing for clinical text, convolutional networks for imaging analysis, and temporal models for continuous vital sign interpretation. These components will be integrated via ensemble methods to generate risk scores updated in real time. HPC infrastructure is critical for training these models on retrospective datasets (>500,000 ED encounters) and simulating operational workflows under varying patient influx scenarios. Anticipated outcomes include validated prediction tools for sepsis onset within 1–3 hours of triage, mortality risk stratification for trauma patients, and optimized bed assignment algorithms to reduce ED boarding times. Successful implementation will provide a scalable computational framework to enhance clinical decision-making, reduce preventable morbidity, and improve resource utilization in emergency care. The requested resources will enable processing of terabytes of multimodal data, parallelized hyperparameter optimization, and deployment of low-latency inference pipelines, which are infeasible with standard clinical computing systems. This work aligns with national priorities to integrate advanced analytics into emergency medicine, offering a template for data-driven acute care innovation.
cip_definition: Research focused on Emergency Medicine

abstract: Forensic anthropology faces critical challenges in analyzing skeletal remains for medicolegal investigations, particularly when dealing with fragmented, degraded, or commingled remains. Traditional analytical methods often lack the precision and scalability required to address complex taphonomic processes, biological profile estimation under suboptimal conditions, or high-dimensional datasets from advanced imaging techniques. This project proposes the development of computational models to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of skeletal analysis by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will focus on three interconnected aims: (1) creating machine learning algorithms to automate the classification of skeletal trauma and taphonomic alterations using micro-CT and 3D surface scan data; (2) simulating population-specific osteological variation through probabilistic modeling to improve ancestry and sex estimation in diverse forensic contexts; and (3) optimizing Bayesian frameworks for integrating multi-modal data (e.g., isotopic, genomic, morphometric) in identification workflows. These objectives require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale imaging datasets, Monte Carlo simulations for uncertainty quantification, and iterative training of deep neural networks—tasks exceeding the capacity of standard laboratory computing infrastructure. The proposed HPC implementation will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for image analysis and distributed memory systems for large-scale statistical modeling. Expected outcomes include open-source software tools for forensic practitioners, validated protocols for computationally intensive analytical pipelines, and novel insights into skeletal biomechanics under taphonomic stress. By bridging gaps between anthropological theory and computational innovation, this work aims to establish reproducible, data-driven standards for forensic casework while advancing methodological rigor in skeletal identification. The resource allocation will directly support critical advancements in medicolegal death investigation capabilities, with implications for humanitarian efforts and judicial systems worldwide.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of the biological sciences and skeletal anthropology in medicolegal death investigations. Includes instruction in biological anthropology theory, crime scene investigation, forensic anthropology field methods, forensic anthropological techniques and procedures, human anatomy, methods of human identification, mortuary archaeology, osteology, and taphonomy.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of complex fault system interactions and their implications for seismic hazard assessment through high-resolution 3D numerical modeling. Current models of fault networks often oversimplify mechanical coupling between adjacent faults or neglect time-dependent stress evolution, limiting their predictive capability for multi-fault rupture scenarios. We propose to develop a parallelized finite element framework to simulate stress transfer and rupture propagation across geometrically intricate fault systems over decadal to millennial timescales. The computational approach integrates rate-and-state friction laws, viscoelastic crustal rheology, and dynamic rupture physics, requiring high spatial resolution (≤100 m grid spacing) to capture fault zone heterogeneity and off-fault damage effects. The simulations will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers and adaptive mesh refinement to manage the computational load across multi-scale domains. Key parameters will be constrained by geodetic and paleoseismic datasets from the [specific region/system, if applicable]. The expected outcomes include (1) quantification of stress transfer thresholds that trigger cascading ruptures in geometrically complex fault systems, (2) improved probabilistic forecasts of earthquake clustering behavior, and (3) validation of model predictions against observed surface deformation patterns from satellite InSAR time series. By addressing computational bottlenecks in simulating coupled fault systems, this work will provide a framework for evaluating worst-case multi-segment rupture scenarios that current empirical methods may underestimate. The resulting open-source code modules will enable reproducible analysis of fault network dynamics, directly supporting seismic hazard mitigation efforts in tectonically active regions. Successful implementation requires sustained access to HPC resources capable of supporting large-scale coupled simulations with >10^8 degrees of freedom and petascale output datasets for time series analysis.
cip_title: Geological and Earth Sciences/ Geosciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in geological and related sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of geoenvironmental challenges, such as the design of safe and sustainable waste containment systems under variable climatic and seismic loads, demands advanced computational tools to account for coupled thermo-hydro-mechanical-chemical (THMC) processes in soil-geosynthetic systems. Current analytical and empirical models often fail to capture the nonlinear interactions between soil behavior, contaminant transport, and structural integrity over multi-decadal timescales, particularly in heterogeneous or unsaturated soils. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity numerical framework to simulate the long-term performance of geosynthetic-lined landfill systems and soil-improvement strategies under dynamic environmental stressors. Leveraging finite element methods (FEM) coupled with machine learning surrogates, we will model 3D multiphysics interactions, including cyclic wetting-drying effects on clay liners, diffusion-advection of contaminants through composite barriers, and seismic-induced pore pressure changes in reinforced slopes. The computational workflow will integrate open-source libraries (e.g., OpenGeoSys, FEniCS) with custom Python-based optimization routines to assess failure probabilities using Monte Carlo simulations informed by field data from instrumented sites. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve mesoscale heterogeneities in soil-geomembrane interfaces, conduct parametric studies across 10^4+ realizations of climate scenarios, and train neural networks for rapid risk assessment. Expected outcomes include validated predictive tools to optimize liner material selection, improve slope stability design under earthquake loading, and quantify time-dependent leakage risks in containment systems. This work will directly support regulatory decision-making for landfill siting and provide open-access simulation templates for the geotechnical community, advancing the integration of computational geomechanics into sustainable infrastructure design. By addressing critical gaps in modeling coupled environmental-mechanical degradation, the project aims to reduce long-term contamination risks while enhancing the climate resilience of geoenvironmental infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply geotechnical engineering methods, which deal with the analysis, design and construction of earth and earth supported structures, to the application of environmental problems, such as waste containment, waste disposal, construction of land fills, soil permeation, soil analysis, and soil improvement. Includes instruction in soil mechanics, soil dynamics, soil behavior, waste management and containment systems, geosynthetics, geochemistry, earth structures, geoenvironmental engineering, geotechnical engineering, earthquake engineering, and foundation engineering

abstract: Traumatic brain injuries (TBIs) present complex, heterogeneous challenges in educational settings due to the dynamic interplay of cognitive, sensory, and motor impairments. Current pedagogical strategies for TBI survivors often lack personalization and adaptability, as educators face limited tools to predict how specific interventions will interact with an individual’s evolving neurophysiological state. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to simulate and optimize individualized teaching strategies for TBI-affected learners, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model neurocognitive recovery trajectories and intervention outcomes. The research problem centers on the need for data-driven, dynamically adaptive educational plans that account for the nonlinear recovery patterns and variable responsiveness to interventions observed in TBI populations. Using anonymized neuroimaging, behavioral, and academic performance datasets from clinical-educational partnerships, we will train machine learning models to identify biomarkers of responsiveness to specific pedagogical approaches. Agent-based modeling will simulate classroom interactions, incorporating stochastic representations of TBI-related impairments (e.g., attention fluctuations, memory encoding variability) to test intervention sequences under diverse scenarios. HPC resources are essential for processing high-dimensional neurocognitive data, running parallelized simulations of long-term recovery pathways, and optimizing multi-objective outcomes (academic progress, emotional regulation, and motor skill integration). Expected outcomes include 1) a validated predictive toolkit for personalizing lesson plans and rehabilitation-education integrations, 2) generative AI models to propose context-aware instructional adaptations for educators, and 3) open-source simulation modules for teacher training programs. This work directly addresses gaps in trauma-informed pedagogical training by providing computationally derived insights into neuroplasticity-education interactions, ultimately aiming to reduce trial-and-error inefficiencies in special education settings serving TBI survivors.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Traumatic Brain Injuries
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults who are surviving and recovering from brain and brain stem injuries affecting their cognitive, perceptive, and motor functions. Includes instruction in neurophysiology and neuropathology; speech, other sensory, and motor pathologies; emotional and cognitive disabilities; physical and occupational rehabilitation techniques; developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising brain-injured students, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable food production and safety necessitates advanced computational approaches to optimize food processing and preservation techniques. This project seeks to develop a multi-scale computational framework to model microbial dynamics in complex food matrices, with a focus on spoilage organisms and pathogens under varying environmental conditions. Current predictive models lack the resolution to capture heterogeneous microenvironments within food systems, limiting their utility in designing targeted interventions. We propose integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), machine learning, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to bridge this gap. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for simulating microbial population interactions at multiple scales, from molecular-level protein-lipid interactions in cell membranes to colony-scale spatial competition. The ABM component will leverage parallel computing to simulate 10^6–10^7 individual microbial agents across dynamic physicochemical gradients, while MD simulations will characterize membrane permeability changes in response to antimicrobial compounds. A convolutional neural network (CNN) will be trained on hyperspectral imaging data of food samples to correlate simulated microbial behavior with empirical spoilage patterns. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive maps of microbial growth hotspots in heterogeneous food matrices, (2) optimized combinations of hurdle technologies (e.g., pH, temperature, preservatives) to extend shelf life, and (3) mechanistic insights into membrane-level responses to stress factors. This work will directly inform the design of energy-efficient processing protocols and reduce food waste by enabling precision preservation strategies. The computational framework will be shared as an open-source tool for the food science community, facilitating broader applications in product development and safety assurance. Successful implementation requires sustained access to GPU nodes for MD/ML workloads and high-memory nodes for large-scale ABM simulations.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: Any instructional program in food sciences and technology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of optimizing hardware-software co-design for energy-efficient edge computing systems, which are critical for supporting low-latency applications in distributed IoT networks. Current architectures struggle to balance computational performance with power constraints, particularly in dynamic environments where workload demands and resource availability fluctuate unpredictably. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a novel framework that integrates adaptive machine learning models with real-time hardware reconfiguration strategies. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate heterogeneous edge computing nodes, evaluate multi-objective optimization algorithms for task scheduling, and train neural networks to predict optimal hardware configurations under varying operational conditions. Key computational methods include large-scale Monte Carlo simulations to assess system reliability, parallelized genetic algorithms for exploring design trade-offs, and distributed deep learning pipelines to model hardware-software interactions. The project will also validate results using FPGA emulation workflows accelerated through HPC clusters. Expected outcomes include a publicly available benchmarking suite for edge computing architectures, energy-aware scheduling heuristics with provable performance bounds, and quantifiable guidelines for co-designing reconfigurable hardware with adaptive software controllers. By enabling more efficient utilization of edge resources, this work aims to directly impact emerging applications in autonomous systems and smart infrastructure while advancing methodologies for cross-layer optimization in computer engineering. The scale of simulations—requiring thousands of concurrent parameter sweeps and tera-scale dataset generation—necessitates dedicated HPC allocations to achieve statistically significant results within practical timeframes.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of computer hardware and software systems and related equipment and facilities; and the analysis of specific problems of computer applications to various tasks.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in digital rhetoric and multimodal composition, addressing the challenge of analyzing large-scale, heterogeneous datasets of written and visual texts in online environments. Current methods for studying digital writing practices, particularly in social media, collaborative platforms, and multimedia-rich educational contexts, are constrained by the limited scalability of manual text analysis and off-the-shelf computational tools. The proposed research will employ NLP techniques, machine learning models, and network analysis to examine patterns in rhetorical strategies, genre evolution, and audience engagement across diverse digital communities. Key computational tasks include training custom transformer-based models to detect rhetorical moves in multimodal texts (e.g., image-text interactions in memes or infographics), clustering discourse communities based on stylistic and argumentative features, and simulating the diffusion of compositional norms in networked writing environments. These analyses will utilize existing corpora of 10M+ public forum posts, educational portfolios, and social media artifacts, requiring GPU-accelerated processing for transformer model fine-tuning and large-scale graph computations. Anticipated outcomes include new frameworks for understanding how digital platforms reshape persuasive communication, data-driven insights into cross-cultural literacy practices, and open-source tools for computational rhetoric analysis. The project will directly inform pedagogical innovations in composition studies, particularly for teaching multimodal writing in technologically mediated contexts, while contributing methodological advances to humanities computing. By integrating HPC capabilities with humanistic inquiry, this work aims to bridge gaps between traditional rhetorical theory and the computational demands of studying contemporary digital discourse at scale.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the humanistic and scientific study of rhetoric, composition, literacy, and language/linguistic theories and their practical and pedagogical applications. Includes instruction in historical and contemporary rhetoric/composition theories; composition and criticism of written, visual, and mixed-media texts; analysis of literacy practices in cultural and cross-cultural contexts; and writing program administration.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model emergent dynamics in hybrid ecological-technological systems (HETS), where human-engineered infrastructures interact with ecological processes in nonlinear and often unpredictable ways. The research addresses a critical gap in systems science: current models often treat human and ecological systems as separate domains, limiting their ability to forecast cascading failures in scenarios such as coastal urban flooding (where stormwater infrastructure interfaces with wetland resilience) or renewable energy grids (where turbine placement impacts migratory bird behavior). Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we will integrate agent-based modeling, network theory, and stochastic differential equations to capture bidirectional feedback loops across scales. The computational approach combines real-time sensor data assimilation from IoT-enabled environmental monitors with multi-layer graph representations of infrastructure-ecology couplings. Key challenges include scaling adaptive mesh refinement for spatially heterogeneous systems and optimizing Monte Carlo simulations for rare-event probability estimation in high-dimensional parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include: (1) a modular, open-source toolkit for HETS simulation, validated against case studies in urban watershed management and agrovoltaic energy systems; (2) quantitative metrics for systemic resilience that incorporate both engineering reliability and ecological stability thresholds; (3) sensitivity analyses identifying critical leverage points for mitigating collapse risks. By unifying principles from environmental physics, control theory, and landscape ecology, this work will provide policymakers with actionable models to navigate trade-offs between technological efficiency and ecosystem conservation in complex adaptive systems. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the memory-intensive demands of coupled multiscale simulations and enabling ensemble forecasting under diverse climate and urbanization scenarios.
cip_definition: A program with a multidisciplinary approach to the analysis and solution of complex problems, requiring a combined approach using data and models from the natural, social, technological, behavioral and life sciences, and other specialized fields.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance the predictive understanding of atmospheric blocking events, persistent high-pressure systems that disrupt mid-latitude weather patterns and drive extreme events such as heatwaves, droughts, and prolonged precipitation. Current global climate models struggle to accurately simulate the frequency, duration, and spatial distribution of blocking events, limiting their utility for seasonal forecasting and climate change projections. To address this gap, we propose a high-resolution modeling study using the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model coupled with a customized spectral nudging technique, aiming to isolate the role of mesoscale processes and regional land-atmosphere interactions in blocking formation and decay. The simulations will target historical blocking episodes over the North Atlantic and Pacific sectors, with grid spacings down to 4 km to resolve critical processes like diabatic heating, cloud-microphysical feedbacks, and topographic influences. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to conduct these computationally intensive simulations, which require ~10,000 core-hours per ensemble member across multiple decades of reanalysis-driven runs. Additional workflows will employ Lagrangian trajectory analysis and machine learning-based pattern recognition to identify precursors and nonlinear interactions governing block persistence. Expected outcomes include improved parameterizations of blocking dynamics in coarser climate models and actionable insights into how anthropogenic warming may alter blocking regimes. This work directly supports climate resilience planning by reducing uncertainties in extreme weather risks. The requested allocation will enable storage and processing of ~200 TB of simulation output, leveraging parallelized Python and Fortran codes for efficient data handling. By integrating high-resolution modeling with advanced diagnostics, this project bridges critical gaps in atmospheric dynamics research while training early-career scientists in cutting-edge computational techniques.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in atmospheric sciences and meteorology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational tools to optimize dynamic, data-driven design processes in commercial and advertising art, addressing the growing demand for hyper-personalized visual content across digital platforms. Current workflows struggle to efficiently integrate real-time consumer analytics with high-fidelity artistic rendering, particularly when scaling to accommodate large datasets or complex interactive media. To bridge this gap, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining generative adversarial networks (GANs) for adaptive asset creation, Monte Carlo methods for predicting visual engagement patterns, and distributed rendering pipelines for rapid iteration. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train multi-modal machine learning models on diverse datasets of successful advertising campaigns, consumer behavior metrics, and aesthetic preference studies. Key challenges include parallel processing of high-resolution 3D visual assets, real-time style transfer across heterogeneous media formats, and maintaining artistic coherence while automating scalable variations. The computational architecture will be stress-tested using commercial-scale advertising scenarios requiring simultaneous generation of thousands of context-aware design variants. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for AI-assisted creative workflows, quantitative models correlating computational aesthetic features with audience engagement, and GPU-accelerated rendering techniques that reduce production time for complex campaigns by 40-60%. This work will establish new methodological intersections between data science and visual communication design, empowering artists to create more impactful, audience-responsive commercial art while maintaining creative control. By demonstrating how HPC resources can enhance rather than replace human-centered design processes, the project aims to redefine computational tools as collaborative partners in advertising innovation.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program in the applied visual arts that prepares individuals to use artistic techniques to effectively communicate ideas and information to business and consumer audiences via illustrations and other forms of digital or printed media. Includes instruction in concept design, layout, paste-up, and techniques such as engraving, etching, silkscreen, lithography, offset, drawing and cartooning, painting, collage, and computer graphics.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the growing complexity of optimizing cross-border digital trade compliance under fragmented and evolving regulatory frameworks. As global e-commerce expands, businesses face mounting challenges in navigating real-time compliance checks, tariff classifications, and export control screenings across jurisdictions, particularly when handling dynamic product data (e.g., software updates, AI-driven services). Traditional rule-based systems struggle to process multimodal trade documents, multilingual regulatory texts, and adaptive supply chain configurations efficiently. We propose developing a machine learning framework leveraging transformer architectures and graph neural networks to model multi-jurisdictional trade rules as interconnected decision graphs. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for training models on heterogeneous datasets spanning 150+ national regulatory corpuses, 10 million+ global trade records, and synthetic scenarios simulating emergent trade barriers. The computational workflow will integrate natural language processing for real-time regulation parsing, reinforcement learning for compliance pathway optimization, and uncertainty quantification to flag high-risk transactions. Expected outcomes include an open-source API for automated compliance scoring and a novel metric quantifying regulatory divergence costs in digital trade corridors. This work aims to reduce computational bottlenecks in cross-border decision-making while providing policymakers with simulation tools to assess the systemic impacts of new digital trade agreements. By focusing on the computational scalability of compliance systems, the project bridges gaps between international business operations, computational linguistics, and regulatory informatics—an emerging nexus requiring HPC capabilities to manage the combinatorial complexity of global digital commerce.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage international businesses and/or business operations. Includes instruction in the principles and processes of export sales, trade controls, foreign operations and related problems, monetary issues, international business policy, and applications to doing business in specific countries and markets.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize supply chain resilience and inventory management strategies for agricultural retailers and wholesalers, with a focus on mitigating disruptions caused by climate variability and fluctuating input costs. Agricultural supply chains face increasing pressure from unpredictable weather patterns, shifting pest and disease pressures, and volatile global markets for fertilizers, seeds, and equipment. Existing inventory models often fail to account for the complex interdependencies between agronomic variables, seasonal demand cycles, and multi-tier supplier networks. We propose a hybrid simulation-optimization approach integrating agent-based modeling, machine learning, and stochastic programming to analyze dynamic decision-making across agricultural supply networks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to model region-specific climate scenarios (e.g., drought probabilities, extreme weather events) alongside economic variables such as commodity price fluctuations and transportation costs. The computational workflow will leverage historical sales data, climate projection datasets, and supplier lead time records to train predictive models for input demand forecasting. Parallelized optimization routines will identify robust inventory policies that balance service-level targets with risk mitigation across decentralized distribution networks. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support toolkit for agricultural suppliers, validated through case studies with farm cooperatives in drought-prone regions. This work will advance computational methodologies for agricultural supply chain management while directly addressing operational challenges faced by retailers and wholesalers in maintaining affordable, timely access to critical farm inputs. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling memory-intensive simulations of multi-echelon distribution networks and computationally demanding scenario analyses at spatial resolutions relevant to regional agricultural economies.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_title: Agricultural/ Farm Supplies Retailing and Wholesaling
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to sell agricultural products and supplies, provide support services to agricultural enterprises, and purchase and market agricultural products. Includes instruction in basic business management, marketing, retailing and wholesaling operations, and applicable principles of agriculture and agricultural operations.

abstract: The increasing complexity of human-device interaction in assistive technologies necessitates adaptive systems capable of interpreting multimodal biological signals with low latency and high fidelity. This project seeks to develop a computational framework for real-time processing of heterogeneous sensor data—including electromyography (EMG), electroencephalography (EEG), and inertial measurement units (IMUs)—to enable responsive neuro-inspired control of wearable assistive devices. Current systems suffer from integration bottlenecks, where delays in synthesizing disparate data streams degrade usability, particularly for users with motor impairments. Leveraging a hybrid architecture combining spiking neural networks (SNNs) and transformer-based attention mechanisms, the proposed framework aims to dynamically prioritize sensor inputs based on contextual relevance and temporal criticality. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training large-scale models on aggregated biosignal datasets, simulating real-world latency scenarios, and optimizing embedded deployment parameters for resource-constrained edge devices. The computational workflow includes neuromorphic simulation via NEST, parallelized hyperparameter optimization, and hardware-in-the-loop testing using FPGA emulation. Expected outcomes include a publicly available benchmark dataset of annotated multimodal biosignals, an open-source inference pipeline for adaptive sensor fusion, and quantifiable reductions in decision latency (target: <15ms) across diverse user cohorts. By advancing the integration of event-driven and continuous-time processing paradigms, this research addresses a critical gap in personalized assistive technology while contributing novel methods for embedded AI in biomedical applications. Success will directly support the development of more intuitive human-machine interfaces, with broader implications for real-time systems in healthcare and rehabilitation robotics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of technological information systems, including computing systems, as solutions to business and research data and communications support needs. Includes instruction in the principles of computer hardware and software components, algorithms, databases, telecommunications, user tactics, application testing, and human interface design.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for optimizing the integration of biophilic design principles into urban-scale sustainable architecture. While biophilic design—centered on integrating natural systems into built environments—has gained traction in theory, its practical implementation at city scales remains constrained by the complexity of modeling dynamic ecological, social, and material interactions. Traditional simulation tools lack the capacity to holistically analyze how biophilic elements (e.g., green facades, permeable materials, habitat corridors) interact with urban microclimates, energy consumption patterns, and human behavioral dynamics over time. The research will address this gap by constructing a multi-agent simulation platform that couples parametric architectural modeling with environmental fluid dynamics, socio-spatial network analysis, and machine learning-driven optimization. High-fidelity simulations will model urban blocks under varying biophilic design scenarios, incorporating real-world climate data, material life-cycle assessments, and pedestrian mobility datasets. Computational workflows will prioritize scalability, enabling the assessment of design trade-offs across thousands of parameter combinations, from localized thermal performance to citywide biodiversity impacts. The HPC environment is critical for managing the heterogeneous data streams and parallelized simulations required to resolve feedback loops between human activity, ecological processes, and structural resilience. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible digital toolkit for urban designers, offering evidence-based thresholds for biophilic element density, material compatibility, and cost-benefit analyses aligned with IPCC sustainability targets. By bridging computational design and ecological urbanism, this work aims to establish quantifiable metrics for “living infrastructure” performance, advancing a niche intersection of sustainable architecture, computational ecology, and urban policy innovation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological, physical, and social science in the design of sustainable cities and metropolitan regions. Includes instruction in community revitalization, community economic development, construction technology, design innovation, environmental economics, ethics, justice and politics, sustainable materials, sustainability theory, structural materials, and urbanism.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the neural circuit mechanisms underlying context-dependent decision-making in rodents, with a focus on how dynamic interactions between prefrontal cortex and basal ganglia networks modulate behavioral flexibility. A critical gap persists in understanding how real-time, population-level neural activity integrates sensory cues, internal states, and learned associations to drive adaptive choices—a process frequently impaired in Parkinson’s disease and obsessive-compulsive disorder. To address this, we propose a computational neuroscience approach combining large-scale spiking neural network (SNN) simulations with analysis of in vivo electrophysiological and calcium imaging datasets. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to model networks of >100,000 neurons incorporating biophysically realistic dopamine-dependent plasticity rules, while simultaneously optimizing parameters against experimental recordings from behaving animals. The SNN architecture will replicate multiregional connectivity derived from viral tracing studies and incorporate activity-dependent fMRI signatures to bridge cellular and systems-level dynamics. Parallelized parameter sweeps will identify circuit configurations that reproduce behavioral phenotypes observed during probabilistic reward tasks. Concurrently, machine learning pipelines will process terabytes of spike-sorting and imaging data to detect state-specific oscillatory motifs and project neural trajectories into low-dimensional manifolds. By iteratively aligning model outputs with empirical data, we aim to establish how cortico-striatal communication gates exploratory versus exploitative actions through phase-amplitude coupling mechanisms. Expected outcomes include 1) a validated computational framework linking synaptic plasticity rules to network-level decision-making processes, 2) predictive models of how dopaminergic depletion alters computational hierarchies in disease states, and 3) open-source tools for simulating large-scale neural circuits with clinically translatable biomarkers. This work will advance fundamental knowledge of brain-behavior relationships while providing a platform to virtually test neuromodulation strategies for neuropsychiatric disorders.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure and function of the central and peripheral nervous system in vertebrates and invertebrates as it relates to control of behavior. Includes instruction in neuronal systems and circuits, higher level studies of behavior and cognition, computational neurobiology, and behavioral manifestations of central nervous system diseases and disorders.

abstract: The proliferation of dynamic, user-centric web applications demands increasingly sophisticated methods to optimize real-time content delivery while balancing computational efficiency and user experience. This project addresses the challenge of adaptive resource allocation for personalized multimedia streaming in large-scale, heterogeneous web environments. Traditional server-side optimization frameworks struggle to dynamically reconcile fluctuating user demand patterns, device-specific rendering constraints, and quality-of-service requirements—particularly when operating across distributed edge computing architectures. We propose a hybrid computational strategy combining graph neural networks (GNNs) with multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) to model complex dependencies between user behavior, network topology, and media encoding parameters. The research will leverage high-performance computing resources to 1) train GNNs on terabyte-scale clickstream datasets augmented with synthetic edge network topologies, 2) simulate MORL decision-making processes across millions of concurrent user sessions under varying latency constraints, and 3) validate optimization policies through discrete-event modeling of content delivery networks. Key innovations include the development of a novel attention mechanism for cross-modal feature alignment between user interaction sequences and media asset metadata, as well as a distributed training framework for MORL agents operating in partially observable network environments. Expected outcomes include an open-source optimization engine capable of reducing median page load times by 15-20% while maintaining adaptive video quality thresholds, alongside fundamental insights into computational tradeoffs in edge-based web resource management. This work bridges critical gaps between information systems design, distributed computing, and human-centered web architecture, advancing capabilities for next-generation webmaster tools in an era of exponentially growing multimedia demands.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop and maintain web servers and the hosted web pages at one or a group of web sites, and to function as designated webmasters. Includes instruction in computer systems and networks, server installation and maintenance, web page design and editing, information resources management, web policy and procedures, Internet applications of information systems security, user interfacing and usability research, and relevant management and communications skills.

abstract: The increasing prevalence of complex dermatological conditions in companion animals, such as canine atopic dermatitis, feline autoimmune skin disorders, and multi-drug-resistant cutaneous infections, demands advanced approaches to understand disease mechanisms and optimize therapies. Current clinical research faces challenges in integrating multi-modal data—including genomic, histopathological, microbiome, and environmental variables—to predict treatment outcomes or identify molecular targets. This project proposes a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model host-microbe interactions, immune responses, and genetic predispositions in veterinary dermatology. We will develop machine learning pipelines to analyze heterogeneous datasets from 1,200 clinical cases (retrospective and prospective) encompassing skin transcriptomics, 16S/ITS microbiome sequencing, and longitudinal treatment records. Agent-based models will simulate epidermal barrier dysfunction and inflammatory cascades under varying therapeutic regimens, while molecular dynamics simulations will explore ligand-receptor interactions in allergic pathways. Computational workflows will be optimized for parallel processing to handle high-dimensional data and stochastic modeling scenarios. Expected outcomes include predictive biomarkers for treatment resistance, in silico screening of novel topical therapeutics, and personalized intervention strategies for refractory cases. By establishing scalable models of cutaneous immunobiology, this work aims to reduce reliance on iterative in vivo trials and accelerate translational insights. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of multi-scale simulations that are infeasible on local clusters, particularly for parameter-space explorations of complex systems such as biofilm-mediated infections. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits for veterinary researchers, fostering collaborative innovation in dermatologic care. This project bridges clinical veterinary medicine and computational systems biology, addressing critical gaps in precision dermatology while advancing methodological paradigms for analyzing animal health data.
cip_definition: Research focused on the delivery of specialized care to animals with diseases of the skin, scales, feathers, hair, nails and mucous membranes. May included related research in dermatologic surgical procedures, cutaneous allergies, and diagnostic and therapeutic techniques.

abstract: This research seeks to address the challenge of modeling and optimizing decentralized information ecosystems in underserved rural communities, where fragmented access to digital infrastructure exacerbates disparities in healthcare and agricultural knowledge dissemination. Traditional centralized informatics approaches often fail in these contexts due to intermittent connectivity, heterogeneous data formats, and diverse user capabilities. We propose a novel computational framework integrating adaptive information architecture design with human-centered trust metrics to analyze and improve community-specific knowledge networks. The project employs agent-based modeling to simulate multi-layer interactions between human users, legacy technologies, and intermittent cloud resources, incorporating real-world data from partner communities in three geographically distinct regions. High-performance computing resources are required to handle the stochastic optimization of network topologies across thousands of parallel scenarios, particularly for simulating latency-tolerant synchronization protocols in low-connectivity environments. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify patterns in community-generated content flows, while graph neural networks will model the emergence of trust relationships within constrained information environments. Expected outcomes include a generalizable toolkit for designing resilient socio-technical systems that balance local information preservation with global knowledge integration. The computational models will advance informatics theory by formalizing metrics for "information equity" that account for technological, linguistic, and cultural dimensions of access. Results will directly inform the deployment of adaptive mobile platforms being co-developed with regional NGOs, potentially impacting over 200 rural communities currently underserved by conventional digital infrastructure solutions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on computer systems from a user-centered perspective and studies the structure, behavior and interactions of natural and artificial systems that store, process and communicate information. Includes instruction in information sciences, human computer interaction, information system analysis and design, telecommunications structure and information architecture and management.
