abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of generative design frameworks for adaptive urban microclimates, a niche interdisciplinary domain within architectural sciences. Traditional architectural simulations prioritize static environmental performance metrics (e.g., energy efficiency, thermal comfort) but lack dynamic, context-aware models that integrate real-time socio-environmental data streams, cultural behavioral patterns, and material aging processes. This gap limits the ability to design urban architectures that adaptively respond to evolving climate stressors and heterogeneous human needs. The proposed work will address this by constructing a multi-agent computational model that simulates interactions between built environments, transient microclimate conditions, and pedestrian behavior. The framework will employ a hybrid approach combining graph neural networks (GNNs) to model spatial connectivity, convolutional recurrent networks (CRNNs) to process time-series environmental data from IoT sensors, and reinforcement learning (RL) to optimize adaptive façade and circulation systems. HPC resources are critical for training these models at urban scales, requiring parallelized simulations across thousands of agent-environment interaction scenarios and high-resolution computational fluid dynamics (CFD) datasets. Expected outcomes include: (1) an open-source toolkit for simulating feedback loops between architectural interventions and localized climate impacts; (2) predictive metrics for evaluating design resilience against stochastic weather events; and (3) evidence-based protocols for deployable kinetic architectural components. By bridging architectural design, urban climatology, and computational social science methods, this work aims to establish new methodologies for context-responsive architecture while demonstrating how HPC can enable novel research trajectories in underdeveloped areas of architectural technology.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in architectural sciences and technology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Clinical pathology laboratories generate vast volumes of complex, multidimensional data from high-throughput sequencing, proteomics, and imaging technologies. However, conventional analytical workflows struggle to integrate these heterogeneous datasets efficiently, limiting the ability to uncover subtle biomarkers or model disease mechanisms with the resolution required for precision diagnostics. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a scalable computational framework for integrative analysis of clinical pathology data. The primary research objective is to identify robust molecular signatures of hematologic malignancies by combining whole-genome sequencing, flow cytometry, and immunohistochemistry data from patient cohorts. Key computational challenges include managing petabyte-scale datasets, optimizing parallelized bioinformatics pipelines for variant calling and clonal evolution analysis, and training deep learning models to correlate molecular profiles with clinical outcomes. The HPC environment will enable rapid execution of resource-intensive tasks, such as GPU-accelerated neural network training on whole-slide images and genome-wide association studies across thousands of samples. Expected outcomes include (1) novel algorithms for automated detection of minimal residual disease using multimodal data fusion, (2) predictive models linking genetic aberrations to chemotherapy response in leukemia subtypes, and (3) open-source software tools containerized for clinical laboratory deployment. Successful implementation will advance diagnostic accuracy while maintaining compliance with clinical-grade reproducibility standards. By overcoming current computational bottlenecks, this work aims to establish a paradigm for real-time, data-driven decision support in molecular pathology, directly impacting patient stratification and therapeutic monitoring. The requested HPC resources—particularly high-memory nodes, GPU clusters, and parallel file storage—are critical for processing timesensitive clinical datasets at scale, bridging the gap between research discoveries and translatable diagnostic innovations.
cip_definition: Research focused on the clinical laboratory analysis and diagnosis of disease. Includes instruction in performing clinical chemistry, cytogenetics, immunology, laboratory management, microbiology, molecular biology, quality control, serology, toxicology, and virology.

abstract: Veterinary dentistry faces significant challenges in addressing species-specific anatomical variations, complex biomechanical interactions during mastication, and the development of effective treatment protocols for diverse pathological conditions. Current approaches rely heavily on manual analysis of clinical data and small-scale experimental models, limiting our ability to characterize population-level trends, simulate complex oral biomechanics, or predict treatment outcomes across different animal species. This project proposes to develop computational models leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-modal datasets encompassing 3D dental scans, biomechanical force measurements, microbial community profiles, and longitudinal treatment outcomes from companion animals and zoo species. Machine learning approaches will be applied to identify patterns in dental wear, periodontal disease progression, and species-specific risk factors, while finite element analysis simulations will model stress distributions in abnormal occlusions and dental prostheses. A parallelized computational pipeline will integrate µCT-derived mandibular morphology data with mastication kinematics from motion capture systems, enabling species-specific comparisons at unprecedented resolution. The HPC environment is critical for processing terabytes of multi-center clinical data, running iterative simulations of biomechanical interactions, and training deep learning models on heterogeneous imaging datasets. Expected outcomes include predictive models for early detection of malocclusion syndromes in brachycephalic breeds, optimized dental implant designs for large carnivores, and computational frameworks for evaluating antimicrobial treatment efficacy against oral biofilm communities. Results will be disseminated through an open-access simulation toolkit to support evidence-based treatment planning in veterinary dental practice. This work will establish new computational methodologies for translational oral health research while addressing critical gaps in veterinary dental care capacity across clinical and conservation contexts.
cip_definition: Research focused on the application of dental care procedures to the teeth, eating surfaces, and oral cavities of animals. May included related research in the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases and abnormalities of animal teeth and gums and related parts of the oral cavity; and related anatomical and physiological principles.

abstract: Administrators in international schools operate within complex, dynamic environments shaped by globalization, multicultural student populations, and diverse regulatory frameworks. Traditional decision-making models often fail to account for the interdependencies among cultural, pedagogical, and logistical factors, leading to suboptimal resource allocation and policy outcomes. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework to simulate and analyze the systemic challenges faced by international school leaders. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will construct agent-based models that replicate stakeholder interactions across varied cultural and institutional contexts. These models will integrate multi-source data—including enrollment patterns, staff mobility, budget cycles, and accreditation requirements—to test scenarios such as curriculum adaptation to demographic shifts, crisis response strategies, and equitable resource distribution. Machine learning algorithms will further identify predictive patterns in administrative decision outcomes across geographically dispersed schools. The computational intensity of simulating thousands of agent interactions and processing transnational datasets necessitates cluster computing capabilities for parallel processing and large-scale optimization. Expected outcomes include an open-access decision support toolkit for administrators, validated through case studies with the Council of International Schools network. By quantifying the impact of cultural variables on leadership effectiveness and institutional sustainability, this research aims to advance evidence-based practices in international education administration while establishing computational social science methodologies as critical tools for 21st-century educational leadership.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and practice of administration in international schools, the study of international education as an object of applied research, and which may prepare individuals to function as administrators in such settings. Includes instruction in culture in the classroom, educational leadership, globalization, instructional design and technology, international research methods, evaluation, and education policy.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize the design of adaptive communal spaces in healthcare environments, integrating architectural principles with epidemiological and behavioral dynamics to mitigate pathogen transmission while supporting patient well-being. Traditional healthcare design prioritizes static layouts, but emerging evidence suggests that dynamic, responsive environments—tailored to real-time occupancy, activity patterns, and pathogen loads—could reduce infection risks without compromising therapeutic benefits of social interaction. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how spatial configurations, material properties, and human movement interact to influence airborne disease spread in settings such as hospital atria, rehabilitation centers, and long-term care facilities. Using agent-based modeling (ABM) coupled with computational fluid dynamics (CFD), we will simulate pathogen dispersion under diverse design scenarios, incorporating variables such as ventilation efficiency, surface porosity, and occupant density. Machine learning algorithms will identify optimal spatial reconfigurations and material selections under evolving conditions, validated against empirical data from sensor-equipped pilot environments. The computational workflow requires parallelized simulations across thousands of parameter combinations to capture nonlinear interactions between design variables and health outcomes. Expected outcomes include predictive models for infection-resistant space planning, a framework for real-time adaptive design interventions, and evidence-based guidelines for material innovation in high-risk settings. By bridging architecture, environmental health, and computational science, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for designing health-promoting built environments that dynamically respond to public health challenges. The HPC resources are essential to handle the high-dimensional parameter space, stochastic variability in human behavior, and fine-grained spatial-temporal resolution required for robust, generalizable insights.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the impact of design and architecture on the health of individuals and larger populations, and how to create settings that promote health, healing, and well-being. Includes instruction in architecture, interior design, human health services, communication studies, medical and clinical innovations, behavioral and engineering sciences, hospitals and health systems, and environmental conditions that influence health.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the impact of enrollment trends, demographic shifts, and financial aid policies on institutional sustainability in higher education. As universities face mounting pressures from fluctuating enrollment patterns, changing student demographics, and evolving funding landscapes, administrators require predictive tools to optimize resource allocation and strategic planning. Traditional linear models often fail to capture the dynamic interdependencies between these variables, limiting their utility for decision-making. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled agent-based modeling (ABM) approach that simulates multi-year enrollment scenarios under varying policy and economic conditions. The model will integrate institutional datasets (e.g., applicant demographics, financial aid awards, retention rates) with external data sources (e.g., labor market trends, census projections) to simulate student decision-making processes, institutional revenue streams, and operational costs. Machine learning algorithms will be employed to refine parameter estimation and validate model outputs against historical patterns. By leveraging parallel computing capabilities, we aim to run thousands of parameterized scenarios to identify optimal financial aid distribution strategies, predict enrollment cliffs, and quantify the fiscal impacts of alternative tuition models. Expected outcomes include a scalable tool for higher education administrators to proactively address enrollment challenges, mitigate financial risks, and evaluate equity implications of policy changes. The computational intensity of simulating diverse student populations and longitudinal interactions necessitates access to HPC resources for memory-intensive simulations and rapid iteration. This work aligns with national priorities in higher education administration by advancing data-driven approaches to institutional resilience while addressing critical gaps in predictive analytics for enrollment management and strategic finance.
detailed_field: Higher education and community college administration
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and practice of administration in four-year colleges, universities and higher education systems, the study of higher education as an object of applied research, and which may prepare individuals to function as administrators in such settings. Includes instruction in higher education economics and finance; policy and planning studies; curriculum; faculty and labor relations; higher education law; college student services; research on higher education; institutional research; marketing and promotion; and issues of evaluation, accountability and philosophy.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the transnational circulation of cultural narratives within the British Commonwealth, focusing on underrepresented voices in postcolonial literary and archival materials. The research problem centers on identifying patterns of cultural exchange, adaptation, and resistance across Commonwealth nations through large-scale textual and multimedia corpora spanning the 20th and 21st centuries. Current scholarship lacks systematic methodologies for tracing how shared sociocultural themes—such as hybrid identities, diasporic memory, and decolonial discourse—evolve across linguistic, geographic, and temporal boundaries. To address this gap, the project will employ computational text analysis, multilingual semantic modeling, and network graph algorithms to process over 10 million pages of digitized novels, periodicals, oral histories, and visual media from institutional repositories in six Commonwealth countries. HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based language models on low-resource creole and postcolonial English variants, clustering thematic trajectories across heterogeneous datasets, and visualizing dynamic knowledge networks. Expected outcomes include (1) a novel framework for mapping intercultural dialogue in Commonwealth studies, (2) open-access tools for corpus-based analysis of narrative transmission, and (3) new insights into gender- and ethnicity-mediated cultural production in regions transitioning from colonial dependency to globalized nationhood. By integrating computational methods with critical theory from cultural and group studies, this work will advance interdisciplinary approaches to understanding collective memory and identity formation in pluralistic societies. The scale of data processing, parallelized model training, and real-time network rendering necessitate dedicated GPU nodes, distributed storage, and high-memory capacity to achieve research objectives within proposed timelines.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples and countries comprising components of the historical British Empire and modern British Commonwealth, including migration patterns, shared sociocultural and political features and problems, and contemporary relations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance community psychology research by modeling the dynamics of social change and evaluating intervention strategies in complex community systems. The research problem centers on understanding how multi-level interventions—such as community-wide education campaigns or policy-driven resource redistribution—interact with cultural, ecological, and systemic factors to mitigate social pathologies (e.g., systemic inequities, community trauma). Traditional analytical methods struggle to capture the nonlinear, interdependent relationships inherent in these systems, particularly when scaling to real-world population sizes or incorporating longitudinal data. To address this gap, we propose a computational approach integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) and network analysis to simulate community interactions under varying intervention scenarios. The ABM framework will parameterize individual and institutional agents using empirical data from public health records, community surveys, and social service databases, incorporating variables such as cultural stress, access to resources, and social network structures. HPC resources are critical for scaling these simulations to represent populations of 100,000+ agents, enabling real-time analysis of emergent group behaviors and systemic outcomes. Machine learning techniques will further identify patterns in intervention efficacy across diverse demographic and cultural contexts. Expected outcomes include predictive models that quantify the impact of prevention strategies on community resilience, as well as actionable insights for optimizing resource allocation in social services. By elucidating how intervention timing, targeting, and cultural adaptation influence large-scale social change, this work aims to equip practitioners and policymakers with evidence-based tools to address systemic inequities. The project aligns with community psychology’s emphasis on primary prevention and ecological systems theory, while advancing computational social science methodologies through scalable, open-source modeling frameworks.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply psychological principles to the analysis of social problems, and the implementation of intervention strategies for addressing these problems. Includes instruction in social ecology, primary and secondary prevention of social pathologies, social intervention strategies and tactics, large group counseling, social services systems behavior, creating settings, cultural stress, and the dynamics of social change.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research on cultural exchange and urbanization in the ancient Mediterranean and Near East (circa 2000 BCE–500 CE). Traditional archaeological and textual analyses struggle to synthesize the vast, fragmented datasets—including cuneiform tablets, ceramic distributions, architectural remains, and climate proxy records—that document interconnected regional systems. The research problem centers on modeling how environmental constraints, resource networks, and ideological practices shaped the growth and decline of urban hubs. A computational approach is critical to integrate multi-source spatial, temporal, and textual data at scales unachievable through manual methods. The project will develop agent-based models (ABMs) simulating trade dynamics and demographic shifts, paired with natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to analyze semantic patterns in Akkadian, Greek, and Latin corpora. These will be cross-referenced with geospatial analyses of settlement patterns derived from satellite imagery and legacy excavation records using machine learning (ML) classifiers. HPC resources will enable iterative parameter testing across hypothetical scenarios (e.g., drought impacts on Hittite grain distribution) and large-scale corpus comparisons to trace cultural transmission. Expected outcomes include: (1) dynamic visualizations of interaction networks across Anatolia, Mesopotamia, and the Levant; (2) quantitative frameworks to assess the role of maritime vs. overland routes in sustaining urban systems; and (3) open-access tools for diachronic analysis of multilingual textual traditions. By bridging archaeological, philological, and environmental datasets through computationally intensive methods, this work will provide novel insights into resilience and connectivity in premodern societies, while establishing scalable digital methodologies for humanities scholarship. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated ML training, high-memory simulations of population movements, and parallel processing of 3D artifact scans across a projected 12-month workflow.
cip_title: Classical, Ancient Mediterranean, and Near Eastern Studies and Archaeology
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the classical ancient civilizations of the ancient Near East, Europe, and the Mediterranean Sea, such as Athens, Anatolia, Egypt, Greece, Israel, Mesopotamia, North Africa, and Rome. Includes instruction in ancient languages, ancient history, archaeology, anthropology, Greek and Roman mythology, philosophy, and religion.

abstract: Environmental law enforcement agencies face increasing challenges in monitoring and mitigating complex threats to natural ecosystems, such as illegal resource extraction, habitat encroachment, and pollution events. Traditional surveillance and compliance verification methods often lack the capacity to integrate multi-scale environmental data streams or predict emerging risks in dynamic landscapes. This project proposes to develop a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze heterogeneous datasets—including satellite imagery, climate models, species population trends, and real-time sensor networks—for proactive threat detection and enforcement prioritization. Machine learning models will be trained to identify patterns indicative of illicit activities, while agent-based simulations will evaluate the effectiveness of patrol strategies under varying ecological and socioeconomic conditions. Spatial-temporal analytics will map high-risk zones using historical violation records and environmental vulnerability indices. The computational pipeline will optimize emergency response protocols for wildfire containment and ecological damage mitigation through fluid dynamics modeling of pollutant dispersion and fire spread. Expected outcomes include predictive risk assessment tools to guide field operations, evidence-based policy recommendations for regulatory adjustments, and open-source algorithms for environmental monitoring. By enabling rapid processing of petabyte-scale datasets and complex system simulations, this research aims to transform reactive enforcement paradigms into anticipatory conservation strategies, ultimately strengthening the protection of critical ecosystems and human communities dependent on their services.
detailed_field: Environmental/ natural resources management and policy
cip_title: Environmental/ Natural Resources Law Enforcement and Protective Services
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to enforce natural resource and environmental protection regulations and laws; and to perform emergency duties to protect human life, property and natural resources, including fire prevention and control measures, and emergency and rescue procedures. Includes instruction in natural and physical sciences, natural resource management, outdoor field skills, firearms and outdoor equipment and vehicle operation, evidence collection and environmental sampling and monitoring, natural resource legislation, environmental compliance techniques, patrol procedures, investigation and report writing, interpersonal skills and crisis intervention, community liaison, public safety, public education, and public relations. Note: this program was re-instated after being deleted from CIP 2000; previously, it was coded as 03.0203.

abstract: The project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the role of submesoscale ocean dynamics—processes occurring at scales of 1-10 km—in mediating vertical nutrient fluxes and phytoplankton productivity in oligotrophic regions. While these processes are hypothesized to significantly influence marine ecosystem resilience and carbon export, their transient nature and fine spatial resolution have made them challenging to observe or simulate accurately. This research proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to run a series of nested ocean circulation-biogeochemistry models at unprecedented resolution (horizontal grid ≤ 500 m) across the subtropical Pacific. The computational framework will integrate the MIT General Circulation Model (MITgcm) with a biogeochemical module tracking multiple nutrient species and phytoplankton functional types, explicitly resolving submesoscale instabilities, fronts, and eddy-wind interactions. Simulations will be forced with reanalysis atmospheric data and validated against autonomous underwater vehicle transects and satellite-derived productivity metrics. The HPC demand arises from the need to concurrently handle ~20 million grid cells, adaptive time-stepping for numerical stability, and ensemble runs spanning interannual climate variability (El Niño/La Niña cycles). Anticipated outcomes include quantifying the contribution of submesoscale features to annual primary production budgets and identifying thresholds in wind-forcing regimes that enhance vertical nutrient supply. Results will directly inform the scalability of Earth system model parameterizations and provide mechanistic insights into how climate-driven changes in ocean stratification may alter productivity in nutrient-limited ecosystems. The generated datasets, comprising 500+ TB of 4D hydrodynamic and biogeochemical fields, will be curated for community reuse in model intercomparison studies. This work underscores the necessity of HPC resources to bridge observational limitations and advance predictive capacity for marine biogeochemical cycles under global change.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the ocean/marine sciences, not elsewhere classified.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable Bayesian hierarchical models for high-dimensional spatiotemporal data, addressing computational bottlenecks in uncertainty quantification for complex statistical inference. Modern applications in epidemiology, environmental monitoring, and public policy increasingly demand models that integrate large, heterogeneous datasets with spatially and temporally varying parameters. However, conventional Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods suffer from prohibitive computational costs when applied to such high-dimensional settings, limiting their utility for real-time decision-making. To overcome these challenges, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) with distributed variational inference, optimized for parallelization on high-performance computing (HPC) clusters. The approach leverages GPU-accelerated tensor operations for gradient calculations and implements domain decomposition strategies to partition spatial grids across nodes, reducing memory constraints. A key innovation involves adaptive tuning of proposal distributions using stochastic optimization, which minimizes convergence time in hierarchical models with thousands of latent variables. The computational workflow will be validated on synthetic data with known ground truth and applied to a case study analyzing climate-driven disease spread across urban networks, integrating satellite-derived environmental variables and anonymized health records. Expected outcomes include (1) open-source software for efficient Bayesian inference on spatiotemporal problems, (2) benchmarks comparing computational scalability across HPC architectures, and (3) novel statistical insights into uncertainty propagation in multi-scale epidemiological models. By enabling faster convergence and lower memory overhead than existing MCMC toolkits, this work will advance the practical feasibility of fully Bayesian approaches for large-scale public health interventions. The requested computing resources are critical for testing distributed memory configurations and optimizing load balancing across up to 256 nodes, given the project’s emphasis on weak scaling to terabyte-scale datasets.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the relationships between groups of measurements, and similarities and differences, using probability theory and techniques derived from it. Includes instruction in the principles in probability theory, binomial distribution, regression analysis, standard deviation, stochastic processes, Monte Carlo method, Bayesian statistics, non-parametric statistics, sampling theory, and statistical techniques.

abstract: The safe and efficient operation of advanced nuclear reactors requires high-fidelity multiphysics simulations to address complex, coupled phenomena in neutron transport, thermal-fluid dynamics, and structural mechanics. Current modeling approaches for lead-cooled fast reactors (LFRs) often rely on simplified approximations due to computational limitations, introducing uncertainties in predicting thermal striping, coolant-solid interactions, and long-term material degradation under extreme neutron flux and temperature gradients. This project seeks to develop a scalable, high-resolution computational framework to resolve these multiphysics interactions at unprecedented spatial and temporal scales, enabling the optimization of LFR fuel assembly designs and safety systems. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement a hybrid Monte Carlo–computational fluid dynamics (CFD) methodology with adaptive mesh refinement, coupling OpenMC and NekRS via in-memory data transfer to minimize latency. Machine learning surrogates will accelerate uncertainty quantification for transient scenarios, including loss-of-flow accidents and coolant contamination events. Key challenges include managing the heterogeneous computing requirements of neutron transport (particle-based) and CFD (spectral element) solvers while maintaining numerical stability across differing time-stepping schemes. The proposed simulations will generate terabyte-scale datasets characterizing localized stress-corrosion cracking risks in cladding materials and identifying flow-induced vibration hotspots in helical coil steam generators. Outcomes will directly inform the design of a prototypical 100 MW LFR test facility under development by an international consortium, reducing reliance on physical mockups for regulatory validation. This work bridges gaps between traditional nuclear engineering and emerging computational techniques, advancing predictive capabilities for next-generation reactor systems while establishing open-source benchmarks for multiphysics integration in HPC environments. Successful implementation will enhance the viability of LFRs as low-carbon baseload power sources, supporting global decarbonization goals.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems for controlling and manipulating nuclear energy, including nuclear power plant design, fission reactor design, fusion reactor design, reactor control and safety systems design, power transfer systems, containment vessels and structures design; and the analysis of related engineering problems such as fission and fusion processes, human and environmental factors, construction, and operational considerations.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive modeling framework for optimizing personalized care plans for individuals with developmental disabilities. Current approaches to designing these plans rely heavily on qualitative assessments and manual data integration, leading to inefficiencies in adapting interventions to evolving needs. The research problem centers on the computational challenges of synthesizing heterogeneous data—including longitudinal behavioral records, sensory processing profiles, and environmental context data—into dynamic, actionable models that can predict individual responses to specific support strategies. The project will employ machine learning techniques, particularly hybrid architectures combining transformer-based temporal modeling with graph neural networks, to analyze multimodal datasets spanning neurodiversity cohorts. Computational workflows will prioritize privacy-preserving federated learning to handle sensitive health data, while agent-based simulations will test hypothetical intervention scenarios in silico. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source toolkit for generating evidence-based recommendations to guide developmental services workers in tailoring communication, skill-building activities, and community integration supports. By enabling real-time analysis of complex behavioral patterns and environmental interactions, this work aims to establish a novel computational paradigm for disability support services—one that bridges gaps between developmental psychology, assistive technology design, and data-driven decision-making. The requested HPC resources are critical for training large-scale models on distributed datasets and running parallelized simulations of intervention efficacy across diverse virtual cohorts, tasks that exceed the capacity of standard institutional computing infrastructure. Successful implementation could transform how developmental services workers allocate limited resources while maintaining responsiveness to individual needs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply practical knowledge and skills to support individuals with a variety of physical, mental or developmental disabilities in a family or community setting. Includes instruction in health care, basic nutrition, pharmacology, nursing, autism, mental health, psychology, sociology, behavioral analysis, communication, intervention, counseling and community services, and developmental services, such as literacy and life skills training.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive modeling framework to optimize the lifecycle management and hazard mitigation of aging munitions systems, with a focus on corrosion-induced degradation in storage environments. The primary research problem centers on the lack of high-fidelity computational tools capable of simulating complex interactions between environmental variables, material properties, and ordnance geometries over multi-decadal timescales. Current empirical approaches struggle to account for localized microclimate variations, heterogeneous material responses, and emergent failure modes in mixed munitions stockpiles. The proposed computational approach integrates multi-physics simulations (combining computational fluid dynamics, electrochemical reaction modeling, and structural mechanics) with machine learning techniques to predict corrosion propagation paths and critical failure thresholds. High-performance computing resources will enable parametric studies across diverse environmental scenarios (humidity, temperature fluctuations, chemical exposure) while maintaining resolution at sub-millimeter scales for critical interfaces. A novel adaptive meshing strategy will be implemented to balance accuracy and computational cost across spatial and temporal domains. The research will leverage existing materials degradation datasets from military repositories while generating new validation benchmarks through parallel physical experiments on surrogate systems. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool for prioritizing munitions inspections, optimizing storage configurations, and forecasting maintenance requirements with quantified uncertainty bounds. This work addresses a critical gap in ordnance sustainment by transitioning from reactive to predictive maintenance paradigms, directly supporting Department of Defense priorities for readiness enhancement and risk reduction in legacy weapons systems. The computational framework will be designed for eventual integration with DoD logistics platforms, providing a template for data-driven asset management in specialized military applications.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, technology and maintenance of ground or sea-based weapons systems, ordinance and munitions. Includes instruction in basic sciences, electronics, systems technology, fluid power, computer science, conventional weapons systems, nuclear weapons systems, munitions systems, storage and safety, equipment operation, guidance and control systems, hazardous materials, corrosion control, nondestructive testing and quality control, and maintenance management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to model and optimize phonon-mediated thermal transport in nanostructured quantum circuits, a critical challenge in advancing scalable quantum computing architectures. While quantum coherence and entanglement dynamics are well-studied, the engineering of thermal dissipation pathways in superconducting qubit arrays remains poorly understood, particularly at the intersection of quantum device physics and nanoscale heat transfer. Current analytical models fail to capture the anisotropic phonon scattering effects and non-equilibrium thermal gradients inherent to multilayer superconducting circuits operating at cryogenic temperatures. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a multiscale simulation approach combining ab initio density functional theory (DFT) calculations of phonon dispersion in superconducting materials with finite-element modeling of transient heat flow across heterogeneous interfaces. The workflow will integrate GPU-accelerated molecular dynamics simulations to resolve defect-mediated phonon scattering at material boundaries, coupled with Monte Carlo methods for probabilistic heat flux mapping in 3D circuit geometries. By parameterizing temperature-dependent quasiparticle generation rates and their impact on qubit decoherence times, this framework aims to establish design principles for thermally resilient quantum processors. The computational outcomes will directly inform experimental collaborations focused on epitaxial growth of low-disorder heterostructures, with potential to reduce thermal noise-induced error rates by an order of magnitude. This research bridges quantum engineering and thermal sciences, addressing a critical roadblock in quantum hardware scalability while advancing computational methodologies for coupled quantum-thermal systems.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the use of physics principles in the analysis and evaluation of engineering problems and other scientific applications. Includes instruction in high- and low-temperature phenomena, computational physics, superconductivity, applied thermodynamics, molecular and particle physics applications, and space science research.

abstract: Clinical research trials generate vast multimodal datasets, yet current analytical workflows often fail to integrate real-time physiological, behavioral, and patient-reported outcomes at scale. This project proposes developing a high-performance computing (HPC) framework to analyze dynamic interactions between wearable device metrics, electronic health record (EHR) data, and adaptive patient feedback in decentralized clinical trials. The research addresses critical gaps in processing temporally dense biosensor data (e.g., continuous glucose monitoring, actigraphy) alongside irregularly sampled EHR entries and qualitative patient inputs—a computational challenge requiring parallelized architectures. Our approach combines graph neural networks to model temporal dependencies in heterogeneous data streams with federated learning techniques to preserve participant privacy across distributed trial sites. The HPC environment will enable simultaneous training of multiple predictive models examining (1) early warning signals for adverse event prediction using anomaly detection in high-frequency biosensor data, and (2) personalized intervention timing optimization through reinforcement learning simulations. A custom workflow manager will orchestrate containerized analyses across GPU nodes, integrating raw data from OpenClinica, Fitbit API, and REDCap platforms. Expected outcomes include an open-source pipeline for multimodal clinical trial analytics, validated against three ongoing neurology trials (n=420 participants) measuring intervention efficacy in epilepsy and migraine management. This resource will empower clinical research coordinators to identify subpopulation response patterns, optimize monitoring protocols, and reduce computational bottlenecks in complex trial designs. By enabling real-time analysis of terabyte-scale datasets, the project advances precision medicine capabilities while maintaining regulatory compliance through auditable data provenance tracking—a critical requirement in therapeutic development.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for careers as clinical research administrators or clinical research coordinators where they work under the supervision of a Principal Investigator to organize, coordinate and administer clinical research trials. Includes instruction in pharmacology, medical terminology, foundations of clinical research, project management, ethics, research design and data management, and legal and regulatory compliance .

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of regulatory compliance frameworks by developing a computational model to simulate and predict the cascading impacts of multi-jurisdictional legal changes on organizational compliance strategies. The research problem centers on the dynamic, interdependent nature of modern compliance obligations, where updates to financial regulations, data privacy laws, and industry-specific mandates create compound effects that traditional legal analysis struggles to anticipate. Using high-performance computing resources, the project will process and analyze 1.2+ terabytes of structured and unstructured regulatory data spanning 15 jurisdictions, including legislative texts, enforcement actions, and case law from 2010–2024. Computational methods will combine natural language processing (NLP) for semantic analysis of legal amendments with graph-based network modeling to map dependencies between regulatory clauses. A machine learning layer will train on historical compliance violation patterns to identify high-risk intersections between evolving requirements. The proposed simulations will model hypothetical regulatory change scenarios, quantifying their potential operational impacts through probabilistic risk scoring. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for compliance officers to visualize regulatory exposure hotspots and test mitigation strategies under varying conditions. By bridging computational social science methods with legal informatics, this work aims to advance predictive capabilities in compliance risk management while establishing scalable methodologies for analyzing large-scale legal systems. The requested computing resources are critical for maintaining low-latency processing of real-time regulatory updates and enabling complex network analyses that exceed the capacity of standard legal research platforms.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations for lawyers and non-legal professionals in compliance, ethics, internal monitoring, regulatory affairs, and related areas.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational musicology research focused on large-scale analysis of cross-cultural musical patterns and their evolution. The core challenge lies in processing and interpreting vast, heterogeneous music datasets—including audio recordings, symbolic notation, and ethnographic metadata—to identify structural and stylistic relationships across global traditions. Traditional methods lack the scalability to analyze such datasets, particularly when integrating multimodal inputs (e.g., audio, text, and performance context) or modeling temporal shifts in musical practices over decades. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining signal processing, machine learning, and network analysis. Audio recordings will be processed using parallelized spectral feature extraction (e.g., chroma vectors, MFCCs) and transformer-based models for melodic motif detection. Symbolic data (MIDI, sheet music) will undergo graph-theoretic analysis to map harmonic and rhythmic networks, while NLP techniques will parse textual metadata for cultural and historical context. A federated learning pipeline will then correlate these modalities to identify latent patterns, supported by HPC-enabled simulations of cultural transmission dynamics. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible database of annotated cross-cultural musical features, (2) novel algorithms for detecting stylistic convergence/divergence in music history, and (3) computational evidence supporting or revising existing theories of globalized musical exchange. This work directly supports curricular goals in music theory and ethnomusicology by providing data-driven tools to analyze repertoire diversity, while advancing methodological innovation in computational performing arts research. The scale of data (≥50 TB audio, 10M+ symbolic scores) and complexity of real-time feature alignment across distributed nodes necessitate HPC infrastructure for feasible execution, particularly GPU clusters for deep learning workflows and high-memory nodes for large-network computations.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the introductory study and appreciation of music and the performing arts. Includes instruction in music, dance, and other performing arts media.

abstract: Endocrine signaling pathways play a critical role in hormone-driven cancers, yet the dynamic mechanisms by which endocrine factors regulate tumor progression remain poorly characterized. This project seeks to address the gap in understanding how hormone-receptor interactions and downstream signaling cascades influence cellular communication and protein secretion within tumor microenvironments. Specifically, we aim to model the spatiotemporal dynamics of endocrine-mediated cellular regulation in breast and prostate cancers, where dysregulated hormone signaling is a known driver of oncogenesis. A key challenge lies in integrating heterogeneous experimental datasets—including hormone secretion rates, receptor trafficking patterns, and intracellular signaling kinetics—into a unified computational framework. To achieve this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale simulations that couple agent-based models of endocrine-responsive tumor cells with continuum-scale representations of extracellular hormone gradients. These simulations will incorporate empirical data from live-cell imaging and radioautography studies to parameterize membrane biogenesis, protein secretion dynamics, and ligand-receptor binding affinities. The computational pipeline will further employ sensitivity analyses to identify critical regulatory nodes in endocrine signaling networks that may serve as therapeutic targets. By resolving the interplay between endocrine factor diffusion, cellular uptake, and intracellular signaling kinetics, this work will elucidate mechanisms underlying hormone resistance in metastatic cancers. Expected outcomes include predictive models of endocrine-driven tumor progression and actionable insights into microenvironmental conditions that amplify or suppress oncogenic signaling. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the high-dimensional parameter space, iterative model optimization, and large-scale simulation batches required to achieve statistical robustness. This research directly aligns with the program’s focus on endocrine physiology and cellular communication, advancing translational applications in oncology while avoiding overlap with excluded computational biology domains.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the composition, manufacture, and secretion of protein compounds by cells and glands and the role of endocrine substances in bodily processes. Includes instruction in protein chemistry, protein secretion, membrane biogenesis and transfer methods, cellular communication, gene and cell regulation, cytochemistry, fractionation, radioautography, and applications such as neuroendocrinology.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a data-driven computational framework to optimize the design of personalized educational interventions for individuals with multiple disabilities (MD). Students with MD exhibit heterogeneous combinations of sensory, motor, cognitive, and socioemotional impairments, making it challenging to generalize effective teaching strategies across individuals. Current approaches to creating individualized education programs (IEPs) rely heavily on educator expertise and qualitative assessments, which may overlook complex interactions between disabilities and limit scalability. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multimodal educational datasets—including behavioral, physiological, and learning outcome data—and simulate intervention efficacy across diverse disability profiles. Machine learning models will be trained on anonymized student records and real-time classroom interaction data to identify patterns linking specific disability combinations, instructional methods, and learning outcomes. Agent-based modeling will simulate how varying classroom environments and assistive technologies interact with individual student profiles. The computational workload requires parallel processing of high-dimensional data (e.g., eye-tracking, gesture recognition, and biometric signals) and large-scale parameter sweeps to evaluate intervention scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for generating evidence-based IEP recommendations, validated against longitudinal classroom data from three special education schools. This work will provide educators with a predictive framework to anticipate student needs, reduce trial-and-error in intervention design, and improve resource allocation for assistive technologies. By quantifying relationships between multidimensional disabilities and pedagogical strategies, the project aims to advance precision education paradigms in special needs teaching while maintaining strict ethical standards for student data privacy.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Multiple Disabilities
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with multiple disabilities which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with multiple disabilities, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising students with multiple handicaps, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: Acupuncture and Oriental Medicine (AOM) integrates traditional diagnostic and therapeutic practices with modern biomedical principles, yet the systemic mechanisms underlying its efficacy remain underexplored at a multiscale biological level. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the complex physiological and biochemical interactions modulated by acupuncture and herbal interventions. The research problem centers on the lack of computational frameworks capable of simulating the dynamic effects of acupuncture point stimulation on neural, circulatory, and immune networks, as well as the pharmacodynamics of multi-herb formulations. To resolve this, we propose multiscale molecular dynamics simulations to characterize how mechanical needle manipulation influences cellular ion channels and cytokine signaling pathways, coupled with machine learning analysis of clinical datasets to correlate acupuncture parameters (depth, stimulation technique) with patient-reported outcomes. For herbal research, ensemble docking and network pharmacology models will predict herb-target interactions and evaluate synergy within classical formulas. These computational workflows demand significant parallel processing and memory allocation due to the scale of omics data integration and real-time visualization of biomechanical responses. Anticipated outcomes include mechanistic insights into AOM’s role in pain modulation and autonomic regulation, predictive models for optimizing point selection and herbal synergies, and a publicly accessible simulation toolkit for training practitioners. By elucidating AOM’s scientific foundations through computational rigor, this work aims to strengthen its evidence-based integration into multidisciplinary care, advancing both traditional knowledge and precision health innovation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of acupuncture, a Chinese system of health care and healing based on the use of pulse diagnosis, acupuncture point selection, and needle insertion, as well as herbs and other Asian treatment modalities. Includes instruction in basic Western medical sciences, Asian philosophy, Chinese medical anatomy and physiology, Chinese herbs, diagnostic techniques, patient observation and communication, acupuncture points and point selection, acupuncture techniques, acupuncture treatment of disease, pain management, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design and assembly processes of prefabricated metal structures, addressing critical challenges in efficiency, structural performance, and cost-effectiveness. Current methods for assembling industrial and commercial metal buildings rely heavily on generalized codes and manual calculations, which often lead to over-engineering, material waste, or suboptimal load distribution under dynamic environmental conditions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach to simulate and analyze the behavior of metal building systems across diverse configurations and stress scenarios. The research will employ finite element analysis (FEA) to model complex interactions between prefabricated components, including nonlinear effects from wind, seismic activity, and thermal expansion. Machine learning algorithms will be integrated to iteratively refine structural designs, balancing material usage, fabrication constraints, and safety margins. Additionally, parametric studies will evaluate assembly workflows to identify bottlenecks in component alignment and fastening techniques. By leveraging GPU-accelerated computing resources, these simulations will process high-resolution 3D models of entire building assemblies, incorporating real-world variability in material properties and geometric tolerances. The outcomes will include an open-access database of optimized design templates, predictive tools for assembly time estimation, and recommendations for code updates to reflect performance-based criteria. This work is expected to reduce construction costs by up to 20% for typical metal structures while improving compliance with evolving sustainability standards. The computational pipeline will also serve as an educational resource for training students in advanced simulation methods, bridging gaps between traditional metalworking practices and data-driven engineering. Successful implementation of this project will position metal building assembly as a leader in adopting HPC for industrial applications within the technical trades.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to construct industrial, storage, and commercial metal structures using prefabricated framing and siding components. Includes instruction in sheet metal working, ironworking, assembly and fastening techniques, blueprint reading, site preparation, structural design principles, safety, and applicable codes and regulations.

abstract: Current nutritional frameworks often fail to account for the dynamic interplay between dietary components, host physiology, and environmental factors, leading to suboptimal dietary recommendations. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a multi-scale computational model that integrates heterogeneous datasets spanning food chemistry, gut microbiota activity, and host metabolic responses. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will employ agent-based modeling and machine learning to simulate nutrient metabolism at the individual level, incorporating variability in enzymatic activity, microbial community dynamics, and epigenetic modifications. The computational framework will process high-resolution mass spectrometry data from food metabolomics, metagenomic sequences of gut microbiomes, and longitudinal health metrics from clinical cohorts. By simulating interactions across these scales, the project aims to predict personalized nutrient bioavailability and metabolic outcomes under varying dietary patterns. The expected outcomes include a novel computational platform capable of generating tailored dietary strategies that optimize health outcomes based on individual biochemical profiles. This resource will provide actionable insights for precision nutrition, addressing challenges in metabolic syndrome, micronutrient deficiencies, and diet-related chronic diseases. The integration of HPC-driven simulations with translational nutrition science represents a significant advancement, enabling the exploration of complex, non-linear relationships that traditional reductionist approaches cannot capture. Ultimately, this work will establish a foundation for data-driven dietary interventions, bridging gaps between agricultural production, food science, and individualized healthcare.
cip_definition: A scientific program that focuses on the utilization of food for human growth and metabolism, in both normal and dysfunctional states, from the interdisciplinary perspective of the agricultural, human, biological, and biomedical sciences. Includes instruction in food science, biochemistry, physiology, dietetics, food and nutrition studies, biotechnology, biophysics, and the clinical sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize decision-making frameworks for household resource allocation under dynamic socioeconomic stressors, a critical challenge in Family and Consumer Sciences (FCS). Traditional approaches to analyzing household financial resilience, resource distribution, and consumer behavior often rely on static, survey-based datasets, limiting their capacity to account for real-time variables such as inflation volatility, shifting labor markets, or localized disruptions to community services. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based modeling (ABM) platform that simulates multi-scale interactions between household decision-making, economic policy shifts, and regional resource availability. The ABM framework will integrate heterogeneous data streams, including anonymized consumer transaction records, public health advisories, and geospatial employment trends, to generate predictive insights into adaptive strategies for households navigating financial instability. Computational demands arise from the need to process high-dimensional datasets, calibrate millions of agent interactions, and run ensemble simulations across diverse demographic and economic scenarios. By employing parallelized Monte Carlo methods and machine learning-driven parameter optimization, the project aims to identify scalable interventions for FCS professionals, such as personalized budgeting algorithms and community-specific resource distribution protocols. Anticipated outcomes include open-access tools for simulating policy impacts on household well-being and a computational taxonomy of risk-mitigation behaviors tailored to underserved populations. This work bridges gaps between computational social science and applied human sciences, offering a novel methodology for translating HPC capabilities into actionable strategies for family resource management and consumer education.
cip_title: Family and Consumer Sciences/ Human Sciences Business Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in family and consumer sciences/human sciences business services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing rehabilitation program outcomes in correctional facilities through predictive modeling of participant behavior and program efficacy. Current approaches often rely on static, retrospective analyses that fail to account for dynamic interpersonal dynamics, resource constraints, and evolving individual risk factors. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing an adaptive simulation framework using agent-based modeling (ABM) coupled with machine learning to analyze how program design variables interact with population characteristics in complex custodial environments. The computational model will integrate anonymized historical data from multiple correctional systems—including participant demographics, behavioral logs, and post-release outcomes—with real-time facility operation parameters. High-performance computing resources are critical for scaling simulations to reflect population-level interactions across multi-year horizons while maintaining granular individual-level behavioral rules. Key computational challenges include parallelizing thousands of agent decision trees, optimizing memory-intensive social network analyses among transient populations, and validating models against sparse outcome datasets through ensemble machine learning techniques. Expected outcomes include an open-source tool for predicting rehabilitation program success probabilities under varying resource allocation scenarios, identifying critical intervention thresholds for at-risk participants, and modeling the cascading effects of staffing changes or policy adjustments. This interdisciplinary approach bridges correctional theory with computational social science methodologies, offering evidence-based strategies to improve rehabilitation efficiency without compromising facility security. The resulting framework will provide administrators with a novel decision-support system to maximize limited resources while addressing recidivism reduction goals mandated by recent criminal justice reforms.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in corrections and criminal justice, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The proposed research seeks to advance foundational problems in algebraic number theory and arithmetic geometry through large-scale computational experiments. The project focuses on two interconnected objectives: (1) investigating the distribution of class groups in families of number fields with prescribed ramification properties, and (2) analyzing the geometric structure of modular curves at primes of bad reduction. A key challenge lies in handling the exponential growth of computational complexity as field discriminants increase and modular parameters become large, necessitating high-performance resources. The research will employ optimized C++/MPI implementations of lattice-based algorithms for class group computations, combined with parallelized Gröbner basis calculations in Magma to study singularities in modular curve models. For the number-theoretic component, distributed computing will enable systematic sampling of class groups across families of quintic fields, testing refined versions of the Cohen-Lenstra heuristics. In parallel, GPU-accelerated symbolic computations will characterize reduction types of modular curves at primes dividing the level, with implications for local-global compatibility in Galois representations. Expected outcomes include new conjectures about higher-rank class group statistics in non-abelian extensions and explicit equations governing modular curve singularities—results that will inform ongoing work in Iwasawa theory and the geometric Langlands program. The generated datasets will be disseminated through an interactive LMFDB-compatible database, creating community resources for further theoretical analysis. This computationally intensive approach bridges abstract algebraic structures with empirical pattern discovery, addressing questions inaccessible to purely analytic methods while maintaining direct relevance to core problems in modern number theory.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the expression of quantities and their relationships by means of symbols, vectors, matrices, and equations, and the properties of integers. Includes instruction in algebraic structures, quadratic and automorphic forms, combinatorics, linear algebra, and algebraic geometry.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of identity formation and resistance within digital spaces used by marginalized cultural and gender groups, with a focus on multilingual, non-Western online communities. Despite growing scholarship on digital activism, there remains a critical gap in large-scale, intersectional analyses of how marginalized groups negotiate systemic inequities and co-create counter-narratives across linguistic and cultural boundaries. The research will employ computational text analysis and network science methods to process terabytes of social media data, including non-Latin script texts from platforms popular in Global South contexts. Key computational challenges include implementing transformer-based language models fine-tuned for low-resource languages, conducting multilevel network analysis of cross-community solidarity patterns, and running agent-based simulations of discourse diffusion under different moderation policies. These tasks require high-performance computing resources due to the scale of data (estimated 10^7 posts across 15 languages), need for parallel processing of multimodal content, and complexity of simulating intersectional identity interactions in evolving digital ecosystems. Expected outcomes include 1) new computational frameworks for analyzing power asymmetries in multilingual digital spaces, 2) identification of cross-cultural patterns in community-led resistance strategies, and 3) open-source tools for ethically monitoring platform governance impacts on marginalized users. By leveraging GPU-accelerated natural language processing and distributed computing for large graph analyses, this work aims to advance both computational social science methodologies and substantive theories of digital cultural resilience. The resource request supports critical infrastructure for handling sensitive data through secure, on-premise clusters while maintaining community partnership protocols essential for decolonial computing approaches in cultural studies.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_title: Ethnic, Cultural Minority, Gender, and Group Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in ethnic, cultural minority, gender, and group studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze the relationship between digital art creation practices and pedagogical outcomes in K–12 art education. While art teacher education programs increasingly emphasize digital tools, there is limited empirical understanding of how specific software workflows, interface interactions, or creative constraints influence skill development in pre-service teachers and their future students. The research will utilize high-performance computing resources to process multimodal datasets from classroom observations, digital art portfolios, and biometric feedback (e.g., eye-tracking during software use). Machine learning models, including convolutional neural networks for image analysis and temporal transformers for interaction pattern recognition, will be trained to identify correlations between digital art-making processes and measurable competencies in areas like compositional decision-making, technical experimentation, and adaptive problem-solving. By parallelizing the analysis of high-resolution artwork timelines and user behavior logs across GPU nodes, the project aims to overcome computational bottlenecks in processing terabytes of temporally dense creative process data. Expected outcomes include (1) evidence-based guidelines for optimizing digital art tool instruction in teacher preparation programs and (2) open-source visualization tools to help educators assess developmental trajectories in trainee portfolios. This work addresses a critical gap in art education research by applying scalable computational methods traditionally reserved for STEM domains to questions of pedagogical design in the arts, ultimately aiming to improve how future art teachers scaffold technology-mediated creative learning.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach art and art appreciation programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the spatial and temporal evolution of cultural narratives across Asian diasporas, with a focus on underrepresented linguistic and regional communities. The research problem centers on disentangling how diasporic groups in Southeast Asia, the Indian Ocean rim, and the Pacific have preserved, adapted, or hybridized cultural practices—documented in multilingual texts, oral histories, and community archives—amidst globalization and displacement. Existing scholarship often relies on fragmented qualitative case studies; this project instead employs computational text analysis and network modeling to systematically map cultural transmission pathways at scale. Key methods include transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) for low-resource languages (e.g., Konkani, Hakka, Sundanese) to extract semantic patterns from digitized manuscripts and interviews, coupled with temporal graph neural networks to model intercultural exchange dynamics across centuries. The computational workflow requires processing terabytes of heterogeneous data—including OCR outputs from non-Latin scripts, audio transcriptions, and georeferenced historical maps—necessitating GPU-accelerated training and distributed memory parallelism. Expected outcomes include an open-access digital atlas visualizing narrative diffusion, a corpus of annotated multilingual texts for low-resource language NLP research, and quantitative frameworks to assess cultural resilience. By bridging computational scalability with area studies expertise, this work aims to advance methodologies for studying intangible cultural heritage while centering marginalized voices in transnational Asian histories. The requested HPC resources are critical to handling memory-intensive graph computations and fine-tuning language models for underrepresented dialects, tasks infeasible on standard academic infrastructure.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of the Asian Continent, including the study of the Asian diasporas overseas.

abstract: This research project seeks to advance the design and operational efficiency of next-generation marine vessels through high-fidelity computational modeling of fluid-structure interactions in dynamic ocean environments. A critical challenge in naval architecture lies in predicting hydrodynamic performance and structural response under complex, multiphase flow conditions—particularly where wave action, cavitation, and turbulent boundary layers induce time-varying loads on hulls and appendages. Current design methodologies often rely on simplified empirical correlations or decoupled analyses that inadequately capture coupled physics, leading to conservative designs with excess weight, reduced efficiency, or unanticipated failure modes. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) for large-eddy simulation (LES) of multiphase flows with nonlinear finite element analysis (FEA) of composite hull structures. The simulations will resolve microscale bubble dynamics in cavitating flows, wave slam events, and their synergistic effects on structural fatigue in novel materials. Machine learning techniques will be applied to accelerate the identification of critical load cases from stochastic sea state data. The research will leverage high-performance computing resources to achieve the necessary spatiotemporal resolution across billion-element meshes, requiring petascale parallelization and GPU-accelerated solvers. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for cavitation-induced erosion, slamming pressures, and hydroelastic vibrations, enabling optimized hull forms with improved fuel efficiency and service life. The computational tools developed will provide a foundation for digital twin frameworks applicable to autonomous surface vessels and subsea platforms, directly supporting the Navy’s priorities in sustainable maritime systems and resilient infrastructure. By bridging high-resolution fluid dynamics with materials-aware structural modeling, this work aims to establish new best practices for risk-informed design in marine engineering.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of self-propelled, stationary, or towed vessels operating on or under the water, including inland, coastal and ocean environments; and the analysis of related engineering problems such as corrosion, power transfer, pressure, hull efficiency, stress factors, safety and life support, environmental hazards and factors, and specific use requirements.

abstract: This project seeks to address foundational questions in mathematical logic concerning the consistency, categoricity, and computational properties of axiomatic systems within model theory, recursion theory, and set theory. A central challenge in these areas is the combinatorial and infinitary nature of proofs and constructions, which often resist traditional analytical methods. For instance, determining the existence of minimal models for fragments of Zermelo-Fraenkel set theory with large cardinal axioms requires enumerating and verifying vast configurations of set-theoretic structures. Similarly, analyzing the degree spectra of computable models or the Turing degrees of axiom systems demands extensive computation to map interactions between recursion-theoretic hierarchies and logical definability. To overcome these barriers, we propose employing high-performance computing (HPC) to automate the exploration of such structures. Key computational tasks include (1) implementing parallelized satisfiability modulo theories (SMT) solvers to verify consistency properties across axiomatic extensions, (2) deploying distributed algorithms to generate and classify non-well-founded models in infinitary logic, and (3) simulating recursive functionals to quantify the computational complexity of theoremhood in subsystems of second-order arithmetic. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated frameworks for symbolic computation and hybrid CPU-GPU architectures to manage memory-intensive tasks, such as constructing ultrafilters in Boolean algebras or resolving forcing conditions in set-theoretic independence proofs. Expected outcomes include the identification of new consistency boundaries for cardinal arithmetic, a refined taxonomy of algorithmic unsolvability in model existence problems, and open-source tools for large-scale logical structure analysis. These results will advance the metamathematical understanding of axiomatic systems while providing a computational methodology for addressing long-standing conjectures in pure logic. The requested resources are critical due to the exponential scaling of search spaces in these problems, rendering conventional computing methods infeasible.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study foundations of mathematics, including model theory, recursion theory and set theory.

abstract: The graphic communications industry faces escalating demands for customized, sustainable, and cost-effective printing solutions, driven by dynamic market needs and environmental regulations. Current printing management practices often struggle to balance operational efficiency with ecological impact, particularly in complex workflows involving variable job specifications, tight deadlines, and multi-stage quality assurance. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing advanced computational models to optimize end-to-end printing processes, from design iteration to logistics planning. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a multi-faceted approach integrating machine learning, discrete-event simulation, and real-time data analytics. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on historical production data to predict material waste, equipment downtime, and optimal job scheduling parameters. Concurrently, large-scale simulations will model plant layouts, supply chain interactions, and distribution networks under diverse scenarios to identify bottlenecks and resource allocation strategies. The computational workflow will incorporate real-time sensor data from printing equipment to enable adaptive quality control systems, reducing defects and rework cycles.
