By parallelizing these tasks across HPC clusters, the project aims to achieve scalability for enterprise-level operations and rapid iteration of design-to-production pipelines. Anticipated outcomes include a decision-support framework that enhances operational agility, reduces carbon footprints through minimized material usage, and lowers production costs by 15–20% in benchmarked use cases. This research will provide actionable insights for industry stakeholders, advancing the integration of computational tools in non-traditional sectors like graphic communications while aligning technical training programs with emerging technological paradigms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical and managerial knowledge and skills to the processes and procedures of managing printing operations from initial design through finished product distribution. Includes instruction in the principles of graphic communications design and production; quality control; printing operations management; computerization; printing plant management; business finance and marketing; logistics and distribution; personnel supervision and leadership; and professional standards in the graphic communications industry.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of creating high-fidelity, real-time animations and visual effects (VFX) for immersive media, interactive applications, and virtual production. As the animation and VFX industries increasingly prioritize hyper-realistic simulations—such as fluid dynamics, deformable materials, and large-scale particle systems—existing workflows struggle to balance rendering quality with interactivity. Conventional single-GPU setups and consumer-grade hardware lack the capacity to process complex physics-based models or AI-driven denoising in real time, leading to iterative bottlenecks in creative workflows. To overcome these limitations, this project proposes the development of a scalable, GPU-accelerated pipeline optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) clusters. The computational approach integrates parallelized physics solvers using OpenCL and CUDA frameworks, machine learning-based super-resolution techniques, and distributed rendering protocols to enable efficient resource allocation across multi-node systems. Key objectives include reducing simulation times for cloth-fluid interaction scenarios by 40–60%, enabling real-time ray tracing for dynamic scenes with over 10 million polygons, and testing adaptive neural networks to predict and precompute lighting data in interactive environments. Outcomes will be validated through case studies involving virtual reality (VR) storytelling and real-time film previsualization, with performance benchmarks compared against industry-standard tools like Houdini and Unreal Engine. Successful implementation will provide a framework for resource-efficient, artist-driven workflows in academic and professional settings, bridging gaps between computational feasibility and creative ambition. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling memory-intensive tasks, such as 4K texture streaming and multi-agent crowd simulations, which exceed the capabilities of local workstations. This work aims to advance both technical methodologies and practical applications in digital content creation, fostering innovation in communication, entertainment, and experiential media.
cip_title: Animation, Interactive Technology, Video Graphics, and Special Effects
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to use computer applications and related visual and sound imaging techniques to manipulate images and information originating as film, video, still photographs, digital copy, soundtracks, and physical objects in order to communicate messages simulating real-world content. Includes instruction in specialized camerawork and equipment operation and maintenance, image capture, computer programming, dubbing, CAD applications, and applications to specific commercial, industrial, and entertainment needs.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in precision veterinary care by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex interactions between animal health parameters, treatment protocols, and disease outcomes. Veterinary medicine faces challenges in predicting individualized therapeutic responses due to the biological diversity of species, breeds, and physiological conditions. Existing clinical decision-making tools often rely on generalized data, limiting their utility in optimizing care for specific patients. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a computational framework integrating machine learning (ML) and multi-scale pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) modeling. The research will utilize anonymized clinical datasets—including hematological, biochemical, and imaging data from companion animals and livestock—to train ML models that predict treatment efficacy and adverse event risks. Concurrently, HPC-enabled PK/PD simulations will model drug metabolism dynamics across species-specific physiological parameters, such as metabolic rate and organ function. These models will be validated against retrospective clinical outcomes data from partner veterinary hospitals. The computational workload necessitates HPC resources due to the high dimensionality of datasets (>10^6 data points), parallelized parameter optimization for ML architectures, and stochastic simulations of drug interactions across biological scales. Expected outcomes include an open-access decision-support tool for veterinary professionals, enabling tailored dosing regimens and improved prognostication for conditions like sepsis, chronic renal disease, and post-surgical complications. By enhancing the precision of veterinary interventions, this work aims to reduce trial-and-error treatment approaches, lower healthcare costs, and improve welfare outcomes for animal patients. The project aligns with advancing educational objectives in veterinary technology by providing a scalable computational resource for training students in data-driven clinical practices.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Veterinary/ Animal Health Technology and Veterinary Assistant
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of veterinarians, laboratory animal specialists, and zoological professionals, to provide patient management, care, and clinical procedures assistance as well as owner communication. Includes instruction in animal nursing care, animal health and nutrition, animal handling, clinical pathology, radiology, anesthesiology, dental prophylaxis, surgical assisting, clinical laboratory procedures, office administration skills, patient and owner management, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of high-impact weather systems in a changing climate by improving the representation of mesoscale convective processes in regional atmospheric models. Current models struggle to resolve critical interactions between microphysics, turbulence, and large-scale dynamics that govern the intensity and evolution of severe storms, leading to uncertainties in predictions of extreme precipitation and convective initiation. To address this gap, we propose a series of high-resolution numerical experiments using the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model at convection-permitting resolutions (1-3 km grid spacing) across selected case studies of historic storm systems in the central United States. The simulations will incorporate advanced spectral bin microphysics schemes and large-eddy simulation (LES) techniques to explicitly represent cloud-aerosol interactions and subgrid-scale turbulent motions typically parameterized in coarser models. Computational demands are substantial, requiring access to high-performance computing resources for ensemble-based sensitivity analyses (50+ members per case) and multi-day simulations with frequent data output to capture rapidly evolving storm structures. The requested allocation would support 800,000 core-hours on parallelized CPU clusters, supplemented by GPU-accelerated preprocessing for initial condition optimization. Expected outcomes include new insights into how aerosol loading and land-surface heterogeneity modulate convective system organization, with direct implications for improving short-term severe weather forecasts and climate projection downscaling methods. Results will be disseminated through open-source model configurations and a publicly accessible database of high-resolution simulation outputs, providing community resources for studying precipitation extremes under projected warming scenarios. By bridging scale gaps in current modeling frameworks, this work aims to enhance predictive capacity for weather hazards that pose growing risks to infrastructure and ecosystems.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific study of the composition and behavior of the atmospheric envelopes surrounding the earth, the effect of earth's atmosphere on terrestrial weather, and related problems of environment and climate. Includes instruction in atmospheric chemistry and physics, atmospheric dynamics, climatology and climate change, weather simulation, weather forecasting, climate modeling and mathematical theory; and studies of specific phenomena such as clouds, weather systems, storms, and precipitation patterns.

abstract: Genetic counseling faces a critical challenge in interpreting complex genomic data alongside heterogeneous clinical and familial information to deliver personalized risk assessments. Current methods for integrating multi-omics data, phenotypic profiles, and dynamic family histories remain fragmented, often relying on static models that inadequately capture the interplay of genetic, environmental, and epigenetic factors. This project proposes the development of a scalable, machine learning-driven framework to model multifactorial inheritance patterns and predict individualized disease penetrance, with a focus on rare variants and conditions with incomplete penetrance. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process large-scale genomic datasets (including whole-exome sequencing and methylation arrays), integrate longitudinal clinical data from electronic health records, and simulate population-level genetic risk distributions using stochastic methods. Deep learning architectures, such as graph neural networks, will be trained to identify non-linear interactions between genetic variants and clinical covariates, while federated learning protocols will address data privacy constraints inherent to sensitive health information. The computational workflow will emphasize interpretability, generating actionable probabilistic risk scores and visualizable decision pathways for clinical use. Expected outcomes include a novel open-source toolkit for dynamic risk stratification, validated against retrospective cohorts of patients with hereditary cancer syndromes and neurogenetic disorders. By enhancing the precision and adaptability of risk assessment models, this work aims to empower genetic counselors with data-driven tools to address variants of uncertain significance, reduce diagnostic latency, and tailor counseling strategies to evolving patient needs. The project’s computational demands—including parallelized variant annotation, large-scale hyperparameter optimization, and real-time simulation of inheritance scenarios—necessitate access to HPC infrastructure with GPU-accelerated nodes and high-memory capacity.
detailed_field: Mental health, counseling, and therapy services and sciences
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to counsel patients and families concerning inherited genetic disorders and diseases; assess risk factors and planning options associated with potential and actual inherited conditions; and serve as patient advocates and provide referral services in relation to private and public support services. Includes instruction in clinical/medical genetics, methods of genetic testing, interviewing and counseling skills, genetic and support services delivery, principles of public health, medical ethics, law and regulations, patient advocacy, and professional standards.

abstract: Directed energy systems represent a critical frontier in modern defense technology, requiring advanced computational tools to address complex challenges in beam propagation, system resilience, and operational optimization. This project seeks to develop high-fidelity models for laser weapon systems operating in dynamic atmospheric conditions, with a focus on mitigating nonlinear optical effects and thermal blooming that degrade beam efficacy. Current analytical frameworks inadequately capture the interplay between turbulence, particulate matter, and high-energy laser interactions at scale, particularly in urban or maritime environments where humidity and aerosol densities vary unpredictably. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose a multi-scale simulation architecture integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), Maxwell’s equations solvers, and machine learning-driven adaptive optics control algorithms. The computational workflow will employ GPU-accelerated ray tracing to model photon-matter interactions across kilometer-scale propagation paths while resolving micron-level thermal gradients in beam-forming optics. A novel feature involves coupling discrete element methods with quantum cascade laser simulations to assess degradation pathways in high-power fiber laser arrays under sustained operation. Validation will utilize classified field test datasets from military partners, enabling iterative refinement of predictive models. Anticipated outcomes include a validated open-source framework for directed energy system simulation, real-time beam correction protocols resilient to adversarial countermeasures, and thermal management strategies extending operational lifetimes by 40-60%. This work bridges gaps between photonic theory and deployable military systems, directly informing next-generation energy weapon design while establishing computational best practices for a domain where experimental testing remains logistically prohibitive and cost-intensive.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of lasers and other directed energy phenomena and their application to the creation of energy beam weapons systems. Includes instruction in photonics, electro-optics, microwave phenomena, laser chemistry, spectroscopy, chemical lasers, fibre lasers, imaging and optics, laser propagation and control, laser communication, infrared remote sensing, modeling and simulation, and related technologies.

abstract: Urban systems are complex, dynamic entities shaped by intersecting social, economic, and environmental factors, yet traditional planning models often rely on static or siloed data that fail to capture emergent behaviors and feedback loops. This project seeks to develop an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework to simulate the long-term impacts of adaptive zoning policies on neighborhood resilience, integrating real-time socioeconomic datasets with geospatial urban form data. The research addresses a critical gap in planning practice: the inability to predict how incremental regulatory changes—such as mixed-use allowances or green infrastructure mandates—interact with resident mobility patterns, local economic shifts, and climate stressors at hyperlocal scales over decadal timeframes. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, the model will parameterize over 10 million individual agents (households, businesses, municipal entities) across a prototypical midsize city, incorporating machine learning-derived behavioral patterns from anonymized mobility traces, property records, and community survey data. Computational challenges include resolving stochastic micro-decisions into macro-level urban morphology changes while maintaining spatial granularity below 50m resolution. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated open-source toolkit for adaptive policy testing under multiple climate and economic scenarios, (2) quantitative evidence on policy sequencing strategies that minimize displacement risks during green transitions, and (3) novel metrics for evaluating regulatory frameworks based on emergent neighborhood cohesion indices. By enabling planners to stress-test interventions against coupled human-environment dynamics at unprecedented scale, this work bridges computational social science and urban design, offering a paradigm shift from reactive to anticipatory governance models. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated simulations across 15 policy variants, each requiring ~8,000 core-hours to achieve statistical significance through Monte Carlo iterations.
detailed_field: City/ urban, community, and regional planning
cip_title: City/ Urban, Community, and Regional Planning
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply principles of planning, analysis, and architecture to the development and improvement of urban areas and surrounding regions, and to function as professional planners. Includes instruction in principles of architecture; master plan development; service, communications, and transportation systems design; community and commercial development; zoning; land use planning; applied economics; policy analysis; applicable laws and regulations; and professional responsibilities and managerial duties.

abstract: The dynamic interplay between protein structure and function underpins essential biochemical processes, yet mechanistic details of enzyme catalysis and allosteric regulation remain incompletely resolved. This project seeks to elucidate the conformational dynamics and energy landscapes governing two understudied enzymatic systems: (1) a eukaryotic metabolic kinase implicated in redox homeostasis, and (2) a bacterial methyltransferase involved in antibiotic resistance. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to capture transient intermediate states and quantify the thermodynamic drivers of conformational changes at atomic resolution. We propose an integrated computational strategy combining enhanced sampling molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with free energy calculations to model enzymatic mechanisms across biologically relevant timescales. Multi-microsecond MD trajectories will be generated using specialized force fields (CHARMM36m, AMBER ff19SB) optimized for phosphorylated residues and cofactor interactions. Markov state models will identify metastable conformational states, while thermodynamic integration and metadynamics will quantify activation barriers and allosteric coupling energies. The computational workflow requires high-performance computing resources due to the systems' size (≥150,000 atoms), need for extensive conformational sampling (aggregate simulation time >100 μs), and iterative quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) refinements. Expected outcomes include (a) mechanistic models explaining catalytic rate enhancements in the kinase system, (b) identification of allosteric networks in the methyltransferase that could inform inhibitor design, and (c) validation of machine learning-guided adaptive sampling protocols for enzyme systems. This work will advance fundamental understanding of enzymatic regulation while establishing computational frameworks applicable to diverse biomolecular systems. Successful implementation requires dedicated GPU nodes for parallel trajectory generation and high-memory CPU allocations for energy landscape analysis, resources not currently available through institutional clusters.
cip_definition: A program of study that combines the biological sub-disciplines of biochemistry and molecular biology. Includes instruction in general biology, general and organic chemistry, physics, biochemistry, molecular biology, immunology, microbiology, genetics, and cellular biology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research on the structural evolution and sociolinguistic dynamics of modern Filipino/Tagalog, with a focus on its literary and pragmatic applications. The central research problem lies in the scarcity of large-scale, data-driven analyses of Filipino/Tagalog’s morphological complexity, dialectal variations, and usage patterns across formal and informal contexts (e.g., literature, digital communication, technical domains). While qualitative studies dominate the field, computational approaches remain underexplored due to resource limitations, particularly for processing historical texts, contemporary corpora, and multilingual datasets. This project proposes a dual computational methodology: 1) deploying natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to analyze syntactic and semantic shifts in Tagalog literature across the 20th–21st centuries, using transformer-based models fine-tuned on curated literary works, and 2) implementing graph-based algorithms to map code-switching behaviors and loanword integration in technical domains (e.g., STEM, legal texts). The workflows will require parallelized processing of over 10TB of text corpora, including digitized archives from the National Library of the Philippines, modern social media datasets, and domain-specific publications. HPC resources will enable rapid training of language models, large-scale sentiment analysis of literary themes, and network analysis of lexical borrowing patterns. Expected outcomes include the first diachronic digital corpus of Filipino/Tagalog literature annotated for stylistic and grammatical features, open-source NLP tools optimized for Tagalog’s agglutinative morphology, and quantitative frameworks for assessing language standardization efforts. These resources will directly support pedagogical innovations in Tagalog instruction and provide empirical foundations for language policy in multilingual technical domains. By bridging computational linguistics with Philippine literary studies, this project aims to establish scalable methodologies for underrepresented languages while preserving the cultural specificity of Filipino/Tagalog’s linguistic heritage.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the modern Filipino/Tagalog language as used in the Philippines. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Forest ecosystems are increasingly vulnerable to climate change-induced stressors such as drought, wildfires, and pest outbreaks, challenging their resilience and sustainable management. Current empirical models struggle to capture the complex, nonlinear interactions between biotic and abiotic factors at scales relevant to management decisions. This project proposes to develop a spatially explicit, process-based modeling framework to simulate forest dynamics under varying climate scenarios and management interventions. The research integrates high-resolution remote sensing data, climate projections, and field-collected forest inventory datasets to parameterize a coupled hydrology-ecosystem model that predicts tree growth, mortality, and regeneration cycles. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to execute large-scale simulations across heterogeneous landscapes, perform sensitivity analyses via Monte Carlo methods, and apply machine learning algorithms to identify critical thresholds in ecosystem stability. The computational approach will enable multi-decadal projections of forest composition and carbon sequestration potential under alternative silvicultural strategies, including thinning regimes and species diversification. By quantifying trade-offs between timber yield, biodiversity, and climate resilience, this work will provide actionable insights for adaptive forest management. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for optimizing restoration plans in fire-prone regions and maps of habitat suitability shifts for keystone tree species. The project addresses a critical gap in scaling plot-level ecological knowledge to landscape-level decision-making, directly supporting climate-smart forestry practices. Access to HPC infrastructure is essential to manage the computational burden of iterative, fine-grained simulations and to facilitate rapid scenario testing, which traditional computing resources cannot feasibly support within project timelines.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of one or more forest-related sciences to the study of environmental factors affecting forests and the growth and management of forest resources. Includes instruction in forest biology, forest hydrology, forest mensuration, silviculture, forest soils, water resources, environmental science, forest resources management, and wood science.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a digital humanities study analyzing the transnational evolution of feminist thought and cultural production as documented in women’s literature, art criticism, and grassroots periodicals from 1960–2000. The research addresses a critical gap in Women’s Studies: the lack of large-scale, cross-cultural analyses tracing how feminist ideas and creative practices circulated among diverse communities globally, particularly in underrepresented regions. Traditional methods struggle to synthesize the scale and linguistic diversity of primary sources, including digitized archives of feminist journals, multilingual literature, and visual art collections. Using natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision techniques, we will computationally map thematic networks, conceptual shifts, and artistic influences across these materials. Key tasks include training multilingual transformer models to detect feminist discourse in English, Spanish, and Hindi texts; applying topic modeling to identify region-specific and transnational intellectual trends; and employing graph algorithms to visualize connections between authors, artists, and activist networks. HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of unstructured data, run parallelized analyses of image-text relationships in art criticism, and train custom machine learning models for non-Western linguistic and cultural contexts. Outcomes will include an open-access interactive platform showcasing transnational feminist networks, a public dataset of annotated materials for future scholarship, and methodological frameworks for decolonial computational analysis in gender studies. This work will deepen understanding of how marginalized feminist voices shaped global cultural movements while demonstrating the value of HPC-driven approaches in humanities research. By centering computational rigor and inclusivity, the project aims to reshape archival practices in Women’s Studies and empower interdisciplinary collaborations at the intersection of technology, culture, and gender equity.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of women, and the development of modern feminism in relation to the roles played by women in different periods and locations in North America and the world. Programs may focus on literature, philosophy, and the arts as much as on social studies and policy.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of predictive analytics and machine learning models tailored to optimize children and youth library services. While libraries serving young populations collect vast amounts of data—including program attendance, material circulation, digital resource usage, and demographic information—existing tools for analyzing these datasets are often siloed, inefficient, or incapable of identifying nuanced patterns critical to service personalization. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by integrating heterogeneous data streams to model engagement dynamics, predict program efficacy, and recommend culturally responsive resource allocation strategies. The computational approach will employ graph neural networks (GNNs) to map relationships between user behavior, program outcomes, and collection diversity, alongside natural language processing (NLP) techniques to analyze textual feedback from youth patrons and caregivers. These models will be trained on multi-year datasets from urban and rural library systems, incorporating privacy-preserving federated learning frameworks to address data sensitivity. The project will further utilize agent-based modeling to simulate the impact of proposed service changes on equitable access and long-term literacy outcomes. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for real-time decision support, enabling librarians to dynamically adapt programming, collections, and outreach efforts. By quantifying the interplay between service design and community needs, this work aims to establish scalable, data-driven methodologies for enhancing equity in youth library services—a specialized niche intersecting information science, computational social research, and education technology. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing terabyte-scale datasets, iterating complex model architectures, and ensuring low-latency analysis in resource-constrained library environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide library and information services and programming for children and young adults. Includes instruction in information needs of children and young adults, resources and services for children and young adults, literature for youth, storytelling, multi-ethnic materials, library management, and information technology for librarians.

abstract: The integration of dynamic market simulations into vocational sales and marketing teacher education remains underdeveloped, limiting instructors’ ability to prepare learners for real-world complexities. Current pedagogical tools often rely on static case studies or simplified scenarios, which fail to capture the high-dimensional, rapidly evolving nature of modern consumer markets. This project seeks to address this gap by developing and validating computational models of market ecosystems for use in distributive education classrooms. The research will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning techniques to simulate heterogeneous consumer behaviors, competitive interactions, and multi-channel marketing dynamics at scale. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for three components: (1) training deep reinforcement learning agents to emulate realistic buyer decision processes using historical sales data, (2) running large-scale parameter sweeps to model diverse market conditions across geographical and demographic contexts, and (3) optimizing parallelized ABM simulations that capture emergent market phenomena through millions of agent interactions. The computational framework will be validated against real-world marketing campaign data from industry partners, with statistical verification of model fidelity. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation platform that enables vocational educators to generate adaptive, data-driven marketing scenarios for classroom use. This resource will directly enhance the pedagogical capacity of marketing operations instructors by providing interactive tools that bridge theoretical concepts with applied decision-making under uncertainty. Successful implementation will be measured through pilot deployments in teacher education programs, assessing both instructor adoption rates and improvements in student competency metrics related to market analysis and strategy development. The project contributes to the advancement of vocational education by establishing scalable computational methods for workforce-relevant skill development in marketing and distribution.
cip_title: Sales and Marketing Operations/ Marketing and Distribution Teacher Education
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach vocational sales and marketing operations/marketing and distributive education programs at various educational levels.

abstract: The increasing complexity of veterinary practice management demands advanced tools to optimize administrative workflows, enhance client communication, and ensure regulatory compliance. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to analyze large-scale operational data from veterinary clinics, including appointment scheduling patterns, electronic health record (EHR) metadata, and client interaction logs. Current administrative systems in veterinary settings rely on fragmented software solutions ill-equipped to handle the growing volume of multimodal data, leading to inefficiencies in resource allocation and decision-making. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, this study will employ natural language processing (NLP) to automate the categorization of client communications (e.g., emails, voicemails) and machine learning models to predict bottlenecks in veterinary workflow cycles. A hybrid architecture combining graph neural networks and time-series analysis will map interdependencies between administrative tasks, clinical workflows, and external factors such as seasonal demand fluctuations. The computational pipeline will process anonymized datasets spanning 50+ veterinary practices, totaling approximately 250 TB of structured and unstructured data. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for veterinary administrators to simulate staffing scenarios, forecast peak service demands, and optimize appointment scheduling algorithms while maintaining compliance with veterinary ethics standards and data privacy regulations. By applying HPC capabilities to non-clinical aspects of veterinary operations, this research aims to establish computational benchmarks for administrative efficiency in animal healthcare—a critical yet understudied domain at the intersection of professional services management, data science, and veterinary practice. Results will directly inform the development of next-generation practice management systems tailored to the unique needs of veterinary administrative professionals.
cip_title: Veterinary Administrative/ Executive Assistant and Veterinary Secretary
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform the duties of special assistants and personal secretaries for practicing veterinarians, veterinary health care facilities and services administrators, and other veterinary professionals. Includes instruction in business and veterinary communications, veterinary terminology, principles of veterinary health care operations, public relations and interpersonal communications, software applications, record-keeping and filing systems, scheduling and meeting planning, applicable policy and regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized facial treatment protocols by modeling the biomechanical and biochemical interactions of cosmetic products with diverse skin types and conditions. Despite advances in cosmetology, current approaches to facial treatments remain largely empirical, with limited quantitative understanding of how mechanical techniques (e.g., massage pressure patterns) and product formulations interact dynamically with skin microstructure, microbial ecosystems, and transient physiological states. The research problem centers on bridging this gap through high-fidelity simulations that integrate heterogeneous data—including client-specific skin elasticity metrics, pore geometry, microbial load, and inflammatory markers—to predict treatment efficacy and safety. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), we propose a multi-scale modeling approach combining finite element analysis for tissue deformation, agent-based simulations for product absorption dynamics, and machine learning to correlate treatment parameters with clinical outcomes from a retrospective dataset of 15,000 anonymized client records. Key challenges include resolving real-time feedback between manual manipulation techniques and viscoelastic skin response, as well as simulating the diffusion kinetics of active ingredients across stratified skin layers under varying pH and moisture conditions. The computational pipeline will be validated against in vitro measurements from synthetic skin analogs and optical coherence tomography imaging. Outcomes will include an open-access decision-support tool for practitioners to simulate treatment scenarios, optimize pressure gradients and product sequences, and mitigate adverse reactions in sensitive populations. By establishing a predictive link between biomechanical inputs and aesthetic or therapeutic endpoints, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in facial care, reduce trial-and-error methodologies, and provide a foundation for AI-driven personalization in non-clinical skincare. The project’s computational demands necessitate GPU-accelerated nodes for parallelized finite element solvers and large-memory allocations for 3D epidermal microstructure reconstruction.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to massage and treat the face, neck, and scalp with chemical and cosmetic preparations, and to function as licensed facial specialists in specialized and full service salons.  Includes instruction in facial surface anatomy; skin properties; skin decontamination and infection control; facial massage; facial makeup; facial wrapping; selection and application of creams, lotions, oils, and other chemicals and cosmetics; European and other facial techniques; client evaluation and care; applicable laws and regulations; and business practices.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize construction site management processes by integrating real-time data analytics, dynamic scheduling, and risk prediction models. The construction industry faces persistent challenges in resource allocation, schedule delays, and safety incidents, often exacerbated by the complex interplay of labor dynamics, equipment availability, and environmental variables. Traditional manual planning methods struggle to account for these multidimensional uncertainties, leading to costly rework and inefficiencies. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled approach combining agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo simulations, and deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to create adaptive decision-support tools. Agent-based models will simulate interactions between workers, machinery, and site conditions, while Monte Carlo methods will quantify risks associated with weather, supply chain disruptions, and labor productivity fluctuations. DRL algorithms will then iteratively optimize schedules and resource distribution under simulated constraints. The computational intensity of training these models—particularly the need for parallelized simulations across thousands of scenarios—requires access to HPC resources for GPU-accelerated workloads and large-scale parameter sweeps. Expected outcomes include predictive models capable of recommending real-time adjustments to site operations, a risk-aware scheduling toolkit that reduces project overruns by ≥15% in simulated trials, and a safety incident prediction system with ≥90% accuracy validated against historical accident datasets. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this research aims to advance data-driven construction management practices, reduce reliance on heuristic decision-making, and provide a scalable computational foundation for future integration with IoT-enabled construction sites. The resulting tools will be validated using anonymized data from ongoing infrastructure projects, with open-source code releases planned to benefit industry and academic stakeholders.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to supervise, manage, and inspect construction sites, buildings, and associated facilities. Includes instruction in site safety, personnel supervision, labor relations, diversity training, construction documentation, scheduling, resource and cost control, bid strategies, rework prevention, construction insurance and bonding, accident management and investigation, applicable law and regulations, and communication skills.

abstract: Liver transplantation remains a critical intervention for end-stage liver disease, yet post-transplant outcomes are hindered by variability in graft survival, immunosuppression-related complications, and immune rejection. Current risk stratification tools lack the granularity to integrate multi-modal clinical, genomic, and imaging data, limiting personalized therapeutic strategies. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models that optimize pre- and post-transplant care by synthesizing heterogeneous data streams. The research will analyze a retrospective cohort of 2,500 liver transplant recipients, integrating electronic health records (EHRs), longitudinal allograft imaging, donor-recipient HLA sequencing, and single-cell RNA sequencing of graft biopsies. Deep learning architectures, including transformer-based models and graph neural networks, will be trained to identify dynamic risk profiles for graft dysfunction, infection, and drug toxicity. Computational fluid dynamics simulations will model hemodynamic changes in portal hypertension pre-transplant, correlating with post-surgical outcomes. HPC resources are essential for managing the scale of genomic data (∼50 TB), parallelizing hyperparameter optimization across 10,000+ model configurations, and enabling real-time inference for clinical decision support. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated risk prediction platform for acute rejection and immunosuppression dosing, (2) mechanistic insights into immune-microenvironment interactions driving graft tolerance, and (3) open-source tools for transplant hepatologists to simulate patient-specific post-transplant trajectories. This work addresses a critical gap in transplant hepatology by bridging computational innovation with clinical workflows, ultimately aiming to reduce 5-year graft failure rates by 15-20% and improve personalized care pathways for this high-risk population.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians with special knowledge and the skill required of a gastroenterologist to care for patients prior to and following hepatic transplantation that spans all phases of liver transplantation.

abstract: The increasing complexity of managing geriatric patients with multiple chronic conditions necessitates advanced computational approaches to optimize therapeutic strategies and predict clinical outcomes. Polypharmacy and adverse drug reactions (ADRs) in elderly populations remain critical challenges, with limited tools to model drug-drug interactions, age-related pharmacokinetic changes, and patient-specific risk factors at scale. This project proposes developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to simulate drug response dynamics, predict ADR risks, and personalize treatment regimens for older adults. Using de-identified electronic health records (EHRs) from 50,000+ geriatric patients across acute, ambulatory, and long-term care settings, we will train machine learning models to identify risk patterns associated with multi-morbidity management. Concurrently, physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling will simulate age-related changes in drug metabolism, leveraging parallelized computational workflows to process 10,000+ drug combination scenarios. A federated learning architecture will enable secure analysis of distributed EHR data from partner institutions while preserving patient privacy. The HPC infrastructure will also support genome-wide association studies (GWAS) to identify pharmacogenomic factors influencing drug efficacy in elderly subgroups. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive model for ADR risk stratification, validated against prospective clinical data; (2) optimized drug interaction databases incorporating geriatric-specific pharmacokinetic parameters; and (3) open-source tools for simulating treatment outcomes under diverse physiological aging trajectories. This work addresses a critical gap in geriatric clinical decision support by integrating large-scale real-world data with mechanistic modeling, ultimately aiming to reduce preventable medication harm in aging populations. The requested computing resources will enable processing of multi-terabyte datasets and computationally intensive simulations that are infeasible on local clusters, directly supporting translational advances in personalized geriatric care.
cip_definition: Research focused on the care and management of elderly patients in acute, ambulatory, community and long-term care settings, and the treatment of diseases and conditions associated with the aging process. Includes instruction in ethical and legal issues, behavioral aspects of illness, socioeconomic factors in care and rehabilitation therapies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in digital rhetoric and multimodal composition, addressing gaps in scalable analysis of large-scale, heterogeneous textual and visual datasets. While contemporary rhetoric and composition scholarship emphasizes the dynamic interplay of digital media, audience engagement, and persuasive strategies, existing methodologies struggle to systematically analyze the evolving patterns of rhetorical adaptation across platforms (e.g., social media, interactive websites, multimedia essays). The computational limitations of conventional tools restrict the scope of inquiry, particularly when examining millions of multimodal artifacts or modeling complex interactions between rhetorical choices, cultural contexts, and audience behaviors over time. To address this, we propose developing a computational framework combining natural language processing (NLP), computer vision techniques, and network analysis to identify and visualize rhetorical strategies at scale. The project will process diverse corpora—including publicly archived digital writing, anonymized student compositions, and cross-platform social media content—using transformer-based models fine-tuned for rhetorical feature extraction (e.g., ethos appeals, visual argument structures, intertextual citation patterns). HPC resources will enable parallelized training of these models, large-scale sentiment and topic coherence analysis, and dynamic network mapping of rhetorical influence across discourse communities. Expected outcomes include: (1) a reproducible pipeline for computational rhetoric analysis, (2) new insights into how digital writing practices adapt to shifting cultural and technological norms, and (3) open-access datasets annotated for rhetorical features. This work will directly inform pedagogy by identifying emerging compositional trends and providing empirically grounded frameworks for teaching multimodal literacy. By integrating computational methods with humanistic inquiry, the project aims to establish a model for data-driven rhetoric and composition research while advancing disciplinary conversations about scalability, ethics, and interpretation in the digital humanities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the humanistic and scientific study of rhetoric, composition, literacy, and language/linguistic theories and their practical and pedagogical applications. Includes instruction in historical and contemporary rhetoric/composition theories; composition and criticism of written, visual, and mixed-media texts; analysis of literacy practices in cultural and cross-cultural contexts; and writing program administration.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of multiscale computational models for optimizing the design and functional integration of neural interface systems. Neural interfaces, such as brain-machine interfaces (BMIs) and peripheral nerve stimulators, face critical challenges in balancing biocompatibility, signal resolution, and long-term stability due to the dynamic interplay between engineered materials and biological tissues. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to capture the spatiotemporal complexity of bioelectrical, mechanical, and biochemical interactions at the neural-tissue-device interface. To address this, we propose a coupled computational framework integrating finite element modeling (FEM) of microscale electrode-tissue mechanics, agent-based simulations of neuroinflammatory responses, and machine learning-driven optimization of device geometries. The FEM module will resolve mechanical strain distributions and ion transport dynamics under physiological motion, while the agent-based model will simulate immune cell recruitment and oxidative stress patterns over weeks-long timelines. A reinforcement learning algorithm will iteratively adjust electrode topology and surface coatings to minimize predicted inflammatory cascades without sacrificing electrical performance. This computationally intensive workflow requires parallelized solvers, large-scale parameter sweeps, and high-throughput data integration, necessitating HPC resources for memory-intensive simulations and GPU-accelerated training of neural networks. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for chronic neural interface performance and optimized design guidelines for next-generation electrodes, reducing reliance on iterative animal testing. The results will directly inform ongoing experimental collaborations focused on minimally invasive neuromodulation devices for treating Parkinson’s disease and neuropathic pain. By bridging molecular-scale biological responses to macroscale device functionality, this work aims to establish a computational pipeline for accelerating the translation of bioengineered neural technologies into clinical practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of biomedical and health systems and products such as integrated biomedical systems, instrumentation, medical information systems, artificial organs and prostheses, and health management and care delivery systems.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive modeling framework to optimize task allocation and patient care outcomes for health aides and attendants in high-demand clinical and homecare settings. Health aides face dynamic workloads, with patient needs varying widely due to factors such as acuity levels, mobility constraints, and chronic conditions. Current scheduling and task prioritization systems often rely on static protocols, which may not adapt efficiently to real-time changes in patient status or staffing constraints. To address this gap, we propose a machine learning approach integrating electronic health record (EHR) data, wearable sensor metrics, and environmental inputs to model patient needs and caregiver workflows. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for training deep reinforcement learning agents on multi-modal datasets spanning millions of patient-caregiver interactions, as well as for simulating care delivery scenarios under diverse constraints. The computational pipeline includes natural language processing of clinical notes, time-series analysis of biometric streams, and graph-based modeling of care networks. Expected outcomes include (1) a dynamic task prioritization algorithm that reduces response times for critical patient needs by ≥20% in simulated environments, and (2) identification of modifiable workflow patterns associated with improved patient satisfaction and reduced caregiver burnout. The models will be validated against retrospective datasets from partnered home health agencies before prospective pilot testing. By leveraging HPC capabilities to process heterogeneous data at scale, this work aims to provide evidence-based tools that enhance the efficacy of health aides while maintaining alignment with human-centered care principles. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits and training modules tailored for vocational programs in patient care assistance.
cip_definition: Any other instructional program that prepares individuals to provide routine patient care and assistance.

abstract: Aircraft powerplant systems are subject to extreme operational conditions, requiring precise maintenance protocols and performance optimization to ensure safety, reliability, and fuel efficiency. Current industry practices rely on empirical models and time-intensive physical testing, which struggle to account for dynamic interactions between thermal, mechanical, and fluid systems in modern engines. This project proposes the development of a high-fidelity multiphysics simulation framework to model aircraft powerplant behavior under diverse operational stresses, with a focus on predicting component degradation, optimizing maintenance intervals, and validating novel materials for high-temperature applications. The research will employ computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to analyze combustion dynamics and cooling efficiency, finite element analysis (FEA) to assess thermal-mechanical stresses in turbine blades and casings, and machine learning algorithms to correlate sensor data with failure modes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to resolving the complex, coupled interactions between these systems at relevant temporal and spatial scales, particularly when simulating transient events such as rapid throttle changes or icing conditions. Expected outcomes include predictive models for identifying early-stage bearing wear, combustion instability, and fatigue cracks in critical components, validated against experimental data from partner maintenance facilities. The resulting tools will enable technicians to prioritize inspections, reduce unplanned downtime, and extend engine service life. By integrating HPC-driven insights into technician training curricula, this work also aims to bridge advanced computational analysis with hands-on maintenance practices, fostering a new paradigm of data-informed decision-making in aviation maintenance workflows. The project directly addresses industry demands for sustainable aviation technologies and aligns with next-generation powerplant certification standards emphasizing digital twin integration.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain all types of aircraft powerplant and related systems. Instruction includes engine inspection and maintenance, lubrication and cooling, electrical and ignition systems, carburetion, fuels and fuel systems, propeller and fan assemblies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the transnational evolution of German-language cultural narratives across diasporic communities in Central and Eastern Europe from the 19th century to the present. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how decentralized German-speaking minority groups—such as the Volga Germans, Transylvanian Saxons, and Baltic Germans—negotiated cultural identity through media, literature, and correspondence, particularly under shifting geopolitical conditions. The core challenge lies in processing and interpreting fragmented, multilingual archival materials—including digitized newspapers, personal letters, and community records—that exhibit complex linguistic variation, temporal discontinuities, and region-specific contextual references. Computational methods will integrate transformer-based language models fine-tuned on historical German dialects, dynamic network analysis to map cultural exchange patterns, and spatial-temporal visualization tools to track narrative diffusion. HPC resources are essential for training domain-specific natural language processing models on heterogeneous textual corpora (estimated at 15TB), running iterative simulations of cultural transmission pathways, and managing graph databases capturing multi-century interpersonal and institutional connections. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital atlas of German diasporic cultural production, quantitative frameworks for assessing hybrid identity formation in minority communities, and methodological advances in computational humanities for non-Anglocentric contexts. By enabling large-scale synthesis of dispersed archival evidence, this project aims to redefine scholarly paradigms of German cultural influence beyond national borders while preserving the historical agency of marginalized groups often omitted from state-centered narratives. The resource allocation will directly support 4-6 concurrent computational workflows over 18 months, with parallelization requirements necessitating sustained access to GPU clusters and high-memory nodes.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of Germany, the neighboring countries of Austria and Switzerland, the German minorities in neighboring European countries, and the historical areas of German influence across Europe and overseas.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance precision and efficiency in carpentry practice through computational modeling and simulation, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address challenges in structural design, material optimization, and workflow planning. Traditional carpentry methods rely heavily on manual calculations and physical prototyping, which can be time-intensive and limited in evaluating complex structural scenarios or material interactions. To overcome these constraints, this research proposes developing computational frameworks to simulate load-bearing dynamics, environmental impacts on wooden structures, and resource-efficient fabrication workflows. Finite element analysis (FEA) will model stress distribution in custom joints and framing systems under variable loads, while machine learning algorithms will predict optimal material selections based on mechanical properties, cost, and sustainability metrics. Additionally, procedural modeling tools will automate the translation of blueprints into 3D construction sequences, integrating job estimating metrics to minimize waste. These computationally intensive tasks require HPC resources to process large datasets—including high-resolution material scans, climate data, and architectural schematics—and to iteratively refine models through parameter sweeps. Outcomes will include open-access simulation tools tailored for carpentry education, validated protocols for resilient wooden structure design, and data-driven guidelines for balancing structural integrity with material efficiency. By bridging computational innovation with hands-on carpentry, this project aims to modernize technical training, reduce trial-and-error in construction, and advance sustainable practices in the field. The requested HPC allocation will enable scalable parallel processing for real-time simulations, supporting both research and pedagogical applications in training the next generation of carpenters.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to lay out, cut, fabricate, erect, install, and repair wooden structures and fixtures, using hand and power tools. Includes instruction in technical mathematics, framing, construction materials and selection, job estimating, blueprint reading, foundations and roughing-in, finish carpentry techniques, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the psychosomatic mechanisms underlying transpersonal and spiritual counseling practices using advanced computational modeling. While transpersonal psychology emphasizes the integration of spiritual experiences with psychological healing, the dynamic interplay between somatic states, emotional regulation, and spiritual practices remains poorly quantified. Current research lacks robust frameworks to model how interventions like guided meditation, ritual-based therapies, or expressive movement influence neural, emotional, and physiological systems holistically. To address this gap, we propose developing multiscale computational models that simulate interactions between self-reported spiritual experiences, biometric data (e.g., heart rate variability, EEG), and behavioral outcomes from counseling sessions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to process high-dimensional datasets—including longitudinal qualitative narratives and real-time biosensor data—and to train agent-based models that map how individualized spiritual practices affect collective wellness in group therapy contexts. Machine learning pipelines will identify latent patterns in therapeutic trance states, while network analysis will characterize resilience in clients’ spiritual-emotional frameworks across diverse cultural contexts. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational toolkit for predicting optimal transpersonal interventions based on client-specific consciousness profiles, (2) evidence-based insights into the neurophysiological correlates of spiritual healing practices, and (3) open-access visualization tools to help practitioners tailor rituals or meditative protocols. By bridging computational rigor with transpersonal paradigms, this work aims to advance empirical foundations for spiritual psychology while fostering scalable, culturally responsive counseling strategies. The requested HPC allocation will enable large-scale simulations of consciousness-state transitions and parallel processing of multimodal data, which are infeasible with standard laboratory resources. This project aligns with the program’s focus on synthesizing spiritual wellness with therapeutic innovation, offering novel methodologies to study human consciousness in applied counseling settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to pursue spiritual and psychological practices for counseling. Includes instruction in emotional intelligence, expressive movement, healing practices and rituals, human consciousness, movement and meditation, psychosomatic connection, spiritual systems and wellness, transpersonal counseling, and therapeutic trance.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research in thanatology, specifically addressing the dynamic interplay between biological, psychological, and sociocultural factors influencing end-of-life experiences and bereavement outcomes. The research problem centers on the lack of integrative computational models capable of analyzing multimodal datasets—including clinical biomarkers, psychometric surveys, social network interactions, and qualitative narratives—to predict individualized trajectories of terminal illness adaptation and grief resolution. Current approaches in thanatology remain siloed, limiting their ability to capture the nonlinear interactions between physiological decline, emotional resilience, and cultural belief systems. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM) and Bayesian network analysis to simulate how multiscale variables co-evolve during palliative care transitions and postmortem adjustment phases. The ABM component will simulate decision-making processes among patients, caregivers, and clinicians under resource-constrained scenarios, while Bayesian networks will infer latent dependencies between biomarkers (e.g., cortisol levels, inflammatory markers) and psychosocial metrics (e.g., anticipatory grief scales, social support indices). HPC resources are critical for processing high-dimensional datasets (>10^6 variables) from partnered hospice centers and longitudinal bereavement studies, enabling parallelized parameter optimization and sensitivity analyses across stochastic simulations. Expected outcomes include predictive models identifying high-risk cohorts for complicated grief, optimized intervention timelines for palliative care teams, and a publicly accessible computational toolkit for thanatology researchers. By bridging quantitative biology with sociocultural analytics, this work aims to establish a novel paradigm for personalized end-of-life care while demonstrating the transformative role of HPC in emergent interdisciplinary domains.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the biological, philosophical, psychological, sociological, and theological aspects of death, dying, and bereavement. Includes instruction in counseling, ethics, grief, palliative and hospice care, philosophy, thanatology, and theology.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize in-flight emergency response protocols for airline crews, with a focus on enhancing passenger safety and operational efficiency under constrained cabin environments. The research addresses a critical gap in current training methodologies, which often rely on static simulations that inadequately capture the dynamic, high-stress scenarios faced by flight attendants during emergencies such as rapid decompression, fire outbreaks, or medical crises. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to create multi-agent simulations that model human behavior, cabin geometry, and environmental variables in real time. These simulations will integrate computational fluid dynamics to map airflow patterns during smoke/fire events, finite element analysis to predict structural stress impacts on evacuation routes, and machine learning algorithms to predict passenger decision-making under stress. A key innovation involves coupling agent-based models with virtual reality (VR) interfaces to generate adaptive training scenarios that respond dynamically to crew actions. The computational demands of this work—particularly the need for parallel processing of complex physical interactions and large-scale behavioral datasets—require dedicated HPC allocation to achieve the necessary resolution and simulation speed. Expected outcomes include data-driven revisions to emergency protocol design, evidence-based recommendations for cabin configuration optimizations, and AI-enhanced training modules that adapt to individual learner performance. By quantifying relationships between crew response times, spatial constraints, and passenger demographics, this research aims to establish new standards for aviation safety training while reducing reliance on costly physical mock-ups. The resulting framework will be validated against historical incident data and peer-reviewed emergency response benchmarks, with implications for both commercial aviation and regulatory policy development.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the performance of a variety of personal services conducive to the safety and comfort of airline passengers during flight, including verifying tickets, explaining the use of safety equipment, providing passenger services, and responding to in-flight emergencies.

abstract: This research project seeks to advance the understanding of hydrogen bonding dynamics in liquid-phase environments and their influence on reaction mechanisms, with a focus on solvation effects in aqueous organic reactions. Despite the critical role of hydrogen bonding in mediating chemical reactivity and selectivity, accurately modeling these interactions at the quantum mechanical level remains computationally prohibitive due to the need for explicit solvation and long simulation timescales. We propose a multi-scale computational approach combining ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations with machine learning-accelerated free energy sampling to resolve the interplay between solvent structuring and reaction pathways. High-level density functional theory (DFT) and coupled-cluster calculations will be used to parameterize a neural network potential, enabling microsecond-scale simulations of reactive trajectories with quantum accuracy. The HPC resources will support parallelized AIMD workflows across thousands of cores, leveraging GPU-optimized quantum chemistry codes to handle systems of 500–1,000 atoms. Expected outcomes include resolving solvent-driven kinetic bottlenecks in prototypical organic reactions, such as nucleophilic substitutions, and establishing transferable protocols for simulating hydrogen-bonded networks in complex liquid environments. This work will provide foundational insights into solvent effects on reaction rates and selectivity, with implications for predictive modeling in synthetic chemistry and enzymology. The resulting datasets and machine learning frameworks will be disseminated to the theoretical chemistry community, enhancing capabilities for data-driven discovery of solvent-mediated reaction pathways.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of mathematical and computational methods and fundamental laws of physics to describe chemical phenomena and to develop empirical models of molecules and their interactions. Includes instruction in properties of small, isolated molecules; dynamics of elementary chemical processes; reaction pathways of organic molecules; hydrogen bonding patterns in liquids; reaction rates of biological pathways; and advanced computational techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in the design and optimization of energy-efficient, high-performance computer hardware systems through advanced computational modeling and simulation. As hardware complexity grows—driven by demands for edge computing, AI acceleration, and heterogeneous architectures—traditional design methodologies struggle to balance power consumption, thermal management, and computational throughput. We propose a multi-physics simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model next-generation integrated circuits and hardware subsystems at unprecedented scales. The computational approach integrates finite-element analysis for thermal-electrical coupling, Monte Carlo methods for manufacturing variability prediction, and machine learning-driven topology optimization to co-design chip layouts and cooling solutions. By parallelizing these workflows across GPU-accelerated nodes, we aim to reduce simulation times for 3D-stacked architectures and photonic interconnects from weeks to days while maintaining nanometer-scale fidelity. The project will also develop open-source tools for automated design space exploration, enabling rapid benchmarking of novel materials and transistor geometries. Expected outcomes include validated models for low-power, high-reliability hardware configurations targeting IoT and data center applications, with projected energy savings of 15-20% over current commercial designs. These advancements will directly support academic research in reconfigurable computing and fault-tolerant systems while providing industry-relevant datasets for sustainable hardware innovation. The requested HPC allocation is essential to manage the terabyte-scale datasets and iterative optimization loops inherent to multi-objective hardware co-design, which cannot feasibly run on local clusters. This work bridges computational engineering and applied computer hardware research, offering foundational insights for next-generation device development.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development, and evaluation of computer hardware and related peripheral equipment. Includes instruction in computer circuit and chip design, circuitry, computer systems design, computer equipment design, computer layout planning, testing procedures, and related computer theory and software topics.

abstract: The rising complexity of pharmaceutical markets and healthcare policy demands advanced analytical tools to evaluate cost-effectiveness, pricing strategies, and population health outcomes. Current pharmacoeconomic models often rely on simplified assumptions or aggregated data, limiting their capacity to capture real-world heterogeneity in patient responses, treatment pathways, and market dynamics. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution simulation framework integrating real-world data (RWD) from electronic health records, insurance claims, and pharmaceutical supply chains to model the economic and clinical impacts of novel therapies under diverse policy scenarios. The research will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate interactions between patients, providers, payers, and manufacturers, coupled with machine learning algorithms to predict individual-level treatment outcomes and costs. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for scaling these computationally intensive simulations across large synthetic populations (10⁶–10⁷ agents) and iterating policy parameters (e.g., reimbursement thresholds, value-based pricing contracts) with Monte Carlo sensitivity analyses. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized optimization routines to identify formulary designs and pricing policies that balance affordability, manufacturer incentives, and population health gains. Outcomes will include open-source tools for dynamic cost-effectiveness analysis and policy briefs quantifying trade-offs between therapeutic innovation, healthcare expenditure, and equity. By enabling granular, systems-level pharmacoeconomic modeling, this project aims to inform evidence-based decision-making for payers, regulators, and manufacturers while advancing methodological integration of RWD and computational economics in pharmaceutical sciences.
detailed_field: Pharmacy, pharmaceutical sciences, and administration nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of economics and policy analysis to the study of the relationship of pharmacy services and pharmaceutical processes and products to the health care system and their impact on health care organizations. Includes instruction in health economics, pharmacoeconomics, health care systems, health care organization and management, statistics and biostatistics, outcomes research, health care policy, pharmacy services, and pharmaceutical industry operations.

abstract: Climate change and emerging pathogens present critical challenges to global agricultural productivity, necessitating advanced strategies to enhance crop and livestock resilience. This project seeks to utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to accelerate genomic and transcriptomic analyses aimed at identifying genetic and molecular mechanisms underlying stress tolerance in key agricultural species. The research focuses on two interconnected objectives: (1) decoding the genetic architecture of drought resistance in staple cereal crops through genome-wide association studies (GWAS) and machine learning-driven genomic prediction, and (2) modeling host-pathogen interactions in livestock using multi-omics integration to pinpoint virulence factors and immune response pathways. Computational workflows will process petabytes of sequencing data from diverse germplasm libraries and experimental infection trials, employing parallelized pipelines for variant calling, phylogenomic reconstruction, and network-based systems biology. HPC resources are essential for deploying deep learning models to predict phenotype-genotype associations under simulated climate scenarios and for conducting molecular dynamics simulations of protein-ligand interactions critical to disease resistance. The scale of these datasets—encompassing thousands of genomes, epigenomes, and transcriptomes—exceeds the capacity of local computing infrastructure, particularly for memory-intensive tasks such as pan-genome graph construction and population-scale haplotype analysis. Expected outcomes include the identification of candidate genes for precision breeding, predictive models of pathogen evolution, and optimized protocols for computational genomics in non-model agricultural species. By bridging genomic innovation with scalable computational workflows, this work will provide actionable insights to mitigate yield losses, reduce reliance on chemical interventions, and strengthen genetic conservation efforts. The resulting datasets and analytical frameworks will be disseminated through open-access platforms to support global agricultural research communities.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_title: Agricultural/ Animal/ Plant/ Veterinary Science and Related Fields, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in agricultural, animal, plant, or veterinary science and related fields, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of multifactorial diseases in domestic and wild animals, driven by dynamic host-pathogen-environment interactions, poses significant challenges for timely diagnosis and targeted intervention. Current approaches in veterinary pathology often struggle to integrate large-scale genomic, proteomic, and environmental datasets required to disentangle these interactions, particularly in cases of emerging infectious diseases or toxin-mediated pathologies. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models of disease pathogenesis and host response. We propose a computational framework combining machine learning, molecular dynamics simulations, and multi-omics network analysis to investigate three priority areas: 1) host immune evasion mechanisms in persistent viral infections of livestock, 2) metabolic pathway disruptions in mycotoxin-exposed avian species, and 3) genetic determinants of antibiotic resistance in zoonotic bacterial pathogens. HPC resources will enable genome-scale phylogenetic reconstructions, atomistic modeling of pathogen-host protein interactions, and integration of clinical pathology data from veterinary diagnostic laboratories. Key computational workflows include GPU-accelerated deep learning for histopathology image analysis, parallelized molecular docking studies to identify therapeutic targets, and Bayesian network models to map environmental risk factors to disease outcomes. Expected outcomes include novel biomarkers for early disease detection, predictive models of antimicrobial resistance spread, and mechanistic insights into toxin-induced cellular damage. These results will directly enhance diagnostic accuracy in veterinary pathology while informing the development of targeted therapeutics and prophylactic strategies. By bridging computational biology with veterinary medicine, this research aims to establish scalable analytical pipelines for investigating complex animal diseases, ultimately supporting food security and One Health initiatives through improved disease management in agricultural systems.
