major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the development and process of disease in domestic and wild animals and applications to diagnosis, prevention, and treatment. Includes instruction in pathogenesis, immunoparasitology, viral therapy, inherited metabolic diseases, environmental toxicology, anatomical and clinical pathology, necropsy and biopsy techniques, clinical laboratory analysis, pathological interpretation, and disease diagnosis.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance the development of adaptive pedagogical tools for Teaching French as a Second or Foreign Language (TFSL) by leveraging large-scale computational analysis of learner interactions. A critical challenge in TFSL is the lack of personalized feedback mechanisms that address diverse learner errors in real time, particularly in morphosyntax and phonology, which are influenced by learners’ first languages. Current approaches rely on static error corpora or manual analysis, limiting scalability and responsiveness. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to model learner language acquisition patterns and automate error detection. The research will utilize anonymized learner data (written and spoken production) from multilingual classrooms, comprising over 50,000 annotated utterances across proficiency levels. Computational methods include transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) models fine-tuned for error classification, dynamic time warping algorithms for phonetic deviation analysis, and probabilistic graphical models to map interlanguage development trajectories. These methods require parallelized training on GPU clusters due to the volume of multimodal data and the complexity of modeling cross-linguistic interference. Outcomes will include (1) an open-source error annotation pipeline for French learner corpora, (2) a real-time feedback prototype integrated into digital TFSL platforms, and (3) empirical insights into the impact of L1-specific error patterns on pedagogical sequencing. By enabling rapid analysis of learner data at scale, this work will directly inform the design of teacher training materials focused on data-driven instruction, bridging gaps between theoretical linguistics and classroom practice. The requested HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of audio-textual data and optimize models for latency-sensitive educational applications, advancing the integration of computational linguistics into language teacher education.
cip_title: Teaching French as a Second or Foreign Language
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and practice of teaching French to students who are not proficient in French or who do not speak, read, or write French, and prepares individuals to serve as teachers and administrators.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational journalism research focused on analyzing large-scale multimedia news datasets. The proliferation of digital news content—spanning text, images, and video—presents challenges in systematically evaluating journalistic practices, such as bias detection, source verification, and ethical compliance. Traditional manual methods are insufficient for processing terabytes of unstructured data from global news outlets and social media platforms. This research aims to develop scalable computational tools to automate the analysis of narrative patterns, visual rhetoric, and information dissemination dynamics across diverse media ecosystems. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models fine-tuned for news corpora, to identify framing biases and trace the evolution of narratives over time. Concurrently, computer vision algorithms will analyze photojournalistic content to assess compositional trends and contextual alignment with textual reporting. Network analysis will map the diffusion of news stories across platforms, identifying amplification hubs and potential misinformation pathways. These methods require significant computational resources due to the scale of datasets (petabyte-level archives), the complexity of multimodal integration, and the need for real-time processing in case studies of breaking news events. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for newsroom analytics, empirical insights into cross-cultural reporting disparities, and frameworks for assessing compliance with journalistic ethics in automated content generation. By enabling large-scale, longitudinal studies of news production, this work will inform policy discussions on media accountability and provide pedagogical resources for training journalists in data-driven storytelling. The requested HPC allocation will support GPU-accelerated model training, distributed storage for heterogeneous media datasets, and parallelized simulations of information spread scenarios.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory and practice of gathering, processing, and delivering news and that prepares individuals to be professional print journalists, news editors, and news managers. Includes instruction in news writing and editing; reporting; photojournalism; layout and graphic design; journalism law and policy; professional standards and ethics; research methods; and journalism history and criticism.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the challenge of optimizing interdisciplinary performance integration in musical theatre through computational modeling and analysis. Despite the inherently collaborative nature of musical theatre, the synchronization of acting, vocal delivery, dance choreography, and technical elements (e.g., lighting, sound) remains a complex, trial-and-error process during rehearsals. This research aims to develop a computational framework to simulate and analyze these interactions, enabling data-driven refinements to staging, timing, and artistic cohesion. Motion capture data from dance sequences, vocal recordings, and script annotations will be integrated into agent-based models representing performer movements, vocal dynamics, and audience perspective simulations. These models will be coupled with machine learning algorithms to identify patterns in successful integrations of music, dialogue, and choreography across historical and contemporary productions. High-fidelity physics-based simulations of acoustic propagation and stage lighting interactions will further assess how technical designs affect performer-audience engagement. The computational intensity of processing multimodal performance data, training predictive models, and running iterative simulations necessitates HPC resources for parallelized workflows and large-scale data storage. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to guide rehearsal prioritization, dynamic visualizations of performance synchronization, and quantitative metrics for evaluating artistic cohesion. By translating artistic intuition into computationally analyzable parameters, this work aims to reduce production timelines, enhance pedagogical tools for training performers, and establish a foundation for data-informed artistic decision-making in the performing arts. The project bridges computational methodologies with creative practice, offering novel insights into the optimization of live multidisciplinary performances.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and techniques for integrating theatre, music, and dance into a unified production. Includes instruction in acting, dance, voice, technical theater, musical genres, piano, and history of musical theater.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of sedimentary basin evolution and its linkages to Earth system dynamics through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled numerical modeling. The research addresses a critical gap in stratigraphic studies: the inability to resolve multi-scale interactions between sediment transport processes, tectonic forcing, and climatic variability over geologic timescales. Current models often simplify these feedbacks due to computational limitations, hindering predictions of basin architecture and its environmental record. Here, we propose to develop and apply a coupled 3D stratigraphic forward model (SFM) that integrates fault-driven subsidence, fluvial-alluvial sediment routing, and climate-modulated weathering. The SFM will leverage adaptive mesh refinement to capture meter-scale stratigraphic heterogeneity across basin-scale domains (100+ km). Model parameter spaces will be constrained using Bayesian inference, calibrated against field datasets from Cenozoic terrestrial basins in active tectonic settings. HPC resources are essential to achieve the required spatiotemporal resolution, as simulations involve solving coupled partial differential equations for sediment mass balance, fluid flow, and crustal deformation across 10^6–10^7 computational cells. Parallelized workflows will enable ensemble runs to quantify uncertainties in paleoenvironmental reconstructions. Expected outcomes include (1) a quantitative framework linking basin-scale stratigraphic patterns to tectonic-climatic drivers, (2) validation of model predictions against high-resolution stratigraphic sections, and (3) open-source release of optimized code for community use. This work will provide novel insights into how sedimentary systems encode Earth surface evolution, with applications to hydrocarbon reservoir characterization, carbon sequestration site assessment, and interpretation of ancient climate archives. The computational infrastructure will support future studies of dynamic topography and landscape response to anthropogenic climate change, establishing a foundation for next-generation stratigraphic modeling.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of sedimentary rocks and the processes that shaped the surface of the Earth and how those processes have interacted to control the Earth system.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize individualized training protocols for working animals, with a focus on service dogs and search-and-rescue canines. Current methods for training animals in high-stakes roles rely heavily on generalized behavioral principles and trainer intuition, resulting in variable success rates and prolonged training timelines. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model complex interactions between animal cognition, physiological states, and environmental variables. The research will integrate heterogeneous datasets, including biometric data (heart rate, cortisol levels), behavioral video logs, and historical training outcomes, to identify predictive patterns in animal learning efficiency. Machine learning models, including recurrent neural networks and multi-agent reinforcement learning systems, will be trained to simulate how individual animals respond to specific stimuli, rewards, and stressors under dynamic conditions. These simulations will enable probabilistic forecasting of optimal training sequences while accounting for breed-specific traits, task complexity, and handler-animal dyad dynamics. The computational pipeline will require parallelized processing of high-dimensional sensor data and real-time adaptation of training scenarios across parameter spaces exceeding 10^6 permutations. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool that reduces training time by 30-50% for complex tasks compared to conventional methods, validated through partnerships with accredited service animal organizations. By quantifying previously intangible aspects of interspecies communication, this work aims to establish computational ethology as a rigorous subfield within animal training sciences while improving welfare standards and operational readiness for animals in critical societal roles.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach and exercise animals for leisure, sport, show, and professional purposes. Includes instruction in animal psychology, health, and safety; human-animal interaction; learning and behavior styles associated with different breeds and species; and the technical and pedagogical aspects of training animals for such specific functions as obedient household pets, performing show animals, animal athletes, caregiving (e.g., seeing-eye dogs), search and rescue, and police/security work.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the modeling and optimization of mineral extraction and processing systems, with a focus on addressing inefficiencies in comminution (rock-breaking) and mineral separation processes. Traditional physical experiments and simplified simulations fail to capture the multiscale complexity of ore fragmentation, particle transport, and interfacial phenomena in mineral slurries, leading to suboptimal energy use and recovery rates. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational framework integrating discrete element modeling (DEM), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to simulate ore breakage, slurry flow, and mineral liberation at unprecedented resolution. HPC resources will enable parallelized, coupled DEM-CFD simulations of industrial-scale grinding mills and flotation cells, incorporating realistic particle size distributions, rheological properties, and turbulence effects. Deep neural networks will be trained on simulation data to predict optimal operational parameters (e.g., mill speed, slurry density) under varying ore grades. The project will also employ molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate reagent adsorption kinetics at mineral surfaces, informing the design of selective collectors. Outcomes include validated models for predicting energy-efficient comminution pathways and enhanced recovery strategies for critical minerals in low-grade deposits. By integrating HPC-driven insights into process design, this work aims to reduce energy consumption by 15-20% in grinding circuits and improve mineral recovery rates by 5-10%, directly supporting sustainable resource utilization. The resulting datasets and open-source simulation tools will be disseminated to the mining engineering community, fostering broader adoption of computational methods in mineral systems optimization.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of mineral extraction, processing and refining systems, including open pit and shaft mines, prospecting and site analysis equipment and instruments, environmental and safety systems, mine equipment and facilities, mineral processing and refining methods and systems, and logistics and communications systems.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop computational models to optimize embalming protocols and enhance the preservation of human remains under diverse environmental and physiological conditions. Current embalming practices rely on generalized chemical formulations and manual adjustments, which may not account for variables such as regional climate extremes, variations in body composition, or microbial resistance patterns. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach integrating fluid dynamics, biochemical reaction modeling, and machine learning. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations will map the diffusion of embalming agents through tissue matrices under varying temperatures and humidity levels, while molecular dynamics (MD) simulations will model interactions between preservative chemicals, cellular structures, and microbial communities. Concurrently, a machine learning framework trained on anonymized mortuary case data—including body mass index, cause of death, and postmortem intervals—will predict optimal fluid compositions and injection pressures for individual cases. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to identify climate-specific formulations and simulate rare scenarios, such as delayed embalming or advanced decomposition states. Expected outcomes include a digital twin framework for virtual embalming trials, reducing material waste and improving restoration outcomes, as well as predictive tools for managing antimicrobial resistance in thanatopractic contexts. By bridging mortuary science with computational chemistry and data analytics, this project aims to establish evidence-based protocols that enhance preservation quality, support culturally sensitive practices, and address emerging challenges such as climate-driven decomposition variability. The computational workflows developed will be shared as open-source templates to foster collaboration between mortuary researchers and computational scientists in this understudied domain.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for licensure as embalmers and morticians.  Includes instruction in pathogenic microbiology, systematic pathology, thanatochemistry, gross anatomy, clinical mortuary science, embalming, restorative art, applicable laws and regulations, and special services such as cremation and preparations required by specific religious communities.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a cross-linguistic analysis of narrative structures in 20th-century Francophone and Lusophone African novels, alongside their Arabic and indigenous language literary counterparts. While comparative literary scholarship has long recognized the interplay between colonial languages and local storytelling traditions in these works, existing studies remain limited by manual close-reading methods, which struggle to systematically map stylistic and thematic convergences across vast multilingual corpora. The proposed research addresses this gap by employing computational text analysis to identify patterns in narrative voice, metaphor usage, and temporal representation within a corpus of 500+ novels digitized in French, Portuguese, Arabic, and Bambara. Key computational methods include multilingual sentence embeddings for cross-lingual semantic alignment, transformer-based models for detecting code-switching phenomena, and graph-theoretical approaches to trace character network evolution across texts. These analyses require HPC capabilities due to the scale of parallel processing needed for training language-specific models, the memory-intensive nature of aligning heterogeneous textual representations, and the iterative optimization of comparative metrics across four linguistic systems. Anticipated outcomes include a computational framework for quantifying cross-cultural narrative adaptation, a publicly accessible database of annotated literary features, and new theoretical insights into how postcolonial authors reconfigure European literary forms through indigenous aesthetic practices. By enabling systematic comparisons at unprecedented scale, this project aims to redefine methodological paradigms in multilingual literary studies while contributing open-source tools for computational humanities research in under-resourced languages.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on two or more literary traditions in the original languages or in translation. Includes instruction in comparative linguistics; applicable foreign languages; English/French language and literature; literary criticism; and applications to genre, period, national, and textual studies as well as literary forms such as poetry, prose, and drama.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and validate computational models to optimize the design of adaptive educational tools for students with visual impairments (VI). Despite advances in assistive technologies, a critical gap remains in dynamically personalizing instructional materials based on real-time analysis of student interactions, sensory input preferences, and learning outcomes. Current methods often rely on static, one-size-fits-all approaches, which fail to account for the diverse needs of VI learners, including variations in residual vision, haptic sensitivity, and cognitive processing. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multimodal datasets—including eye-tracking (for low-vision users), haptic device inputs, and speech interactions—to train machine learning models that predict optimal instructional strategies. The computational workflow will integrate unsupervised clustering of interaction patterns, reinforcement learning to simulate adaptive lesson planning, and agent-based modeling to test hypothetical teaching scenarios. Key challenges include processing high-frequency sensor data from assistive devices in real time, managing the combinatorial complexity of multimodal input combinations, and simulating longitudinal learning trajectories. Access to HPC resources will enable parallelized model training across thousands of parameter configurations, large-scale synthetic data generation for underrepresented VI profiles, and sensitivity analyses to identify robust instructional design principles. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for adaptive content generation, validated against empirical data from VI classrooms, and evidence-based guidelines for tailoring tactile-audio interfaces. This work directly supports teacher education by providing scalable tools to model individualized learning pathways, thereby equipping educators with data-driven strategies to address the heterogeneity of VI student needs. The computational infrastructure developed will also serve as a template for future research in sensory-informed educational technology.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Vision Impairments Including Blindness
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with visual disabilities which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with visual impairments, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising blind or visually handicapped students, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the optimization of task allocation and workflow efficiency in clerical environments through advanced computational modeling, with a focus on mitigating cognitive and ergonomic strain in hybrid office settings. As organizations increasingly adopt digital tools and hybrid work models, clerical workers face fragmented workflows, uneven task loads, and poorly integrated human-technology interfaces, leading to productivity loss and increased occupational health risks. Current studies lack granular simulations of how micro-level decisions—such as document routing prioritization, interruptive task management, and ergonomic workspace configurations—collectively impact operational outcomes. The project will develop an agent-based model integrating behavioral data from motion capture studies, productivity logs, and environmental sensors to simulate clerical ecosystems at unprecedented resolution. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to process multimodal datasets spanning 12+ months of observational data from participating organizations, train machine learning classifiers for real-time task complexity estimation, and run parallelized simulations testing 50,000+ workflow permutations. Computational experiments will evaluate interventions including dynamic task redistribution algorithms, adaptive interface designs, and posture-aware scheduling systems. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for balancing efficiency metrics with physiological strain indicators, validated against biometric wearables data from 150 clerical workers. Results will inform the development of open-source tools for small-to-medium enterprises to optimize administrative ecosystems without specialized HR infrastructure. By bridging operations research, occupational health, and human-computer interaction, this work addresses a critical gap in evidence-based strategies for sustainable clerical work design in digitally transformed environments.
cip_title: General Office Occupations and Clerical Services
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide basic administrative support under the supervision of office managers, administrative assistants, secretaries, and other office personnel. Includes instruction in typing, keyboarding, filing, general business correspondence, office equipment operation, and communications skills.

abstract: Periodontal diseases, characterized by complex interactions between microbial communities, host immune responses, and biomechanical factors, remain a leading cause of tooth loss and systemic health complications. Current clinical strategies often lack precision due to incomplete understanding of disease heterogeneity, host-microbe dynamics, and biomechanical stressors affecting periodontal tissues and implants. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-scale computational models integrating genomic, microbiomic, and biomechanical data. The research will focus on two interconnected aims: (1) simulating spatially resolved microbial biofilm interactions with host immune cells using agent-based modeling to identify critical drivers of periodontal inflammation and bone loss, and (2) applying finite element analysis to optimize dental implant design and placement by modeling bone remodeling under varying occlusal loads and peri-implant microbiome conditions. Machine learning pipelines will analyze high-dimensional datasets from clinical cohorts (including 16S rRNA sequencing, cytokine profiles, and 3D radiographic imaging) to predict disease progression and implant success rates. HPC resources are essential for handling terabyte-scale datasets, running parallelized simulations of biofilm-host interfaces (>10^6 agents), and iterating complex biomechanical models with patient-specific anatomies. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms for personalized treatment planning, identification of microbial and biomechanical biomarkers for early intervention, and data-driven guidelines for implant surface modifications. By elucidating mechanistic links between microbial ecology, biomechanics, and tissue destruction, this work aims to advance precision periodontology, reduce implant failure rates, and inform targeted antimicrobial therapies. The computational framework developed will be shared as an open-source toolkit for translational periodontal research.
cip_definition: Research focused on the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases affecting the gums and supporting structures of the teeth, and in the placement and maintenance of dental implants.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the understanding of hyper-personalized consumer decision-making in fragmented digital marketplaces, an emerging interdisciplinary niche at the intersection of computational behavioral science, machine learning, and marketing analytics. The core research problem addresses the computational limitations of current models in capturing real-time, multi-platform consumer interactions, which often involve terabytes of unstructured data from social media, IoT devices, and transaction records. Existing approaches struggle to integrate these heterogeneous datasets while accounting for dynamic psychological factors (e.g., attention scarcity, contextual emotion shifts) that drive purchasing decisions in omnichannel environments. To overcome these barriers, we propose a hybrid computational architecture combining graph neural networks (GNNs) with agent-based simulation frameworks. The GNN component will process cross-platform consumer interaction graphs at scale, identifying latent behavioral patterns, while millions of parallelized agent simulations replicate how micro-level cognitive biases and social influences propagate through digital networks. HPC resources are critical for training deep reinforcement learning models that optimize agent decision policies across GPU-accelerated simulations, as well as for maintaining low-latency processing of streaming data during validation phases using real-world e-commerce datasets. Expected outcomes include a novel open-source framework for simulating "digital twin" consumer populations, enabling businesses to stress-test marketing strategies under dynamically evolving market conditions. This work aims to establish methodological foundations for ethical hyper-personalization at scale, with direct applications in predictive demand forecasting, churn reduction, and adaptive pricing models. By bridging gaps between computational social science and marketing operations, the project will provide actionable insights for businesses navigating increasingly complex consumer ecosystems while avoiding reliance on traditional demographic segmentation paradigms.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in general marketing and marketing research, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance the modeling of aerothermodynamic phenomena in hypersonic re-entry vehicles through high-fidelity simulations of transitional flow regimes and material response under extreme thermal loads. Current predictive tools for coupled fluid-structure interactions in rarefied and continuum flow regimes lack the resolution to capture multiscale turbulence, gas-surface chemistry, and ablation effects simultaneously, leading to uncertainties in thermal protection system (TPS) design for crewed and uncrewed spacecraft. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating direct numerical simulation (DNS) of compressible Navier-Stokes equations with a kinetic Monte Carlo approach for surface degradation modeling. The simulations will leverage adaptive mesh refinement to resolve boundary layer transitions, shock-shock interactions, and carbon-composite material pyrolysis across Mach 10–25 conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical due to the need for billion-cell meshes, transient simulations spanning milliseconds to seconds of physical time, and ensemble runs to quantify uncertainty in material property inputs. Expected outcomes include validated models for oxide layer formation and recession rates in phenolic-impregnated carbon ablators, with direct applications to next-generation lunar return capsules and Mars ascent vehicles. The computational datasets will inform reduced-order models for real-time trajectory planning tools and establish best practices for coupling hypersonic flow solvers with material response codes at scale. Successful implementation requires access to parallel architectures optimized for memory-intensive workloads, with allocations supporting 10,000+ core-hour jobs and petabyte-scale output for post-processing vortex dynamics and heat flux distributions. This work aligns with national priorities in safe human space exploration and addresses foundational gaps in aerothermoelasticity identified in the Decadal Survey on Aeronautics.
major_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering
detailed_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering nec
cip_title: Aerospace, Aeronautical, and Astronautical/ Space Engineering, Other
cip_definition: Any program in aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, or space engineering, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Molecular genetic pathology faces critical challenges in diagnosing Mendelian disorders, developmental conditions, infectious diseases, and malignancies due to the complexity of genomic variants, heterogeneous data integration, and limitations in current bioinformatic tools. This project aims to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and refine computational workflows for large-scale genomic data analysis. We propose to analyze whole-genome and transcriptome sequencing data from 5,000 patients with undiagnosed Mendelian disorders and malignancies, integrating multi-omic datasets (including epigenomic and proteomic data) to improve variant interpretation accuracy. A key focus will be optimizing machine learning models for pathogenicity prediction, prioritizing non-coding variants, and identifying structural variants through GPU-accelerated algorithms. Custom pipelines will be developed to detect somatic mosaicism in developmental disorders and low-frequency viral integration sites in malignancies, requiring parallelized processing of high-depth sequencing data. Additionally, we will simulate population-scale genomic networks to model genotype-phenotype associations in rare disorders, a task computationally infeasible without HPC infrastructure. These efforts will be validated against clinical outcomes and functional genomic datasets. The anticipated outcomes include novel diagnostic biomarkers, improved classification frameworks for variants of uncertain significance, and scalable tools for clinical-grade analysis of complex genomic data. This research will directly enhance diagnostic precision, inform therapeutic strategies, and establish a computational foundation for future studies in molecular genetic pathology. Access to HPC resources is essential to manage data storage (~1 PB), enable rapid processing of tertiary analyses, and support the iterative training of deep learning models, which are central to achieving these objectives.
cip_definition: Research on how to make or confirm diagnoses of Mendelian genetic disorders, disorders of human development, infectious diseases and malignancies, and to assess the natural history of those disorders, using the principles, theory, and technologies of molecular biology and molecular genetics.

abstract: Cardiovascular complications arising from cancer therapies, particularly chemotherapy-induced cardiotoxicity and vascular dysfunction, represent a critical challenge in patient care. Current predictive models lack the resolution to capture the dynamic interplay between hemodynamic forces, tissue-level remodeling, and cellular responses that drive these adverse outcomes. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a multiscale computational framework to simulate the physiological impact of cancer therapies on cardiovascular structure and function. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate patient-specific hemodynamic data derived from clinical imaging with finite element modeling of cardiac tissue mechanics and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of vascular adaptation. The models will incorporate physiological parameters such as arterial stiffness, endothelial shear stress, and microvascular permeability to quantify chemotherapy-induced changes in vascular tone and myocardial contractility. Machine learning algorithms will be applied to analyze longitudinal clinical datasets, identifying patterns in blood flow dynamics and tissue remodeling predictive of adverse outcomes. The computational pipeline will be validated against in vitro and ex vivo experimental data from vascular tissue models exposed to chemotherapeutic agents. By elucidating the mechanistic links between cancer therapies and cardiovascular dysfunction, this work aims to generate predictive tools for risk stratification and personalized treatment optimization. The outcomes will advance translational strategies to mitigate cardiovascular morbidity in cancer survivors while informing the development of targeted interventions to preserve vascular and cardiac health. This project directly aligns with the Cardiovascular Science program’s focus on translational physiology and its intersection with oncology, offering novel insights into shared mechanisms of vascular pathology in cancer and cardiovascular disease.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure and functioning of the heart, vascular system, and blood in animals and human beings and the disorders and diseases associated with the cardiovascular system. Includes instruction in cardiovascular physiology, blood physiology, vasculature, vascular metabolism, neural control of cardiovascular function, microvascular permeability and membrane transport, cardiac contraction mechanisms, homeostasis, and applications to topics such as arteriosclerosis, heart disease, diabetes, vascular remodeling, transplantation, transfusion, and pacemakers and artificial organs.

abstract: Sleep disorders, such as insomnia, obstructive sleep apnea, and circadian rhythm disruptions, represent a critical public health burden with poorly understood pathophysiological mechanisms. Current diagnostic and therapeutic approaches often rely on simplified heuristics that fail to account for the dynamic, multiscale interactions between neural, cardiovascular, and respiratory systems during sleep. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-resolution computational model of sleep physiology to identify novel biomarkers and optimize personalized treatment strategies. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate multimodal datasets, including polysomnography, electroencephalography (EEG), and continuous cardiovascular monitoring, from a cohort of 2,000 patients with heterogeneous sleep disorders. A hybrid approach combining dynamical systems modeling and machine learning will be employed to simulate interactions between brainstem nuclei, autonomic nervous system activity, and systemic physiological responses across sleep stages. Key computational challenges include real-time processing of terabyte-scale biosignal data, parameter optimization for nonlinear differential equations representing neural oscillators, and ensemble modeling to capture inter-individual variability. The HPC environment is essential for parallelizing large-scale simulations, training deep neural networks on high-dimensional time-series data, and conducting sensitivity analyses across parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include the identification of mechanistic links between transient cortical oscillations and cardiorespiratory instability, as well as data-driven criteria for stratifying patients into subphenotypes with distinct therapeutic responses. This work will provide a foundational framework for precision sleep medicine, enabling the development of adaptive interventions tailored to individual physiological signatures. By open-sourcing the computational tools and models, the project will also establish a scalable platform for collaborative research into sleep-related comorbidities, such as cardiovascular disease and neurodegenerative disorders.
cip_definition: Research focused on Sleep Medicine

abstract: This project seeks to advance the development of adaptive radar signal processing frameworks for contested electromagnetic environments by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Modern military radar systems face escalating challenges from dynamic interference, spectrum congestion, and adversarial countermeasures, necessitating real-time, intelligent signal adaptation. However, existing optimization methods struggle to balance computational efficiency with the fidelity required for multi-domain operational scenarios. The research addresses this gap by developing a hybrid computational architecture integrating machine learning-driven predictive models with physics-based radar simulations. Key objectives include (1) simulating high-resolution, multi-sensor radar environments under diverse interference profiles, (2) training neural networks to predict optimal waveform and filtering parameters, and (3) validating adaptive control algorithms through hardware-in-the-loop virtual testing. The computational approach combines Monte Carlo simulations of radar cross-section variability, finite-difference time-domain modeling of propagation effects, and parallelized reinforcement learning for policy optimization. HPC resources are critical for managing the combinatorial complexity of threat scenarios, particularly when modeling coordinated electronic warfare attacks across terrestrial and airborne platforms. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for rapid radar configuration prototyping and quantitative benchmarks comparing algorithmic adaptability against conventional rule-based systems. This work directly supports next-generation cognitive radar development by establishing computationally tractable methods for maintaining detection performance in spectrally contested battlespaces. Successful implementation will provide validated models for transitioning machine learning capabilities to fielded systems while maintaining compliance with military spectrum regulations and operational security constraints.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, technology and maintenance of air, sea and ground-based radar systems. Includes instruction in electronic principles and digital techniques, transistors and solid-state component theory, radar systems; maintenance technology, data processing systems, wiring and circuit schematics, maintenance management, safety procedures, and applications to specific systems and services.

abstract: Medical office management faces growing complexity due to evolving regulatory requirements, dynamic patient scheduling demands, and the integration of heterogeneous data streams from electronic health records (EHRs), billing systems, and operational workflows. Current decision-support tools often rely on simplified heuristics that fail to capture the nonlinear interactions between administrative variables, leading to suboptimal resource allocation and operational inefficiencies. This project proposes the development of a high-resolution computational framework to model medical office operations as adaptive systems, with the goal of identifying context-sensitive strategies for staff scheduling, patient flow optimization, and compliance risk mitigation. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we will implement agent-based modeling to simulate interactions between patients, providers, and administrative staff under diverse operational scenarios. The framework will integrate real-world datasets spanning appointment histories, EHR metadata, and staffing patterns, processed through graph neural networks to identify latent dependencies between operational parameters. Temporal convolution networks will be trained to predict bottlenecks in patient throughput, while reinforcement learning architectures will explore optimal policy adaptations under constraints such as budget limitations or emergent regulatory changes. Validation will occur through retrospective analysis of historical clinic performance data and prospective pilot testing in three outpatient facilities. Expected outcomes include predictive models capable of recommending dynamic staffing adjustments, automated identification of compliance vulnerabilities in billing practices, and scenario-testing interfaces for administrators. By bridging computational systems science with healthcare operations management, this work aims to establish a foundation for data-driven decision-making in medical administration, reducing operational costs by an estimated 12-18% in modeled environments while maintaining patient care quality standards. The computational infrastructure developed will serve as a template for scalable, adaptive management systems in medium-sized healthcare practices.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the specialized business functions of a medical or clinical office. Includes instruction in business office operations, business and financial record-keeping, personnel supervision, medical and health care policy administration, conference planning, scheduling and coordination, public relations, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: The increasing complexity of radioisotopic analyses in clinical pathology demands advanced computational tools to optimize accuracy, efficiency, and safety in handling radionuclide-derived data. Current in vitro diagnostic workflows—including gamma spectroscopy, liquid scintillation counting, and mass spectrometry of body fluids and tissues—generate large, heterogeneous datasets that challenge conventional statistical methods. These limitations hinder the precision of low-abundance isotope quantification, complicate spectral deconvolution in multi-radionuclide samples, and impede the development of robust quality control protocols. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these gaps through computational modeling and machine learning approaches. We propose to develop Monte Carlo simulations of radiation transport in detector systems to refine calibration algorithms, reducing measurement variability caused by matrix effects in biological samples. Parallelized Bayesian inference frameworks will be implemented to improve spectral resolution and isotope identification in complex mixtures. Additionally, deep learning models will be trained on historical laboratory data to predict instrument performance degradation and automate anomaly detection in quality assurance workflows. These tasks require scalable GPU-accelerated nodes for neural network training, distributed memory systems for large-scale spectral dataset processing, and high-throughput storage for archiving simulation outputs. Outcomes will include validated open-source tools for isotope quantification, optimized protocols for minimizing radioactive waste through targeted analyses, and predictive models to enhance laboratory safety by forecasting isotope decay-related risks. By integrating computational advances with radioisotopic pathology, this work aims to elevate diagnostic accuracy, reduce operational costs, and standardize best practices for radionuclide handling in clinical laboratories, directly benefiting precision medicine initiatives reliant on in vitro isotopic diagnostics.
cip_definition: Research focused on the use of radionuclides in the study of body fluids, excreta, or tissues quantified outside the body. May included related research in laboratory management and safety, quality control, instrumentation, isotope storage and in vitro analyses.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the systemic interplay between metabolic dysregulation and tissue-level stress responses in complex, multifactorial diseases. Despite advances in understanding individual molecular pathways, integrative models capturing how metabolic disturbances propagate across organ systems remain underdeveloped, limiting translational insights. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework that integrates multi-scale physiological data—including dynamic metabolite profiles, tissue-specific transcriptomic signatures, and clinical biomarkers—to map cross-organ communication networks under disease conditions. The project will employ agent-based modeling to simulate metabolic flux redistribution during stress, combined with Bayesian network inference to identify critical nodes governing systemic adaptation or failure. These methods require iterative parameter optimization and large-scale ensemble simulations to account for biological variability, necessitating HPC capabilities for parallelized computation and high-memory data processing. Anticipated outcomes include the identification of conserved regulatory hubs that mediate interorgan crosstalk during metabolic stress, as well as predictive models of disease progression tailored to heterogeneous patient populations. By elucidating how localized metabolic disruptions escalate into systemic pathophysiology, this work aims to advance biomarker discovery and inform therapeutic strategies targeting network-level resilience. The requested computing resources will enable the analysis of complex, high-dimensional datasets that exceed the capacity of standard laboratory infrastructure, ensuring robust validation of hypotheses across simulated and experimental datasets. This project aligns with the broader mission of integrative biomedical sciences by bridging molecular mechanisms with organism-level outcomes, fostering a systems-oriented understanding of disease.
cip_definition: A general, program that focuses on the integrative scientific study of biological issues related to health and medicine, or a program in one or more of the biomedical sciences that is undifferentiated as to title. Includes instruction in any of the basic medical sciences at the research level; biological science research in biomedical faculties; and general studies encompassing a variety of the biomedical disciplines.

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize dynamic decision-making in multi-echelon parts warehousing networks through the development of a high-fidelity computational framework that integrates real-time inventory tracking, predictive demand modeling, and autonomous replenishment algorithms. The core challenge lies in balancing competing operational constraints—including spatial limitations in storage facilities, heterogeneous part perishability rates, and stochastic supplier lead times—while maintaining service-level agreements for diverse customer segments. Current heuristic-based approaches fail to account for the nonlinear interactions between these variables at enterprise scale, particularly when managing millions of SKUs across distributed fulfillment centers. The proposed solution leverages high-performance computing resources to implement a hybrid simulation-optimization architecture combining discrete-event modeling of warehouse operations with reinforcement learning agents trained on historical transaction data. Key computational components include: 1) GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo simulations for risk propagation across supply chain tiers, 2) graph neural networks to model part substitution patterns and counter service interactions, and 3) distributed optimization solvers for simultaneous capacity allocation across network nodes. The research will validate the framework using a novel dataset comprising IoT sensor streams from automated storage systems, supplier quality metrics, and technician repair histories. Anticipated outcomes include a decision-support system capable of generating adaptive replenishment policies that reduce excess inventory holdings by ≥18% while maintaining 99.5% same-day fulfillment rates, along with open-source tools for simulating cascading stockout scenarios in critical parts distribution networks. This work bridges gaps between operations research, industrial engineering, and computational logistics, offering methodological advances in handling time-dependent constraints within large-scale inventory systems.
cip_title: Parts, Warehousing, and Inventory Management Operations
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide administrative, technical, and managerial support in the operation of warehouses, control of inventory, parts identification, and the performance of counter services for customers. Includes instruction in record-keeping, equipment operation, database entry, supply logistics, shop operations and math, and customer and supplier relations.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in modeling large-scale, heterogeneous educational datasets to identify nuanced predictors of student outcomes. Educational research increasingly relies on high-dimensional data from longitudinal assessments, digital learning platforms, and multi-institutional studies. Traditional statistical approaches often struggle to account for nested data structures (e.g., students within schools, districts, or regions), temporal dependencies, and complex interaction effects while maintaining computational feasibility. The proposed research will develop and validate advanced multilevel structural equation models with Bayesian inference to simultaneously model latent constructs, hierarchical dependencies, and time-varying covariates across diverse educational contexts. These models require iterative sampling techniques (e.g., Hamiltonian Monte Carlo) and intensive matrix operations that scale cubically with the number of latent variables—a computational barrier for standard workstations when applied to datasets with millions of observations from national education surveys. The requested high-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable parallelized parameter estimation across multiple chains, distributed memory architectures for massive matrix computations, and GPU-accelerated gradient evaluations. Additionally, the project will implement machine learning ensemble methods to compare predictive accuracy against traditional psychometric models, leveraging HPC capabilities for hyperparameter tuning and cross-validation across stratified subsamples. Anticipated outcomes include (1) optimized algorithms for detecting cross-level mediation effects in educational interventions, (2) scalable methods for handling missing data in longitudinal educational assessments, and (3) open-source computational tools for reproducible education research. This work will directly inform evidence-based strategies for addressing achievement gaps by identifying context-specific predictors of learning outcomes while advancing methodological frameworks for complex educational data analysis. The computational infrastructure will support both proposed analyses of the National Educational Longitudinal Study (N=25,000 students, 15,000 variables) and ongoing simulations of intervention scenarios through agent-based modeling.
detailed_field: Educational assessment, evaluation, and research methods
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of statistics to the analysis and solution of educational research problems, and the development of technical designs for research studies. Includes instruction in mathematical statistics, research design, computer applications, instrument design, research methodologies, and applications to research problems in specific education subjects.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize workflow dynamics in commercial kitchens, with a focus on improving training protocols and operational efficiency for kitchen support staff. While culinary education traditionally emphasizes hands-on practice, the complexity of real-world kitchen environments—with variables such as equipment layouts, staff coordination, and time-sensitive task management—presents challenges in systematically identifying inefficiencies or stress-testing training scenarios. Current pedagogical tools lack the capacity to simulate the nonlinear interactions between personnel, equipment, and workflows at scale. To address this gap, we propose the development of a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) to simulate kitchen operations under diverse constraints. The ABM component will map interactions between kitchen staff (agents), equipment, and spatial configurations, while ML algorithms will analyze historical performance data to predict bottlenecks and recommend workflow adjustments. High-fidelity simulations will incorporate real-world data on meal preparation times, equipment failure rates, and sanitation protocols. By scaling these simulations across HPC clusters, we aim to quantify the impact of variables such as kitchen layout modifications, staff rotation schedules, and equipment redundancy on throughput and error rates. Expected outcomes include actionable insights for optimizing training curricula, reducing food waste through improved task sequencing, and informing equipment procurement strategies. This work bridges computational modeling and culinary education, offering a novel methodology to advance workforce readiness in food service—a critical sector with high attrition rates and evolving operational demands. The project’s computational outputs will be disseminated as open-access training modules for culinary institutions, contributing to data-driven standards in non-science vocational education.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve under the supervision of chefs and other food service professionals as kitchen support staff and commercial food preparation workers.  Includes instruction in kitchen organization and operations, sanitation and quality control, basic food preparation and cooking skills, kitchen and kitchen equipment maintenance, and quantity food measurement and monitoring.

abstract: Disasters, whether natural or anthropogenic, strain healthcare systems by generating sudden, large-scale demands for medical resources amid compromised infrastructure. Current resource allocation strategies often rely on static protocols that fail to adapt to dynamic, uncertain disaster conditions, leading to suboptimal care delivery. This project seeks to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for real-time, adaptive resource allocation in disaster medicine, integrating multi-source data to optimize clinical outcomes. The research problem centers on balancing competing priorities—such as triage accuracy, resource scarcity, and logistical constraints—while maintaining operational flexibility under rapidly evolving scenarios. Using anonymized clinical data from past disasters (e.g., earthquake responses, mass casualty incidents), geospatial datasets, and simulated crisis scenarios, we will construct a multi-agent simulation model to replicate patient influx, resource availability, and transport networks. Machine learning algorithms will be deployed to predict time-critical resource needs (e.g., blood products, ventilators, personnel) across spatial and temporal scales, while mixed-integer linear programming will optimize allocation decisions under constraints. HPC resources are essential to handle the computational complexity of parallelized simulations, iterative model training on heterogeneous datasets, and sensitivity analyses across thousands of scenario permutations. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool capable of recommending resource distribution strategies that minimize preventable mortality and logistical bottlenecks. This tool will be designed for integration with existing emergency management platforms, providing actionable insights to EMS teams, hospital systems, and public health agencies. By bridging computational modeling and clinical priorities, this work aims to establish a scalable paradigm for adaptive disaster response, directly addressing gaps in timeliness and equity of care identified in global humanitarian guidelines.
cip_definition: Research on how to provide care for the victims of natural and man-made disasters with specific consideration given to timeliness and availability of resources. Includes instruction in emergency medicine and its associated acute care specialties, public health, emergency management, humanitarian services, and prehospital emergency medical services (EMS).

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of high-impact atmospheric phenomena, particularly mesoscale convective systems (MCSs) and their role in extreme precipitation events, using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current operational forecasting models struggle to resolve the fine-scale dynamics and microphysical processes driving MCS initiation, evolution, and rainfall extremes, limiting predictive accuracy. To address this gap, we propose a novel computational framework combining convection-permitting numerical simulations with ensemble-based sensitivity analysis. The Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model will be employed at 3-km horizontal resolution over climatologically vulnerable regions, explicitly resolving convective processes while incorporating stochastic parameterizations to quantify uncertainties in cloud microphysics and boundary layer turbulence. Multi-physics ensemble simulations will generate probabilistic forecasts of MCS behavior under varying thermodynamic and aerosol conditions, with a focus on quantifying how warming scenarios modulate storm intensity and precipitation extremes. The computational workload demands substantial HPC resources due to the high spatial resolution, large domain sizes, and ensemble member counts required to capture event variability and statistical significance. Anticipated outcomes include improved process-level insights into convective system predictability, refined metrics for extreme rainfall projection, and open-source datasets to support regional climate adaptation strategies. By elucidating scale interactions between resolved dynamics and subgrid processes, this work aims to reduce uncertainties in both short-term hazard forecasting and long-term climate risk assessments. The requested allocation will enable the execution of over 50 simulated case studies, each spanning 72-hour integration periods, with post-processing workflows leveraging parallel I/O and in-memory analytics to manage petabyte-scale output. Results will directly inform NOAA and IPCC initiatives on extreme weather attribution and resilience planning, bridging critical gaps in atmospheric science and computational meteorology.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in atmospheric sciences and meteorology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Protective services operations face increasingly complex challenges in dynamic environments, requiring real-time decision-making informed by heterogeneous data streams, threat prediction, and operational adaptability. Current methodologies for physical security planning often rely on static risk assessments or simplified simulations, which fail to capture the interplay of human behavior, environmental variables, and adversarial tactics in high-stakes scenarios. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to model multi-agent interactions during protective operations, integrating real-time geospatial data, behavioral analytics, and threat evolution patterns. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute large-scale simulations of urban evacuation protocols, adversarial crowd behavior during high-profile events, and rapid response scenarios involving weapons of mass destruction (WMD) threats. Agent-based modeling will simulate civilians, security personnel, and hostile actors, incorporating machine learning-driven decision trees to replicate adaptive threat behaviors and stress-induced human responses. Computational fluid dynamics modules will assess contamination spread in enclosed spaces, while reinforcement learning algorithms will optimize resource allocation for perimeter control and emergency medical response. The simulations will be validated against historical incident datasets and real-world security exercise metrics. Outcomes will include predictive tools for identifying systemic vulnerabilities in protection plans, dynamic risk heatmaps for operational adjustments, and evidence-based protocols for minimizing collateral harm during armed engagements. By bridging computational modeling with operational security tactics, this project aims to advance the scalability and precision of protective services training and contingency planning, addressing critical gaps in current physical security paradigms. The HPC infrastructure is essential to achieve the latency-tolerant parallelism required for real-time scenario testing and to manage the computational intensity of multi-physics, multi-agent simulations at urban scales.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles and techniques of providing physical security protection to clients in various environments and situations. Includes instruction in security intelligence and information resources, operations planning and surveying, operations security, weapons and explosives, defense and offense techniques, security and surveillance systems, communications systems, perimeter and access control, weapons of mass destruction, contingency planning, crowd control, cover and evacuation, combat and vehicle techniques, and applicable legal and administrative responsibilities.

abstract: The increasing complexity of drug discovery and toxicological risk assessment demands advanced computational tools to predict adverse outcomes with higher accuracy. A critical challenge in pharmacology is understanding the mechanistic basis of organ-specific toxicity, particularly hepatotoxicity, which remains a leading cause of drug attrition in clinical trials. Current in vitro and in silico models often fail to capture the dynamic interplay between drug metabolism, cellular stress pathways, and tissue-level responses. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a multi-scale computational framework integrating physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling, agent-based simulations of hepatic cellular networks, and machine learning-driven toxicity prediction. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize PBPK models using population-level pharmacokinetic data, simulate heterogeneous cell populations under varying drug exposures, and train deep neural networks on high-dimensional toxicogenomics datasets. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated molecular dynamics to model drug-enzyme interactions (e.g., cytochrome P450 isoforms) and parallelized Monte Carlo methods to quantify uncertainty in toxicity thresholds. Expected outcomes include: (1) predictive models for hepatotoxicity risk stratification across diverse chemical classes, (2) mechanistic insights into metabolic activation pathways contributing to liver injury, and (3) a publicly accessible database of simulated toxicity trajectories for 200+ known hepatotoxicants. By bridging gaps between subcellular drug metabolism and tissue-level adverse outcomes, this work will enhance preclinical safety evaluation and inform the design of safer therapeutics. The requested HPC allocation will enable large-scale parameter sweeps (>10,000 CPU-core hours), storage of petabyte-scale simulation outputs, and real-time analytics through distributed computing pipelines, which are computationally intractable with standard laboratory infrastructure.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in pharmacology and toxicology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of predictive models for identifying early risk factors associated with student behavioral challenges in K–12 educational settings. School psychologists face growing demands to design proactive, data-informed interventions, yet existing tools for analyzing complex, multidimensional student data—including academic performance, socio-emotional assessments, and demographic variables—lack the computational power to model nonlinear interactions or longitudinal patterns at scale. The research problem centers on overcoming limitations in traditional statistical methods, which struggle to integrate high-dimensional datasets (e.g., behavioral observation logs, school climate surveys, and individualized education program records) while accounting for contextual factors such as classroom dynamics and community resources. To address this, the project will employ machine learning techniques, including ensemble models and graph neural networks, to identify latent predictors of behavioral outcomes and simulate intervention efficacy across diverse student subgroups. Computational workflows will process anonymized datasets from partner school districts, encompassing over 50,000 student records with 200+ variables per case, to train models that optimize for both accuracy and interpretability in real-world school contexts. By parallelizing model training and validation cycles on HPC clusters, the project aims to reduce runtime for iterative hypothesis testing from weeks to days, enabling rapid refinement of actionable insights. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for school psychologists to prioritize intervention targets based on risk trajectories and resource availability. This work will directly inform equitable resource allocation strategies in education, particularly for underserved populations disproportionately impacted by behavioral health disparities. The requested computing resources are critical to handling memory-intensive tasks, such as graph-based analyses of social networks within schools, and ensuring scalability as datasets expand. Findings will contribute to the broader integration of computational social science methodologies into school psychology practice, bridging gaps between counseling theory and data-driven decision-making.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply clinical and counseling psychology principles to the diagnosis and treatment of student behavioral problems. Includes instruction in child and/or adolescent development; learning theory; testing, observation and other procedures for assessing educational, personality, intelligence and motor skill development; therapeutic intervention strategies for students and families; identification and classification of disabilities and disorders affecting learning; school psychological services planning; supervised counseling practice; ethical standards; and applicable regulations.

abstract: The proposed research investigates the dynamics of cultural identity formation and transformation within diasporic communities through computational analysis of multilingual digital archives and social media data. The project addresses the challenge of tracing nuanced identity markers—such as language use, symbolic references, and community engagement—across dispersed and heterogeneous datasets, which traditional qualitative methods struggle to systematize at scale. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, this study employs a mixed-methods framework integrating natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and machine learning classification to map temporal and spatial patterns in identity expression. Computational workflows will process terabytes of unstructured text, images, and audiovisual content, utilizing parallelized pipelines for data ingestion, multilingual entity recognition, and sentiment analysis. Graph-based models will reconstruct intercommunity networks, while transformer-based architectures (e.g., BERT variants) will classify emergent themes related to hybridity, belonging, and resistance. The scale of data and complexity of multimodal integration necessitate HPC infrastructure for efficient storage, distributed training, and real-time visualization of multidimensional relationships. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible annotated corpus of diasporic digital expression, novel computational methods for interdisciplinary identity studies, and empirical insights into how globalized communication platforms reshape collective cultural consciousness. By bridging computational scalability with theoretical rigor in group studies, this project aims to establish new paradigms for analyzing intersectional identities in digitally mediated contexts, with implications for cultural preservation initiatives and equitable representation in algorithmic systems.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_title: Area, Ethnic, Cultural, Gender, and Group Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in area, ethnic, cultural, gender, or group studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize dynamic pricing and resource allocation strategies for multi-venue hospitality ecosystems using high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex, real-time interactions between traveler behavior, seasonal demand fluctuations, and operational constraints. Current pricing models in hospitality management often operate in silos, failing to account for cross-sector dependencies (e.g., how concert events impact hotel occupancy and restaurant demand) or hyperlocal externalities like transportation disruptions. We propose developing an agent-based simulation framework that integrates heterogeneous data streams—including tourist mobility patterns, event calendars, and competitive market pricing—to simulate decision-making scenarios across interconnected hospitality services. The computational model will employ parallelized Monte Carlo methods to evaluate pricing strategies under stochastic demand conditions, coupled with graph neural networks to capture spatial-temporal relationships between venues. By leveraging HPC resources, we aim to process multi-terabyte datasets encompassing five years of tourism records, weather data, and social media sentiment across 12 major global destinations. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolkit for revenue resilience during demand shocks and a novel metric for "hospitality ecosystem saturation" to guide capacity planning. This work bridges computational economics and operations research, advancing decision-making in tourism-dependent economies while addressing scalability challenges in legacy hospitality management systems. The proposed models will be validated against real-world data from a pilot partnership with a multinational resort operator, with iterative refinements enabled by GPU-accelerated optimization loops. Results will provide actionable insights for coordinating pricing, staffing, and inventory decisions across spatially distributed service networks, particularly in emerging markets where tourism infrastructure growth outpaces existing analytical capabilities.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as general managers and directors of hospitality operations on a system-wide basis, including both travel arrangements and promotion and the provision of traveler facilities. Includes instruction in principles of operations in the travel and tourism, hotel and lodging facilities, food services, and recreation facilities industries; hospitality marketing strategies; hospitality planning; management and coordination of franchise and unit operations; business management; accounting and financial management; hospitality transportation and logistics; and hospitality industry policies and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for optimizing precision meat-cutting processes in commercial settings, integrating advanced data analytics with biomechanical modeling. The research problem centers on inefficiencies in traditional meat-cutting practices, which rely heavily on manual expertise and often result in inconsistent yields, product waste, and economic losses. While existing training programs emphasize hands-on skill development, there is a critical gap in quantitatively modeling the relationship between anatomical variation in animal carcasses, tool kinematics, and cut quality. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining 3D imaging, finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning to simulate tissue deformation during cutting. High-resolution scans of beef, pork, and poultry primals will inform anatomically accurate models, while FEA will simulate blade interactions with heterogeneous muscle-fascia-fat composites under varying cutting speeds and angles. Concurrently, reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively optimize cut paths to maximize yield and minimize tool wear. The computational workflow requires parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes for real-time simulation and parameter optimization. Expected outcomes include predictive models for ideal cutting strategies based on carcass morphology, a digital twin framework for virtual butcher training, and data-driven recommendations for blade design improvements. By quantifying previously tacit aspects of meat-cutting expertise, this research aims to reduce industry waste by an estimated 8-12%, enhance training efficiency, and establish computational meat science as a novel interdisciplinary domain bridging food technology, biomechanics, and applied data science.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to receive, cut, and package animal meat products in commercial establishments and to function as licensed meat cutters/butchers.  Includes instruction in product recognition for beef, veal, lamb, pork, poultry, and fancy and smoked meats; retail and wholesale cutting and specialty cuts; packaging and counter display; shop safety; meat sanitation, storage and rotation; quality control; meat handling laws and regulations; and customer service.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to optimize the analysis of multidimensional datasets generated by heterogeneous scientific experiments, addressing the growing challenge of efficiently processing and interpreting complex, high-volume data in resource-constrained research environments. The research problem centers on the limitations of existing laboratory informatics tools, which struggle to integrate disparate data types—such as spectral, imaging, and time-series measurements—while maintaining computational efficiency and analytical rigor. To overcome these barriers, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement parallelized data processing pipelines combining machine learning-driven feature extraction, physics-informed neural networks, and graph-based data fusion algorithms. The computational approach will focus on three pillars: (1) distributed computing architectures for real-time preprocessing of terabyte-scale experimental datasets, (2) hybrid quantum-classical optimization techniques for enhancing pattern recognition in noisy datasets, and (3) containerized workflows to ensure reproducibility across experimental modalities. The project will validate these methods through case studies spanning materials characterization, chemical reaction dynamics, and biological system modeling, using benchmark datasets from collaborating experimental laboratories. Expected outcomes include an open-source software package for adaptive data integration, demonstrated reductions in computational overhead for common analytical tasks (projected 40-60% improvement versus existing tools), and new protocols for maintaining data provenance in multiuser HPC environments. By creating a unified platform that bridges experimental data streams with advanced computational analytics, this work aims to significantly enhance research throughput in laboratory settings while establishing best practices for FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) data management in science-related technologies.
