The requested computing resources—including GPU-accelerated nodes and high-memory processors—are critical for testing the framework at biologically and physically relevant scales, enabling translation from computational prototypes to practical laboratory implementations.
cip_definition: A general program that prepares individuals to apply scientific principles and technical skills in support of scientific research and development. Includes instruction in standard laboratory practices and procedures; techniques for analysis, testing and inspection; laboratory instrumentation and equipment operation and maintenance; laboratory and materials handling safety; and computer applications.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the design, safety, and maintenance protocols of recreational vehicle (RV) systems, with a focus on integrating multi-physics simulations to address complex engineering challenges. RVs are subject to dynamic mechanical, thermal, and environmental stresses during operation, yet traditional testing methods for critical systems—such as hydraulic braking, electrical networks, propane distribution, and structural frames—are time-intensive and limited in their ability to predict failure modes under real-world conditions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach combining finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to simulate interactions between mechanical, electrical, and fluid systems under diverse operating scenarios. Key objectives include modeling stress distribution in welded joints during towing, predicting thermal profiles of propane appliances under extreme temperatures, and analyzing corrosion propagation in aluminum frames exposed to road salts. These simulations will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers and parallelized workflows to handle large-scale datasets spanning material properties, environmental conditions, and usage patterns. The outcomes will inform the development of predictive maintenance algorithms and design guidelines to enhance component longevity and safety. Additionally, the project will generate open-access training modules to introduce RV technicians to computational diagnostics, bridging gaps between traditional hands-on repair practices and data-driven decision-making. By enabling high-fidelity virtual testing, this work aims to reduce reliance on physical prototypes, lower R&D costs for manufacturers, and advance technical education in the RV service sector. Access to HPC resources is critical to achieving the required resolution for multi-system simulations and ensuring scalable, reproducible results across heterogeneous RV configurations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to build, test, inspect, repair, service and maintain recreational vehicles, systems, and interior and exterior components. Includes instruction in brake, hydraulic, and towing systems; electrical systems; propane systems and propane and electric appliances; carpentry; plumbing; welding; and structural frames.

abstract: Occupational and Environmental Health Nursing (OEHN) practitioners face complex challenges in assessing multifactorial health risks arising from workplace exposures, which often involve dynamic interactions between environmental contaminants, occupational tasks, and individual health factors. Current risk assessment models lack the computational power to integrate real-time sensor data, longitudinal health records, and workplace exposure metrics at scale, limiting proactive interventions. This project proposes developing a machine learning framework to predict adverse health outcomes in worker populations by analyzing high-dimensional datasets from wearable sensors, employer safety reports, and electronic health records. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will train ensemble models to identify exposure-response patterns across diverse occupational settings, including manufacturing, healthcare, and agriculture. Computational workflows will integrate time-series analysis of physiological data, natural language processing of clinical notes, and geospatial mapping of exposure hotspots. A novel agent-based simulation component will model intervention scenarios to evaluate mitigation strategies under varying workplace conditions. The scale of data—anticipated to include >10 million worker-hours of sensor data and >50,000 occupational health records—necessitates parallelized processing and GPU-accelerated model training. Expected outcomes include a predictive tool for early identification of at-risk workers, validated thresholds for exposure limits in understudied industries, and a simulation platform to optimize workplace safety protocols. This work directly addresses gaps in evidence-based practice for OEHN professionals by enabling data-driven decision-making at individual and population levels. Successful implementation will advance computational methods in occupational health surveillance while providing scalable infrastructure for future studies on emerging workplace hazards. By prioritizing HPC capabilities, this project bridges nursing science with computational analytics to strengthen health protections for workers in high-risk environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to deliver nursing health care services to workers and worker populations in clinical settings and at job sites. Includes instruction in public and community health, occupational safety and health, occupational health surveillance, case management, fitness for duty testing, medication, allergies and immunization, emergency and ambulatory care, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: Health education plays a critical role in promoting lifelong wellness, yet the development of evidence-based pedagogical strategies for training health educators remains understudied. Current approaches to evaluating teaching effectiveness in health education often rely on small-scale qualitative assessments or self-reported data, limiting the ability to generalize findings or model complex interactions between instructional methods, learner engagement, and knowledge retention. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large multimodal datasets from simulated and real-world health education classrooms. The research will employ machine learning techniques to process video recordings, biometric feedback (e.g., eye-tracking, heart rate), and pre/post-assessment data from 500+ teacher candidates across diverse virtual teaching scenarios. Computational models will be developed to quantify relationships between specific teaching behaviors (e.g., questioning techniques, multimedia use), student attention patterns, and learning outcomes. A parallel agent-based modeling framework will simulate how variations in health education curricula propagate through student populations with differing socioeconomic and cultural backgrounds. By utilizing GPU-accelerated deep learning architectures and distributed memory processing, these analyses will identify optimal instructional strategies while accounting for multidimensional confounding variables. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models linking pedagogical approaches to competency development in health-specific domains (e.g., sexual health, substance abuse prevention), and (2) open-source tools for generating personalized training modules that adapt to teacher candidates’ evolving skills. The computational workflow will directly inform the redesign of clinical practice components in health teacher education programs, with potential to improve the scalability and efficacy of training pipelines addressing national shortages of qualified health educators.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach health education programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale, multi-source social datasets for understanding how structural inequalities shape community resilience during environmental crises. As climate-related disasters intensify, marginalized populations face disproportionate risks, yet existing sociological models often lack the granularity and computational capacity to simulate dynamic interactions between institutional policies, demographic shifts, and localized adaptive behaviors. The research addresses this gap by developing agent-based models (ABMs) that integrate census microdata, geospatial risk assessments, and qualitative community survey data to simulate decision-making processes in urban and rural contexts under varying disaster scenarios. Computational workflows will employ parallel processing to handle heterogeneous data inputs, including NLP-driven analysis of interview transcripts and social media narratives, paired with demographic simulations of migration patterns and resource access. By scaling these models to regional populations (n ≈ 10^6 agents), the project aims to identify policy-relevant thresholds where targeted interventions—such as equitable infrastructure investments or participatory disaster planning—could mitigate cascading inequalities. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible computational toolkit for applied sociologists, validated against case studies from three U.S. regions undergoing rapid environmental and demographic change. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing memory-intensive simulations, iterative parameter testing, and sensitivity analyses across diverse socioeconomic scenarios. Results will advance methodological integration of computational social science with public sociology, offering evidence-based frameworks for policymakers to prioritize equity in climate adaptation strategies. This work aligns with the program’s emphasis on applied sociological research by bridging theoretical insights on structural inequality with actionable models for real-world intervention.
detailed_field: Sociology, demography, and population studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of sociological theory, methods, skills, and research to resolve particular issues in real-world settings. Includes instruction in data collection, group and organizational dynamics, participatory action research, program evaluation, sociological research methods, and sociological theory.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing pedagogical strategies for teaching psychology at the secondary school level. While existing studies in psychology education have identified evidence-based instructional practices, there remains a critical gap in modeling how these practices interact with diverse student cognitive profiles, classroom dynamics, and longitudinal learning outcomes at scale. Current experimental and observational methods are limited in their ability to simulate complex, multivariate educational environments, particularly when analyzing the emergent effects of interventions across large, heterogeneous populations. To address this, we propose developing computational models that integrate cognitive science principles, educational psychology theories, and real-world classroom data. Agent-based modeling (ABM) will simulate student learning trajectories under varying instructional conditions, incorporating parameters such as working memory capacity, prior knowledge, and engagement levels derived from empirical datasets. Machine learning techniques, including neural networks and ensemble methods, will be applied to analyze multi-modal educational data (e.g., assessment results, discourse patterns, and behavioral logs) to identify predictive relationships between teaching strategies and learning outcomes. The computational workload necessitates HPC capabilities due to the iterative nature of model calibration, the scale of parameter space exploration (10,000+ simulated classroom configurations), and the processing demands of natural language analysis across millions of student-generated text responses. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for predicting the efficacy of psychology-specific pedagogical approaches, actionable insights for personalizing instruction, and open-source tools for simulating classroom scenarios in teacher training programs. This work directly supports the Science and Mathematics Education field by demonstrating how computational methods can enhance empirical research in teacher education, ultimately contributing to more effective preparation of psychology educators and improved secondary-level student outcomes in psychological literacy.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach general psychology at the secondary school level.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the complex interplay between legal frameworks and entrepreneurial innovation across jurisdictions. Entrepreneurship law—encompassing intellectual property, corporate governance, regulatory compliance, and funding mechanisms—faces a critical challenge: the rapid evolution of technology and markets outpaces traditional legal analysis, creating uncertainty for startups and policymakers. Conventional legal research methods struggle to process the scale and dynamism of global regulatory data, judicial decisions, and policy documents, limiting actionable insights. This project proposes a computational approach to map, model, and predict legal risk landscapes for entrepreneurs. Using natural language processing (NLP) and graph-based analytics, we will process multi-terabyte datasets of legal texts (statutes, case law, administrative rulings) from 50+ jurisdictions, augmented by real-time regulatory updates and entrepreneurial outcome data. Machine learning models will identify latent patterns in regulatory ambiguity, enforcement trends, and cross-jurisdictional conflicts, while agent-based simulations will test how hypothetical policy changes affect startup viability. The computational pipeline requires HPC capabilities for parallel text processing, large-scale graph construction (capturing legal citation networks and policy diffusion), and ensemble modeling to account for jurisdictional variability. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework to quantify legal friction points for emerging technologies (e.g., AI-driven ventures, decentralized finance) and a policy optimization toolkit to balance innovation incentives with public interest safeguards. By bridging computational social science and legal informatics, this work aims to advance data-driven entrepreneurship law scholarship while providing scalable tools for legal practitioners, incubators, and regulatory bodies navigating the intersection of law and disruptive innovation.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting entrepreneurship and innovation.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of lithospheric deformation processes during continental collision zones, with a focus on resolving the feedback mechanisms between crustal shortening, metamorphic reactions, and magma emplacement. Current limitations in modeling these coupled thermo-mechanical-chemical systems stem from insufficient spatial resolution to capture critical small-scale features (e.g., shear zone nucleation, magma channelization) while maintaining regional-scale tectonic context. We propose to develop and deploy 3D high-resolution numerical models using advanced finite-element methods with adaptive mesh refinement, coupled with thermodynamic databases for phase equilibria calculations. The computational framework will integrate ASPECT (Advanced Solver for Problems in Earth's Convection) with customized modules for strain localization and melt migration, leveraging parallel computing architectures to handle ~1 billion degree-of-freedom systems. Simulations will be constrained by published geophysical data from the Himalayan-Tibetan orogeny and compared to field-based structural and petrological observations. The HPC resources will enable multi-scale simulations spanning spatial resolutions from meters to hundreds of kilometers and temporal scales from years to millions of years. Expected outcomes include (1) quantification of energy partitioning between viscous heating and metamorphic reactions during mountain building, (2) improved predictive capability for intracontinental earthquake nucleation zones under varying rheological regimes, and (3) new insights into the role of partial melting in strain localization. Results will provide testable hypotheses for future field campaigns and laboratory experiments, while the developed computational tools will be made openly available to the geodynamics community. This work directly addresses fundamental gaps in linking micro-scale rock mechanics to macro-scale tectonic processes, with implications for natural hazard assessment and resource exploration in active collision zones.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the earth; the forces acting upon it; and the behavior of the solids, liquids and gases comprising it. Includes instruction in historical geology, geomorphology, and sedimentology, the chemistry of rocks and soils, stratigraphy, mineralogy, petrology, geostatistics, volcanology, glaciology, geophysical principles, and applications to research and industrial problems.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing complex organizational decision-making processes under dynamic market conditions, a critical problem in business administration. Traditional analytical models often fail to capture the interdependencies, nonlinear interactions, and real-time data flows inherent in modern business ecosystems, limiting their utility for strategic planning and operational efficiency. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation framework to model large-scale organizational systems, integrating agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo methods, and machine learning-driven predictive analytics. The computational approach will focus on simulating multi-stakeholder decision networks, supply chain dynamics, and resource allocation scenarios across varying market uncertainties. By leveraging parallel processing capabilities, the framework will enable rapid iteration of "what-if" scenarios at unprecedented granularity, including real-time sensitivity analyses for strategic variables such as workforce distribution, capital investment, and risk mitigation strategies. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into adaptive management practices, data-driven protocols for balancing short-term operational demands with long-term strategic goals, and scalable models for organizational resilience. The HPC infrastructure is essential to handle the project’s computational demands, which involve terabytes of synthetic and real-world business operation data, complex optimization algorithms, and ensemble simulations across distributed nodes. Results will advance theoretical understanding of computational organizational design while providing practical tools for managers to test strategies in silico before implementation. This work will contribute directly to the emerging field of computational business analytics, bridging gaps between management theory and data-intensive decision support systems. The proposed resource allocation will support both the development of open-source simulation tools for academic use and industry partnerships to validate models against real-world business cases.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on developing and expanding the theory and research in regards to the planning, organizing, directing , and controlling the functions and processes of a firm or organization.

abstract: The increasing demand for personalized and adaptive music education necessitates innovative approaches to understanding how diverse pedagogical strategies influence learning outcomes. Traditional methods in music pedagogy often rely on qualitative assessments and anecdotal evidence, limiting scalability and generalizability. This project seeks to address this gap by developing computational models to analyze and predict the efficacy of instructional techniques across varied learner profiles, instrument proficiencies, and musical genres. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will process large-scale datasets comprising audio recordings, student performance metrics, and longitudinal practice logs to identify patterns in skill acquisition and retention. Machine learning algorithms, including recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and clustering methods, will be trained to correlate pedagogical interventions—such as feedback timing, repertoire selection, and technical exercises—with measurable progress in students’ technical proficiency and artistic expression. Additionally, agent-based simulations will model hypothetical teaching scenarios to optimize curriculum design for heterogeneous classrooms. The computational workload involves real-time audio feature extraction, parallelized model training across thousands of learner trajectories, and Monte Carlo simulations to assess robustness under varying conditions. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for tailoring instruction to individual needs, data-driven recommendations for balancing theoretical and practical training, and open-source tools for educators to simulate pedagogical strategies. By integrating computational rigor with music education theory, this research aims to establish a new paradigm for evidence-based pedagogy, enhancing accessibility and effectiveness in music instruction. The project’s scale and complexity—requiring rapid processing of multi-terabyte datasets and high-fidelity simulations of interactive learning environments—necessitate dedicated HPC allocation to achieve timely and impactful results.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide musical instruction and tutoring to clients in private and institutional settings. Includes instruction in music theory, music composition, mastery of one or more instruments, familiarity with various musical genres and styles, principles of music education, and client communications.

abstract: The intricate organization of neuronal circuits underpins both normal brain function and the pathological mechanisms of central nervous system (CNS) disorders. However, existing neuroanatomical datasets lack the resolution and scale required to map synaptic connectivity across entire brain regions, particularly in disease models. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze and model large-scale, three-dimensional electron microscopy (EM) datasets of murine hippocampal circuits in neurodegenerative conditions. A primary challenge lies in reconstructing terabyte-scale EM image stacks to trace axonal projections, dendritic arborizations, and synaptic contacts at nanometer resolution. Manual annotation is infeasible due to data volume, necessitating automated pipelines for image segmentation, feature extraction, and network analysis. We will implement a hybrid computational approach combining deep learning-based segmentation (using 3D U-Net architectures) with graph-theoretical modeling to quantify synaptic connectivity patterns. HPC resources will accelerate the training of segmentation models on GPU clusters, enable parallel processing of image volumes across multiple nodes, and support the integration of molecular labeling data (e.g., immunohistochemistry) to correlate structural changes with molecular pathology. Expected outcomes include: (1) a scalable computational workflow for synapse-level circuit reconstruction in disease-relevant brain regions, (2) quantitative maps of altered connectivity in tauopathy and amyloidosis models, and (3) open-source tools for merging multiscale neuroanatomical data. This work will directly inform hypotheses about how specific circuit disruptions contribute to cognitive decline in Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias. By bridging ultra-structural neuroanatomy with computational neuroscience, the project aims to establish a framework for identifying critical vulnerability points in pathological neural networks, with implications for targeted therapeutic strategies. The requested HPC allocation is essential to overcome current bottlenecks in processing petabytes of imaging data and performing network simulations at biological fidelity.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the structure of the central and peripheral nervous system in vertebrates or the nervous system of invertebrates. Includes instruction in cellular and circuit anatomy, mapping of neuronal pathways, anatomical distribution and mapping of neuronal signaling molecules and their receptors, and the anatomical basis of central nervous system diseases and disorders.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamic interplay of biopsychosocial factors influencing self-management behaviors in adults with type 2 diabetes. While behavioral interventions in health psychology often target individual-level cognitive or social drivers of adherence, gaps persist in modeling how physiological stressors (e.g., glycemic variability), contextual social determinants (e.g., caregiver support), and real-time decision-making interact across time. To address this, we propose developing a multilevel computational model integrating longitudinal electronic health records, ecological momentary assessment (EMA) data, and experimentally induced stress biomarkers. The computational approach employs hybrid agent-based modeling (ABM) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to simulate individual and social network dynamics. ABM will capture how peer support networks and environmental constraints shape daily adherence choices, while RNNs will analyze temporal patterns in physiological (continuous glucose monitoring) and behavioral (smartphone-reported diet/exercise) data to predict high-risk periods for nonadherence. HPC resources are critical for scaling simulations to heterogeneous population cohorts (n ≈ 50,000 synthetic agents), optimizing hyperparameters for personalized prediction, and conducting sensitivity analyses across diverse sociocultural contexts. Expected outcomes include identifying modifiable leverage points where behavioral interventions could disrupt negative feedback loops—for instance, tailoring telehealth prompts to moments when social isolation coincides with glucose spikes. By quantifying how micro-level decisions aggregate into macro-level health outcomes, this work aims to advance precision health strategies in counseling contexts, offering clinicians a decision-support tool for sequencing multimodal interventions. The computational framework will be disseminated as open-source software, enabling health psychology researchers to adapt biopsychosocial models for other chronic conditions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the psychological study of health and illness, and recovery, from the perspective that these phenomena arise from a combination of physical, behavioral, and social conditions. Includes instruction in abnormal and social psychology, psychophysiology, psychopharmacology, learning processes, clinical and behavioral therapies, biopsychosocial modeling, clinical procedures and assessment, preventive education, psychotherapy, rehabilitation processes, and research methods.

abstract: Aging is associated with significant heterogeneity in cognitive trajectories, yet the dynamic interplay between neurobiological, psychosocial, and environmental factors driving this variability remains poorly understood. This project leverages high-performance computing (HPC) to model longitudinal interactions between multimodal aging processes, with a focus on identifying adaptive pathways that promote cognitive resilience in older adults. We propose a computational framework integrating neuroimaging (resting-state fMRI, diffusion tensor imaging), behavioral assessments, and real-world activity data (GPS, wearable sensors) from a 10-year cohort study of adults aged 60-90 (N=1,200). The research addresses two core challenges: 1) characterizing non-linear temporal dependencies between neural network reorganization, social engagement patterns, and environmental exposures, and 2) simulating how micro-scale changes in these systems propagate to macro-scale cognitive outcomes. Computational methods include coupled ordinary differential equation systems to model neuropsychosocial dynamics, graph neural networks to analyze time-varying brain-environment connectivity, and agent-based modeling to test intervention scenarios. HPC resources are essential for processing high-dimensional datasets (>2PB raw sensor data), training deep learning architectures on spatiotemporal features, and running large-scale parameter sweeps in sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include 1) a validated computational model of cognitive aging pathways, 2) predictive biomarkers of resilience tied to modifiable lifestyle factors, and 3) open-source tools for simulating personalized aging trajectories under different intervention constraints. By bridging systems-level neuroscience with ecological assessments of daily functioning, this work advances translational applications in aging research while addressing critical gaps in scalable methods for analyzing heterogeneous developmental processes. Results will inform targeted community programs and policy decisions aimed at optimizing cognitive healthspan through computationally guided, person-centered strategies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the characteristics of aging populations and the needs of older individuals in family and institutional settings. Includes instruction in the biological and psychological stages of aging; the provision of dependent care; serving the social, economic, and psychological needs of aging adults; related public policy issues; and adult community resources.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to optimize parametric design workflows in drafting and engineering technology applications, with a focus on reducing iterative design cycles and material inefficiencies in complex assemblies. Current drafting software tools struggle to efficiently process multi-variable design scenarios involving large-scale component interactions, particularly when integrating real-world constraints such as thermal expansion, load distribution, and manufacturability. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parallelize finite element analysis (FEA) simulations and machine learning-driven topology optimization across thousands of design permutations. The computational approach combines CAD-based parametric modeling libraries with GPU-accelerated solvers to evaluate structural and functional performance under dynamically adjustable constraints. Key innovations include adaptive mesh refinement algorithms to balance simulation accuracy with computational cost and graph neural networks to predict failure modes in multi-material assemblies. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for educational use in drafting technology programs, enabling students to explore high-fidelity simulations of industrial-scale systems while adhering to ASME Y14.5-2018 standards. The project will also generate benchmark datasets correlating digital twin accuracy with physical prototyping results, addressing a critical need for validated predictive models in vocational engineering technology training. By reducing simulation time from days to hours, this resource will directly enhance curriculum delivery in computer-aided design (CAD) courses while providing industry partners with actionable insights into sustainable material usage. The requested computing allocation will support containerized workflows on Slurm-managed clusters, with an emphasis on scaling MPI-enabled optimization tasks across heterogeneous node architectures.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to generally apply technical skills to create working drawings and computer simulations for a variety of applications. Includes instruction in specification interpretation, dimensioning techniques, drafting calculations, material estimation, technical communications, computer applications, and interpersonal communications.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a real-time adaptive control system for next-generation neuroprosthetic devices that integrate bidirectional neural interfaces with wearable robotic exoskeletons. Current systems face critical limitations in dynamically interpreting user intent while delivering proprioceptive feedback, particularly during complex locomotor tasks. The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in decoding high-dimensional neural data (ECoG, EMG) and synthesizing responsive mechanical assistance within physiologically relevant latencies (<50ms). We propose a hybrid computational architecture leveraging federated learning for personalized intent recognition models and physics-informed neural networks for predictive gait optimization. High-performance computing resources will enable parallel training of patient-specific neural decoders across multiple GPU nodes while simultaneously simulating musculoskeletal dynamics and exoskeleton interaction forces through multibody finite element analysis. The computational workflow will integrate heterogeneous data streams from our partner rehabilitation center, including motion capture, embedded force sensors, and chronic neural recordings from ongoing clinical trials. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for co-adaptive neuro-mechanical control that maintains synchronization across timescales spanning milliseconds (neural processing) to seconds (gait adaptation). Successful implementation could demonstrate clinically significant improvements in stair negotiation and obstacle avoidance tasks for lower-limb prosthesis users, measured through validated mobility metrics. This work bridges gaps between computational neuroscience and rehabilitation robotics by addressing the temporal hierarchy of sensorimotor integration—a prerequisite for restoring naturalistic movement patterns in patients with spinal cord injuries or stroke-related mobility impairments. The requested resources directly support large-scale parameter optimization and validation of our novel control paradigm against existing clinical datasets.
cip_title: Assistive/ Augmentative Technology and Rehabilitation Engineering
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the principles of psychology, engineering, and occupational therapy to the design and implementation of technological interventions and systems to promote patient rehabilitation and function. Includes instruction in ergonomics, seating and mobility design, universal and near environment systems design, rehabilitation research, rehabilitation biomechanics, access and communications design, microprocessor-based technologies, neurological trauma, standards and testing, and service delivery management.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize decentralized entrepreneurial ecosystems, focusing on resource allocation dynamics in peer-to-peer (P2P) platforms that operate without centralized governance. Traditional entrepreneurship research often assumes structured organizational frameworks, but emerging decentralized models—such as blockchain-based cooperatives or distributed creator economies—introduce novel challenges in coordinating labor, capital, and innovation. The core research problem centers on simulating how autonomous agents (entrepreneurs, micro-investors, and consumers) interact under varying incentive structures, regulatory constraints, and resource scarcity, with the aim of identifying scalable governance protocols. Computational methods will integrate agent-based modeling (ABM) with reinforcement learning to simulate multi-stakeholder decision-making in dynamic, open-network environments. Large-scale parameter sweeps will test hypotheses about trust mechanisms, tokenized reward systems, and failure resilience, using synthetic datasets calibrated to real-world platform data. Expected outcomes include a computational framework to predict systemic vulnerabilities in decentralized ventures and actionable insights for designing self-sustaining entrepreneurial networks. This work bridges computational social science, mechanism design, and distributed systems theory, offering a foundation for policy and platform architecture in understudied, rapidly evolving business environments. The requested HPC resources are critical to handling the combinatorial complexity of agent interactions, enabling real-time simulation of networks exceeding 100,000 nodes and supporting probabilistic scenario analysis at scale. Results will be disseminated through open-source tools for ecosystem simulation, empowering practitioners to prototype governance models without relying on costly trial-and-error approaches.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to perform development, marketing and management functions associated with owning and operating a business.

abstract: The increasing complexity of air traffic management systems, driven by rising global air traffic density and evolving operational demands, necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize safety, efficiency, and scalability. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity simulation framework for evaluating dynamic air traffic control (ATC) strategies under heterogeneous flight conditions, including extreme weather events, congested airspace, and mixed autonomous/human-piloted operations. Current ATC training and operational models rely on static scenarios or simplified simulations, limiting their ability to predict emergent behaviors or stress-test novel control algorithms in real time. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to construct a multi-agent, physics-informed simulation environment that integrates real-time radar data, weather forecasting inputs, and stochastic flight trajectory modeling. The computational approach will employ parallelized Monte Carlo methods to simulate thousands of concurrent flight paths, agent-based modeling to capture controller-pilot decision-making dynamics, and machine learning techniques to identify high-risk conflict scenarios. Key challenges include managing large-scale spatiotemporal datasets from FAA archives, optimizing distributed memory usage for real-time visualization, and validating simulation outputs against historical incident reports. The expected outcomes include (1) a scalable ATC decision-support tool capable of predicting traffic bottlenecks with 90% accuracy under variable conditions, (2) quantitative metrics for evaluating controller workload and system resilience, and (3) open-source simulation modules for training next-generation ATC personnel in complex, high-stakes scenarios. By utilizing HPC resources, this project aims to bridge the gap between theoretical airspace management models and operational requirements, directly supporting the FAA’s modernization initiatives while reducing computational barriers to innovation in ATC research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to air-traffic management and control, usually with additional training at the FAA Flight Control Center in a cooperative education program. Includes instruction in flight control, the use of radar and electronic scanning devices, plotting of flights, radio communication, interpretation of weather conditions affecting flights, flight instrumentation used by pilots, and maintenance of flight-control center or control-tower log books.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the design and safety of industrial steam boiler systems through high-fidelity computational modeling of thermomechanical and fluid dynamic behaviors under extreme operating conditions. Boiler systems face persistent challenges, including stress-induced material fatigue, localized overheating, and complex multiphase flow dynamics, which contribute to inefficiencies and safety risks. Traditional experimental methods are limited in resolving these phenomena at the spatiotemporal scales required for predictive insights. To address this gap, we propose a multi-physics simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model boiler components with unprecedented resolution. The computational approach integrates finite element analysis (FEA) for stress distribution in welded joints, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for steam-water flow interactions, and machine learning algorithms to optimize material selection under cyclic thermal loading. Simulations will parameterize variables such as pressure gradients, weld geometry, and alloy properties, validated against experimental data from laboratory-scale boiler prototypes. The HPC environment is critical for scaling these simulations to real-world boiler geometries, enabling parallelized computation of billion-element meshes and transient analyses spanning operational cycles. Expected outcomes include predictive models for failure-prone regions in boiler assemblies, data-driven recommendations for weld configurations and material composites, and a publicly accessible simulation toolkit for boiler design optimization. By elucidating the interplay between mechanical stress, thermal transfer, and fluid dynamics in boiler systems, this work aims to reduce unplanned downtime in industrial energy infrastructure, enhance safety standards, and inform updates to boiler fabrication codes. The project will also serve as a training platform for boilermaking students in computational methods, bridging gaps between traditional technical education and modern simulation-driven engineering.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to fabricate and repair steam boiler components. Includes instruction in principles of steam power, material selection, welding, riveting, sealing materials, pressure testing, pipefitting, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: The increasing complexity of dynamic aerospace threat environments demands advanced computational tools to optimize real-time decision-making and mission resilience in contested operational domains. This project addresses the challenge of modeling multi-domain aerospace operations under uncertainty, with a focus on rapidly evolving adversarial tactics and resource constraints inherent to military contexts. Current simulation frameworks lack the fidelity to capture emergent behaviors in large-scale, networked systems or the computational speed required for predictive scenario analysis. To bridge this gap, we propose developing an adaptive simulation environment leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to integrate real-time sensor data streams, probabilistic threat assessments, and multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) models. The computational approach will employ distributed Monte Carlo methods to evaluate mission-critical variables across millions of concurrent scenarios, including electronic warfare conditions, swarm tactics, and degraded communications environments. Hybrid neural networks will be trained on synthetic and historical operational datasets to predict system failure cascades and optimize resource reallocation strategies. Key innovations include a novel quantum-inspired optimization layer for rapid contingency planning and a digital twin architecture capable of simulating joint air-space cyber-physical systems at unprecedented scale. Expected outcomes include validated frameworks for predictive battle damage assessment, automated course-of-action generation, and vulnerability prioritization matrices tailored to next-generation aerospace platforms. This work directly supports enhanced operational readiness by providing decision superiority tools that account for the interdependencies between advanced propulsion systems, networked sensors, and human-machine teaming architectures. The requested HPC resources are essential for achieving the necessary computational throughput to model theater-scale engagements with microsecond temporal resolution while maintaining the security protocols required for sensitive military applications.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, technology and maintenance of systems and equipment used in aerospace operations. Includes instruction in astronomy and astronautics, solid state theory, air and space operations, electronics, computer science, aviation and space flight safety, life support systems, flight operations management systems, programming, propulsion systems, weaponry, maintenance management and applications to specific systems and operations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the neurophysiological and biomechanical mechanisms underlying dance movement therapy (DMT) as an intervention for trauma-related anxiety disorders, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex interactions between motor behavior, neural activity, and psychological outcomes. Despite growing clinical interest in DMT, the field lacks robust quantitative frameworks to explain how structured dance modalities influence neural plasticity, emotional regulation, and sensorimotor integration. Current limitations stem from the multidimensional nature of therapeutic movement data—including high-resolution motion capture, EEG recordings, and physiological biomarkers—which requires advanced computational methods to analyze temporal, spatial, and spectral relationships at scale. The research will develop a novel computational pipeline integrating deep learning architectures with dynamical systems modeling to (1) identify movement signatures predictive of therapeutic response, (2) simulate neural correlates of improvisational dance sequences, and (3) optimize personalized intervention protocols through reinforcement learning. Motion data from clinical DMT sessions (360 Hz capture rate) will be fused with concurrent EEG and heart rate variability metrics, generating petabyte-scale datasets necessitating GPU-accelerated processing for real-time feature extraction. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model linking specific movement parameters to amygdala-prefrontal cortex functional connectivity changes, quantified via fMRI-validated simulations. By establishing computational biomarkers for DMT efficacy, this work aims to bridge gaps between embodied therapeutic practices and systems neuroscience, while providing open-source tools for movement analysis in clinical research. The resource-intensive nature of modeling whole-body kinematics alongside multiscale neurophysiological data underscores the critical need for HPC allocation, enabling advances in evidence-based frameworks for somatic therapies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, in consultation with other rehabilitation team members or in private practice, to use the therapeutic application of creative dance movement to assist in promoting client rehabilitation and physical, emotional, and mental health. Includes instruction in neuroanatomy, personality development, movement and motor behavior, psychology, dance, creative expression modalities, improvisation, group psychology and leadership, client evaluation and supervision, dance therapy practice, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern industrial and operational systems demands advanced computational tools to address challenges in optimization, uncertainty quantification, and real-time decision-making. This project seeks to develop a scalable, high-performance computing (HPC) framework to model and optimize large-scale systems with interdependent human, logistical, and informational components. A central focus is the integration of stochastic optimization and discrete-event simulation to address resource allocation problems in dynamic environments, such as manufacturing process flows or distributed supply chains, where traditional analytical methods fail to account for high-dimensional decision spaces and time-varying constraints. The research will employ parallelized mixed-integer programming solvers and agent-based simulation techniques to evaluate system performance under probabilistic disruptions, including demand variability and resource intermittency. Machine learning surrogates will be trained on HPC-generated datasets to accelerate scenario evaluation, enabling rapid trade-off analyses between cost, resilience, and sustainability metrics. Key deliverables include an open-source toolkit for systems-level resource allocation, validated through case studies on multi-echelon inventory networks and service facility scheduling. The computational demands of this work—particularly the need to solve stochastic optimization models with millions of variables and simulate heterogeneous agent interactions at scale—necessitate access to GPU-accelerated nodes and distributed-memory architectures. Expected outcomes include quantifiable strategies for balancing capital expenditure and operational flexibility in industrial systems, as well as methodological advances in decomposing complex systems engineering problems into computationally tractable submodels. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this research aims to bridge gaps between theoretical systems engineering principles and practical implementations in sectors requiring robust, adaptive resource management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of total systems solutions to a wide variety of engineering problems, including the integration of human, physical, energy, communications, management, and information requirements as needed, and the application of requisite analytical methods to specific situations.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance the personalization and scalability of online teaching strategies by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model dynamic learner-instructor interactions in virtual environments. A critical challenge in online education is tailoring instructional approaches to diverse learner needs while maintaining pedagogical efficacy at scale. Current methods for analyzing behavioral patterns, performance trends, and engagement metrics in learning management systems (LMS) often rely on static, aggregate-level data, limiting real-time adaptability. To address this gap, we propose developing computational models that simulate multi-agent interactions across heterogeneous learner profiles, instructional modalities, and assessment frameworks. These simulations will integrate machine learning algorithms trained on anonymized LMS datasets (e.g., discussion forum interactions, assignment submissions, and multimedia resource usage) to predict optimal pedagogical interventions under varying constraints. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel processing of temporal interaction networks and probabilistic testing of adaptive instructional designs. Key outcomes include a framework for real-time pedagogical decision-making and evidence-based guidelines for dynamically restructuring course content based on emergent learner behaviors. By quantifying how computational latency and resource allocation impact the fidelity of adaptive systems, this work will inform the design of next-generation online teaching tools capable of balancing responsiveness with computational efficiency. The results will directly benefit teacher education programs by providing empirically validated strategies for implementing scalable, personalized instruction in virtual classrooms.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students at various academic levels through online instructional technologies. Includes instruction in andragogy, pedagogy, assessment, instructional design and technology, and learning science.

abstract: The analysis of complex chemical mixtures remains a critical challenge in analytical chemistry, particularly in scenarios requiring high sensitivity and selectivity for trace components in environmental, biological, and pharmaceutical systems. Traditional experimental methods, such as chromatography and spectroscopy, often face limitations in resolving overlapping signals or predicting optimal separation conditions, leading to time-consuming iterative workflows. This project seeks to address these challenges by integrating computational modeling with experimental data to enhance the precision and efficiency of analytical method development. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform large-scale quantum mechanical calculations and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, which will model solute-solvent interactions, stationary phase behaviors in chromatographic systems, and photophysical properties of analytes in spectroscopic techniques. These simulations will generate datasets correlating molecular structures with retention times, spectral signatures, and intermolecular forces, enabling the identification of optimal separation conditions and spectral deconvolution parameters. Additionally, machine learning algorithms will be trained on simulation outputs and experimental data to predict analytical performance metrics under untested conditions. The computational workflow will reduce reliance on trial-and-error experimentation, accelerate method optimization, and improve detection limits for low-abundance species. Expected outcomes include the development of open-source tools for predictive analytical method design and validated protocols for coupling computational predictions with laboratory workflows. This work will directly support ongoing research in environmental pollutant tracking and pharmaceutical impurity profiling, where rapid, accurate analysis of complex matrices is essential. The requested HPC resources are critical due to the high computational cost of ab initio calculations, the need for parallelized MD simulations across diverse chemical systems, and the scale of data processing required for machine learning model training. By bridging computational and experimental analytical chemistry, this project aims to advance the field’s capacity to address real-world problems with data-driven precision.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of techniques for analyzing and describing matter, including its precise composition and the interrelationships of constituent elements and compounds. Includes instruction in spectroscopy, chromatography, atomic absorption, photometry, chemical modeling, mathematical analysis, laboratory analysis procedures and equipment maintenance, and applications to specific research, industrial and health problems.

abstract: Neurodegenerative and neuromuscular diseases present complex diagnostic challenges due to heterogeneous molecular and histopathological signatures. Current methodologies in neuropathology often rely on manual, subjective interpretation of nerve tissue biopsies or postmortem analyses, which limits the detection of subtle, early-stage disease markers and hinders the development of personalized therapeutic strategies. This project seeks to address these limitations by integrating high-resolution histopathological imaging, multi-omics data, and computational modeling to identify predictive biomarkers and disease mechanisms. The primary research problem involves analyzing spatially resolved cellular interactions in nerve tissues across diverse neurological conditions, including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, to uncover patterns undetectable through conventional techniques. The computational approach combines deep learning-based image segmentation of myelination patterns and axonal degeneration in whole-slide imaging (WSI) datasets with graph neural networks (GNNs) to model neuron-glia interaction networks. Multi-omics integration—including single-nucleus RNA sequencing and proteomic profiles from biopsy cohorts—will be performed using variational autoencoders (VAEs) to link molecular subtypes to histopathological phenotypes. These analyses require high-performance computing (HPC) resources due to the scale of WSI data (≥10 TB), the complexity of training 3D convolutional neural networks on multi-gigapixel images, and the iterative optimization of multimodal fusion models. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel biomarkers for early disease stratification, predictive models of neurodegeneration progression, and open-source tools for automated neuropathology workflows. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project aims to advance precision diagnostics and contribute foundational insights into the spatial biology of neurological disorders, directly supporting translational research in clinical neuropathology.
cip_definition: Research focused on the laboratory analysis of nerve tissues and the clinical diagnosis of neurological and neuromuscular diseases. May included related research in nerve biopsies and necropsies.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the historical and sociocultural dynamics shaping educational policy diffusion across diverse geopolitical contexts from the 20th century to the present. While qualitative studies have dominated the analysis of educational policy as a social institution, this work adopts a mixed-methods computational approach to systematically examine macro-scale patterns and micro-level mechanisms of policy adoption, resistance, and adaptation. The central research problem concerns how ideological frameworks—including colonialism, neoliberalism, and human rights discourses—interact with local educational practices to produce heterogeneous outcomes in curriculum standardization efforts. To address this, the project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques on a novel corpus of 1.2 million digitized policy documents, educational reports, and oral history transcripts from 14 nations, alongside agent-based modeling (ABM) simulations of policy implementation networks. The computational workflow requires high-performance computing resources for three critical tasks: (1) training transformer-based language models to detect semantic shifts in policy rhetoric across temporal and cultural contexts, (2) running large-scale ABM simulations incorporating demographic, economic, and institutional variables at regional granularity, and (3) performing network analysis on cross-national policy influence patterns using dynamic graph neural networks. Expected outcomes include a computational framework for mapping the epistemic boundaries of "educational transfer" as a contested social process, quantitative evidence challenging linear narratives of policy convergence, and open-access tools for analyzing power asymmetries in transnational educational governance. By integrating computational social science methods with critical philosophical perspectives, this research aims to advance interdisciplinary methodologies for studying education as both a vehicle for social reproduction and a site of emancipatory struggle. The requested resources will enable processing of multilingual archival materials at scale while maintaining the interpretive depth necessary for grounded theoretical development in educational philosophy.
cip_title: Social and Philosophical Foundations of Education
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of education as a social and cultural institution, and the educational process as an object of humanistic inquiry. Includes instruction in such subjects as the philosophy of education, history of education, educational literature, educational anthropology, sociology of education, economics and politics of education, educational policy studies, and studies of education in relation to specific populations, issues, social phenomena, and types of work.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced optimization frameworks for next-generation wireless communication systems, with a focus on enhancing spectral efficiency and reliability in densely deployed 5G/6G networks and Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystems. The proliferation of heterogeneous devices, dynamic traffic patterns, and stringent quality-of-service requirements in modern telecommunications infrastructure necessitates computationally intensive modeling to address challenges in interference mitigation, resource allocation, and adaptive beamforming. We propose a multi-scale computational approach integrating machine learning-driven channel estimation, large-scale optimization of massive MIMO (multiple-input multiple-output) configurations, and stochastic modeling of millimeter-wave propagation in urban environments. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will be critical for executing parallelized electromagnetic simulations using finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) methods, training deep neural networks for real-time signal processing, and solving non-convex optimization problems across distributed antenna systems. The research will leverage GPU-accelerated computing to analyze terabyte-scale datasets of channel state information and network traffic logs collected from experimental testbeds. Expected outcomes include novel algorithms for dynamic spectrum sharing, optimized precoding matrices for reduced inter-cell interference, and validated models for energy-efficient beam alignment in reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted networks. These advancements will directly inform the design of scalable, low-latency communication protocols for smart city applications and industrial IoT deployments. The requested computing resources will enable parameter sweeps across thousands of network topology variations and physical-layer configurations that are infeasible with existing campus cluster capabilities, significantly accelerating the translation of theoretical models into practical implementation guidelines for telecom operators and standards bodies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development, and maintenance of telecommunications technology, networks, and systems. Includes instruction in telecommunications, computer networking, communications networks and systems, signals, circuits, fiber optics, and wireless systems and technology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the interconnections between linguistic diversity, digital cultural heritage, and identity formation across Southeast Asia, with a focus on underrepresented minority communities. The research addresses a critical gap in the preservation and computational study of non-dominant cultural narratives, particularly those expressed through endangered languages, oral traditions, and ephemeral digital media (e.g., social media, community forums) produced by diaspora groups. Current methodologies lack the capacity to process large-scale, multilingual datasets spanning formal archives and informal digital repositories, hindering holistic understandings of cultural continuity and transformation. The project will employ NLP techniques optimized for low-resource languages—including transformer models fine-tuned on regional dialects—to analyze textual and audio-visual materials from curated collections and web archives. Computational ethnolinguistic mapping will be implemented to trace semantic shifts in cultural keywords across time and migrant communities, while network analysis will identify patterns in cross-cultural knowledge exchange. HPC resources are essential for training custom embeddings on mixed-modality data (text, image, audio) and simulating language-culture interaction models at scale. Expected outcomes include an open-access repository of processed datasets, computational workflows tailored to Southeast Asian contexts, and visualizations of cultural discourse networks. These resources will support scholars in interpreting how digitalization impacts identity negotiation in marginalized communities, offering methodological innovations for regional studies beyond conventional text-centric approaches. The project aligns with institutional priorities in decolonial digital humanities and strengthens interdisciplinary collaborations with Southeast Asian cultural organizations.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of Southeast Asia, defined as including Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, The Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Viet Nam; related borderlands and island groups; and including the study of migration patterns and overseas diasporas.

abstract: Optimizing climate control and resource allocation in greenhouse ecosystems presents complex challenges due to the nonlinear interactions between biological processes, environmental variables, and operational parameters. Current practices often rely on generalized protocols that inadequately account for spatial heterogeneity in microclimates, species-specific physiological responses, or real-time energy trade-offs, resulting in suboptimal yields and resource inefficiencies. This project seeks to develop a computational modeling framework to dynamically simulate and optimize greenhouse operations through high-performance computing (HPC). We propose integrating multi-agent plant growth models with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to resolve fine-scale environmental gradients in temperature, humidity, and light distribution across greenhouse architectures. Machine learning techniques, including recurrent neural networks and reinforcement learning, will be applied to historical and real-time sensor data to predict crop responses to environmental perturbations and optimize control strategies for irrigation, ventilation, and supplemental lighting. The HPC environment will enable parallel execution of ensemble simulations to quantify uncertainty in growth predictions and test resilience under varying climate scenarios. Additionally, we will implement graph-based optimization algorithms to model resource distribution networks, minimizing energy and water use while maintaining production targets. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system capable of recommending adaptive control parameters for diverse crop species, reducing energy consumption by 15–20% in simulated greenhouse prototypes, and improving yield predictability through stress-response forecasting. This research will provide a foundational computational toolkit for precision greenhouse management, enabling data-driven operational strategies that enhance sustainability and productivity in controlled-environment agriculture.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to produce, store, and deliver plant species in controlled indoor environments for wholesale, commercial, research, or other purposes. Includes instruction in applicable principles of plant science; climate, irrigation, and nutrition control equipment operation and maintenance; facilities management; inventory control; safety procedures; and personnel supervision.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between shifting environmental conditions and population mobility patterns in vulnerable regions, with a focus on improving predictive models of demographic resilience under climate stress. Current population projections often inadequately integrate high-resolution environmental data with sociobehavioral migration drivers, limiting their utility for anticipating displacement cascades or evaluating intervention scenarios. Our research employs an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework to simulate multi-scale population-environment interactions, incorporating spatially explicit climate projections (e.g., drought frequency, extreme heat events), demographic microdata, and longitudinal survey data on migration decision-making. The computational demands of this approach necessitate high-performance computing resources to manage three critical challenges: 1) Parallel processing of ensemble climate scenarios at 1km² resolution across decade-scale time horizons, 2) Bayesian calibration of agent decision algorithms against heterogeneous regional survey datasets, and 3) Real-time visualization of emergent migration networks under alternative policy interventions. By leveraging GPU-accelerated parameter space exploration and distributed memory architectures, we aim to overcome current limitations in spatial demography that arise from oversimplified environmental feedback mechanisms. Expected outcomes include an open-source modeling platform for climate-demography simulations, novel metrics of population vulnerability that integrate biophysical and social thresholds, and evidence-based projections of migration pressures under IPCC climate pathways. This work will advance methodological integration in population studies while providing actionable insights for stakeholders addressing climate adaptation challenges. The requested computing resources will enable unprecedented spatial granularity and temporal depth in simulating human-environment systems, directly addressing core gaps in demographic theory regarding nonlinear population responses to environmental change.
detailed_field: Sociology, demography, and population studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of population models and population phenomena, and related problems of social structure and behavior. Includes instruction in population growth, spatial distribution, mortality and fertility factors, migration, dynamic population modeling, population estimation and projection, mathematical and statistical analysis of population data, population policy studies, and applications to problems in economics and government planning.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the computational complexity of tax compliance strategies under dynamic regulatory conditions in U.S. jurisdictions. The increasing intricacy of federal and state tax codes, combined with the rapid evolution of digital asset reporting requirements, has created a landscape where traditional legal analysis struggles to model the cascading effects of policy changes or taxpayer behavior at scale. The project addresses this gap by developing agent-based simulations to evaluate how hypothetical tax reforms—such as modifications to depreciation schedules, cryptocurrency reporting thresholds, or cross-state income apportionment rules—interact with taxpayer decision-making algorithms. Computational methods will integrate large-scale datasets, including anonymized tax return data, economic indicators, and textual analysis of legal documents, to parameterize multi-agent models. These models will simulate scenarios involving heterogeneous agents (e.g., corporations, high-net-worth individuals, gig economy workers) operating across multiple jurisdictions, with reinforcement learning techniques applied to approximate adaptive compliance strategies. A key innovation involves coupling natural language processing (NLP) of tax code revisions with real-time adjustments to agent behavior rules, enabling analysis of how regulatory ambiguity influences compliance costs. Expected outcomes include quantitative estimates of the computational resources required by taxpayers to maintain compliance under proposed legislative changes, identification of systemic vulnerabilities in current regulatory architectures, and predictive metrics for the administrative burden of emerging tax policies. The results aim to inform both legislative design and private-sector compliance infrastructure development while establishing a methodological framework for computational legal analysis in taxation. This work occupies an interdisciplinary niche at the intersection of computational social science, regulatory theory, and professional tax practice, requiring HPC capabilities to manage the combinatorial complexity of multi-jurisdictional rules and large agent populations.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of tax law and taxation procedures in U.S. or Canadian jurisdictions affecting individuals and corporations.

abstract: The biological effects of ionizing radiation arise from complex molecular interactions that drive DNA damage, protein dysfunction, and cellular repair processes. Current gaps in understanding the precise biophysical mechanisms of radiation-induced damage at the atomic and molecular levels limit the development of targeted radioprotective strategies and precision radiotherapies. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model radiation-induced perturbations in critical biomolecular systems, with a focus on DNA-protein interactions and repair enzyme dynamics. We propose a multi-scale computational approach integrating quantum mechanical (QM) simulations of radiation-induced ionization events, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of DNA damage recognition by repair proteins, and kinetic modeling of repair pathway activation. QM simulations will quantify ionization cross-sections and radical formation in DNA backbone components and associated water molecules, providing energetics for parametrizing coarse-grained MD models. Large-scale MD simulations will then track the structural dynamics of DNA repair complexes (e.g., base excision repair glycosylases) as they recognize and process radiation-induced lesions under varying ionization densities. Parallelized kinetic Monte Carlo methods will model the competition between lesion accumulation and repair kinetics in simulated chromatin environments. These simulations require HPC resources due to the femtosecond-scale resolution needed for QM accuracy, microsecond-scale MD trajectories for conformational sampling, and the combinatorial complexity of lesion-repairer interactions across biologically relevant timescales. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into how radiation quality (e.g., linear energy transfer) influences lesion complexity and repair fidelity, as well as predictive models linking molecular-scale damage to cellular survival curves. This work will advance radiobiology by establishing a computational framework to dissect the biophysical determinants of radiation toxicity, with implications for optimizing therapeutic radiation regimens and mitigating off-target effects in healthy tissues.
detailed_field: Biochemistry, biophysics, and molecular biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the effects of radiation on organisms and biological systems. Includes instruction in particle physics, ionization, and biophysics of radiation perturbations, cellular and organismic repair systems, genetic and pathological effects of radiation, and the measurement of radiation dosages.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the structure and dynamics of neutron-rich nuclei, which exhibit exotic behaviors such as halo formations, extended density distributions, and anomalous decay modes. Traditional nuclear models, which rely on phenomenological potentials and simplified interactions, struggle to predict these features accurately. To overcome these limitations, we propose large-scale ab initio calculations using high-performance computing (HPC) resources to solve the nuclear many-body problem with realistic nucleon-nucleon and three-nucleon interactions derived from chiral effective field theory. The computational approach will employ the coupled-cluster method and configuration-interaction techniques, optimized for parallel architectures to handle the exponential scaling of model spaces with increasing nucleon numbers. Key simulations will focus on isotopes near the neutron dripline, such as oxygen-24 and calcium-60, where experimental data are sparse but critical for testing fundamental nuclear forces. These calculations will leverage advanced numerical algorithms, including iterative eigensolvers and tensor contractions, distributed across thousands of CPU cores to manage memory and processing demands. Additionally, machine learning tools will be integrated to classify wavefunction correlations and optimize basis selection. The expected outcomes include precise predictions of nuclear binding energies, excited-state spectra, and beta-decay rates, which will guide upcoming experiments at rare-isotope beam facilities. The results will also refine constraints on three-nucleon force parameters, enhancing the predictive power of nuclear models for astrophysically relevant reactions and symmetry energy studies. By utilizing HPC resources, this work will bridge the gap between theoretical frameworks and observable nuclear phenomena, advancing our understanding of strong interactions in quantum many-body systems while providing foundational data for applications in nuclear energy and isotope science.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the properties and behavior of atomic nuclei. Includes instruction in nuclear reaction theory, quantum mechanics, energy conservation, nuclear fission and fusion, strong and weak forces, nuclear modeling, nuclear decay, nucleon scattering, pairing, photon and electron reactions, the physics of nuclear effects, statistical methods, and research equipment operation and maintenance.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the challenge of optimizing equitable access and ecological sustainability in urban park systems, a critical issue within Parks, Recreation, and Leisure Studies. Urban parks face competing demands: increasing visitor use, preserving biodiversity, and mitigating climate impacts. Traditional planning methods struggle to model the dynamic interplay of these factors at scale. The project will develop a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), geospatial analytics, and machine learning (ML) to simulate visitor behavior, ecosystem stressors, and climate scenarios across heterogeneous urban landscapes. Using anonymized mobility data, ecological surveys, and climate projections, the ABM will simulate visitation patterns under varying park designs, while ML algorithms predict long-term biodiversity responses to human activity and environmental changes.
