Computational experiments will compare neural architecture configurations for capturing cross-property demand spillover effects and evaluate constraint-handling methods for maintaining service quality thresholds during capacity reallocations. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support toolkit that balances profitability with carbon footprint reduction targets, along with new metrics for resilient resource deployment in tourism-dependent regions. By integrating operations research, environmental science, and AI ethics considerations specific to hospitality contexts, this work aims to advance computational social science methodologies while addressing pressing industry challenges in post-pandemic recovery and climate adaptation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as general managers and directors of hospitality operations on a system-wide basis, including both travel arrangements and promotion and the provision of traveler facilities. Includes instruction in principles of operations in the travel and tourism, hotel and lodging facilities, food services, and recreation facilities industries; hospitality marketing strategies; hospitality planning; management and coordination of franchise and unit operations; business management; accounting and financial management; hospitality transportation and logistics; and hospitality industry policies and regulations.

abstract: Breastfeeding is a critical public health priority with demonstrated benefits for maternal and infant health, yet many individuals face significant challenges in initiating or sustaining lactation due to physiological, sociocultural, and systemic barriers. This project seeks to address gaps in predictive modeling and intervention design for lactation support by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze complex, multi-dimensional datasets. The research problem centers on identifying modifiable risk factors for lactation difficulties and optimizing evidence-based strategies for lactation consultants. Using anonymized clinical data from electronic health records (demographics, lactation histories, biometric measurements) and qualitative inputs from patient-reported experiences, we will develop machine learning models to predict lactation outcomes and simulate the impact of targeted interventions. Computational methods include natural language processing (NLP) of clinical notes to extract latent themes in care barriers, agent-based modeling to evaluate community-level effects of lactation education campaigns, and Bayesian network analysis to map interactions between biological variables (e.g., hormonal profiles, infant latch dynamics) and social determinants of health. HPC resources are essential for processing large-scale datasets, training deep learning architectures, and running iterative simulations under diverse scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive tool to prioritize high-risk populations for early lactation support, (2) actionable insights into intervention efficacy across demographic subgroups, and (3) open-source computational frameworks tailored to lactation research. By integrating computational rigor with clinical expertise, this work aims to advance equitable access to lactation care, reduce disparities in breastfeeding duration, and inform policy decisions for maternal-child health systems. The project aligns with the Lactation Consultant program’s focus on evidence-based practice and advocacy by translating data-driven findings into scalable solutions for clinical and community settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide lactation management services and breastfeeding support to women, and to work as a Lactation Consultant in a variety of clinical settings. Includes instruction in anatomy and physiology of lactation, nutrition, breastfeeding techniques and technologies, common concerns and solutions, management of special situations, breastfeeding instruction, professional and legal concerns, and advocacy.

abstract: Applied behavior analysis (ABA) relies on data-driven methodologies to design and optimize interventions that improve outcomes for individuals with developmental disabilities, including autism spectrum disorder. However, existing approaches to analyzing behavioral data often face limitations in scalability, personalization, and real-time adaptability due to the computational complexity of modeling dynamic, individualized behavior patterns across diverse settings. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing and validating computational models of behavioral change processes using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will leverage large-scale datasets comprising longitudinal behavior records, environmental context variables, and intervention histories from clinical and community settings. Machine learning techniques, including recurrent neural networks and reinforcement learning algorithms, will be employed to identify latent patterns in behavior-environment interactions and predict individualized response trajectories. Agent-based modeling will simulate the emergent effects of intervention variations across heterogeneous populations, while Monte Carlo methods will quantify uncertainty in treatment effect estimates under real-world conditions. By parallelizing these computationally intensive tasks across HPC clusters, the project aims to generate actionable insights into optimal intervention timing, dosage, and adaptation strategies that traditional statistical methods cannot feasibly produce. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for behavior analysts to design personalized interventions using predictive modeling, as well as evidence-based frameworks for scaling effective ABA practices across service delivery systems. The computational infrastructure will specifically support research into reducing disparities in intervention access and effectiveness for underserved populations. This work advances the scientific rigor of ABA by enabling complex, data-intensive analyses critical for addressing the multifaceted needs of neurodiverse individuals while adhering to the ethical principles of behavioral research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of principles of learning and behavior to enhance the development, abilities, and choices of children and adults; and that prepares individuals to address the behavioral needs of individuals, especially those with developmental disabilities and autism. Includes instruction in behavior analysis and learning, behavioral and functional assessment, developmental psychology, applied behavioral analysis in developmental disabilities and autism, applied behavioral analysis in mental health and aging, research methods, evaluation of interventions, and professional and ethical issues.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive modeling framework to understand the spatiotemporal dynamics of understudied arboviral diseases in rapidly urbanizing tropical regions, with a focus on interactions between climate anomalies, human mobility, and vector adaptation. Despite increasing incidence of diseases like Mayaro and Oropouche fevers, current public health strategies remain reactive due to gaps in modeling how urbanization gradients and microclimate variability influence transmission bottlenecks between sylvatic and peri-urban cycles. We propose an agent-based model integrating high-resolution climate projections, cellular automata representing vector breeding niche plasticity, and anonymized mobile device-derived mobility patterns across a 10-year retrospective study domain in the Amazon Basin. The computational workflow will employ hybrid machine learning (graph neural networks) and mechanistic modeling to identify tipping points in spillover risk under combined socioeconomic and environmental change scenarios. High-performance computing resources are essential for parameterizing the model’s 1km²-scale spatial resolution across 500,000+ agents, parallel simulation of 10^4 climate-urbanization permutations, and real-time assimilation of heterogeneous datasets (satellite phenology, genomic surveillance, and municipal health records). Expected outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for forecasting emerging arbovirus hotspots, maps of sentinel zones for proactive surveillance, and evolutionary risk scores quantifying potential viral adaptation to urban Aedes vectors. By bridging landscape ecology, computational epidemiology, and climate science, this work aims to transform resource-limited health systems’ capacity to preempt tropical viral emergence rather than respond to outbreaks. The requested resources will directly enable ensemble simulations at scales required to capture nonlinear feedbacks between human and vector populations—a computational challenge currently constraining precision in tropical disease forecasting.
cip_definition: A program that prepares clinicians to prevent and control vector-borne and tropical infectious diseases. Includes instruction in microbiology, parasitology, mycology, virology, vector biology, vaccinology, laboratory diagnosis, travelers' health, epidemiology, and disease management.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of regulatory compliance in multinational organizations by developing computational tools to analyze and predict legal obligations across dynamic, multi-jurisdictional frameworks. As global regulations proliferate and evolve rapidly, manual tracking of compliance requirements has become error-prone and resource-intensive, creating significant operational and financial risks. The research leverages high-performance computing (HPC) to process vast corpora of legal texts, regulatory updates, and enforcement actions, with the goal of automating the identification of compliance obligations, conflicts, and emerging risks. The computational approach combines natural language processing (NLP) tailored to legal syntax, graph-based analytics to map interdependencies between regulations, and machine learning models trained on historical compliance violations to forecast high-risk areas. By integrating heterogeneous data sources—including statutes, case law, administrative rulings, and internal organizational policies—the system will generate adaptive compliance frameworks that update in near real-time. Key technical challenges include scaling semantic analysis for low-resource legal languages, resolving ambiguities in cross-jurisdictional terminology, and ensuring interpretability of risk predictions for legal professionals. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for compliance gap analysis, a predictive dashboard for regulatory trend monitoring, and a benchmark dataset linking regulatory features to enforcement patterns. This work bridges computational methods and legal theory, offering a novel paradigm for proactive compliance management while contributing to the emerging field of computational legal studies. The requested HPC resources are critical for training large language models on specialized legal corpora and simulating regulatory network dynamics at scale, tasks that exceed the capacity of standard institutional infrastructure. By reducing the latency between regulatory changes and organizational response, this research aims to enhance ethical governance, minimize compliance costs, and mitigate systemic risks in global operations.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations for lawyers and non-legal professionals in compliance, ethics, internal monitoring, regulatory affairs, and related areas.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) protocols and improve clinical outcomes for decompression illness, non-healing wounds, and radiation-induced tissue damage through advanced computational modeling of physiological responses under hyperbaric conditions. Current HBOT treatment schedules rely on empirical data and generalized frameworks, which may inadequately address patient-specific factors such as tissue perfusion heterogeneity, gas solubility dynamics, and oxidative stress thresholds. To address this gap, we propose developing multi-scale computational models integrating fluid dynamics, gas transport, and cellular metabolic pathways under varying hyperbaric exposures. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable simulations of gas bubble formation and resolution in decompression sickness using three-dimensional fluid-structure interaction models, coupled with pharmacokinetic modeling of oxygen radical scavenging in ischemic tissues. Machine learning algorithms will analyze multi-parametric clinical datasets from 450 historical diving injury cases and 300 HBOT-treated chronic wound patients to identify predictive biomarkers for treatment response. Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will assess probabilistic risks of oxygen toxicity across diverse patient phenotypes, informing adaptive treatment algorithms. The computational framework will be validated against real-time tissue oxygenation data from hyperbaric chamber trials and retrospective clinical outcomes. Expected outcomes include personalized HBOT dosing schedules, risk stratification tools for iatrogenic complications, and predictive models for wound healing trajectories. This work will directly enhance evidence-based protocol design for diving injury management while advancing mechanistic understanding of hyperbaric interventions in complex tissue repair processes. By leveraging HPC capabilities to manage large-scale biomechanical simulations and high-dimensional clinical data integration, the project aims to establish a translational pipeline from computational discovery to optimized therapeutic strategies in undersea and hyperbaric medicine.
cip_definition: Research on how to treat decompression illness and diving accident cases; to use hyperbaric oxygen therapy treatment for conditions such as carbon monoxide poisoning, gas gangrene, non-healing wounds, tissue damage from radiation and burns, and bone infections; to serve as consultant in all aspects of hyperbaric chamber operations; and to assess risks and apply appropriate standards to prevent disease and disability in divers and other persons working in altered atmospheric conditions.

abstract: Medical education faces growing complexity in training healthcare professionals to meet evolving clinical demands, yet evidence-based approaches to optimize curricular design, delivery, and evaluation remain underdeveloped. This project seeks to address critical gaps in medical education research by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze multimodal educational datasets and simulate training interventions. The research problem centers on identifying scalable, personalized strategies for teaching clinical reasoning, procedural skills, and interdisciplinary collaboration across diverse learner cohorts (medical students, residents, and faculty). Current limitations stem from the inability to process large-scale behavioral data—including simulated patient interactions, procedural competency metrics, and longitudinal performance records—while accounting for contextual variables such as specialty-specific requirements and individual learning trajectories. We propose developing machine learning models to analyze structured and unstructured educational data sources, including virtual patient simulations (video/audio recordings), electronic learning platform engagement logs, and competency assessment outcomes. Computational workflows will integrate natural language processing for qualitative feedback analysis, computer vision for procedural skill assessment in simulation labs, and reinforcement learning to model adaptive curriculum pathways. These methods require HPC resources due to the volume of video data (>10,000 hours), complexity of multimodal data fusion, and need for real-time parameter optimization in training simulations. Anticipated outcomes include (1) predictive models identifying at-risk learners through early performance patterns, (2) validated metrics for evaluating team-based clinical training efficacy, and (3) generative AI tools for creating personalized case scenarios. By establishing computational frameworks for medical education research, this work aims to advance evidence-based curriculum design while addressing critical workforce training needs in healthcare. The requested computing resources will enable processing of sensitive educational data in secure environments while maintaining the low-latency requirements of interactive simulation analyses.
cip_definition: Research on how to teach deliver, design, and evaluate courses and curricula for medical students, residents, and faculty.

abstract: Dental implant success hinges on the complex interplay between biomechanical forces, osseointegration dynamics, and patient-specific anatomical constraints. Despite advances in implantology, unpredictable bone resorption and peri-implantitis remain significant causes of long-term failure, with conventional clinical methods offering limited predictive capacity for individual biomechanical responses. This project proposes a computational framework to model multiscale interactions between dental implants and host tissues under dynamic physiological loads, integrating finite element analysis (FEA) with agent-based modeling (ABM) of cellular osseointegration processes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve time-dependent micromechanical stresses across implant interfaces while simulating osteoblast-osteoclast activity at cellular resolution across clinically relevant timescales (6–24 months). Patient-specific mandibular anatomy derived from cone-beam CT scans will inform FEA meshes, with material properties calibrated via nanoindentation data from cadaveric bone samples. The ABM component will incorporate mechanobiological rules governing bone remodeling, informed by gene expression profiles from single-cell RNA sequencing of peri-implant tissues in a murine model. Parallelized simulations will assess how variables including implant thread geometry, alloy surface treatments, and occlusal loading patterns influence strain distributions and biological integration. Expected outcomes include predictive models identifying failure-prone implant configurations, optimization guidelines for prosthodontic load distribution, and a novel metric quantifying "biomechanical compatibility" for patient-specific treatment planning. By bridging continuum mechanics with cellular-scale biology, this work aims to establish computational workflows for next-generation personalized implantology, reducing revision surgeries and improving functional outcomes. The scale of 3D transient simulations (>10^8 elements) and coupled ABM-FEA parameter optimization necessitates HPC capabilities exceeding local cluster capacities, particularly for GPU-accelerated solver routines and large parameter space exploration.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on dental implantology. Includes instruction in diagnosis and treatment planning, surgical protocols, implant placement, sinus grafting, guided bone regeneration, soft tissue grafting, prosthetic protocols, prosthesis design, and aftercare.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate how postsecondary instructors adapt learner-centered teaching strategies when integrating emerging educational technologies, with a focus on identifying scalable practices that improve equity in diverse classrooms. Despite growing emphasis on active learning and inclusive pedagogy, many instructors struggle to implement these approaches effectively in technology-mediated environments, particularly when addressing variability in student backgrounds, digital literacy, and engagement. Current frameworks often lack empirical validation under real-world computational constraints, such as limited tools for real-time adaptive feedback or dynamic assessment. To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based simulations of virtual classrooms to model instructor decision-making and student outcomes under varied pedagogical and technological conditions. Simulations will incorporate empirical data from learning management systems, student assessment records, and instructor surveys across multiple disciplines. Machine learning techniques, including clustering and reinforcement learning, will identify patterns in effective teaching adaptations, while natural language processing will analyze qualitative feedback from instructors and students. The computational workload requires high-performance resources due to the scale of simulations (parallelized across thousands of agent configurations) and the complexity of training models on multimodal datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models of how specific technology integrations influence equity gaps in course outcomes, (2) a framework for designing adaptive professional development resources that help instructors align tool use with learner-centered principles, and (3) open-source code for simulating pedagogical scenarios that reflect diverse institutional contexts. This work directly supports teacher education programs in preparing faculty to critically evaluate and implement educational technologies, with implications for improving instructional design practices in STEM and humanities disciplines. Results will be disseminated through workshops for postsecondary teaching centers and a public repository of simulation tools.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach at a postsecondary institution. Includes instruction in andragogy, assessment, classroom motivation, instructional design and technology, learner-centered teaching, learning science, syllabus construction, and teaching critical thinking.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the design of dynamic, stimuli-responsive nanoscale systems through multiscale computational modeling, enabling precise control over self-assembling nanomaterials for adaptive applications. Current challenges in nanoengineering arise from the complex interplay of quantum, molecular, and continuum-scale phenomena in nanodevices, particularly those exhibiting time-dependent reconfiguration under external stimuli (e.g., thermal, optical, or electrochemical inputs). Traditional modeling approaches often fail to capture the coupled physics and kinetics governing these systems, limiting predictive design capabilities. To address this gap, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating density functional tight-binding (DFTB) simulations, coarse-grained molecular dynamics, and continuum-scale phase-field models with machine learning-driven optimization. The computational workflow will focus on two interconnected thrusts: (1) simulating light-activated molecular switches embedded in programmable DNA origami scaffolds, and (2) modeling electric field-guided nanoparticle assembly in tunable ionic liquid matrices. Both systems require parallelized simulations across spatial scales (0.1-100 nm) and temporal domains (fs to ms) to resolve emergent hierarchical structures and switching dynamics. The HPC resources will enable parameter space exploration through massively parallel simulations, coupled with neural network surrogates to accelerate design optimization. Anticipated outcomes include new fundamental insights into energy landscape engineering for reconfigurable nanosystems and validated protocols for designing nanoscale actuators and adaptive metamaterials. This work directly supports emerging applications in programmable drug delivery systems and responsive energy storage interfaces while establishing computational methodologies for next-generation nanoscale engineering. Successful implementation will require sustained access to GPU-accelerated nodes for quantum-mechanical calculations and high-memory nodes for large-scale molecular assemblies, with expected utilization of 500,000 core-hours annually. The resulting open-source simulation tools and datasets will be disseminated to advance research in this emerging interdisciplinary domain.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the engineering of systems at the atomic or molecular level (in the range of 1-100 nanometers) building from knowledge across engineering disciplines.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance the pedagogical training of Latin educators by analyzing historical and contemporary Latin language usage patterns. Despite Latin’s status as a foundational language for many academic disciplines, current teacher education programs often rely on static, text-based curricula that inadequately address the evolving challenges of teaching Latin as a non-spoken language in diverse classroom settings. The research problem centers on identifying gaps in existing pedagogical strategies by modeling the syntactic, morphological, and semantic complexity of Latin texts across genres and historical periods. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques to process a corpus of digitized Latin texts (spanning Classical to Medieval periods) and generate adaptive learning modules. Computational methods will include tokenization and dependency parsing using Latin-specific NLP pipelines, machine learning-driven analysis of student interaction data from pilot teaching modules, and agent-based simulations of classroom dynamics under varying instructional approaches. The scalability of these analyses—particularly the parallel processing of large text corpora and real-time simulation of learner outcomes—necessitates access to HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include (1) a data-driven framework for optimizing Latin grammar and vocabulary instruction based on frequency and difficulty metrics, (2) generative models for creating context-aware translation exercises, and (3) evidence-based recommendations for integrating computational tools into Latin teacher training programs. By bridging classical philology with modern computational pedagogy, this work aims to empower educators with dynamic, empirically validated teaching strategies, ultimately improving student engagement and proficiency in Latin language acquisition. The proposed computational workflows will be shared as open-source resources for the broader classics education community.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach Latin at various grade levels.

abstract: Comprehensive Transition and Postsecondary (CTP) programs aim to empower students with intellectual disabilities through academic, social, and vocational skill development. However, a critical gap persists in systematically evaluating how individualized program components interact to influence long-term employment outcomes. This project proposes a computational study to model the multifaceted dynamics of CTP interventions and their impact on workforce integration. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will develop agent-based simulations to replicate student pathways through academic modules, social skill-building activities, and workplace training. These simulations will integrate anonymized longitudinal data from existing CTP cohorts, including academic performance metrics, behavioral assessments, and post-program employment records. Machine learning methods will identify patterns in skill acquisition timelines, social network influences, and barriers to employment. The computational framework will also test hypothetical program modifications—such as adjusted curricula or mentorship structures—to predict their efficacy under diverse demographic and socioeconomic conditions. By parallelizing simulations across HPC nodes, we aim to analyze millions of parameter combinations, enabling robust sensitivity analyses and optimization of intervention strategies. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for CTP program success, actionable insights for personalized student support plans, and scalable tools for adaptive program design. This work addresses the urgent need for data-driven approaches in special education research, where interdisciplinary methodologies bridging education, psychology, and computational science remain underutilized. The requested computing resources are essential to handle the high-dimensional data and complex system dynamics inherent in modeling human-centered interventions at scale. Results will be disseminated to CTP practitioners and policymakers to inform evidence-based reforms, ultimately advancing equitable access to postsecondary education and meaningful employment for neurodiverse learners.
cip_definition: A comprehensive transition and postsecondary (CTP) program that provides students with intellectual disabilities with academic enrichment, socialization, independent living skills, self-advocacy skills, and integrated work experiences and career skills that lead to gainful employment.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in modeling complex behavioral datasets derived from large-scale experimental psychology studies. Traditional computational methods often struggle with the multidimensional nature of behavioral data—such as high-frequency reaction times, eye-tracking metrics, and dynamic neural correlates—limiting the granularity and scalability of analyses. The research problem centers on developing robust computational frameworks to analyze these datasets efficiently, enabling precise quantification of latent cognitive processes (e.g., decision-making, attentional allocation) under controlled experimental conditions. The proposed work combines hierarchical Bayesian modeling, reinforcement learning algorithms, and agent-based simulations to disentangle interactions between individual differences, task parameters, and behavioral outcomes. HPC resources are essential for parallelizing computationally intensive tasks, including parameter estimation across massive parameter spaces, Monte Carlo simulations of cognitive models, and real-time analysis of streaming data from multi-participant experiments. Expected outcomes include (1) validated models of behavior that integrate neurocognitive mechanisms with observable responses, (2) scalable tools for detecting nonlinear patterns in longitudinal behavioral data, and (3) open-source computational pipelines to facilitate reproducibility in experimental psychology. By overcoming hardware limitations that currently restrict model complexity and dataset sizes, this work will advance the field’s capacity to test mechanistic hypotheses about behavior at unprecedented resolution. The resulting methodologies will directly inform the design of future experiments, enhance statistical power in studies with rare populations or finely manipulated variables, and establish best practices for computational resource allocation in behavioral research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of behavior under experimental conditions and the analysis of controlled behavioral responses. Includes instruction in learning theory, research design and experimental methods, psychological measurement, statistical design and methods, analysis of cognitive and behavioral variables, and the conduct of specialized and large-scale studies.

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize the design and application of advanced insulation systems through computational modeling to address energy efficiency, safety, and material performance challenges in industrial and building environments. Insulation materials and configurations must balance thermal resistance, fire safety, acoustic dampening, and structural durability under dynamic operating conditions. However, current empirical methods for evaluating insulation performance are limited in capturing multi-physics interactions, long-term degradation effects, and emergent risks such as thermal bridging or combustion dynamics. This project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate multi-scale, multi-physical processes in insulation systems, including heat transfer, fluid dynamics, and material stress responses. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations will model atomic-scale interactions in novel insulation composites, while finite element analysis (FEA) will assess macroscopic thermal and mechanical behaviors across diverse geometries and environmental conditions. Machine learning models trained on simulation datasets will identify optimal material combinations and installation patterns, with validation against experimental data from partner industrial labs. The computational workflow will also integrate fire propagation models to evaluate flame-retardant material performance and asbestos substitute safety. By leveraging parallelized simulations across HPC clusters, the project aims to generate predictive tools for insulation system longevity and failure modes under extreme temperatures, moisture, and mechanical loads. Expected outcomes include a computational framework for virtual prototyping of insulation solutions, reducing reliance on physical testing, and data-driven guidelines for retrofitting aging systems. The results will directly inform curriculum updates in insulator training programs, particularly in safety protocols and material selection for complex installations. This work addresses critical gaps in sustainable infrastructure and industrial energy conservation, with potential applications in HVAC, power generation, and aerospace sectors.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply insulation materials to pipes, boilers, ducts, refrigeration systems, and related equipment to reduce the passage of heat, cold, sound, or fire. Includes instruction in insulation specifications, measuring and cutting insulating material, applying and securing insulation, installing vapor barriers, insulation system maintenance, asbestos removal and abatement, and safety training.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of large-scale artistic style evolution and material degradation in pre-modern panel paintings, with a focus on European works from the 13th to 16th centuries. A central challenge in art historical research lies in systematically analyzing subtle patterns of brushwork, pigment distribution, and craquelure networks across thousands of high-resolution multispectral images—datasets too vast and complex for conventional computational methods. Furthermore, modeling the long-term chemical interactions between layered materials (e.g., tempera, oil binders, varnishes) requires intensive simulation capabilities beyond current departmental infrastructure. The proposed computational approach integrates three components: (1) deep learning models trained on hyperspectral imaging data to detect micro-scale stylistic features and workshop attributions; (2) graph-based analysis of craquelure patterns to establish chronological relationships within artist groupings; and (3) molecular dynamics simulations of binder-pigment interactions under varying environmental conditions. By parallelizing these workflows across GPU-accelerated nodes, we aim to process >50TB of archival imaging data from six international collections while simulating century-scale degradation processes at nanosecond resolution. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible framework for computational style analysis, predictive models of material instability in mixed-media artworks, and new empirical evidence regarding collaborative practices in early Renaissance workshops. This interdisciplinary methodology bridges art historical connoisseurship with computational materials science, offering conservationists data-driven strategies for preventive care while enabling art historians to test longstanding theories about artistic influence and workshop production at unprecedented scale. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling memory-intensive image processing tasks and achieving viable simulation timescales for molecular interactions.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the historical development of art as social and intellectual phenomenon, the analysis of works of art, and art conservation. Includes instruction in the theory of art, art history research methods, connoisseurship, the preservation and conservation of works of art, and the study of specific periods, cultures, styles, and themes.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance aviation safety and operational efficiency through advanced computational modeling of flight dynamics, crew decision-making, and emergency scenario resolution. Commercial aviation faces persistent challenges in mitigating human factors errors, optimizing fuel-efficient flight paths under dynamic weather conditions, and improving response protocols for rare but critical system failures. Current training simulations and operational models often lack the resolution to capture complex, interacting variables that influence real-world flight outcomes. To address this gap, we propose developing high-fidelity simulations of multi-crew flight operations using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The computational framework will integrate three core components: 1) computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models of aircraft performance under extreme atmospheric conditions, 2) machine learning algorithms trained on flight recorder data to predict stress-induced decision-making patterns, and 3) agent-based modeling of crew communication protocols during cascading system failures. These models will be validated against FAA incident reports and real-time flight data from partner airlines. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing terabyte-scale datasets from flight sensors, running parallelized Monte Carlo simulations of emergency scenarios, and achieving the millisecond-level temporal resolution required for realistic crew interaction modeling. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for identifying high-risk operational patterns, optimized checklist redesigns for abnormal situations, and evidence-based recommendations for simulator training enhancements. The results will directly inform curriculum updates in crew resource management courses while providing aviation regulators with quantitative frameworks for evaluating procedural changes. By leveraging large-scale computational resources, this project aims to bridge critical gaps between theoretical flight training and the complex realities of modern commercial aviation operations.
cip_title: Airline/ Commercial/ Professional Pilot and Flight Crew
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the flying and/or navigation of commercial passenger and cargo, agricultural, public service, corporate and rescue fixed wing aircraft. Includes instruction in principles of aircraft design and performance, aircraft flight systems and controls, flight crew operations and procedures, radio communications, navigation procedures and systems, airways safety and traffic regulations, and governmental rules and regulations pertaining to piloting aircraft. Programs may qualify individuals to sit for the FAA commercial and airline aircrew examinations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the emergent dynamics of host-microbe-environment interactions in chronic inflammatory diseases, an area requiring integrative analysis of multi-scale biological systems. Chronic inflammatory conditions such as inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) involve complex feedback loops between host immune pathways, microbiome metabolic activity, and environmental triggers. Traditional reductionist approaches struggle to capture these interactions, which span molecular, cellular, organismal, and ecological scales. We propose developing a multi-layered computational model integrating longitudinal clinical datasets, host transcriptomic profiles, spatially resolved microbiome sequencing data, and environmental exposure metadata. The model will employ agent-based simulations to represent immune cell populations, microbial communities, and epithelial tissue dynamics, coupled with differential equation frameworks to model nutrient gradients and inflammatory signaling. HPC resources are essential for parameter optimization across heterogeneous datasets (using parallelized Monte Carlo methods) and for simulating system-scale interactions at biologically relevant resolutions. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of critical thresholds in microbiome diversity that predict mucosal healing versus disease progression, (2) spatial mapping of host-microbe metabolic cross-talk hotspots in inflamed tissues, and (3) predictive frameworks for personalized dietary or probiotic interventions. This work bridges immunology, microbial ecology, and systems biology while avoiding molecular-level reductionism, aligning with the interdisciplinary mandate of integrative biosciences. The computational pipelines developed will be shared as open-source tools for analyzing other complex biological systems where cross-scale interactions drive phenotypic outcomes. By elucidating principles of stability and resilience in host-microbe networks, this research aims to advance translational strategies for chronic inflammatory diseases.
cip_title: Integrative/ Interdisciplinary Biology, Biosciences, and Biomedical Sciences
cip_definition: A program that crosses multiple specializations within the biological and biomedical sciences. Includes instruction in general biological research and variety of specializations.

abstract: Community organizations play a critical role in addressing systemic inequities and improving social outcomes, yet they often lack access to advanced tools for modeling complex community dynamics or optimizing resource distribution. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop a computational framework for simulating community-level social systems and evaluating the efficacy of advocacy strategies. The research problem centers on the challenge of predicting how interventions—such as public health campaigns, housing programs, or workforce development initiatives—interact with socioeconomic variables, spatial inequities, and institutional policies at scale. Traditional qualitative or small-scale quantitative approaches struggle to account for nonlinear feedback loops, heterogeneous population needs, and long-term systemic effects. To overcome these limitations, the project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate individual and organizational decision-making within dynamic community contexts, integrated with geospatial analysis of public datasets (e.g., census records, service utilization metrics). Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify patterns in historical program outcomes and predict intervention impacts under varying resource allocation scenarios. HPC resources are essential to process large-scale demographic datasets, run thousands of parallel simulations to test policy alternatives, and optimize stochastic models for accuracy. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for evaluating the equity and efficiency of service delivery models, which will be disseminated to community partners via an open-access platform. The project aims to advance computational social science methodologies within public administration while providing actionable insights for organizations working to reduce disparities in underserved populations. By enabling data-driven advocacy strategies, this work has the potential to strengthen community resilience and inform policy decisions at local and regional levels.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theories, principles, and practice of organizing and providing services to communities. May prepare individuals to apply such knowledge and skills in community service positions.

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize dynamic pricing and resource allocation models for decentralized hospitality ecosystems, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address the computational complexity of multi-agent systems in shared-economy environments. Traditional revenue management frameworks struggle to accommodate the real-time interdependencies between heterogeneous stakeholders—including short-term rental hosts, co-working spaces, and experience providers—who operate within overlapping geographic and temporal service windows. The project will develop a graph-based reinforcement learning (RL) framework to model competitive and cooperative behaviors across these agents, integrating stochastic demand forecasts, hyperlocal event data, and cross-platform pricing signals. HPC resources will enable parallelized training of RL agents across thousands of simulated market scenarios, incorporating GPU-accelerated graph neural networks to capture spatial-temporal dependencies at urban district scales. Key challenges include mitigating partial observability in distributed decision-making and balancing individual profit motives with collective system efficiency. The computational workflow will utilize containerized microservices for scalable parameter tuning, with validation against real-world data from three metropolitan testbed regions. Expected outcomes include a novel decision support system that improves regional occupancy rates by 8-12% while reducing price volatility for consumers, demonstrating how decentralized hospitality networks can achieve system-wide Nash equilibria without centralized coordination. This work bridges algorithmic game theory, urban informatics, and service operations, offering computational tools for emerging hospitality models that transcend traditional organizational boundaries.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in hospitality service management, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale study on the dynamics of structural inequalities in urban communities, with a focus on evaluating policy interventions designed to improve social equity. Applied sociology research often confronts challenges in modeling complex, multi-level social systems due to limitations in traditional computational tools, which struggle to integrate heterogeneous data sources—such as census records, longitudinal surveys, and real-time digital trace data—while accounting for temporal and spatial dependencies. This project addresses these gaps by developing agent-based models (ABMs) and machine learning pipelines to simulate community-level interactions, policy impacts, and emergent inequalities across diverse demographic groups. The ABM framework will simulate decision-making processes among individuals, organizations, and institutions, incorporating granular data on housing, employment, education, and public service access. Concurrently, natural language processing (NLP) methods will analyze unstructured text from public meetings, social media, and policy documents to identify barriers to equitable resource allocation. HPC resources are critical for scaling these computationally intensive simulations to reflect realistic population sizes (1M+ agents) and for training deep learning models on multi-terabyte datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) identifying key leverage points for reducing disparities in community resource access, (2) generating evidence-based recommendations for participatory action research initiatives, and (3) producing open-source tools to enhance reproducibility in computational sociology. By integrating sociological theory with advanced computational methods, this work aims to provide actionable insights for policymakers and advance methodological innovation in public sociology, particularly in evaluating the long-term efficacy of equity-focused interventions.
detailed_field: Sociology, demography, and population studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of sociological theory, methods, skills, and research to resolve particular issues in real-world settings. Includes instruction in data collection, group and organizational dynamics, participatory action research, program evaluation, sociological research methods, and sociological theory.

abstract: Dispute resolution processes are inherently complex, influenced by dynamic human behaviors, contextual variables, and evolving legal or cultural norms. Traditional qualitative methods, while valuable, often struggle to systematically analyze large-scale dispute datasets or model the nonlinear interactions that shape outcomes. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing computational frameworks to analyze historical dispute cases, simulate negotiation scenarios, and identify patterns that optimize resolution strategies. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multimodal datasets—including legal texts, demographic records, and behavioral transcripts—and to run agent-based models (ABMs) simulating multi-party negotiations under diverse conditions. Machine learning techniques, such as natural language processing (NLP) and clustering algorithms, will be applied to categorize dispute types, predict outcomes based on contextual factors, and quantify the efficacy of different mediation approaches. Parallel computing will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to test hypotheses about how variables like power imbalances, cultural communication styles, or institutional constraints affect resolution trajectories. Expected outcomes include predictive models to assist practitioners in tailoring strategies to specific dispute contexts, data-driven insights into systemic biases in arbitration outcomes, and a publicly accessible repository of annotated dispute case simulations. By integrating computational social science with dispute resolution theory, this project aims to advance evidence-based practices in mediation and arbitration while establishing scalable methodologies for interdisciplinary research at the intersection of law, behavioral science, and data science. The requested HPC resources are critical to handling the computational intensity of ABMs, NLP pipelines, and high-dimensional dataset analyses, which exceed the capacity of standard institutional computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that provides individuals with skills in negotiation, mediation, and arbitration, that can be applied to resolve disputes in a variety of settings, including business, legal, domestic, and labor relations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and validate computational models to optimize pedagogical strategies for training secondary psychology educators, addressing the gap in evidence-based approaches for integrating data-driven instructional tools into teacher education programs. While psychology education increasingly emphasizes quantitative reasoning and digital literacy, existing teacher preparation frameworks often lack systematic methods to evaluate how emerging computational techniques—such as simulation-based learning or real-time classroom analytics—can enhance pedagogical content knowledge. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-modal datasets from simulated teaching environments, including structured lesson plans, dynamic student response patterns, and instructor feedback from three partner teacher training institutions. Agent-based modeling will simulate classroom interactions under diverse instructional scenarios, while natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will assess the alignment between taught psychological concepts and learners’ conceptual understanding. Machine learning models will identify predictive relationships between specific pedagogical interventions (e.g., case-based learning modules, adaptive assessment tools) and pre-service teachers’ competency development. The computational workload necessitates parallel processing for large-scale parameter optimization across educational variables and Monte Carlo simulations to account for variability in learner populations. Anticipated outcomes include a validated framework for embedding computational thinking into psychology teacher curricula, evidence-based guidelines for data-informed instructional design, and open-source tools to help educators visualize the longitudinal impacts of pedagogical choices. By establishing scalable methods to evaluate teaching effectiveness in psychology education, this work aims to directly improve secondary students’ critical engagement with psychological science while advancing computational applications in subject-specific teacher preparation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach general psychology at the secondary school level.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address the growing challenge of optimizing personalized fitness regimens by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex interactions between biomechanical, physiological, and behavioral variables in real-world training environments. While advances in wearable technology and exercise science have generated vast datasets on individual performance metrics, current analytical tools lack the computational power to integrate multimodal data—such as motion capture, metabolic rates, muscle activation patterns, and psychological feedback—into dynamic, adaptive training models. This project will develop a computational framework to simulate individualized exercise adaptations, employing machine learning algorithms to predict optimal training loads, recovery intervals, and injury risk thresholds. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of high-resolution biomechanical datasets from 3D motion analysis systems, coupled with physiological data streams from wearable sensors, to create probabilistic models of training efficacy. A novel aspect involves agent-based modeling of client adherence factors, incorporating behavioral psychology principles to simulate long-term engagement patterns under varying program designs. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for fitness professionals to generate evidence-based, personalized programs that balance performance gains with injury prevention. By bridging computational modeling with practical fitness programming, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven decision-making in non-clinical physical fitness settings, with potential applications in preventive health strategies and adaptive training technologies. The computational demands of real-time multisensor integration and large-scale parameter optimization necessitate HPC resources to achieve the required latency and precision for actionable insights.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for employment in health and fitness clubs, wellness centers, public and private recreation facilities, hospitals and corporate fitness programs where they will perform a variety of instructional and administrative duties. Includes instruction in human anatomy and physiology, fitness techniques, exercise science, personal training, nutrition, and customer service.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between geopolitical risk fluctuations and global supply chain resilience using high-performance computing (HPC) to model multi-agent trade networks under stochastic disruption scenarios. While traditional international business research often focuses on macroeconomic policy or firm-level strategy, this study addresses an emerging niche: computational simulation of geopolitical "shocks" (e.g., sanctions, regional conflicts, trade embargoes) and their cascading impacts on transnational production networks. The core problem lies in the inability of conventional linear econometric models to capture the nonlinear, adaptive behaviors of multinational enterprises (MNEs) and suppliers when facing compound uncertainties. The project will develop a GPU-accelerated agent-based model simulating 50,000+ node trade networks across 190 countries, incorporating real-world data on export controls, shipping routes, and corporate diversification patterns. Computational methods will integrate game-theoretic decision algorithms for MNEs, Monte Carlo simulations for risk propagation, and natural language processing (NLP) to extract geopolitical event triggers from multilingual news corpora. By leveraging HPC resources, the model will achieve unprecedented granularity in representing temporal (sub-daily) and spatial (port-level) resolution across decadal time horizons. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework to quantify second-order supply chain vulnerabilities, identify critical chokepoints in strategic industries (e.g., semiconductors, rare earth minerals), and test adaptive strategies under hybrid warfare conditions. The computational toolkit will enable policymakers and businesses to stress-test trade diversification plans while advancing methodological integration of complexity science and international business theory.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage international businesses and/or business operations. Includes instruction in the principles and processes of export sales, trade controls, foreign operations and related problems, monetary issues, international business policy, and applications to doing business in specific countries and markets.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the emergence and persistence of collective social behaviors through large-scale agent-based modeling (ABM). A core challenge in social psychology lies in bridging micro-level cognitive processes (e.g., social learning, attitude formation) with macro-level group dynamics (e.g., polarization, norm enforcement). Traditional experimental methods struggle to capture nonlinear interactions in heterogeneous populations over extended timescales, while analytical models often oversimplify human behavior. We propose a computational framework simulating 100,000+ autonomous agents with empirically validated decision rules derived from social cognition theories (e.g., dual-process models, attribution biases). Agents will interact in dynamically evolving networks reflecting real-world social ecologies, with parameters systematically varied to test competing hypotheses about mechanisms driving phenomena such as rumor propagation in crisis scenarios or the stability of cooperative norms under shifting group membership. The computational intensity arises from (1) parallelized Monte Carlo sampling to explore high-dimensional parameter spaces, (2) evolutionary algorithms optimizing agent strategies over generational timescales, and (3) network analysis pipelines quantifying emergent clustering and influence hierarchies. Expected outcomes include identifying critical thresholds in social system resilience, validating computational signatures of latent cognitive states against existing behavioral datasets, and generating testable predictions for field experiments on collective decision-making. By integrating psychological realism with computational scalability, this work aims to advance theoretical models of social complexity while providing open-source simulation tools for the broader research community. The requested resources will enable simulations at unprecedented granularity, with individual runs requiring weeks of equivalent single-core computation to track agent states at sub-daily resolution across year-long timelines.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of individual behavior in group contexts, group behavior, and associated phenomena. Includes instruction in social learning theory, group theory and dynamics, sex roles, social cognition and inference, attribution theory, attitude formation, criminal behavior and other social pathologies, altruistic behavior, social development, and social ecology.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in the automated analysis of complex tissue microenvironments by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to develop advanced computational models for histologic data. Histologic technicians routinely generate high-resolution tissue sections, yet current workflows rely heavily on manual or semi-automated morphometric assessments, which are time-consuming, prone to inter-observer variability, and ill-suited for analyzing multidimensional interactions between cellular and extracellular components. The research problem centers on creating scalable, AI-driven tools to decode spatial, structural, and textural patterns in gigapixel whole-slide images (WSIs) and 3D histologic reconstructions, enabling precise quantification of features such as extracellular matrix remodeling, rare cell populations, and microvascular networks. The computational approach integrates convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with graph-based algorithms to model tissue architecture, trained on a curated dataset of annotated WSIs spanning diverse pathologies. HPC resources will facilitate parallel processing of terabyte-scale image datasets, hyperparameter optimization of deep learning architectures, and simulation of 3D tissue reconstructions from serial sections. Additionally, the project will develop open-source tools to automate quality control steps in histology workflows, including artifact detection and staining consistency metrics. Expected outcomes include validated models for detecting subvisual prognostic biomarkers in fibrotic and neoplastic tissues, a computational pipeline for correlating 3D histologic features with clinical outcomes, and a publicly accessible repository of annotated datasets. By bridging computational science and histologic practice, this work aims to transform tissue analysis into a quantitative, systems-level discipline, directly enhancing diagnostic precision and supporting translational research in understudied diseases. The requested HPC allocation is essential for handling memory-intensive image processing tasks and accelerating model training cycles beyond the capacity of local institutional resources.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of histotechnologists and other clinical laboratory scientists, to prepare and process tissue samples and perform routine histologic procedures and tests. Includes instruction in fixation, dehydration, embedding, sectioning, decalcification, microincineration, mounting, routine and special steaming, laboratory mathematics, laboratory procedures and safety, instrumentation and microscopy, computer applications, preparation of museum specimens, and recording and administrative procedures.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize tax compliance strategies for multinational enterprises (MNEs) operating in dynamically evolving regulatory environments. The computational challenge arises from the complexity of modern tax systems, where overlapping jurisdictions, transient bilateral agreements, and real-time economic data create a high-dimensional optimization problem. Traditional analytical methods fail to account for stochastic variables—such as fluctuating exchange rates, sudden policy shifts, or supply chain disruptions—that significantly impact tax liabilities. To address this gap, we propose developing an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework integrated with reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms to simulate MNE decision-making under uncertainty. The ABM will represent MNEs, tax authorities, and regulatory bodies as autonomous agents interacting within a multi-jurisdictional environment, while RL will train adaptive strategies for tax-efficient resource allocation. HPC resources are critical to manage the combinatorial explosion of scenarios, particularly when modeling cascading effects of tax policy changes across global networks spanning 100+ jurisdictions. Computational workflows will parallelize Monte Carlo simulations to assess probabilistic outcomes of tax planning strategies, incorporating real-world datasets on cross-border transactions, treaty networks, and historical audit outcomes. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool capable of identifying robust tax strategies that minimize compliance risks while adhering to evolving OECD guidelines and local regulations. This work aims to advance computational taxation as an interdisciplinary field, bridging operations research, behavioral economics, and legal informatics. By quantifying the systemic impacts of tax optimization, the project will provide policymakers with evidence-based insights into unintended consequences of regulatory frameworks, while helping businesses navigate volatile fiscal landscapes efficiently.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide tax advice and management services to individuals and corporations. Includes instruction in tax law and regulations, tax record systems, individual and corporate income taxation, tax planning, partnerships and fiduciary relationships, estates and trusts, property depreciation, capital gains and losses, dispositions, transfers, liquidity, valuation, and applications to specific tax problems.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the growing demand for computationally intensive typographic design processes in digital media production. Current software tools for dynamic text composition—particularly for high-resolution, multi-platform publishing—struggle to efficiently render complex layouts integrating variable fonts, adaptive kerning, and real-time accessibility adjustments (e.g., dyslexia-friendly formatting). The project proposes developing a GPU-accelerated framework for optimizing automated typographic workflows, leveraging high-performance computing resources to overcome latency and scalability barriers in existing composition systems. Using parallelized layout engines and machine learning models trained on typographic design patterns, we aim to simulate and evaluate text composition scenarios at production-scale resolutions (8K+), accounting for diverse output devices and user interaction parameters. Methods will include benchmarking existing CPU-bound composition pipelines, prototyping OpenCL-optimized rendering modules, and training transformer-based models on a corpus of 50,000 professionally designed publication layouts to predict context-aware formatting adjustments. The computational workload requires access to GPU clusters capable of processing terabyte-scale font datasets and simultaneous rendering tasks across multiple virtualized design environments. Expected outcomes include a quantifiable reduction in layout computation times for complex documents (targeting 60-75% improvement over industry-standard tools), as well as novel metrics for evaluating typographic accessibility in dynamic content. Results will directly benefit digital publishing workflows and open-source design tools, while advancing pedagogical resources for next-generation typography operators working with AI-assisted composition systems. This work bridges critical gaps between traditional graphic design principles and modern computational demands, ensuring robust typographic practices can scale alongside emerging immersive media formats.
cip_title: Computer Typography and Composition Equipment Operator
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to design and execute page formats, layouts and text composition, and to make typographical selections using computer graphics and other computer-assisted design programs.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing complex organizational decision-making processes under uncertainty, a critical issue in business administration and management. Traditional analytical models often fail to capture the dynamic interactions of market variables, resource constraints, and human behavioral factors, limiting their utility for strategic planning. To overcome these limitations, the research proposes the development of a high-fidelity computational framework leveraging agent-based modeling (ABM) and large-scale Monte Carlo simulations. These methods will integrate heterogeneous data sources—including historical financial performance, real-time market feeds, and employee behavior datasets—to model scenarios such as supply chain disruptions, workforce allocation shifts, and competitive market entry strategies. The computational intensity of simulating thousands of interdependent agents and stochastic variables necessitates access to high-performance computing (HPC) resources, particularly for parallelized scenario testing and sensitivity analyses. Key deliverables include a scalable decision-support tool capable of identifying robust strategies under varying risk thresholds and a comparative analysis of optimization algorithms (e.g., genetic algorithms vs. deep reinforcement learning) for managerial decision contexts. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into adaptive resource allocation frameworks and a methodological contribution to computational management science. By enabling rapid, data-driven exploration of high-dimensional problem spaces, this work aims to advance evidence-based management practices while reducing reliance on heuristic approaches. The requested HPC resources are essential to handle memory-intensive simulations and iterative model refinement, which would otherwise be infeasible on standard computing infrastructure. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits for the academic community and case studies demonstrating applications in operations management and strategic planning.
cip_title: Business Administration, Management and Operations, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in business and administration, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance the efficiency and scalability of legal document analysis through advanced natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques, tailored to the specialized needs of paralegal workflows. Legal professionals routinely manage vast, unstructured corpora of case law, contracts, and regulatory texts, where manual review remains time-intensive and error-prone. While existing tools offer basic keyword search capabilities, they lack the capacity to infer contextual relationships, predict case outcomes, or identify subtle precedents across jurisdictions. This research addresses these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train domain-specific large language models (LLMs) on multi-terabyte legal datasets, including court opinions, legislative histories, and anonymized case files. The computational approach integrates transformer-based architectures optimized for legal semantics, graph neural networks to map citation networks, and ensemble methods to classify document relevance and procedural risks. By parallelizing model training across GPU clusters, the project aims to reduce inference latency for real-time applications, such as automated brief drafting or compliance auditing. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for semantic legal search, anomaly detection in contractual clauses, and predictive analytics for case strategy development. These resources will be validated against manually annotated benchmarks by practicing paralegals, with performance metrics emphasizing precision, scalability, and interpretability. The project’s significance lies in bridging computational innovation with legal practice, offering a replicable framework for integrating HPC into non-STEM disciplines while adhering to ethical standards for data confidentiality and algorithmic transparency. Results will advance the emerging field of computational legal studies and empower paralegal teams to manage complex litigation and transactional workloads with greater accuracy and reduced operational costs.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform research, drafting, investigatory, record-keeping and related administrative functions under the supervision of an attorney or court. Includes instruction in legal research, drafting legal documents, appraising, pleading, courthouse procedures, and legal specializations.

abstract: The controlled use of explosives in construction and demolition requires precise optimization of blast parameters to balance efficacy, safety, and environmental impact. Current empirical models and simplified simulations often fail to capture the complex, dynamic interactions between explosive charges, geologic substrates, and structural materials, leading to suboptimal outcomes such as overbreak, flyrock, or incomplete fragmentation. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing high-fidelity computational models to simulate blasting processes under diverse real-world conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will employ multi-physics simulations integrating finite element analysis (FEA), smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH), and machine learning (ML) to model shockwave propagation, fracture mechanics, and debris dispersion at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions. Key variables—including charge geometry, detonation timing, rock mass properties, and confinement effects—will be systematically analyzed to identify optimal blast configurations. The computational framework will be validated against field data from controlled demolition and quarrying case studies, with iterative refinement to improve predictive accuracy. By enabling granular parameter optimization, this research aims to reduce material waste, enhance safety protocols, and minimize environmental disruption in blasting operations. The resulting models will also support the development of open-access training tools for blasting technicians, addressing a critical gap in practical, simulation-driven education. Successful implementation of this project will advance the integration of computational science into explosive engineering, fostering innovation in a field traditionally reliant on heuristic methods. Access to HPC resources is essential to manage the extreme computational demands of 3D transient dynamics simulations and large-scale parameter space exploration, which are infeasible with conventional computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in using a variety of explosive materials to aid in the construction process. Includes instruction in safety procedures for storing, handling, placement, charge power determination, drilling, pounding, building demolition, preparing rocky surfaces for building foundations and demolition of explosives.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a multidisciplinary investigation into the spatial and temporal dynamics of historical cultural exchange through large-scale analysis of digitized archival materials. The research problem centers on the fragmented and heterogeneous nature of global historical records, which have been digitized in varying formats and languages, complicating efforts to trace cross-regional influences in art, literature, and social practices from the 15th to 19th centuries. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to synthesize these datasets at scale, leaving gaps in understanding how cultural ideas propagated across geographies and time periods. To address this, the project will employ computational methods including natural language processing (NLP) for multilingual text analysis, neural network-based image recognition to classify artistic motifs in digitized artworks, and geospatial network modeling to map the diffusion of cultural practices. HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based language models on multilingual corpora (spanning English, Spanish, Arabic, and Mandarin sources), processing high-resolution image datasets (>50,000 items), and simulating large-scale network interactions across historical trade routes. Expected outcomes include (1) the development of open-source tools for integrating heterogeneous humanities datasets, (2) dynamic visualizations of cultural exchange patterns accessible via a public-facing web portal, and (3) new interdisciplinary frameworks for analyzing transnational historical narratives. The computational workflows will be designed for reproducibility, with containerized pipelines to support future research in digital archives and cultural analytics. By enabling the synthesis of previously siloed datasets, this work aims to reshape scholarly and public understanding of premodern globalization while demonstrating scalable methodologies for humanities-driven HPC applications.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the use of new technologies, advanced computing, and public engagement to investigate and analyze questions in the humanities. Includes instruction in anthropology, art, data mining and machine learning, design, digital archives, geospatial technologies, history, human-computer interface design, literature, markup languages, social media technologies, and software development.

abstract: This project investigates the dynamic interplay between multilingual digital communication patterns and emergent language practices in understudied online communities, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze large-scale, multimodal interaction data. While prior sociolinguistic research has focused on established platforms like Twitter or Facebook, less attention has been paid to niche platforms (e.g., gaming forums, decentralized social networks) where rapid code-switching, hybrid lexical innovations, and non-standard orthographic conventions challenge traditional models of language contact. The research addresses two gaps: (1) insufficient computational tools to track real-time language convergence in distributed, ephemeral digital spaces, and (2) limited empirical data on how platform-specific affordances shape dialectal evolution in marginalized linguistic communities. Using a mixed-methods framework, we will apply transformer-based NLP models fine-tuned for low-resource languages and dialectal variants to process 10+ terabytes of timestamped user-generated text, audio, and visual-gestural metadata from three case study platforms. Graph neural networks will map cross-linguistic influence networks, while agent-based simulations, calibrated with empirical data, will test hypotheses about innovation diffusion under varying platform architectures. HPC resources are critical for training domain-specific embeddings across 15+ languages, parallelizing large-language-model inference, and running iterative simulations at scale.
