Expected outcomes include (1) a novel computational framework for modeling multi-layered language contact in digital ecosystems, (2) evidence-based principles for designing inclusive language technologies that accommodate emergent hybrid practices, and (3) public datasets documenting under-resourced digital vernaculars. This work advances applied linguistics by bridging micro-level interaction analysis with macro-scale language change dynamics, offering methodological innovations for studying globalization’s impact on 21st-century multilingualism. Results will directly inform language policy for digital civic spaces and adaptive pedagogical tools for translingual competencies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on language-related concerns in the everyday world, including language education, acquisition of first and additional languages, discourse analysis, language assessment, literacy, and language policy and planning. Includes instruction in linguistic theory; language teaching and learning; discourse analysis; language and cognition; and language, culture, and identity.

abstract: The apparel and textile manufacturing industry faces critical challenges in balancing sustainability, efficiency, and consumer demands amid global supply chain complexities. Traditional methods of design iteration, material optimization, and production planning remain resource-intensive, often relying on trial-and-error processes that generate excessive waste and energy consumption. This project seeks to address these challenges through the development of a computational framework integrating generative design algorithms, discrete-event simulation, and machine learning to optimize textile product lifecycles. The research will focus on creating high-fidelity models that simulate material behavior under dynamic environmental and mechanical stresses, predict consumer trend adoption, and automate resource allocation across distributed manufacturing systems. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large datasets spanning historical production metrics, real-time sensor inputs from manufacturing equipment, and multi-modal consumer preference data. Computational methods will include physics-informed neural networks for predicting textile durability, graph-based optimization for minimizing cutting waste in pattern generation, and agent-based modeling to evaluate decentralized production scenarios. Expected outcomes include a scalable digital twin platform capable of reducing material waste by 15–20% in prototyping phases, accelerating design-to-production timelines by 30%, and dynamically aligning production schedules with carbon footprint targets. By bridging gaps between computational engineering, sustainable design, and industrial systems, this work aims to establish a novel paradigm for agile, data-driven textile manufacturing. The resulting tools will provide open-source modules for small-to-medium enterprises, democratizing access to advanced computational resources in an industry historically reliant on manual expertise. This project underscores the transformative potential of HPC in non-traditional STEM domains, offering a template for interdisciplinary innovation in emergent technological niches.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, development, and production of textile products and related processes and systems. Includes instruction in functional and aesthetic design, human factors research, production planning, manufacturing processes, quality assessment, and distribution systems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a digital humanities study of cultural narratives in Polish diaspora communities through large-scale textual and visual analysis. The research problem centers on identifying patterns of collective memory, identity formation, and cultural adaptation within Polish émigré publications (1945–1990), including periodicals, memoirs, and community archives, which remain understudied due to their fragmented, multilingual nature and the technical challenges of processing non-Latin scripts at scale. The computational approach integrates optical character recognition (OCR) fine-tuned for mid-20th-century Polish typography, transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) models for semantic analysis of Polish, English, and German texts, and graph-based network analysis to map transnational connections between diaspora nodes. Key technical challenges include managing OCR errors across degraded print sources, cross-lingual sentiment analysis to trace evolving attitudes toward post-war Poland, and processing high-resolution scanned materials (estimated 15 TB uncompressed). The project will employ distributed computing to parallelize text extraction pipelines, GPU-accelerated fine-tuning of multilingual BERT variants, and spatial-temporal visualization of diaspora networks using community detection algorithms. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible corpus of processed texts, an interactive map visualizing cultural exchange hubs, and quantitative insights into how gender roles and regional identities were renegotiated in diaspora contexts. This work will provide the first computationally derived framework for understanding Polish émigré cultural production as a dynamic system, offering methodological innovations for Slavic digital humanities while preserving vulnerable archival materials. The requested HPC resources are critical due to the scale of data, need for rapid iteration on custom OCR/NLP workflows, and memory-intensive network analysis across temporal slices.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of Poland and the current and historical inhabitants of the Polish lands, including borderlands, from earliest times to the present.

abstract: The integration of high-performance computing (HPC) resources into radiologic physics research is critical to address complex challenges in radiation therapy treatment planning. Current clinical methods for optimizing radiation dose delivery often rely on simplified models that inadequately account for dynamic patient-specific variables, such as tissue heterogeneity, organ motion, and real-time anatomical changes. These limitations can lead to suboptimal therapeutic outcomes, including underdosing of tumors or overdosing of adjacent healthy tissues. This project proposes to develop a computational framework leveraging Monte Carlo simulations and machine learning (ML) to model radiation transport with unprecedented spatial and temporal resolution. The framework will incorporate patient-specific data from CT/MRI imaging, radiobiological parameters, and real-time tracking of anatomical motion to predict dose distributions in dynamic, heterogeneous tissues. HPC resources are essential to execute these simulations at scale, as each patient case requires ~10^6 particle histories per beam angle, with iterative optimization across thousands of potential beam configurations. Parallelized GPU-accelerated computing will enable rapid convergence of ML models trained on multi-institutional datasets to predict optimal beam angles and weighting. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated, open-source simulation toolkit for adaptive radiotherapy planning, (2) quantitative evidence of reduced dose variability (±2% accuracy) compared to current clinical standards, and (3) predictive models for long-term toxicity risks based on 4D dose accumulation maps. By enabling real-time adaptation to anatomical changes during treatment, this work aims to improve tumor control rates while minimizing radiation-induced complications, directly advancing precision medicine in oncology. The computational infrastructure developed will also serve as a foundational resource for future studies in radiologic physics, including applications in FLASH radiotherapy and combined modality therapy optimization.
cip_definition: Research focused on that branch of physics which includes the physical aspects of radiation therapy, radiologic diagnosis, and/or nuclear medicine. Radiologic physicists must specialize in at least one of the three subspecialty areas: therapeutic radiological physics, diagnostic radiological physics, and/or medical nuclear physics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of predictive models for roofing material performance under dynamic environmental conditions. Current roofing systems face challenges in balancing durability, energy efficiency, and cost-effectiveness, particularly as climate variability intensifies. Traditional experimental methods to evaluate material degradation, thermal dynamics, and structural resilience are time-intensive and limited in scope. This research addresses these gaps by creating computational frameworks to simulate multi-physics interactions affecting roofing systems, including moisture penetration, thermal expansion, wind shear forces, and long-term UV exposure. Using finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD), we will model stress distributions, heat transfer, and fluid-structure interactions across diverse roofing geometries and material composites. Machine learning algorithms will be integrated to optimize material selection and installation patterns based on regional climate data. The HPC environment is critical for scaling these simulations to real-world complexity, enabling parametric studies across thousands of material configurations and environmental scenarios. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin framework for roofing systems, predictive metrics for material lifespan under extreme weather, and data-driven guidelines for region-specific roofing designs. These results will directly inform curriculum updates in the Roofer program, ensuring alignment with emerging industry standards for sustainable construction. By reducing reliance on physical prototyping, the project also aims to lower costs and accelerate innovation in roofing material development. The computational workflows and datasets generated will be made accessible to vocational training institutions, fostering broader adoption of simulation-driven design in trade professions. This work underscores the transformative potential of HPC in bridging technical education with cutting-edge computational research to address real-world infrastructure challenges.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to prepare, install, and maintain exterior roofing materials and roofs. Includes instruction in building materials, flashing, lag bolts, site safety, equipment operation and maintenance, layering, site preparation, basic internal structural design, finishing, waterproofing, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of keyboard performance practice through computational analysis of historical and contemporary playing techniques. A central challenge in keyboard pedagogy lies in systematically quantifying stylistic nuances—such as articulation, dynamic shading, and tempo modulation—across diverse repertoires and performers. Current manual analysis methods are time-intensive and lack scalability, limiting researchers’ ability to identify patterns in large corpora of performances or model the physiological mechanics of advanced techniques. To address this, we propose developing machine learning models trained on multimodal performance data (audio, MIDI, motion-capture) to automate the extraction of interpretative features and simulate biomechanical constraints during virtuosic passages. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of over 10,000 recorded performances from archival and contemporary sources, as well as finite element simulations of hand kinematics during complex figurations. Additionally, real-time rendering of acoustic environments (e.g., liturgical spaces for organ service playing) will be implemented using wave equation solvers to study how performers adapt technique to architectural acoustics. Outcomes will include an open-access database of annotated performance features, predictive models linking pedagogical strategies to technical outcomes, and interactive tools for educators to visualize stylistic trends. By bridging computational musicology and performance practice, this work aims to establish scalable frameworks for preserving interpretative traditions while informing the development of adaptive teaching methodologies. The requested resources are critical for handling the project’s data volume and computational intensity, which exceed the capacity of local workstations, particularly in training deep neural networks on high-dimensional performance data and running physics-based simulations at millisecond resolution.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to master the piano, organ, or related keyboard instruments and performing art as solo, ensemble, and/or accompanist performers. Includes instruction in piano and keyboard pedagogy, ensemble playing, accompanying, service playing, repertoire, keyboard and pedal skills, recital, and personal style development.

abstract: Agricultural production systems face increasing pressure to optimize yields, resource efficiency, and environmental resilience amid climate variability and growing food demand. This project seeks to develop a computational framework for simulating and predicting crop responses to dynamic agronomic management strategies under region-specific climate stressors. Current limitations in modeling high-resolution interactions between plant physiology, soil heterogeneity, and microclimate patterns hinder precision agriculture applications at scale. To address this gap, we propose coupling process-based crop growth models with machine learning algorithms to analyze multi-modal datasets, including hyperspectral imagery, soil sensor networks, and historical yield records. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parameterize and validate 3D root-soil-water models, run ensemble climate scenarios, and train neural networks for real-time decision support. Key computational challenges include parallelizing finite element simulations of water-nutrient transport in heterogeneous soil profiles and processing terabyte-scale remote sensing time series. Successful implementation will enable (1) identification of genotype-specific irrigation and fertilization schedules that minimize water use while maintaining productivity, and (2) predictive mapping of yield stability under drought-heatwave compound events. Outcomes will directly inform field trials conducted through our agricultural extension partnerships, targeting row crop systems in water-stressed regions. By integrating HPC capabilities with farm-scale data streams, this work advances computational agriculture methodologies while providing actionable insights for sustainable intensification. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale parameter optimization runs, and storage of synthetic datasets generated through in silico experimentation across 10+ crop varieties and 30-year climate horizons.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in agricultural production operations, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing fluid power systems for energy efficiency and reliability through advanced computational modeling of transient hydraulic phenomena. Fluid power systems, particularly in industrial and mobile applications, face dynamic operational stresses, multi-phase flow interactions, and complex fluid-structure coupling that are poorly captured by conventional steady-state models. Current design practices rely on empirical correlations and simplified simulations, leading to suboptimal component sizing, elevated energy losses, and unanticipated maintenance requirements. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-fidelity computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to resolve time-dependent turbulence, cavitation dynamics, and pressure wave propagation in large-scale hydraulic networks. The computational approach combines implicit large eddy simulation (LES) for turbulence modeling, volume-of-fluid (VOF) methods for multi-phase flows, and partitioned fluid-structure interaction (FSI) algorithms to capture bidirectional coupling between hydraulic fluids and system components. Simulations will target industrially relevant configurations, including variable displacement pump cavitation under load transients, pressure ripple attenuation in multi-branch manifolds, and accumulator-mediated energy recovery in hybrid hydraulic machinery. HPC resources are essential to achieve the required spatial-temporal resolution across million-element meshes with microsecond-scale timestepping over physical timescales exceeding operational cycles. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for transient system behavior, optimized damping strategies for pressure pulsations, and machine learning-derived surrogate models for real-time control applications. This work will directly advance the design of next-generation fluid power systems with reduced energy consumption (targeting 15-20% efficiency gains) and enhanced durability, while establishing an open-source simulation database to accelerate workforce training in advanced hydraulic technologies. Successful implementation requires sustained access to GPU-accelerated nodes for parallelized solver workloads and dedicated storage for petascale simulation datasets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing and using fluid power and transportation systems. Includes instruction in fluid mechanics and hydraulics principles, fluid power systems, pipeline and pumping systems, design and operational testing, inspection and maintenance procedures, related instrumentation, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design and management of urban green spaces through data-driven simulations of human-nature interactions. While parks and recreational facilities are critical for community well-being and ecological sustainability, existing planning tools often rely on static, demographic-based metrics, neglecting dynamic behavioral patterns and real-time environmental feedback. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) approach integrated with geospatial analytics and machine learning to simulate visitor behavior, resource utilization, and ecological impacts under varying design scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale datasets—including mobility traces, vegetation health metrics, and microclimate sensor data—and to run iterative simulations that account for heterogeneous user preferences, seasonal variations, and climate stressors. The model will parameterize site-specific constraints such as terrain topology, infrastructure capacity, and biodiversity corridors, enabling dynamic trade-off analyses between recreational accessibility, maintenance costs, and ecosystem services. By coupling reinforcement learning algorithms with multi-objective optimization, the framework will generate adaptive management strategies that balance human-centric outcomes (e.g., visitor satisfaction, equitable access) with environmental resilience metrics (e.g., soil erosion thresholds, pollinator habitat retention). Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool for municipal planners, validated against empirical data from three case study cities, and a public dashboard to visualize trade-offs in proposed park designs. This work bridges computational social science, landscape ecology, and urban informatics, advancing methodological innovation in leisure facilities management while addressing pressing challenges in equitable green space allocation amid urban densification and climate change.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_title: Parks, Recreation, and Leisure Facilities Management, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in parks, recreation, and leisure facilities management, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The proposed research seeks to elucidate the dynamic interplay between pathogenic microbial evasion mechanisms and host immune responses, with a focus on Staphylococcus aureus and its adaptation to innate immune defenses. A critical gap exists in understanding how spatial heterogeneity within infection microenvironments shapes bacterial survival and immune cell efficacy. Traditional in vitro models lack the resolution to capture multicellular interactions in real time, while in vivo systems introduce confounding variables. To address this, we will develop agent-based computational models simulating host-pathogen encounters at single-cell resolution, integrating empirical data from time-lapse microscopy, bacterial mutant libraries, and cytokine secretion profiles. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize stochastic simulations of neutrophil recruitment, bacterial quorum signaling, and phagosomal escape dynamics across biologically relevant timescales (0–48 hours). Each simulation will track >10^6 interacting agents (immune cells, bacteria, host tissue) with variable motility, adhesion, and metabolic states. Parallelized workflows will enable parameter sweeps to test hypotheses regarding the role of biofilm matrix composition in resisting reactive oxygen species and the threshold of T-cell activation required for adaptive immunity recruitment. Validation will employ murine infection models with immune cell depletion strains and bacterial transcriptional reporters. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework mapping microenvironmental variables (pH, oxygen tension, extracellular DNA concentration) to infection outcomes, identifying novel targets for immune-boosting therapies. This work will advance our mechanistic understanding of persistent Staphylococcal infections in immunocompromised hosts while establishing scalable computational methods for studying spatial immunology in other host-microbe systems. The requested HPC allocation will directly support iterative model optimization, large-scale sensitivity analyses, and public sharing of modular simulation code via containerized workflows.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the microorganisms that cause disease and the host immune response to them. Includes instruction in microbiology, microbial genetics, molecular virology, pathogenic bacteriology, disease mechanisms, immunology, immunogenetics, autoimmunity, and bioinformatics.

abstract: Climate change and anthropogenic landscape modifications are rapidly altering habitat suitability for aquatic and terrestrial species, necessitating advanced predictive models to inform adaptive management strategies. This project seeks to develop a spatially explicit, multi-species simulation framework to assess climate resilience and habitat connectivity across freshwater and coastal ecosystems in the Pacific Northwest. The research integrates high-resolution remote sensing data, species occurrence records, and hydrodynamic models to quantify how shifting temperature regimes, hydrologic patterns, and land-use changes affect critical life history stages for anadromous fish populations and their associated riparian predators. Computational challenges arise from the need to process petabyte-scale environmental datasets, implement individual-based movement models across heterogeneous landscapes, and run ensemble climate projections at 10m spatial resolution. We request allocation of high-performance computing resources to parallelize three core components: (1) machine learning classification of LiDAR and multispectral imagery to map microhabitat features, (2) hydrodynamic simulations of stream networks under variable snowpack and precipitation scenarios, and (3) Bayesian network analysis of species-environment interactions across temporal scales. The computational workflow will leverage GPU acceleration for convolutional neural networks and distributed memory processing for landscape genetic analyses. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of climate refugia, prioritized corridors for habitat restoration, and open-source tools for optimizing protected area networks under multiple climate futures. This work directly supports state and tribal wildlife agencies in implementing climate-adaptive management plans while advancing computational ecology methods for coupled human-natural systems. By quantifying threshold responses in critical ecosystems, the project aims to reduce uncertainty in conservation decision-making under rapid environmental change.
cip_title: Wildlife, Fish and Wildlands Science and Management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to conserve and manage wilderness areas and the flora, marine and aquatic life therein, and manage wildlife reservations and zoological/aquarium facilities for recreational, commercial, and ecological purposes. Includes instruction in wildlife biology, marine/aquatic biology, environmental science, freshwater and saltwater ecosystems, natural resources management and policy, outdoor recreation and parks management, the design and operation of natural and artificial wildlife habitats, applicable law and regulations, and related administrative and communications skills.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational linguistic research on Albanian language dialects and historical texts. Despite Albanian’s unique Indo-European lineage and rich dialectal diversity—particularly the divergence between Gheg and Tosk—digital tools for systematic analysis of its linguistic features remain underdeveloped. Current challenges include processing large-scale corpora of regional texts, modeling phonetic and morphosyntactic variations, and tracing diachronic shifts in usage, which require intensive computational workflows. The proposed research will employ natural language processing (NLP) methods to analyze digitized Albanian texts spanning the 19th century to the present, focusing on dialect classification, lexico-semantic evolution, and cross-dialectal phonemic modeling. Key computational tasks include training transformer-based models for low-resource language applications, parallelized corpus alignment, and phonetic transcription using recurrent neural networks. HPC resources are critical for managing memory-intensive tasks, such as processing terabytes of unstructured text data, optimizing hyperparameters for dialect-specific models, and running comparative simulations across linguistic variables. Expected outcomes include open-access datasets of annotated Albanian texts, a computational framework for dialectal feature extraction, and tools to automate phonetic transcription for regional variants. These resources will directly support philological research on Albanian/Illyrian language history, enhance pedagogical materials for language preservation, and provide methodological templates for under-resourced languages. By integrating computational linguistics with Albanian philology, this project aims to bridge gaps in digital humanities infrastructure while contributing new insights into the sociolinguistic dynamics of the Balkan region.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Albanian language. Includes instruction in Albanian/Illyrian philology; Ghegg and Tosk dialects; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale textual and computational analysis of early Christian theological debates and their philosophical underpinnings. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how doctrinal differences emerged among early Christian communities by systematically analyzing patterns in theological argumentation, scriptural interpretation, and rhetorical strategies across key texts from the first five centuries CE. The primary challenge lies in processing and correlating heterogeneous data—including Greek and Latin patristic writings, conciliar documents, and non-canonical texts—while accounting for linguistic nuance, historical context, and philosophical frameworks. Computational methods will integrate natural language processing (NLP) techniques, semantic network analysis, and phylogenetic modeling to trace doctrinal developments and ideological divergences. Custom algorithms will be developed to identify theological concepts across multilingual corpora, map argumentative structures, and model the diffusion of ideas in relation to geopolitical and cultural factors. HPC resources are essential for training transformer-based language models on niche historical texts, running large-scale simulations of doctrinal transmission, and performing Bayesian phylogenetic inferences on complex textual traditions. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible knowledge graph linking theological arguments to their philosophical antecedents, quantitative models of doctrinal evolution, and visualizations of ideological networks across early Christian communities. These results will provide new insights into the interplay between Christian thought and Hellenistic philosophy, clarify mechanisms of theological conflict and synthesis, and offer methodological frameworks for computational humanities in religious studies. The project bridges traditional theological scholarship with data-driven approaches, demonstrating how advanced computing can illuminate historical processes central to the formation of Christian intellectual traditions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the philosophy and teachings of Jesus Christ and his apostles, and the subsequent intellectual and cultural movements and institutions based on Christianity. Includes instruction in Christian sacred scripture, Christian literature and philosophy, and studies of one or more of the main branches of the faith and their cultural context including Orthodoxy, Roman Catholicism, Protestantism, Evangelicalism, and others.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of integrating dynamic, multi-sensory elements in contemporary theatrical productions through advanced computational modeling and simulation. Modern theatre design increasingly relies on the interplay of lighting, sound, material properties, and spatial configurations to create immersive environments, yet existing tools for predicting these interactions remain fragmented and computationally limited. We propose the development of a unified simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model real-time interactions between acoustic propagation, spectral lighting effects, and dynamic set geometries. The research problem centers on overcoming the latency and scale constraints of current software, which struggles to simulate high-fidelity, time-dependent scenarios—such as moving set pieces interacting with spatially adaptive soundscapes—without sacrificing resolution or interactivity. Computational methods will combine finite element analysis for acoustic wave propagation, ray-tracing algorithms for spectral light distribution, and agent-based modeling for audience perspective validation. These components will be parallelized to optimize resource allocation across HPC nodes, enabling iterative testing of design variables (e.g., material reflectivity, speaker array configurations, motorized rigging trajectories) within a virtual performance space. Expected outcomes include a scalable toolkit for predicting perceptual outcomes of design choices, reducing reliance on physical prototypes during pre-production. The project will further quantify how computational previsualization impacts collaborative workflows between designers, directors, and technical teams. By enabling rapid, data-driven optimization of multi-sensory design parameters, this work aims to advance the technical artistry of theatre while establishing a methodological bridge between performing arts practice and computational engineering. Results will be validated through case studies involving regional theatre partners, with open-source code modules disseminated to the academic theatre community.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_title: Technical Theatre/ Theatre Design and Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply artistic, technical and dramatic principles and techniques to the communication of dramatic information, ideas, moods, and feelings through technical theatre methods. Includes instruction in set design, lighting design, sound effects, theatre acoustics, scene painting, property management, costume design, and technical direction and production and use of computer applications to support these functions.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate genetic determinants of differential susceptibility to environmental toxicants, with a focus on molecular mechanisms underlying toxin-receptor interactions and xenobiotic metabolism. A critical challenge in molecular toxicology lies in predicting how genetic polymorphisms influence individual responses to pollutants, particularly in understudied populations. To address this, we propose integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of toxin-protein binding events with machine learning analysis of pharmacogenetic datasets. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale MD simulations (µs-ms timescales) of priority pulmonary toxicants—including particulate matter and industrial solvents—interacting with metabolizing enzymes (e.g., CYP450 isoforms) and DNA repair complexes. Concurrently, we will train ensemble models on multi-ethnic genomic data to identify allelic variants associated with dysregulated detoxification pathways. The computational workflow will cross-validate simulation-derived binding affinity metrics with population-level evidence of metabolic dysfunction, focusing on redox-sensitive signaling cascades implicated in oxidative stress. Key deliverables include predictive models of toxin susceptibility stratified by genetic background, atomistic resolution maps of high-risk toxin-receptor interactions, and mechanistic hypotheses for transgenic validation. This dual-scale approach addresses a critical gap in molecular dosimetry by linking population genomics to mechanistic toxicology. The requested resources will directly support urgent investigations into gene-environment interactions driving disparities in chemical exposure outcomes, with translational implications for personalized risk assessment and targeted countermeasures against undercharacterized toxic threats.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the genetic determinants of susceptibility to external pollutants and poisons; the interaction of toxic agents with biological systems at the molecular and cellular levels; and the development of countermeasures and treatments. Includes instruction in pharmacogenetics, biomolecular structure, gene expression and regulation, transgenic modeling, toxic events signaling, transcriptional activation, mutagenesis and carcinogenesis, pulmonary toxicology, xenobiotic metabolism, oxidative stress, risk assessment, molecular dosimetry, and studies of specific toxins and treatment therapies.

abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable packaging solutions requires innovative approaches to optimize material performance while minimizing environmental impact. Current challenges in Packaging Science involve designing materials that balance mechanical durability, barrier properties, and biodegradability under dynamic real-world conditions. Traditional experimental methods are limited in their ability to predict complex interactions between multi-layered packaging structures, environmental stressors, and degradation kinetics. This project seeks to address these gaps through a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and simulate next-generation packaging systems. The research will focus on three interconnected objectives: (1) developing multi-scale models to predict the mechanical and chemical behavior of bio-based polymer composites under varying humidity, temperature, and load conditions; (2) simulating enzymatic and hydrolytic degradation pathways to quantify time-dependent biodegradation profiles; and (3) optimizing structural geometries for hybrid packaging systems combining rigid and flexible components. Computational methods will integrate molecular dynamics simulations, finite element analysis, and machine learning-driven optimization algorithms to explore vast design spaces. HPC resources are critical for handling the high dimensionality of material combinations, transient boundary conditions, and stochastic degradation processes inherent to these simulations. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for accelerating the development of packaging materials with tunable lifetimes, reduced carbon footprints, and enhanced recyclability. The results will advance fundamental understanding of bio-polymer behavior at multiple scales while providing industry stakeholders with actionable insights for sustainable design. By bridging gaps between materials science, environmental engineering, and computational modeling, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven packaging innovation aligned with circular economy principles.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of scientific, technological, design, and business principles to the development of packages and packaging materials, including raw material production, conversion of raw materials into usable forms, design, distribution, and post-use recycling and reuse. Includes instruction in principles of packaging, materials sciences, distribution and transportation, engineering and technology, graphic design, packaging regulations, and business and marketing.

abstract: The emergence and spread of antimicrobial-resistant (AMR) pathogens in veterinary clinical settings pose a critical threat to animal health, food security, and zoonotic disease management. Current limitations in predicting AMR evolution and transmission dynamics stem from the complexity of microbial genomics, host-pathogen interactions, and environmental variables in livestock populations. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model AMR dynamics across scales, from molecular mechanisms to herd-level epidemiological patterns. We propose a multi-modal computational approach integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of resistance-conferring mutations in bacterial proteins with agent-based models (ABMs) simulating pathogen transmission in heterogeneous livestock populations. MD simulations will employ all-atom and coarse-grained methods to predict structural impacts of mutations in key AMR-associated proteins (e.g., beta-lactamases, efflux pumps), while ABMs will incorporate geospatial data, veterinary treatment protocols, and animal movement patterns to map resistance spread. Machine learning models trained on multi-omics datasets (metagenomic, transcriptomic) from clinical veterinary samples will identify biomarkers associated with resistance emergence. The HPC infrastructure is essential for managing petabytes of genomic data, running parallelized simulations across parameter spaces, and optimizing predictive algorithms through iterative learning. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for AMR hotspot identification in veterinary populations, mechanistic insights into resistance evolution under treatment pressures, and decision-support tools for targeted antimicrobial stewardship in livestock management. By bridging molecular and population-level analyses, this work aims to directly inform clinical veterinary practices while contributing foundational knowledge to the One Health initiative's efforts against AMR.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_title: Veterinary Sciences/ Veterinary Clinical Sciences, General
cip_definition: An integrated program of study in one or more of the veterinary medical or clinical sciences or a program undifferentiated as to title.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in public policy implementation by developing computational models to optimize resource allocation strategies during large-scale public emergencies. Public administrators often face dynamic, high-stakes decision-making environments where inefficiencies in distributing personnel, equipment, and funding can exacerbate crises. Current approaches rely heavily on static prioritization frameworks that fail to account for real-time data streams, interdependencies between response systems, and cascading societal impacts. To bridge this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation platform integrating agent-based modeling, geospatial analytics, and machine learning to dynamically model emergency scenarios. The computational framework will process heterogeneous datasets—including infrastructure inventories, population mobility patterns, and historical response records—to simulate thousands of resource allocation pathways under varying crisis conditions. Bayesian optimization techniques will identify strategies that balance competing priorities such as equity, cost-effectiveness, and risk mitigation. By leveraging parallel computing architectures, the models will iteratively refine decision parameters through multi-objective optimization, enabling administrators to test policies against probabilistic scenarios ranging from natural disasters to public health emergencies. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support toolkit that quantifies trade-offs in resource deployment strategies, validated through case studies of flood response planning in urban municipalities. The project will advance computational public administration methodologies by establishing scalable protocols for data-driven policy testing, ultimately contributing to more adaptive and transparent governance systems. Access to HPC resources is essential given the need for high-resolution spatial-temporal simulations, complex parameter space exploration, and rapid sensitivity analyses required for real-world policy applications.
cip_definition: A program that combines the fields of Public Policy and Public Administration with an emphasis on issues related to public policy. Includes instruction in the role of economic and political factors in public decision-making and policy formulation, resource allocation and decision modeling, cost/benefit analysis, statistical methods, principles of public administration; the management of public policy; and applications to specific public policy topics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of financial derivatives and systemic risk interdependencies in global markets demands advanced computational tools capable of handling high-dimensional, non-linear models. Existing approaches for portfolio credit risk assessment and multi-asset derivative pricing often rely on simplifications that fail to capture tail dependencies, stochastic volatility regimes, and dynamic correlation structures—leading to significant model risk. This project seeks to develop and validate a hybrid computational framework combining Monte Carlo simulations, sparse grid methods for partial differential equations (PDEs), and machine learning-driven approximation techniques to address these limitations. The research will focus on two interconnected challenges: (1) pricing bespoke multi-asset derivatives with path-dependent payoffs under stochastic local volatility models, and (2) quantifying contagion risk in large-scale credit portfolios during market crises. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the exponential growth in computational complexity inherent to these tasks. Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will leverage GPU acceleration to handle millions of asset paths with stochastic jump components, while distributed-memory architectures will enable the solution of high-dimensional PDEs through adaptive sparse grid collocation. The machine learning component will employ neural operators trained on HPC-generated synthetic data to accelerate real-time risk calculations. Expected outcomes include open-source computational tools for robust risk management, validated against historical crisis datasets, and novel insights into systemic risk propagation mechanisms. This work aims to bridge critical gaps in computational finance by providing institutions with scalable, high-fidelity modeling capabilities that enhance stability in rapidly evolving markets.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of mathematics and statistics to the finance industry, including the development, critique, and use of various financial models. Includes instruction in probability theory, statistical analysis, numerical methods, computation and simulation methods, stochastic processes, economics, and financial markets and applications.

abstract: Physical therapy interventions aim to restore functional mobility through personalized therapeutic exercise regimens, yet current methods for optimizing treatment parameters rely on generalized guidelines rather than patient-specific biomechanical and physiological data. This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model musculoskeletal adaptation during rehabilitation, enabling data-driven customization of exercise prescriptions. The research problem centers on integrating heterogeneous datasets—including motion capture kinematics, electromyography (EMG), medical imaging, and wearable sensor outputs—into dynamic simulations of tissue healing and neuromuscular adaptation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to address the computational complexity of multi-scale modeling, which spans molecular pathways of muscle repair, finite element analysis of joint loading, and system-level motor control dynamics. A hybrid approach combining mechanistic modeling (via OpenSim and FEBio) with machine learning will be implemented to predict optimal exercise intensity, duration, and modality for individuals recovering from rotator cuff injuries, a condition with high recurrence rates due to suboptimal loading regimens. Monte Carlo simulations will quantify uncertainty in tissue response predictions across diverse patient demographics. Expected outcomes include: 1) an open-source computational toolkit for physical therapists to simulate rehabilitation scenarios, 2) clinically validated thresholds for tendon strain thresholds during progressive loading, and 3) predictive algorithms linking early-phase recovery biomarkers to long-term functional outcomes. By leveraging HPC capabilities to process terabytes of longitudinal patient data and execute parallelized biomechanical simulations, this work will advance precision rehabilitation strategies that minimize re-injury risks while accelerating recovery timelines. The resource allocation will directly support 12 clinical case studies and the development of AI-driven decision support tools for implementation in outpatient physical therapy clinics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to evaluate, examine, diagnose, and alleviate physical functional impairments and limitations caused by injury or disease through the design and implementation of therapeutic interventions to promote fitness and health. Includes instruction in anatomy, behavioral sciences, biology, biomechanics, biophysical agents, care plan development and documentation, cellular histology, clinical evaluation and measurement, clinical reasoning, communication, exercise physiology, kinesiology, neuroscience, pharmacology, pathology, physiology, professional standards and ethics, rehabilitation psychology, and therapeutic exercise.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale analysis of cross-platform digital communication patterns and their influence on public opinion formation. The research problem centers on the rapid proliferation of AI-generated content (e.g., synthetic text, deepfake media) across social networks, messaging apps, and news platforms, which complicates efforts to understand how information credibility and ideological polarization emerge in hybrid media ecosystems. Traditional computational tools struggle to process the volume, velocity, and multimodality of contemporary digital communication data, necessitating scalable infrastructure. The project will apply natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to detect AI-generated text in multilingual corpora (X/Twitter, Telegram, TikTok), train transformer-based models to classify persuasive strategies in synthetic media, and simulate information diffusion networks using temporal graph neural networks (GNNs). Agent-based modeling will further test how algorithmic content prioritization interacts with human cognitive biases to amplify misperceptions. By integrating these computational methods, the study aims to map systemic vulnerabilities in digital communication architectures that exacerbate distrust in institutions. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible dataset of annotated AI-generated content, novel metrics for platform-level resilience to synthetic media manipulation, and evidence-based frameworks for mitigating polarization in algorithmically mediated spaces. The research will directly inform communication theories of technology affordances and media effects while offering practical insights for policymakers and platform designers addressing epistemic risks in the AI era. HPC resources are critical to managing the project’s terabyte-scale data ingestion, parallelized model training, and real-time network simulations, which exceed the capacity of local computing environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on research and research methods in communication, and that spans the study of mass communication/media studies, old and new media technologies, social and political applications, and speech communication and rhetoric. Includes instruction in quantitative and qualitative methods of inquiry; interpersonal, group, organizational, and intercultural communication; theories of communication; critical thinking, argumentation, and persuasion; written communication; printed, electronic, and digital media; rhetorical tradition and criticism; media, society, and culture; consequences and effects of mass media; and media social science and criticism.

abstract: Veterinary toxicology faces a critical challenge in predicting and mitigating adverse health effects caused by synthetic and naturally occurring chemical exposures in animals. Current approaches to risk assessment rely heavily on time-consuming in vivo studies and limited mechanistic data, which fail to account for the vast chemical diversity and complex interactions affecting toxicity outcomes. This project proposes a computational framework to model chemical interactions with biological targets and predict species-specific toxicological responses, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will integrate molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to characterize toxin-receptor binding dynamics across veterinary-relevant species, including companion animals and livestock, with machine learning (ML) models trained on multi-omics datasets (transcriptomic, metabolomic) from clinical toxicology cases. Key objectives include mapping structural determinants of toxin affinity for neural, hepatic, and reproductive system targets; simulating dose-response relationships under varying physiological conditions; and identifying genetic susceptibility markers for adverse outcomes. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of MD simulations across diverse chemical classes (e.g., pesticides, mycotoxins, pharmaceuticals) and support the training of deep neural networks on heterogeneous datasets encompassing 50,000+ historical exposure records. Expected outcomes include predictive models for acute and chronic toxicity thresholds, a computational biomarker panel for rapid clinical risk stratification, and mechanistic insights into interspecies variability in chemical sensitivity. This work will directly inform evidence-based treatment protocols, regulatory guidelines for veterinary drug residues, and targeted antidote development, addressing critical gaps in clinical veterinary toxicology while reducing reliance on animal testing. By bridging computational chemistry with clinical data science, the project establishes a scalable paradigm for precision toxicology in veterinary medicine.
cip_definition: Research focused on the clinical application of research on the nature and extent of adverse effects of synthetic and naturally occurring chemical substances on animals. May included related research in chemical mechanisms and the specialties of reproductive, developmental, genetic, forensic, inhalation and neurobehavioral toxicology.

abstract: Cultural resource management (CRM) faces significant challenges in balancing the preservation of heritage sites with evolving socio-economic demands, environmental stressors, and policy constraints. Current approaches often lack the capacity to integrate large-scale spatial, temporal, and socio-cultural datasets, limiting predictive accuracy in risk assessment and policy design. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to model the long-term impacts of environmental change, urban development, and policy interventions on cultural heritage systems. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate stakeholder decision-making processes and their interactions with cultural landscapes, combined with geospatial machine learning to analyze multi-source data (e.g., satellite imagery, archaeological records, climate projections). The ABM will incorporate dynamic variables such as site vulnerability indices, funding allocation scenarios, and visitor impact trajectories, while geospatial analyses will identify patterns of site degradation and predict future risk zones. Computational demands arise from the need to process high-resolution spatial datasets, run millions of parallel simulations to account for uncertainty, and optimize preservation strategies via iterative policy testing. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool for policymakers to evaluate trade-offs between preservation priorities, economic development, and environmental sustainability. This work will advance CRM by enabling data-driven prioritization of at-risk sites, optimizing resource allocation, and fostering interdisciplinary collaboration between computational social science, heritage conservation, and policy analysis. The HPC infrastructure is critical to handling the project’s scale, ensuring robust validation of models, and generating actionable insights for stakeholders managing cultural resources under complex, real-world constraints.
cip_title: Cultural Resource Management and Policy Analysis
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of cultural studies, public policy analysis, and management skills to planning, promoting, and implementing programs to preserve and protect cultural heritage sites and artifacts. Includes instruction in historical preservation and conservation, business management, policy analysis, applied economics, public relations, applied history, historical archaeology, and environmental impact studies.

abstract: The formation and evolution of galactic structures in the early universe remain poorly understood due to the complex interplay of dark matter dynamics, baryonic feedback processes, and interstellar medium interactions. Current simulations struggle to resolve the multiphase gas physics and turbulence essential for modeling star formation in high-redshift galaxies, limiting our ability to interpret observations from next-generation telescopes. This project seeks to address these gaps by conducting high-resolution cosmological hydrodynamical simulations of Milky Way-like progenitors at redshifts \( z \sim 2-6 \), leveraging adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) techniques to model small-scale processes such as molecular cloud formation, stellar feedback, and metal enrichment. The simulations will integrate state-of-the-art subgrid prescriptions for radiation transport and non-equilibrium chemistry, validated against recent JWST and ALMA data. Computational demands necessitate sustained access to high-performance computing resources to manage the \(\sim 10^{10}\)-particle scale of the simulations, including GPU-accelerated gravity solvers and distributed-memory radiative transfer calculations. Expected outcomes include new constraints on the role of early stellar populations in driving galactic winds, the impact of turbulence on disk stability, and the emergence of metallicity gradients in young galaxies. These results will directly inform observational strategies for upcoming facilities like the Extremely Large Telescope and the Square Kilometre Array, while advancing numerical methods for multiscale astrophysical modeling. The generated datasets—approximately 500 TB of raw simulation outputs—will be made publicly available through a community-accessible portal, supporting cross-disciplinary studies in galactic archaeology and reionization-era cosmology. By bridging gaps between theory and observation, this work aims to establish a foundational framework for understanding hierarchical galaxy assembly in the first billion years of cosmic history.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the planetary, galactic, and stellar phenomena occurring in outer space. Includes instruction in celestial mechanics, cosmology, stellar physics, galactic evolution, quasars, stellar distribution and motion, interstellar medium, atomic and molecular constituents of astronomical phenomena, planetary science, solar system evolution, and specific methodologies such as optical astronomy, radioastronomy, and theoretical astronomy.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive maintenance and performance optimization in motorcycle engines through computational modeling and simulation. Modern motorcycle engines integrate complex mechanical, thermal, and electrical systems, yet traditional maintenance protocols often rely on static schedules or reactive diagnostics, leading to inefficiencies, increased downtime, and higher operational costs. The research problem centers on developing dynamic, data-driven models to predict component wear, combustion inefficiencies, and system failures under diverse operating conditions. To address this, the project will employ multiphysics simulations combining computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for analyzing combustion dynamics and cooling system efficiency, finite element analysis (FEA) for stress and thermal degradation modeling of critical components (e.g., pistons, crankshafts), and machine learning (ML) to correlate sensor data with failure probabilities. HPC resources are essential to process high-resolution 3D simulations of engine subsystems, train ML algorithms on large datasets of engine performance metrics, and optimize parameters in real-time scenarios. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks to identify early signs of component degradation, optimize fuel injection and ignition timing under variable loads, and recommend context-aware maintenance intervals. These tools aim to reduce unplanned repairs by 20–30%, improve fuel efficiency by 10–15%, and extend engine lifespan. By integrating HPC-driven insights into motorcycle maintenance training programs, this research will empower technicians with advanced diagnostic strategies, bridging gaps between empirical practices and computational innovation in vocational technical education. The project’s computational workflows and open-source models will also serve as a template for adapting HPC methodologies to other small-engine repair domains.
cip_title: Motorcycle Maintenance and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain motorcycles and other similar powered vehicles. Includes instruction in lubrication and cooling systems, electrical and ignition systems, carburetion, fuel systems and adjustments of moving parts.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in predicting aerothermal-structural interactions during hypersonic flight, where extreme aerodynamic heating and dynamic loads threaten vehicle integrity. Current models often decouple fluid dynamics, heat transfer, and structural deformation, leading to inaccuracies in design margins for thermal protection systems (TPS) and airframe components. To overcome these limitations, we propose a tightly coupled computational framework integrating high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD), transient heat transfer analysis, and nonlinear structural mechanics. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to resolve multiscale phenomena, including turbulent boundary layer dynamics, nonequilibrium gas chemistry in plasma formations, and anisotropic material degradation in ceramic matrix composites. Direct numerical simulations of hypersonic flowfields will be paired with finite element models of TPS assemblies under spatially varying thermal gradients, enabling probabilistic assessments of failure modes. A key innovation involves machine learning-augmented surrogate models to accelerate iterative fluid-structure interaction analyses while preserving physics-based fidelity. The computational workflow will be validated against experimental shock tunnel data and in-flight measurements from collaborative hypersonics programs. Successful implementation will advance predictive capabilities for reusable spacecraft re-entry systems and next-generation high-Mach vehicles, directly supporting national priorities in aerospace resilience. The requested HPC allocation will enable parametric studies across flight regimes (Mach 5–15) and material configurations, requiring millions of core-hours for large-eddy simulations, conjugate heat transfer solvers, and uncertainty quantification via Monte Carlo sampling. Outcomes will include open-source modules for coupled multiphysics analysis and design guidelines for adaptive TPS architectures, significantly reducing reliance on over-conservative empirical margins in hypersonic engineering.
major_field: Aerospace, aeronautical, astronautical, and space engineering
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of physical systems used in manufacturing and aircraft, missiles, space vehicles, and their system. Combines instruction in mechanical and aerospace engineering.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and analyze emergent vulnerabilities in socio-technical security systems, with a focus on scenarios where human behavior and institutional policies intersect with technological infrastructure. Traditional security research often prioritizes technical vulnerabilities (e.g., software exploits, hardware failures), yet systemic risks increasingly arise from complex interactions between organizational decision-making, procedural adaptations, and adaptive adversarial strategies. Such dynamics are poorly captured by existing tools, which lack the capacity to simulate hybrid human-technical systems at scale. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) approach integrated with natural language processing (NLP) to analyze policy documents, incident reports, and adversarial tactics. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to support large-scale simulations involving thousands of autonomous agents representing stakeholders (e.g., employees, threat actors, policymakers) operating under dynamically evolving rulesets derived from real-world data. Computational experiments will test how variations in training protocols, communication latency, and compliance incentives affect systemic resilience. By coupling ABM with Monte Carlo methods, we aim to quantify probabilistic risk cascades and identify leverage points for mitigating unintended consequences of security policies. Outcomes will include open-source simulation tools tailored for non-technical security domains, such as organizational fraud prevention or critical infrastructure governance, where human factors dominate risk profiles. This work bridges computational social science and security science, offering a novel methodology to anticipate emergent threats in contexts where purely technical models fall short. The requested resources will enable parameter sweeps across high-dimensional scenarios, reducing computational bottlenecks in simulating rare but high-impact events. Results will inform adaptive security frameworks for institutions operating in rapidly changing regulatory and threat landscapes.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in security science and technology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical gaps in modeling complex chemical systems with quantum mechanical accuracy, focusing on two interconnected challenges in theoretical chemistry: (1) elucidating hydrogen bonding networks in aqueous environments governing proton transfer mechanisms, and (2) predicting reaction pathways for enzymatic processes involving transition metal clusters. Current empirical force fields struggle to capture the multiconfigurational nature of these systems, while conventional quantum chemical methods remain computationally intractable for biologically relevant timescales. This project will employ hybrid ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) coupled with machine learning-accelerated multireference coupled cluster theory (ML-MRCC) to bridge this methodological gap. The computational workflow integrates three innovations: (a) automated active space selection for metal-containing active sites using graph neural networks, (b) on-the-fly reparameterization of density functional tight binding (DFTB) models using MRCC benchmark data, and (c) enhanced sampling protocols leveraging metadynamics and path collective variables. These developments will be implemented through customized extensions to the CP2K and ORCA software packages. The requested high-performance computing resources will enable simulations spanning 10-100 ns timescales for proton transport in confined water channels and catalytic cycles in nitrogenase-inspired model complexes. Expected outcomes include (i) quantitative descriptors for proton mobility in nanoconfined aqueous systems, (ii) mechanistic insights into substrate activation at FeMo-cofactor analogues, and (iii) open-source machine learning force fields trained on >1,000 MRCC single-point calculations. This work will establish new computational standards for modeling reactive intermediates in biological and solvated environments while providing benchmark datasets for the theoretical chemistry community. The allocation of 500,000 node-hours on a GPU-accelerated architecture is essential for achieving the target system sizes (500-1,000 atoms) and statistical sampling requirements.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of mathematical and computational methods and fundamental laws of physics to describe chemical phenomena and to develop empirical models of molecules and their interactions. Includes instruction in properties of small, isolated molecules; dynamics of elementary chemical processes; reaction pathways of organic molecules; hydrogen bonding patterns in liquids; reaction rates of biological pathways; and advanced computational techniques.

abstract: Social entrepreneurship ventures face unique challenges in balancing financial sustainability with mission-driven impact, particularly when navigating dynamic socio-economic environments and resource constraints. Traditional business models often fail to account for the complex interdependencies between stakeholder networks, funding volatility, and non-linear impact metrics inherent to social enterprises. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to simulate and optimize resource allocation strategies for social entrepreneurship initiatives under uncertainty. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will build agent-based models to capture multi-stakeholder interactions—including donors, beneficiaries, and partner organizations—and integrate stochastic optimization methods to evaluate adaptive resource deployment scenarios. The computational architecture will incorporate real-world datasets on philanthropic giving patterns, regional socio-economic indicators, and historical project outcomes from a network of 500+ social enterprises. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify latent variables influencing impact scalability, while Monte Carlo simulations will assess risk profiles of alternative funding models. Key deliverables include an open-source toolkit for dynamic resource optimization, predictive analytics modules for impact forecasting, and policy recommendations for improving resilience in social entrepreneurship ecosystems. By enabling large-scale parallelization of scenario testing, HPC resources are critical to handling the high-dimensional parameter space and combinatorial complexity of stakeholder decision pathways. Outcomes will advance both academic understanding of resource agility in mission-driven ventures and practical frameworks for maximizing social return on investment. The project will disseminate findings through partnerships with social enterprise incubators and a public web interface for interactive model exploration.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on blending entrepreneurial ideas and management skills for issue advocacy and social change. Includes instruction in philanthropy, business modeling, design, entrepreneurship, finance, investing, resource management, project management, prototype development, and marketing.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance early childhood pedagogical strategies by analyzing large-scale, multimodal datasets of preschool classroom interactions. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how dynamic, real-time teacher-student and peer interactions influence skill acquisition in literacy, numeracy, and socioemotional development. Current observational coding methods are limited in temporal resolution and scalability, hindering systematic analysis of behavioral patterns across diverse educational contexts. To overcome this, we propose developing machine learning models to process video, audio, and sensor data from 200+ classrooms, capturing micro-level gestures, vocal prosody, and spatial proximity metrics. Deep neural networks will be trained to classify instructional strategies, child engagement states, and emergent communication patterns, while reinforcement learning simulations will model how minor adjustments in teacher responsiveness propagate through classroom networks. The computational workflow requires parallelized processing of petabyte-scale datasets, necessitating GPU-accelerated nodes for vision and speech tasks, and high-memory nodes for graph-based social network analyses. Expected outcomes include (1) evidence-based frameworks for optimizing lesson pacing and individualized support in mixed-ability settings, (2) predictive models identifying interaction patterns correlated with developmental gains, and (3) open-source tools enabling teachers to simulate classroom scenarios. By quantifying previously intangible aspects of early learning environments, this work will directly inform teacher training programs and curricular designs, ultimately supporting equitable skill development during this foundational educational period. The scale and complexity of spatiotemporal analysis across heterogeneous data streams make HPC resources indispensable for achieving statistically robust, generalizable results within operational timeframes.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students in formal settings prior to beginning regular elementary school, usually ranging in age from three to six years (or grade one), depending on the school system or state regulations. Includes preparation to teach all relevant subject matter.

abstract: This project seeks to develop predictive models to optimize personalized care plans for adults with complex chronic conditions, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address gaps in scalable clinical decision support. Adult patients with comorbidities such as diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and respiratory disorders often exhibit heterogeneous responses to interventions, complicating the design of effective, individualized treatment strategies. Traditional statistical methods struggle to integrate high-dimensional data from electronic health records (EHRs), wearable devices, and genomic biomarkers while accounting for dynamic interactions between physiological, behavioral, and environmental factors. We propose a computational framework combining deep learning and agent-based modeling to simulate patient trajectories under varying care protocols. Recurrent neural networks will process longitudinal EHR data to identify latent risk patterns, while reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively optimize intervention sequences (e.g., medication adjustments, education schedules) in simulated patient cohorts. Agent-based models will incorporate population-level social determinants of health to evaluate equity in predicted outcomes. The HPC environment is critical for training models on multi-terabyte datasets spanning 50,000+ patients from three health systems, enabling parallelized hyperparameter tuning and validation across demographic subgroups. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated pipeline for generating patient-specific care recommendations with uncertainty quantification, (2) comparative analysis of intervention efficacy across socioeconomic strata, and (3) open-source tools to help nurses prioritize high-impact actions in time-constrained settings. By elucidating how multimodal data can guide dynamic care planning, this work aims to reduce preventable hospitalizations and disparities in adult health outcomes while advancing nursing informatics methodologies. The scalability of the framework will be assessed for eventual integration into clinical workflows, with particular attention to computational feasibility in resource-limited care environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to provide general care for adult patients. Includes instruction in adult primary care, adult pathophysiology, clinical management of medication and treatments, patient assessment and education, patient referral, and planning adult health maintenance programs.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in medical office administration through the development of predictive models and simulation tools to optimize resource allocation, staff scheduling, and patient flow management. Medical offices face increasing complexity due to fluctuating patient volumes, regulatory demands, and the need to balance operational costs with quality of care. Traditional manual scheduling and ad hoc decision-making often lead to bottlenecks, staff burnout, and patient dissatisfaction. To overcome these challenges, this research proposes a computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale electronic health record (EHR) datasets, simulate operational scenarios, and train machine learning models. Key objectives include designing discrete-event simulations to model patient intake and workflow dynamics, applying clustering algorithms to identify patterns in no-show appointments, and optimizing staff schedules via genetic algorithms. The computational workload requires HPC capabilities due to the scale of EHR data (spanning millions of patient interactions), the need for real-time simulations of multi-departmental workflows, and iterative model training for predictive accuracy. Expected outcomes include data-driven tools to forecast daily patient volumes, recommend adaptive staffing levels, and reduce wait times through dynamic scheduling. These tools will be validated against historical operational data from partner clinics. The project’s significance lies in its potential to transform medical office management by enabling proactive, evidence-based decisions, reducing operational costs by an estimated 10–15%, and improving patient access to care. By integrating HPC-driven analytics with healthcare administration frameworks, this work aims to establish scalable best practices for the field while providing a template for computational resource utilization in non-clinical healthcare research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the specialized business functions of a medical or clinical office. Includes instruction in business office operations, business and financial record-keeping, personnel supervision, medical and health care policy administration, conference planning, scheduling and coordination, public relations, and applicable law and regulations.

abstract: The dynamics of rapidly rotating planetary atmospheres, such as those of gas giants and ice giants, remain poorly understood due to the complex interplay between turbulence, radiative transfer, and large-scale circulation. Current global circulation models (GCMs) struggle to resolve the multiscale processes driving phenomena like jet stream stability, polar vortices, and cloud formation, particularly under extreme rotational and thermal conditions. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing and deploying a next-generation, high-resolution atmospheric model optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) systems. The research will focus on Jupiter and Neptune as case studies, leveraging recent observational data from Juno and ground-based telescopes to constrain simulations. The computational approach integrates a scalable, three-dimensional non-hydrostatic dynamical core with parameterizations for radiative transfer, moist convection, and cloud microphysics, all optimized for parallel processing on GPU-accelerated architectures.
