Simulations will resolve features down to 10 km horizontally, capturing interactions between planetary-scale waves and small-scale turbulent eddies that are critical to angular momentum transport. A series of parameter sensitivity experiments will quantify the roles of radiative forcing, latent heat release, and boundary layer processes in shaping atmospheric superrotation and storm systems. The outcomes will advance fundamental understanding of planetary climate dynamics, provide benchmarks for interpreting observational campaigns such as the James Webb Space Telescope’s solar system targets, and improve the physical fidelity of exoplanet analog models. This work requires access to HPC resources capable of sustaining 200,000 core-hours per simulation, with dedicated GPU nodes and high-throughput storage for petascale output datasets. The resulting open-source model framework will serve as a community resource for future studies of planetary atmospheres across our solar system and beyond.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of planets and their planetary systems, small objects, and related gravitational systems. Includes instruction in the structure and composition of planetary surfaces and interiors, planetary atmospheres, moons, ring systems, gas clouds, magnetospheres, satellites, orbital mechanics, asteroids and comets, solar system evolution and dynamics, planetary evolution, gravitational physics, and radiation physics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern theatrical productions, which integrate dynamic spatial, auditory, and narrative elements, presents significant challenges in pre-production planning and real-time performance optimization. Traditional rehearsal and design methods often rely on iterative physical adjustments, which are time-intensive, resource-limited, and unable to model the interdependencies of variables such as actor positioning, acoustic propagation, lighting interactions, and audience immersion. This project proposes the development of a computational simulation framework to address these challenges, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and analyze multi-dimensional production parameters. The research will employ agent-based modeling to simulate actor movement patterns and ensemble coordination across diverse stage geometries, coupled with finite element analysis to predict acoustic behavior and lighting dispersion in complex set designs. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on historical performance data to identify optimal blocking strategies and emotional impact correlations, while real-time ray tracing will visualize audience sightline obstructions and spatial engagement metrics. These computationally intensive tasks require parallel processing capabilities to handle large-scale parametric studies of design alternatives and predictive scenario testing. The outcomes will include an open-source toolkit for directors and production teams to virtually prototype stagings, quantify artistic choices, and preemptively resolve technical conflicts. By enabling data-informed creative decisions, this work aims to reduce production costs, minimize technical rehearsals, and enhance performative coherence. The project bridges computational analytics with artistic practice, establishing a methodological precedent for integrating HPC-driven simulation into performing arts pedagogy and professional theatrical workflows.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the planning, design, preparation, and production of plays and other theatrical entertainment programs. Includes instruction in theatrical design, program management, dramatic production, rehearsal management, personnel management and casting, actor coaching, directing concepts and techniques, theater history, scene work, script interpretation, business management, marketing, public relations, and communications skills.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling frameworks for hyperlocal urban microclimate design, a niche within environmental design that intersects spatial analytics, thermodynamics, and human-centered artificial intelligence. Traditional environmental design tools struggle to resolve the dynamic interactions between built environments, vegetation, and atmospheric processes at sub-neighborhood scales, limiting the precision of heat mitigation strategies in rapidly urbanizing regions. To address this gap, we propose developing a coupled simulation system integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD) with machine learning (ML)-driven pedestrian behavior modeling. The CFD component will simulate airflow, solar radiation, and surface temperature distributions at resolutions under 1 meter, while the ML module will predict how residents adapt their movement and activity patterns in response to microclimatic conditions. This dual approach requires iterative, high-resolution 3D simulations across diurnal and seasonal cycles, necessitating parallelized GPU-accelerated computing to manage the computational load. Key challenges include optimizing data transfer between CFD solvers (OpenFOAM) and ML agents (PyTorch) in a distributed HPC environment and validating models against LiDAR-scanned urban morphologies and IoT sensor networks deployed in pilot sites. Outcomes will include open-source tools for simulating human-environment thermal feedback loops and a decision-support framework to prioritize design interventions—such as green infrastructure placement or material reflectance adjustments—that reduce urban heat island effects while maintaining public space usability. By bridging fine-grained environmental modeling with human behavioral dynamics, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for climate-responsive urban design, offering scalable computational strategies to enhance thermal comfort and energy efficiency in communities disproportionately impacted by rising global temperatures.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in environmental design, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize customer experience and operational efficiency in casino environments through advanced computational modeling of dynamic human behavior and resource utilization patterns. The research problem centers on the lack of granular, real-time decision-making frameworks for managing heterogeneous guest flows, service interactions, and facility demands in large-scale gaming and hospitality ecosystems. Current industry practices rely on static scheduling and heuristic-based resource allocation, leading to suboptimal staff deployment, energy consumption, and crowd management during peak operational periods. The project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) integrated with machine learning to simulate multi-agent systems representing guests, employees, and physical infrastructure across temporal and spatial dimensions. High-performance computing resources are required to process high-resolution behavioral datasets (including anonymized mobility patterns, service request logs, and environmental sensor data) while running parallelized simulations of alternative operational scenarios. Computational outputs will be validated against empirical data from partner casino operators to identify optimal staffing ratios, facility maintenance schedules, and emergency response protocols. Expected outcomes include predictive models capable of recommending adaptive resource allocation strategies that balance guest satisfaction metrics with operational cost targets. This interdisciplinary approach bridges computational social science, operations research, and hospitality management, establishing a novel methodology for complex service environment optimization. The resulting framework aims to reduce operational waste by an estimated 12-18% in simulated scenarios while maintaining service quality benchmarks, demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC applications in non-traditional, service-oriented domains.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in casino operations and services not listed above.

abstract: The development of next-generation energy technologies increasingly relies on understanding complex physical systems that span multiple scales of space, time, and energy. This project focuses on advancing predictive models for magnetically confined plasma dynamics in fusion reactors, where turbulent fluctuations disrupt stability and limit efficiency. Current simulations struggle to resolve the interplay between global magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) instabilities and fine-scale kinetic turbulence, creating critical gaps in optimizing confinement configurations. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework coupling MHD solvers with gyrokinetic particle-in-cell methods, enabling self-consistent analysis of plasma behavior across disparate scales. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the extreme resolution requirements (up to 10^10 grid points) and the nonlinear coupling of electromagnetic fields, ion dynamics, and microturbulence. Simulations will leverage adaptive mesh refinement and hybrid MPI-OpenMP parallelization to efficiently distribute workloads across nodes. The proposed work builds on pilot studies demonstrating scalable performance on intermediate-sized clusters but requires expanded allocations to achieve the necessary spatiotemporal fidelity. Expected outcomes include identifying operational regimes that suppress turbulent transport while maintaining global stability, directly informing the design of upcoming fusion pilot plants. Additionally, the computational methodologies developed—particularly for cross-scale coupling and load-balanced particle-field interactions—will advance broader efforts in multi-physics plasma modeling. By bridging critical gaps in fusion energy science, this research aligns with global priorities for sustainable energy innovation while pushing the boundaries of physics-based HPC applications. Successful implementation will require sustained access to GPU-accelerated systems and high-memory nodes to manage data-intensive workflows, with an estimated allocation of 2.5 million core-hours annually.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of physics to a technical discipline or with the interface between physics and other disciplines.

abstract: This project seeks to address unresolved questions in the transmission and evolution of classical texts through computational analysis of linguistic and stylistic patterns across large, multilingual corpora. Despite advances in philological methods, debates persist regarding authorship attribution, textual interpolation, and cross-cultural influences in understudied works from antiquity. Traditional close-reading approaches struggle to systematically analyze features such as syntactic complexity, metrical variation, or semantic networks at scale, particularly when comparing texts across Greek, Latin, and other ancient Mediterranean languages. The proposed research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to implement natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for morphologically rich ancient languages, enabling the identification of subtle stylistic markers and intertextual relationships. Key computational methods include graph-based analysis of citation networks, transformer models fine-tuned on classical languages for semantic similarity detection, and phylogenetic algorithms adapted for textual stemmatics. By processing digitized manuscripts, inscriptions, and scholarly commentaries through parallelized workflows, the project aims to reconstruct fragmentary textual traditions and test hypotheses about cultural exchange. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital toolkit for classical language analysis, new empirical evidence for contested authorship cases in Hellenistic poetry, and methodological frameworks for integrating computational stylometry with traditional hermeneutics. This interdisciplinary approach bridges humanistic inquiry with data-intensive techniques, offering novel pathways to resolve long-standing philological controversies while advancing computational methods for non-English, low-resource languages. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling memory-intensive tasks such as training language models on rare dialectal variants and conducting Monte Carlo simulations to assess statistical significance in stylistic comparisons.
cip_title: Classics and Classical Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in classics and classical languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate syntactic variation across under-resourced Slavic languages through computational analysis, addressing gaps in understanding their structural evolution and contact-induced changes. Traditional comparative methods, limited by manual data processing and small sample sizes, struggle to capture the full complexity of syntactic phenomena across geographically dispersed dialects. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, this study will apply natural language processing (NLP) techniques to parse and annotate a multi-gigabyte corpus comprising historical and contemporary texts from East Slavic (e.g., Ukrainian, Belarusian) and West Slavic (e.g., Slovak, Sorbian) languages. Parallelized dependency parsing models will be trained to identify clause-level structures, while graph-based algorithms will map syntactic convergence patterns across language boundaries. The computational workflow requires distributed memory systems for corpus preprocessing, GPU-accelerated training of transformer-based models for morphosyntactic disambiguation, and large-scale storage for annotated linguistic datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable pipeline for syntactic analysis of morphologically rich languages, (2) quantitative evidence of contact effects in border regions, and (3) open-access resources supporting computational research in Slavic linguistics. By enabling rapid analysis of cross-dialectal features and diachronic shifts, this project will advance theoretical frameworks in language contact studies and provide methodological foundations for computational approaches to lesser-studied Indo-European languages. The requested HPC allocation is critical to overcoming memory and processing constraints inherent in handling heterogeneous text sources and computationally intensive NLP tasks at this scale.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Slavic, Baltic, and Albanian Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: A program that focuses on Slavic languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving role of digital communication in non-ordained Women’s Ministry programs, a specialized niche within Humanities that intersects gender studies, theology, and social dynamics. While Women’s Ministry programs prioritize spiritual and leadership development for women in faith-based communities, there is limited quantitative research on how digital platforms—such as virtual Bible studies, online counseling sessions, and social media outreach—shape theological discourse, community formation, and leadership efficacy. The research problem centers on identifying patterns in digital engagement that correlate with measurable outcomes in spiritual growth, leadership retention, and intergenerational mentorship, particularly in underrepresented cultural contexts. Using computational text analysis, network modeling, and machine learning, this study will process unstructured data from ministry forums, sermon transcripts, and anonymized counseling logs (spanning 15+ years and multiple denominations) to map theological themes, communication hierarchies, and sentiment trends. HPC resources are critical for training transformer-based models to classify nuanced theological arguments, simulating network resilience under varying leadership structures, and conducting large-scale sentiment analysis across multilingual datasets. Expected outcomes include a framework for optimizing digital ministry strategies, predictive tools for identifying at-risk participants, and open-access datasets illuminating the interplay between gender, technology, and spiritual practice. By integrating computational methods with qualitative insights, this project aims to advance evidence-based practices in Women’s Ministry while contributing to broader Humanities discourse on technology’s role in marginalized community-building.
cip_definition: A program that prepares non-ordained women to provide spiritual, counseling, and leadership services to other women in local churches, parachurch organizations, and other settings. Includes instruction in foundations of women's ministry, women's ministry in the local church, spiritual formation, women's evangelism and discipleship, bible study and theology, homiletics, lay counseling, women's issues, and leadership training.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of large-scale music performance datasets, with a focus on identifying patterns in expressive timing, dynamic articulation, and ensemble synchronization across diverse musical traditions. While human-driven musicological analysis remains foundational, current methods struggle to efficiently process the growing volume of high-resolution audio and sensor-based performance data (e.g., MIDI, motion-capture recordings). The research problem centers on developing scalable computational models to quantify and compare nuanced performance practices, enabling systematic study of cultural, pedagogical, and aesthetic factors shaping musical expression. Proposed methods include parallelized audio feature extraction using Fourier and wavelet transforms, graph-based network analysis of ensemble interaction dynamics, and machine learning classifiers trained on annotated performance corpora. These workflows will be optimized for GPU-accelerated processing to handle terabyte-scale datasets encompassing solo and ensemble recordings from global traditions. Anticipated outcomes include: (1) open-source tools for automated performance feature visualization, lowering barriers for music educators and researchers without computational backgrounds; (2) quantitative frameworks to assess the impact of pedagogical approaches on performance practices; and (3) novel datasets mapping correlations between annotated expressive techniques and listener perception metrics. By enabling large-scale comparative studies, this work aims to bridge gaps between empirical musicology and community-driven artistic practices, offering new pathways for preserving intangible cultural heritage and informing curriculum design in music education. The requested HPC resources are critical for overcoming memory and runtime constraints inherent in processing polyphonic audio at scale, particularly for real-world educational applications requiring near-real-time feedback during ensemble rehearsals.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the introductory study and appreciation of music and the performing arts. Includes instruction in music, dance, and other performing arts media.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable optimization models for dynamic resource allocation in large-scale operational systems with stochastic demand and human-in-the-loop decision-making. A key challenge in such systems—common in logistics, manufacturing, and emergency response—is balancing real-time adaptability with computational tractability when human expertise interacts with automated recommendations. Current methods often simplify uncertainty representations or discretize time horizons coarsely to maintain solvability, sacrificing fidelity to real-world dynamics. We propose a two-stage computational framework integrating high-dimensional stochastic programming with online learning. The first stage employs parallelizable Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS) to precompute robust baseline policies under diverse scenarios, while the second stage uses distributed reinforcement learning to adapt these policies to real-time data streams. The hybrid approach requires significant HPC resources due to the curse of dimensionality: scenarios scale combinatorially with the number of decision nodes, and policy updates involve solving non-convex, mixed-integer problems across thousands of parallel threads. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated optimization libraries and MPI-based decomposition algorithms to manage memory and communication bottlenecks. Expected outcomes include (1) a novel open-source solver for human-augmented stochastic optimization, (2) theoretical advances in convergence guarantees for parallelized MCTS in continuous action spaces, and (3) validated case studies on hospital resource scheduling during demand surges, demonstrating 15-30% improvements in wait time variability over existing methods. By enabling finer temporal and spatial resolution in models, this work aims to bridge gaps between prescriptive analytics and human operational judgment while advancing HPC applications in operations research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development and application of complex mathematical or simulation models to solve problems involving operational systems, where the system concerned is subject to human intervention. Includes instruction in advanced multivariate analysis, application of judgment and statistical tests, optimization theory and techniques, resource allocation theory, mathematical modeling, control theory, statistical analysis, and applications to specific research problems. These programs have a mathematical focus.

abstract: Livestock breeding programs face challenges in balancing genetic improvement with maintaining genetic diversity and resilience to environmental stressors. Current genomic selection models often oversimplify genotype-environment interactions and polygenic trait architectures, limiting their predictive accuracy across diverse production systems. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework integrating whole-genome sequencing, longitudinal environmental data, and deep phenotyping to optimize breeding strategies for climate-resilient livestock. We will employ Bayesian neural networks and multi-trait genomic prediction models to analyze terabyte-scale datasets encompassing 500,000 cattle genotypes paired with 10-year environmental records across 42 production systems. The computational workflow requires distributed-memory parallelization for Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling across 100,000 genomic loci, coupled with GPU-accelerated training of attention-based neural networks to detect non-linear epistatic interactions. High-performance computing resources will enable 1) genome-environment association studies at nucleotide resolution, 2) simulation of selection outcomes under 20 climate change scenarios, and 3) real-time optimization of mating schemes considering inbreeding coefficients and trait covariance matrices. Validation will utilize historical breeding data from three continental beef cattle populations (N=1.2 million animals). The resulting framework aims to increase the rate of genetic gain by 18-22% while maintaining diversity levels above conservation thresholds, directly addressing the trade-off between productivity and genetic erosion. This work will provide open-source tools for implementing precision breeding protocols and establish computational benchmarks for integrating systems biology approaches into animal genetic improvement programs. Successful implementation could redefine selection paradigms for sustainable intensification of livestock production.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of genetics and genetic engineering to the improvement of agricultural animal health, the development of new animal breeds, and the selective improvement of agricultural animal populations. Includes instruction in genetics, genetic engineering, population genetics, animal health, animal husbandry, and biotechnology.

abstract: The management of complex urological conditions, such as prostate cancer and treatment-resistant benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), remains limited by heterogeneous patient responses to therapies and incomplete molecular stratification. This project seeks to address these challenges by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-modal clinical, genomic, and imaging datasets, enabling the development of predictive models for personalized treatment optimization. The primary research problem centers on integrating large-scale molecular data (e.g., single-cell RNA sequencing, proteomics) with dynamic imaging biomarkers (e.g., multiparametric MRI radiomics) and longitudinal electronic health records to identify subtype-specific therapeutic vulnerabilities. Computational methods will include the implementation of deep learning architectures for radiomic feature extraction, Bayesian network modeling to map genotype-phenotype interactions, and agent-based simulations of tumor-immune microenvironment dynamics in localized prostate cancer. These workflows require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets, stochastic optimization of high-dimensional parameter spaces, and real-time visualization of spatially resolved molecular networks—tasks infeasible without HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include (1) validated algorithms for non-invasive classification of prostate cancer aggressiveness using MRI-derived radiomic signatures, (2) mechanistic models predicting BPH progression based on stromal-epithelial crosstalk, and (3) open-source tools for federated analysis of distributed urology datasets while preserving patient privacy. By elucidating context-specific disease drivers and optimizing therapeutic targeting, this work aims to advance precision urology paradigms, reduce overtreatment of indolent conditions, and improve functional outcomes for patients undergoing surgical or radiation-based interventions. The requested computing resources will directly enable throughput scaling, reproducibility of complex simulations, and timely translation of findings into ongoing clinical trials evaluating adaptive treatment protocols.
cip_definition: Research focused on Urology

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale analysis of trade networks and cultural exchange in the medieval Near East (7th–15th centuries CE). The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how regional economic systems influenced social and political structures across interconnected but understudied zones, including the Abbasid Caliphate, Seljuk Sultanate, and Crusader States. Despite rich archival and archaeological evidence, synthesizing dispersed datasets—including multilingual coinage inscriptions, caravan itineraries, and pottery provenance records—remains computationally prohibitive using conventional methods. The project will develop a geospatial-temporal model integrating these heterogeneous sources to reconstruct dynamic trade corridors, quantify material circulation patterns, and simulate resource distribution under varying political conditions. Computational workflows will employ natural language processing (NLP) for automated translation and semantic analysis of Arabic, Persian, and Syriac texts, paired with kernel-based spatial statistics to map artifact distributions against environmental and infrastructural layers. Agent-based modeling will test hypotheses about the resilience of trade networks during conflicts and ecological stressors. By deploying these methods on HPC clusters, the team will process ~10 TB of digitized manuscripts, archaeological reports, and remote sensing data while running thousands of parameterized simulations. Anticipated outcomes include (1) an open-access geodatabase linking material culture to historical trade routes, (2) quantitative frameworks for assessing connectivity in fragmentary historical records, and (3) visualizations of shifting economic influence zones. This work will provide historians with scalable tools to analyze cross-regional systems, offering new insights into how resource mobility shaped state formation and intercultural contact in a pivotal era. The computational pipelines developed will also set precedents for data-driven methodologies in premodern Near Eastern studies, a field traditionally reliant on qualitative source criticism.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of the societies, cultures, and institutions of the one or more of the peoples of North Africa, Southwestern Asia, Asia Minor, and the Arabian Peninsula, from their origins to the present. Includes instruction in the historiography of specific cultures and periods; sources and materials; historical research methods; and applications to the study of specific themes, issues, periods, and institutions.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable optimization frameworks for dynamic resource allocation in large-scale, stochastic operational systems, with applications in logistics, healthcare, and manufacturing. A key challenge in such systems is balancing real-time decision-making under uncertainty with computational tractability, particularly when human interventions introduce nonlinear constraints or feedback dependencies. Current approaches often rely on simplifications that compromise solution quality or fail to adapt to high-dimensional state spaces. To address this, we propose a hybrid methodology integrating stochastic programming, decomposition techniques, and reinforcement learning. The core computational effort involves solving families of mixed-integer linear programs with embedded Monte Carlo simulations to approximate complex probability distributions. Parallelizable Benders decomposition will be implemented to exploit problem structure, while neural network surrogates will accelerate policy evaluations in multi-stage decision trees. The research requires high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage memory-intensive matrix operations during branch-and-bound processes, parallel evaluation of scenario trees with >10^4 nodes, and distributed training of surrogate models. Expected outcomes include (1) novel convergence guarantees for decomposition algorithms in non-convex stochastic programs with endogenous uncertainty, (2) open-source software for adaptive resource allocation under intermittent observation regimes, and (3) benchmark solutions for industrial-scale case studies provided by our manufacturing collaborators. The HPC infrastructure is critical for testing theoretical advances against problems of practical scale, where sequential solvers exceed time/memory limits. Success in this work will provide operations researchers with rigorously validated tools to optimize high-stakes systems—from emergency response networks to just-in-time production lines—while maintaining mathematical fidelity to real-world stochastic dynamics and control constraints.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development and application of complex mathematical or simulation models to solve problems involving operational systems, where the system concerned is subject to human intervention. Includes instruction in advanced multivariate analysis, application of judgment and statistical tests, optimization theory and techniques, resource allocation theory, mathematical modeling, control theory, statistical analysis, and applications to specific research problems. These programs have a mathematical focus.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the growing challenge of optimizing real-time knowledge synthesis across decentralized organizational networks, a critical gap in contemporary knowledge management (KM) systems. Traditional KM frameworks struggle to dynamically integrate unstructured data—such as collaborative platform interactions, sensor-driven operational logs, and cross-departmental multimedia communications—into coherent, actionable insights. The computational complexity of analyzing these heterogeneous, high-velocity data streams at scale necessitates advanced parallel processing capabilities beyond conventional infrastructure. This project proposes the development of a graph-based neural architecture enhanced by natural language processing (NLP) transformers to model implicit knowledge relationships and emergent patterns within distributed organizational ecosystems. The computational approach will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train multi-modal machine learning models on terabyte-scale datasets, simulating enterprise-wide knowledge flows under varying operational constraints. Key innovations include adaptive clustering algorithms to map tacit knowledge networks and reinforcement learning agents to prioritize resource allocation for critical information pathways. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for autonomous knowledge curation, reducing latency in decision-critical information retrieval by an estimated 40-60% in simulated environments. The project will further generate benchmark datasets for evaluating KM systems under dynamic, large-scale conditions, addressing the absence of standardized testing protocols for next-generation organizational learning tools. By demonstrating how HPC-enabled architectures can transform passive data repositories into proactive knowledge engines, this research aims to redefine strategic resource optimization in complex business environments, with particular relevance to multinational organizations and crisis response scenarios.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of knowledge management in government agencies and corporations for the purpose of supporting stated organizational goals and objectives, and prepares individuals to function as information resource managers. Includes instruction in information technology, principles of computer and information systems, management information systems, applicable policy and regulations, and operations and personnel management.

abstract: The increasing complexity of building systems, coupled with demands for energy efficiency and sustainable operations, necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize maintenance strategies and system performance. This project seeks to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for simulating and analyzing integrated building systems—including HVAC, electrical networks, plumbing, and structural components—under dynamic real-world conditions. Current maintenance protocols often rely on static schedules or reactive measures, leading to inefficiencies, higher costs, and premature equipment failures. By integrating sensor data, historical maintenance records, and physics-based models, this research aims to create predictive maintenance algorithms that adapt to usage patterns, environmental factors, and system interdependencies. The computational approach combines finite element analysis (FEA) for structural stress modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for HVAC and plumbing performance, and machine learning to predict fault propagation across interconnected systems. HPC resources are critical to handle the scale of parallel simulations required for multi-system optimization, particularly when evaluating scenarios such as extreme weather events, occupancy fluctuations, or energy demand spikes. Expected outcomes include a scalable digital twin platform capable of identifying failure risks, recommending prioritized maintenance actions, and simulating the long-term impacts of retrofitting or operational changes. This work will provide actionable insights for reducing energy waste in commercial and industrial buildings while extending equipment lifespans. The resulting models and datasets will also serve as educational resources for training programs in building maintenance, bridging gaps between traditional technical skills and data-driven decision-making. By leveraging HPC, this project addresses a critical need for adaptive, system-level approaches in building management, with potential applications in smart infrastructure and climate-resilient design.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to keep a building functioning, and to service a variety of structures including commercial and industrial buildings and mobile homes. Includes instruction in the basic maintenance and repair skills required to service building systems, such as air conditioning, heating, plumbing, electrical, major appliances, and other mechanical systems.

abstract: Dental clinical research faces significant challenges in integrating heterogeneous data types to address multifactorial oral diseases, which account for substantial global health burdens. Traditional analytical approaches often fail to capture complex interactions between genetic predispositions, microbial communities, and treatment outcomes, particularly in conditions like peri-implantitis and caries progression. This project proposes to employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable multi-scale modeling of oral disease systems through three synergistic aims. First, we will develop machine learning architectures to analyze terabyte-scale 3D intraoral scan datasets paired with longitudinal electronic health records from 8,000 patients, identifying predictive patterns in restoration failure rates. Second, molecular dynamics simulations will investigate adhesive-dentin interface behaviors under physiological stress conditions, informing next-generation biomaterial designs. Third, agent-based models of oral biofilm formation will integrate metagenomic sequencing data from 200 clinical samples to simulate pathogen-commensal interactions under varying pH and nutrient conditions. Computational demands include GPU-accelerated training of convolutional neural networks on hyperspectral imaging data, parallelized simulation of 10-million-atom systems across 500-nanosecond trajectories, and stochastic modeling of microbial population dynamics across 10^6 parameter combinations. Anticipated outcomes comprise clinically validated predictive algorithms for prosthetic complications, atomistic insights into interfacial degradation mechanisms, and quantitative frameworks for personalized biofilm modulation strategies. By resolving current bottlenecks in data synthesis and mechanistic modeling, this work will establish computational dentistry pipelines to optimize evidence-based treatment planning, reduce implant failure rates, and advance preventive care paradigms. The HPC infrastructure will crucially support time-sensitive analyses across 12 ongoing clinical studies while providing a scalable platform for dental informatics training programs.
cip_definition: An integrated or undifferentiated program that generally prepares dentists in one or more of the oral sciences and advanced/graduate dentistry specialties.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in airport ground operations through the development of a simulation-optimization framework that integrates real-time decision-making with predictive analytics. Airport ground operations—including gate allocation, baggage handling, ground support coordination, and taxiway routing—are complex, dynamic systems influenced by stochastic variables such as weather, flight delays, and passenger volume. Traditional heuristic approaches often fail to adapt to real-time disruptions, leading to cascading delays, increased fuel consumption, and operational costs. To overcome these limitations, this research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model large-scale airport environments and optimize resource allocation under uncertainty. Agent-based modeling will simulate interactions between aircraft, ground vehicles, and personnel, while reinforcement learning algorithms will iteratively refine decision policies to minimize turnaround time and resource idle periods. Monte Carlo methods will assess risk under diverse disruption scenarios, and graph-based network analysis will optimize taxiway routing to reduce apron congestion. The computational demands of training deep reinforcement learning models on high-resolution spatial-temporal datasets, coupled with the parallel processing requirements of simulating thousands of operational scenarios, necessitate access to HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool capable of dynamically adjusting resource allocation strategies in response to real-time operational data. This tool will provide aviation managers with actionable insights to improve on-time performance, reduce fuel waste, and lower operational costs. The project’s significance lies in bridging the gap between theoretical optimization models and practical, real-world aviation management, offering a replicable framework for enhancing efficiency in airport operations while maintaining safety and regulatory compliance. Results will be validated against historical operational data from a major U.S. hub airport, with potential applicability to global aviation enterprises.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the management of aviation industry operations and services. Includes instruction in airport operations, ground traffic direction, ground support and flightline operations, passenger and cargo operations, flight safety and security operations, aviation industry regulation, and related business aspects of managing aviation enterprises.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize resource allocation strategies for social enterprises operating in dynamic, resource-constrained environments. Social entrepreneurship initiatives often face unique challenges, including balancing financial sustainability with mission-driven outcomes, navigating multi-stakeholder ecosystems, and adapting to rapidly shifting socio-economic conditions. Existing decision-making models, which largely rely on static cost-benefit analyses or qualitative case studies, fail to account for the nonlinear interdependencies and real-time feedback loops inherent in these systems. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) approach integrated with machine learning (ML) to simulate complex interactions between social enterprises, beneficiaries, investors, and external factors such as policy changes or market disruptions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to scaling these simulations across diverse geographic and demographic contexts while incorporating high-resolution datasets on economic indicators, climate vulnerabilities, and community needs. The computational workflow will involve parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to explore scenario robustness, graph neural networks to model stakeholder networks, and multi-objective optimization algorithms to identify Pareto-efficient resource allocation policies. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for adaptive decision-making in social entrepreneurship, actionable insights into trade-offs between short-term scalability and long-term impact, and predictive metrics for resilience under systemic shocks. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project aims to advance evidence-based strategies for social enterprises operating at the intersection of equity, innovation, and sustainability, ultimately contributing to scalable solutions for global challenges such as poverty alleviation and climate justice.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on blending entrepreneurial ideas and management skills for issue advocacy and social change. Includes instruction in philanthropy, business modeling, design, entrepreneurship, finance, investing, resource management, project management, prototype development, and marketing.

abstract: Cancer treatment resistance remains a critical barrier to improving patient outcomes, with tumor heterogeneity, clonal evolution, and dynamic molecular adaptations driving therapeutic failure. While multi-omics profiling provides unprecedented insights into these mechanisms, integrating genomic, transcriptomic, epigenomic, and proteomic datasets at scale remains computationally intractable for conventional systems. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable the development of predictive models of treatment resistance in solid tumors, leveraging machine learning and spatial transcriptomics to map tumor microenvironmental dynamics. We propose a computational workflow combining bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing data from metastatic melanoma and non-small cell lung cancer cohorts with longitudinal clinical outcomes. Graph neural networks will model cell-cell interaction networks within tumor-immune ecosystems, while Bayesian hierarchical models will quantify the emergence of resistance-associated mutations under therapeutic pressure. Molecular dynamics simulations will further characterize structural impacts of novel resistance mutations in kinase domains identified through these analyses. The HPC environment is essential for processing >50 TB of raw sequencing data, training deep learning architectures with hyperparameter optimization, and running large-scale parallelized simulations. Expected outcomes include: (1) identification of microenvironmental signatures predictive of early resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors, (2) a ranked catalog of high-risk adaptive mutations in targeted therapy pathways, and (3) open-source tools for real-time resistance monitoring using liquid biopsy data. This work directly addresses the NCI’s priority of translating complex tumor dynamics into clinically actionable biomarkers, with potential to guide adaptive therapy protocols and combination treatment strategies. By centralizing computational toxicology and evolutionary modeling within a clinical oncology framework, the project bridges critical gaps between cancer systems biology and precision medicine implementation.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and treatment of all types of cancer and other benign and malignant tumors; this includes deciding on and administering therapy for these malignancies, as well as consulting with surgeons and radiotherapists on other treatments for cancer.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the complex interplay between transnational digital platforms and cultural identity formation in understudied regions, leveraging computational social science methods to analyze large-scale, multilingual datasets. As global digital infrastructures increasingly mediate cultural exchange, tensions arise between homogenization and hyper-localization, particularly in communities with limited representation in mainstream platform governance. The research problem centers on identifying patterns of cultural adaptation, resistance, and innovation through digital interactions across Southeast Asia’s borderland regions, where overlapping linguistic, ethnic, and political identities challenge conventional globalization narratives. Current methodologies lack the capacity to process heterogeneous data types—including non-Roman script social media posts, encrypted messaging app metadata, and cross-platform meme diffusion—while preserving contextual cultural meaning. The proposed computational approach combines transformer-based multilingual natural language processing with spatial agent-based modeling, requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources to handle three core tasks: 1) training custom language models on low-resource dialects and creole languages, 2) simulating cross-border information flows through adaptive network architectures, and 3) analyzing temporal sentiment shifts in relation to real-world geopolitical events. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of petabyte-scale datasets from diverse sources, including scraped platform data, ethnographic fieldwork transcripts, and historical archives. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for quantifying cultural hybridization dynamics in digital spaces, predictive models of identity-driven platform engagement, and visual analytics tools for policymakers addressing digital sovereignty challenges. This work bridges computational linguistics, cultural anthropology, and political geography while developing open-source tools for ethical analysis of marginalized communities’ digital footprints. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated model training, distributed storage for sensitive data governance, and real-time simulation of multi-agent interactions across 12 simulated cultural boundary conditions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on global and international issues from the perspective of the social sciences, social services, and related fields.

abstract: The human gut microbiota plays a critical role in modulating host metabolism, yet the mechanisms linking dietary patterns to microbial dynamics and metabolic health remain poorly understood. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-resolution computational framework to model diet-microbiota-host interactions in the context of obesity and type 2 diabetes. Current limitations stem from the complexity of integrating multi-omics datasets (metagenomic, metabolomic, and host transcriptomic) with dynamic models of nutrient flux, microbial ecology, and metabolic regulation. To overcome these challenges, we propose a hybrid approach combining agent-based modeling, genome-scale metabolic network reconstructions, and machine learning to simulate how specific dietary components—such as fiber diversity or saturated fat intake—reshape microbial community structure and function, subsequently influencing host inflammation and insulin sensitivity. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize and validate these models using longitudinal human cohort data, enabling the parallel processing of terabyte-scale omics datasets and stochastic simulations of microbial ecosystems under varying dietary conditions. The computational pipeline will also leverage probabilistic graphical models to identify key microbial taxa and metabolic pathways that mediate dietary effects on glycemic control. Expected outcomes include predictive models capable of personalizing dietary recommendations based on an individual’s microbial profile and mechanistic insights into how diet-induced microbiota shifts contribute to metabolic dysfunction. This work bridges nutritional biochemistry, systems biology, and computational ecology, offering a novel platform to explore diet as a modifiable factor in metabolic disease. By elucidating microbiota-dependent mechanisms of nutrient utilization, the project will advance translational applications in precision nutrition while providing scalable computational tools for future studies at the intersection of diet, microbiology, and chronic disease.
cip_definition: A scientific program that focuses on the utilization of food for human growth and metabolism, in both normal and dysfunctional states, from the interdisciplinary perspective of the agricultural, human, biological, and biomedical sciences. Includes instruction in food science, biochemistry, physiology, dietetics, food and nutrition studies, biotechnology, biophysics, and the clinical sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a novel computational framework for optimizing energy-efficient data warehousing architectures in distributed environments, integrating real-time adaptive indexing with renewable energy availability. Modern data warehouses face escalating energy demands due to exponential data growth and the computational intensity of concurrent analytical queries, yet existing resource allocation models prioritize performance metrics without holistically addressing dynamic energy constraints. The research problem centers on balancing query latency, storage efficiency, and carbon footprint reduction in geo-distributed warehouses powered by intermittent renewable sources. We propose a hybrid agent-based simulation and reinforcement learning approach to model multi-objective trade-offs across hardware, software, and energy subsystems. High-performance computing resources will enable large-scale simulations of warehouse clusters under diverse energy profiles, query workloads, and network topologies. Key computational methods include: 1) time-series forecasting of regional renewable energy capacity using transformer neural networks, 2) dynamic workload partitioning via graph-based query dependency analysis, and 3) adaptive columnar indexing strategies optimized through multi-agent deep Q-learning. The framework will incorporate real-world meteorological data and query traces from public sector databases to validate models. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for energy-aware warehouse configuration, empirical benchmarks demonstrating 30-50% reductions in non-renewable energy consumption compared to static allocation baselines, and theoretical insights into stability-complexity trade-offs in self-adaptive database systems. This work bridges gaps between sustainable computing, distributed systems optimization, and data management, offering actionable strategies for organizations transitioning to green IT infrastructures while maintaining analytical performance.
cip_title: Data Modeling/ Warehousing and Database Administration
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to design and manage the construction of databases and related software programs and applications, including the linking of individual data sets to create complex searchable databases (warehousing) and the use of analytical search tools (mining). Includes instruction in database theory, logic, and semantics; operational and warehouse modeling; dimensionality; attributes and hierarchies; data definition; technical architecture; access and security design; integration; formatting and extraction; data delivery; index design; implementation problems; planning and budgeting; and client and networking issues.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of Slavic linguistic diversity, particularly focusing on understudied dialects and historical language shifts. Slavic languages exhibit complex morphological structures and dialectal variation that challenge traditional linguistic models, yet large-scale quantitative studies remain scarce due to computational limitations. The research problem centers on modeling phonetic, syntactic, and lexical changes across Eastern Slavic dialects (e.g., Ukrainian, Belarusian, and Russian regional varieties) and their contact zones with West Slavic languages. The computational approach integrates corpus linguistics, machine learning, and phylogenetic methods to analyze digitized historical texts, contemporary speech corpora, and dialectal archives. Neural networks will be trained to detect patterns in sound shifts and morphosyntactic variation, while Bayesian phylogenetic models will reconstruct divergence timelines. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of unstructured text/audio data, optimizing transformer-based models for low-resource languages, and running parallelized simulations of language contact scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-access database of annotated dialect features, (2) dynamic visualizations of language change trajectories, and (3) methodological frameworks for computational dialectology applicable to other Slavic subgroups. By enabling rigorous analysis of non-standardized language varieties, this work will advance preservation efforts for endangered dialects and inform theoretical debates about Slavic language classification. The requested computing infrastructure will directly support scalability in training domain-specific NLP tools, which currently lack robustness for Slavic linguistic contexts beyond major standardized languages.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Slavic Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the Slavic languages of Central and Eastern Europe. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for optimizing dynamic resource allocation during multi-jurisdictional disaster responses, with a focus on bridging gaps in real-time decision-making under uncertainty. Traditional crisis management models often rely on static contingency plans or simplified simulations that inadequately capture the interdependencies between infrastructure systems, population mobility, and resource supply chains during evolving disasters. The proposed research addresses this limitation by integrating stochastic optimization, agent-based modeling, and real-time data assimilation to simulate complex disaster scenarios, including cascading failures in critical infrastructure and competing demands for emergency services. Computational workflows will leverage parallelized Monte Carlo methods to evaluate thousands of scenario permutations, incorporating heterogeneous data streams such as geospatial damage assessments, hospital capacity telemetry, and transportation network status updates. Key innovations include the development of adaptive graph neural networks to model interdependencies between response nodes and the implementation of multi-objective optimization algorithms that balance competing priorities (e.g., evacuation efficiency vs. first responder safety). The HPC environment is critical for maintaining the temporal fidelity of these simulations, particularly when modeling metropolitan-scale disasters with high-resolution spatial data and sub-hourly decision cycles. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for crisis managers that provides probabilistic guidance on resource deployment strategies, vulnerability assessments of existing response plans under novel threat scenarios, and quantitative metrics for inter-agency coordination efficiency. By explicitly addressing the computational intensity of modeling adaptive human behaviors and infrastructure resilience simultaneously, this work aims to advance incident command systems beyond current heuristic-based approaches while maintaining operational interpretability for non-technical stakeholders.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the application of the incident command system model to formulating and implementing effective response to natural and man-made disasters. Includes instruction in contingency planning, hazard and risk assessment, joint operations, law and ethics, emergency response and recovery, event mitigation, emergency rescue and medical operations, incident command, terrorism and national security issues, law enforcement, relief administration, volunteer and citizen coordination, public relations and applications to specific types of incidents.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of preparing science educators to design and implement computationally rich, inquiry-based curricula that align with Next Generation Science Standards (NGSS). While K-12 science education increasingly emphasizes data literacy, computational thinking, and modeling, many pre-service and in-service teachers lack exposure to the tools and methodologies required to integrate these elements effectively into classroom instruction. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-supported platform for simulating classroom-scale scientific investigations, enabling teachers to prototype and evaluate data-driven pedagogical strategies in a controlled, scalable environment. The research will leverage agent-based modeling frameworks to simulate student interactions with multi-modal datasets (e.g., climate records, biodiversity surveys, physics sensor arrays) under varying instructional conditions. Monte Carlo methods will be employed to assess the robustness of lesson designs across diverse learner populations, while machine learning classifiers will identify patterns in simulated student outcomes correlated with specific teaching interventions. By parallelizing these simulations across HPC nodes, we aim to generate adaptive training modules that help teachers optimize inquiry sequences, anticipate conceptual misconceptions, and scaffold computational workflows for heterogeneous classrooms. Expected outcomes include a validated suite of open-access curricular templates, a teacher dashboard for analyzing simulation-derived pedagogical insights, and evidence-based guidelines for embedding computational practices in science teacher preparation programs. This work will advance science education by creating scalable methods to equip teachers with the technical and pedagogical skills needed to foster authentic scientific practices, ultimately contributing to a more STEM-literate society. The requested computing resources are essential for handling the stochastic, high-dimensional parameter space of classroom simulations and ensuring statistically significant results across demographic and curricular variables.
cip_title: Science Teacher Education/ General Science Teacher Education
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach general science programs, or a combination of the biological and physical science subject matter areas, at various educational levels.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing dynamic decision-making in complex supply chain networks under uncertainty, a critical problem in business administration and management. Traditional analytical models often fail to capture the interdependencies, real-time disruptions, and behavioral factors inherent in global supply chains, limiting their practical utility. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation framework that integrates agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo methods, and machine learning to evaluate adaptive inventory and logistics strategies. The computational model will simulate multi-echelon supply networks with 10,000+ node configurations, incorporating stochastic demand shocks, supplier reliability data, and transportation bottlenecks. By parallelizing scenario analyses across HPC clusters, we aim to assess resilience strategies—such as flexible sourcing protocols and buffer stock policies—at unprecedented granularity while reducing simulation runtime from weeks to hours. Initial pilot studies on regional pharmaceutical supply chains demonstrate the method’s ability to quantify trade-offs between cost efficiency and disruption risks. Scaling this work requires dedicated HPC resources to manage memory-intensive optimization tasks and generative AI components that predict emergent bottlenecks. Expected outcomes include a decision support tool for supply chain managers, validated through partnerships with three multinational firms, and new insights into balancing lean operations with robustness. This project will advance computational methods in operations management while providing actionable frameworks to mitigate systemic risks in critical industries. The requested computing infrastructure is essential to handle petabyte-scale logistics datasets and deliver real-time prescriptive analytics at enterprise-relevant resolution.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to plan, organize, direct, and control the functions and processes of a firm or organization. Includes instruction in management theory, human resources management and behavior, accounting and other quantitative methods, purchasing and logistics, organization and production, marketing, and business decision-making.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision medicine in pediatric care by integrating multi-omics, clinical, and environmental data to model developmental trajectories and disease risks from infancy through adolescence. Pediatric diseases often arise from complex interactions between genetic susceptibility, environmental exposures, and developmental processes, yet current analytical frameworks struggle to disentangle these factors at scale. To address this gap, we propose a computational pipeline combining genome-wide association studies (GWAS), longitudinal electronic health record (EHR) analysis, and machine learning to identify dynamic risk profiles for conditions such as asthma, congenital heart defects, and neurodevelopmental disorders. The HPC infrastructure will enable processing of terabyte-scale datasets, including whole-genome sequences from 10,000 participants in the ongoing Pediatric Lifecourse Cohort Study, real-time environmental sensor data, and high-resolution EHRs spanning 15 years. Parallelized Bayesian hierarchical models will assess gene-environment interactions, while graph neural networks will map temporal patterns in disease progression. Computational fluid dynamics simulations will further model respiratory function in pediatric asthma cases using 3D airway reconstructions from clinical imaging. The anticipated outcomes include predictive algorithms for early intervention, risk stratification tools for critical care prioritization, and mechanistic insights into developmental windows of vulnerability. By overcoming current bottlenecks in data integration and complex systems modeling, this work aims to transform evidence-based guidelines for preventive care, reduce disparities in pediatric outcomes, and inform targeted therapeutic development. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the computational demands of iterative model training, large-scale simulations, and secure, federated analysis across multi-institutional datasets.
cip_definition: Research focused on the comprehensive care and treatment of all aspects of human growth and development from conception through fetal life, infancy, childhood and adolescence, including preventive and therapeutic regimes. May included related research in behavioral aspects of illness, related family and community medicine issues, and emergency and critical care procedures.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze institutional inequities in postsecondary student outcomes using integrated, multi-source datasets. Institutional researchers increasingly face challenges in synthesizing complex educational data—including enrollment records, course performance, co-curricular engagement, and longitudinal degree completion metrics—to identify systemic barriers to equity. Traditional statistical tools often struggle with the scale (millions of records), temporal granularity, and high dimensionality of these datasets, particularly when modeling intersectional student identities and institutional policy impacts. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement distributed data mining pipelines and machine learning models that quantify how institutional practices differentially predict outcomes across student subgroups. Methods include (1) scalable entity resolution to harmonize disconnected administrative databases, (2) GPU-accelerated survival analysis to model time-to-degree variations, and (3) ensemble classifiers to identify critical intervention points in academic pathways. By processing 10+ years of anonymized student records from three public universities (totaling ~2.3TB), the project will generate interpretable risk profiles for historically marginalized populations and simulate the equity impacts of hypothetical policy changes. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source toolkit for higher education institutions to conduct large-scale equity audits, validated through partnerships with institutional research offices. This work advances methodological capacity in education research by enabling causal inference across heterogeneous datasets while maintaining compliance with FERPA and institutional data governance standards. The requested HPC resources are essential for training complex models with nested random effects, conducting millions of policy simulations, and achieving the processing throughput required to operationalize equity analytics in university decision cycles.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares an individual to be an institutional researcher at a postsecondary educational institution. Includes instruction in data analysis, data-driven decision-making, data mining, higher education administration and organization, research methods, and statistics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational tools to enhance the planning and execution of theatrical productions by addressing the challenge of dynamically optimizing stage configurations, actor-blocking patterns, and audience experience in complex performance spaces. Traditional methods for pre-visualizing spatial and temporal relationships in theater rely on static models or iterative physical rehearsals, limiting creative experimentation and efficient resource use. We propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to simulate multi-variable scenarios, integrating 3D spatial modeling, real-time audience sightline analysis, and acoustic propagation algorithms. By parameterizing variables such as set design geometry, actor movement trajectories, and venue-specific acoustics, the system will generate predictive models of how artistic choices impact sightlines, sound distribution, and spatial storytelling efficacy across diverse audience positions. Machine learning techniques will be applied to historical production data to identify patterns in effective blocking strategies, while fluid dynamics simulations will model airflow for vocal projection optimization in non-traditional performance environments. The computational intensity of rendering these interdependent variables in real time necessitates GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory resources to handle high-resolution venue scans and complex agent-based models of crowd perception. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for directors and production designers to virtually prototype staging concepts, quantitatively evaluate trade-offs between artistic vision and technical constraints, and democratize access to advanced previsualization typically limited to high-budget productions. This interdisciplinary approach bridges performing arts practice with computational analytics, offering new methodologies for data-informed creative decision-making while preserving artistic intuition. Results will be validated through collaborative case studies with regional theaters, measuring reductions in technical rehearsal time and improvements in audience engagement metrics. The project aims to establish a replicable computational workflow that redefines preparatory processes in theatrical production, fostering innovation in spatial storytelling and resource-efficient design.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the planning, design, preparation, and production of plays and other theatrical entertainment programs. Includes instruction in theatrical design, program management, dramatic production, rehearsal management, personnel management and casting, actor coaching, directing concepts and techniques, theater history, scene work, script interpretation, business management, marketing, public relations, and communications skills.

abstract: This project proposes the development of a high-resolution computational model to analyze the impact of decentralized urban green infrastructure investments on commercial real estate valuation dynamics. Current appraisal methodologies inadequately capture the nonlinear relationships between distributed sustainability features (e.g., green roofs, permeable surfaces, micro-parks) and spatial price differentials, particularly in dense urban cores. The research will leverage high-performance computing resources to process lidar-derived 3D urban morphology data, decade-level property transaction records, and IoT sensor networks measuring microclimate changes across 12 major metropolitan areas. A hybrid machine learning architecture combining graph convolutional networks and temporal transformers will be implemented to model the diffusion of sustainability-driven value premiums through urban real estate markets. The computational framework will enable simultaneous analysis of (1) hyperlocal environmental improvements, (2) zoning regulation scenarios, and (3) investor behavior patterns at an unprecedented 10-meter spatial resolution. Validation will utilize multi-agent simulations of commercial property transactions under varying climate policy regimes. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolkit quantifying the capitalization rates of green infrastructure at portfolio scales and evidence-based policy recommendations for municipal public-private partnership structures. By establishing computational links between micro-scale ecological enhancements and macroeconomic real estate trends, this research aims to create new paradigms for valuing distributed sustainability assets while informing climate-resilient urban development strategies. The project requires advanced GPU capabilities for training spatial-temporal models on 350+ TB of heterogeneous urban datasets, with particular emphasis on memory-intensive processing of 4D climate impact projections.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop, buy, sell, appraise, and manage real estate. Includes instruction in land use development policy, real estate law, real estate marketing procedures, agency management, brokerage, property inspection and appraisal, real estate investing, leased and rental properties, commercial real estate, and property management.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the pedagogical efficacy and cultural adaptability of digital religious education curricula across diverse global faith communities. While religious education programs are critical for sustaining traditions, existing studies rarely address how digitally mediated instruction—such as virtual scripture study, AI-driven moral reasoning simulations, or cross-cultural interfaith dialogue platforms—impacts learning outcomes in varied socioreligious contexts. The computational challenge lies in modeling complex, nonlinear relationships between instructional design variables (e.g., multimedia integration, adaptive feedback systems) and learner engagement metrics across disparate datasets, which include multilingual textual corpora, behavioral interaction logs, and ethnographic surveys from over 20 religious traditions. Using a mixed-methods framework, the project will apply natural language processing (NLP) to classify thematic patterns in learner feedback, agent-based modeling to simulate community-specific adoption of digital tools, and deep learning architectures to predict long-term knowledge retention rates. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of unstructured data, training multimodal neural networks, and running large-scale sensitivity analyses on pedagogical parameters. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable computational model for optimizing faith-specific educational interventions, an open-access repository of annotated intercultural religious education datasets, and evidence-based guidelines for mitigating biases in AI-generated spiritual content. By bridging computational social science and religious pedagogy, this work aims to establish a methodological foundation for data-driven decision-making in religious education—a field historically reliant on qualitative approaches—while addressing urgent gaps in equitable resource allocation for underrepresented faith communities in digital spaces.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory and practice of providing educational services to members of faith communities, within the context of a particular religion, and that prepares individuals to serve as religious educators. Includes instruction in planning and teaching lessons, organizing and supervising instructional activities, designing and developing instructional materials, and administering religious education programs and facilities.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the design of adaptive human-machine interfaces for individuals with severe motor impairments, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address the combinatorial complexity of personalized rehabilitation engineering. Current assistive technologies, such as eye-tracking systems or brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), often require labor-intensive calibration and lack robust adaptability to users’ fluctuating physiological states, environmental conditions, or progressive disabilities. To overcome these limitations, we propose a machine learning-driven approach integrating multimodal data—including electromyography (EMG), electroencephalography (EEG), and inertial measurement unit (IMU) signals—with biomechanical simulations to model user-device interactions in real time. The core computational challenge involves training deep reinforcement learning models to predict optimal device configurations while accounting for dynamic constraints such as muscle fatigue, spasticity, and postural instability. HPC resources are critical to support large-scale parameter sweeps during model training, finite element analysis of ergonomic device components, and Monte Carlo simulations of environmental variability (e.g., lighting, noise). Expected outcomes include an open-source toolbox for adaptive interface design, validated through virtual patient cohorts representing diverse neuromuscular pathologies. This work will advance the scalability of personalized assistive technologies, reduce trial-and-error prototyping costs, and improve functional outcomes for users with complex rehabilitation needs. By enabling rapid, simulation-guided optimization of augmentative systems, the project aligns with broader goals of democratizing access to high-quality assistive devices in underserved populations.
cip_title: Assistive/ Augmentative Technology and Rehabilitation Engineering
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply the principles of psychology, engineering, and occupational therapy to the design and implementation of technological interventions and systems to promote patient rehabilitation and function.
