Includes instruction in ergonomics, seating and mobility design, universal and near environment systems design, rehabilitation research, rehabilitation biomechanics, access and communications design, microprocessor-based technologies, neurological trauma, standards and testing, and service delivery management.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on the detection and analysis of synthetic media in journalism, addressing the growing threat of AI-generated misinformation to public trust in news ecosystems. As deepfakes and algorithmically manipulated text, images, and video become increasingly sophisticated, journalists face unprecedented challenges in verifying content and maintaining ethical reporting standards. The research problem centers on developing scalable computational tools to identify synthetic media artifacts, trace their dissemination patterns across digital platforms, and assess their impact on news consumption behaviors. The project will employ a multimodal approach, combining natural language processing (NLP) models to detect AI-generated text, computer vision techniques to analyze visual inconsistencies in photojournalism and video content, and network analysis to map the spread of suspected synthetic media through social and news media channels. These methods require HPC resources to process terabytes of multimedia data from public social media APIs, news archives, and partnered journalistic organizations, as well as to train ensemble models that integrate diverse detection signals. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for newsrooms to prioritize suspect content for human review, a dataset of annotated synthetic media cases, and empirical insights into how synthetic content interacts with traditional news cycles. By enhancing computational support for verification workflows, this research aims to strengthen journalistic capacity to uphold accuracy and transparency in an era of rapidly evolving digital deception. The project aligns with journalism’s core mission of responsible reporting while contributing new methodologies at the intersection of media ethics, digital forensics, and computational social science.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory and practice of gathering, processing, and delivering news and that prepares individuals to be professional print journalists, news editors, and news managers. Includes instruction in news writing and editing; reporting; photojournalism; layout and graphic design; journalism law and policy; professional standards and ethics; research methods; and journalism history and criticism.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and evaluate computational models of classroom dynamics to enhance the training of elementary educators through simulated, data-driven scenarios. A critical challenge in teacher preparation is providing novice educators with exposure to diverse, unpredictable classroom environments that require adaptive instructional strategies. Current training methods often rely on limited in-person practicum opportunities, which may not adequately prepare teachers for the variability of real-world student behaviors, learning needs, and engagement patterns. To address this gap, we propose creating high-fidelity simulations of K-6 classrooms using agent-based modeling and machine learning techniques. These simulations will integrate anonymized datasets of student interactions, academic performance metrics, and demographic variables to generate dynamic virtual classrooms. The project will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to run parallelized, large-scale simulations that model complex variables such as individualized student learning trajectories, group behavior dynamics, and teacher decision-making outcomes under time constraints. Computational experiments will test hypotheses about how different pedagogical approaches—including differentiated instruction, behavior management strategies, and culturally responsive teaching methods—affect simulated student engagement and learning outcomes. The HPC infrastructure is essential for handling the real-time processing of multivariate interactions across thousands of simulated classroom "sessions" while maintaining granular temporal resolution. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-access repository of validated classroom simulation scenarios for teacher education programs, (2) quantitative frameworks linking specific teaching strategies to predicted student outcomes, and (3) AI-driven feedback tools to help pre-service teachers refine their instructional techniques. By bridging computational modeling and elementary pedagogy, this work aims to create transformative resources for evidence-based teacher training while maintaining strict ethical standards for data anonymity and bias mitigation in educational AI systems.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students in the elementary grades, which may include kindergarten through grade eight, depending on the school system or state regulations. Includes preparation to teach all elementary education subject matter.

abstract: Oral and maxillofacial pathologies, such as oral squamous cell carcinoma, osteonecrosis, and fibro-osseous lesions, present significant diagnostic and prognostic challenges due to their heterogeneous clinical, molecular, and radiographic features. Current approaches often lack the computational power to integrate multi-modal data—including high-resolution histopathology images, 3D radiographic volumes, genomic profiles, and clinical metadata—limiting the development of precision diagnostic frameworks. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to build predictive models that unify diverse data types for improved disease classification and management. The primary research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in processing large-scale, multi-dimensional datasets while identifying latent biomarkers of disease progression. We propose a hybrid computational approach combining deep learning architectures, such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for image analysis and transformer-based models for multi-omics integration, with graph-based analytics to map spatial relationships in tissue microenvironment data. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of whole-slide histopathology images (≥100,000x100,000 pixels), GPU-accelerated training of 3D convolutional models for CBCT/MRI volumes, and large-scale molecular dynamics simulations to study protein interactions in disease-specific pathways. Additionally, we will implement federated learning frameworks to collaborate with multi-institutional datasets while maintaining data privacy. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational pipeline for automated detection of malignant transformation in oral epithelial dysplasia, (2) predictive models linking radiographic bone patterns to genetic variants in osteonecrosis, and (3) open-source tools for spatial transcriptomics analysis in tumor microenvironments. By enabling rapid integration of terabyte-scale datasets, this work will advance personalized risk stratification, reduce diagnostic subjectivity, and uncover novel therapeutic targets. The requested computing resources are critical to handling the project’s data volume and algorithmic complexity, which exceed the capacity of local clinical workstations. Outcomes will directly contribute to improving diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic decision-making for over 500,000 annual patients affected by oral-maxillofacial diseases worldwide.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and management of diseases affecting the oral and maxillofacial regions, using clinical, radiographic, microscopic, biochemical, or other examinations.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize urban food systems by integrating ecological, economic, and social dynamics into a unified computational framework, addressing critical gaps in sustainability planning. Urban regions face escalating pressures to balance food security, resource efficiency, and equitable access while minimizing environmental harm. Current models often treat these dimensions in isolation, neglecting feedback loops between localized urban agriculture, global supply chains, waste management, and community behavior. To overcome this limitation, we propose a multi-agent simulation platform coupled with spatially explicit network analysis to capture cross-scale interactions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize the system using heterogeneous datasets—including satellite-derived land use, real-time transportation logs, and socioeconomic surveys—and simulate scenarios under varying climate, policy, and market conditions. Agent-based modeling will represent stakeholders (e.g., households, distributors, policymakers) adapting to resource constraints, while machine learning techniques will identify emergent patterns in resilience and vulnerability across demographic groups. The computational framework will quantify trade-offs between centralized vs. decentralized food systems, evaluate circular economy interventions, and project long-term outcomes for carbon emissions, water use, and food equity. Expected outcomes include actionable metrics for cities to prioritize context-specific sustainability strategies, such as optimizing green infrastructure placement or incentivizing waste-to-energy transitions. By bridging urban ecology, supply chain logistics, and social justice analytics, this work advances interdisciplinary methodologies for complex system governance and provides scalable tools to align United Nations Sustainable Development Goals with local realities. The requested HPC allocation will enable unprecedented resolution in modeling urban food networks, facilitating rapid iteration of policy-sensitive scenarios critical for mitigating climate risks and fostering equitable resource distribution.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the concept of sustainability from an interdisciplinary perspective. Includes instruction in sustainable development, environmental policies, ethics, ecology, landscape architecture, city and regional planning, economics, natural resources, sociology, and anthropology.

abstract: Urban horticulture systems face unique challenges due to heterogeneous microclimates, fragmented growing spaces, and dynamic interactions between built environments and plant ecophysiology. Optimizing crop productivity and resource efficiency in these contexts requires high-resolution modeling of complex abiotic-biotic interactions, which remains computationally intractable with conventional methods. This project seeks to develop and apply a scalable computational framework integrating multi-domain datasets—including 3D urban topography, hyperlocal weather patterns, soil sensor networks, and plant phenotyping—to simulate and predict outcomes for diverse urban horticulture configurations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable parallelized execution of agent-based models simulating plant growth under variable light, heat, and pollution gradients, coupled with machine learning algorithms to identify genotype-environment-management synergies. Key objectives include parameterizing site-specific responses of leafy greens and fruiting crops to urban stressors, optimizing irrigation schedules via real-time soil moisture forecasting, and evaluating trade-offs between yield, energy use, and ecosystem services across rooftop, vertical, and community garden systems. The computational pipeline will leverage GPU acceleration for large-scale spatial analyses and ensemble modeling to account for uncertainty in climate projections. Outcomes will generate actionable insights for adaptive urban agriculture planning, including cultivar recommendations, microclimate mitigation strategies, and policy guidelines to enhance food security in metropolitan areas. By establishing an open-source modeling toolkit validated against experimental urban farms in three cities, this work aims to advance computational horticulture as a decision-support tool for sustainable urbanization. The requested HPC allocation is critical for managing petabyte-scale environmental datasets and achieving the resolution required to resolve fine-grained interactions between infrastructure, ecology, and crop performance in heterogeneous urban landscapes.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on principles and techniques for the production of horticultural crops in an urban environment. Includes instruction in ecology, environmental sustainability, food production systems, and plant and soil sciences.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to advance precision medicine in otolaryngology by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze complex multi-modal datasets from patients with head and neck cancers (HNCs). Despite advances in genomic and imaging technologies, integrating heterogeneous data types—such as bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, radiomics, and clinical outcomes—remains a critical challenge. Current analytical pipelines lack the computational scalability to identify robust biomarkers or model tumor-immune microenvironment interactions at the resolution required for personalized therapeutic strategies. This project will develop and deploy machine learning frameworks optimized for HPC environments to unify these datasets, enabling the identification of molecular signatures predictive of treatment response and metastasis. Computational workflows will include graph neural networks to model spatial tumor-immune cell interactions from multiplex immunohistochemistry data, Bayesian hierarchical models to resolve subtype heterogeneity in multi-omics cohorts, and fluid dynamics simulations to assess upper airway functional outcomes post-surgery. Anticipated outcomes include (1) validated predictive models for immunotherapy response in HNCs, (2) open-source tools for integrative analysis of otolaryngologic imaging and genomic data, and (3) patient-specific biomechanical simulations to optimize surgical planning. The scale of these analyses—requiring parallel processing of >10 TB of imaging data, >100,000-cell single-cell datasets, and finite element modeling with 10^6-node meshes—necessitates dedicated HPC resources for memory-intensive tasks and GPU-accelerated model training. By bridging computational innovation with clinical translation, this work aims to establish a pipeline for data-driven decision-making in otolaryngology, ultimately improving survival and quality of life for patients with complex head and neck disorders.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians to diagnose and provide medical and/or surgical therapy or prevention of diseases, allergies, neoplasms, deformities, disorders, and injuries of the ears, nose, sinuses, throat, respiratory and upper alimentary systems, face, jaws, and the other head and neck systems.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the role of dynamic cognitive load modulation in virtual learning environments (VLEs) through computational modeling and real-time simulation. As digital education tools become increasingly complex, learners face challenges in managing cognitive resources effectively, leading to disparities in engagement and knowledge retention. Traditional pedagogical models struggle to adapt to individual cognitive thresholds, particularly in heterogeneous or large-scale virtual classrooms. To address this gap, we propose developing a high-fidelity neural network framework that simulates learner-environment interactions under varying cognitive load conditions. The model will integrate psychometric data, eye-tracking patterns, and physiological response datasets to predict optimal load thresholds for different learning modalities (e.g., immersive VR vs. 2D interfaces). High-performance computing resources are essential to process multimodal data streams concurrently, train reinforcement learning agents that adapt content delivery in simulated environments, and run parallelized Monte Carlo simulations assessing scalability across diverse demographic profiles. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolkit for educators to design cognitively sustainable VLEs and evidence-based thresholds for adaptive content pacing algorithms. This work bridges educational psychology, computational neuroscience, and human-computer interaction, offering a novel framework to address equity in digital learning by computationally modeling the biological and environmental constraints of cognitive capacity. Results will be validated against empirical classroom studies, with open-source code and simulation templates disseminated to support personalized learning infrastructure development.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general theory and practice of learning and teaching, the basic principles of educational psychology, the art of teaching, the planning and administration of educational activities, school safety and health issues, and the social foundations of education.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling of biomechanical and microbiological interactions within root canal systems, addressing critical gaps in understanding treatment outcomes for pulpal and periradicular diseases. Despite advances in endodontic techniques, unpredictable failures persist due to complex factors such as incomplete biofilm eradication, residual stress from instrumentation, and variable root canal anatomy. Current experimental methods struggle to capture these multi-scale dynamics, necessitating a computational approach. The research will develop a multi-physics model integrating finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate mechanical stress distributions during root canal preparation, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to map irrigant flow and antimicrobial efficacy in anatomically complex canals, and agent-based modeling to predict bacterial biofilm resilience. High-resolution micro-CT scans of extracted teeth will inform anatomically accurate geometries, while machine learning algorithms will analyze clinical datasets to correlate simulation results with real-world treatment success rates. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational load of 3D simulations across spatial scales (µm to mm) and time-resolved processes (seconds to weeks). Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for optimizing irrigation protocols, instrument selection, and biofilm-targeting strategies tailored to patient-specific canal morphology. This work will provide foundational insights into the biomechanical drivers of postoperative healing or failure, directly informing clinical guidelines and educational tools. By bridging computational innovation with endodontic practice, the project aims to reduce treatment variability, improve long-term tooth retention, and address disparities in outcomes linked to anatomical complexity.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of the morphology, physiology, and pathology of human dental pulp and periradicular tissues, and prepares dentists to diagnose and treat internal diseases and injuries of teeth. Includes instruction in theory and practice of endodontics; pulpal disease; relationship of endodontic conditions to other dental/oral health issues; endodontic operative technique; and patient care and management.

abstract: The brewing industry faces persistent challenges in optimizing fermentation processes, where microbial dynamics and metabolic interactions critically influence product quality, consistency, and efficiency. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to resolve the complexity of microbial ecosystems in brewing, particularly under varying raw material inputs and environmental conditions. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale computational models that simulate yeast metabolism and microbial community interactions during fermentation. By integrating genome-scale metabolic models of Saccharomyces cerevisiae and non-Saccharomyces species with dynamic fermentation parameters (e.g., temperature, pH, sugar profiles), we aim to predict metabolic fluxes, stress responses, and byproduct formation under diverse brewing scenarios. Computational workflows will employ constraint-based modeling, agent-based simulations, and machine learning to analyze multi-omics datasets (transcriptomics, metabolomics) from experimental fermentations. HPC resources are essential to handle the combinatorial complexity of microbial interactions, parameterize models using high-dimensional data, and conduct sensitivity analyses across thousands of simulated conditions. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for strain selection, process optimization, and contamination mitigation, directly addressing industry needs for precision in scaling novel beer styles and reducing production losses. The project will also advance methodologies for modeling microbial ecosystems in food systems, with broader applications in agricultural biotechnology. By bridging brewing science with computational biology, this work aligns with agricultural innovation goals, emphasizing sustainable resource use and value-added product development within the food and beverage sector.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the business, science, and technology of beer brewing operations. Includes instruction in biology, biochemistry, brewing, entrepreneurship, fermentation, malting, marketing, microbiology, quality control, and sanitation.

abstract: This project investigates the interplay between visual environmental stimuli and cognitive restoration through an interdisciplinary lens integrating environmental psychology, computational neuroscience, and urban design. While exposure to natural environments is known to reduce cognitive fatigue, the specific visual features driving restorative effects—such as fractal patterns, color spectra, and spatial complexity—remain poorly quantified. Current analytical approaches lack the resolution to model how dynamic, high-dimensional visual inputs interact with individual neurocognitive processes. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework combining eye-tracking, EEG, and behavioral data from 300 participants exposed to immersive virtual environments simulating natural and urban settings. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable three key innovations: (1) large-scale parallel processing of multimodal data streams (120Hz gaze paths, 256-channel EEG, and continuous affect ratings) across participants; (2) training deep convolutional neural networks to identify latent visual features predictive of alpha-band EEG modulation and self-reported restoration; and (3) agent-based modeling of attention restoration dynamics through GPU-accelerated simulations incorporating individual differences in perceptual styles. The computational pipeline will leverage PyTorch and CUDA-optimized libraries for real-time data fusion, while graph neural networks will map how specific environmental attributes propagate through cognitive subsystems. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model of visual restoration potential and an open-source toolkit for simulating cognitive impacts of architectural designs. By establishing quantitative links between environmental aesthetics and neural markers of cognitive recovery, this work aims to advance evidence-based strategies for mental health-promoting urban planning while developing novel methods for scaling ecological psychology research through computational modeling. The requested HPC infrastructure is critical for managing the project's data intensity (estimated 450TB of raw neurobehavioral data) and supporting the complex parameter spaces of our machine learning architectures.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in psychology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance precision breeding strategies for livestock disease resistance by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze complex genomic and phenotypic datasets. Current methods for identifying disease-resilient traits in agricultural animals are limited by computational bottlenecks in processing multi-omics data (genome, transcriptome, epigenome) and modeling gene-environment interactions at scale. The research problem centers on improving the accuracy of genomic selection models to address emerging zoonotic threats and antimicrobial resistance challenges in veterinary and agricultural systems. We propose a computational pipeline integrating machine learning algorithms with genome-wide association studies (GWAS) to identify candidate loci linked to disease resilience in cattle populations exposed to bovine respiratory disease complex (BRDC). HPC resources will enable the parallelized analysis of terabyte-scale datasets, including whole-genome sequences from 5,000 individuals, longitudinal health records, and environmental stressor metadata. Key computational steps include (1) dimensionality reduction of SNP arrays using variational autoencoders, (2) Bayesian network modeling of host-pathogen interaction dynamics, and (3) validation through in silico simulations of selective breeding scenarios. The project builds on preliminary work demonstrating 12-18% improvements in prediction accuracy for BRDC susceptibility when using graph neural networks versus traditional linear models. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for accelerated trait discovery, validated molecular markers for producer breeding programs, and quantitative models of genetic-by-management interaction effects. By enabling rapid analysis of complex trait architectures, this work will directly support veterinary preparatory programs training future professionals in advanced agricultural biotechnology applications. The requested computing resources are critical for achieving the necessary scale and resolution to inform sustainable livestock management practices amid climate-driven disease pressures.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: Any instructional program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in agriculture or veterinary medicine or science, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the sociocultural dynamics of sports fandom as a driver of collective identity formation in digital spaces. While sports studies traditionally relies on qualitative and small-scale quantitative methods, the scale and complexity of modern fan interactions—spanning social media platforms, streaming services, and augmented reality applications—demand computational approaches to analyze multimodal, longitudinal datasets. The research focuses on three interrelated problems: (1) modeling the emergence of transnational fan communities around emerging sports leagues, (2) quantifying the interplay between real-world athletic performance and digital fan engagement metrics, and (3) identifying patterns of cultural hybridity in fan-created content across linguistic and geopolitical boundaries. Computational methods will include large-language model (LLM) fine-tuning for multilingual sentiment analysis of fan discourse, graph neural networks to map community evolution across platforms, and agent-based simulations to test hypotheses about information cascades in fan networks. The workflow integrates terabyte-scale datasets from proprietary sports analytics APIs, public social media archives, and digitized historical records of fandom practices. By establishing a pipeline for sports cultural analytics, this project aims to produce both theoretical insights into 21st-century collective identity formation and practical tools for understanding fan-driven economic ecosystems. Anticipated outcomes include the first longitudinal map of fan network topology across major emerging sports markets, a computational framework for predicting community fracture points during cultural controversies, and open-source tools for ethical sports big data analysis. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling memory-intensive graph computations, training domain-specific LLMs on sports discourse corpora, and running parallelized simulations of fan interaction scenarios at societally relevant scales.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the psychological, sociological, and historical aspects of sport and physical activity. Includes instruction in theory of sport, sport psychology, sport in American society, gender and race/ethnicity and sport, and sports history.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive analytics framework to optimize wholesale purchasing decisions in fashion merchandising by integrating real-time consumer sentiment analysis, supply chain dynamics, and macroeconomic trend modeling. The challenge lies in aligning volatile consumer preferences—driven by rapidly evolving social media trends and cultural shifts—with production lead times and supplier constraints. Traditional linear regression models fail to capture the nonlinear interdependencies between hyper-localized trend signals, global logistics disruptions, and wholesale buyer behavior. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational architecture combining transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) for social media text/image analysis, graph neural networks (GNNs) to model supplier-retailer networks, and agent-based simulations of bulk purchasing decisions. The research will leverage high-performance computing resources to train multi-modal models on petabytes of structured (historical purchase orders, inventory turnover rates) and unstructured data (Instagram posts, TikTok videos, influencer content) while simulating supply chain scenarios across 18 global fashion hubs. Computational experiments will benchmark proposed models against industry-standard forecasting tools using custom loss functions that prioritize minimizing both overstock waste and opportunity costs from understocking trending items. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision support system capable of recommending optimized wholesale purchase quantities with 72-hour trend anticipation windows, demonstrated to reduce deadstock by an estimated 34-41% in pilot simulations using historical data from mid-sized apparel brands. This interdisciplinary approach bridges computational social science, operations research, and fashion studies, offering a novel methodology for responsive resource allocation in trend-driven industries.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to promote product lines/brands, and organize promotional campaigns, at the wholesale level to attract retailer interest, wholesale purchasing, and supply contracts. Includes instruction in wholesaling, wholesale advertising, selling, and customer relations.

abstract: The accelerating impacts of climate change, habitat fragmentation, and invasive species necessitate advanced predictive tools to optimize conservation strategies for terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems. This project seeks to develop a spatially explicit modeling framework to forecast wildlife population dynamics and habitat suitability under multiple environmental stressors, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome current computational limitations. The research focuses on three interconnected challenges: (1) simulating fine-scale species-environment interactions across heterogeneous landscapes, (2) integrating genomic data to assess adaptive potential in climate-vulnerable species, and (3) evaluating the efficacy of proposed management interventions under diverse climate scenarios. Computational methods will combine agent-based models (ABMs) with machine learning approaches to analyze movement patterns, resource use, and genetic connectivity using multi-terabyte datasets from GPS collars, environmental sensors, and whole-genome sequencing. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of ensemble climate projections (CMIP6) at 1km resolution, nested within regional hydrological models to assess surface water availability for aquatic species. Expected outcomes include the identification of climate-resilient habitat corridors, genomic markers associated with thermal tolerance in keystone species, and decision-support tools for prioritizing restoration efforts. By quantifying trade-offs between conservation actions under uncertainty, this work will provide actionable strategies for maintaining biodiversity in managed wildlands and protected areas. The scale of spatiotemporal data integration and the need for real-time parameter optimization in adaptive management scenarios exceed the capabilities of local computing infrastructure, necessitating dedicated HPC allocation. This project directly supports the program’s mission to advance evidence-based wildlands management while training students in computational ecology techniques.
cip_title: Wildlife, Fish and Wildlands Science and Management
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to conserve and manage wilderness areas and the flora, marine and aquatic life therein, and manage wildlife reservations and zoological/aquarium facilities for recreational, commercial, and ecological purposes. Includes instruction in wildlife biology, marine/aquatic biology, environmental science, freshwater and saltwater ecosystems, natural resources management and policy, outdoor recreation and parks management, the design and operation of natural and artificial wildlife habitats, applicable law and regulations, and related administrative and communications skills.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of personalized rehabilitation protocols through computational modeling of human movement biomechanics. A critical challenge in exercise science and therapeutic rehabilitation lies in predicting how individual variations in anatomy, neuromuscular control, and tissue properties influence movement outcomes. Current approaches often rely on generic biomechanical models or limited experimental data, which fail to capture the complexity of inter-individual differences, leading to suboptimal rehabilitation strategies. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating subject-specific musculoskeletal modeling, motor control simulations, and machine learning to predict functional recovery trajectories under varying therapeutic interventions. High-resolution biomechanical models will be generated from clinical motion capture, electromyography, and medical imaging data, while motor control strategies will be simulated using reinforcement learning algorithms optimized for neuromuscular coordination. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational demands of (1) large-scale parameter sweeps evaluating rehabilitation scenarios across diverse patient populations, (2) finite element analysis of soft tissue mechanics during dynamic movements, and (3) training deep neural networks to identify biomarkers of rehabilitation efficacy. Expected outcomes include a validated computational platform for optimizing patient-specific exercise prescriptions and assistive device designs, with direct applications in post-stroke rehabilitation and osteoarthritis management. The project will also yield open-source tools for movement analysis, enhancing reproducibility in kinesiology research. By bridging computational biomechanics and clinical practice, this work aims to establish a paradigm shift toward data-driven, individualized rehabilitation, reducing trial-and-error in therapy design while advancing computational methods for human movement science.
cip_definition: A scientific program that focuses on the anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, and biophysics of human movement, and applications to exercise and therapeutic rehabilitation. Includes instruction in biomechanics, motor behavior, motor development and coordination, motor neurophysiology, performance research, rehabilitative therapies, the development of diagnostic and rehabilitative methods and equipment, and related analytical methods and procedures in applied exercise and therapeutic rehabilitation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop data-driven, adaptive interventions for K–12 students with emotional disturbances (ED) by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex interactions between behavioral, academic, and environmental factors. Students with ED often exhibit dynamic, context-sensitive behaviors that challenge traditional linear intervention frameworks. Current approaches struggle to predict how individualized education plan (IEP) strategies perform across diverse classroom settings, limiting educators’ ability to proactively adjust support. To address this, we propose a computational study integrating machine learning (ML) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate student-environment interactions at scale. Using anonymized longitudinal data from 15 school districts—including behavioral logs, academic performance metrics, and IEP records—we will train ensemble ML models to identify predictors of intervention success. Parallelized ABM simulations will then test how these predictors interact with variable classroom conditions (e.g., peer dynamics, educator ratios). HPC resources are critical for processing multimodal datasets (∼50 TB) and iteratively running 10,000+ simulations with varying parameters. Outcomes will include (1) a validated framework for predicting intervention efficacy under real-world constraints, (2) adaptive decision-support tools for educators to tailor strategies in response to behavioral shifts, and (3) open-source simulation modules for teacher training programs. By quantifying nonlinear relationships between interventions and student outcomes, this work aims to advance precision education for students with ED while reducing the trial-and-error burden on teachers. The scalability of our computational approach will also enable future expansion to underrepresented ED subtypes and rural educational contexts with limited clinical resources.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Emotional Disturbances
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with emotional conditions which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with emotional disturbances, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising individuals with emotional disturbances, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: Modern power plant operations require increasingly sophisticated computational tools to address challenges in efficiency optimization, emissions reduction, and system reliability under dynamic operating conditions. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to model coupled thermofluid processes in fossil fuel-based power generation systems, with a focus on optimizing flue gas desulfurization (FGD) scrubber performance. Current industry models rely on simplified assumptions that inadequately capture multiphase flow dynamics, chemical reaction kinetics, and particulate interactions at scale, limiting predictive accuracy for pollution control systems. To address this gap, we propose large-scale simulations using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) coupled with discrete element methods (DEM) to resolve turbulent gas-liquid-solid interactions within industrial-scale scrubbers. The research will employ finite volume discretization of Navier-Stokes equations with reactive transport, enhanced by machine learning techniques to accelerate parameter space exploration for operational optimization. High-performance computing resources are essential to handle the computational domain's spatial resolution (exceeding 100 million grid cells) and temporal scales spanning milliseconds to operational hours. Anticipated outcomes include validated predictive models for sulfur dioxide capture efficiency under variable load conditions, identification of optimal reagent injection strategies, and quantitative analysis of fouling mitigation approaches. These results will directly inform retrofit strategies for aging power infrastructure while supporting compliance with tightening emissions regulations. The developed computational framework will be adaptable to other pollution control systems and contribute open-source tools for multiphysics simulation in power plant technology. By integrating HPC-driven insights with operational data analytics, this work advances the engineering technologies required for sustainable power generation infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in the operation and maintenance of electricity generating power plants. Includes instruction in basic electricity, electrical power, generator operations, industrial controls, power plant instrumentation, power plant theory, pollution control, reactor theory, thermodynamics, turbines, and water chemistry.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize administrative workflows in veterinary practices through the integration of natural language processing (NLP) and predictive analytics. Veterinary administrative professionals face unique challenges in managing high-volume, heterogeneous data—including medical records, client communications, regulatory documentation, and scheduling logistics—while adhering to strict ethical and operational standards. Existing tools often lack domain-specific customization, leading to inefficiencies in data retrieval, communication tracking, and resource coordination. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train and deploy machine learning models tailored to veterinary administrative contexts. Key objectives include automating the categorization of veterinary medical correspondence using NLP models fine-tuned on domain-specific terminology, predicting scheduling conflicts through temporal network analysis of clinic operations, and simulating resource allocation scenarios under variable caseload conditions. The computational pipeline will process anonymized historical datasets from partnering veterinary clinics, encompassing 10M+ structured and unstructured data points. HPC infrastructure is critical for scaling transformer-based NLP architectures, conducting parallelized Monte Carlo simulations of clinic workflows, and iteratively optimizing ensemble models for decision support. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source toolkit for veterinary administrative staff, capable of reducing task completion times by 20-30% in pilot studies, while maintaining compliance with veterinary data privacy regulations. By merging computational scalability with domain-specific administrative needs, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for intelligent workflow management in veterinary practice, with potential applications in allied health administration fields.
cip_title: Veterinary Administrative/ Executive Assistant and Veterinary Secretary
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform the duties of special assistants and personal secretaries for practicing veterinarians, veterinary health care facilities and services administrators, and other veterinary professionals. Includes instruction in business and veterinary communications, veterinary terminology, principles of veterinary health care operations, public relations and interpersonal communications, software applications, record-keeping and filing systems, scheduling and meeting planning, applicable policy and regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of biological systems necessitates advanced computational tools to model dynamic, multi-scale interactions that underlie cellular processes. This project seeks to develop a scalable, machine learning-integrated framework for predicting context-dependent protein interaction networks, a challenge limited by current methods that often neglect temporal and environmental heterogeneity. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate molecular dynamics simulations with graph neural networks (GNNs) to model how protein interactions evolve under varying metabolic and signaling conditions. The computational pipeline will first simulate atomic-level protein dynamics using enhanced sampling techniques, generating time-resolved structural ensembles. These data will train a GNN architecture to predict interaction propensities across diverse cellular contexts, incorporating multi-omics inputs (e.g., transcriptomic and proteomic profiles) as conditional variables. Key innovations include adaptive graph attention mechanisms to prioritize biophysically relevant interactions and a transfer learning strategy to generalize across cell types. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing the iterative simulation-training cycle, which requires parallel processing of >10,000 GPU-hours for molecular dynamics datasets and distributed training of high-parameter GNNs. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible repository of context-aware interaction predictions for 200+ human proteins implicated in dysregulated signaling pathways, (2) validation of network rewiring events in cancer cell models via collaboration with experimental groups, and (3) open-source software for community-driven extension of the framework. This work will advance computational biology by bridging gaps between structural bioinformatics and systems biology, providing a paradigm for modeling adaptive molecular networks. The resource allocation will directly support scalability to genome-scale analyses, enabling future applications in personalized therapeutic targeting.
detailed_field: Bioinformatics, biostatistics, and computational biology nec
cip_title: Biomathematics, Bioinformatics, and Computational Biology, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in biomathematics, bioinformatics, and computational biology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance applied psychology research on optimizing workplace mental health interventions in high-stress industries. Despite evidence supporting organizational well-being programs, scalable implementation remains challenging due to variability in employee needs, intervention timing, and contextual factors. Current statistical models lack the capacity to handle dynamic, multilevel datasets (e.g., longitudinal employee surveys, productivity metrics, and real-time biometric data) that capture the interplay between individual psychological states and organizational outcomes. To address this, we propose developing agent-based computational models (ABMs) simulating employee behavior and intervention effects under diverse workplace conditions. These models will integrate empirical data from a 12-month organizational study (N = 2,500 employees) with existing psychological frameworks on stress, resilience, and team dynamics. HPC resources are critical for running large-scale parameter sweeps and sensitivity analyses to identify intervention configurations that maximize effectiveness across heterogeneous subgroups. Parallelized Monte Carlo methods will assess robustness under stochastic variations, while machine learning pipelines will analyze emergent patterns in intervention outcomes. Expected outcomes include actionable guidelines for adaptive, personalized mental health support systems in workplace settings, as well as open-source computational tools for applied psychologists to model complex human behavior in organizational contexts. This work bridges gaps between psychological theory and practical implementation, offering a scalable framework to evaluate interventions before real-world deployment. By utilizing HPC capabilities, the project aims to advance methodological innovation in applied psychology, ensuring solutions are both empirically grounded and computationally tractable for stakeholders in industry and public health.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of psychological theories and methods to real-world settings and problems, such as business and industry, government, education, military, and community settings. Includes instruction in applications of psychology, industrial/organizational psychology, developmental psychology, social psychology, cognitive psychology, counseling, human factors, research methods and statistics, and program evaluation.

abstract: This research project seeks to optimize real-time decision-making in customer service support operations through advanced computational modeling of dynamic interaction networks. Call centers and teleservice environments face persistent challenges in balancing service quality, operational efficiency, and workforce constraints, particularly as customer expectations evolve toward hyper-personalized, omnichannel support. Traditional queuing theory and discrete event simulation approaches struggle to account for the complex interdependencies between heterogeneous customer profiles, agent skill matrices, multi-platform communication flows, and real-time sentiment dynamics. The proposed work will develop an adaptive neural architecture combining graph neural networks (GNNs) with reinforcement learning to model emergent patterns in large-scale customer-agent interaction systems. High-performance computing resources are required to process historical interaction datasets encompassing 2.5 million voice and digital customer service transcripts, train multi-modal models integrating linguistic, paralinguistic, and operational telemetry, and simulate system behavior under variable demand scenarios. The computational framework will incorporate transformer-based natural language processing to analyze unstructured dialog data, coupled with temporal graph convolutions to capture time-dependent service process flows. Expected outcomes include predictive models for service outcome optimization, real-time recommendation systems for adaptive resource allocation, and sensitivity analyses identifying critical leverage points in customer journey workflows. By bridging computational social science techniques with operational analytics, this research aims to advance the design of next-generation customer service systems capable of maintaining service integrity during demand surges while reducing average handling time. The resulting methodologies could inform both technological infrastructure investments and workforce training paradigms in the $350 billion global contact center industry.
cip_title: Customer Service Support/ Call Center/ Teleservice Operation
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist customers with inquiries and problems in frontline call centers, help desks, teleservice centers, and online. Includes instruction in user interfaces and user behavior, principles of hardware and software systems operation, customer interaction skills, telephone and e-mailing skills, data entry, and database and Internet searching and retrieval.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework for analyzing complex, interdependent risks in multi-line insurance portfolios, with a focus on improving dynamic risk modeling under evolving economic and environmental conditions. Traditional actuarial models often rely on simplifying assumptions to handle computational constraints, limiting their ability to capture nonlinear dependencies, high-dimensional interactions, and real-time data streams. The proposed research will address these gaps by implementing parallelized Monte Carlo simulations, adaptive machine learning algorithms, and stochastic optimization techniques to model cascading risks in large portfolios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the iterative optimization of risk transfer strategies across millions of simulated scenarios, particularly when integrating climate projections, claims histories, and macroeconomic indicators at scale. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated libraries for deep reinforcement learning to identify robust hedging policies, while distributed computing frameworks will enable sensitivity analyses across heterogeneous risk factors. Expected outcomes include a novel open-source toolkit for granular risk aggregation, capable of quantifying tail dependencies and systemic risk spillovers in real time. This work will directly inform the design of next-generation insurance products, including parametric triggers for climate-related perils and capital allocation frameworks for cyber risk portfolios. By overcoming current limitations in computational actuarial methods, the project aims to advance risk-informed decision-making for insurers operating in volatile environments, with potential applications in regulatory stress testing and enterprise risk management. The requested HPC resources will support benchmarking against industry-standard models, validation using terabyte-scale claims datasets, and the publication of reproducible case studies demonstrating scalability gains over conventional actuarial software.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the mathematical and statistical analysis of risk, and their applications to insurance and other business management problems. Includes instruction in forecasting theory, quantitative and non-quantitative risk measurement methodologies, development of risk tables, secondary data analysis, and computer-assisted research methods.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance generative design methodologies in architectural sciences, focusing on the integration of cultural heritage data with adaptive spatial planning. Traditional generative design tools often prioritize structural efficiency or environmental performance metrics but lack frameworks to systematically incorporate intangible cultural narratives, localized socio-historical contexts, or community-driven spatial preferences. This gap limits the ability of architects and urban planners to create culturally resonant, adaptive environments in rapidly urbanizing regions. The research proposes a computational pipeline combining graph neural networks (GNNs) and transformer-based models to analyze heterogeneous datasets—including historical archives, geospatial patterns, and participatory community inputs—and generate design alternatives that balance technical feasibility with cultural continuity. Key computational challenges include scaling multi-modal data fusion (3D scans, textual records, and ethnographic surveys) and optimizing iterative design evaluations across hybrid CPU-GPU architectures. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized training of deep learning models on terabyte-scale datasets, real-time simulation of design scenarios under dynamic socio-environmental constraints, and sensitivity analyses to identify critical cultural variables influencing spatial outcomes. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational framework for culturally informed generative design, validated through case studies in heritage-sensitive urban redevelopment zones. This work aims to establish a new paradigm in architectural technology, bridging computational efficiency with ethnographic rigor, while contributing scalable methods for interdisciplinary research intersecting machine learning, cultural preservation, and spatial design. The requested resources will directly support high-fidelity simulations, reduce latency in multi-objective optimization tasks, and facilitate knowledge transfer to practitioners in regions lacking access to advanced computational tools.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in architectural sciences and technology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize diagnostic and repair workflows for complex computer hardware systems, with a focus on improving the efficiency and reliability of fault detection in high-performance computing (HPC) environments. As modern computing systems grow in scale and heterogeneity—integrating multi-core processors, GPUs, and specialized accelerators—traditional diagnostic tools often fail to account for dynamic thermal, electrical, and mechanical interactions between components. This limitation leads to prolonged downtime, misdiagnoses, and suboptimal repair outcomes. To address this gap, we propose a two-phase computational approach. First, we will train machine learning models on synthetic and real-world datasets of hardware failure signatures, including thermal profiles, voltage fluctuations, and error logs, to predict component degradation and pinpoint faults. Second, we will simulate stress-test scenarios using finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to model heat dissipation, power delivery stability, and physical wear under varying workloads. These simulations will inform hardware design modifications and repair protocols to mitigate failure risks. The project requires access to HPC resources to handle large-scale parallel processing for training deep neural networks on multi-terabyte datasets and running high-fidelity physical simulations. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source diagnostic toolkit for technicians to prioritize repair tasks based on predictive analytics, (2) validated guidelines for optimizing cooling and power supply configurations in heterogeneous systems, and (3) a curated repository of simulation data to enhance training materials for computer repair education. By bridging computational modeling with applied hardware maintenance, this work aims to reduce operational costs for HPC facilities while advancing pedagogical resources in computer repair technology.
cip_title: Computer Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair computers and related instruments. Includes instruction in power supplies, number systems, memory structure, buffers and registers, microprocessor design, peripheral equipment, programming, and networking.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and evaluate computational models to enhance pedagogical strategies for technology education, specifically in industrial arts contexts. A critical challenge in preparing future technology educators is the limited availability of data-driven methods to simulate and optimize hands-on technical skill instruction across diverse classroom environments. Traditional approaches often rely on static lesson plans that inadequately address variable student skill progression, safety considerations in technical tasks, and adaptive integration of emerging manufacturing technologies. To address this gap, we propose creating a high-fidelity simulation framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model dynamic technology classrooms. The framework will integrate multi-agent systems to represent student interactions with tools and materials, coupled with physics-based simulations of workshop environments. Machine learning algorithms will analyze historical student performance data to predict skill acquisition bottlenecks and recommend personalized instructional adjustments. By parallelizing simulations of classroom scenarios across varying student cohorts and technical domains (e.g., woodworking, digital fabrication), the HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration of teaching strategies while maintaining safety constraints. Expected outcomes include validated models for optimizing equipment allocation, time management in project-based learning, and adaptive assessment protocols for technical competencies. This research will directly inform the development of a decision-support tool for teacher candidates in industrial arts programs, providing evidence-based strategies to balance hands-on instruction with evolving technological demands. The computational framework and resulting datasets will be disseminated through open educational resources tailored for technology education programs, potentially impacting curriculum design in over 200 accredited industrial arts teacher preparation programs nationally.
cip_title: Technology Teacher Education/ Industrial Arts Teacher Education
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach technology education/industrial arts programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize institutional foodservice operations through advanced computational modeling of dynamic supply chain and labor allocation challenges, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address inefficiencies in real-time decision-making. Traditional foodservice management relies on static models ill-equipped to handle fluctuating demand, perishable inventory constraints, and staff scheduling variables in institutional settings such as hospitals, universities, and correctional facilities. The research problem centers on developing a scalable simulation framework to model complex interactions between procurement workflows, nutritional compliance, waste reduction targets, and workforce productivity—a gap exacerbated by the absence of integrated computational tools tailored to non-commercial food systems. The computational approach combines discrete-event simulation, agent-based modeling, and machine learning algorithms to process multi-source operational data, including historical meal demand patterns, real-time IoT sensor inputs from storage facilities, and staff performance metrics. HPC resources will enable parallelized scenario testing across diverse institutional profiles (e.g., varying bed counts in hospitals or academic calendars in universities) while maintaining sub-hourly temporal resolution for 12-month operational cycles. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system capable of predicting optimal vendor order thresholds, dynamically adjusting prep schedules to minimize waste, and balancing temporary staffing needs against overtime costs. Validation will utilize anonymized data from a multi-state hospital network, with model accuracy benchmarks targeting ≥15% reduction in perishable stockouts and 20% improvement in labor-hour utilization compared to current industry standards. By formalizing computational strategies for these understudied operational intersections, this work aims to establish scalable best practices for resource-constrained institutional foodservices while advancing methodological innovation in non-STEM applied systems analytics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and practices relating to the administration of food service systems in institutional settings, and that prepares individuals to manage such operations in public and private facilities. Includes instruction in human nutrition, food safety, the design and organization of food service systems, purchasing, personnel management, and related business practices.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern electrical and electronic systems necessitates advanced diagnostic and predictive maintenance strategies to minimize equipment downtime and repair costs. Current methodologies in electrical/electronics equipment repair often rely on reactive troubleshooting or static maintenance schedules, which are inefficient for dynamic, interconnected systems. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to simulate failure modes, optimize diagnostic protocols, and predict maintenance needs for industrial and consumer electrical equipment. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will model multi-physics interactions within electrical circuits, electromechanical components, and environmental stressors (e.g., thermal cycling, vibration) using finite element analysis (FEA) and time-domain circuit simulations. Machine learning models will be trained on synthetic and experimental datasets to correlate sensor data with degradation patterns. The computational workflow will integrate parametric sweeps across component tolerances, load conditions, and failure thresholds to establish robust fault-detection algorithms. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin platform for equipment health monitoring and a decision-support tool for technicians prioritizing repair tasks. By enabling granular simulation of transient electrical behaviors and wear mechanisms at scale, this work addresses critical gaps in predictive maintenance capabilities for aging infrastructure. The HPC environment is essential to manage the computational burden of parallelized simulations spanning thousands of operational scenarios, which would otherwise be intractable on local hardware. Successful implementation will provide actionable insights for optimizing repair workflows, reducing energy waste from inefficient equipment, and informing curriculum updates in technician training programs. Resource allocation will directly support the generation of open-access simulation templates and benchmarking datasets tailored to common repair challenges in power distribution, motor control, and embedded systems.
cip_title: Electrical/ Electronics Equipment Installation and Repair Technology/ Technician, General
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to operate, maintain, and repair electrical and electronic equipment. Includes instruction in electrical circuitry, simple gearing, linkages and lubrication of machines and appliances, and the use of testing equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in somatic psychology by analyzing complex, multimodal datasets capturing the interplay between physiological, behavioral, and psychological states during body-mind interventions. While somatic practices such as yoga, Tai Chi, and authentic movement are increasingly integrated into therapeutic contexts, their mechanisms of action remain understudied due to the dynamic, nonlinear interactions between bodily movements, autonomic responses, and emotional-cognitive shifts. Traditional analytical methods struggle to model these high-dimensional, time-sensitive processes, limiting the scalability and precision of evidence-based protocols. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework combining machine learning (ML), dynamical systems modeling, and network analysis to identify patterns predictive of therapeutic outcomes. Wearable biometric data (e.g., heart rate variability, electrodermal activity, motion capture) and self-reported affective states will be collected from 300 participants engaged in structured somatic interventions. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, training of deep learning models to classify intervention-specific physiological signatures, and simulation of body-mind feedback loops using coupled oscillator models. Agent-based modeling will further explore how individual somatic experiences scale to group dynamics in therapeutic settings. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a validated ML pipeline for predicting optimal somatic interventions based on baseline client profiles, (2) mechanistic insights into how specific movement practices modulate stress response networks, and (3) open-source tools for clinicians to quantitatively assess client progress. By bridging embodied therapeutic practices with computational rigor, this work aims to establish somatic psychology as a data-informed discipline within counseling and applied psychology, fostering personalized, culturally responsive interventions for trauma, anxiety, and relational challenges.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on a holistic approach to solving interpersonal issues and psychological problems. Includes instruction in authentic movement, body-mind balance and integration, contact improvisation, dance, Pilates, Tai Chi, relaxation techniques, and Yoga.

abstract: This project proposes the development of an adaptive, AI-driven simulation environment to optimize training protocols for teaching assistants (TAs) in large-scale, heterogeneous classroom settings. While TAs play a critical role in bridging instructional gaps, existing training frameworks lack personalized, data-driven approaches to address the dynamic challenges of diverse student populations and hybrid learning modalities. The research problem centers on creating computational models that predict TA-student interaction outcomes, identify skill gaps in real-time pedagogical support, and generate scenario-based training modules tailored to individual TA strengths and classroom needs. Using high-performance computing resources, we will implement a multimodal machine learning pipeline integrating natural language processing (NLP) of student-TA dialogue, computer vision analysis of classroom engagement metrics, and reinforcement learning to simulate decision-making pathways. Datasets will include de-identified video recordings from STEM discussion sections, anonymized student performance metrics, and TA feedback logs across 50+ courses. The computational workflow involves training transformer-based models on interaction patterns, clustering TA intervention strategies, and validating simulations against ground-truthed observational studies. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for generating TA competency profiles, predictive analytics tools for instructors to allocate TA resources efficiently, and evidence-based guidelines for adaptive training in emerging educational technologies. This work occupies a novel niche at the intersection of educational psychology, human-computer interaction, and computational pedagogy, offering scalable solutions to enhance equity in academic support systems without overlapping with traditional teacher education domains. The requested HPC resources are critical for processing multimodal data streams, running parallelized simulations of classroom scenarios, and iterating deep learning architectures to accommodate ethical AI constraints in educational contexts.
cip_definition: Any teaching assistant/aide program, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational tools to address the challenges of creating scalable, high-fidelity digital illustrations that integrate dynamic data sources and real-time interactivity. Traditional illustration workflows often struggle to adapt to scenarios requiring rapid iteration, such as interactive children’s books, augmented reality (AR) visualizations, or data-driven editorial graphics. The research problem centers on overcoming the computational bottlenecks in rendering complex, multi-layered visual narratives that respond to user input or live data streams. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to simulate and optimize these processes, particularly for projects involving large-scale datasets, physics-based simulations of artistic media (e.g., watercolor diffusion, ink dispersion), or AI-driven style transfer across thousands of frames. The computational approach combines procedural generation algorithms, neural networks trained on artistic style corpora, and GPU-accelerated rendering pipelines. For example, one proposed method involves using generative adversarial networks (GANs) to automate texture synthesis for background elements in storyboard illustrations, reducing manual labor while preserving artistic intent. Another focus area is real-time collaboration tools for distributed illustration teams, requiring low-latency synchronization of high-resolution assets. The project will leverage HPC clusters to parallelize tasks such as batch processing of 3D model textures, training domain-specific AI models on historical illustration datasets, and stress-testing interactive platforms under simulated user loads. Expected outcomes include open-source software plugins for popular illustration tools, optimized workflows for data-intensive projects, and case studies demonstrating reduced production timelines for complex commissions. By bridging computational efficiency with artistic nuance, this work aims to expand the scope of illustration as a medium for responsive, adaptive storytelling in education, journalism, and entertainment, while establishing best practices for integrating HPC resources into creative disciplines.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to use artistic techniques to develop and execute interpretations of the concepts of authors and designers to specifications. Includes instruction in book illustration, fashion illustration, map illustration, rendering, exhibit preparation, textual layout, cartooning, and the use of various artistic techniques as requested by clients.

abstract: The rapid growth of global air traffic, coupled with increasing demands for operational efficiency and environmental sustainability, necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize air transportation systems. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity simulation framework for analyzing and improving air traffic flow management (ATFM) under dynamic weather disruptions and airspace capacity constraints. Current ATFM models struggle to integrate real-time weather data, stochastic demand patterns, and multi-objective optimization at scale, leading to suboptimal decisions that propagate delays and increase fuel consumption. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo simulations, and deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithms. The framework will simulate network-wide aircraft movements at 1-second resolution across 24-hour operational windows, incorporating live weather radar inputs and probabilistic passenger demand forecasts. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training DRL agents on historical flight data spanning 10 million+ records, running parallelized scenario analyses for continental-scale airspaces, and solving mixed-integer linear programming problems for slot allocation. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support system capable of reducing average delay propagation by 15-20% and curbing CO2 emissions through improved trajectory optimization. The research will also generate open-source datasets of simulated air traffic scenarios under varying disruption levels, supporting broader academic investigations into resilient aviation infrastructure. By leveraging GPU-accelerated computing and distributed memory architectures, this project aims to advance the computational frontiers of air transportation research while addressing critical industry challenges in capacity management and environmental performance.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in aviation and air transportation services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to enhance the predictive modeling and operational planning capabilities of protective services through advanced computational simulations of dynamic threat scenarios. Protective operations in high-risk environments—such as executive protection, critical infrastructure security, and event crowd control—require real-time decision-making under uncertainty, yet current planning tools often rely on static risk assessments or generalized protocols. To address this gap, the research will develop agent-based models (ABMs) and machine learning (ML) frameworks to simulate adversarial behavior, environmental variables, and protective team responses at scale. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to iteratively test thousands of scenario permutations, incorporating real-world datasets on historical security incidents, geospatial layouts, and crowd dynamics. Key computational challenges include optimizing parallelized simulations of multi-agent interactions, integrating heterogeneous data streams (e.g., sensor feeds, threat intelligence), and training ML classifiers to identify emergent threat patterns from sparse or noisy inputs. The project will validate models against case studies from protective operations training exercises, with sensitivity analyses to quantify the impact of variables such as team size, communication latency, and adversarial adaptability. Expected outcomes include a modular simulation toolkit for operational planners, enabling proactive identification of vulnerabilities in protection strategies and adaptive resource allocation under constrained conditions. By bridging computational modeling and operational security practices, this work aims to establish a foundation for data-driven protective tactics while addressing ethical and legal implications of predictive analytics in physical security contexts. The requested HPC resources will support GPU-accelerated ML training and large-scale ABM ensembles, which are infeasible on local infrastructure due to memory and processing constraints.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles and techniques of providing physical security protection to clients in various environments and situations. Includes instruction in security intelligence and information resources, operations planning and surveying, operations security, weapons and explosives, defense and offense techniques, security and surveillance systems, communications systems, perimeter and access control, weapons of mass destruction, contingency planning, crowd control, cover and evacuation, combat and vehicle techniques, and applicable legal and administrative responsibilities.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the development of predictive models for optimizing in-situ recovery processes in unconventional hydrocarbon reservoirs, a critical challenge in petroleum engineering technologies. Current methods for simulating multiphase fluid flow and heat transfer in fractured shale or tight sandstone formations are limited by oversimplified geomechanical assumptions and computational inefficiencies, leading to unreliable predictions of extraction efficiency. To address this, we propose a high-fidelity computational framework integrating discrete fracture network (DFN) modeling with coupled thermo-hydro-mechanical (THM) simulations. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement parallelized finite element-discrete element hybrid algorithms capable of resolving microscale fracture propagation dynamics alongside reservoir-scale fluid transport.
