Key computational challenges include managing adaptive mesh refinement for evolving fracture geometries and solving nonlinear multiphysics interactions across 10^6+ grid cells. The proposed work will validate models against field data from instrumented test wells, incorporating distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) measurements to constrain fracture behavior. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation toolkit for predicting production rates under varying operational parameters (e.g., injection pressures, proppant concentrations) and geological uncertainties. This research will directly support the development of more sustainable extraction protocols by enabling precise identification of optimal recovery strategies while minimizing environmental footprint. The required HPC resources will facilitate parameter sensitivity studies at unprecedented spatial resolutions (sub-meter scale) across kilometer-scale reservoir domains, reducing reliance on costly physical trials. Successful implementation promises to bridge critical gaps between theoretical multiphysics models and practical engineering solutions for unconventional resource development.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in mining and petroleum engineering technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Complications in obstetrics and gynecological conditions, such as preterm birth, preeclampsia, and ovarian cancer, present significant clinical challenges due to their heterogeneous etiologies and variable patient outcomes. Current risk stratification tools lack the precision to account for complex interactions between genetic, epigenetic, and environmental factors, limiting their utility in personalized care. This project proposes to address these gaps by developing predictive computational models that integrate multi-modal data, including whole-genome sequencing, placental transcriptomics, longitudinal electronic health records, and dynamic imaging biomarkers. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage and analyze large-scale datasets from multi-center cohorts, including over 30,000 pregnancies and 5,000 gynecologic oncology cases. Machine learning frameworks, such as graph neural networks and ensemble methods, will be implemented to identify subtype-specific risk profiles and predict adverse outcomes. For placental insufficiency studies, spatially resolved transcriptomic data will be analyzed using GPU-accelerated image segmentation and tensor decomposition to map molecular gradients associated with hypoxia. In parallel, molecular dynamics simulations will model protein interactions in ovarian cancer chemoresistance pathways, requiring petascale computing for free energy calculations. Expected outcomes include validated algorithms for early detection of preterm labor, biomarkers for preeclampsia progression, and mechanistic insights into tumor microenvironment adaptation. These tools will be disseminated as open-source packages to enable replication in diverse populations. The project’s computational demands—including terabyte-scale data storage, parallelized processing of 3D imaging datasets, and iterative model training—necessitate dedicated HPC allocation to achieve clinically actionable timelines. By bridging clinical obstetrics and computational innovation, this work aims to advance precision medicine frameworks that reduce disparities in maternal and gynecologic healthcare outcomes.
cip_definition: Research focused on Obstetrics and Gynecology

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of systemic inequities in family law adjudication, specifically examining how algorithmic tools and large-scale data analysis can uncover patterns in judicial decision-making across child custody, elder guardianship, and domestic violence protection orders. While family law operates within established legal frameworks, the integration of computational methods remains underdeveloped compared to other legal domains. The research problem centers on the lack of granular, longitudinal datasets and analytical tools capable of modeling how intersecting factors—such as socioeconomic status, geographic location, and implicit judicial bias—influence case outcomes over time. Using a mixed-methods approach, we will apply natural language processing (NLP) to anonymized court records (spanning 2010–2023 from six U.S. states) and develop machine learning models to identify predictors of disproportionate outcomes for marginalized groups. Computational workloads will focus on entity recognition in unstructured legal texts, temporal network analysis of precedent citations, and agent-based modeling of policy intervention scenarios. The scale of data (estimated at 12TB of text and metadata) and the need for real-time simulation of multi-variable legal ecosystems necessitate HPC infrastructure for parallel processing and GPU-accelerated model training. Expected outcomes include 1) a novel taxonomy of bias indicators in family law proceedings, 2) predictive frameworks for evaluating proposed legislative reforms, and 3) open-source tools enabling courts to audit decision patterns using privacy-preserving federated learning techniques. By bridging computational social science and legal informatics, this work aims to establish reproducible methodologies for equity analysis in non-quantitative legal domains while addressing critical gaps in access to justice research. The requested resources will directly support the creation of the first large-scale computational model bank specific to lifespan family law outcomes, with implications for judicial training, policy design, and AI governance in public-sector legal systems.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting domestic relations across the lifespan.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize resource allocation and scalability strategies for education ventures in diverse socioeconomic contexts. A critical challenge in education entrepreneurship is predicting how innovations—such as new learning technologies, alternative school models, or community education programs—will perform when scaled across regions with varying economic constraints, policy environments, and demographic needs. Existing decision-making tools often rely on static cost-benefit analyses, which fail to capture dynamic interactions between market forces, stakeholder behaviors, and systemic inequities. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) approach simulating how education ventures interact with complex adaptive systems, including funding networks, regulatory landscapes, and community adoption patterns. The model will integrate real-world datasets on regional education expenditures, philanthropic investment trends, student mobility, and labor market outcomes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to run thousands of parameterized simulations that account for uncertainty in policy shifts, demographic changes, and economic volatility. Parallel computing will enable sensitivity analyses to identify leverage points for improving financial sustainability and equitable impact. Machine learning components will further analyze simulation outputs to recommend adaptive business strategies under constrained resources. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible decision-support tool for education entrepreneurs and policymakers, validated through case studies of existing ventures. This work will advance human-centered design in education innovation by quantifying risks and opportunities in scaling context-sensitive solutions. The computational framework will also contribute novel methods to the field of education leadership by bridging systems thinking, econometrics, and venture design—ultimately supporting data-driven strategies to maximize the reach and efficacy of educational innovations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to create, fund, and manage innovations in education. Includes instruction in philanthropy, business modeling, the design of learning environments, the economics of education, entrepreneurship, evaluation, finance, human-centered design, investing, resource management, project management, and marketing.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced simulation frameworks for optimizing next-generation power electronics systems, which face critical challenges in efficiency, thermal management, and reliability under high-power, variable-load conditions. Current design methodologies struggle to model the tightly coupled electrical, thermal, and electromagnetic behaviors of wide-bandgap semiconductor devices (e.g., SiC, GaN) in real-time operational scenarios, limiting their adoption in renewable energy integration and industrial electrification. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled multi-physics approach combining finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning-driven optimization. The computational workflow will simulate transient device-electrothermal interactions at microsecond timescales while resolving millimeter-scale spatial variations in heat distribution and electromagnetic fields. Parallelized solvers will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes to handle large parameter spaces spanning material properties, switching frequencies, and cooling configurations. Machine learning surrogate models will then identify Pareto-optimal designs balancing efficiency, thermal stability, and cost. The HPC resources will enable parametric sweeps across 10,000+ simulation instances, which would be computationally intractable on local clusters. Expected outcomes include validated models for 1.2 kV SiC-based converters operating at >98% efficiency, predictive thermal management strategies for 500+ kW industrial drives, and an open-source toolchain for power electronics co-design. These results will directly support the development of sustainable energy infrastructure and high-efficiency electrification technologies, aligning with national priorities for grid modernization and decarbonization. The resource request targets 200,000 node-hours on GPU-equipped clusters to accommodate the multi-scale, multi-physics nature of the simulations over an 18-month research period.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in electrical and electronic engineering-related technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale computational analysis of syntactic and morphological variation across understudied Germanic language varieties, particularly focusing on Frisian, Low German, and regional dialects of Dutch. While these languages hold critical insights into historical language contact and divergence within the Germanic family, their structural complexity and dialectal diversity pose challenges for traditional manual analysis. The research problem centers on quantifying patterns of variation in verb-second (V2) word order and case marking erosion—phenomena pivotal to understanding syntactic change—across digitized corpora comprising historical texts, modern speech transcripts, and elicited production data. Computational methods will include automated dependency parsing using transformer-based models (e.g., BERT) fine-tuned for non-standardized orthographies, coupled with phylogenetic algorithms to model diachronic relationships. HPC resources are essential for training these models on heterogeneous data (≈10 TB), running parallelized simulations of syntactic change, and processing high-dimensional linguistic features via cluster analysis. Expected outcomes include (1) a typological map of V2 constraints across microvarieties, clarifying the interplay between language contact and internal innovation, and (2) an open-access database of annotated syntactic structures, enabling future comparative research. By integrating computational linguistics with philological expertise, this work will provide novel methodologies for analyzing non-standardized languages while addressing theoretical debates about the uniformity and divergence of Germanic syntax. The scalability of the approach also lays groundwork for applications to other lesser-resourced language families within the humanities.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Germanic Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in Germanic languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational tools to enhance pedagogical strategies in drama and dance education by analyzing the biomechanical and expressive qualities of student performance. While traditional teacher training emphasizes qualitative assessment of movement and expression, current methods lack scalable frameworks for quantifying progress or personalizing feedback. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process large-scale motion-capture datasets and simulate dynamic teaching environments. The research will focus on two interconnected objectives: (1) creating machine learning models to classify movement patterns and correlate them with skill development stages in dance, and (2) generating 3D simulations of classroom scenarios to model how varying instructional approaches impact student engagement in drama exercises. Motion data will be collected from student teachers and their pupils during rehearsals, using inertial measurement units (IMUs) and optical tracking systems. These datasets will train convolutional neural networks to identify technical proficiency and expressive nuance, while agent-based modeling will simulate peer interactions during improvisational theater activities. The computational demands of processing high-frequency kinematic data (sampled at 200Hz) and rendering real-time, multi-agent virtual environments necessitate parallelized GPU computing and distributed memory architectures. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for drama and dance educators to visualize student progress metrics, predict learning bottlenecks, and test instructional interventions in silico. By bridging performing arts pedagogy with computational analytics, this work aims to establish evidence-based practices for training teachers in embodied art forms, ultimately improving how movement-based creativity is taught across K-12 and higher education settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach drama and/or dance programs at various educational levels.

abstract: The increasing demand for safe and effective blood products, coupled with the complexity of donor-recipient immunological compatibility, presents critical challenges in transfusion medicine. Current blood bank protocols rely on serological testing and antigen matching, but these methods struggle to predict rare alloimmunization events or fully account for the dynamic biochemical changes in stored blood products. This project seeks to develop a computational framework integrating multi-omics data from stored red blood cell (RBC) units with immunological compatibility modeling to optimize transfusion outcomes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale datasets encompassing metabolomic profiles, RBC membrane proteomics, and donor-recipient human leukocyte antigen (HLA)/KIR genotype pairs, which collectively influence post-transfusion hemolysis and adverse immune responses. Machine learning models will be trained on retrospective clinical data to identify biomarkers of RBC storage lesion severity and predict alloimmunization risks in diverse patient populations. Concurrently, molecular dynamics simulations will model antigen-antibody interactions under varying storage conditions to refine compatibility assessments. The computational pipeline will also incorporate real-time sensor data from smart blood storage devices to dynamically adjust shelf-life predictions. Expected outcomes include a predictive tool for personalized blood product selection, validated against prospective clinical cohorts, and a novel risk stratification system for transfusion-related complications. This work bridges gaps in hematology, immunology, and computational biology, offering a data-driven approach to enhance blood bank operations while addressing unmet needs in precision transfusion medicine. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project aims to reduce discard rates of expired units, mitigate adverse transfusion reactions, and establish scalable protocols for emerging cellular therapy products requiring similar storage and compatibility frameworks.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform routine and specialized blood testing procedures, collect and process blood donations, and support physicians and other clinicians administering transfusion therapy. Includes instruction in basic cellular biology, immunohematology, blood bank procedures, blood typing, antigen and antibody identification tests, hemolytic and transfusion responses and diseases, donor selection, blood drawing and storage, blood separation, viral marker testing, laboratory and personnel supervision, safety and sterilization, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: Pediatric liver transplantation remains a critical intervention for children with end-stage liver disease, yet significant challenges persist in predicting graft survival, optimizing immunosuppression, and mitigating post-transplant complications. Current clinical models lack the granularity to integrate multi-dimensional data—including dynamic immune profiles, metabolomic fluctuations, and longitudinal clinical variables—that underlie heterogeneous outcomes in pediatric patients. This project proposes a computational approach to bridge this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models of graft rejection and immune tolerance. We will analyze multi-omic datasets (genomic, proteomic, metabolomic) from a longitudinal cohort of 500 pediatric liver transplant recipients, alongside high-resolution clinical data from electronic health records, including immunosuppression pharmacokinetics, infection episodes, and graft function metrics. Machine learning frameworks, such as ensemble neural networks and Bayesian hierarchical models, will be employed to identify biomarkers of early rejection and predictors of long-term tolerance. These models will be iteratively trained and validated using HPC-enabled parallel processing to manage the computational intensity of large-scale data integration and hyperparameter optimization. Additionally, agent-based simulations of alloreactive immune responses will explore mechanistic drivers of graft injury under varying immunosuppressive regimens. The anticipated outcomes include (1) a validated risk stratification tool for personalized post-transplant monitoring, (2) dynamic biomarkers to guide immunosuppression tapering, and (3) mechanistic insights into pediatric-specific immune tolerance pathways. By synthesizing complex biological and clinical data, this work aims to reduce rejection rates, minimize drug toxicity, and improve quality of life for pediatric transplant recipients. The HPC infrastructure is essential to handle the terabyte-scale datasets, computationally demanding algorithms, and iterative simulations required to achieve clinically actionable results within a translational research timeline.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians with special knowledge, skill, and expertise required of pediatric gastroenterologists to care for children and young adults prior to and following hepatic transplantation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in real-time legal transcription and captioning, an interdisciplinary niche within court reporting that intersects computational linguistics, accessibility technology, and judicial workflow optimization. Current court reporting systems face limitations in processing speed, accuracy, and adaptability when handling complex legal terminology, overlapping speech, or low-quality audio inputs, particularly in high-stakes environments such as multi-accents, multilingual proceedings, or remote testimony scenarios. The research problem centers on developing a scalable computational framework to enhance real-time transcription fidelity while maintaining compliance with legal standards for verbatim accuracy. The proposed approach combines machine learning models for domain-specific speech recognition (trained on legal corpora) with natural language processing (NLP) techniques to contextualize utterances within procedural norms, statutory language, and case-specific glossaries. HPC resources will enable parallelized training of neural networks on heterogeneous datasets—including historical court transcripts, simulated audio distortions, and synthetic edge cases—to improve robustness against acoustic variability and dialect diversity. Additionally, real-time inference pipelines will be optimized using GPU-accelerated architectures to reduce latency below human perception thresholds (≤100ms). Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adaptive legal transcription, validated against certified court reporter benchmarks, and a public dataset of annotated legal proceedings to support future research. The project’s significance lies in its potential to democratize access to accurate captioning in underserved jurisdictions, reduce cognitive load for human reporters, and establish computational best practices for ethical AI integration in legally sensitive contexts. By bridging gaps between linguistic precision, computational efficiency, and judicial integrity, this work aims to set a precedent for emerging technologies in non-STEM disciplines that prioritize equitable access to justice.
cip_title: Court Reporting and Captioning/ Court Reporter
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to record and transcribe examinations, testimony, judicial orders and instructions, legal opinions, and other formal proceedings via print or electronic methods. Includes instruction in legal terminology, legal transcription, shorthand, verbatim recording, equipment operation and procedures, applicable regulations, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of precision manufacturing in tool and die applications demands advanced computational methods to optimize tool design, material behavior, and process parameters. Traditional trial-and-error approaches for developing dies, jigs, and fixtures are time-consuming, costly, and insufficient for modern high-tolerance components, particularly when working with advanced alloys or complex geometries. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation framework to model multi-stage metal forming processes, including thermal, mechanical, and microstructural interactions. The research will focus on two core challenges: (1) predicting springback and residual stresses in stamped components through coupled finite element analysis (FEA) and (2) optimizing die surface treatments to mitigate wear under high-cycle forging conditions. Computational workflows will integrate physics-based simulations with machine learning algorithms to identify correlations between tool geometry, material properties, and process variables. Large-scale parametric studies will be conducted using HPC resources to resolve micron-scale features in die cavities and simulate multi-pass forming operations with adaptive remeshing. Expected outcomes include predictive models for tool life estimation, data-driven recommendations for process parameter optimization, and open-access datasets of simulated forming scenarios tailored to common tool and die applications. By reducing physical prototyping iterations by an estimated 40–60%, this work aims to lower production costs and energy consumption while improving part consistency in small-batch manufacturing. The computational framework will also serve as an educational resource for training tool and die technicians in simulation-driven design, bridging gaps between traditional craftsmanship and digital manufacturing methodologies. Successful implementation will demonstrate the transformative potential of HPC in advancing precision metalworking technologies, with direct relevance to aerospace, automotive, and medical device industries reliant on high-performance tooling systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to operate machine tools used in the forming of metal components, as well as the fabrication of special tools, dies, jigs and fixtures used in cutting, working and finishing metal components.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on real-time public sentiment analysis and crisis communication modeling in the context of digital media environments. Public relations professionals increasingly face challenges in managing organizational reputations amid the rapid dissemination of information—and misinformation—across social platforms, yet existing tools for monitoring and predicting stakeholder responses remain limited in scalability and temporal resolution. The research problem centers on developing dynamic, data-driven models to simulate public perception shifts during crises, optimize message timing/content, and mitigate reputational risks. Computational methods will integrate natural language processing (NLP) for large-scale social media text analysis, network analysis to map stakeholder interactions, and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate information diffusion patterns under varying scenarios. These approaches require processing terabytes of unstructured text, video metadata, and user engagement metrics, necessitating parallelized computing architectures for training deep learning models (e.g., transformer-based classifiers) and running iterative simulations. Expected outcomes include (1) a framework for predictive analytics in crisis communication, enabling organizations to proactively adjust messaging strategies based on simulated public reactions, and (2) open-source tools for real-time sentiment tracking across multilingual platforms. By employing HPC resources, the project aims to overcome latency and scalability barriers inherent in traditional sentiment analysis software, providing granular insights into how microtargeted content influences stakeholder trust. This work will directly inform curriculum development in image management and offer empirical evidence for optimizing resource allocation in PR campaigns. The computational infrastructure will also support student-led research initiatives on algorithmic bias in communication tools, aligning with the program’s focus on ethical media engagement.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theories and methods for managing the media image of a business, organization, or individual and the communication process with stakeholders, constituencies, audiences, and the general public; and that prepares individuals to function as public relations assistants, technicians, and managers. Includes instruction in public relations theory; related principles of advertising, marketing, and journalism; message/image design; image management; special event management; media relations; community relations; public affairs; and internal communications.

abstract: The increasing prevalence of complex dermatological conditions in companion and livestock animals—including immune-mediated disorders, antibiotic-resistant infections, and environmentally triggered allergies—demands advanced computational approaches to improve diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic outcomes. Current methods for analyzing heterogeneous datasets (e.g., genomic, metagenomic, histopathological imaging, and longitudinal clinical records) remain siloed, limiting insights into disease mechanisms and personalized treatment strategies. This project proposes to integrate multi-modal data using high-performance computing (HPC) to model host-microbe interactions, predict treatment responses, and identify biomarkers for early disease detection. A central focus is developing machine learning (ML) frameworks to analyze high-resolution 3D skin lesion reconstructions from veterinary confocal microscopy and optical coherence tomography, coupled with shotgun metagenomic sequencing of cutaneous microbiomes. These datasets, often exceeding terabytes per patient, require distributed computing for real-time processing and iterative model training. Agent-based simulations will further explore immune cell dynamics in allergic dermatitis, leveraging GPU-accelerated parameter sweeps to model cytokine cascades and therapeutic interventions. Computational pipelines will be validated against retrospective clinical data from 1,200 canine, feline, and equine cases, with prospective testing in partnership with three veterinary dermatology clinics. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models linking microbiome dysbiosis to treatment-resistant pyoderma, (2) automated tools for quantifying epidermal barrier defects in histopathology images, and (3) open-source software for simulating topical drug permeation across species-specific skin architectures. By harnessing HPC resources, this work aims to bridge translational gaps in veterinary dermatology, enabling data-driven decision support systems that improve animal welfare and reduce reliance on empirical therapies. All code and anonymized datasets will be shared via public repositories to foster collaboration in comparative dermatology research.
cip_definition: Research focused on the delivery of specialized care to animals with diseases of the skin, scales, feathers, hair, nails and mucous membranes. May included related research in dermatologic surgical procedures, cutaneous allergies, and diagnostic and therapeutic techniques.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern computational systems necessitates the integration of computer science and engineering principles to address challenges in scalability, efficiency, and real-time processing. This project seeks to develop a novel framework for optimizing heterogeneous computing architectures—spanning CPUs, GPUs, and specialized accelerators—to support next-generation machine learning (ML) workloads with stringent latency and energy constraints. A key research problem lies in dynamically balancing computational resources across diverse hardware components while maintaining model accuracy and minimizing power consumption. Current static resource allocation strategies fail to adapt to variable workloads, leading to inefficiencies that limit scalability in applications such as autonomous systems and real-time data analytics. To address this, we propose a hybrid approach combining reinforcement learning (RL)-based schedulers with fine-grained performance modeling. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate large-scale distributed systems, train RL agents on multi-node clusters, and validate models against benchmarks spanning computer vision, natural language processing, and sensor networks. Computational methods will include parallelized Monte Carlo tree search for policy optimization, hardware-accelerated discrete-event simulations, and energy profiling via FPGA emulation. Expected outcomes include an open-source resource management toolkit capable of autonomously tuning hardware-software configurations for domain-specific tasks, reducing energy use by an estimated 30–50% compared to state-of-the-art schedulers. This work will advance interdisciplinary research in edge computing and adaptive systems, providing methodologies to bridge the gap between theoretical ML advances and practical engineering constraints. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling the project’s massive hyperparameter search space and simulating heterogeneous architectures at scale.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of computer science and computer engineering principles or a specialization which includes expertise in both computer engineering and computer science.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing the integrity and scalability of blockchain-based carbon accounting systems, an emerging interdisciplinary niche at the intersection of sustainability reporting, cryptographic verification, and regulatory compliance. Traditional carbon accounting methods face challenges in data transparency, auditability, and real-time reconciliation across global supply chains. While blockchain technology offers potential solutions through distributed ledger systems, there remains a critical gap in understanding how such systems perform under the complex, high-volume transactional environments typical of multinational enterprises. The research will employ agent-based modeling to simulate supply chain networks with varying geographic, regulatory, and operational constraints, coupled with cryptographic proof-of-concept validations for emission data verification. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute large-scale simulations that mirror real-world conditions, including 10,000+ node networks, probabilistic fraud scenarios, and multi-jurisdictional compliance rule sets. Parallel computing architectures will be leveraged to optimize consensus algorithm efficiency analyses, while machine learning methods will identify patterns in simulated emissions data that may indicate systemic reporting inaccuracies or manipulation. Expected outcomes include 1) performance benchmarks for blockchain implementations in carbon accounting contexts, 2) a taxonomy of failure modes in decentralized verification systems, and 3) open-source tools for auditing computational trust mechanisms in sustainability reports. This work addresses urgent needs in both corporate accountability and climate finance by providing empirically grounded insights into next-generation accounting infrastructures, with direct implications for ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance) reporting standards and carbon credit market design.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in accounting, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address the complex challenge of optimizing interdisciplinary synchronization in musical theatre productions. While the integration of live vocal performance, choreography, and technical staging is central to the art form, the dynamic interplay between these elements remains poorly quantified, limiting data-driven approaches to rehearsal planning, creative iteration, and pedagogical refinement. Our research will develop computational models to analyze and simulate multi-modal performance data, including synchronized motion capture (mocap) from choreography, high-resolution acoustic profiles of vocal performances, and real-time stage technical cues. Key computational challenges include processing terabytes of mocap and audio-visual data, training machine learning models to identify patterns in performer coordination, and simulating audience sightline-acoustic interactions across virtual venue geometries. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of ensemble kinematic data, GPU-accelerated acoustic propagation modeling, and large-scale parameter sweeps to evaluate staging configurations. Expected outcomes include: (1) predictive tools for identifying synchronization bottlenecks in complex choreography-vocal sequences, (2) a framework for simulating audience perceptual experiences under different staging conditions, and (3) open-source datasets linking biomechanical, acoustic, and technical theatre parameters. This work will provide the first quantitative methodology for evaluating integrative musical theatre performance at scale, with applications to curriculum development, virtual rehearsal systems, and accessibility-focused staging adaptations. By bridging computational analysis with performing arts praxis, the project aims to establish new standards for evidence-based creative decision-making in musical theatre production and education.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and techniques for integrating theatre, music, and dance into a unified production. Includes instruction in acting, dance, voice, technical theater, musical genres, piano, and history of musical theater.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational text analysis of Jewish philosophical and religious manuscripts, with a focus on tracing the evolution of hermeneutical and ethical frameworks across diasporic contexts. The central research problem lies in the fragmented and multilingual nature of Jewish textual traditions, which span Hebrew, Aramaic, Judeo-Arabic, and other languages, often embedded in commentaries spanning centuries. Traditional close-reading methods struggle to systematically analyze conceptual shifts, intertextual dependencies, or geographic-cultural variations at scale. Our computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques optimized for Semitic languages, including transformer-based models fine-tuned on rabbinic corpora, to map philosophical argumentation structures, semantic networks, and citation patterns across digitized manuscripts. Key datasets include the Bar-Ilan Responsa Project, the Sefaria Library, and newly digitized Kabbalistic works from the 13th–18th centuries. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel processing of these texts, training multilingual embeddings to detect latent theological or ethical concepts, and network analysis of intellectual influence across temporal and spatial axes (e.g., comparing Sephardic and Ashkenazi interpretive traditions). Expected outcomes include (1) identification of previously unrecognized doctrinal synergies or tensions between philosophical schools, (2) quantitative models of how legal-ethical reasoning adapted to diaspora conditions, and (3) an open-access computational toolkit for Jewish textual analysis. This work will provide novel insights into Judaism’s intellectual adaptability while demonstrating how HPC can address enduring challenges in religious studies, such as analyzing multilayered commentary traditions or reconciling normative texts with lived ethical practice. The project bridges computational humanities and Judaic studies, offering methodological frameworks applicable to other religious traditions with complex textual histories.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, culture, and religion of the Jewish people. Includes instruction in Jewish religious heritage, sacred texts, and law; Jewish philosophy and intellectual history; Jewish life and culture, both in Israel and the Jewish Diaspora; historical Jewish minority cultures such as the Yiddish, Sephardic, and other; anti-Semitism, gentile relations and Shoa; Zionism; and modern developments within Judaism.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern computational problems in applied mathematics demands innovative algorithms capable of leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) architectures efficiently. This project seeks to address scalability challenges in solving large-scale, sparse linear systems arising from discretized partial differential equations (PDEs), which are foundational to simulations in fluid dynamics, materials science, and multiscale modeling. Traditional iterative solvers, such as preconditioned Krylov subspace methods, often struggle with convergence and parallel efficiency when applied to ill-conditioned systems with millions of degrees of freedom. To overcome these limitations, we propose developing a hybrid algorithmic framework combining adaptive multigrid techniques with matrix-free operator approximations and asynchronous communication protocols optimized for distributed-memory systems. The computational approach will integrate numerical analysis, combinatorial graph partitioning for load balancing, and runtime system adaptations to minimize synchronization overhead. Key innovations include the design of a data-aware preconditioner that dynamically adjusts to local matrix structures and a fault-tolerant iterative scheme for exascale environments. The project will validate these methods using HPC clusters to solve 3D elliptic boundary-value problems and coupled advection-diffusion systems, benchmarking against state-of-the-art libraries like PETSc and Trilinos. Expected outcomes include a 30–50% reduction in time-to-solution for target problem classes, quantified scalability analyses up to 10,000 cores, and open-source software modules for the computational mathematics community. This work will advance the integration of numerical theory with modern HPC practices, enabling more efficient simulations in engineering and scientific domains reliant on PDE-based modeling. The requested resources are essential for profiling memory-bandwidth constraints, optimizing communication patterns, and testing robustness across heterogeneous architectures.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of mathematics to the theory, architecture, and design of computers, computational techniques, and algorithms. Includes instruction in computer theory, cybernetics, numerical analysis, algorithm development, binary structures, combinatorics, advanced statistics, and related topics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cross-cultural environmental decision-making in marginalized communities using an interdisciplinary framework that integrates computational social science, environmental anthropology, and complex systems modeling. The research problem centers on understanding how non-linear interactions between localized ecological knowledge, socio-political constraints, and climate change impacts shape adaptive strategies in underserved regions—a phenomenon that resists analysis through singular disciplinary lenses. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to develop agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate decision-making processes across multiple temporal and spatial scales, informed by ethnographic fieldwork data from three case study regions (Southeast Asia, East Africa, and the Arctic). Computational challenges include processing heterogeneous datasets (qualitative narratives, ecological surveys, climate projections) through natural language processing pipelines and spatial network analyses, followed by parameterization of ABMs to test hypotheses about resilience thresholds. The models will incorporate machine learning techniques to identify emergent patterns in adaptive behavior under varying climate scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) a novel computational framework for analyzing socio-ecological systems across disciplinary boundaries, (2) evidence-based insights into leverage points for equitable climate adaptation policies, and (3) open-source tools for culturally grounded resilience assessments. This work requires HPC resources to manage the combinatorial complexity of modeling 10^4–10^5 agents with heterogeneous belief systems, real-world climate data assimilation at 1km resolution, and Monte Carlo simulations across parameter spaces. Results will advance methodological integration in interdisciplinary studies while addressing urgent questions about environmental justice in the climate crisis.
cip_definition: A program that derives from two or more distinct programs and that is integrated around a unifying theme or topic that cannot be subsumed under a single discipline or occupational field.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in the evolution of Greek linguistic and literary traditions across three critical phases: Classical Attic, Koine (Hellenistic/Biblical), and Medieval Byzantine Greek. A central challenge in philological studies of this scope is the analysis of syntactic, morphological, and lexical patterns across vast, chronologically dispersed corpora—a task hindered by the limitations of manual methods and conventional computing tools. By applying computational linguistics and machine learning techniques to digitized texts spanning over 1,500 years, this project aims to systematically map linguistic shifts, dialectal variations, and stylistic innovations, while identifying previously undetected intertextual relationships between secular and theological works. The computational pipeline includes preprocessing and aligning texts from heterogeneous sources (e.g., papyri, codices, inscriptions), training transformer-based models for context-aware semantic analysis, and deploying graph algorithms to model syntactic changes. HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of textual data, optimize neural networks for low-resource historical languages, and run parallelized simulations of linguistic diffusion across regions and eras. Expected outcomes include an open-access database of annotated texts with linked metadata, a suite of tools for automated dialect classification and dating of fragmentary works, and quantitative models tracing the influence of Classical rhetoric on Byzantine theological literature. This interdisciplinary approach bridges traditional philology with data-driven methodologies, offering new frameworks for understanding Greek as a dynamic, continuous literary tradition. Results will support scholarly efforts to reconstruct damaged manuscripts, refine chronologies of anonymous texts, and illuminate the sociocultural factors shaping language change in the ancient Mediterranean and Byzantine worlds.
cip_title: Ancient/ Classical Greek Language and Literature
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Greek language and literature from its origins through the fall of the Byzantine (Eastern Roman) Empire, as a secular and/or theological subject. Includes instruction in philology, Attic and Hellenistic dialects, Koine (Biblical) Greek, and Medieval or Byzantine Greek.

abstract: Animal nutrition research faces a critical challenge in understanding the complex interactions between dietary components, host metabolism, and gut microbiota, which collectively influence nutrient utilization, animal health, and environmental sustainability. Current models struggle to predict outcomes across diverse species, diets, and physiological states due to the high dimensionality of metabolic networks and the nonlinear dynamics of microbial communities. This project proposes to develop a multi-scale computational framework integrating metagenomic, metabolomic, and physiological data to simulate nutrient-microbiome-host interactions in ruminants and monogastric livestock. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize genome-scale metabolic models of microbial consortia, optimize dynamic systems models of nutrient absorption, and apply machine learning to identify feed formulations that maximize nutrient efficiency while minimizing greenhouse gas emissions. The computational workflow will leverage existing datasets from in vivo trials and generate new simulations to explore nutrient partitioning under varying dietary regimes. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms linking specific feed additives (e.g., enzymes, prebiotics) to microbiome resilience and host metabolic responses, as well as decision-support tools for precision feeding strategies. By elucidating mechanisms driving variability in nutrient use efficiency, this work will advance fundamental knowledge in animal biochemistry while addressing urgent agricultural needs: reducing feed costs, improving livestock productivity, and mitigating environmental impacts of animal production. The requested HPC allocation will enable large-scale parallel simulations, Bayesian inference for model calibration, and high-throughput analysis of multi-omics data, which are computationally prohibitive on local clusters.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the biology and chemistry of proteins, fats, carbohydrates, water, vitamins, and feed additives as related to animal health and the production of improved animal products. Includes instruction in nutrition science, animal health and physiology, biochemistry, cellular and molecular biology, animal husbandry, and food science.

abstract: Pediatric hematologic and oncologic malignancies present unique challenges due to their molecular heterogeneity, developmental context, and the critical need for therapies that minimize long-term toxicity. While advances in genomic profiling have identified potential therapeutic targets, translating these findings into clinically actionable strategies remains limited by the complexity of tumor-stroma interactions, dynamic treatment resistance mechanisms, and the lack of predictive models tailored to pediatric biology. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address these gaps through multi-scale computational modeling. We propose integrating single-cell RNA sequencing data from 500+ pediatric leukemia and solid tumor samples (collated from multi-institutional cohorts and public repositories) with spatially resolved proteomic profiles and longitudinal clinical outcomes. Custom algorithms will map clonal evolution patterns under therapy pressure using Bayesian phylogenetic inference and stochastic differential equations, optimized for parallel processing. Molecular dynamics simulations of high-priority mutated proteins (e.g., ALK, RAS isoforms) will predict conformation-specific drug binding affinities, requiring GPU-accelerated sampling of >10^6 conformational states. Machine learning models trained on these datasets will identify microenvironmental signatures predictive of relapse risk, validated against in vitro organoid co-culture experiments. The computational workflow will utilize containerized pipelines for reproducibility, with an estimated need for 1.2 million CPU-core hours and 200 TB of temporary storage to manage intermediate outputs. Anticipated outcomes include the identification of resistance-associated stromal crosstalk pathways, prioritized drug candidates for high-risk subgroups, and a predictive framework for personalizing consolidation therapy intensity. By elucidating context-specific vulnerability networks, this work aims to accelerate the development of precision strategies that improve survival while reducing late effects in pediatric patients. The generated models and datasets will be shared via a FAIR-compliant portal to foster collaborative innovation in the field.
cip_definition: Research focused on Pediatric Hematology-Oncology

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the dynamic interplay between cultural practices and animal welfare outcomes across human societies, a critical but underexplored nexus in anthrozoology. While prior studies have examined localized human-animal relationships, scalable computational frameworks are lacking for modeling how culturally mediated behaviors—such as ritualistic practices, agricultural methods, or urban development patterns—impact animal populations, welfare metrics, and conservation efforts. Our research integrates ethnographic datasets, historical records, and ecological surveys to construct agent-based models (ABMs) simulating bidirectional interactions between human communities and animal systems under varying sociocultural scenarios. These models incorporate spatial, temporal, and behavioral variables, including animal sentience proxies, human ethical frameworks, and resource allocation dynamics. HPC resources are essential to run parallelized, high-resolution simulations across diverse cultural contexts (e.g., Indigenous pastoralist societies, industrialized urban centers) while accounting for global stressors like climate change and habitat fragmentation. Machine learning pipelines will further identify emergent patterns in cross-cultural animal welfare trade-offs and resilience thresholds. Anticipated outcomes include predictive tools to optimize culturally sensitive conservation policies, ethical guidelines for interspecies coexistence, and a scalable computational platform for interdisciplinary anthrozoological research. By bridging anthropological nuance with zoological data at unprecedented granularity, this work advances a novel framework for understanding how human cultural evolution shapes—and is shaped by—multispecies interdependencies, offering actionable insights for global biodiversity challenges.
cip_definition: A program of study that combines anthropology and zoology in order to examine the relationship between animals and humans. Includes instruction in animal behavior and communication, animal welfare, animal conservation, animal training, animal-assisted therapy techniques, biology, ethics, and education.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address challenges in analyzing large-scale multimedia news datasets and simulating real-time broadcast journalism workflows. As digital news production grows in complexity—spanning live video streams, social media integration, and multi-platform content distribution—journalism programs require advanced tools to study evolving audience engagement patterns, ethical decision-making in dynamic reporting contexts, and the technical demands of modern newsroom systems. However, existing computational methods for processing audiovisual archives, natural language transcripts, and viewer interaction metadata remain fragmented and resource-limited. This research will develop parallelized workflows for 1) processing terabytes of broadcast footage using computer vision and speech recognition models to identify bias markers in visual framing and verbal narratives, 2) simulating information dissemination networks to model how breaking news propagates across hybrid media ecosystems, and 3) training transformer-based models on journalism ethics corpora to analyze real-time editorial choices during crisis reporting scenarios. The computational approach integrates GPU-accelerated media processing, graph-based network simulations, and NLP fine-tuning pipelines, requiring scalable storage and multi-node processing capabilities. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for journalism education that enables students to quantitatively assess ethical tensions in historical case studies, predict the societal impact of framing techniques, and optimize cross-platform news delivery strategies. By bridging computational social science methods with broadcast journalism practice, this work aims to establish reproducible standards for data-driven media analysis while preparing students to navigate the technical and ethical complexities of next-generation news environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the methods and techniques for reporting, producing, and delivering news and news programs via radio, television, and video/film media; and that prepares individuals to be professional broadcast journalists, editors, producers, directors, and managers. Includes instruction in the principles of broadcast technology; broadcast reporting; on- and off-camera and microphone procedures and techniques; program, sound, and video/film editing; program design and production; media law and policy; and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational literary analysis and generative text modeling within creative writing research. While traditional creative writing scholarship emphasizes close reading and qualitative critique, the proliferation of digitized texts and advances in natural language processing (NLP) present new opportunities to quantitatively analyze stylistic patterns, narrative structures, and linguistic innovation at scale. However, existing tools lack the capacity to process large literary corpora or model complex generative tasks, limiting their utility for rigorous creative research. Our work addresses this gap by developing machine learning pipelines to analyze 50,000+ contemporary short stories and novels, identifying latent stylistic signatures across genres and authors. Using transformer-based models fine-tuned on annotated literary datasets, we will computationally map rhetorical devices, syntactical trends, and semantic shifts in experimental fiction. Parallel GPU-accelerated workflows will enable generative experiments with neural storytelling architectures, simulating nonlinear narrative dynamics and reader-response patterns through agent-based modeling. These methods require HPC infrastructure to manage distributed training of large language models, iterative hyperparameter optimization, and real-time interaction with generative outputs during writer-researcher collaboration. Outcomes will include open-source tools for computational stylistics, a public corpus of analyzed texts with metadata, and a framework for integrating data-driven insights into creative practice. By bridging computational methods and humanistic inquiry, this project aims to expand critical discourse on literary innovation while equipping writers with empirically grounded strategies for narrative experimentation. The requested resources will directly support GPU-intensive tasks, including fine-tuning GPT-4 for genre-aware story generation and running multi-agent simulations of narrative coherence in interactive fiction. Results will be disseminated through workshops, a project repository, and peer-reviewed publications at the intersection of digital humanities and creative writing.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the process and techniques of original composition in various literary forms such as the short story, poetry, the novel, and others. Includes instruction in technical and editorial skills, criticism, and the marketing of finished manuscripts.

abstract: The maintenance of industrial machinery, such as pumps, conveyor systems, and turbines, faces persistent challenges due to unpredictable mechanical failures, leading to costly downtime and safety risks. Current predictive maintenance approaches often rely on oversimplified models or static thresholds, which fail to account for complex interactions between mechanical, thermal, and fluid dynamic stresses in real-world operating conditions. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-fidelity computational framework to simulate multi-physics interactions and predict failure modes in industrial equipment. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute large-scale finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations, capturing nonlinear wear patterns, vibration-induced fatigue, and thermal degradation under dynamic loads. These simulations will be integrated with machine learning models trained on operational sensor data to establish adaptive failure prediction algorithms. The computational workflow will require parallel processing capabilities to manage the high dimensionality of multi-physics datasets and the iterative optimization of predictive models. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin platform for industrial equipment that enables real-time health monitoring and probabilistic lifetime estimation. This resource will provide maintenance technicians with actionable insights to prioritize interventions, optimize spare parts logistics, and transition from schedule-based to condition-based maintenance paradigms. The project will also yield open-source tools for simulating wear processes in common industrial components, contributing to workforce training resources in predictive maintenance technologies. By reducing unplanned downtime and extending asset lifespans, this research aligns with industry priorities for operational efficiency and sustainability in manufacturing, energy, and transportation sectors.
cip_title: Industrial Mechanics and Maintenance Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair and maintain industrial machinery and equipment such as cranes, pumps, engines and motors, pneumatic tools, conveyor systems, production machinery, marine deck machinery, and steam propulsion, refinery, and pipeline-distribution systems.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable algorithms for real-time optimization of large-scale machine learning models deployed in distributed edge computing environments. Current deep learning architectures face critical inefficiencies when adapted to resource-constrained devices, including latency bottlenecks and excessive energy consumption during inference. These challenges stem from the inherent complexity of modern neural networks and the dynamic nature of edge computing workloads, which existing pruning and quantization methods fail to address robustly. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining adaptive model compression, hardware-aware neural architecture search (NAS), and federated learning techniques. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate heterogeneous edge networks with up to 10,000 nodes, train baseline models on multimodal datasets (including real-world IoT sensor streams and synthetic benchmarks), and iteratively optimize architectures using multi-objective evolutionary algorithms. Key computational demands include GPU-accelerated gradient computations for NAS, distributed parameter tuning via MPI-based parallelism, and large-scale hyperparameter optimization across competing objectives (accuracy, latency, memory footprint). Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly available benchmark suite for edge-focused model compression, (2) novel convergence guarantees for federated NAS protocols under non-IID data distributions, and (3) energy-efficient model templates demonstrating 40-60% latency reduction compared to existing MobileNet and EfficientNet baselines on ARM-based prototypes. By enabling sustainable deployment of complex AI models across decentralized systems, this work directly advances computational research in embedded machine learning while providing methodological foundations for resource-aware algorithm design. The requested allocation supports critical memory-intensive workloads that exceed local cluster capabilities, particularly large-scale device heterogeneity simulations and parallel NAS evaluations across multiple constraint profiles.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on computer theory, computing problems and solutions, and the design of computer systems and user interfaces from a scientific perspective. Includes instruction in the principles of computational science, computer development and programming, and applications to a variety of end-use situations.

abstract: The safe and efficient use of nuclear and industrial radiologic technologies relies on precise modeling of radiation interactions with materials and systems. Current challenges include optimizing radiation shielding designs, predicting material degradation under prolonged exposure, and improving real-time monitoring algorithms for complex environments. These problems demand high-fidelity simulations that account for multi-physics phenomena, such as coupled radiation transport, thermal effects, and structural deformation, which exceed the capabilities of standard computing resources. This project requests high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational methods for radiation-matter interaction studies. The research will employ Monte Carlo radiation transport simulations using Geant4 and MCNP frameworks, integrated with finite element analysis for thermo-mechanical modeling. Machine learning techniques will be applied to accelerate parameter optimization for shielding materials and automate anomaly detection in radiation sensor networks. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes for parallelized particle transport calculations and CPU clusters for coupled multiphysics simulations. Expected outcomes include validated models for predicting radiation-induced material behavior in next-generation nuclear reactors, optimized shielding configurations for industrial radiography devices, and AI-enhanced protocols for radiation safety monitoring. These results will directly support the development of safer, more efficient radiologic technologies in energy production, nondestructive testing, and medical applications. The project will also produce open-source tools to streamline radiation simulation workflows, fostering collaboration across the science-related technologies community. By addressing critical computational bottlenecks, this work aims to bridge gaps between theoretical models and real-world implementation in radiation-dependent industries.
cip_title: Nuclear and Industrial Radiologic Technologies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in nuclear and industrial radiologic technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the documentation and computational modeling of under-resourced Uralic languages, with a focus on Karelian and Sami dialects. The core challenge lies in the morphological complexity and dialectal diversity of these languages, which have limited digital corpora and require computationally intensive analysis to model phonological, syntactic, and semantic patterns effectively. Traditional methods struggle to process the agglutinative structures and non-standard orthographies inherent to these languages at scale, hindering efforts to preserve endangered dialects and analyze historical linguistic shifts. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational approach combining rule-based morphological parsers with transformer-based neural models (e.g., BERT variants), trained on newly digitized textual and oral corpora. These datasets include transcribed folklore narratives, modern community recordings, and legacy lexical databases, which require significant preprocessing via GPU-accelerated pipelines for normalization, tokenization, and alignment. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale comparative analyses across dialects, simulating phonetic change trajectories through phylogenetic algorithms, and generating probabilistic models of grammatical evolution. Expected outcomes include open-access tools for automated morphological disambiguation, a cross-dialectal similarity matrix to inform language revitalization strategies, and a publicly deployable API for real-time Sami-Karelian machine translation. By bridging computational linguistics with Uralic philology, this work aims to establish scalable methodologies for analyzing low-resource languages while contributing directly to community-led preservation initiatives. The requested resources are critical for handling memory-intensive tasks such as training multilingual embeddings on distributed clusters and processing terabytes of audio-data-derived spectrograms for prosodic analysis. Results will be disseminated through the Digital Uralic Atlas platform, providing both scholarly and public stakeholders with tools to engage critically with endangered linguistic heritage.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on Uralic languages, including, but not limited to, Finnish, Estonian, Karelian, and Sami. Includes instruction in philology; oral and written literatures; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Allergic, asthmatic, and immunologic diseases exhibit complex, heterogeneous pathophysiology driven by dynamic interactions between genetic, environmental, and immunological factors. Current treatment strategies often rely on generalized protocols, leaving subsets of patients with suboptimal outcomes due to interindividual variability in disease mechanisms and therapeutic responses. This project seeks to address this gap by developing computational models to predict patient-specific disease trajectories and optimize personalized treatment strategies. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale, multi-modal datasets, including longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs), multi-omics profiles (genomic, proteomic, transcriptomic), and real-time immunological biomarkers from 1,200 patients with severe asthma and comorbid immune dysregulation. Machine learning approaches—including ensemble classifiers and graph neural networks—will be applied to identify latent biomarkers of treatment resistance and disease progression. Agent-based modeling will simulate immune cell signaling pathways to map how specific genetic variants and environmental exposures synergistically drive pathological inflammation. These computational workflows require HPC capabilities due to the high dimensionality of the data (>50,000 features per patient), iterative model training across hyperparameter spaces, and the need for real-time integration of streaming biomarker data during clinical validation phases. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms to stratify patients by likely response to biologic therapies (e.g., anti-IL-5, anti-IgE), (2) mechanistic models linking specific T-cell receptor clonotypes to exacerbation risk, and (3) an open-source computational toolkit for simulating personalized immune responses to candidate therapies. By elucidating patient-specific disease drivers, this work aims to reduce trial-and-error prescribing, improve control of refractory symptoms, and provide a scalable framework for precision immunology. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage memory-intensive omics analyses, parallelize stochastic simulations, and deploy GPU-accelerated deep learning architectures within clinically actionable timeframes.
cip_definition: Research focused on the delivery of skilled medical care to patients suffering from allergic, asthmatic, and immunologic diseases. Requires completion of a prior residency program in internal medicine or pediatrics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the efficacy of culturally embedded spiritual narratives in pastoral counseling sessions using advanced computational text analysis, aiming to bridge gaps in empirical methodologies within specialized ministries. While pastoral counseling emphasizes holistic care, rigorous quantitative studies on the linguistic and narrative patterns that correlate with therapeutic outcomes remain scarce. This research will analyze a curated corpus of anonymized counseling session transcripts (n=10,000+) from diverse religious communities, employing natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques to identify latent semantic structures, emotional tone shifts, and narrative coherence markers. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing this large-scale textual dataset, enabling the training of transformer-based models (e.g., BERT variants fine-tuned on theological and psychological lexicons) to classify counselor interventions and client responses. Concurrently, network analysis will map the interplay between scriptural references, metaphor usage, and self-reported client resilience metrics. The project will validate findings through collaboration with practicing pastoral counselors, iteratively refining models to account for denominational and cultural nuances. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for evaluating narrative efficacy in spiritual care, open-source tools for real-time discourse analysis in counseling training, and empirically grounded insights into how faith-based narratives mediate psychological outcomes. By integrating computational linguistics with pastoral theology, this work addresses a critical gap in interdisciplinary humanities research, offering methodological innovations for both ministry practice and the digital humanities.
cip_title: Pastoral Counseling and Specialized Ministries, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in pastoral counseling and specialized ministries, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the efficacy of adaptive religious education curricula in multicultural, interfaith communities. While traditional religious pedagogy often relies on static, denomination-specific materials, growing demographic diversity and evolving theological dialogues demand dynamic frameworks that reconcile doctrinal fidelity with inclusive educational practices. The central research problem lies in modeling how hybrid curricula—integrating scriptural hermeneutics, sociocultural contextualization, and participatory learning—impact long-term faith formation across heterogeneous learner groups. To address this, the project employs a mixed-methods computational approach: natural language processing (NLP) will analyze semantic patterns in interdenominational educational texts, agent-based modeling (ABM) will simulate learner engagement under variable theological and cultural parameters, and network analysis will map knowledge transfer efficiency within digitally augmented religious communities. HPC resources are critical for processing multilingual corpora (sacred texts, lesson plans, and learner feedback), running large-scale ABM simulations with granular socioreligious variables, and training machine learning classifiers to predict curricular outcomes across divergent ethical and epistemological frameworks. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable digital toolkit for optimizing context-sensitive religious education design, validated through collaboration with interfaith organizations piloting adaptive curricula. This work contributes to understudied intersections of computational humanities, pedagogical innovation, and religious pluralism, offering methodological frameworks to address tensions between tradition and adaptation in faith-based education. By quantifying previously qualitative dynamics in religious learning, the project aims to establish benchmarks for equitable spiritual formation in increasingly complex socioreligious landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theory and practice of providing educational services to members of faith communities, within the context of a particular religion, and that prepares individuals to serve as religious educators. Includes instruction in planning and teaching lessons, organizing and supervising instructional activities, designing and developing instructional materials, and administering religious education programs and facilities.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize mineral extraction processes and enhance safety protocols in underground mining environments. A critical challenge in modern mining technology is the accurate prediction of subsurface geological conditions and their dynamic impacts on both operational efficiency and hazard mitigation. Traditional analytical methods struggle to integrate high-resolution geospatial data, real-time sensor inputs, and multiphysics interactions at the scale required for complex ore bodies. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement large-scale simulations of rock mechanics, fluid flow in fractured reservoirs, and stress redistribution during excavation. Finite element modeling (FEM) and discrete element method (DEM) frameworks will be parallelized to analyze 3D geological structures derived from LiDAR and borehole data, enabling probabilistic assessments of ore grade variability and stability risks. Additionally, machine learning algorithms will be trained on historical incident datasets to predict equipment failure modes and gas dispersion patterns in confined mine shafts. The computational workflows will require distributed memory architectures for stochastic modeling of heterogeneous rock masses and GPU acceleration for neural network training. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for optimizing drill-and-blast patterns, reducing energy consumption in mineral processing, and automating risk alerts for ground subsidence or ventilation failures. This work will directly support the development of adaptive mining strategies that balance productivity with worker safety, while providing a scalable computational framework for the industry’s transition toward data-driven decision-making. The requested HPC resources are essential to achieve the spatial and temporal resolutions necessary for actionable insights, advancing both academic research and practical applications in mineral resource management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the development and operation of mines and related mineral processing facilities. Includes instruction in principles of mineral extraction and related geology, mineral field mapping and site analysis, testing and sampling methods, instrument calibration, assay analysis, test equipment operation and maintenance, mine environment and safety monitoring procedures, mine inspection procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the diachronic and synchronic evolution of understudied Romance language varieties in the Iberian Peninsula, focusing on computational modeling of phonetic, syntactic, and lexical shifts influenced by sociolinguistic factors. While prior studies have analyzed major Romance languages like Spanish and Portuguese, lesser-documented varieties such as Aragonese, Asturian, and Mirandese remain underexplored due to fragmented datasets and the computational complexity of modeling cross-regional language contact. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze a multilingual corpus comprising digitized historical texts (13th–19th centuries), modern oral recordings, and dialectal surveys. Machine learning pipelines will be developed to train probabilistic models of sound change, identify syntactic borrowing patterns, and simulate language convergence scenarios under varying sociopolitical constraints. The computational workflow will integrate natural language processing (NLP) tools optimized for historical orthography, phonetic alignment algorithms for speech data, and graph-based networks to map contact-induced changes. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible database of annotated linguistic features, (2) quantitative models tracing the divergence of Iberian Romance varieties from shared Latin roots, and (3) frameworks to predict language vitality under demographic shifts.
