By bridging computational linguistics with philological scholarship, this work aims to advance understanding of language change mechanisms while providing methodological tools for endangered language documentation. The scale of data (≈50 TB of text/audio) and iterative model training necessitate HPC capabilities for parallel processing, large-memory nodes, and GPU-accelerated deep learning, which are unavailable in local departmental infrastructure.
cip_title: Romance Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in Romance languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of thermal and non-thermal food processing techniques, addressing critical challenges in nutrient retention, microbial safety, and energy efficiency. Traditional empirical methods for optimizing parameters such as heating time, pressure, and chemical treatment intensity are resource-intensive and limited in generalizability. To overcome these constraints, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to model interactions between food matrices, processing conditions, and microbial or enzymatic activity. MD simulations will elucidate atomic-scale interactions of heat-resistant enzymes and pathogens (e.g., *Bacillus cereus* spores) with food components under varying thermal and high-pressure processing regimes. CFD models will predict heat and mass transfer dynamics in heterogeneous food systems, while ML algorithms trained on these datasets will identify optimal processing parameters for diverse agricultural products. The HPC environment is essential for parallelizing large-scale simulations, managing terabytes of structural and spectral data from food component libraries, and iterating ML models. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to minimize nutrient degradation (e.g., lysine loss in baked goods) while ensuring microbial safety, reducing energy consumption by up to 30% compared to conventional methods. These results will directly inform scalable strategies for extending shelf life without synthetic additives, aligning with global demands for sustainable food processing. By bridging molecular-scale insights with industrial-scale applicability, this work will advance computational methodologies in food science and provide open-source models for the broader agricultural research community.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological, chemical, and physical principles to the study of converting raw agricultural products into processed forms suitable for direct human consumption, and the storage of such products. Includes instruction in applicable aspects of the agricultural sciences, human physiology and nutrition, food chemistry, agricultural products processing, food additives, food preparation and packaging, food storage and shipment, and related aspects of human health and safety including toxicology and pathology.

abstract: This project seeks to elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying voltage-gated ion channel dynamics, a critical component of cellular signaling and bioelectrical regulation. Despite extensive structural data, the precise conformational transitions that enable ion selectivity and gating remain poorly resolved due to the transient, large-scale motions involved. We propose an integrated computational approach combining all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with enhanced sampling techniques to map the free energy landscapes governing these transitions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate multi-microsecond trajectories of full-length ion channels embedded in lipid bilayers under physiological electric fields, capturing rare but functionally relevant states. System sizes will exceed 500,000 atoms, requiring GPU-accelerated MD codes (e.g., AMBER, NAMD) to achieve feasible timescales. Parallel tempering and metadynamics will be employed to overcome energy barriers, while machine learning-driven analysis will identify conserved allosteric networks from terabytes of trajectory data. Expected outcomes include (1) atomistic models of voltage-sensing domain cooperativity during activation, (2) quantitative predictions of how disease-associated mutations alter gating energetics, and (3) dynamic maps of lipid-protein interactions modulating channel function. These results will directly inform ongoing electrophysiology experiments in our lab, bridging molecular-scale simulations with macroscopic functional measurements. The computational workflows developed will be adaptable to other membrane protein systems, advancing broader efforts in structure-guided drug discovery. By resolving long-standing debates about coupling mechanisms in these essential biomolecules, this work will establish predictive frameworks for manipulating channel behavior—a cornerstone for developing therapies targeting cardiac arrhythmias, epilepsy, and channelopathies. The scale of conformational sampling and data generation necessitates dedicated HPC allocation to achieve statistically robust insights into these nanosecond-to-millisecond biophysical processes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of physics principles to the scientific study of the mechanisms of biological processes and assemblies at all levels of complexity. Includes instruction in research methods and equipment operation and applications to subjects such as bioenergetics, biophysical theory and modeling, electrophysics, membrane biology, channels, receptors and transporters, contractility and muscle function, protein shaping and folding, molecular and supramolecular structures and assemblies, and computational science.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize personalized fashion and fabric recommendations by integrating generative design, material simulation, and consumer behavior modeling—a novel interdisciplinary effort bridging computational aesthetics, textile physics, and human-computer interaction. The research addresses the challenge of delivering real-time, sustainable style solutions that balance individual preferences, fabric performance metrics, and environmental impact—a gap in current advisory systems that rely on static databases or qualitative heuristics. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we propose a hybrid architecture combining graph neural networks (to model style compatibility across 50+ cultural aesthetics) with discrete element method simulations (predicting drape, wear patterns, and durability across 10,000+ fabric blends). A parallelized multi-objective optimization layer will reconcile competing parameters including cost, carbon footprint, and client-specific body kinematics captured through motion-capture datasets. The computational intensity arises from iterative material simulations at micrometer resolutions and real-time rendering of 3D virtual try-ons across diverse demographic morphologies. Expected outcomes include: (1) an open-source fabric digital twin library correlating microstructure scans with mechanical properties, (2) a dynamic preference inference engine adapting to shifting sustainability regulations and cultural trends, and (3) GPU-accelerated APIs for boutique-scale customization systems. This work pioneers quantitative methods in computational stylistics, offering the fashion industry tools to reduce sample waste by 37% (projected via Monte Carlo simulations) while maintaining client satisfaction—a critical advancement as global apparel demand grows amid tightening ecological constraints. The resource request supports tera-scale fabric simulations, distributed hyperparameter tuning across style subspaces, and climate-specific degradation modeling through physics-informed ML.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to assist in apparel and fashion selection, style coordination, customer sales and consulting, fabric selection, clothing specifications, and contract buying activities. Includes instruction in supplying regular clothing needs or acting as a consultant for special events such as weddings.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive language learning tools for multilingual classrooms, addressing the critical challenge of personalizing English language instruction for learners with diverse linguistic and cultural backgrounds. A central problem in Teaching English as a Second Language (TESL) is the lack of scalable, data-driven methods to analyze real-time language acquisition patterns and optimize pedagogical interventions. Current approaches often rely on static curricula or manual instructor assessments, which struggle to accommodate the dynamic, heterogeneous needs of learners. To address this, we propose a computational framework combining natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) to model learner interactions, predict proficiency gaps, and generate tailored instructional recommendations. The project will process multimodal datasets—including transcribed speech, written assignments, and behavioral engagement metrics from ESL classrooms—to train neural network models that identify patterns in grammatical errors, pronunciation shifts, and vocabulary acquisition trajectories. HPC resources are essential for scaling these analyses across thousands of learner profiles, enabling parallel processing of high-dimensional linguistic data and iterative refinement of predictive models. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for ESL instructors, designed to automate formative assessments and suggest targeted teaching strategies aligned with individual learner needs. Additionally, the project will produce a corpus of annotated multilingual learner interactions, facilitating future research on cross-linguistic transfer in ESL contexts. By integrating computational linguistics with TESL pedagogy, this work aims to enhance the precision and inclusivity of language instruction while reducing the administrative burden on educators, ultimately supporting equitable outcomes for linguistically diverse student populations.
cip_title: Teaching English as a Second or Foreign Language/ ESL Language Instructor
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and practice of teaching English to students who are not proficient in English or who do not speak, read or write English, and that may prepare individuals to function as teachers and administrators in such programs.

abstract: Pediatric rehabilitation medicine faces significant challenges in predicting and optimizing treatment outcomes for children and young adults with congenital or childhood-onset physical impairments. Current clinical models often struggle to integrate heterogeneous data types—such as electronic health records (EHRs), neuroimaging, wearable sensor outputs, and psychosocial assessments—into unified frameworks for personalized care. This project proposes to address this gap by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled platform to model multifactorial interactions influencing functional outcomes. The research will focus on two core aims: (1) creating predictive algorithms to identify optimal rehabilitation pathways using longitudinal EHR data and motion-capture biomechanical datasets, and (2) simulating neurodevelopmental trajectories through whole-brain computational models derived from diffusion tensor imaging and functional MRI. Machine learning approaches, including graph neural networks and multimodal transformers, will be deployed to analyze temporal patterns in rehabilitation progress while accounting for individual variability in musculoskeletal development, cognitive profiles, and environmental factors. The computational workflow will require large-scale parallel processing for parameter optimization in patient-specific biomechanical simulations and Bayesian inference frameworks for treatment effect estimation. By leveraging GPU-accelerated computing clusters, the team will perform iterative analyses across multi-terabyte datasets encompassing >5,000 historical cases from collaborating children’s hospitals. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for gross motor function improvement in cerebral palsy cohorts and a computational toolset for simulating intervention impacts on neural plasticity. This resource-intensive approach aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven decision-making in pediatric rehabilitation, with potential to reduce trial-and-error treatment strategies while addressing critical gaps in understanding lifespan implications of childhood interventions. The resulting infrastructure will be shared as open-source modules to support reproducibility in rehabilitation science.
cip_definition: Research on how to use an interdisciplinary approach to prevent, diagnose, treat, and manage congenital and childhood-onset physical impairments in children and young adults, including related medical, physical, functional, psychosocial, and vocational limitations or conditions.

abstract: This project seeks to elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying allosteric regulation in a model multienzyme complex central to nucleotide biosynthesis, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome current limitations in simulating large, dynamic macromolecular assemblies. Despite extensive biochemical characterization, the structural dynamics driving long-range communication between catalytic and regulatory subunits remain poorly resolved. Traditional experimental techniques struggle to capture transient conformational states, while classical molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of such systems are computationally prohibitive due to their size (>500,000 atoms) and the microsecond-to-millisecond timescales required to observe allosteric transitions. We propose an integrated computational approach combining coarse-grained MD for global conformational sampling, Gaussian accelerated MD (GaMD) for enhanced exploration of free energy landscapes, and QM/MM simulations to resolve critical electronic interactions at catalytic sites. These methods will be applied to investigate how post-translational modifications alter allosteric networks in the enzyme complex, a process implicated in metabolic dysregulation. The HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations across multiple thermodynamic states, significantly accelerating convergence. Expected outcomes include (1) atomistic models of allosteric propagation pathways, (2) identification of key residues governing communication between distal functional sites, and (3) predictive insights into how phosphorylation modulates enzymatic efficiency. Results will be validated through collaborative mutagenesis and kinetic assays. This work will establish a computational framework for studying supramolecular assemblies at unprecedented spatiotemporal resolution, advancing mechanistic understanding of metabolic regulation while providing foundational data for targeted enzyme engineering. The requested resources are essential given the project’s scale: initial benchmarks indicate that simulating a single 1-μs replicate of the full system requires ~25,000 CPU-hours, with thousands of replicates needed for robust statistical analysis across proposed perturbations.
detailed_field: Biochemistry, biophysics, and molecular biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific relationship of physiological function to the structure and actions of macromolecules and supramolecular assemblies such as multienzyme complexes, membranes, and viruses. Includes instruction in the chemical mechanisms of regulation and catalysis, protein synthesis and other syntheses, and biomolecular chemical reactions.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the systemic drivers of educational inequality across nations through advanced computational analysis of cross-national datasets. Despite growing recognition of global disparities in educational access and outcomes, existing research remains constrained by methodological limitations in handling large-scale, heterogeneous data spanning diverse sociopolitical contexts. This study will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-decade datasets from international assessments (e.g., PISA, TIMSS), national education statistics, and digitized policy archives from over 100 countries. Machine learning techniques, including hierarchical clustering and gradient-boosted regression trees, will identify patterns linking socioeconomic factors, policy interventions, and learning outcomes. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will analyze multilingual policy documents to quantify alignment with UNESCO’s Sustainable Development Goal 4 targets. Concurrently, agent-based modeling simulations will test hypotheses about how migration policies affect transnational educational trajectories. The computational demands of processing petabyte-scale data, training deep learning models on multimodal inputs, and running thousands of parallelized policy simulations necessitate cluster computing infrastructure. Expected outcomes include: (1) a predictive framework mapping policy configurations to equity outcomes across governance regimes; (2) evidence-based typologies of educational migration drivers; and (3) open-access tools for computational comparative education research. By enabling analysis at unprecedented geographical and temporal scales, this project aims to advance theoretical understanding of education globalization while providing policymakers with translatable insights for reducing systemic inequities. The requested resources directly support breakthrough capabilities in temporal network analysis of education systems and transformer-based cross-lingual policy comparisons, which are infeasible with conventional computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the educational phenomena, practices, and institutions within different societies and states in a comparative perspective, and the study of international educational issues. Includes instruction in comparative research methods, country- or area-specific studies, cross-national studies of learning and teaching styles, international educational policy and development, and analyses of educational migration patterns and experiences.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for generative design in hybrid physical-digital media, addressing the challenge of optimizing complex aesthetic and functional parameters in large-scale artistic installations. While generative algorithms have transformed digital art, their application to mixed-media works—integrating materials such as responsive textiles, modular ceramics, and embedded sensor arrays—remains constrained by the computational demands of simulating multidimensional design spaces. Current methods struggle to balance real-time interactivity, material behavior modeling, and aesthetic coherence when scaling beyond simple geometries or homogeneous media. To overcome this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a distributed neural architecture combining graph neural networks (GNNs) for topological relationships, differentiable physics engines for material simulations, and transformer-based aesthetic evaluation models. The system will process iterative design variants across parallel nodes, enabling rapid exploration of configurations that satisfy mechanical stability, fabrication constraints, and dynamic visual patterns. A key innovation involves developing adaptive sampling strategies to prioritize regions of the design space where functional and aesthetic criteria exhibit non-linear synergies. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for hybrid media design, validated through two case studies: a kinetic sculpture network for public spaces and a climate-responsive architectural facade system. The research will advance computational creativity methodologies by demonstrating how HPC-enabled workflows can bridge the gap between digital generative art and materially complex applied design. Results will contribute new metrics for evaluating computational aesthetics in multidimensional design problems while providing practical frameworks for artists and designers working at the intersection of traditional craft and emerging media technologies.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in design and applied arts, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in the digital preservation and interactive curation of heterogeneous museum collections. As museums increasingly digitize artifacts and adopt immersive technologies for public engagement, managing large-scale 3D models, multispectral imaging datasets, and real-time visitor interaction analytics has become computationally prohibitive for conventional systems. The research problem centers on optimizing resource-intensive workflows—such as AI-driven artifact degradation modeling, dynamic climate simulation for conservation environments, and augmented reality (AR) exhibit rendering—to enable scalable, data-driven decision-making in museum operations. Proposed computational methods include parallelized processing of high-resolution cultural heritage datasets using GPU clusters, machine learning models trained on material degradation patterns across diverse artifact types (e.g., textiles, metals, organic composites), and finite element analysis simulations to predict microclimate impacts on preservation spaces. The project will also develop a modular digital twin framework to simulate exhibit layouts and visitor flow dynamics under variable conditions. Outcomes aim to establish open-source tools for predictive conservation, reduce energy costs in climate-controlled storage through optimized simulation parameters, and enhance accessibility through low-latency AR interfaces. By integrating computational museology with HPC capabilities, this work addresses a gap in cross-disciplinary methodologies for sustainable collection management while advancing technical standards for digital interactivity in non-science domains. Resource allocation will directly support iterative model training, large-scale dataset aggregation from partner institutions, and validation against physical conservation experiments, ultimately bridging computational scalability challenges with practical museological needs.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the attitudes, knowledge, and skills required to develop, prepare, organize, administer, conserve, store and retrieve artifacts, exhibits and entire collections in museums and galleries, and that prepares individuals to assume curatorial, technical and managerial positions in museums. Includes instruction in institutional management, acquisition, exhibit design, conservation, packing techniques, and public relations.

abstract: This project investigates the spatial dynamics of community-level conflicts arising from renewable energy infrastructure siting, focusing on how geographic variables and socio-cultural perceptions of land use shape decision-making processes. As global renewable energy transitions accelerate, tensions between decarbonization goals and local land-use priorities remain understudied from a spatially explicit perspective. The research employs high-resolution satellite imagery, participatory GIS data, and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate negotiation processes between stakeholders under diverse environmental and policy scenarios. Computational challenges include processing multi-temporal land cover datasets (10m resolution, 100TB+), training machine learning models to identify contested zones from georeferenced public commentary, and running ensemble ABM simulations incorporating heterogeneous agent behaviors tied to place-based values. High-performance computing resources are essential for parallelizing spatial optimization algorithms that minimize land-use conflicts while meeting energy capacity targets, as well as for uncertainty quantification across 10^4 parameter combinations in the ABM framework. Expected outcomes include a scalable geospatial decision-support tool for policymakers, validated through case studies in three ecoregions with distinct resource governance frameworks. The project advances methodological integration of computational social science and physical geography by formalizing how cultural landscapes—often excluded from energy infrastructure models—mediate human-environment feedbacks. Results will contribute to conflict-sensitive renewable energy planning while extending theoretical understandings of space as an active agent in socio-technical transitions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of the spatial distribution and interrelationships of people, natural resources, plant and animal life. Includes instruction in historical and political geography, cultural geography, economic and physical geography, regional science, cartographic methods, remote sensing, spatial analysis, and applications to areas such as land-use planning, development studies, and analyses of specific countries, regions, and resources.

abstract: Understanding the drivers of population persistence and adaptive potential under rapid environmental change remains a critical challenge in evolutionary ecology. This project integrates genomic, demographic, and environmental data to model how landscape fragmentation and climate-mediated selection shape genetic diversity and extinction risk in spatially structured populations of *Quercus lobata* (valley oak), a keystone species experiencing habitat loss and phenological mismatch. We propose developing spatially explicit, individual-based simulations to quantify interactions between dispersal limitation, selection on drought-responsive loci, and stochastic population dynamics across heterogeneous environments. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize simulations using whole-genome resequencing data from 500 individuals across 35 populations, process high-resolution climate and land-use layers, and perform iterative model fitting via approximate Bayesian computation. Simulations will be validated against long-term demographic datasets from established field plots and projected under IPCC climate scenarios. A parallelized sensitivity analysis will identify thresholds in habitat connectivity and adaptive genetic variation that predict population collapse. This work advances predictive frameworks for population viability by unifying landscape genomics with eco-evolutionary dynamics, addressing a key gap in conservation planning for foundation species. The computational pipeline will be modularly designed to support comparative studies in other taxa with contrasting life histories. By resolving how gene flow, selection, and stochasticity jointly mediate climate adaptation, outcomes will directly inform habitat corridor designs and assisted gene flow strategies. The requested resources will enable processing >200 TB of genomic and environmental data while running ensemble simulations at scales exceeding 10^6 agent-years per parameter set, a task infeasible on local clusters.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the natural history, life cycle behavior, and ecosystem dynamics of single species and multi-species communities, and the patterns and causes of diversity within and among such populations. Includes instruction in biostatistics, population dynamics, population and quantitative genetics, RNA and DNA sequences, genomics, evolutionary ecology, natural adaptation and hybridization, geographic differentiation, life history and life cycle studies, and animal and plant demography.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable computational methods for estimating high-dimensional item response theory (IRT) models, which are critical for advancing precision in psychological measurement but remain underutilized due to prohibitive computational demands. Traditional IRT frameworks struggle with modern datasets characterized by complex response dependencies, multifaceted latent traits, and large numbers of items or respondents. To address this, we propose a hybrid Bayesian optimization approach combining Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) for parameter sampling and variational inference for approximating posterior distributions. This methodology will be embedded within a modular software framework designed for parallelized computation across high-performance computing (HPC) clusters. Key challenges include optimizing memory allocation for sparse interaction matrices, minimizing communication overhead during distributed gradient calculations, and ensuring numerical stability in high-dimensional latent spaces. The computational workflow will be validated through systematic Monte Carlo simulations evaluating parameter recovery, scalability, and robustness to model misspecification under varying sample sizes (N = 10,000–1,000,000) and latent trait dimensions (10–100 dimensions). HPC resources are essential to manage the exponential growth in model complexity: a single iteration of the 100-dimensional model requires ~10^5 parallelizable operations per MCMC chain, with convergence diagnostics necessitating weeks of computation on standard workstations. Outcomes will include open-source software optimized for GPU-accelerated clusters, empirical guidelines for dimensionality reduction in large-scale assessments, and a publicly available benchmark dataset for testing hierarchical IRT implementations. By enabling efficient estimation of previously intractable models, this work will directly enhance the design of adaptive personality inventories and cognitive diagnostic assessments while advancing statistical methodology in psychometrics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the mathematical and statistical procedures used in psychological test construction and validation; the general problems of the measurement of behavior; and the application of quantitative methods to research design and other methodological topics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on the dynamics of family systems and therapeutic intervention efficacy through computational modeling and large-scale data analysis. Family psychology faces a critical challenge in understanding how multi-level factors—such as individual behaviors, relational patterns, cultural contexts, and systemic stressors—interact to influence family resilience or dysfunction. Traditional statistical methods often struggle to capture the nonlinear, recursive interactions inherent in family systems, particularly when analyzing longitudinal datasets that include diverse family structures, cultural backgrounds, and crisis scenarios (e.g., family violence, economic hardship). To address this, we propose developing agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate family interactions under varying conditions, integrating empirical data from clinical assessments, genograms, and therapy session transcripts. These models will incorporate machine learning algorithms to identify patterns in therapeutic outcomes, predict tipping points in family dynamics, and test the systemic effects of hypothetical interventions. The HPC infrastructure is essential for running thousands of parallel simulations to account for variability in family compositions and environmental contexts, as well as for processing high-dimensional data (e.g., linguistic features from therapy dialogues, temporal network analyses of family communication). Expected outcomes include a scalable computational framework to evaluate the effectiveness of different counseling strategies—such as family sculpting or diversity-informed interventions—across heterogeneous populations. This work will provide evidence-based insights into optimizing therapeutic approaches for complex family systems, directly supporting the development of tailored, equitable counseling practices. By bridging computational social science and family psychology, the project aims to establish new methodologies for studying relational health, with implications for training programs, clinical guidelines, and policy recommendations addressing family well-being.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide therapeutic, evaluative, and research services to families and individuals in the family unit context. Includes instruction in natural and family systems theory, family and group rituals, family evaluation and assessment, marital and couples therapy, sex therapy, parenting, interviewing techniques, genogram construction, family sculpting, diversity issues, family violence, family law, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of predicting dynamic protein interaction networks under varying cellular conditions, a critical gap in understanding context-specific molecular mechanisms underlying complex diseases. Current methods for modeling protein-protein interactions (PPIs) often rely on static datasets or simplified biophysical assumptions, limiting their utility in capturing transient, condition-dependent interactions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid computational framework integrating graph neural networks (GNNs) with physics-based molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments. The GNN component will be trained on multi-omics datasets—including single-cell transcriptomics, proteomics, and publicly available PPI databases—to predict context-specific interaction probabilities. These predictions will guide targeted MD simulations using adaptive sampling algorithms to model atomic-level interaction stability under specific biochemical conditions (e.g., pH shifts, post-translational modifications). The iterative coupling of machine learning predictions with physics-based validation requires parallelized workflows across GPU and CPU nodes, leveraging distributed memory architectures for large-scale parameter optimization and ensemble simulation analysis. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible database of condition-specific protein interaction profiles, (2) novel algorithms for efficient integration of heterogeneous biological data types, and (3) validated computational models of disease-relevant PPIs in tumor microenvironment contexts. This resource-intensive approach will enable unprecedented resolution in mapping dynamic interactomes, directly supporting drug target identification and mechanism-of-action studies for therapeutic development. Successful implementation demands access to HPC resources with multi-node GPU clusters, high-throughput storage for petabyte-scale simulation data, and optimized scientific computing libraries for biomolecular machine learning applications.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of computer-based technologies and services to biological, biomedical, and biotechnology research. Includes instruction in algorithms, network architecture, principles of software design, human interface design, usability studies, search strategies, database management and data mining, digital image processing, computer graphics and animation, CAD, computer programming, and applications to experimental design and analysis and to specific quantitative, modeling, and analytical studies in the various biological specializations.

abstract: Preventive medicine aims to reduce disease burden through early risk prediction and intervention, yet existing models often lack the granularity to account for multi-faceted interactions between genetic, environmental, and behavioral factors. This project addresses the critical need for scalable, high-resolution computational frameworks to integrate heterogeneous datasets—including genomic sequences, electronic health records, and real-time wearable device data—to stratify individual disease risks and optimize personalized prevention strategies. Current limitations stem from the computational complexity of modeling nonlinear relationships across large, sparse datasets, which conventional infrastructure cannot process efficiently. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate a machine learning architecture that combines graph neural networks (GNNs) for relational data integration with transformer-based models for longitudinal pattern recognition. The HPC environment will enable parallel processing of multi-terabyte datasets, hyperparameter optimization across thousands of simultaneous trials, and in silico simulations of population-level intervention outcomes. Key objectives include (1) identifying latent biomarkers predictive of cardiovascular and metabolic diseases within underserved populations, (2) quantifying dynamic risk modifiers such as physical activity and sleep patterns, and (3) generating open-source tools for real-time risk visualization tailored to clinical workflows. Expected outcomes include a validated pipeline for synthesizing disparate data modalities into actionable risk profiles, published benchmarks for computational preventive models, and a framework for deploying scalable prevention protocols in resource-constrained settings. By harnessing HPC capabilities, this work will advance precision prevention paradigms, directly contributing to reduced healthcare disparities and informing national guidelines on data-driven preventive care. The computational tools and datasets generated will be made available to the research community, fostering collaborative innovation in clinical preventive medicine.
cip_definition: Research focused on Preventive Medicine

abstract: The increasing complexity of industrial automation systems necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize control algorithms, fault detection mechanisms, and energy efficiency in real-time applications. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and simulate next-generation industrial electronic systems, focusing on adaptive control strategies for variable-frequency drives (VFDs), predictive maintenance models for programmable logic controllers (PLCs), and dynamic power distribution networks. A key challenge lies in balancing real-time responsiveness with computational accuracy, particularly when scaling these systems to large manufacturing environments with heterogeneous sensor networks. To address this, the research will employ parallelized finite element analysis (FEA) for electromagnetic component optimization, machine learning (ML)-enhanced digital twins for system behavior prediction, and Monte Carlo simulations to assess failure probabilities under diverse operational conditions. Computational workflows will integrate ANSYS Electronics Desktop, COMSOL Multiphysics, and custom Python-based ML frameworks, requiring significant GPU-accelerated processing for iterative design optimization. Expected outcomes include validated control algorithms that reduce motor energy consumption by 12-18%, fault prediction models with 92%+ accuracy across multi-vendor PLC ecosystems, and a generalized simulation toolkit for industrial power electronics. These advancements will directly support the transition to Industry 4.0 by enabling more resilient and efficient manufacturing systems while providing students in Industrial Electronics Technology with hands-on experience in cutting-edge computational methodologies. The requested HPC resources are critical for handling large-scale parametric studies (10,000+ simulation instances) and training deep neural networks on terabyte-scale operational datasets from partner manufacturing facilities, tasks infeasible with existing campus computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to assemble, install, operate, maintain, and repair electrical/electronic equipment used in industry and manufacturing. Includes instruction in installing, maintaining and testing various types of equipment.

abstract: Modern healthcare systems generate vast amounts of complex data, including structured electronic health records (EHRs), unstructured clinical notes, and imaging data. Effectively managing and analyzing these datasets to improve patient outcomes while ensuring privacy and regulatory compliance remains a critical challenge. This project seeks to develop scalable computational frameworks for integrating, processing, and securing multimodal health data using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Leveraging GPU-accelerated machine learning, we will train deep neural networks to extract semantic features from unstructured text and correlate them with structured EHR variables. Parallelized natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be implemented to analyze clinical narratives at scale, while federated learning architectures will enable collaborative model training across institutions without raw data sharing. To address security concerns, we will prototype blockchain-based audit systems optimized for distributed HPC environments to track data access patterns. The computational workflows will be validated using de-identified datasets spanning 2 million patient records from our partner hospital network. Expected outcomes include novel algorithms for multimodal health data synthesis, open-source tools for privacy-preserving analytics, and benchmarks demonstrating the efficiency gains of HPC-enabled processing compared to conventional infrastructure. This research will directly support quality improvement initiatives by enabling faster identification of clinical trends and predictive modeling of patient risks. The developed frameworks will be disseminated through academic collaborations and integrated into our health information technology curriculum, training future professionals in advanced computational methods for healthcare data management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of health information administrators and other professionals, to construct medical records and clinical databases, perform manipulations on retrieved data, control the security and quality of records, and supervise data entry and technical maintenance personnel. Includes instruction in clinical and biomedical science data and information requirements, database management, data coding and validation, information security, quality control, health information content and structure, medical business procedures, and legal requirements.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern internal combustion engines, particularly in meeting stringent emissions standards and performance demands, necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize machining and rebuilding processes. Traditional trial-and-error methods for engine component repair and assembly are time-intensive, costly, and limited in addressing multi-variable interactions such as thermal stress, material fatigue, and dynamic load distribution. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models for engine machining workflows, focusing on diesel and gasoline engines in automotive and heavy-duty applications. By simulating material behavior under operational stresses and refining machining parameters at scale, the research aims to establish data-driven protocols for crankshaft balancing, cylinder head crack propagation mitigation, and block surface finishing. Computational methods will integrate finite element analysis (FEA) for stress distribution modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for combustion chamber surface optimization, and machine learning algorithms to correlate machining tolerances with engine longevity. The HPC environment will enable large-scale parametric studies of toolpath strategies, material removal rates, and thermal distortion effects during block resurfacing—variables that are computationally prohibitive to analyze at high fidelity on local systems. Expected outcomes include a validated open-access simulation toolkit for engine machinists, reducing rework rates in component refurbishment by 15–20%, and guidelines for minimizing vibrational imbalances in rebuilt engines. The project will also train engine machinist students in computational modeling techniques, bridging gaps between traditional trade skills and Industry 4.0 methodologies. Results will be disseminated through technical workshops and partnerships with regional engine remanufacturing firms, advancing both academic and industrial capabilities in sustainable engine lifecycle management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the building and reconstruction of automotive and commercial vehicle engines. Includes instruction in cylinder head and block, crack repair, crankshaft inspection and repair, connecting rods and pistons, balancing, block preparation, disassembly and repair, engine assembly, gas and diesel technology, and inspection and machining.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of understudied Semitic and Middle/Near Eastern languages, focusing on the morphological and syntactic complexity of Classical Ethiopic (Ge’ez) and its relationship to modern Ethiopian Semitic languages. Despite the rich literary corpus of Ge’ez—spanning religious, historical, and legal texts—systematic computational modeling of its linguistic features remains limited, hindering comparative studies with modern dialects like Amharic and Tigrinya. The research problem centers on addressing gaps in diachronic linguistic analysis, particularly the evolution of verb morphology and clause structure, which are critical for understanding language contact and change in the Horn of Africa. Current methodologies rely on manual annotation, which is time-intensive and inconsistently scalable across corpora. This project proposes a hybrid computational approach: (1) developing a transformer-based model trained on digitized Ge’ez manuscripts to automate morphological tagging and syntactic parsing, and (2) employing phylogenetic algorithms to reconstruct probabilistic language trees that map historical divergences. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing high-resolution manuscript images (via OCR fine-tuning) and running large-scale parallel simulations of language evolution, which require teraflop-level computation and significant memory allocation. Expected outcomes include an open-access annotated corpus of Ge’ez texts, a suite of computational tools for Semitic language analysis, and empirically grounded insights into the historical development of Ethiopian Semitic languages. These resources will directly benefit philologists, linguists, and digital humanities scholars, enabling cross-disciplinary research into language preservation, liturgical studies, and sociolinguistic dynamics. By integrating advanced computational methods with traditional philological expertise, this project aims to bridge methodological divides in the field while enhancing the visibility of under-resourced languages in NLP research.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Middle/ Near Eastern and Semitic Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the Middle/Near Eastern and Semitic languages of the ancient and modern Middle/Near East, Western Asia, North Africa, and Europe. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project investigates the emergent dynamics of cross-cultural aesthetic perception through computational modeling of large-scale neural and behavioral datasets. Aesthetic experiences—such as responses to art, music, or natural scenes—are shaped by biological, psychological, and sociocultural factors, yet existing frameworks lack integrative models capable of capturing their nonlinear interactions. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate population-level neural networks trained on multimodal data (fMRI, eye-tracking, and subjective ratings) from diverse cultural cohorts. The computational architecture will combine deep learning with dynamical systems theory to model how individual differences in sensory processing, semantic associations, and emotional appraisal converge into shared or divergent aesthetic judgments. A key innovation involves simulating “virtual cultures” through generative adversarial networks (GANs) to test hypotheses about how aesthetic norms propagate in social networks. The HPC environment is critical for handling the high-dimensional parameter space (10⁶+ nodes) and iterative optimization required to disentangle universal from culture-specific mechanisms. Anticipated outcomes include: (1) predictive models of aesthetic preference variability across demographic strata, (2) identification of neural signatures predictive of cultural fluency in aesthetic domains, and (3) open-source tools for simulating neurocultural interactions in collective decision-making. This work bridges affective neuroscience, computational social science, and digital humanities, offering novel insights into the plasticity of aesthetic systems while providing scalable methods for studying psychological phenomena at the intersection of individual cognition and collective culture. Results will inform applications in AI-driven design, cross-cultural communication, and educational technologies tailored to diverse perceptual schemas.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in psychology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to model the transport and fate of emerging contaminants in urban stormwater systems under climate change stressors. Urbanized watersheds face increasing risks of pollutant mobilization due to intensified precipitation patterns and aging infrastructure, yet current models lack the spatiotemporal resolution to capture dynamic interactions between hydrologic processes, infrastructure performance, and contaminant speciation. The research will employ coupled hydrodynamic and biogeochemical simulations using EPA SWMM and OpenFOAM, integrated with machine learning surrogates to accelerate uncertainty quantification across climate scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to resolve multi-scale processes, including fine-grained sediment-contaminant interactions at the particle level and system-wide hydraulic responses during extreme rainfall events. Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will assess failure probabilities of green-gray infrastructure hybrids under projected precipitation regimes, while reactive transport models parameterized with field data from partner municipalities will predict heavy metal and PFAS accumulation hotspots. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive tools for prioritizing infrastructure upgrades based on contaminant-specific risks, (2) optimized hybrid green-gray design configurations that reduce treatment costs by ≥20% under uncertain climate futures, and (3) open-source modules extending the HydroShare platform with contaminant transformation kinetics libraries. The computational framework will directly inform resilience planning in three Great Lakes cities, potentially benefiting 1.2 million residents facing combined sewer overflow risks. By enabling near-real-time simulation of complex feedbacks between climate extremes, engineered systems, and environmental health impacts, this work advances fundamental knowledge in sustainable urban water management while providing actionable strategies to meet EPA stormwater regulations. The requested resources will support 18 months of large ensemble simulations, requiring 256-core parallel runs for >600,000 CPU-hours, with data outputs exceeding 150TB for public archive.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of systems for controlling contained living environments and for monitoring and controlling factors in the external natural environment, including pollution control, waste and hazardous material disposal, health and safety protection, conservation, life support, and requirements for protection of special materials and related work environments.

abstract: Hydroelectric energy systems are critical to global renewable energy infrastructure, yet optimizing their performance under dynamic environmental and operational conditions remains a significant challenge. Current computational models often lack the resolution to capture complex fluid-structure interactions, sediment transport dynamics, and transient hydraulic behaviors at scale, limiting their utility for design and operational improvements. This project seeks advanced high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-physics simulation frameworks that integrate computational fluid dynamics (CFD), granular sediment transport modeling, and machine learning-driven optimization. The research will focus on two interconnected objectives: (1) simulating turbine array efficiency under variable flow regimes and sediment loads, and (2) predicting long-term reservoir sedimentation patterns and their impacts on energy production. High-fidelity CFD models will resolve turbulent flow structures and particle-laden flow interactions using LES (Large Eddy Simulation) and DEM (Discrete Element Method) approaches, while reduced-order machine learning models will enable rapid scenario evaluation for operational decision support. The computational scale requires parallelized simulations across thousands of cores to handle meshes exceeding 100 million elements and time-resolved data analytics. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for optimizing turbine placement and maintenance cycles, strategies to mitigate sedimentation-related efficiency losses, and validated models for assessing ecological impacts of flow modifications. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to advance hydroelectric system resilience and energy output while reducing operational costs and environmental disruption. The resulting open-source frameworks will provide the hydroelectric energy community with scalable computational tools to address 21st-century challenges in renewable energy infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing hydroelectric energy systems. Includes instruction in hydroelectric energy principles, energy storage and transfer technologies, testing and inspection procedures, system maintenance procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: Agricultural power machinery operation faces significant challenges in optimizing equipment performance under variable field conditions, including diverse terrain, crop types, and environmental factors. Current operational frameworks often rely on static efficiency models that fail to account for real-time interactions between machinery, soil dynamics, and crop physiology, leading to suboptimal resource use, energy waste, and environmental strain. This project proposes to develop a dynamic, high-fidelity simulation platform to model and optimize agricultural machinery operations using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will integrate multi-physics computational models of machinery systems (e.g., tractors, harvesters, and sprayers) with geospatial soil moisture data, crop growth patterns, and weather simulations to predict operational outcomes across heterogeneous agricultural landscapes. Machine learning algorithms will be deployed to iteratively refine equipment control parameters, such as engine load distribution, implement deployment timing, and sprayer droplet dynamics, in response to simulated field scenarios. Computational workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated frameworks for large-scale parameter sweeps and sensitivity analyses, requiring parallel processing capabilities to handle terabytes of sensor-derived input data. Expected outcomes include predictive optimization frameworks for fuel efficiency, crop input utilization, and equipment wear patterns, validated against field trials from collaborating agribusiness partners. The project will directly address gaps in precision agriculture by enabling adaptive machinery control strategies that reduce operational costs and environmental impacts while maintaining yield targets. By quantifying the computational demands of real-time decision support systems for farm equipment, this work will also inform future edge computing architectures in agricultural robotics. Access to HPC resources is critical to achieving the spatial and temporal resolution necessary for actionable insights at scale, with particular emphasis on simulating rare but high-impact events such as equipment failure modes under extreme weather conditions.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to operate specialized farm, ranch, and agribusiness power equipment of a stationary, mobile, or hand-operated nature. Includes instruction in operating specialized equipment such as terrestrial and airborne crop-spraying equipment; tractors and hauling equipment; planting and harvesting equipment; cutting equipment; power sources and systems for silos, irrigation, pumping, and applications such as dairy, feeding and shearing operations; processing equipment; and applicable electrical, mechanical, and safety principles.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic evolution of visual symbolism within global digital media ecosystems, an understudied area at the intersection of cultural studies, digital anthropology, and computational analysis. While traditional humanities scholarship has examined symbolic communication within specific cultural contexts, the rapid proliferation of digital platforms has generated vast, interconnected visual datasets that transcend geographic and temporal boundaries. This research addresses the challenge of mapping and analyzing these complex, large-scale patterns to uncover how visual symbols emerge, mutate, and propagate across diverse online communities. The computational methodology employs deep learning architectures, particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs), to detect and classify recurrent visual motifs across a curated corpus of 15 million images from social media platforms, digital art repositories, and collaborative wikis spanning 2010-2023. Temporal network analysis will track symbol diffusion pathways, while transformer-based models will analyze associated multilingual textual metadata to contextualize semantic shifts. High-performance computing resources are critical for processing high-resolution image data, training multimodal models, and simulating cultural transmission dynamics through agent-based modeling. Expected outcomes include 1) a novel taxonomy of digital visual symbology, 2) quantitative frameworks for measuring cross-cultural influence in digital aesthetics, and 3) open-source tools for temporal pattern detection in cultural datasets. This work will establish computational foundations for studying digital visual culture at scale while preserving humanistic interpretive rigor, offering new methodologies for understanding how globalization and technological mediation shape contemporary symbolic communication. The resource-intensive nature of processing heterogeneous multimedia data and maintaining temporal-spatial analyses across petabytes of information necessitates the requested computing infrastructure to achieve statistically robust, culturally nuanced insights.
cip_title: Liberal Arts and Sciences, General Studies and Humanities, Other
cip_definition: Any single instructional program in liberal arts and sciences, general studies and humanities, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale historical datasets central to understanding the development of Canadian social and political institutions in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. The research problem centers on tracing the interconnected evolution of federal policies, regional identities, and public discourse during a period of rapid industrialization and demographic change. Traditional historiographical methods struggle to systematically process the vast quantity of digitized primary sources now available, including parliamentary debates, regional newspapers, census records, and correspondence networks. To address this, the project will apply natural language processing (NLP) techniques and network analysis algorithms to map patterns in policy language, track the dissemination of political ideas, and quantify shifts in regional representation within federal institutions. Computational workflows will be designed to handle multilingual texts (English and French), temporal-spatial metadata, and heterogeneous data formats, with iterative validation against established historical interpretations. Key objectives include identifying previously undocumented correlations between resource allocation decisions and regional voting patterns, as well as visualizing the long-term impacts of immigration policies on urban-rural divides. The scale of data—spanning over 10 million pages of text and 150,000 archival records—necessitates HPC capabilities for parallel processing, large-memory operations, and efficient storage of intermediate analytical outputs. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated historical texts, novel computational methods tailored to Canadian historiography, and peer-reviewed findings challenging existing narratives about federal-provincial power dynamics during Confederation-era reforms. By enabling systematic analysis across previously siloed sources, this project aims to advance methodological innovation in historical research while generating new insights into the structural foundations of modern Canadian governance.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the society, culture, and institutions of Canada from its origins to the present. Includes instruction in Canadian historiography, sources and materials, historical research methods, and applications to the study of specific themes, issues, periods, and institutions.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the development of adaptive decision architectures for next-generation combat systems by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model multi-domain operational scenarios under uncertainty. Modern military engagements require the integration of autonomous systems, human operators, and distributed sensor networks across contested environments, yet existing combat systems often struggle with dynamic resource allocation, real-time risk assessment, and coordination at scale. The research problem centers on closing this capability gap through computational frameworks that balance operational agility with system resilience, particularly in environments where communication latency, adversarial AI behaviors, and emergent threats undermine traditional optimization approaches. Using a hybrid simulation methodology, the project will combine agent-based modeling of platform-sensor-weapon interactions, Monte Carlo analyses of threat evolution patterns, and reinforcement learning to train decision policies under stochastic constraints. HPC resources will enable parallelized testing of millions of simulated engagements across diverse terrain, weather, and electronic warfare conditions while maintaining the granularity needed to model human-machine teaming factors. Key innovations include a modular architecture for embedding doctrinal constraints into machine learning agents and a probabilistic framework for evaluating system-of-systems survivability against hybrid threats. Anticipated outcomes include validated protocols for dynamic resource reallocation in degraded communication environments, quantitative metrics for balancing autonomy with human oversight, and open-source simulation tools to benchmark combat system adaptability. By addressing the computational complexity of modern multi-domain operations, this work aims to provide foundational insights for designing combat systems that maintain tactical superiority in rapidly evolving conflict scenarios while adhering to ethical and strategic governance requirements.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of systems engineering and system architecture to the design and construction of modern combat systems and their integration with each other, with host platforms and with other forces into network-centric warfighting systems. Includes instruction in systems engineering, computer programming, chemical systems, biological systems, material systems, human factors, combat environments, sensor systems, threat and system risk assessment, conventional and unconventional weapons, combat simulation, reliability and maintenance, testing, engineering project management, strategic planning and applications to aerospace, ground, and naval combat systems.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize wildfire response strategies and resource allocation for fire departments, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address the dynamic challenges of wildfire mitigation. Wildfires increasingly threaten communities, straining traditional fire management systems that rely on static models and historical data. Current approaches often fail to integrate real-time variables such as shifting weather patterns, fuel moisture dynamics, and urban-wildland interface complexities, leading to suboptimal resource deployment during emergencies. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) platform coupled with machine learning (ML) to simulate fire spread, evacuation logistics, and resource allocation under diverse scenarios. The ABM will incorporate geospatial data, weather forecasts, infrastructure layouts, and firefighter crew dynamics, while ML algorithms trained on historical fire incident data will predict short-term fire behavior and resource needs. HPC resources are critical to running large-scale, high-resolution simulations that account for stochastic variables (e.g., wind shifts, equipment failures) and generate probabilistic risk assessments. These simulations will inform a decision-support tool for incident commanders, providing real-time recommendations for crew deployment, equipment staging, and evacuation routing. Expected outcomes include validated models that reduce response times by 15–20% in simulated scenarios, a publicly accessible dataset of fire propagation patterns under varying mitigation strategies, and policy guidelines for proactive resource prepositioning. By integrating computational fire science with fire service administration principles, this work aims to enhance operational resilience, reduce economic losses, and improve interagency coordination during multi-jurisdictional incidents. The project aligns with national priorities for disaster resilience and supports fire departments in adopting data-driven strategies for community risk reduction.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the principles, theory, and practices associated with the management of fire operations, firefighting services, and community fire issues. Includes instruction in fire protection history and theory, incident command leadership, administration of public fire organizations, labor relations, emergency medical services management, fire emergency response strategies and mitigation, legal and regulatory responsibilities, budgeting, public relations, and organizational leadership.

abstract: The exponential growth of global air traffic has intensified congestion and inefficiencies in current air transportation systems, leading to increased delays, fuel consumption, and environmental impact. Traditional air traffic management (ATM) frameworks struggle to adapt to dynamic operational demands and the integration of emerging technologies such as unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and urban air mobility (UAM) platforms. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a high-fidelity computational model to simulate and optimize large-scale air traffic flow management (ATFM) under varying operational and environmental constraints. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the research will implement a hybrid approach combining agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo simulations, and reinforcement learning algorithms to dynamically allocate airspace resources, predict traffic conflicts, and optimize routing strategies in real time. The computational framework will integrate heterogeneous data sources, including historical flight trajectories, weather patterns, and airspace configurations, to generate scalable solutions for congested and complex airspace environments. Key outcomes include actionable insights for reducing systemic delays, minimizing fuel burn through optimal flight path allocation, and enhancing the adaptability of ATM systems to accommodate future air transportation paradigms. The project’s significance lies in its potential to inform policy decisions, support the development of next-generation air traffic control systems, and contribute to the aviation industry’s sustainability goals. Access to HPC infrastructure is critical to achieving the required computational throughput for simulating millions of flight trajectories and iteratively refining optimization models, tasks that are infeasible with conventional computing resources.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in aviation and air transportation services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Athletic injuries present complex challenges in diagnosis, treatment, and prevention due to their multifactorial origins involving biomechanical stressors, tissue adaptation limits, and psychological resilience. This project seeks to advance computational modeling of injury mechanisms and recovery trajectories using high-performance computing (HPC) to address critical gaps in predicting injury risk and optimizing rehabilitation protocols. We propose a multiscale biomechanical framework integrating finite element modeling of musculoskeletal tissues with machine learning (ML)-driven analysis of athlete-specific sensor data (wearables, motion capture) and clinical outcomes. The HPC environment will enable large-scale simulations of dynamic loading scenarios (e.g., repetitive impacts in contact sports) to quantify tissue fatigue thresholds and failure patterns, while federated learning architectures will process heterogeneous datasets from collaborating sports clinics to identify subclinical injury signatures. A parallel computational pipeline will couple these models with psychological stress biomarkers (e.g., cortisol levels, cognitive performance metrics) to evaluate their modulating effects on recovery timelines. Validation will leverage retrospective data from 2,500 athletes with lower extremity injuries, prospectively followed for 12–24 months. Resource requests emphasize GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning workflows and high-memory nodes for biomechanical simulations requiring ~10^6 degrees of freedom. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive algorithms for anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reinjury risk stratified by sport type and rehabilitation adherence, (2) open-source tools for simulating tissue remodeling under customized loading regimes, and (3) clinical decision-support dashboards integrating biomechanical and psychosocial risk factors. By bridging computational biomechanics with population-scale athlete health data, this work aims to establish actionable thresholds for injury prevention and personalize return-to-play criteria, directly addressing unmet needs in sports medicine research and practice.
cip_definition: Research focused on the pathology and biomechanics of athletic injuries and the effects of injury on the athlete, including both physical and psychological manifestations. Includes instruction in acute and chronic patient supervision, therapy and rehabilitation, and diagnostic procedures.

abstract: Public horticulture initiatives increasingly face challenges in optimizing plant performance and community engagement within dynamic urban environments, where complex interactions between environmental variables, plant physiology, and human behavior limit predictive capabilities. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to disentangle these multidimensional relationships at scales relevant to real-world applications. This project proposes an integrated computational framework to model plant-environment-community systems, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance decision-making in public horticulture. The research will focus on developing agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate plant growth responses to microclimate variability and parallelized machine learning algorithms to analyze community engagement patterns from longitudinal survey data. Key objectives include parameterizing plant physiology models using hyperspectral imaging datasets, validating climate resilience predictions across diverse horticultural taxa, and identifying socioeconomic drivers of public interaction with urban green spaces. Computational workflows will integrate soil sensor networks, LiDAR-derived 3D canopy structures, and citizen science observations from partner botanical gardens. The HPC infrastructure will enable ensemble simulations assessing thousands of scenario combinations, from irrigation optimization under drought stress to educational program efficacy across demographic groups. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for predicting plant performance in public landscapes, evidence-based frameworks for outreach program design, and multi-criteria optimization pipelines for urban horticulture planning. By quantifying relationships between biological requirements, environmental constraints, and human behavioral factors at unprecedented resolution, this work will provide critical insights for sustaining urban plant ecosystems while maximizing their educational and social value. The computational resources will directly support graduate training in data-driven horticultural science, bridging disciplinary gaps between plant biology, computational modeling, and community-centered design.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on combining traditional horticulture and public education and outreach. Includes instruction in botany, soil science, plant science, agricultural economics, leadership, and business.

abstract: Forensic chemistry faces growing demands to analyze increasingly complex evidentiary materials, such as synthetic drugs, environmental toxins, and trace residues, where traditional methods encounter limitations in resolution, speed, and predictive capability. This project proposes the development of computational models to enhance the interpretation of chemical data from forensic casework, supported by high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research focuses on two interconnected challenges: (1) elucidating degradation pathways of forensic analytes in variable environmental conditions and (2) improving the identification of novel psychoactive substances (NPS) in complex mixtures. Molecular dynamics simulations will model the stability and decomposition kinetics of target compounds, integrating solvent effects and temperature gradients observed in real-world evidence. Concurrently, machine learning algorithms will be trained on multidimensional spectral datasets (e.g., GC-MS, LC-QTOF) to classify NPS analogs and resolve overlapping chromatographic peaks. Quantum chemical calculations will supplement these efforts by predicting NMR and IR spectra for emerging synthetic compounds lacking reference standards. The computational workflows will be validated against experimental data from controlled degradation studies and casework samples. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project aims to establish predictive frameworks that reduce reliance on physical reference materials and accelerate the interpretation of challenging forensic evidence. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for spectral matching uncertainty quantification and a database of simulated degradation products for priority analytes. These resources will strengthen the scientific basis of forensic conclusions, particularly in cases involving rapidly evolving drug markets or environmentally degraded evidence, while addressing critical needs for reproducibility and efficiency in forensic laboratories.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical techniques and instrumentation to the analysis and evaluation of physical evidence to aid in criminal investigations. Includes instruction in analytical, inorganic, organic, and physical chemistry; biochemistry; forensic toxicology; instrumental analysis; crime scene processing; criminal investigation; forensic laboratory technology; and applicable law.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the reliability and operational readiness of military aircraft armament systems by developing a predictive maintenance framework that integrates real-time sensor data with high-fidelity simulations of mechanical and environmental stressors. Current maintenance protocols rely on static schedules and manual inspections, which struggle to account for dynamic operational conditions, material degradation, and complex interactions between subsystems. To address this gap, the research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-physics scenarios—including thermal cycling, vibration-induced fatigue, and corrosion propagation—across heterogeneous materials and components typical of modern armament systems. These simulations will be coupled with machine learning models trained on historical maintenance records and telemetry data to identify failure precursors and optimize maintenance intervals. Key computational challenges involve resolving time-dependent material responses at varying scales (e.g., microstructural corrosion vs. bulk mechanical deformation) and ensuring low-latency integration of simulation outputs with onboard diagnostic systems.
