The proposed work will leverage distributed-memory parallelization for large-scale finite element analysis and GPU-accelerated neural networks to enable near-real-time predictive analytics. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin framework capable of reducing unplanned downtime by 20–30% in modeled systems and a generalized methodology for prioritizing component replacements under constrained logistics scenarios. By bridging computational mechanics, materials science, and operational data analytics, this project aims to establish a new paradigm for sustainment of mission-critical military hardware, directly supporting enhanced fleet readiness and cost-effective lifecycle management.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, technology and maintenance of aircraft weapons systems and associated peripherals. Includes instruction in basic science and quantitative methods, computer science, electronics, engineering graphics, fluid power, heavy equipment operation, armament systems, weapon materials and processes, weapon safety, corrosion control, aircraft systems maintenance, and maintenance management.

abstract: Pediatric musculoskeletal disorders present unique challenges due to the dynamic nature of growing bones and the long-term consequences of treatment decisions. Current approaches to surgical planning and outcome prediction for conditions such as scoliosis, growth plate injuries, and congenital limb deformities rely on generalized population data or static imaging, which fail to account for patient-specific biomechanical variability and longitudinal growth patterns. This project proposes to address these limitations by developing a computational framework integrating patient-specific biomechanical modeling, longitudinal growth simulations, and machine learning to optimize treatment strategies. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to perform large-scale finite element analyses of spinal and limb biomechanics under varying surgical scenarios, coupled with predictive models of bone remodeling and growth trajectories derived from clinical imaging datasets. Multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithms will be trained on synthetic and retrospective clinical data to identify optimal surgical parameters for individual patients. The computational pipeline will require parallel processing of high-resolution 3D imaging data (CT/MRI), automated mesh generation for heterogeneous bone and soft tissue structures, and iterative simulations across parameter spaces representing anatomical variability and growth rates. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for postoperative outcomes in early-onset scoliosis correction and physeal fracture repair, as well as an open-source computational toolkit for simulating growth-modulating interventions. This work will enable personalized surgical planning that accounts for dynamic skeletal development, potentially reducing revision rates and improving functional outcomes in pediatric patients. The scale of data processing (terabytes of imaging data from 500+ retrospective cases) and the computational intensity of coupled biomechanical-growth simulations necessitate HPC resources to achieve clinically relevant turnaround times. Successful implementation will advance precision medicine in pediatric orthopedics by bridging gaps between static clinical imaging and the dynamic biological processes governing musculoskeletal growth.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, surgical and non-surgical treatment, and management of musculoskeletal diseases, abnormalities and trauma in infants, children, and adolescents.

abstract: Costume design for theatre and performing arts requires integrating aesthetic, historical, and functional considerations, yet traditional methods often struggle with the dynamic interplay of materials, movement, and environmental factors. This project seeks to develop a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate and optimize costume designs under realistic performance conditions. The research addresses the challenge of predicting how diverse fabrics interact with complex human motion, stage lighting, and durability requirements across extended productions. By employing physics-based simulations and machine learning models trained on historical costume data, the project aims to create predictive tools for draping, stress distribution, and visual effects under varying scenarios. HPC resources are essential to handle the high-dimensional parameter space, including material properties, biomechanical motion capture data, and real-time rendering of textile behavior at scale. Anticipated outcomes include a suite of open-source tools enabling designers to prototype virtually, reducing reliance on physical iterations and material waste. Additionally, the project will generate datasets correlating historical design choices with performance outcomes, offering new insights into sustainable practices and period-accurate adaptations. This work bridges computational innovation with artistic practice, empowering costume designers to explore creative solutions while addressing practical constraints in live performance environments. The proposed methods have the potential to transform pedagogical approaches in the field, providing students with advanced simulation capabilities to enhance their technical and conceptual skills.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to design and select costumes for characters in theatre and the performing arts and to serve as part of a production team. Includes instruction in costume design, script analysis, theory and criticism, period styles, history of costume, stage makeup, rendering, and costume construction.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the diachronic syntactic evolution of Romance languages through large-scale computational analysis of historical and contemporary textual corpora. Despite rich literary traditions, comparative studies of syntactic structures across major Romance languages (e.g., French, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese) remain limited by the manual analysis of fragmentary datasets. The proposed research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze multi-gigabyte corpora spanning the 12th to 21st centuries, enabling systematic tracking of syntactic phenomena such as clitic placement, verb movement, and subordination patterns. Computational methods will include natural language processing (NLP) pipelines tailored for historical texts, machine learning classifiers to detect syntactic shifts, and phylogenetic algorithms to model divergence pathways. HPC capabilities are critical for handling memory-intensive tasks, including parallel processing of heterogeneous text formats and training neural models on centuries-spanning linguistic data. Expected outcomes include (1) a granular reconstruction of syntactic change timelines across four languages, (2) open-source tools for diachronic Romance linguistics analysis, and (3) empirically grounded insights into the interplay between language contact and syntactic innovation. By leveraging computational scalability, this project aims to overcome traditional limitations in corpus size and temporal resolution, offering new methodologies for interdisciplinary research at the intersection of linguistics and digital humanities. The resulting datasets and analytical frameworks will be disseminated through a public repository, fostering collaborative advancements in Romance language studies.
cip_title: Romance Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in Romance languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) in children, including autism spectrum disorder, cerebral palsy, and genetic syndromes, are marked by heterogeneous clinical presentations and multifactorial etiologies involving genetic, epigenetic, and environmental interactions. Current challenges in optimizing therapeutic interventions stem from limited understanding of how these factors converge to influence neural circuit development and functional outcomes. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze large-scale, multi-modal datasets, including whole-genome sequencing, functional neuroimaging (fMRI, DTI), and longitudinal clinical phenotyping data from a cohort of 2,000 children with NDDs. The computational approach will integrate deep learning models to identify predictive biomarkers of treatment response and developmental trajectories, coupled with network-based analyses to map dysregulated brain connectivity patterns. Additionally, mechanistic simulations of neurodevelopmental processes—such as synaptic pruning and myelination—will be performed using biophysically detailed models to test hypotheses about intervention targets. HPC resources are critical for managing the scale and complexity of these analyses, which involve processing terabytes of imaging data, running genome-wide association studies with combinatorial epigenetic interactions, and executing computationally intensive neural simulations. Expected outcomes include the identification of subtype-specific therapeutic pathways, personalized intervention strategies tailored to genetic and neural profiles, and publicly shared computational tools for analyzing NDD heterogeneity. This work will advance precision medicine in pediatric neurodevelopment by bridging molecular mechanisms with clinical phenotypes, ultimately enabling data-driven guidelines to improve functional outcomes in children with NDDs.
cip_definition: Research on how to treat children having developmental delays or learning disorders, including those associated with visual and hearing impairment, developmental delays, cerebral palsy, spina bifida, autism, and other chronic neurologic conditions.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize predictive maintenance protocols for electromechanical business machines, addressing the growing complexity of integrated mechanical, electrical, and software systems in modern office equipment. Current diagnostic approaches rely heavily on manual troubleshooting and static repair guidelines, which struggle to account for dynamic interactions between components or cumulative wear patterns. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-physics failure scenarios across diverse machine architectures, including printers, document scanners, and networked fiscal devices. Computational models will integrate finite element analysis (FEA) for mechanical stress modeling, circuit simulation for electronic component degradation, and machine learning algorithms trained on historical repair datasets to predict failure probabilities. These models will be validated against empirical data from sensor-equipped testbeds replicating real-world operating conditions. The scale of these simulations—particularly the need to process high-resolution 3D mechanical models alongside real-time sensor data streams—necessitates parallelized computing architectures and GPU-accelerated workloads. Expected outcomes include a predictive maintenance toolkit that identifies likely failure points in specific machine configurations, recommends component-specific intervention thresholds, and generates adaptive repair workflows. This work will directly enhance technician training programs by providing data-driven case studies and virtual troubleshooting environments while advancing academic understanding of failure propagation in hybrid electromechanical systems. The resulting framework aims to reduce average machine downtime by 25-40% in small-to-medium business environments, with broader implications for sustaining legacy office equipment in resource-constrained settings.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to maintain and repair a variety of office machines, such as typewriters, word processing and dictation machines, calculators, data processing equipment, duplicating machines, and mailing machines. Includes instruction in diagnostic techniques, the use of testing equipment, and the principles of mechanics, electricity, and electronics as they relate to the repair of business machines.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize decision-making processes for educational supervisors managing resource allocation across K-12 instructional environments. A critical challenge in educational leadership is dynamically aligning limited resources—such as staff, curricular materials, and professional development budgets—with evolving instructional needs, student demographics, and institutional goals. Traditional qualitative approaches often lack the scalability and predictive capacity to address these multidimensional constraints. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to build agent-based simulation models that integrate real-world data on school operations, staff performance metrics, and student outcomes. These models will simulate scenarios under variable constraints (e.g., budget cuts, shifting enrollment, curriculum updates) to identify resource distribution strategies that maximize instructional coherence and equity. Machine learning techniques will further refine predictive analytics by correlating historical allocation patterns with longitudinal academic performance data. The computational workload requires parallel processing to handle large-scale datasets from partner school districts, including anonymized records spanning 10+ years of staffing, standardized assessments, and curriculum adoption cycles. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for simulating resource allocation policies, validated against case studies from urban and rural districts. This work will provide educational supervisors with evidence-based strategies to balance operational demands with pedagogical priorities, particularly in under-resourced settings. By quantifying the impact of allocation decisions on instructional quality, the project aims to advance leadership practices in curriculum supervision while fostering equitable access to educational resources. The HPC infrastructure is essential to achieve the necessary computational throughput for scenario testing and sensitivity analyses at district-level granularity.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to supervise instructional and support personnel at the school building, facility or staff level. Includes instruction in the principles of staffing and organization, the supervision of learning activities, personnel relations, administrative duties related to departmental or unit management, and specific applications to various educational settings and curricula.

abstract: The sustainable production of bioenergy from plant and microbial feedstocks requires balancing environmental resilience, resource efficiency, and economic viability. Current models often fail to capture the complex, multi-scale interactions between bioprocessing dynamics, regional ecosystem constraints, and supply chain logistics, limiting the accuracy of sustainability assessments. This project seeks to address these gaps by developing an integrated computational framework to optimize bioenergy systems across spatial, temporal, and biological scales. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate feedstock cultivation impacts on watershed hydrology, microbial metabolic networks for biofuel conversion, and lifecycle emissions under diverse climate and land-use scenarios. Leveraging geospatial datasets, genome-scale metabolic models, and agent-based supply chain simulations, the framework will evaluate trade-offs between biofuel yield, water use, soil health, and economic returns. Computational workflows will combine machine learning for parameter optimization, hydrodynamic modeling to predict nutrient runoff, and flux balance analysis to engineer microbial consortia for enhanced bioseparations. By parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations across thousands of scenarios, the project will quantify uncertainties in feedstock viability under climate variability and identify region-specific strategies to minimize ecosystem disruption. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for policymakers and industry to prioritize bioenergy pathways that align with conservation goals, such as reducing freshwater withdrawals or protecting carbon-rich soils. The research will also advance methodologies for coupling ecological and bioprocess models—a critical step in scaling sustainable bioenergy. Access to HPC resources is vital to manage the petabyte-scale integration of remote sensing data, genomic databases, and real-time sensor inputs from partner biorefineries, enabling predictive analytics at unprecedented resolution. This work directly supports national priorities for decarbonizing energy systems while safeguarding natural resources.
detailed_field: Environmental/ natural resources management and policy
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the environmental and economic impact of using plants and microbes for the production of bio-based fuels such as ethanol and biodiesel. Includes instruction in biochemical engineering, bioprocessing, bioseparations, conversion, feedstock, economics, environmental sustainability, hydrology, and natural resource management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing hyper-personalized consumer merchandising strategies in dynamic retail environments, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address the scalability challenges of real-time, multi-modal data integration. Traditional approaches to consumer behavior modeling in retail management often rely on static demographic segments or aggregated historical sales data, limiting responsiveness to rapidly shifting preferences, cross-channel interactions, and contextual factors such as localized cultural trends or supply chain disruptions. The research problem centers on creating adaptive systems capable of synthesizing real-time inputs—including social sentiment analysis, in-store IoT sensor data, inventory fluctuations, and micro-influencer engagement metrics—into granular predictions of individual consumer actions at regional scales. The computational approach combines graph neural networks (GNNs) to model complex buyer-product-environment relationships, federated learning architectures to preserve privacy across decentralized retail partners, and agent-based simulations to stress-test promotion strategies under diverse market conditions. By deploying these models on HPC clusters, the project aims to achieve sub-hourly model retraining cycles across petabyte-scale datasets encompassing 50+ international markets. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for simulating the second-order effects of merchandising decisions on brand perception and supply chain resilience, validated through partnerships with three multinational retailers. This work bridges computational social science, distributed systems engineering, and retail operations management, offering novel methodologies for ethical hyper-personalization while avoiding surveillance capitalism paradigms. Successful implementation could reduce overstock waste by 18-22% in pilot sectors and improve marginalized consumer groups' access to culturally relevant products through predictive equity audits embedded in the optimization pipeline.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on product and service promotion from the perspective of individual and family consumers and that prepares individuals to function as consumer management and marketing consultants in for-profit and non-profit enterprises. Includes instruction in applied market research, consumer behavior, product sourcing and distribution, profitability, customer feedback and evaluation methods, promotion and retailing campaign development, and applications to specific domestic and international consumer markets.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale textual analysis study examining how writers adapt compositional strategies across genres, media, and cultural contexts. While traditional writing studies rely on manual close reading or small-sample qualitative methods, this research addresses the challenge of systematically analyzing stylistic, rhetorical, and linguistic patterns in heterogeneous digital writing corpora spanning professional, academic, and public domains. The computational approach integrates natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques to model compositional features—such as syntactic complexity, multimodal integration, audience adaptation markers, and genre-specific discourse structures—across millions of documents. Key tasks include training transformer-based models on domain-specific writing samples, conducting cross-corpus rhetorical analysis via graph-based representation learning, and simulating audience reception through agent-based modeling. HPC resources are critical for processing terabytes of text and multimedia data, running parallelized feature extraction pipelines, and iteratively refining computational models that account for the dynamic interplay between writerly choices and contextual constraints. Anticipated outcomes include 1) scalable frameworks for mapping writing practices in digitally mediated environments, 2) open-access tools to support adaptive writing pedagogy through data-driven genre analysis, and 3) theoretical contributions to understanding how emerging writing technologies reshape compositional processes. By bridging computational methods with writing studies’ humanistic foundations, this project aims to provide novel insights into the sociotechnical dimensions of contemporary writing while demonstrating how HPC can expand the scale and precision of textual research in the humanities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on writing for applied and liberal arts purposes. Includes instruction in writing and document design in multiple genres, modes, and media; writing technologies; research, evaluation, and use of information; editing and publishing; theories and processes of composing; rhetorical theories, traditions, and analysis; communication across audiences, contexts, and cultures; and practical applications for professional, technical, organizational, academic, and public settings.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the role of ecological interactions and environmental shifts in shaping macroevolutionary patterns of morphological diversity across deep time. A critical gap persists in linking fine-scale biomechanical constraints and adaptive landscapes to long-term phenotypic evolution, particularly in vertebrate clades with complex functional traits. To address this, we propose integrating fossil-derived morphometric datasets with computational simulations of phenotypic adaptation under dynamic environmental scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute agent-based models that simulate selection pressures on biomechanical traits (e.g., craniodental morphology, limb biomechanics) across phylogenies, while accounting for stochastic extinction and speciation events. These models will incorporate 3D geometric morphometric data from fossil and extant species, coupled with paleoclimate proxies, to quantify how functional trade-offs and environmental gradients interact to drive evolutionary radiations or stasis. Additionally, large-scale phylogenetic comparative analyses will be conducted using Bayesian frameworks to infer rates of morphological evolution and test hypotheses about adaptive convergence. The computational workload involves iterative simulations across parameter spaces representing varying selection regimes, necessitating parallel processing and substantial memory allocation. Expected outcomes include identifying biomechanical and ecological thresholds that precipitate major evolutionary transitions, such as locomotor adaptations in response to habitat fragmentation. This work will advance systematic biology by bridging microevolutionary processes with macroevolutionary trends, offering a predictive framework for how clades respond to environmental perturbations. Results will also inform conservation paleobiology, providing empirical benchmarks for assessing modern biodiversity loss. The requested HPC resources will enable processing of terabytes of morphometric data and reduce runtime for complex simulations from months to days, ensuring feasibility within project timelines.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the genetic, developmental, functional, and morphological patterns and processes, and theoretical principles; and the emergence and mutation of organisms over time. Includes instruction in molecular and morphological systematics; genetics and development; evolutionary transformation; paleobiology and paleontology; morphogenesis; mutation; locomotor, biomechanical and craniodental form and function; evolutionary theory; and systematic biology.

abstract: This project seeks to advance metallurgical process optimization through high-fidelity computational modeling of phase transformations in industrial alloys under dynamic thermal and mechanical conditions. A critical challenge in metallurgical technology is predicting microstructure evolution during heat treatment and forming operations, as existing empirical models struggle to account for multi-scale interactions between grain boundary dynamics, solute diffusion, and stress-strain heterogeneity. To address this, we propose a multi-physics framework combining phase-field modeling with crystal plasticity finite element methods, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to resolve spatially and temporally varying phenomena across relevant length scales (nanometers to millimeters). The computational workflow will integrate open-source tools (e.g., MOOSE Framework) with custom solvers for alloy-specific thermodynamics, validated against experimental dilatometry and electron backscatter diffraction data from collaborating industrial partners. Simulations will target two industrially significant systems: (1) carbide precipitation in tool steels during tempering, and (2) recrystallization kinetics in aluminum-magnesium alloys under hot rolling conditions. The HPC resources will enable parametric studies across process variable spaces (heating/cooling rates, strain rates, initial textures) that are experimentally prohibitive to explore. Expected outcomes include predictive models correlating thermal-mechanical histories with final microstructure attributes (grain size, phase distribution, defect density), directly informing process optimization for enhanced hardness and fatigue resistance in manufactured components. By bridging the gap between laboratory-scale characterization and production-scale metallurgy, this work will provide technologists with computational tools to reduce trial-and-error in alloy development while maintaining alignment with industry-standard testing and quality control protocols. The requested computing resources are essential given the memory-intensive nature of 3D microstructure simulations and the need for high-throughput parameter sweeps to establish statistically robust process-structure-property relationships.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and metallurgists engaged in developing and using industrial metals and manufacturing processes. Includes instruction in principles of metallurgy, related manufacturing systems, laboratory techniques, testing and inspection procedures, instrument calibration, system and equipment maintenance and repair, applications to specific processes, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical challenges in computational linguistics research focused on American Sign Language (ASL). ASL, as a visual-gestural language with complex morphological and syntactic structures, presents unique analytical hurdles that traditional text- or audio-based computational models struggle to capture. Current tools for ASL processing—such as automated transcription, syntactic parsing, and translation into English—remain underdeveloped due to the spatial, dynamic, and multi-channel nature of signing. This research aims to bridge this gap by developing scalable computational methods to analyze large-scale ASL video corpora, model linguistic patterns, and simulate historical language evolution within Deaf communities. The project will employ machine learning frameworks, including 3D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformer-based architectures, to process temporal-spatial features of sign production, alongside graph-based models to represent syntactic dependencies. These methods require intensive parallel computing for training on multi-modal datasets (video, motion capture, and gloss annotations) and for running simulations of ASL morphological variation across regional dialects. A key innovation involves adapting natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to handle ASL’s non-linear grammar, enabling automated segmentation of signs into morphemic components and improving translation fidelity. Outcomes will include open-source tools for ASL linguistic analysis, datasets annotated with computational syntax trees, and quantitative models of ASL’s historical development. By advancing computational support for ASL research, this work will enhance linguistic scholarship on visual languages, inform the design of assistive technologies for Deaf individuals, and contribute to the preservation of ASL as a cultural and educational resource. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the high-dimensional data and iterative model training demanded by this research, which cannot feasibly be conducted on standard computing infrastructure.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on American Sign Language as a visual and motor medium of communication and discourse for deaf individuals and deaf culture. Includes instruction in the development of ASL, ASL morphology and syntax, signing technique, English translation of ASL, formal and colloquial ASL, and ASL transcription.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the dynamic interactions between household consumption patterns, retail market fluctuations, and macroeconomic policy impacts within the context of Business Family and Consumer Sciences. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how micro-level family economic decisions aggregate to influence regional retail ecosystems, particularly under conditions of economic volatility. Traditional analytical methods lack the capacity to process high-dimensional datasets—including real-time consumer spending data, demographic variables, and supply chain logistics—while accounting for nonlinear feedback loops between household behavior and market responses. To overcome these limitations, the project proposes an agent-based modeling (ABM) approach enhanced by machine learning techniques, simulating decision-making processes across diverse household archetypes and business entities. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute large-scale parallel simulations, train predictive models on heterogeneous data streams (e.g., transaction records, social sentiment analysis), and optimize scenario testing for policy interventions. Computational workflows will integrate econometric models with behavioral theory to quantify resilience thresholds in family budgeting strategies and evaluate the cascading effects of retail pricing algorithms on household welfare. Expected outcomes include a novel decision-support toolkit for policymakers and business leaders to anticipate unintended consequences of economic shocks, optimize resource allocation in community support programs, and improve equity in access to essential goods. The project’s interdisciplinary methodology bridges computational social science, consumer economics, and data-driven family resource management, establishing a replicable framework for analyzing complex socio-economic systems at unprecedented scale. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work advances both theoretical understanding of consumption ecosystems and practical strategies for enhancing household economic security in rapidly evolving markets.
cip_title: Business Family and Consumer Sciences/ Human Sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the relationship between the economy and the consuming individual and family. Includes instruction in consumption theory and practice, the production and distribution of retail goods and services, and the management of business enterprises.

abstract: Gastrointestinal disorders, such as inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and colorectal cancer, involve complex interactions between genetic, immunological, and microbial factors. Current clinical approaches often lack predictive precision due to the multifactorial nature of these conditions, necessitating advanced computational models to unravel underlying mechanisms. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-omics datasets (genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metagenomic) from patient cohorts, integrating these with clinical data to identify biomarkers and therapeutic targets. A key challenge lies in processing and interpreting the high-dimensional, heterogeneous data generated by next-generation sequencing and mass spectrometry, which demands scalable computational infrastructure. We propose a hybrid machine learning and network biology approach to model disease pathways, host-microbiome interactions, and treatment response variability. Deep learning architectures, including graph neural networks, will be trained on multi-omics data to predict disease progression and drug efficacy, while mechanistic agent-based models will simulate mucosal immune dynamics in silico. The computational workflow will require parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets, optimization of hyperparameters across thousands of concurrent jobs, and real-time visualization of spatial-temporal simulations. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel microbial signatures associated with IBD subtypes, predictive models for personalized biologic therapy selection, and a publicly accessible computational platform for simulating gut inflammation scenarios. By elucidating the systems-level drivers of gastrointestinal pathology, this work aims to advance precision medicine in gastroenterology, reducing diagnostic delays and optimizing therapeutic strategies. The requested HPC resources are critical to achieving the project’s goals, as standard clinical workstations lack the capacity to handle the computational intensity of these analyses. Successful implementation will provide a template for data-driven gastroenterology research, bridging clinical observations with molecular mechanisms at scale.
cip_definition: Research focused on Gastroenterology

abstract: Pediatric infectious diseases present unique challenges due to the dynamic interplay between developing immune systems, pathogen evolution, and heterogenous clinical outcomes. Current limitations in predicting disease progression, optimizing treatment regimens, and understanding host-pathogen interactions in children necessitate advanced computational approaches. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-modal clinical, genomic, and immunological datasets from pediatric patients with complex or treatment-resistant infections. We will employ machine learning models to integrate longitudinal electronic health records, pathogen whole-genome sequencing, and single-cell immune profiling data from cohorts of children with sepsis, recurrent antibiotic-resistant infections, and rare tropical diseases. Computational workflows will identify biomarkers of disease severity, predict responses to antimicrobial therapies, and model immune reconstitution patterns during recovery. Molecular dynamics simulations will further investigate how age-specific variations in host proteins influence pathogen binding and drug efficacy. By parallelizing these analyses across HPC nodes, we aim to overcome bottlenecks in processing high-dimensional datasets and achieve the resolution required to dissect pediatric-specific disease mechanisms. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms to guide personalized antimicrobial selection, novel insights into age-related susceptibility factors, and optimized dosing strategies for investigational therapies in children. This work will directly inform clinical trials and bedside decision-making for infections with high morbidity in pediatric populations, ultimately reducing treatment failures and long-term complications. The requested computing resources are essential to handle the scale and complexity of these analyses, which cannot feasibly be executed on local clinical research infrastructure.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of infectious diseases in children; and to effect a better outcome for pediatric infections with complicated courses, underlying diseases that predispose to unusual or severe infections, unclear diagnoses, uncommon diseases, and complex or investigational treatments.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the coupled thermal-hydrological-mechanical-chemical (THMC) processes governing the formation of magmatic-hydrothermal ore deposits, with a focus on porphyry copper systems. A critical gap exists in understanding how dynamic feedbacks between fluid flow, fracture propagation, and mineral precipitation control the localization of economic metal concentrations. Current laboratory experiments and field observations cannot resolve the spatial-temporal scales of these interactions, while existing numerical models often oversimplify multi-physics couplings. We propose to develop 3D high-resolution simulations integrating computational fluid dynamics, geomechanics, and reactive transport modeling using open-source codes (e.g., OpenFOAM, PFLOTRAN) modified with custom constitutive relationships for rock deformation and sulfide precipitation kinetics. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to handle the nonlinear system of partial differential equations across heterogeneous domains exceeding 10^8 grid cells, with adaptive meshing for evolving fracture networks. Machine learning techniques will be applied to reduce computational costs in sensitivity analyses of key parameters (e.g., magma chamber depth, host rock permeability). The simulations will be validated against petrological data from well-characterized porphyry deposits and experimental fracture-sealing datasets. Expected outcomes include (1) quantitative models linking geophysical signals (seismic velocity, resistivity) to subsurface mineralization patterns, (2) predictive frameworks for ore deposit geometry based on pre-mineralization lithospheric conditions, and (3) open-access code modules for THMC modeling in igneous systems. This work will provide novel constraints on the timescales of ore-forming processes while advancing computational methods for analyzing multi-physics interactions in geochemistry. The requested HPC allocation will enable parameter space exploration at unprecedented resolution, addressing fundamental questions about energy and mass transfer during upper crustal magma degassing.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the igneous, metamorphic, and hydrothermal processes within the earth and the mineral, fluid, rock, and ore deposits resulting from them. Includes instruction in mineralogy, crystallography, petrology, volcanology, economic geology, meteoritics, geochemical reactions, deposition, compound transformation, core studies, theoretical geochemistry, computer applications, and laboratory studies.

abstract: The proliferation of digital workflows in modern printing demands advanced computational tools to optimize press operations, reduce material waste, and improve color accuracy. This project seeks to address inefficiencies in analog and hybrid printing systems by developing machine learning models to predict optimal press configurations under variable substrate, ink, and environmental conditions. Current industry practices rely on operator experience and trial-and-error adjustments, leading to significant material waste and downtime. The proposed research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-physics interactions in offset and digital printing processes, including ink transfer dynamics, paper deformation, and drying behavior. A hybrid computational approach will combine finite element analysis (FEA) for mechanical stress modeling with convolutional neural networks (CNNs) trained on high-resolution spectral imaging data of print defects. Researchers will validate models using real-world data from sensor-equipped Heidelberg Speedmaster and HP Indigo presses, provided by industry partners. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for predictive press calibration that reduces setup waste by an estimated 15-30% while maintaining color consistency across substrates. The computational workflows developed will also enable virtual training environments for press operators, addressing skill gaps in an evolving industry. By integrating HPC-driven simulations with practical printing workflows, this project bridges a critical gap between traditional print production and computational engineering methods, offering measurable sustainability benefits for the communication and journalism sectors reliant on physical media. Resource allocation will specifically support GPU-accelerated training of defect detection models and large-scale parameter sweeps to account for diverse material combinations in commercial printing.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to set up, operate, and maintain printing presses.

abstract: Polymer chemistry faces significant challenges in predicting and controlling the dynamic behavior of synthesized macromolecules under varying environmental and operational conditions. A critical unsolved problem lies in understanding how polymerization pathways, molecular architecture, and intermolecular interactions collectively influence the stability, reactivity, and phase transitions of functional polymers. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model polymerization kinetics, polymer-solvent dynamics, and degradation mechanisms at atomistic and mesoscopic scales. The proposed work will employ molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with reactive force fields to track bond formation/cleavage during polymerization, hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) methods to study electronic interactions in catalytic polymer systems, and coarse-grained models to probe long-timescale phase behavior. These simulations will be validated against experimental data from collaborators on polymer rheology and spectroscopic characterization. The computational workflow requires large-scale parallelization to manage systems containing >100,000 atoms over microsecond trajectories, as well as advanced sampling techniques to access rare transition states in degradation pathways. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive frameworks for designing polymers with tailored thermal stability and solvent resistance, (2) mechanistic insights into how branching density and copolymer sequences affect ion transport in electrolyte applications, and (3) identification of kinetic bottlenecks in sustainable polymer upcycling processes. By bridging molecular-scale interactions to bulk material properties, this research will directly inform the synthesis of next-generation polymers for energy storage and environmentally degradable materials. The requested HPC resources are essential to overcome current limitations in system size and sampling fidelity, enabling unprecedented resolution of transient intermediates and interfacial phenomena critical to industrial polymer applications.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of synthesized macromolecules and their interactions with other substances. Includes instruction in molecular bonding theory, polymerization, properties and behavior of unstable compounds, the development of tailored polymers, transition phenomena, and applications to specific industrial problems and technologies.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the operational dynamics and socio-cultural impacts of military logistics in 19th-century conflicts, with a focus on the Napoleonic Wars and the American Civil War. Traditional historiography often treats logistical systems as static or secondary to battlefield tactics, but emerging digitized datasets—including supply chain records, troop movement logs, and regional economic data—enable a granular, data-driven reassessment of how logistics shaped strategic outcomes and civilian experiences. The research problem centers on quantifying relationships between logistical efficiency, resource allocation, and societal disruption across diverse theaters of war, accounting for variables such as terrain, technology, and institutional decision-making. Computational methods will include agent-based modeling to simulate supply networks under stochastic conditions (e.g., weather, sabotage), natural language processing (NLP) to extract qualitative insights from officers’ correspondence and civilian accounts, and geospatial network analysis to map logistical bottlenecks and their demographic consequences. These approaches require HPC capabilities to manage terabyte-scale datasets, parallelize simulations across thousands of parameter combinations, and train transformer models on multilingual archival texts. Expected outcomes include identifying previously overlooked patterns in how logistical constraints amplified or mitigated asymmetries between professional and conscripted forces, as well as creating open-access visualization tools to model “what-if” scenarios (e.g., alternative supply routes). The project aims to advance military historiography by integrating quantitative computational methods with traditional archival analysis, offering a template for interdisciplinary research at the intersection of operational history and socio-cultural inquiry. Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed journals, a public database of annotated logistical maps, and workshops for historians on computational methods.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the history of warfare and military institutions in their operational, politico-economic and socio-cultural contexts; including airpower history, naval history, and military history. Includes instruction in military organization, military operations, the history of technology, leadership and biography, military psychology and behavior, international relations and politics, economics, aspects of general and regional history, cultural history and anthropology, historiography, and applicable quantitative methods.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of nonlinear consumer decision processes in fragmented, hyperlocal markets. Traditional marketing research methods struggle to capture the dynamic interplay of geospatial, socioeconomic, and behavioral variables in rapidly evolving urban micro-markets, particularly where digital and physical consumer touchpoints converge. The study addresses this gap by developing a computational framework that integrates real-time mobility data, social media sentiment streams, and granular transaction records to model emergent purchasing patterns at neighborhood-level resolution. Using GPU-accelerated graph neural networks, the project will process terabyte-scale datasets spanning 12 metropolitan regions to identify latent decision pathways influenced by microcultural trends and infrastructure disruptions. A parallelized agent-based modeling system will simulate market responses to localized promotional strategies under varying economic scenarios, requiring iterative optimization of millions of parameter combinations. The computational workflow demands distributed memory architectures for spatial-temporal pattern recognition and high-throughput scaling for Monte Carlo simulations of intervention impacts. Expected outcomes include a novel metric for "neighborhood decision inertia" capable of predicting adoption thresholds for new services, along with an open-source toolkit for hyperlocal campaign optimization. By enabling sub-24-hour recalibration of marketing mixes for microgeographic segments, this research aims to establish a new paradigm for adaptive resource allocation in urban consumer markets while contributing methodological innovations at the intersection of computational social science and marketing analytics. The HPC infrastructure is critical for maintaining chain-of-custody validation across heterogeneous data sources and achieving the necessary processing speeds for real-world applicability in fast-moving consumer goods sectors.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide analytical descriptions of consumer behavior patterns and market environments to marketing managers and other business decision-makers. Includes instruction in survey research methods, research design, new product test marketing, exploratory marketing, consumer needs and preferences analysis, geographic analysis, and applications to specific products and markets.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop an adaptive, real-time decision-support framework for optimizing cross-border freight logistics under volatile regulatory and environmental conditions, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address inefficiencies in customs and transportation workflows. Current systems struggle to dynamically reconcile fluctuating tariffs, evolving trade agreements, and last-mile congestion—particularly in multimodal transport corridors—leading to cascading delays and revenue leakage. The proposed work integrates heterogeneous data streams (e.g., IoT-enabled cargo sensors, regional tariff databases, and weather APIs) with machine learning models to predict inspection probabilities, optimize toll payment sequencing, and preemptively reroute fleets. Computational challenges include training graph neural networks on continental-scale transportation networks (modeled as dynamic hypergraphs with 10^6+ nodes) and solving mixed-integer linear programming models for route optimization under stochastic delay constraints. HPC resources will enable parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to quantify risk exposure across 10,000+ scenario permutations, as well as federated learning across synthetic data representing proprietary customs declarations from 15+ trade jurisdictions. Expected outcomes include: (1) a probabilistic routing engine that reduces mean border wait times by 18-25% in simulated North American trade corridors; (2) anomaly detection algorithms identifying high-risk shipments with 92% precision to streamline customs inspections; and (3) open-source APIs enabling transportation clerks to deploy optimized toll payment sequences in real time. By computationally harmonizing revenue management, regulatory compliance, and fleet telematics, this work advances intelligent transportation systems while addressing critical gaps in business-focused, non-administrative logistics research. The resulting framework will be validated against historical data from cross-border freight operators, with scalability testing for emerging challenges like carbon tariff integration and drone corridor prioritization.
cip_title: Traffic, Customs, and Transportation Clerk/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform duties associated with managing revenue-based customs, traffic, or transportation services, such as control of domestic and international traffic, toll roads and waterways, and to assist in the dispatch and control of fleet-based traffic for businesses and public services. Includes instruction in record-keeping; preparation of customs and transportation documentation; operation of communications equipment; basic transportation operations management; tariffs, rates and fares; revenue collection and change-making; and interpretation of customs or transportation regulations and related legislation, policies, and procedures.

abstract: Cardiac arrhythmias remain a significant cause of morbidity and mortality, with treatment efficacy limited by incomplete understanding of patient-specific arrhythmia mechanisms. Current clinical approaches to ablation therapy rely on intraprocedural mapping, which may fail to account for dynamic electrophysiological properties or heterogeneous substrate interactions. This project proposes a computational framework to model arrhythmia initiation and propagation using patient-derived cardiac imaging and electrophysiological data, aiming to optimize preprocedural planning for catheter ablation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to address the multiscale, nonlinear dynamics of cardiac electrophysiology, which involve solving coupled partial differential equations across high-resolution, anatomically accurate geometries. We will employ finite element methods to simulate action potential propagation using monodomain or bidomain formulations, incorporating tissue anisotropy, fibrosis distribution, and ion channel heterogeneity derived from clinical MRI/CT and voltage mapping data. Machine learning approaches will be integrated to identify predictive features of arrhythmia sustainability from simulated and clinical datasets. The computational pipeline will require parallel processing for parameter optimization, sensitivity analyses, and large-scale cohort simulations. Expected outcomes include validated models predicting optimal ablation targets in atrial fibrillation and ventricular tachycardia cases, correlating simulation results with procedural outcomes from retrospective clinical data. This work will establish a translational bridge between computational cardiology and clinical practice, enabling personalized ablation strategies that account for spatiotemporal complexity inaccessible to conventional diagnostic tools. The requested HPC allocation will support GPU-accelerated simulations, storage of high-fidelity simulation outputs (>100 TB), and iterative model training, which are computationally prohibitive on local infrastructure. Successful implementation could reduce procedural time, radiation exposure, and arrhythmia recurrence rates, advancing precision medicine in cardiac electrophysiology.
cip_definition: Research focused on, within the subspecialty of cardiovascular disease, which prepares physicians in intricate technical procedures to evaluate heart rhythms and determine appropriate treatment.

abstract: This research seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize the integration of dynamic environmental factors—such as fluctuating microclimates, occupant behavior patterns, and real-time energy grid interactions—into adaptive building systems. Current architectural simulations often rely on static models or averaged datasets, limiting their ability to predict performance in increasingly variable urban environments. The project addresses this gap by creating a high-resolution, agent-based modeling platform that synthesizes real-time sensor data, climate projections, and occupant interaction data to simulate building performance under non-stationary conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the framework will employ parallelized Monte Carlo methods to assess probabilistic outcomes of design interventions across thousands of stochastic scenarios, while machine learning techniques will identify optimal adaptive control strategies for building systems. Key challenges include scaling agent-based occupant behavior models to urban densities, resolving microclimate interactions at sub-meter resolutions, and minimizing latency in co-simulations with live energy grid data. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for adaptive building system design, predictive metrics for resilience under climate volatility, and energy-saving protocols that dynamically align building operations with grid decarbonization targets. This work bridges architectural design, urban data science, and distributed systems engineering, offering a replicable methodology for transitioning static building stocks into responsive energy nodes within smart city networks. By quantifying the value of computational agility in building operations, the project aims to inform both retrofitting priorities and next-generation architectural standards, with particular relevance to municipalities targeting net-zero carbon commitments. The requested HPC allocation will enable the intensive parameter space exploration required to generalize findings across diverse climate zones and building typologies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of advanced technology to building design and construction, retrofitting existing buildings, and efficient operation of buildings, including lighting and daylight design, acoustics, solar design, building conservation, and energy-conscious design. Includes instruction in architecture, building technology, civil and structural engineering, mechanical engineering, environmental control systems, sustainability, and computer tools and applications.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of designing stable, efficient biohybrid interfaces that integrate synthetic cellular components with inorganic electronic systems for next-generation biosensing applications. While bioelectronic devices hold promise for real-time monitoring of biomarkers or environmental contaminants, their development is hindered by unpredictable interactions between engineered biological modules (e.g., synthetic lipid membranes, redox-active enzymes) and solid-state surfaces. Traditional trial-and-error approaches struggle to account for the dynamic molecular-scale processes governing charge transfer, interfacial stability, and signal fidelity. To overcome this, we propose a computational framework combining coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) simulations with machine learning-driven optimization to model and predict biointerface behavior. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale CGMD simulations of synthetic cell membranes interacting with nanostructured electrodes under varying electrochemical conditions, capturing phase transitions, protein denaturation, and ion diffusion phenomena. Concurrently, neural networks trained on simulation outputs and experimental datasets will identify optimal pairings of biological components (e.g., genetically modified transmembrane proteins) and electrode materials (e.g., graphene variants, conductive polymers) to maximize signal-to-noise ratios. The project’s computational pipeline will be validated against experimental collaborations fabricating prototype biosensors for dopamine detection, with iterative feedback refining models. Expected outcomes include a predictive atlas of biointerface design rules, reducing development cycles for biosensors by >40%. This work bridges synthetic biology and materials science, advancing foundational knowledge of biotic-abiotic integration while directly supporting applications in precision medicine and decentralized environmental monitoring. By establishing scalable computational strategies to navigate the vast combinatorial space of biohybrid designs, the project addresses a critical bottleneck in translational biotechnology, where interdisciplinary tools are urgently needed to accelerate innovation at the convergence of living and engineered systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of the biological sciences, biochemistry, and genetics to the preparation of new and enhanced agricultural, environmental, clinical, and industrial products, including the commercial exploitation of microbes, plants, and animals. Includes instruction in bioinformatics, gene identification, phylogenetics and comparative genomics, bioinorganic chemistry, immunoassaying, DNA sequencing, xenotransplantation, genetic engineering, industrial microbiology, drug and biologic development, enzyme-based production processes, patent law, biotechnology management and marketing, applicable regulations, and biotechnology ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance clinical decision-support tools tailored to physician assistant (PA) education and practice. The research problem centers on the growing complexity of patient data in primary care settings, where PAs frequently manage cases with overlapping chronic conditions. Current predictive models for treatment outcomes often fail to account for multi-morbidity interactions, leading to suboptimal recommendations. To address this gap, we propose developing a machine learning framework that integrates electronic health record (EHR) data, genomic biomarkers, and social determinants of health to predict individualized treatment responses. The computational approach involves training ensemble models on multi-modal datasets encompassing 500,000+ de-identified patient records, including longitudinal lab results, medication histories, and demographic variables. Deep neural networks will be optimized to identify nonlinear interactions between comorbidities, while natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will extract contextual insights from clinical notes. HPC resources are critical for managing the scale of these computations, particularly for parallelized hyperparameter tuning of ensemble architectures and GPU-accelerated NLP tasks. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source predictive modeling toolkit optimized for PA training programs, (2) validation of key biomarkers influencing treatment efficacy in patients with ≥3 chronic conditions, and (3) a web-based simulation interface for PA students to explore clinical scenarios derived from real-world data patterns. By integrating HPC-driven analytics with PA educational workflows, this work aims to bridge gaps between computational medicine and clinical training, ultimately enhancing evidence-based decision-making skills for future practitioners. The resource request prioritizes GPU node allocations for model training and scalable storage solutions to host anonymized datasets compliant with HIPAA security standards.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional physician assistant program.

abstract: This project seeks to advance engineering education by developing data-driven frameworks to optimize the design and delivery of adaptive, scalable virtual learning environments (VLEs) for complex engineering concepts. A critical challenge in engineering pedagogy lies in effectively translating abstract, system-level principles—such as those in cyber-physical systems or sustainable infrastructure design—into immersive, personalized educational experiences. Current VLEs often rely on static simulations or limited interactivity, which fail to capture the dynamic, interdependent variables inherent to modern engineering systems. To address this gap, we propose a computational research initiative leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model learner interactions, simulate multi-physics educational scenarios, and iteratively optimize pedagogical strategies. The project will employ agent-based modeling to simulate diverse student cohorts interacting with adaptive VLE modules, coupled with reinforcement learning algorithms to dynamically refine content delivery based on real-time performance metrics. Large-scale parametric studies will assess how variations in problem complexity, feedback latency, and visualization fidelity impact conceptual mastery. Computational fluid dynamics simulations will also be integrated to create interactive scenarios for teaching fluid-structure interaction concepts within renewable energy systems. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing high-dimensional interaction data from simulated and real-world learners, training predictive models of skill acquisition trajectories, and rendering multi-scale educational simulations. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for generating context-aware VLEs that automatically adjust complexity thresholds and scaffolding mechanisms, as well as open-source tools for quantifying the resource-performance tradeoffs in virtual engineering education platforms. By establishing computational links between pedagogical theory, cognitive load dynamics, and engineering system behaviors, this work aims to bridge critical gaps in scalable, evidence-based engineering education for emerging interdisciplinary domains.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach engineering and/or engineering subject matter areas, at various educational levels. Includes instruction in general engineering principals or at least one specific engineering discipline and in educational curriculum, instruction, pedagogy.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize mineral extraction processes in underground mines through high-fidelity modeling of rock fragmentation and ore transport dynamics. The research addresses critical inefficiencies in traditional blasting and material handling methods, which often lead to energy waste, equipment wear, and safety risks due to unpredictable fracture propagation and discontinuous flow patterns. We propose a multi-scale simulation approach combining discrete element method (DEM) modeling of fracture mechanics with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for slurry transport analysis, integrated through machine learning-based surrogate models. The computational workflow will process site-specific geological data, including heterogeneous rock strata mappings and real-time sensor feeds from borehole instrumentation, to predict optimal blast patterns and conveyor system configurations. High-performance computing resources are essential to resolve the 10^8+ particle interactions in DEM simulations of bulk rock behavior, coupled with three-dimensional multiphase CFD models of ore-water mixtures at operational scales. Expected outcomes include a decision support tool capable of reducing energy consumption in fragmentation processes by 15-20%, minimizing ore dilution through improved fragmentation targeting, and extending equipment lifespan via predictive wear modeling. The computational platform will also enable scenario testing for novel sensor deployment strategies to enhance mine safety monitoring systems. By leveraging parallelized GPU-accelerated computing for near-real-time simulations, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for adaptive mine operations that responds dynamically to changing geological conditions while maintaining compliance with environmental and safety regulations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in the development and operation of mines and related mineral processing facilities. Includes instruction in principles of mineral extraction and related geology, mineral field mapping and site analysis, testing and sampling methods, instrument calibration, assay analysis, test equipment operation and maintenance, mine environment and safety monitoring procedures, mine inspection procedures, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze large-scale, multimodal datasets of classroom interactions and instructional practices in STEM teacher education. A critical challenge in teacher professional development is the lack of scalable tools to evaluate how novice educators implement evidence-based pedagogical strategies in real-world settings. Current manual observation protocols are resource-intensive and fail to capture longitudinal patterns across diverse teaching contexts. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and model video recordings, audio transcripts, and digital lesson artifacts from 500+ classroom sessions involving pre-service science and mathematics teachers. Machine learning pipelines will be developed to automatically code instructional moves (e.g., questioning techniques, formative assessment practices) using transformer-based NLP models and computer vision algorithms trained on established observation rubrics. Graph neural networks will then analyze temporal relationships between teaching behaviors and student engagement metrics derived from multimodal signals. The computational demands of processing 40+ terabytes of video data, training domain-specific large language models on educational discourse, and running iterative simulations of pedagogical scenario outcomes necessitate GPU-accelerated nodes and distributed storage systems. Expected outcomes include 1) an open-source toolkit for automated teacher practice analysis, 2) evidence-based insights into high-leverage teaching competencies that predict early-career effectiveness, and 3) synthetic training modules generated through agent-based modeling of classroom dynamics. By enabling unprecedented scalability in pedagogical analytics, this work aims to transform how teacher preparation programs diagnose skill gaps and personalize professional learning trajectories, ultimately strengthening STEM instruction in secondary education.
cip_title: Teacher Education and Professional Development, Specific Subject Areas, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in teacher education, specific academic and vocational programs, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive learning technologies tailored for students with low-incidence disabilities, such as complex communication needs or severe cognitive impairments. A critical challenge in special education is designing individualized interventions that account for highly variable learning profiles, sensory processing differences, and non-traditional response modalities. Current approaches often rely on static curricula or manual data analysis, limiting educators’ capacity to dynamically adjust instruction based on real-time student engagement. To address this gap, the research integrates multimodal data streams—including eye-tracking, gesture recognition, and biometric sensors—with machine learning models to predict optimal instructional pathways. Computational workflows will process terabytes of heterogeneous data from classroom observations and assistive technology logs, employing ensemble neural networks to identify patterns in skill acquisition trajectories. HPC resources are essential for training these models at scale, enabling parallelized hyperparameter optimization and synthetic data generation to account for sparse populations. The project further simulates virtual learning environments via agent-based modeling to test intervention strategies under diverse disability profiles before real-world implementation. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source framework for generating personalized special education content and a predictive dashboard to guide teacher decision-making. By reducing the computational barriers to analyzing rare or complex disability datasets, this work aims to democratize access to evidence-based tools for educators serving students with understudied needs, ultimately fostering more equitable learning opportunities.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in special education, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Vascular and Interventional Radiology (VIR) faces critical challenges in optimizing image-guided therapeutic outcomes while minimizing procedural risks, particularly in complex cases involving multi-vessel disease, aberrant anatomy, or advanced pathologies. Current clinical decision-making relies on static imaging and empirical protocols, which inadequately account for patient-specific hemodynamic variations or device-tissue interactions. This project proposes to develop a computational framework integrating real-time imaging data with patient-specific biomechanical simulations to predict outcomes of endovascular interventions. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement fluid-structure interaction models simulating blood flow dynamics, stent deployment mechanics, and embolic agent dispersion across diverse vascular geometries derived from clinical angiographic, CT, and MRI datasets. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on retrospective procedural data to identify predictive features for complications such as stent malapposition or non-target embolization. Computational demands include large-scale parallel processing for 3D hemodynamic simulations, GPU-accelerated deep learning for image segmentation, and ensemble modeling to quantify uncertainty in treatment predictions. Expected outcomes include: (1) validated predictive models for post-interventional outcomes, (2) optimized device selection protocols based on computational prototyping, and (3) an open-source toolkit for real-time simulation-assisted intervention planning. This work addresses a critical gap in personalized interventional radiology by enabling data-driven treatment customization, with potential to reduce revision rates in procedures ranging from visceral artery stenting to tumor embolization. The requested HPC allocation will support the iterative refinement of multiscale models requiring >10,000 core-hours per patient simulation, including validation against a 500-case clinical registry. By bridging computational engineering with clinical VIR practice, this project aims to establish a paradigm shift toward simulation-enhanced image-guided therapy, directly aligning with national priorities for precision medicine in minimally invasive interventions.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares diagnostic radiologists with additional training in image-guided therapies, using fluoroscopy, digital radiography, computed tomography, sonography, and magnetic resonance imaging, to guide small devices inserted into the body through very small openings. These therapies include angioplasty, stent placement, thrombolysis, embolization, biliary and genitourinary drainages, and abscess drainages.

abstract: The physics of polymer systems in melt, solution, and solid states presents unresolved challenges in understanding how multi-scale structural evolution governs macroscopic material behavior. Existing coarse-grained models often fail to capture the interplay between entropic driving forces, topological constraints, and long-range correlations that dictate phenomena such as non-Newtonian flow, glass transition dynamics, and strain-induced crystallization. This project seeks to address these gaps through large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) and hybrid Monte Carlo-MD simulations of model polymer systems under varied thermodynamic and deformation conditions. The research will focus on three interconnected objectives: (1) quantifying the role of chain entanglement density in governing viscoelastic response during nonlinear shear flows, (2) characterizing the coupling between segmental mobility and collective rearrangements near the glass transition, and (3) mapping free energy landscapes for stress-induced crystallization in semi-flexible polymers. Simulations will employ modified Kremer-Grest bead-spring models with tunable persistence lengths and interaction potentials, scaled to system sizes exceeding 10^6 particles to ensure proper representation of long-chain dynamics. Parallel tempering methods will enhance sampling efficiency for glassy systems. High-performance computing resources are essential to achieve the required spatial and temporal resolution, particularly for resolving sub-diffusive motion in entangled melts (10^5-10^7 τ Lennard-Jones time units) and capturing rare nucleation events during crystallization. Expected outcomes include predictive relationships between molecular architecture and bulk rheological properties, validation of mode-coupling theory extensions for polymer glasses, and quantitative criteria for strain-induced phase transitions. The generated datasets will establish structure-property connections at previously inaccessible scales, advancing fundamental physics frameworks for non-equilibrium polymer behavior. Results will be disseminated through open-source simulation tools and a public repository of validated force field parameters.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the mechanical, optical, and transport properties of polymers with respect to the underlying physics and physical chemistry of polymers in melt, solution, and solid state

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing resilient supply chain networks under dynamic disruptions, such as demand volatility, supplier uncertainties, and transportation bottlenecks, through advanced computational modeling. Traditional optimization approaches often struggle with the scale, stochasticity, and real-time decision-making required for modern global supply chains. We propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating machine learning, multi-agent simulation, and stochastic optimization to model complex interdependencies across procurement, production, inventory, and distribution nodes. The computational workflow will employ agent-based modeling to simulate supplier-customer interactions, deep reinforcement learning to adaptively optimize inventory policies and routing decisions, and parallelized Monte Carlo methods to assess risk under diverse disruption scenarios. By leveraging distributed computing architectures, the project will scale to analyze networks with thousands of nodes and high-dimensional decision spaces, enabling scenario testing at granular temporal and spatial resolutions. Anticipated outcomes include actionable strategies for balancing cost efficiency with robustness, quantifying trade-offs between just-in-time and resilience-focused inventory policies, and identifying critical infrastructure vulnerabilities. The computational tools developed will provide a platform for real-time supply chain stress-testing, empowering decision-makers to allocate resources proactively during crises.
