cip_definition: Any instructional program in dance, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of algorithmic fairness and bias in predictive policing systems through large-scale computational simulations. While predictive algorithms are increasingly used to allocate law enforcement resources, their design and deployment often lack transparency, potentially reinforcing systemic inequities. The research problem centers on identifying how training data biases, model architectures, and feedback loops between policing actions and crime reporting interact to produce unequal outcomes across demographic groups. Using high-performance computing resources, we will develop agent-based models that simulate urban crime patterns, police patrol allocation strategies, and community reporting behaviors at city-scale resolution. These models will integrate real-world demographic data, historical crime statistics, and procedural fairness metrics to test hypotheses about algorithmic amplification of disparities. Machine learning techniques will be employed to analyze simulation outputs across thousands of parameter combinations, assessing how different deployment scenarios affect equity metrics. The computational intensity arises from modeling millions of agent interactions across diverse urban landscapes while maintaining granular temporal and spatial resolution. Expected outcomes include a framework for evaluating algorithmic fairness in public safety contexts, quantitative evidence about risk factors for bias propagation, and open-source tools for simulating police-community dynamics. This work bridges computational social science with criminal justice policy analysis, offering novel methodologies to assess emerging technologies in law enforcement. The requested resources will enable parameter space exploration that is infeasible with standard computing infrastructure, directly supporting evidence-based policymaking for equitable public safety strategies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the criminal justice system, its organizational components and processes, and its legal and public policy contexts. Includes instruction in criminal law and policy, police and correctional systems organization, the administration of justice and the judiciary, and public attitudes regarding criminal justice issues.

abstract: Dental implantology faces challenges in predicting long-term biomechanical stability and osseointegration success due to variability in patient anatomy, bone density, and occlusal loading patterns. Traditional clinical methods often rely on generalized protocols, which may not account for patient-specific biomechanical interactions between implants, prosthetics, and bone. This project proposes a computational framework to model the biomechanical and biological responses of dental implants at scale, enabling personalized treatment planning and optimized implant design. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate three-dimensional stress distributions in bone and implant interfaces under dynamic masticatory loads using finite element analysis (FEA), coupled with agent-based modeling of bone remodeling and soft tissue adaptation. Patient-specific anatomies derived from cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) scans will be integrated into these simulations to evaluate the impact of variables such as implant angulation, thread design, and grafting material properties. Additionally, machine learning algorithms will be trained on simulation outputs to identify predictive biomarkers for implant failure and optimize surgical parameters. The computational workload involves iterative, high-resolution FEA across thousands of virtual patient scenarios, requiring parallel processing capabilities for rapid convergence. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for biomechanical risk assessment, data-driven guidelines for graft material selection in low-density bone, and open-source tools for simulating bone-implant interactions. By quantifying the effects of clinical variables in silico, this work aims to reduce post-operative complications, improve prosthetic longevity, and advance computational dentistry methodologies. The scale of data generation and model complexity necessitates HPC infrastructure to achieve clinically relevant resolutions and throughput, which is unfeasible with standard computing resources.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on dental implantology. Includes instruction in diagnosis and treatment planning, surgical protocols, implant placement, sinus grafting, guided bone regeneration, soft tissue grafting, prosthetic protocols, prosthesis design, and aftercare.

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges inherent in optimizing next-generation wireless communication networks for ultra-reliability, energy efficiency, and scalability. As 5G/6G systems evolve, the interplay between dense antenna arrays, dynamic channel conditions, and real-time signal processing introduces non-convex optimization problems that are intractable for classical analytical methods. We propose a hybrid computational framework integrating physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) with large-scale Monte Carlo simulations to model electromagnetic wave propagation, interference patterns, and adaptive beamforming in complex urban environments. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to train PINNs on multi-terabyte datasets of channel state information and to simulate stochastic network behaviors across thousands of spatially distributed nodes. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated tensor operations for neural network training and distributed CPU clusters for parallelized electromagnetic simulations using finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) methods. Expected outcomes include novel algorithms for joint beamforming and resource allocation that reduce latency by 15–20% in millimeter-wave scenarios, alongside open-source tools for simulating terahertz-band channel dynamics. These advances will directly inform the design of energy-efficient massive MIMO systems and contribute to foundational knowledge in electromagnetic-aware network optimization. The requested resources will enable parameter sweeps across 10^4+ configurations, a scale unfeasible on local clusters, while ensuring reproducibility through containerized workflows. By bridging computational electromagnetics and machine learning, this work aims to establish a framework for real-time, physics-constrained network control, with applications to IoT, smart infrastructure, and autonomous vehicle communications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design and development of computer systems. Includes instruction in computer architecture, cybersecurity, electronic circuits, electromagnetism, electronic materials and design, micro-fabrication methods and techniques, signal and image processing, and wireless communication networks.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable algorithms for dynamic graph analysis, addressing the computational challenges of modeling large-scale, evolving networks in real time. Modern applications—such as social network dynamics, distributed systems optimization, and biological interaction networks—require efficient methods to process graphs with millions of nodes and edges that change continuously. Traditional sequential algorithms and static graph frameworks struggle with these demands due to memory constraints and computational latency. The proposed research will integrate combinatorial optimization, parallel computing, and distributed systems design to create novel algorithms that decompose dynamic graphs into temporally coherent substructures, enabling incremental updates and asynchronous processing. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to evaluate these methods at scale, particularly for simulating dynamic networks with synthetic and real-world datasets (e.g., internet topology traces, genomic interaction networks). Key computational tasks include large-scale parallelism using MPI for distributed memory architectures, GPU-accelerated subgraph processing, and adaptive load-balancing strategies to manage irregular workloads. Expected outcomes include (1) open-source software for dynamic graph analysis optimized for HPC environments, (2) theoretical advances in complexity bounds for dynamic graph decomposition, and (3) empirical validation of scalability on graphs exceeding 10^8 edges. This work bridges mathematical rigor—drawing from spectral graph theory and temporal logic—with computational innovation, offering tools that can transform network analysis in interdisciplinary domains. The requested resources will support iterative testing, hyperparameter tuning, and comparative benchmarking against state-of-the-art frameworks, ensuring robustness and practical utility. By addressing the gap between mathematical models and computational feasibility, this project aims to establish a foundation for real-time, large-scale network analytics in both academic and industrial contexts.
cip_definition: A program with a general synthesis of mathematics and computer science or a specialization which draws from mathematics and computer science.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate unresolved questions in the asymptotic enumeration of restricted integer partitions, a core problem in combinatorial number theory. Specifically, we aim to characterize the growth rates of partition functions constrained by divisibility and difference conditions, which are conjectured to exhibit phase transitions between polynomial and quasi-polynomial regimes. Current analytic methods face fundamental barriers in handling the intricate recursive structures of these partition variants, necessitating large-scale computational exploration. The research will employ optimized combinatorial algorithms to generate exact partition counts for integers up to \(10^5\), extending beyond the reach of existing tabulations. High-performance computing resources are critical due to the exponential growth in partition function complexity: brute-force enumeration requires \(O(n^3)\) time and memory for target integer \(n\), while our improved dynamic programming approach reduces this to \(O(n^{3/2} \log n)\) through modular arithmetic optimizations. Parallel implementations will leverage distributed memory architectures to compute sparse congruence classes simultaneously, with MPI-based load balancing addressing irregular work distributions. The resulting datasets will be analyzed through lattice basis reduction and analytic number theory techniques to identify asymptotic signatures. Expected outcomes include rigorous bounds on partition function growth rates, potential counterexamples to conjectured phase transition thresholds in the literature, and open-source release of optimized enumeration libraries. This work directly advances the classification of integer partition universality classes and provides new tools for computational number theory, with implications for adjacent areas including modular form coefficients and representation theory. The requested resources will enable decisive progress on problems where theoretical and computational approaches have previously been disjoint.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the properties of integers, integer-valued functions, including combinatorics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of radionuclide-based in vitro analyses in clinical pathology demands advanced computational tools to optimize diagnostic accuracy, laboratory efficiency, and safety protocols. Current methods for quantifying radioisotopes in biological samples (e.g., blood, urine, biopsied tissues) rely on static calibration models that inadequately account for temporal decay variations, matrix interference effects, and non-linear detector responses. This project proposes to develop dynamic, high-resolution simulation frameworks to address these limitations, requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model multi-physics interactions at scale. We will implement Monte Carlo simulations to track radiation transport through heterogeneous sample matrices and detector systems, coupled with machine learning algorithms trained on experimental datasets to predict isotope-specific decay corrections and quenching effects. Parallelized workflows will process high-throughput spectral data from gamma counters and liquid scintillation systems, integrating time-resolved decay constants and environmental variables (e.g., temperature, pH) to improve quantification accuracy. A secondary aim involves simulating isotope storage conditions to optimize containment geometries and shielding configurations, reducing occupational exposure risks. The computational pipeline will leverage GPU-accelerated nodes for real-time parameter optimization during live experiments, enabled by HPC-scale containerization to maintain reproducibility across clinical laboratories. Expected outcomes include validated models for 10 commonly used diagnostic radionuclides (e.g., Tc-99m, I-131), an open-source analysis toolkit for automated quality control, and evidence-based guidelines for safe isotope handling. By enabling precision-adjusted in vitro radioassays, this work aims to reduce diagnostic errors in conditions such as thyroid dysfunction and metastatic cancer monitoring while advancing computational pathology infrastructure for radiopharmaceutical development. The requested HPC allocation is critical to manage the petabyte-scale datasets and iterative training processes required for robust, generalizable models in this high-dimensional parameter space.
cip_definition: Research focused on the use of radionuclides in the study of body fluids, excreta, or tissues quantified outside the body. May included related research in laboratory management and safety, quality control, instrumentation, isotope storage and in vitro analyses.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the sociocultural networks of 19th-century missionary movements and their role in shaping cross-regional knowledge exchange. While missionary studies traditionally focus on theological or historical narratives, this research applies computational methods to interrogate understudied dimensions of missionary activity—specifically, how missionary networks facilitated the transfer of ecological, linguistic, and medical knowledge between Indigenous communities and colonial institutions. The primary challenge lies in processing and correlating heterogeneous datasets, including digitized missionary journals, colonial administrative records, Indigenous language corpora, and environmental surveys, which span multiple continents and languages. These sources, often fragmented and non-standardized, require advanced computational integration to identify patterns of knowledge circulation obscured by conventional archival methods. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for low-resource languages and historical orthographies to extract semantic and relational data from textual sources. Graph-based network analysis will model the connectivity of missionary nodes and their interlocutors, while geospatial machine learning will track the diffusion of ecological knowledge against environmental variables. By parallelizing these workflows across HPC clusters, the project aims to overcome scalability constraints in handling terabyte-scale datasets and computationally intensive simulations. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible knowledge graph mapping transnational knowledge flows, alongside methodological frameworks for interdisciplinary humanities research at the intersection of colonial studies, environmental history, and digital anthropology. This work will provide new insights into the asymmetrical dynamics of knowledge exchange in missionary contexts, while demonstrating how HPC can enable humanities scholars to address complex, data-rich questions that transcend traditional disciplinary boundaries.
cip_title: Missions/ Missionary Studies and Missiology, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in missions, missionary studies, and missiology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Ensuring the safety and efficacy of blood transfusions remains a critical challenge in transfusion medicine, with persistent risks of adverse immune reactions and supply chain inefficiencies. Current laboratory methods for antigen-antibody compatibility testing, while foundational, face limitations in scalability and predictive power when addressing rare antibodies or complex donor-recipient pairings. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC) framework to model immunohematological interactions, optimize blood component storage protocols, and enhance donor-recipient matching algorithms. Leveraging molecular dynamics simulations, machine learning techniques, and large-scale data analytics, the research will investigate antigen-antibody binding affinities under varying physiological conditions, predict degradation pathways of stored blood components, and identify patterns in donor databases to minimize alloimmunization risks. The computational models will integrate genetic, proteomic, and clinical data to enable multi-parametric risk assessment for transfusion reactions. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for identifying high-risk transfusions, evidence-based guidelines for extending blood product shelf-life, and decision-support systems for rare antibody cases. By addressing computational bottlenecks through parallelized simulations and GPU-accelerated analyses, this work aims to overcome current limitations in serological testing resolution and throughput. The project’s findings will directly inform blood bank operational protocols, reduce transfusion-related complications, and improve resource allocation in blood supply networks. This research bridges critical gaps between clinical hematology practice and computational innovation, establishing a foundation for data-driven advancements in transfusion safety and blood product management.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform routine and specialized blood testing procedures, collect and process blood donations, and support physicians and other clinicians administering transfusion therapy. Includes instruction in basic cellular biology, immunohematology, blood bank procedures, blood typing, antigen and antibody identification tests, hemolytic and transfusion responses and diseases, donor selection, blood drawing and storage, blood separation, viral marker testing, laboratory and personnel supervision, safety and sterilization, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of human-environment interactions in informal urban settlements through advanced geospatial modeling and high-resolution temporal analysis. As cities globally face rapid, unplanned growth, traditional cartographic methods and static geographic information systems (GIS) struggle to capture the fluidity of these environments, where spatial configurations and land use evolve unpredictably. The research problem centers on developing a computational framework to model these dynamic processes at scale, integrating heterogeneous data sources—including satellite imagery, crowd-sourced mobility traces, and socio-economic surveys—to generate predictive maps of settlement morphologies and resource accessibility. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), the project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) coupled with deep learning architectures to simulate how informal settlements adapt to environmental stressors, policy interventions, and community-driven spatial practices. Key computational challenges include processing terabyte-scale raster datasets, optimizing spatial graph algorithms for real-time simulations, and training convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on irregularly sampled geospatial time series. The proposed methods will extend cartographic theory by formalizing probabilistic map projections that account for temporal uncertainty and non-Euclidean urban geometries. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adaptive cartography, validated against case studies in three megacities, which will provide policymakers and grassroots organizations with actionable insights into equitable infrastructure planning. By bridging computational scalability with social science rigor, this work aims to redefine how transient human landscapes are represented, analyzed, and ethically intervened upon in contexts of urban informality.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of map-making and the application of mathematical, computer, and other techniques to the analysis of large amounts of geographic data and the science of mapping geographic information. Includes instruction in cartographic theory and map projections, computer-assisted cartography, geographic information systems, map design and layout, photogrammetry, air photo interpretation, remote sensing, spatial analysis, geodesy, cartographic editing, and applications to specific industrial, commercial, research, and governmental mapping problems.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cross-platform audience engagement in digital media ecosystems through large-scale computational analysis of multimedia content and user interaction data. As radio, television, and digital communication platforms increasingly converge, content producers face challenges in optimizing strategies for audience retention and message dissemination across fragmented, algorithmically mediated environments. The research problem centers on identifying patterns in how users engage with hybrid media formats—such as live-streamed broadcasts with synchronized social media feeds—and how these patterns are shaped by platform-specific algorithms, content type, and temporal factors. To address this, the project will employ machine learning models, including transformer-based architectures and temporal graph neural networks, to analyze multimodal datasets comprising audio, video, text, and user behavior logs from partnered media organizations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for processing terabytes of timestamped media content, training models on heterogeneous data streams, and simulating audience response scenarios under varying platform conditions. The computational workflow will integrate natural language processing for sentiment analysis, computer vision techniques for visual context extraction, and network analysis to map real-time interaction cascades. Expected outcomes include a framework for predicting engagement thresholds in multi-platform media campaigns and actionable insights into content adaptation strategies for evolving digital audiences. By leveraging HPC capabilities to handle the scale and complexity of modern media ecosystems, this research aims to advance empirical understanding of hybrid communication models while providing practitioners with evidence-based tools to navigate algorithmic content distribution. The project will contribute novel methodologies to digital communication research, where computational demands have traditionally outpaced the analytical capacities of standard workstations, particularly in processing synchronized audiovisual and interaction data at industry-relevant scales.
cip_title: Radio, Television, and Digital Communication, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in radio, television, and digital communications, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the dynamic interactions between legal frameworks, market forces, and environmental constraints in urban land development. As real estate and land development law increasingly intersects with complex systems—such as climate adaptation policies, algorithmic valuation tools, and multi-jurisdictional regulatory conflicts—traditional legal analysis struggles to account for nonlinear feedback loops and emergent outcomes. The research problem centers on quantifying how iterative changes to zoning laws, tax incentives, or sustainability mandates propagate through development ecosystems, influencing long-term urban form and equity. Using high-performance computing resources, the project will deploy agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate stakeholder decision-making—including developers, municipalities, and community groups—under varying legal scenarios. Computational legal analytics methods will process structured and unstructured data from case law, municipal codes, and environmental impact reports to parameterize models. A parallel focus involves training graph neural networks (GNNs) to map precedent citation networks in land use litigation, identifying patterns that predict judicial outcomes. The integration of ABM and GNNs aims to reveal latent dependencies between localized legal decisions and systemic risks, such as displacement cascades or infrastructure fragility. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for simulating policy impacts at metropolitan scales and a novel dataset linking legal reasoning architectures to development trajectories. By bridging computational social science with legal informatics, this work advances evidence-based approaches to statutory design while addressing critical gaps in how legal education engages with complex systems analytics. The requested resources will enable large-scale sensitivity analyses across 10^4 parameter combinations and real-time visualization of multi-agent interactions, tasks infeasible without parallelized computing architectures.
cip_title: Real Estate and Land Development Law
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting real estate and land development.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze patterns of cultural and political exchange across the Iberian Atlantic during the late colonial period (1750–1825). Traditional historiography has often treated Spanish America and Brazil as distinct regions, but recent digitization efforts—including colonial administrative records, merchant correspondence, and periodicals from archives in Spain, Mexico, Peru, and Brazil—provide an unprecedented opportunity to investigate interconnected transimperial networks. However, the scale and multilingual nature of these datasets (spanning over 500,000 pages of handwritten and printed texts in Spanish, Portuguese, and indigenous languages) require computational methods to systematically identify actors, institutions, and material flows. This project will employ optical character recognition (OCR) correction tailored to historical scripts, multilingual named entity recognition (NER) models, and network analysis to map relationships between colonial elites, trade hubs, and dissident movements. HPC resources are essential for training transformer-based language models on domain-specific corpora, parallelizing OCR post-processing across thousands of documents, and running dynamic network simulations to test hypotheses about information diffusion. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of transatlantic connections, visualizations of shifting power structures preceding independence movements, and methodological frameworks for integrating computational text analysis with archival historiography. By bridging regional divides in Latin American history, this research aims to redefine understandings of how Enlightenment ideas and revolutionary practices circulated in multilingual, contested colonial spaces. The computational workflows developed will also provide a template for historians working with large-scale, heterogeneous primary sources in other understudied regions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history of the Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking areas of the world, including the Iberian, Latin American, and Lusophone worlds.

abstract: Aircraft powerplant systems operate under extreme thermal, mechanical, and aerodynamic conditions, demanding precise maintenance protocols to ensure safety and efficiency. Current industry practices rely heavily on historical failure data and standardized inspection intervals, which may not fully account for dynamic operational stresses or material degradation patterns unique to modern high-performance engines. This project seeks to address this gap by developing predictive computational models that simulate powerplant component behavior under real-world operating conditions. The research will focus on turbine blade fatigue, combustion chamber thermal dynamics, and fuel system performance variability, integrating multiphysics simulations to map failure risks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale computational fluid dynamics (CFD) datasets, finite element analysis (FEA) of thermal-mechanical stresses, and machine learning algorithms trained on heterogeneous sensor data from engine telemetry. Simulations will model scenarios such as rapid throttle changes, altitude-induced pressure fluctuations, and prolonged exposure to high-temperature gradients, correlating computational outputs with empirical wear data from engine tear-down analyses. The anticipated outcomes include a framework for condition-based maintenance prioritization, reducing unplanned downtime by 15–20% in commercial aviation fleets. Additionally, the project will generate open-access datasets and modular simulation tools adaptable to emerging hybrid-electric propulsion systems, directly supporting technician training programs in diagnosing next-generation powerplant anomalies. By leveraging HPC capabilities to resolve complex, coupled physical interactions at scale, this work aims to advance predictive maintenance strategies while providing a computational foundation for optimizing powerplant lifecycle management in alignment with evolving aviation sustainability goals.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain all types of aircraft powerplant and related systems. Instruction includes engine inspection and maintenance, lubrication and cooling, electrical and ignition systems, carburetion, fuels and fuel systems, propeller and fan assemblies.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize the material behavior of ceramic clays and glazes under varying firing conditions, addressing a critical gap in the empirical understanding of ceramic arts processes. Traditional approaches to ceramic arts rely heavily on trial-and-error experimentation to achieve desired aesthetic and structural outcomes, which is resource-intensive and limits the exploration of novel material combinations. The research problem centers on predicting the relationships between clay composition, glaze chemistry, kiln conditions, and final ceramic properties (e.g., color variation, surface texture, structural integrity) to empower artists with data-driven insights. Using high-performance computing (HPC), we will implement multiphysics simulations integrating thermal dynamics, fluid mechanics, and chemical reaction modeling to replicate kiln environments and material interactions at microscales. Machine learning models will be trained on both simulated data and experimental datasets from historical and contemporary ceramic works to identify predictive patterns. The computational workflow will include parameter sweeps across clay-glaze combinations (e.g., silica-alumina ratios, oxide additives) and firing protocols (temperature ramps, oxidation/reduction cycles). Expected outcomes include an open-access simulation toolkit for artists to virtually test formulations, a database correlating material inputs with artistic outputs, and the discovery of previously undocumented glaze effects achievable through controlled atmospheric conditions. This interdisciplinary approach bridges material science and artistic practice, offering ceramicists a systematic method to innovate while preserving traditional techniques. The requested HPC resources are essential to handle the high-dimensional parameter space and parallelize thermally coupled simulations, which exceed the capacity of local workstations. By reducing the stochasticity inherent in ceramic arts, this project aims to expand creative possibilities and contribute to the sustainability of the field through optimized resource use.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions by producing art works out of clay and similar materials. Includes instruction in handbuilt and wheel thrown techniques; molding; slips and glazes; trimming and decorating; firing and kiln operation; oxidation; mixed media; ceramic murals; and personal style development.

abstract: Naturopathic medicine employs complex, multimodal interventions—such as botanical formulations, dietary modifications, and mind-body therapies—to address chronic disease. However, the mechanistic underpinnings of these interventions remain poorly characterized due to the challenge of modeling nonlinear interactions between multiple therapeutic components, patient-specific variables (e.g., microbiome composition, epigenetic states), and dynamic physiological outcomes. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework to simulate and predict the systems-level effects of naturopathic protocols on metabolic and immune dysfunction in autoimmune conditions. Using high-performance computing resources, we will integrate multi-omics datasets (metagenomic, metabolomic, and transcriptomic profiles from patient cohorts) with clinical data and in silico models of phytochemical bioactivity. Agent-based modeling will simulate host-microbiome interactions under varying dietary and herbal treatment conditions, while graph neural networks will identify critical nodes in immune-metabolic networks that predict therapeutic responsiveness. A novel feature of this work is the incorporation of traditional medicine parameters, including Ayurvedic constitutional types and Chinese medicine organ network relationships, encoded as probabilistic Bayesian priors to inform model architecture. The computational pipeline will be validated against longitudinal data from a pilot clinical trial evaluating naturopathic interventions in rheumatoid arthritis. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive model to optimize personalized treatment combinations, (2) mechanistic insights into synergies between botanicals and lifestyle interventions, and (3) an open-source tool for simulating naturopathic protocols in diverse physiological contexts. This work bridges traditional holistic paradigms with systems biology, advancing both the evidence base and methodological rigor of naturopathic research. The scale of data integration and real-time simulation of multi-organ interactions necessitates access to GPU-accelerated computing clusters and large-memory nodes, which are unavailable in our current institutional infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of naturopathic medicine, an holistic therapeutic approach combining medical knowledge with noninvasive natural, homeopathic, and non-Western therapies and emphasizing disease prevention, wellness, and self-healing. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, epidemiology, neuroscience, biostatistics, public and community health, laboratory and clinical diagnosis, pharmacognosy, botanical medicine, homeopathy, principles of Oriental medicine and Ayurveda, manipulative therapy, naturopathic therapeutics, therapeutic nutrition, case analysis and management, philosophy of naturopathy, patient counseling, practice management, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance simulation-based training and predictive modeling for nursing assistants and patient care aides, addressing critical gaps in personalized patient care and workforce preparedness. Nursing assistants operate in dynamic clinical environments where rapid decision-making under resource constraints impacts patient safety and outcomes. However, existing training tools and care protocols often lack granularity to account for individual patient variability or real-time physiological changes. To address this, we propose developing a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) to simulate patient-aide interactions in high-fidelity virtual environments. The ABM component will model diverse patient profiles (e.g., mobility limitations, cognitive status, chronic conditions) and caregiver workflows, while ML algorithms trained on anonymized electronic health record (EHR) data will predict patient deterioration risks and recommend context-specific interventions. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing multi-terabyte EHR datasets, running parallelized simulations across thousands of patient scenarios, and optimizing neural networks for real-time decision support. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated simulation platform to enhance training efficacy by exposing trainees to rare but high-stakes clinical events, (2) predictive tools to reduce preventable adverse events (e.g., falls, pressure injuries) through early risk identification, and (3) data-driven insights into workload balancing strategies for nursing teams. By bridging computational science and nursing education, this work aims to elevate the quality of bedside care while providing empirical foundations for scalable training solutions in allied health education programs. The requested resources will directly support GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale parameter sweeps for scenario optimization, and secure data storage compliant with healthcare privacy standards.
cip_title: Nursing Assistant/ Aide and Patient Care Assistant/ Aide
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform routine nursing-related services to patients in hospitals or long-term care facilities, under the training and supervision of a registered nurse or licensed practical nurse.

abstract: Therapeutic radiologic physics faces critical challenges in optimizing radiation dose delivery to maximize tumor control while minimizing toxicity to surrounding healthy tissues. Current treatment planning systems rely on simplified models that may inadequately account for dynamic anatomical motion, tissue heterogeneity, and complex radiation transport phenomena, particularly in advanced modalities like proton therapy and magnetic resonance-guided radiotherapy (MRgRT). This project seeks to develop high-fidelity computational models to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will focus on two interconnected aims: (1) creating patient-specific Monte Carlo simulations of coupled photon-electron and proton transport under realistic biological motion conditions, and (2) developing machine learning architectures to predict and mitigate dosimetric uncertainties arising from interfractional anatomical changes. Computational workflows will integrate deformable image registration of longitudinal CT/MRI datasets with GPU-accelerated radiation transport codes (e.g., TOPAS, Geant4) to model 4D dose distributions across treatment fractions. Machine learning models will be trained on simulated and clinical datasets to identify predictive features of dose degradation. The HPC environment is essential for managing the ∼10^6 core-hour demand of Monte Carlo simulations across 200+ patient cases and the distributed training of deep neural networks on multi-institutional datasets. Expected outcomes include validated algorithms for adaptive radiotherapy decision support, improved uncertainty quantification frameworks for treatment planning systems, and open-source tools for benchmarking radiation transport in heterogeneous media. This work directly addresses critical gaps in precision radiation oncology by enabling computationally intensive analyses impractical on local clusters. The resulting methodologies could enhance clinical protocols for dose escalation strategies while maintaining safety margins, potentially impacting over 500,000 annual radiotherapy patients in the US alone. Resource allocation will also support the development of educational modules for medical physics residents, bridging advanced computing techniques with clinical applications.
cip_definition: Research focused on the physical aspects of the therapeutic applications of x-rays, gamma rays, electron, and other charged particle beams, neutrons, and radiations from sealed radionuclide sources; and with the equipment associated with their production and use, including radiation safety. One of the three subspecialties available to residents in radiologic physics who must select one or more subspecialty areas.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing the evolution of legal reasoning in understudied areas of administrative law, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to process large-scale, unstructured legal text corpora. The core problem addressed is the lack of systematic tools to trace how administrative agencies interpret ambiguous statutory language over time, particularly in niche regulatory domains such as digital privacy enforcement and cross-border data governance. Current manual methods for tracking interpretive shifts are resource-intensive and fail to capture latent patterns across millions of documents. The proposed methodology combines natural language processing (NLP) techniques with temporal network analysis to map semantic relationships between regulatory decisions, public commentary, and judicial review outcomes from 2000–2023. Custom transformer-based models will be trained to identify implicit citation behaviors and conceptual drift in agency interpretations, while graph algorithms will quantify the influence of non-precedential guidance documents on subsequent rulings. The computational workflow requires HPC resources for three critical phases: 1) parallel processing of 15+ terabytes of heterogeneous legal texts (final rules, adjudications, amicus briefs), 2) dynamic embedding training across 50+ regulatory subdomains using adaptive attention mechanisms, and 3) multi-scale community detection in temporal knowledge graphs spanning 20+ jurisdictions. Expected outcomes include the first open-source toolkit for predictive modeling of regulatory interpretation trajectories and a novel metric for measuring legal concept stability in emerging policy areas. This work will provide quantitative insights into how administrative legal systems balance statutory fidelity with adaptive governance, offering policymakers evidence-based strategies for improving regulatory transparency. The computational architecture developed through this project will establish scalable methods for legal analytics in non-binary classification domains, advancing interdisciplinary research at the intersection of computational law and regulatory theory.
cip_definition: Any program in law, legal services, and legal studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the identification and functional characterization of structural genetic variants (SVs) contributing to rare developmental disorders. While genome-wide association studies have identified numerous single-nucleotide variants linked to disease, SVs—including deletions, duplications, inversions, and translocations—remain understudied due to computational challenges in detection and interpretation. Current methods for SV analysis struggle with sensitivity and scalability when applied to large-scale whole-genome sequencing (WGS) datasets, limiting insights into their role in Mendelian conditions. We propose developing a novel computational pipeline integrating graph-based genome representations, machine learning–enhanced variant prioritization, and multi-omics functional annotation to resolve SVs at scale. The pipeline will process WGS data from 5,000 trios (affected probands and unaffected parents) from the NIH’s GREGoR Consortium, requiring parallelized alignment, variant calling, and population genetics analyses across petabytes of genomic data. Deep learning models trained on epigenomic profiles (ATAC-seq, Hi-C) will predict SV pathogenicity by assessing disruptions to 3D chromatin architecture and regulatory elements. Resource-intensive tasks include de novo assembly of complex genomic regions, haplotype phasing across diverse populations, and simulating SV effects on gene networks using systems biology models. Anticipated outcomes include 1) a validated, open-source SV detection framework optimized for HPC environments, 2) a catalog of high-confidence pathogenic SVs linked to neurodevelopmental disorders, and 3) mechanistic insights into how noncoding SVs dysregulate developmental pathways. This work will directly enhance clinical diagnostic yield for rare genetic diseases while providing a computational foundation for studying SVs in complex traits. Successful implementation requires access to GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning, high-memory nodes for genome graph traversal, and scalable storage for population-level genomic data.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of human genetics from the standpoint of medical applications such as clinical diagnosis, genetic engineering and therapy, transplantation, and the study of genetic diseases and disabilities and their defense. Includes instruction in human molecular genetics; genetic factors causing disease; changes in gene expression during development, differentiation, and pathogenesis; recombinant DNA; gene therapy; clinical genetics; genetic epidemiology; immunogenetics; cytogenetics; and genetics of specific disorders and diseases.

abstract: Forensic chemistry faces significant challenges in analyzing complex mixtures of trace evidence, such as illicit drugs, explosives, and toxicological samples, where traditional analytical methods struggle with sensitivity, specificity, and rapid processing. This project seeks to address these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational models that enhance the interpretation of spectroscopic and chromatographic data from forensic samples. The research will focus on three interconnected aims: (1) creating machine learning algorithms to deconvolute overlapping spectral signatures in mixtures, (2) simulating degradation pathways of forensic analytes under environmental conditions using quantum chemical calculations, and (3) optimizing probabilistic frameworks for source attribution of trace materials. Computational workflows will integrate density functional theory (DFT) for molecular property prediction, molecular dynamics simulations to model analyte interactions with environmental matrices, and neural networks trained on synthetic datasets mimicking real-world forensic samples. These methods require substantial computational resources due to the complexity of multi-component systems, the need for high-level theory accuracy in degradation modeling, and the iterative nature of training robust machine learning models. The expected outcomes include validated tools for rapid identification of trace evidence components, improved understanding of environmental effects on evidentiary stability, and statistically rigorous protocols for reporting forensic findings. By bridging gaps between analytical chemistry and computational science, this work will empower forensic laboratories to address evolving challenges such as synthetic drug identification and microtrace evidence analysis, ultimately strengthening the reliability of forensic conclusions in legal contexts. Access to HPC infrastructure is critical to achieve the necessary scale and precision for these computationally intensive tasks, which cannot be feasibly executed on local laboratory systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical techniques and instrumentation to the analysis and evaluation of physical evidence to aid in criminal investigations. Includes instruction in analytical, inorganic, organic, and physical chemistry; biochemistry; forensic toxicology; instrumental analysis; crime scene processing; criminal investigation; forensic laboratory technology; and applicable law.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive models that optimize medication safety and operational efficiency in pharmacy settings. A critical challenge in pharmacy practice is the risk of medication errors during dispensing, which can arise from factors such as workflow interruptions, high prescription volumes, or miscommunication. Current approaches to error prevention rely heavily on manual checks, which are time-intensive and inconsistent. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating machine learning (ML) and discrete-event simulation (DES) to analyze historical prescription data, workflow patterns, and error reports. The ML component will identify risk factors and predict error-prone scenarios by training on anonymized datasets spanning prescription records, patient demographics, and staff scheduling logs. Concurrently, DES models will simulate pharmacy workflows under varying conditions (e.g., staffing levels, seasonal demand shifts) to quantify their impact on error rates and processing times. HPC resources are essential to handle the scale and complexity of these tasks, particularly for parallel processing of large datasets (>10^6 prescriptions) and iterative optimization of simulation parameters. Expected outcomes include actionable insights into workflow redesign, real-time error prediction tools, and evidence-based staffing recommendations. By reducing preventable errors and streamlining operations, this research directly supports pharmacy technicians’ roles in ensuring patient safety and maintaining regulatory compliance. The resulting models will be validated using retrospective data from partner community pharmacies, with potential for integration into pharmacy management software to enhance decision-making. This work bridges computational innovation and practical pharmacy operations, advancing the Health Professions field by demonstrating how HPC-driven analytics can transform traditional healthcare workflows.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of pharmacists, to prepare medications, provide medications and related assistance to patients, and manage pharmacy clinical and business operations. Includes instruction in medical and pharmaceutical terminology, principles of pharmacology and pharmaceutics, drug identification, pharmacy laboratory procedures, prescription interpretation, patient communication and education, safety procedures, record-keeping, measurement and testing techniques, pharmacy business operations, prescription preparation, logistics and dispensing operations, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cross-border digital advocacy networks and their impact on multilateral treaty ratification processes, a critical yet understudied facet of contemporary international relations. As non-state actors increasingly leverage digital platforms to influence global governance, traditional diplomatic models struggle to account for the scale, velocity, and decentralized nature of these transnational campaigns. The research employs a novel computational framework combining dynamic network analysis, agent-based modeling, and natural language processing to simulate how digitally mediated advocacy strategies interact with state decision-making systems. High-performance computing resources are essential to process real-time multilingual social media datasets (spanning 10+ diplomatic treaty cases), model adaptive interactions between 50,000+ simulated agents (state actors, NGOs, and citizen networks), and quantify cascading effects across multi-layered communication networks. By integrating machine learning classifiers to detect persuasion patterns in diplomatic correspondence and public discourse, the project aims to identify critical thresholds where digital advocacy accelerates or impedes treaty adoption. Expected outcomes include a predictive model of hybrid diplomacy suitable for testing crisis scenarios, actionable insights for optimizing digital engagement in multilateral negotiations, and an open-source toolkit for simulating tech-mediated diplomatic processes. This interdisciplinary approach advances computational social science methodologies while addressing urgent gaps in understanding how emergent digital ecosystems reshape power structures in global governance.
detailed_field: International relations and national security studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of international politics and institutions, and the conduct of diplomacy and foreign policy. Includes instruction in international relations theory, foreign policy analysis, international law and organization, the comparative study of specific countries and regions, and the theory and practice of diplomacy.

abstract: The increasing complexity of decentralized IT service ecosystems, particularly in edge computing environments with heterogeneous IoT devices, presents critical challenges in dynamic resource coordination. Traditional centralized management frameworks struggle to adapt to the scale, latency sensitivity, and energy constraints of modern applications such as distributed smart grids or real-time industrial automation. This project proposes the development of a novel, decentralized resource allocation framework leveraging multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) and adaptive consensus protocols to optimize computational workflows across edge nodes while minimizing operational overhead. The research addresses the gap in scalable, self-organizing algorithms for IT service administration in environments with intermittent connectivity and competing stakeholder priorities. Computational experiments will simulate large-scale edge networks (10,000+ nodes) under variable load conditions to train and validate MARL policies that balance task throughput, energy efficiency, and fault tolerance. High-performance computing resources are essential for parallelized training of diverse network topologies and stress-testing consensus mechanisms under failure scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source toolkit for adaptive resource negotiation in edge environments, (2) quantitative benchmarks comparing decentralized strategies against conventional orchestration approaches, and (3) novel metrics for evaluating administration overhead in permissionless device coalitions. The work advances IT service management paradigms by introducing biologically inspired coordination mechanisms that could reduce infrastructure provisioning costs by 15-30% in target use cases while maintaining QoS guarantees. Results will directly inform standardization efforts for autonomic computing in 5G/6G-enabled industrial IoT deployments, bridging theoretical distributed systems research with practical IT administration challenges in emergent edge architectures.
cip_title: Computer/ Information Technology Services Administration and Management, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer/information technology services administration and management, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to evaluate the efficacy of online learning interventions across diverse higher education contexts, addressing the challenge of synthesizing large-scale, heterogeneous educational datasets. As institutions increasingly adopt hybrid and fully online modalities, there is a critical need to assess how these interventions impact student outcomes, equity, and institutional resource allocation. Current evaluation methods struggle to integrate multi-source data—such as learning management system (LMS) logs, demographic records, and longitudinal performance metrics—while accounting for institutional variability and confounding factors. This research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze terabyte-scale datasets from 15+ public universities, applying machine learning (ML) and agent-based modeling (ABM) techniques. Computational workflows will include (1) federated learning to train predictive models of student success while preserving data privacy across institutions, (2) network analysis to identify patterns in collaborative online learning behaviors, and (3) simulation of resource allocation scenarios under demographic and policy constraints. The ABM component will model how variations in institutional support structures interact with student engagement data to influence equity gaps. Expected outcomes include open-source tools for real-time intervention evaluation, policy-relevant insights into cost-benefit tradeoffs of digital learning infrastructures, and a benchmark dataset for cross-institutional comparison. By enabling simultaneous analysis of temporal, behavioral, and structural factors at scale, this work advances evaluation research methodologies in higher education while directly informing strategic planning processes. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing distributed data storage, parallelized model training, and complex simulation runs that exceed the capacity of local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and procedures for generating information about educational programs in higher education, staff and methods, and the analysis of such information for planning purposes outside of institutional research. Includes instruction in evaluation theory, evaluation research design and planning, administering evaluations and related data collection activities, data reporting requirements, data analysis and interpretation, and related economic and policy issues in higher education.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing clinical decision-making for acutely ill adult and geriatric patients, who often present with complex, heterogeneous medical conditions that defy conventional risk stratification models. Current approaches to predicting clinical deterioration, adverse drug reactions, and treatment response in this population are limited by their reliance on static variables and inability to process high-dimensional, multimodal data in real time. To overcome these barriers, we propose developing a machine learning framework capable of integrating dynamic electronic health record (EHR) data, high-frequency physiological waveforms, genomic markers, and imaging studies. The computational workload necessitates high-performance computing (HPC) resources due to the scale of data processing required: longitudinal EHR analysis across 50,000+ patient encounters, real-time processing of streaming ICU monitoring data (sampled at 240 Hz), and training of deep learning models for time-series prediction. Key methodologies include graph neural networks to model multi-organ system interactions, transformer architectures for temporal pattern recognition in vital sign trends, and federated learning techniques to preserve data privacy across collaborating institutions. Validation will involve prospective testing against existing clinical scores (e.g., SOFA, APACHE IV) in simulated critical care scenarios. Expected outcomes include a deployable predictive system for early identification of sepsis, delirium, and acute renal injury, with target performance metrics exceeding current clinical benchmarks by ≥15% in sensitivity and specificity. By enabling granular risk stratification tailored to geriatric pathophysiology and polypharmacy profiles, this work aims to reduce preventable complications in acute care settings while establishing a computational template for multimodal data integration in clinical research. The requested HPC resources are essential for managing the petabyte-scale datasets and computationally intensive model training required to achieve clinically actionable precision at the point of care.
cip_definition: Research focused on medical and clinical issues in Adult/Gerontology Acute Care

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize emergency resource allocation during multi-jurisdictional disasters, a critical challenge in public administration. Current approaches to distributing personnel, equipment, and supplies across overlapping government agencies often rely on heuristic methods that fail to account for dynamic risk factors, resource dependencies, and equity considerations. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate thousands of disaster scenarios using agent-based modeling integrated with machine learning. The computational model will incorporate real-world geospatial data, infrastructure networks, and population mobility patterns across a mid-sized U.S. metropolitan region. Key innovations include parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate probabilistic cascading failures in critical supply chains and graph neural networks to predict inter-agency coordination bottlenecks. The HPC environment is essential for processing petabyte-scale datasets from FEMA’s National Incident Management System and Census Bureau microdata while maintaining the temporal resolution required for minute-by-minute emergency response analysis. Expected outcomes include a decision support tool that quantifies trade-offs between efficiency, cost, and equity in disaster preparedness plans, with particular attention to vulnerable populations. The computational framework will be validated through partnerships with three state emergency management agencies. This work advances public administration research by demonstrating how large-scale computational modeling can inform evidence-based policy design for complex governance systems. The project will generate open-source algorithms tailored for non-scientific computing environments, lowering barriers for municipal governments to adopt data-driven resource allocation strategies. Successful implementation could reduce critical response delays by an estimated 15-30% in simulated scenarios, directly supporting more resilient communities.
cip_definition: Any program in public administration, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a digital humanities investigation into the multilingual and multicultural dynamics of medieval Iberian textual production. The Iberian Peninsula’s unique convergence of Christian, Islamic, and Jewish traditions between the 8th and 15th centuries generated a vast corpus of manuscripts, charters, and literary works in Arabic, Hebrew, Latin, and Romance vernaculars. However, systematic analysis of cross-cultural textual exchange remains limited due to the scale, linguistic diversity, and fragmented preservation of these sources. This research addresses this gap by employing computational text analysis and machine learning to identify patterns of cultural hybridity, translation practices, and knowledge transfer across religious and linguistic boundaries. A corpus of digitized texts—including legal documents, poetry, and philosophical treatises—will be processed using natural language processing (NLP) tools optimized for historical languages. Semantic network analysis will map lexical borrowings, intertextual references, and thematic shifts, while transformer-based models will assess stylistic and rhetorical adaptations across translated works. HPC resources are critical for training custom language models on non-standard orthographies and managing the high-dimensional data generated by network analytics. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated texts, visualizations of intercultural connectivity, and quantitative frameworks for assessing the impact of interfaith coexistence on literary and legal traditions. By integrating computational methods with humanistic inquiry, this project aims to redefine narratives of Iberian cultural identity, emphasizing fluidity and collaboration over rigid religious divides. The findings will provide a model for interdisciplinary, data-driven approaches to regional studies while supporting broader scholarly and public engagement with premodern multicultural heritage.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of the peoples of the Iberian Peninsula and related island groups and border regions from earliest times to the present, with particular emphasis on the development of Spain and Portugal but including other historical and current cultures.

abstract: The increasing demand for efficient and sustainable maritime operations necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize vessel performance, safety, and environmental compliance. Current approaches to ship routing, engine efficiency analysis, and hydrodynamic modeling often rely on simplified assumptions or static datasets, limiting their ability to address dynamic real-world conditions such as variable weather, fuel quality, and cargo loads. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution, multi-objective optimization framework for merchant marine operations using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will integrate computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of hull resistance under diverse sea states with machine learning models trained on historical voyage data, engine performance logs, and real-time meteorological inputs. A key innovation is the coupling of these datasets to generate adaptive routing and propulsion strategies that minimize fuel consumption, emissions, and mechanical wear while adhering to safety protocols and maritime regulations. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of vessel hydrodynamics across thousands of wave-frequency scenarios, concurrent training of neural networks on decade-scale operational data, and Monte Carlo analyses of decision pathways under uncertainty. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for optimal speed-profile adjustments, maintenance scheduling based on engine stress predictions, and policy-compliant emissions reporting templates. These results will directly inform both onboard decision-support systems and shore-based fleet management strategies while providing a scalable computational framework for maritime sustainability research. The project will also enhance the academic program's curriculum through case studies demonstrating computational methods in maritime operations, bridging theoretical naval architecture with applied data-driven decision-making. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to advance the technical foundations of efficient commercial shipping while addressing critical gaps in maritime workforce training for complex computational systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as captains, executive officers, engineers and ranking mates on commercially licensed inland, coastal and ocean-going vessels. Includes instruction in maritime traditions and law, maritime policy, economics and management of commercial marine operations, basic naval architecture and engineering, shipboard power systems engineering, crew supervision, and administrative procedures.

abstract: Molecular genetic diagnostics face growing challenges in integrating multi-omics data, resolving complex structural variants, and detecting low-frequency pathogenic variants in heterogeneous samples. Current clinical pipelines often lack the computational scalability to process large genomic datasets efficiently, hindering diagnostic accuracy for Mendelian disorders, malignancies, and infections. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational frameworks for identifying clinically actionable variants, elucidating disease mechanisms, and improving diagnostic workflows. The research will leverage whole-genome sequencing, RNA-seq, and methylation data from patients with unresolved diagnoses, focusing on three aims: (1) optimizing deep learning models for variant prioritization in non-coding regions and repetitive sequences, (2) implementing graph-based genome algorithms to resolve structural rearrangements in developmental disorders, and (3) simulating host-pathogen genomic interactions to improve detection of low-abundance pathogens in immunocompromised patients. HPC resources will enable large-scale parallelization of these tasks, including comparative analyses across 50,000+ clinical genomes, iterative training of neural networks on GPU clusters, and real-time hybrid assembly of metagenomic sequencing data. Expected outcomes include validated computational pipelines for detecting mosaic variants below 5% allele frequency, a novel classifier for pathogenic non-coding variants in developmental disorders, and a cloud-compatible platform for rapid pathogen identification. These tools will address critical bottlenecks in molecular diagnostics, reduce turnaround times for complex cases, and provide insights into genotype-phenotype correlations across diverse populations. By integrating HPC-driven analytics with clinical validation, this work will advance precision diagnostics for rare genetic diseases and inform therapeutic strategies for malignancies with molecular heterogeneity. All pipelines and models will be made open-source to foster collaboration in clinical genomics research.
cip_definition: Research on how to make or confirm diagnoses of Mendelian genetic disorders, disorders of human development, infectious diseases and malignancies, and to assess the natural history of those disorders, using the principles, theory, and technologies of molecular biology and molecular genetics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern energy systems—including power grids, renewable energy infrastructure, and hybrid energy networks—demands advanced maintenance and repair strategies to ensure reliability, efficiency, and resilience. Current approaches often rely on static diagnostic models or reactive protocols, which struggle to address dynamic interdependencies, cascading failures, and the integration of heterogeneous energy assets. This project proposes the development of a predictive maintenance framework for energy systems using high-performance computing (HPC) to enable real-time simulations, anomaly detection, and adaptive repair planning. The research problem centers on overcoming computational bottlenecks in modeling large-scale, multi-physics interactions within energy networks, particularly under fault conditions or transient operational states. The computational approach integrates graph-based network modeling, finite element analysis for component degradation, and machine learning algorithms trained on synthetic and field-collected failure datasets. HPC resources will be critical for parallelizing simulations of system-wide stress scenarios, optimizing fault localization algorithms, and training neural networks to predict component lifespans under variable loads. Expected outcomes include a scalable digital twin platform capable of simulating energy system behavior at unprecedented resolution, reducing diagnostic latency by 40-60% compared to conventional methods, and generating adaptive repair protocols that minimize downtime. The project will also produce open-source tools for technicians to visualize failure propagation pathways and prioritize interventions. By bridging computational engineering with applied maintenance practices, this work aims to advance workforce training in energy systems technologies while directly addressing operational challenges in aging infrastructure and next-generation renewable energy deployments. Results will be validated through partnerships with regional utility providers and wind farm operators, ensuring translational impact.
cip_title: Energy Systems Maintenance and Repair Technologies/ Technicians, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in energy systems maintenance and repair technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of personalized performance optimization in athletes by integrating psychosocial, physiological, and motor behavior data through computational modeling. A critical challenge in performance and sport psychology lies in disentangling the dynamic interactions between psychological states (e.g., stress, focus), physiological markers (e.g., heart rate variability, cortisol levels), and sport-specific motor outcomes (e.g., reaction time, movement precision). Traditional statistical methods often struggle to capture the nonlinear, time-dependent relationships among these multidimensional variables, particularly across diverse athlete populations. To address this, we propose developing machine learning models and agent-based simulations to identify individualized intervention strategies that enhance athletic performance and resilience. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for processing large datasets from wearable biometric sensors, psychometric assessments, and motion-capture systems across 500+ collegiate and professional athletes. Computational workflows will include recurrent neural networks to model temporal patterns in stress-response trajectories, graph-based analyses to map team communication dynamics under competitive pressure, and reinforcement learning frameworks to simulate the efficacy of mindfulness-based interventions on decision-making accuracy. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models to guide real-time biofeedback interventions during training, (2) a scalable framework for personalizing cognitive-behavioral strategies based on athlete-specific neural and behavioral profiles, and (3) open-source simulation tools to help coaches optimize team cohesion strategies. By leveraging HPC capabilities to handle high-dimensional data and complex system dynamics, this work will bridge gaps between sport psychology theory and applied performance enhancement practices, directly supporting the program’s mission to integrate counseling approaches with evidence-based athletic development. Results will be disseminated through partnerships with collegiate athletic departments and the Association for Applied Sport Psychology.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the motor, physiological, and psychosocial aspects of sport behavior. Includes instruction in applied sport psychology, clinical mental health counseling, coaching, exercise physiology, ethical performance enhancement; human development, leadership and team building, mind-body practices, neuroscience, and personality and health.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing computational demands of producing high-resolution, dynamic commercial art in an era where consumer engagement relies on increasingly complex, data-driven visual media. While advancements in generative AI and real-time rendering tools offer new creative possibilities, current consumer-grade hardware limits artists’ ability to efficiently iterate on large-scale projects, integrate multi-modal datasets, or simulate photorealistic outputs for diverse advertising platforms. This research proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and optimize computational workflows for generative design, 3D asset rendering, and adaptive media personalization. The study will employ parallelized neural networks to train custom generative models on heterogeneous datasets (including branded content, consumer behavior metrics, and stylistic precedents), enabling rapid prototyping of context-aware advertising visuals. Additionally, distributed rendering pipelines will be tested to reduce latency in producing 4K/8K outputs for augmented reality (AR) campaigns and interactive digital displays. By analyzing computational bottlenecks in existing design software through GPU-accelerated profiling, the project aims to create open-source tools that streamline resource allocation for common tasks like vector-raster conversion, texture synthesis, and cross-platform format optimization. Outcomes will include a framework for scalable, HPC-enhanced artistic workflows, reducing production timelines for high-fidelity commercial art by an estimated 30–50% while maintaining creative flexibility. This work will provide actionable insights into bridging computational efficiency with artistic intent, directly benefiting educators, digital artists, and advertising firms navigating the technical challenges of modern visual communication. The requested resources—including GPU nodes and high-memory processors—are critical for handling the terabyte-scale asset libraries and latent diffusion models central to this research.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program in the applied visual arts that prepares individuals to use artistic techniques to effectively communicate ideas and information to business and consumer audiences via illustrations and other forms of digital or printed media. Includes instruction in concept design, layout, paste-up, and techniques such as engraving, etching, silkscreen, lithography, offset, drawing and cartooning, painting, collage, and computer graphics.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in agricultural machinery operations—specifically, terrestrial and airborne crop-spraying systems, tractors, and harvesting equipment—by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to optimize performance, energy use, and environmental impact. Current practices often rely on generalized operational protocols, leading to suboptimal resource allocation, excessive chemical application, and unnecessary energy expenditure. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational framework integrating fluid dynamics simulations, machine learning (ML), and real-time sensor data analytics. High-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models will simulate spray dispersion patterns under varying environmental conditions (e.g., wind, humidity) to refine nozzle designs and application rates. Concurrently, ML algorithms trained on historical and experimental datasets will predict optimal equipment parameters—such as ground speed, spray pressure, and power distribution—across diverse field geometries and crop types. These models will be validated against field-collected data from IoT-enabled sensors monitoring machinery performance and crop responses.
