The scale and complexity of these multi-physics simulations, coupled with the need for rapid iteration in predictive ML, necessitate HPC resources to manage large datasets and parallelize computations. Expected outcomes include data-driven operational protocols that reduce chemical usage by 15–20%, lower fuel consumption by 10%, and minimize soil compaction through dynamic load distribution strategies. By enhancing the precision of agricultural machinery, this research aims to advance sustainable farming practices, reduce operational costs, and provide a scalable computational toolkit adaptable to evolving agricultural technologies. The insights gained will also inform safety standards and maintenance schedules, aligning with broader goals of improving efficiency and resilience in agribusiness operations.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to operate specialized farm, ranch, and agribusiness power equipment of a stationary, mobile, or hand-operated nature. Includes instruction in operating specialized equipment such as terrestrial and airborne crop-spraying equipment; tractors and hauling equipment; planting and harvesting equipment; cutting equipment; power sources and systems for silos, irrigation, pumping, and applications such as dairy, feeding and shearing operations; processing equipment; and applicable electrical, mechanical, and safety principles.

abstract: Telemedicine has emerged as a critical tool for expanding equitable access to medical care, yet integrating heterogeneous data streams—including electronic health records (EHRs), imaging, wearable devices, and patient-reported outcomes—into actionable clinical insights remains a significant challenge. Current approaches often lack the computational capacity to process multimodal datasets in real time, limiting their utility for dynamic decision-making in remote care settings. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for multimodal data integration and predictive analytics in telemedicine. The research will focus on three interconnected aims: (1) creating scalable pipelines to harmonize structured and unstructured data from diverse sources, (2) training machine learning models to predict clinical deterioration in chronic disease patients monitored remotely, and (3) optimizing real-time processing of streaming physiological data from wearable sensors. Computational methods will include federated learning architectures to preserve patient privacy while leveraging distributed datasets, transformer-based models for temporal EHR analysis, and GPU-accelerated signal processing algorithms for continuous vital sign interpretation. The HPC resources will enable large-scale hyperparameter optimization, validation across multi-site datasets (>100,000 patient records), and simulation of telemedicine workflows under varying network latency conditions. Expected outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for telemedicine analytics, validated predictive models for early intervention in conditions such as heart failure and diabetes, and performance benchmarks for real-time data processing in resource-constrained settings. This work will directly advance the clinical utility of telemedicine by providing computationally robust methods to synthesize complex data streams, ultimately supporting more precise, proactive, and personalized remote care delivery. By addressing both technical and translational challenges, the project aims to establish a foundation for scalable, evidence-based telemedicine systems that improve outcomes while reducing disparities in healthcare access.
cip_definition: Research on how to bring together technology and clinical medicine to enhance the overall delivery of medical care.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in formal epistemology and computational philosophy, specifically addressing the scalability of Bayesian models for analyzing complex belief-updating processes in multi-agent systems. While Bayesian methods are widely used to model rational belief revision, their application to large-scale, dynamic scenarios—such as simulations of distributed epistemic networks or iterated game-theoretic interactions—remains computationally intractable without specialized infrastructure. The research problem centers on evaluating how constraints imposed by bounded rationality and heterogeneous agent reasoning affect the convergence and stability of collective knowledge systems. To address this, the project will implement parallelized agent-based simulations using modular Bayesian networks, optimized via message-passing interfaces (MPI) to handle thousands of interacting agents with distinct epistemic policies. Computational workflows will integrate symbolic logic libraries for consistency checking and probabilistic reasoning, enabling systematic variation of parameters such as evidence thresholds, trust dynamics, and communication topologies. Expected outcomes include (1) novel insights into the relationship between computational complexity and epistemic coherence in decentralized belief systems, (2) open-source tools for scalable philosophical simulation compatible with common HPC environments, and (3) foundational data to inform meta-ethical analyses of rationality norms in artificial and human networks. By bridging formal philosophy with high-throughput computational experimentation, this work aims to establish new methodologies for testing philosophical theories under empirically-grounded constraints while demonstrating the value of advanced computing resources in humanistic inquiry.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on ideas and their logical structure, including arguments and investigations about abstract and real phenomena. Includes instruction in logic, ethics, aesthetics, epistemology, metaphysics, symbolism, and history of philosophy, and applications to the theoretical foundations and methods of other disciplines.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing demand for scalable, real-time processing of high-resolution audiovisual data in emerging communication environments, such as immersive telepresence and augmented reality (AR) applications. Current workflows struggle to balance low-latency performance with high-fidelity outputs, particularly when handling 360-degree video, spatial audio, and multi-sensor data streams. To overcome these limitations, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and optimize machine learning models for adaptive audiovisual synthesis and compression. The research will focus on training neural networks to dynamically adjust bitrate allocation, spatial resolution, and audio-visual synchronization parameters across heterogeneous networks. Computational workflows will include parallelized rendering simulations using frameworks like NVIDIA Omniverse, distributed training of transformer-based architectures for cross-modal data alignment, and GPU-accelerated testing of edge-computing deployment scenarios. Key challenges include minimizing computational overhead for real-time inference and ensuring robustness under variable bandwidth conditions. Successful implementation will yield open-source tools for content creators and telecommunication providers, reducing infrastructure costs while improving accessibility to high-quality immersive experiences. Outcomes will be validated against industry-standard metrics for latency, perceptual quality, and compression efficiency, with findings disseminated through communications technology conferences. This work directly supports the program’s mission to advance non-STEM innovation in audiovisual systems by providing a computational foundation for next-generation interactive media, with potential applications in remote education, telehealth, and collaborative virtual environments.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in audiovisual communications technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to optimize culturally-responsive pedagogical strategies for International Baccalaureate (IB) classrooms through advanced computational modeling of classroom dynamics. A critical challenge in international education is designing teaching practices that equitably engage students from diverse cultural, linguistic, and cognitive backgrounds. While qualitative studies have identified key principles of cross-cultural pedagogy, there remains a gap in systematically predicting how specific instructional choices interact with classroom heterogeneity to affect learning outcomes. To address this, we propose developing an agent-based model (ABM) simulating student-teacher interactions in virtual IB classrooms. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize thousands of agents with culturally variable traits (e.g., communication styles, prior knowledge frameworks) and test pedagogical interventions under diverse demographic configurations. The model will integrate empirical data from IB teacher surveys, student performance metrics, and classroom observation studies to ground agent behaviors in real-world patterns. Computational experiments will evaluate how variations in lesson pacing, multimodal instruction, and formative assessment strategies influence equitable participation and concept mastery across student subgroups. Sensitivity analyses will identify which cultural or developmental factors most significantly mediate instructional efficacy. Outcomes will inform a scalable framework for IB teacher training, highlighting adaptive practices that maximize inclusivity in heterogeneous classrooms. By leveraging HPC to simulate complex sociocognitive processes, this work bridges educational theory and practical implementation, offering data-driven insights to refine culturally attuned pedagogy. The resulting models and code will be shared as open-access resources for educators and researchers, fostering collaborative innovation in international teacher preparation.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach in schools that are implementing or proposing to implement the International Baccalaureate curriculum. Includes instruction in culturally-responsive classrooms, cross-cultural awareness, foundations of international education, human learning, human development, international teaching and learning, and pedagogy.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in computational resources for Burmese language studies by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze and model linguistic and literary structures unique to Burmese. Despite its rich literary tradition and complex grammatical systems, Burmese remains understudied in computational linguistics due to limited digitized corpora, insufficient NLP tools, and challenges in processing its non-Latin script. This research aims to develop scalable computational methods to advance scholarly analysis, pedagogical tools, and digital preservation efforts for Burmese texts. Key objectives include the creation of a large-scale annotated corpus spanning classical to modern Burmese literature, the training of transformer-based models for syntactic parsing and semantic analysis, and the application of machine learning to identify stylistic patterns in literary genres. The project will employ parallelized text processing pipelines to handle encoding variations and orthographic complexity, while neural architectures will be optimized to capture morphosyntactic features specific to Burmese. Computational workflows will also support OCR enhancement for historical manuscripts and statistical modeling of dialectal variations. By utilizing HPC resources, these tasks—which require intensive memory allocation and GPU acceleration—can efficiently process terabytes of textual data and iteratively refine models. Expected outcomes include open-access datasets, modular NLP tools for low-resource language researchers, and novel insights into Burmese literary evolution. This work will directly benefit linguists, educators, and preservationists by enabling data-driven approaches to studying Burmese, while contributing methodological frameworks applicable to other under-resourced languages. The requested computing infrastructure is essential to overcome current technical barriers, ensuring rigorous, reproducible scholarship in a field where manual analysis remains prohibitively time-intensive.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Burmese language. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Plant hydraulic systems are critical for maintaining water transport efficiency under environmental stress, yet the integration of structural adaptation, fluid dynamics, and mechanical feedback during drought remains poorly resolved. This project seeks to develop a multiscale computational model of plant vascular networks to predict how dynamic xylem embolism repair and tissue biomechanics interact to stabilize water transport in fluctuating arid conditions. Current models treat embolism formation as irreversible or oversimplify tissue-level hydraulic capacitance, limiting predictive power for species with active repair mechanisms. Using high-performance computing (HPC), we will parameterize a 3D lattice Boltzmann framework to simulate water transport in anatomically accurate xylem networks derived from micro-CT scans of drought-stressed woody plants, integrating real-time feedback between hydraulic resistance, osmotic adjustments, and cell wall mechanics. A parallelized multiscale solver will couple this microvascular model with whole-plant hydraulic architecture data to quantify emergent behaviors under stochastic rainfall regimes. Computational experiments will test hypotheses regarding the role of parenchyma-mediated refilling versus passive capillary recovery in maintaining hydraulic resilience. Sensitivity analyses will identify key anatomical and physiological traits conferring drought adaptation in arid-adapted species. The resulting framework will generate testable predictions for plant mortality thresholds under climate variability while providing a novel platform for simulating trait trade-offs in crop engineering. This work requires HPC resources to manage large parameter spaces, high-resolution fluid-structure interaction simulations, and ensemble modeling across ecological scenarios. Outcomes will advance mechanistic understanding of plant drought responses and inform breeding programs targeting hydraulic resilience, directly addressing food security challenges in water-limited ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of plant internal dynamics and systems, plant-environment interaction, and plant life cycles and processes. Includes instruction in cell and molecular biology; plant nutrition; plant respiration; plant growth, behavior, and reproduction; photosynthesis; plant systemics; and ecology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research on under-documented South Asian languages, focusing on the morphosyntactic analysis of endangered Indo-Aryan and Dravidian languages spoken in remote regions of Nepal, India, and Sri Lanka. Despite their cultural significance, many of these languages lack comprehensive grammatical descriptions or digital corpora, hindering both linguistic scholarship and community-led preservation efforts. The research problem centers on developing scalable, automated methods to parse complex agglutinative and inflectional structures in these languages, which challenge rule-based and statistical NLP tools trained on dominant languages. The computational approach integrates transformer-based models with finite-state morphological analyzers, trained on a newly compiled multilingual corpus of transcribed oral narratives, folktales, and ritual speech (≈500,000 tokens across 8 languages). HPC resources will enable large-scale parallel processing of audio recordings (≈2TB) through automated alignment pipelines, GPU-accelerated fine-tuning of pretrained language models, and comparative simulations of dialect variation. Expected outcomes include: (1) open-source morphological parsers for three critically endangered languages (Kusunda, Toda, and Dhivehi), (2) a computational framework adaptable to other low-resource South Asian languages, and (3) quantitative insights into historical language contact patterns through syntactic feature clustering. By reducing reliance on manual annotation, this work aims to accelerate documentation efforts while providing linguistics researchers with reproducible methods for analyzing morphologically rich languages. The requested resources directly address the computational bottlenecks of processing under-resourced languages, particularly memory-intensive tasks like training multilingual embeddings and running iterative alignment algorithms on heterogeneous audio-text data.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: South Asian Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in South Asian languages, literatures, and linguistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of forensic evidence, particularly in cases involving trace chemical mixtures, presents significant challenges for traditional analytical methods. Current techniques for deconvoluting overlapping spectral data from gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) or liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) often lack the resolution and sensitivity required to identify low-abundance compounds in degraded or contaminated samples. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing machine learning (ML) models optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of forensic chemical analysis. The research will focus on two primary objectives: (1) creating scalable algorithms to resolve complex spectral signatures from multi-component forensic samples (e.g., synthetic drug mixtures, environmental toxins in biological matrices) and (2) simulating degradation pathways of forensically relevant compounds under varying environmental conditions using molecular dynamics (MD). HPC resources will enable the training of deep neural networks on curated spectral libraries encompassing >100,000 authenticated forensic samples, as well as the execution of large-scale MD simulations to model compound stability in real-world scenarios (e.g., accelerated UV exposure, microbial interactions). The computational workflows will integrate open-source cheminformatics tools with custom Python scripts for parallelized data processing. Expected outcomes include a validated ML framework for automated compound identification with quantified uncertainty metrics and predictive models for evidence degradation timelines. These tools will directly support forensic casework by reducing turnaround times for toxicology reports, improving error rates in trace evidence analysis, and providing scientifically robust data for legal proceedings. The developed software will be disseminated as modular packages compatible with existing forensic laboratory information management systems (LIMS), ensuring broad applicability across the criminal justice sector.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of chemical techniques and instrumentation to the analysis and evaluation of physical evidence to aid in criminal investigations. Includes instruction in analytical, inorganic, organic, and physical chemistry; biochemistry; forensic toxicology; instrumental analysis; crime scene processing; criminal investigation; forensic laboratory technology; and applicable law.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate emergent collective phenomena in driven-dissipative quantum spin systems using large-scale numerical simulations. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how non-equilibrium quantum systems stabilize under competing interactions, external drives, and environmental dissipation—a fundamental challenge in modern condensed matter physics. Current analytical methods struggle to capture the complex interplay of quantum coherence, many-body interactions, and non-Markovian dissipation in these systems, necessitating advanced computational approaches. We propose to employ tensor network methods combined with variational quantum algorithms to simulate spin-1/2 lattices with time-dependent Hamiltonian drives and spatially inhomogeneous dissipation. The computational framework will leverage hybrid CPU-GPU architectures to optimize matrix product operator (MPO) contractions and time-evolving block decimation (TEBD) routines, enabling the study of system sizes beyond current numerical capabilities (up to N=100 spins). Key objectives include characterizing phase transitions between dynamically stabilized quantum states, identifying signatures of dissipative time-crystalline order, and quantifying entanglement scaling in non-equilibrium steady states. The requested high-performance computing resources will enable parameter space exploration across multiple energy scales and dissipation regimes while maintaining the numerical precision required for quantum trajectory sampling. This work will provide new insights into the control of quantum coherence in open systems, with potential applications in quantum information storage and noise-resilient quantum simulation. Results will be disseminated through open-source code packages for the broader physics community, establishing computational tools for future studies of driven-dissipative quantum matter.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in physical sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the emerging field of computational gastronomy, an interdisciplinary domain within Culinary Science/Culinology that integrates food chemistry, sensory physics, and machine learning to model and optimize complex culinary processes. The research problem centers on the lack of predictive frameworks for texture and flavor evolution in multi-phase food systems under dynamic processing conditions (e.g., sous-vide, fermentation, or extrusion). Traditional experimental approaches struggle to capture the non-linear interactions between biopolymers, colloids, and volatile compounds at relevant spatiotemporal scales, limiting the efficiency of developing novel functional ingredients or culinary techniques. The proposed computational approach combines molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with multiphysics modeling to predict phase transitions and mass transfer phenomena in heterogeneous food matrices, validated against rheological and spectroscopic data. Concurrently, graph neural networks will be trained on curated datasets of ingredient interaction matrices and sensory profiles to identify synergistic flavor-pairing rules beyond heuristic culinary traditions. By parallelizing these workflows across GPU-accelerated nodes, the project aims to establish a scalable digital twin platform for virtual prototyping of hybrid savory-plant-based analogs. Anticipated outcomes include predictive models for emulsion stability in lipid-reduced systems under shear-stress cooking methods and a generative algorithm for optimizing umami-enhancing ingredient combinations in alternative protein matrices. This work addresses critical gaps in food innovation pipelines by enabling first-principles design of sustainable culinary products while advancing computational methods tailored to the unique material complexities of edible systems. The resource allocation will directly support the development of open-source tools for the Culinology community, bridging the gap between culinary arts and precision food engineering.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the blending of food science and the culinary arts and that prepares individuals to work as research chefs and related research and development positions in the food industry. Includes instruction in culinary arts, food chemistry, food safety and quality, food processing, nutrition, and business management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize decision-making processes in multi-domain command and control (MDC2) environments under conditions of uncertainty and adversarial misinformation. Modern military operations require rapid synthesis of heterogeneous data streams—ranging from traditional intelligence reports to real-time sensor feeds and open-source information—amid deliberate attempts to degrade situational awareness. Existing tools often struggle to scale dynamically, reconcile conflicting information, or preserve decision integrity against AI-generated deception tactics. To address this gap, we propose an adaptive graph-based neural architecture that models the evolution of operational picture fidelity as a function of resource allocation, source reliability, and adversarial perturbation. The framework will integrate multi-agent reinforcement learning with game-theoretic counter-deception mechanisms, requiring iterative simulation of thousands of concurrent decision threads across probabilistic threat landscapes. High-performance computing resources are essential to train and validate models using synthetic operational datasets mirroring the scale and complexity of theater-level engagements, including non-kinetic warfare dimensions. Key technical challenges include maintaining computational tractability while scaling to network-centric battle management systems, quantifying the cascading impacts of information corruption, and preserving human-in-the-loop interpretability. Anticipated outcomes include a ranked taxonomy of resource allocation strategies for preserving decision advantage, predictive metrics for vulnerability surfaces in MDC2 workflows, and a validated reference architecture for resilient information prioritization. This work bridges critical gaps between computational social science, adversarial machine learning, and defense-specific operational research, offering methodological innovations applicable to both automated decision-support systems and the design of next-generation command interfaces. Results will be validated against classified and unclassified vignettes developed in partnership with operational military stakeholders.
cip_title: Intelligence, Command Control and Information Operations, Other (MILITARY)
cip_definition: Any instructional program in intelligence, command control and information operations, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The proposed research seeks to elucidate the role of microbial metabolic networks in modulating carbonate mineral precipitation across dynamic redox gradients in sedimentary environments—a process critical to both modern biogeochemical cycles and the interpretation of ancient biosignatures in the geologic record. While microbial influence on mineralization is well-documented, the emergent feedbacks between community-scale metabolic activity, fluid chemistry, and mineral nucleation kinetics remain poorly quantified, particularly under fluctuating redox conditions characteristic of coastal sediments and early Earth analogs. This project integrates genome-resolved metagenomics, reactive transport modeling, and machine learning-driven parameterization to bridge scales from enzymatic processes to ecosystem-level geochemical fluxes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve these multiscale interactions through three primary computational thrusts: (1) agent-based simulations of microbial consortia metabolism coupled to fluid-mineral equilibria, leveraging existing genomic databases to constrain trait-based metabolic models; (2) 3D reactive transport models incorporating experimentally derived rate laws for microbially catalyzed precipitation pathways; and (3) Bayesian uncertainty quantification across these coupled systems to identify dominant controls on mineralization fidelity. The computational framework will be validated against microfluidic sediment analogs and Late Archean carbonate relicts, enabling iterative hypothesis testing. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable modeling platform to predict microbial lithification patterns under variable redox forcings, with applications ranging from interpreting biogenicity in ancient rocks to informing engineered carbon sequestration strategies. By fusing geochemical kinetics with systems biology approaches, this work advances fundamental understanding of how microbial communities architect their mineral environments—a synthesis requiring HPC capabilities to manage complex, high-dimensional simulations that transcend traditional disciplinary boundaries in geobiology.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of how living things interact with geological systems. Includes instruction in evolution of Earth systems, geochemistry, geology, geomicrobiology, marine chemistry, paleobiology, paleoecology, paleontology, and petrology.

abstract: The increasing complexity of marine transportation systems, driven by demands for operational efficiency, environmental sustainability, and safety, necessitates advanced computational tools to address multifaceted challenges. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity simulation framework to optimize vessel routing and port operations under dynamic environmental and regulatory constraints. Current approaches often rely on simplified models that inadequately capture real-world variability, such as fluctuating weather patterns, evolving maritime traffic, and region-specific emission policies. To overcome these limitations, we propose a multi-scale computational model integrating hydrodynamic simulations, machine learning-based traffic prediction, and multi-objective optimization algorithms. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process large-scale datasets, including real-time satellite-derived oceanographic data, historical vessel trajectories, and port infrastructure metrics. Parallelized simulations will evaluate routing scenarios across diverse conditions, balancing fuel efficiency, voyage time, and compliance with International Maritime Organization (IMO) carbon intensity indicators. Additionally, the framework will incorporate stochastic modeling to assess risks associated with extreme weather events and congested waterways. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool capable of generating adaptive routing recommendations and port scheduling strategies, validated against case studies from major shipping corridors. The computational methodology will advance the field by bridging gaps between theoretical optimization models and practical operational constraints, directly contributing to the decarbonization of marine logistics. By utilizing HPC resources, this work will achieve the necessary scale and resolution to inform policy development and industry practices, ultimately supporting the transition toward sustainable marine transportation systems. Results will be disseminated through open-access simulation packages and collaborations with maritime stakeholders.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in water transportation, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the dynamics of household financial decision-making under economic volatility, with a focus on intergenerational resource allocation patterns within diverse family structures. The study addresses a critical gap in understanding how non-linear economic stressors—such as inflation shocks, fluctuating employment markets, and asymmetric access to financial technologies—affect consumption behaviors and intra-family resource distribution across different cultural and socioeconomic contexts. Traditional econometric models struggle to capture the complex, recursive interactions between macro-level economic indicators and micro-level decision-making processes, particularly when accounting for multi-agent household dynamics and evolving social norms. The proposed computational approach combines agent-based modeling (ABM) with machine learning-enhanced scenario analysis to simulate household economies at scale, incorporating heterogeneous decision rules, time-varying preference structures, and network effects from extended kinship systems. A novel feature of the methodology involves integrating natural language processing (NLP) of qualitative family financial narratives with quantitative transaction data, creating hybrid datasets that better reflect the cognitive-emotional dimensions of economic choices. The HPC infrastructure will enable simultaneous execution of thousands of parameterized simulations across multiple demographic configurations while maintaining temporal granularity at weekly intervals over decadal time horizons. Expected outcomes include the development of adaptive forecasting frameworks that can inform both private-sector financial services and public policy interventions aimed at household economic resilience. By creating open-source simulation tools tailored for family financial systems analysis, this work will establish new computational social science methodologies at the intersection of behavioral economics, consumer science, and complex systems theory, advancing research capabilities in understudied areas of human sciences.
cip_title: Business Family and Consumer Sciences/ Human Sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the relationship between the economy and the consuming individual and family. Includes instruction in consumption theory and practice, the production and distribution of retail goods and services, and the management of business enterprises.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the dynamics of decentralized, AI-driven marketplaces using high-performance computing (HPC) to model adaptive pricing algorithms in environments with fragmented data sovereignty. Traditional pricing models struggle to account for real-time, multi-stakeholder interactions in emerging decentralized markets—such as those enabled by blockchain or IoT ecosystems—where participants (e.g., autonomous agents, human buyers, and regulatory nodes) operate with asymmetric information and conflicting incentives. The computational challenge lies in simulating millions of concurrent agents with heterogeneous decision-making frameworks while preserving privacy constraints inherent to these systems. Leveraging HPC resources, the project will deploy a hybrid agent-based modeling (ABM) framework combined with federated reinforcement learning (FRL) to simulate market equilibria under dynamic regulatory and competitive conditions. The ABM layer will model agent behaviors across supply-demand networks, while FRL will train pricing policies in a distributed manner, minimizing data centralization risks. Key outcomes include the development of robust, privacy-preserving pricing strategies that balance efficiency, fairness, and compliance in decentralized commerce. The research will also quantify scalability limits of current decentralized autonomous organization (DAO) market structures under stress scenarios, such as rapid resource scarcity or regulatory shocks. By integrating computational economics with distributed systems design, this work aims to advance strategic decision-making tools for businesses operating in next-generation digital markets while contributing theoretical insights into emergent collective behaviors in decentralized economies. Results will be validated against real-world datasets from tokenized energy markets and decentralized finance (DeFi) platforms, ensuring pragmatic relevance. The project’s computational demands stem from the need to parallelize complex game-theoretic simulations and optimize neural policy networks across thousands of GPU nodes, requiring sustained access to HPC infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general study of business, including the processes of interchanging goods and services (buying, selling and producing), business organization, and accounting as used in profit-making and nonprofit public and private institutions and agencies. The programs may prepare individuals to apply business principles and techniques in various occupational settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for simulating and optimizing the dynamic interplay between cultural heritage structures and evolving urban microclimates, a challenge at the intersection of architectural preservation, climatology, and data-driven design. Traditional preservation methods often rely on static models, failing to account for real-time environmental stressors such as particulate pollution, humidity fluctuations, and thermal expansion in dense urban contexts. To address this gap, we propose a high-fidelity simulation pipeline leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model multi-scale interactions between historical building materials, localized weather patterns, and anthropogenic factors over decadal timescales. The computational approach integrates 3D laser scan datasets of heritage sites with regional climate projections, employing finite element analysis (FEA) for material stress modeling and agent-based systems to simulate cumulative human impact. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify non-linear degradation patterns and optimize preservation strategies through iterative scenario testing. By enabling predictive analysis of structural vulnerabilities under diverse environmental conditions, this research aims to establish a new paradigm for adaptive preservation planning. The anticipated outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for heritage stakeholders and novel metrics for quantifying preservation efficacy in urban systems. Successful implementation requires HPC resources to manage the concurrent processing of terabyte-scale geospatial datasets, real-time fluid dynamics simulations, and parametric optimization tasks that exceed the capabilities of conventional architectural software. This work bridges computational science and cultural heritage management, advancing methodological innovation in a specialized niche of architectural research with implications for sustainable urban development and climate resilience planning.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in architecture, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize crisis response strategies during large-scale, multi-hazard disasters, with a focus on improving the efficiency and adaptability of incident command systems (ICS). Current disaster response models often fail to account for the dynamic interdependencies between variables such as real-time resource availability, evolving environmental conditions, population mobility, and cross-agency communication bottlenecks. To address this gap, we propose an integrated simulation platform leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex disaster scenarios, including cascading events like hurricane-induced infrastructure failure combined with mass casualty incidents. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling to simulate civilian and responder behaviors, network analysis to assess critical infrastructure resilience, and machine learning algorithms to predict incident escalation patterns. HPC resources will enable parallelized scenario testing across thousands of parametric variations, including climate-driven hazard intensities, resource deployment strategies, and ICS organizational structures. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool capable of identifying optimal resource allocation strategies under uncertainty, evaluating the systemic impacts of contingency plans, and stress-testing joint operations protocols for interagency coordination. The simulations will specifically address challenges in volunteer management, medical surge capacity, and critical infrastructure prioritization during compound crises. By incorporating real-time data assimilation capabilities, this framework aims to reduce latency in emergency decision-making while maintaining alignment with ethical and legal constraints inherent in disaster response operations. Results will directly inform ICS training programs and national-level preparedness guidelines, with potential applications in public health emergencies, terrorism response, and climate adaptation planning.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the application of the incident command system model to formulating and implementing effective response to natural and man-made disasters. Includes instruction in contingency planning, hazard and risk assessment, joint operations, law and ethics, emergency response and recovery, event mitigation, emergency rescue and medical operations, incident command, terrorism and national security issues, law enforcement, relief administration, volunteer and citizen coordination, public relations and applications to specific types of incidents.

abstract: Aircraft systems are increasingly reliant on complex avionics architectures that integrate real-time sensor data, automated control algorithms, and fault-tolerant communication networks. Maintaining these systems requires advanced diagnostic tools capable of predicting component degradation and optimizing maintenance schedules. This project seeks to develop a machine learning framework for predictive maintenance of avionics systems by analyzing multi-modal sensor data, including flight control telemetry, environmental sensor readings, and historical maintenance logs. The computational challenges stem from processing high-frequency, heterogeneous datasets spanning terabytes from fleets of aircraft, coupled with the need to train physics-informed neural networks that model component wear under dynamic operational conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle parallelized data ingestion, hyperparameter optimization of ensemble models, and multi-scale simulations of failure propagation in avionic subsystems. The proposed methods combine graph neural networks to model interdependencies among avionics components with reinforcement learning to optimize inspection protocols. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive model for critical failures in navigation and communication systems, reducing unplanned maintenance events by an estimated 30–40%; (2) an open-source toolkit for simulating sensor-to-maintenance decision pipelines under hardware-in-the-loop constraints; and (3) actionable insights into material fatigue patterns in next-generation fly-by-wire systems. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work aims to bridge gaps between data-driven prognostics and domain-specific aviation safety standards, directly enhancing training protocols for avionics technicians through synthetic fault scenario generation. The results will provide a template for scalable maintenance analytics applicable to both legacy aircraft and emerging electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) platforms.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain all types of aircraft operating, control, and electronic systems. Includes instruction in flight instrumentation, aircraft communications and homing systems, radar and other sensory systems, navigation aids, and specialized systems for various types of civilian and military aircraft.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamics of intercultural communication and conflict resolution within digitally mediated environments, integrating computational social science, network analysis, and cultural anthropology. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how algorithmic and structural biases in digital platforms—such as social media, collaborative workspaces, or hybrid education tools—shape intergroup perceptions and exacerbate or mitigate polarization in multicultural settings. Current models often oversimplify cultural variables or fail to account for the nonlinear, context-dependent interactions between diverse social identities, institutional policies, and platform-specific affordances. To address this, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework that simulates large-scale, heterogeneous populations interacting within parameterized digital environments. Agents will be endowed with dynamic cultural traits (e.g., values, communication styles, conflict resolution strategies) informed by empirical data from ethnographic studies and cross-cultural psychology. The ABM will integrate machine learning to analyze real-world datasets—including multilingual social media discourse, organizational diversity training outcomes, and intercultural negotiation records—to calibrate agent behaviors and environmental conditions. HPC resources are essential to iteratively run simulations at scale (10^4–10^5 agents), test emergent hypotheses about intervention efficacy (e.g., moderation policies, algorithmic fairness adjustments), and perform sensitivity analyses across diverse sociocultural contexts. Expected outcomes include predictive models of how digital infrastructure design influences intercultural trust-building, a publicly accessible toolkit for simulating diversity-focused policy impacts, and evidence-based recommendations for mitigating systemic biases in multistakeholder platforms. By bridging computational rigor with qualitative insights, this work advances interdisciplinary methodologies for studying multicultural dynamics in increasingly digitized societies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the dynamic social relations between and among majority and minority groups and different minority groups, and ways to promote mutual tolerance, inter-group cooperation, and the leadership and management of diverse groups and diversity issues in family, educational, recreational, and work settings. Includes instruction in ethnic and cultural studies, group psychology, sociology, anthropology, conflict resolution, human services and resources, and applications to various functional environments.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamics of cross-disciplinary knowledge integration in unstructured academic environments, a critical challenge in multidisciplinary studies. While General Studies programs emphasize broad intellectual exploration, the lack of structured frameworks for synthesizing diverse domains—from humanities to emerging technologies—often limits the coherence and applicability of insights. The research problem centers on identifying scalable computational methods to model, analyze, and visualize interdisciplinary connections within large-scale educational and scholarly datasets. The project will employ machine learning algorithms, network analysis, and natural language processing (NLP) to map conceptual relationships across unstructured curricula, publication corpora, and student outcome data. Key computational tasks include training transformer-based models to detect latent thematic links between disparate disciplines, simulating the impact of curricular flexibility on knowledge retention, and clustering interdisciplinary research trends using high-dimensional data. These methods require HPC resources due to the volume of text-based datasets (e.g., historical course catalogs, academic journals) and the iterative nature of optimizing neural networks for low-resource, multidisciplinary contexts. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for evaluating the efficacy of unstructured academic programs, predictive tools to guide resource allocation in multidisciplinary education, and open-access visualizations of interdisciplinary knowledge networks. The findings will contribute to pedagogical strategies that balance intellectual breadth with analytical rigor, addressing gaps in how institutions support multidisciplinary learning. By quantifying the interplay between unstructured study and intellectual synthesis, this work aims to advance computational approaches to educational design while demonstrating the value of HPC in non-STEM interdisciplinary research.
cip_definition: An undifferentiated program that includes instruction in the general arts, general science, or unstructured studies.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing instructional strategies in STEM education by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and analyze the efficacy of integrated, technology-enhanced learning environments. Despite growing emphasis on interdisciplinary STEM curricula, educators lack robust frameworks to predict how specific pedagogical approaches—such as project-based learning or adaptive educational technologies—affect the development of critical thinking and problem-solving skills in PreK-12 students. Current evaluation methods often rely on static assessments, which fail to capture the dynamic, non-linear interactions between instructional design, student engagement, and learning outcomes. To bridge this gap, we propose a computational study combining agent-based modeling, machine learning, and large-scale data analytics. The research will simulate classroom dynamics using anonymized longitudinal datasets (e.g., student performance metrics, interaction logs from digital learning platforms, and teacher feedback) to identify patterns in skill acquisition and knowledge transfer. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of multimodal data streams, training predictive models to forecast the impact of variables such as lesson sequencing, real-time feedback mechanisms, and collaborative learning structures. Additionally, we will employ natural language processing to analyze qualitative inputs, such as student reflections and teacher journals, enriching quantitative models with contextual insights. Outcomes will include a validated computational framework for designing adaptive STEM curricula, actionable recommendations for scaling effective teaching practices, and open-source tools to help educators visualize the projected outcomes of pedagogical choices. By elucidating the causal relationships between instructional methods and student competencies, this work aims to advance evidence-based strategies for STEM education, ultimately fostering equitable, data-driven teacher leadership and improving readiness in STEM fields for diverse learners.
cip_title: Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) Educational Methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to connect education practices with scientific, engineering, and mathematical principles for PreK-12 students. Includes instruction in critical thinking, curriculum and instruction, history of STEM education, integrating STEM across curricula, learning sciences and technology, STEM education methods, and teacher leadership in STEM education.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the molecular and systemic mechanisms underlying metabolic disorders in ruminants, with a focus on dairy cattle experiencing ketosis—a prevalent and economically significant condition in livestock agriculture. Current experimental approaches to study these disorders face limitations in resolving dynamic, multi-scale interactions between hormonal regulation, tissue-specific metabolism, and systemic pathophysiology. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating multi-omics data (transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic) with physiologically based pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PBPK-PD) models. These models will simulate hormone-receptor binding kinetics, hepatic lipid metabolism, and inter-organ crosstalk under varying metabolic stressors. Machine learning algorithms will identify critical regulatory nodes and predict biomarkers for early disease detection. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational complexity of stochastic molecular dynamics simulations (using tools like GROMACS) and large-scale parameter optimization for organ-level models. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel therapeutic targets to modulate hepatic ketogenesis, predictive models of metabolic resilience, and a publicly accessible database of ruminant-specific physiological parameters. This work will advance precision veterinary medicine by enabling targeted interventions, reducing livestock morbidity, and improving agricultural sustainability. The developed computational pipelines will also provide a template for studying analogous metabolic syndromes in non-mammalian species, broadening translational applications in veterinary physiology.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the functional dynamics of animal biological systems and their relationship to the diagnosis and treatment of disease and injury. Includes instruction in mammalian and non-mammalian physiology, laboratory physiology, physiological responses to the environment, endocrinology, animal biotechnology, mechanisms of hormone action, organ systems, metabolism, and pathophysiology.

abstract: The integration of advanced genomic tools into agricultural animal breeding programs has created unprecedented opportunities to optimize traits such as disease resistance, feed efficiency, and climate adaptability. However, the computational challenges of analyzing high-dimensional genomic data—including whole-genome sequences, epigenetic profiles, and multi-trait phenotypic records—limit the scalability and precision of current breeding strategies. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale genomic prediction and selection analyses for heterogeneous cattle populations. Leveraging statistical models that combine single-step genomic best linear unbiased prediction (ssGBLUP) with deep learning architectures, we aim to disentangle genotype-by-environment interactions and predict breeding values for complex traits under variable management conditions. The computational workflow will process terabytes of genomic data from public repositories and collaborative breeding programs, requiring parallelized Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling and GPU-accelerated neural network training. Key deliverables include optimized algorithms for prioritizing candidate sires and dams, as well as open-source software tailored for livestock genomics. The outcomes will directly inform breeding decisions for three partner herds, targeting a 15–20% acceleration in genetic gain for heat tolerance and methane efficiency traits. By overcoming existing bottlenecks in data integration and model training, this work will establish a replicable framework for precision breeding in ruminants, enhancing the sustainability of livestock systems amid climate volatility. The requested resources are critical to achieving the necessary throughput for these analyses, which involve millions of genetic markers and complex covariance structures. This project bridges gaps between quantitative genetics and computational innovation, offering scalable solutions to global challenges in animal agriculture.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of genetics and genetic engineering to the improvement of agricultural animal health, the development of new animal breeds, and the selective improvement of agricultural animal populations. Includes instruction in genetics, genetic engineering, population genetics, animal health, animal husbandry, and biotechnology.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in real-time voice writing technology, particularly in improving the accuracy and efficiency of automated transcription and captioning systems for diverse communication contexts. Current voice writing tools struggle with processing spontaneous speech, overlapping dialogue, and specialized terminology across media formats (e.g., live broadcasts, courtroom proceedings, multilingual interviews). These limitations hinder accessibility for deaf and hard-of-hearing audiences and reduce reliability in fast-paced professional environments. To overcome these barriers, we propose developing an adaptive neural network architecture optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments. The model will integrate speech recognition, acoustic feature extraction, and contextual language modeling to handle variable speech patterns, background noise, and domain-specific jargon. Computational workflows will leverage GPU-accelerated training on large-scale datasets of annotated speech from media archives, legal depositions, and live event recordings. Key technical challenges include parallel processing of multi-speaker audio streams, low-latency inference for real-time captioning, and dynamic vocabulary adaptation through few-shot learning techniques. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid iteration on transformer-based architectures and comparative analysis of hybrid models combining rule-based shorthand systems with deep learning. Expected outcomes include a 30-50% reduction in word error rates for complex audio inputs compared to existing commercial systems, along with open-source tools for customizable captioning interfaces. This research will directly benefit journalism education by creating publicly accessible transcription benchmarks and interdisciplinary collaboration frameworks between computational linguistics and media studies. By scaling voice writing systems to handle real-world communication complexities, the project aims to advance inclusive access to digital content while establishing best practices for ethically aligned AI-assisted journalism tools.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to use voice writing computer software and speak a verbal shorthand language to create transcripts and screen captioning of live or recorded events intended for the public or a specific audience in a variety of media (e.g., digital, film, print, television) as well as for conferences, conversations, interviews, and meetings. Includes instruction in screen captioning, speed building, spoken shorthand, transcription, and voice input writing.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of sensory perception modeling in immersive culinary environments, a niche interdisciplinary domain intersecting gastronomy, cognitive science, and computational design. Traditional culinary research has focused on ingredient chemistry or nutritional outcomes, leaving a critical gap in understanding how multisensory stimuli—such as visual presentation, ambient sound, and contextual storytelling—collectively shape diners’ experiential and emotional responses. The research problem centers on developing predictive models to simulate and optimize hyper-realistic dining scenarios, enabling chefs and experiential designers to prototype sensory-driven menus or entertainment-based culinary services without costly physical trials. The computational approach integrates three core components: (1) agent-based modeling to simulate diner behavior and decision-making under variable sensory inputs, (2) machine learning algorithms trained on biometric datasets (e.g., eye-tracking, galvanic skin response) to correlate environmental factors with emotional engagement, and (3) fluid dynamics simulations to model the interaction of aroma dispersion with spatial design elements. These methods will be unified within a scalable, GPU-accelerated framework to handle the high-dimensional parameter space of real-world culinary environments. The project’s significance lies in its potential to establish a new paradigm for data-driven culinary innovation, reducing resource-intensive experimentation while enhancing personalized dining experiences. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source toolkit for sensory scenario prototyping, validated through partnerships with experimental restaurants and immersive theater groups. By bridging computational rigor with creative culinary practices, this work aims to catalyze advancements in entertainment-driven gastronomy and expand the methodological toolkit for interdisciplinary research at the intersection of art, technology, and hospitality.
cip_title: Culinary, Entertainment, and Personal Services, Other.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in culinary, entertainment, and personal services not listed above.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of legislative coalition formation in multiparty systems using advanced computational modeling, with a focus on understanding how institutional rules and interest group networks shape policy outcomes. Despite extensive theoretical work on legislative behavior, existing models struggle to capture the nonlinear interactions between formal procedural constraints, informal lobbying networks, and ideological bargaining in large, heterogeneous legislatures—a gap particularly relevant to contemporary challenges in fragmented democracies. The research employs a multi-method computational approach combining agent-based modeling (ABM), network analysis, and machine learning-driven text analysis of legislative records. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for three components: (1) large-scale ABM simulations parameterized with ideological positions of 5,000+ legislators across 30 countries, (2) dynamic network analysis tracking interest group influence through temporal graph neural networks, and (3) transformer-based NLP analysis of parliamentary speech data to detect coalition signaling patterns. The computational architecture will utilize parallelized Monte Carlo methods for sensitivity testing across institutional scenarios and GPU-accelerated graph processing for real-time network visualization. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for predicting coalition stability under different electoral rules, quantitative measures of procedural vs. network-based influence on legislation, and open-source tools for legislative analytics. Results will advance formal theories of institutional design while providing practical insights for constitutional reformers and international governance organizations. The project’s scale—requiring simultaneous processing of 10TB+ structured voting records, 50 million parliamentary speech tokens, and 100,000 simulated legislative sessions—necessitates dedicated HPC allocation beyond standard campus computing capacities. By integrating political theory with computational social science methods, this work aims to establish new standards for data-intensive legislative studies while directly addressing core questions in comparative political institutions.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in political science and government, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive, data-driven instructional strategies for K–12 students with emotional disturbances (ED). Students with ED exhibit complex, heterogeneous needs that challenge traditional one-size-fits-all pedagogical approaches. While individualized education plans (IEPs) are mandated, their design often relies on qualitative observations and static assessments, limiting real-time responsiveness to students’ dynamic emotional and academic states. This research addresses the critical gap in scalable, computationally informed tools to model the interplay between emotional regulation, behavioral triggers, and learning outcomes. Using anonymized longitudinal datasets—including academic performance records, behavioral incident logs, and teacher-reported observational data from six urban school districts—we will train machine learning models to identify patterns in emotional dysregulation and its impact on task engagement. HPC resources are essential for processing multimodal data at scale, running ensemble models to account for contextual variables (e.g., classroom environment, curricular content), and simulating the potential efficacy of targeted interventions across diverse student profiles. The computational pipeline will integrate natural language processing to analyze qualitative IEP notes, reinforcement learning to iteratively refine intervention recommendations, and agent-based modeling to predict how adjustments to instructional pacing or socioemotional supports might alter student outcomes. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for educators to generate dynamic IEP scaffolds, optimized intervention timing protocols, and a teacher training module on interpreting computational insights within ethical frameworks. By bridging educational practice and computational analytics, this work aims to empower teachers with empirically grounded strategies to improve engagement and reduce disparities in academic achievement for students with ED.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Emotional Disturbances
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with emotional conditions which adversely affect their educational performance and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with emotional disturbances, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising individuals with emotional disturbances, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable optimization frameworks for dynamic resource allocation in large-scale, stochastic operational systems, with applications in supply chain resilience, healthcare logistics, and distributed energy networks. A critical challenge in these domains lies in balancing real-time decision-making under uncertainty with complex interdependencies among resources, agents, and constraints. Traditional methods often rely on simplifications that compromise solution quality or computational tractability when applied to industry-relevant problem scales. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid computational approach integrating stochastic programming, agent-based simulation, and machine learning-driven optimization. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable three key innovations: (1) parallel Monte Carlo tree search for multi-stage stochastic optimization under non-stationary uncertainty, (2) distributed decomposition algorithms leveraging heterogeneous computing architectures to solve billion-variable mixed-integer programming models, and (3) neural network surrogates trained on HPC-generated datasets to accelerate real-time decision support. The computational workflows will be implemented using open-source optimization libraries (Pyomo, JuMP) and scaled via MPI and GPU-accelerated frameworks. Expected outcomes include new convergence guarantees for asynchronous stochastic decomposition methods, benchmark solutions for previously intractable problem instances in the Operations Research Library (OR-Lib), and open-access digital twins of critical infrastructure systems. This work directly advances the core mission of industrial engineering and operations research by developing computationally rigorous tools for human-in-the-loop system optimization. The requested resources will support 15M CPU-hours and 50k GPU-hours annually to handle memory-intensive scenario trees, cross-domain simulations, and large-scale hyperparameter tuning. Results will be disseminated through INFORMS journals and community workshops to bridge academic methodology with industrial practice.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development and application of complex mathematical or simulation models to solve problems involving operational systems, where the system concerned is subject to human intervention. Includes instruction in advanced multivariate analysis, application of judgment and statistical tests, optimization theory and techniques, resource allocation theory, mathematical modeling, control theory, statistical analysis, and applications to specific research problems.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the computational modeling of liturgical adaptation patterns across Christian denominations in response to socio-cultural shifts, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale textual and ethnographic datasets. While liturgical studies traditionally focus on theological or historical frameworks, this study adopts an interdisciplinary approach, integrating computational linguistics, network analysis, and cultural analytics to map how liturgical texts, rituals, and community practices evolve under pressures such as globalization, digitalization, and demographic change. The research problem centers on identifying latent patterns in liturgical innovation and conservatism, which are critical for understanding how religious communities negotiate identity and continuity in rapidly changing environments. The computational methodology involves three phases: (1) preprocessing and digitizing a corpus of liturgical texts, rubrics, and pastoral guidelines from 20 denominations spanning 2000–2023; (2) training transformer-based models to detect semantic shifts and syntactic innovations in liturgical language; and (3) applying dynamic network analysis to trace the diffusion of liturgical adaptations across denominational and geographic boundaries. HPC resources are essential for handling the scale and complexity of multimodal data (text, audio, video), enabling parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets and iterative model training. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible interactive visualization platform mapping liturgical change trajectories and a predictive framework for anticipating future adaptations. This work contributes to emerging digital humanities scholarship by bridging computational methods with theological praxis, offering practical tools for faith communities navigating liturgical renewal while advancing methodological innovation in the study of ritual systems as complex adaptive networks.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for ordination as ministers or priests in any of the Christian religious traditions. Includes instruction in the theology and polity of a particular church, church law, liturgy and ritual, principles of pastoral ministry, homiletics, evangelism, church/parish organization and management, Christian ethics, church history, and related studies.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of personalizing instructional strategies for students with diverse learning needs in special education settings. Current approaches to designing and evaluating individualized interventions often rely on manual, time-intensive analyses of student performance, behavioral data, and qualitative teacher observations. These methods struggle to integrate multi-modal datasets at scale, limiting educators’ ability to identify patterns, predict learning trajectories, and adapt evidence-based practices efficiently. To overcome these barriers, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop computational models that analyze large-scale, heterogeneous educational datasets. These include structured records (e.g., academic assessments, attendance) and unstructured data (e.g., teacher narratives, speech-to-text transcripts from classroom interactions). Machine learning techniques, including natural language processing and time-series analysis, will be applied to identify correlations between instructional methods, student engagement, and longitudinal outcomes across varied disabilities and learning environments. Computational simulations will further test hypothetical intervention scenarios to optimize resource allocation for maximal student impact. By automating the synthesis of complex data streams, this project aims to generate actionable insights for educators, such as predictive tools for early intervention and adaptive lesson-planning frameworks tailored to neurodiverse learners. The outcomes will advance the scalability of precision education in special education contexts while maintaining rigorous ethical standards for data privacy and equity. Access to HPC infrastructure is essential to process terabytes of anonymized student records, train deep learning models with sufficient parameter depth, and run iterative simulations within educationally relevant timeframes. This work directly supports the preparation of future special education teachers by providing empirically validated, computationally enhanced strategies to address the variability of student needs in inclusive classrooms.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in special education, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of psychosocial and physiological predictors of athletic performance optimization. The research problem centers on the integration of large-scale, multimodal datasets—including biometric data (e.g., heart rate variability, EEG), psychometric assessments (e.g., resilience, focus), and performance metrics (e.g., reaction times, skill execution accuracy)—to model dynamic interactions between mental training interventions and sport outcomes. Current approaches in performance and sport psychology often rely on small-sample studies or isolated variables, limiting the ability to identify complex, nonlinear relationships or personalize interventions. To address this gap, the project will employ machine learning techniques, including recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and graph-based analytics, to process longitudinal data from 500+ collegiate and elite athletes. These models will identify patterns linking specific mind-body practices (e.g., mindfulness, imagery) to performance outcomes under varying physiological stressors. A second computational strand will utilize agent-based modeling to simulate team cohesion dynamics, incorporating psychosocial variables such as leadership styles and communication networks. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling high-dimensional datasets (10+ TB), parallelizing model training across thousands of iterations, and running real-time simulations of intervention scenarios. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive frameworks to optimize individualized mental skill training regimens, (2) evidence-based protocols for enhancing team synchrony in competitive environments, and (3) open-source tools for sport psychologists to analyze biopsychosocial data streams. By bridging counseling psychology principles with computational rigor, this work aims to establish scalable methodologies for performance enhancement while advancing theoretical understanding of neuromotor-psychosocial integration in athletic contexts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the motor, physiological, and psychosocial aspects of sport behavior. Includes instruction in applied sport psychology, clinical mental health counseling, coaching, exercise physiology, ethical performance enhancement; human development, leadership and team building, mind-body practices, neuroscience, and personality and health.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the complex biomechanical and biochemical interactions underlying periodontal disease progression, with a focus on optimizing personalized treatment strategies. Despite advances in dental diagnostics, the multifactorial etiology of periodontitis—involving host-microbial interactions, inflammatory cascades, and biomechanical stress—remains inadequately characterized. Traditional experimental approaches struggle to model these dynamic, multiscale processes efficiently. This project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a multi-scale computational framework integrating agent-based modeling, finite element analysis, and machine learning. Agent-based models will simulate microbial community dynamics and host immune responses at the cellular level, while finite element models will map mechanical stress distributions in periodontal tissues under varying occlusal loads. Machine learning algorithms, trained on multi-omics datasets (metagenomic, proteomic, and clinical data), will identify predictive biomarkers of disease progression and treatment response. The computational pipeline will be validated against longitudinal clinical data from a cohort of 500 patients with stage III/IV periodontitis. By parallelizing simulations across HPC nodes, we aim to achieve real-time analysis of tissue-level biomechanics and microbial ecology interactions, which is infeasible with conventional computing infrastructure. Expected outcomes include (1) mechanistic insights into synergistic effects of microbial dysbiosis and biomechanical stress on periodontal breakdown, (2) predictive models for individualized risk stratification, and (3) in silico optimization of occlusal adjustment protocols to mitigate inflammation. This work will establish a novel computational platform for accelerating translational research in periodontology, with potential applications to implantology and oral rehabilitation. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the project's computational demands, including processing 40+ TB of multimodal data and executing >10,000 concurrent simulations to capture biological variability.
cip_title: Dental Services and Allied Professions, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in dental services and allied professions, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Maintaining modern building systems—encompassing HVAC, electrical, plumbing, and structural components—requires addressing complex interdependencies between aging infrastructure, energy efficiency demands, and dynamic environmental conditions. Current maintenance strategies often rely on reactive or schedule-based approaches, which can lead to suboptimal resource allocation, unexpected failures, and energy waste. This project seeks to develop a computational framework for predictive, condition-based maintenance by modeling whole-building system interactions under diverse operational and environmental scenarios. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate sensor-derived IoT data from commercial and industrial buildings with physics-based simulations of mechanical system degradation, energy flow dynamics, and failure propagation. Machine learning models will be trained on multi-scale datasets to identify early warning signatures of component failures and optimize maintenance schedules.
