Key computational challenges include resolving time-dependent thermal-hydraulic-electrical couplings in building systems at scale, processing high-resolution sensor streams in real time, and quantifying uncertainty across heterogeneous data sources. The HPC environment will enable parallelized simulations of building clusters, Monte Carlo analyses for risk assessment, and iterative training of neural networks on GPU-accelerated nodes. Successful implementation will yield actionable maintenance prioritization algorithms, reduce unplanned downtime by 25–40% in pilot facilities, and provide energy-saving recommendations through adaptive system controls. Outcomes will advance data-driven decision-making in building operations, directly supporting workforce training initiatives in predictive maintenance technologies. This work aligns with broader sustainability goals by extending equipment lifespans and minimizing resource waste in built environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to keep a building functioning, and to service a variety of structures including commercial and industrial buildings and mobile homes. Includes instruction in the basic maintenance and repair skills required to service building systems, such as air conditioning, heating, plumbing, electrical, major appliances, and other mechanical systems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the spatial and temporal dynamics of cultural identity formation in historical Western Europe through large-scale textual and visual datasets. Focusing on the Iberian Peninsula and the Western Mediterranean (12th–17th centuries), the research addresses a critical gap in understanding how localized cultural narratives—expressed in vernacular literature, religious treatises, and artistic iconography—interacted with broader regional discourses to shape collective identities. The computational challenge lies in processing and correlating fragmented, multilingual primary sources (e.g., digitized manuscripts, municipal records, and art inventories) that exceed the scale feasible for manual analysis. A hybrid method combining natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision techniques will be deployed: transformer-based models fine-tuned on medieval Latin, Arabic, and early Romance texts will identify semantic patterns related to communal self-representation, while convolutional neural networks (CNNs) will classify visual motifs in digitized art and architectural plans. These pipelines will be integrated via graph-based network analysis to map how cultural nodes (e.g., monastic scriptoria, trade hubs) propagated or contested identity markers across time. HPC resources are essential for training domain-specific multilingual models, processing high-resolution image datasets (>50,000 items), and simulating network diffusion dynamics at scale. Expected outcomes include 1) a geotemporal database tracking the evolution of identity-linked symbols and narratives, 2) probabilistic models quantifying the influence of socioeconomic factors on cultural hybridity, and 3) open-source tools for cross-modal analysis of premodern sources. By computationally bridging textual and visual evidence, this work aims to redefine scholarly paradigms of cultural transmission in Western Europe, offering methodological frameworks applicable to underrepresented regions and non-canonical materials.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of historical Western Europe, defined as including Britain, Ireland, France, the Low Countries, the Iberian Peninsula, Italy, the Western Mediterranean, and related island groups and borderlands.

abstract: The increasing complexity of automotive systems, particularly in electrification, autonomous functionality, and energy efficiency, demands advanced computational tools to optimize design and validation processes. This project seeks to address critical challenges in automotive engineering technology by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate multi-physics interactions in next-generation vehicle systems. Current limitations in local computational capacity restrict the fidelity and scalability of simulations for electric vehicle (EV) battery thermal management, aerodynamic optimization of autonomous vehicle platforms, and real-time durability testing of lightweight composite materials. To overcome these barriers, the proposed research will employ parallelized computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models, finite element analysis (FEA) for structural mechanics, and machine learning-driven optimization algorithms. These methods will enable high-resolution simulations of coupled thermal-electrochemical processes in EV batteries under extreme operating conditions, transient aerodynamic loads on vehicle bodies during dynamic maneuvers, and fatigue behavior of advanced material systems. The HPC environment will facilitate parametric studies at unprecedented scales, reducing reliance on physical prototyping and accelerating iterative design refinement. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for battery lifespan, aerodynamically efficient vehicle configurations for reduced energy consumption, and data-driven guidelines for material selection in safety-critical components. By integrating these computational insights, the project aims to advance sustainable automotive technologies while training students in HPC workflows for industry-relevant engineering challenges. The resource allocation will directly support the program’s mission to bridge theoretical principles with technical applications, fostering innovation in automotive system development and testing methodologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers and other professionals engaged in developing, manufacturing and testing self-propelled ground vehicles and their systems. Includes instruction in vehicular systems technology, design and development testing, prototype and operational testing, inspection and maintenance procedures, instrument calibration, test equipment operation and maintenance, and report preparation.

abstract: The increasing frequency of marine heatwaves and shifting nutrient regimes in coastal ecosystems has raised urgent questions about their impacts on microbial community dynamics and biogeochemical cycling. This project seeks to advance predictive understanding of how these stressors alter microbial metabolic networks and carbon export efficiency in temperate and polar coastal systems. We propose a high-resolution, trait-based modeling framework to simulate microbial community interactions, metabolic plasticity, and organic matter remineralization across multiple spatial scales (1 km to 10 m resolution). The model will integrate multi-omics datasets from ongoing field campaigns in the Gulf of Maine and Antarctic Peninsula with hydrodynamic and biogeochemical observations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve (1) submesoscale physical-biological coupling using a nested-grid approach within the Regional Ocean Modeling System (ROMS), and (2) genome-informed flux balance analysis of microbial functional guilds under varying temperature and dissolved organic carbon regimes. Anticipated computational requirements include 200,000 core-hours monthly for ensemble simulations spanning decadal timescales, with parallelized parameter optimization through Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into climate-driven regime shifts in coastal carbon storage capacity, with particular attention to polar systems where microbial responses remain poorly constrained. The resulting open-source model framework will enable improved projections of marine carbon-climate feedbacks while providing critical benchmarks for international programs like GEOTRACES and the UN Ocean Decade. By quantifying thresholds in microbial resilience, this work directly addresses management needs for coastal ecosystems facing unprecedented environmental change.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of biology, chemistry, geology and physics applied to marine, estuarine and coastal environments. Includes instruction in marine biogeochemistry, atmosphere and ocean dynamics, coastal ecology, coastal ocean processes, microbial ecology, marine ecosystem modeling, and polar microbiology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in cross-lingual natural language understanding (NLU), addressing critical gaps in computational models’ ability to generalize across typologically diverse languages. While modern neural architectures excel in high-resource languages like English, their performance drops significantly for languages with limited annotated data or divergent syntactic structures. This limitation stems from insufficient modeling of universal linguistic patterns and inadequate computational scale for training robust multilingual systems. Our interdisciplinary approach integrates theoretical linguistics with machine learning to develop novel neural frameworks that explicitly encode syntactic and semantic universals, such as morphosyntactic alignment and argument structure hierarchies, into transformer-based models. The proposed work involves large-scale pretraining on massively multilingual corpora, covering over 100 languages from 30+ language families, paired with structured linguistic annotations from treebanks and lexical databases. Key computational challenges include optimizing dynamic attention mechanisms for variable morphosyntactic complexity and implementing efficient distributed training pipelines for heterogeneous language data. HPC resources are essential for three phases: (1) pretraining billion-parameter models on GPU clusters using mixed-precision optimization, (2) running parallelized ablation studies to quantify the impact of specific linguistic features on model transferability, and (3) executing fine-grained error analysis across language typology dimensions. Expected outcomes include state-of-the-art benchmarks on cross-lingual tasks (semantic role labeling, coreference resolution), publicly released models with built-in linguistic interpretability features, and theoretical insights about the learnability of linguistic universals in artificial systems. This work bridges computational efficiency with linguistic accountability, offering methodological advances for low-resource NLP while testing hypotheses about language acquisition and representation across human and machine learning paradigms.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the relationship between computer and human language and computational techniques applied to natural language. Includes instruction in computer programming, human languages, linguistic analysis, logic, natural language processing, semantics, machine learning, psycholinguistics, software engineering, and syntax.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational analysis of the development and interrelation of Catholic philosophical and theological concepts across historical texts. The research problem centers on the challenge of systematically tracing the evolution of key doctrinal and ethical frameworks—such as natural law, sacramental theology, and virtue ethics—within vast, multilingual corpora spanning classical, medieval, and modern periods. Traditional humanities methods struggle to process the scale and linguistic diversity of primary sources (e.g., Latin patristic writings, scholastic treatises, modern encyclicals) and their philosophical reception histories. The project will apply natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models fine-tuned for historical Latin and theological vernaculars, to map conceptual networks, semantic shifts, and argumentative patterns. Computational workflows will integrate manuscript transcription (via OCR for early prints), entity recognition for theological terms, and graph-based analysis of citation networks. A pilot study on Thomistic works demonstrated feasibility but requires scaling via parallelized HPC architectures to handle ~50,000 texts across multiple languages. Expected outcomes include: (1) identification of understudied doctrinal influences in Catholic social thought, (2) quantitative models of how metaphysical concepts propagate through institutional discourses, and (3) open-access tools for interdisciplinary scholars analyzing theological-philosophical corpora. By enabling large-scale pattern detection in Catholic intellectual traditions, this work aims to inform contemporary philosophical and ethical debates while demonstrating how computational methods can enrich theological inquiry within digital humanities frameworks. The requested resources are critical for training domain-specific language models and conducting high-dimensional analysis of text networks that cannot be processed on standard academic infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on Catholic thought, culture, and how Catholic tradition informs theology, culture, institutions, and identity. Includes instruction in Biblical Greek, Biblical Hebrew, Catholic bioethics, Catholic social thought, church history, Latin, philosophy, and theology.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to investigate the role of structural genetic variation in shaping phenotypic diversity across bacterial and viral populations, with a focus on mechanisms driving heritable stability and regulatory adaptation. Despite advances in sequencing, the functional and evolutionary implications of large-scale genomic rearrangements—such as inversions, translocations, and mobile element insertions—remain poorly characterized in non-model microbes. This gap limits understanding of how genetic architecture influences pathogen adaptability and host interactions. To address this, we will develop a computational framework integrating comparative genome assembly, epigenetic state prediction, and population genetic modeling. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process terabase-scale sequencing datasets from diverse clinical and environmental isolates, including long-read sequences to resolve complex structural variants. Custom algorithms will map rearrangement breakpoints, infer ancestral recombination events, and correlate variant landscapes with transcriptional regulatory networks. Parallelized simulations will model the fitness effects of structural variants under varying selective pressures, incorporating empirical data on mutation rates and horizontal gene transfer. Machine learning models trained on these outputs will predict variant impacts on gene expression stability and host-pathogen coevolution. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible database linking structural variants to regulatory phenotypes in microbial taxa, (2) novel metrics quantifying genomic instability risks in emerging pathogens, and (3) mechanistic insights into how large-scale genetic reorganization buffers against environmental stress while maintaining heritable integrity. This work will advance foundational knowledge in molecular genetics by bridging genome structure, regulatory dynamics, and evolutionary adaptation, with applications to antimicrobial resistance tracking and synthetic genome engineering. The scale of data integration and iterative modeling required necessitates HPC support for efficient multinode processing, large-memory workloads, and long-term storage of intermediate genomic datasets.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of genetic structures and mechanisms of organisms, including bacteria, phages, and viruses. Includes instruction in the replication, expression, transfer, structure, maintenance, and stability of heritable information in DNA, RNA, and proteins; the regulation of these processes; and neurogenetics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern building systems demands advanced computational tools to optimize energy efficiency, structural resilience, and occupant comfort. Current design practices for building envelopes and environmental control systems often rely on simplified models that inadequately capture dynamic interactions between materials, thermal loads, airflow, and human behavior. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing a high-fidelity, multi-physics simulation framework to evaluate and optimize next-generation architectural systems under realistic operating conditions. The research will focus on integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), finite element analysis (FEA), and agent-based modeling to simulate coupled heat transfer, structural stress, and indoor airflow patterns in mixed-use buildings. Machine learning techniques will be applied to accelerate parametric design exploration, targeting configurations that minimize energy consumption while maintaining thermal comfort and structural integrity across diverse climates. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the spatial and temporal scales required for these simulations, which involve millions of mesh elements, transient boundary conditions, and stochastic occupant behavior models. The project will leverage parallelized solvers and GPU-accelerated workflows to manage computational costs. Expected outcomes include a validated simulation toolkit for architects and engineers, data-driven guidelines for climate-responsive building designs, and predictive models linking material properties to long-term energy performance. This work will directly contribute to sustainable urban development by enabling the design of buildings that adapt to environmental stressors, reduce operational carbon footprints, and enhance resilience against extreme weather events. The requested HPC allocation will support large-scale sensitivity analyses, validation against experimental datasets, and the development of open-access computational workflows for the architectural engineering community.
detailed_field: Civil, environmental, and transportation engineering nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of materials, systems, and methods used to construct and equip buildings intended for human habitation or other purposes.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the transnational circulation of premodern literary and artistic traditions across Asia and their diasporas, with a focus on underrepresented vernacular texts and visual materials. The research problem centers on identifying patterns of cultural exchange and adaptation that have been obscured by the scale and linguistic diversity of primary sources, including manuscripts, inscriptions, and ephemera spanning South, Southeast, and East Asian contexts. Traditional close-reading approaches struggle to systematically trace thematic motifs, stylistic influences, or semantic shifts across these vast, multilingual corpora. To address this, we propose a computational pipeline combining optical character recognition (OCR) fine-tuned for historical Asian scripts, transformer-based multilingual embeddings for cross-linguistic semantic analysis, and graph neural networks to model cultural transmission networks. The HPC infrastructure will enable processing of over 50 TB of digitized materials from partner archives, training domain-specific language models for 15 low-resource languages, and simulating diffusion pathways of narrative elements across geographic and temporal axes. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly accessible knowledge graph mapping connections between regional literary/artistic traditions, 2) quantitative frameworks for assessing hybridity in diasporic cultural production, and 3) methodological advances in computational humanities tailored to non-Western epistemologies. By bridging area studies and machine learning, this work aims to challenge Eurocentric periodizations of cultural development while providing new tools for preserving intangible heritage. The scale of parallelized text and image analysis required—particularly for training multimodal models on rarely studied script-language pairs—necessitates GPU cluster resources beyond local institutional capacity.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of the Asian Continent, including the study of the Asian diasporas overseas.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing ethical decision-making patterns across professional contexts, with a focus on identifying systemic biases and inconsistencies in applied ethics frameworks. Traditional ethical analysis often relies on manual case assessments or small-scale qualitative studies, which struggle to capture the complexity of real-world dilemmas involving large stakeholder networks, dynamic socio-cultural variables, and conflicting normative principles. Our research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and model multi-modal datasets—including historical ethics case databases, public policy documents, and simulated professional scenarios—to quantify how contextual factors influence ethical reasoning. Using natural language processing (NLP), we will analyze over 50,000 documented ethics cases from medical, legal, and environmental domains to identify latent decision-making heuristics. Agent-based modeling will then simulate how these heuristics interact with variables such as organizational hierarchies, regulatory constraints, and cultural norms. The computational workflow requires parallelized processing of unstructured text data, Monte Carlo simulations for scenario testing, and network analysis to map ethical reasoning cascades in multi-actor systems. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible repository of annotated ethics decision trees, (2) predictive models highlighting high-risk scenarios where standard ethical frameworks may fail due to cognitive biases or systemic pressures, and (3) adaptive visualization tools to help ethics boards and educators explore contingency-sensitive solutions. By bridging normative ethical theory with computational social science methods, this project aims to advance evidence-based approaches for professional ethics training and policy design while demonstrating how HPC resources can expand the methodological scope of humanistic inquiry. Resource requests emphasize GPU-optimized nodes for deep learning tasks and high-memory nodes for large-scale network simulations.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of ethical issues in the workplace and public life, and the application of ethical decision-making to the practical problems of society and the professions. Includes instruction in ethical theory; history of ethics; contemporary social dilemmas; methods in applied ethics; and applications including medical ethics, legal ethics, business ethics, environmental ethics, and criminal justice ethics.

abstract: The growing complexity of cloud-native applications operating across heterogeneous, geographically distributed environments has exposed critical gaps in adaptive resource management frameworks, particularly for latency-sensitive workflows with dynamically shifting data dependencies. Traditional cloud orchestration strategies, which prioritize static cost-performance trade-offs, struggle to reconcile real-time application requirements with transient resource availability in multi-cloud or edge-cloud hybrid systems. This project proposes a novel computational framework for intent-driven, self-organizing resource allocation that integrates topological analysis of data flow graphs, reinforcement learning (RL)-based decision engines, and lightweight blockchain-assisted coordination protocols. The research will develop models to dynamically map application components to optimal compute, storage, and network resources by analyzing evolving data dependencies, energy efficiency constraints, and provider-specific service-level agreements. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for simulating large-scale multi-cloud environments, training deep RL agents through parallelized simulations of diverse workload scenarios, and validating consensus mechanisms under Byzantine fault conditions. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for topology-aware resource scheduling, empirical benchmarks comparing coordination strategies in partitioned network environments, and novel metrics for quantifying the stability-efficiency frontier in decentralized cloud resource markets. By addressing the interplay between application semantics, infrastructure dynamics, and decentralized trust mechanisms, this work aims to establish foundational principles for next-generation cloud systems capable of autonomously maintaining performance guarantees amid increasing infrastructure fragmentation and dynamic service requirements.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to design and implement enterprise software systems that rely on distributed computing and service-oriented architecture, including databases, web services, cloud computing, and mobile apps. Includes instruction in data management, distributed and cloud computing, enterprise software architecture, enterprise and cloud security, mobile systems and applications, server administration, and web development.

abstract: Adolescence is marked by dynamic neurobiological and psychosocial changes that shape cognitive and emotional development, yet the mechanisms through which these interacting systems influence decision-making and behavioral outcomes remain poorly understood. This project seeks to model the multilevel interactions between neurodevelopmental trajectories, environmental contexts, and social learning processes during adolescence using computational approaches that require high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current limitations in analyzing high-dimensional longitudinal datasets—integrating neuroimaging, ecological momentary assessments, and social network data—hinder the field’s ability to capture real-time developmental processes. We propose a hybrid methodology combining dynamical systems modeling, graph-based network analyses, and reinforcement learning frameworks to simulate how individual differences in pubertal timing interact with peer influence dynamics to predict risk-taking behaviors. Agent-based models will parameterize decision-making processes under varying social reward contingencies, while Bayesian hierarchical models will assess longitudinal heterogeneity in developmental pathways. These computationally intensive methods demand parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets, stochastic optimization across parameter spaces, and iterative model validation—tasks exceeding the capacity of standard laboratory computing infrastructure. Anticipated outcomes include (1) identification of critical neurosocial tipping points in adolescent risk behavior trajectories, (2) development of open-source tools for multilevel developmental systems modeling, and (3) empirically grounded frameworks for predicting individual differences in adaptive vs. maladaptive developmental outcomes. By leveraging HPC resources, this work aims to advance computational developmental science through scalable models that bridge biological, cognitive, and social domains, ultimately informing targeted prevention strategies and theoretical innovations in adolescent psychology research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the unique stages of psychological growth and development of individuals from adolescence to adulthood. Includes instruction in cognitive and perceptual development, emotional development, personality development, the effects of biological maturation on behavior, theories of cognitive growth and related research methods, testing and assessment methods for different age levels, research on child and adolescent behavior therapy, and the psychology of aging.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an integrated computational framework to evaluate the economic and environmental trade-offs of climate adaptation policies in agricultural systems, with a focus on water resource allocation under shifting precipitation patterns. The research addresses a critical gap in environmental economics: the lack of high-resolution, spatially explicit models that dynamically couple hydrologic systems with market behaviors and policy interventions. Current approaches often rely on static cost-benefit analyses or coarse regional aggregates, limiting their capacity to capture feedbacks between localized resource depletion, adaptive farming decisions, and commodity market responses. We propose a novel combination of dynamic stochastic general equilibrium modeling, agent-based simulations of agricultural decision-making, and high-dimensional spatial econometric techniques. The computational workflow requires processing multi-terabyte climate projection datasets (CMIP6), fine-scale soil moisture observations, and historical agricultural market data across nested spatial scales. Key technical challenges include solving high-dimensional optimization problems for heterogeneous agent networks, implementing Bayesian hierarchical models for spatial uncertainty quantification, and parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations across policy scenarios. Access to high-performance computing resources with GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory capacity is essential to execute these computationally intensive tasks within feasible timeframes. Expected outcomes include (1) quantification of distributional economic impacts from alternative water pricing mechanisms, (2) identification of threshold precipitation levels that trigger nonlinear market adjustments, and (3) policy-ready visualizations of geographically targeted subsidy programs. Results will directly inform ongoing debates about equitable climate adaptation financing in the U.S. Farm Bill reauthorization process while advancing methodological integration of ecological and economic modeling paradigms. The computational tools developed will be made open-source to support replication studies across different agroecological zones.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of economic concepts and methods to the analysis of issues such as air and water pollution, land use planning, waste disposal, invasive species and pest control, conservation policies, and related environmental problems. Includes instruction in cost-benefit analysis, environmental impact assessment, evaluation and assessment of alternative resource management strategies, policy evaluation and monitoring, and descriptive and analytic tools for studying how environmental developments affect the economic system.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an advanced computational framework to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of diagnostic image analysis in radiologic practice, directly supporting the clinical and educational objectives of the Radiologist Assistant (RA) program. Radiologist Assistants require rapid, reliable tools to perform initial assessments of complex imaging datasets, yet existing methods for anomaly detection and image interpretation often lack the speed and precision needed for high-volume clinical environments. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train and deploy deep learning models capable of processing multi-modal imaging data (e.g., MRI, CT, X-ray) while integrating clinical parameters such as patient history, pharmacology data, and pathophysiology. The research will focus on three objectives: (1) optimizing convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and vision transformers for real-time detection of abnormalities in cross-sectional anatomy, (2) developing a federated learning pipeline to aggregate anonymized imaging data from partner healthcare institutions while preserving patient privacy, and (3) creating interactive simulation tools for RA education that utilize AI-generated synthetic imaging datasets. Computational workflows will be parallelized across GPU clusters to handle large-scale 3D image volumes and enable rapid iteration during model training. Validation will involve retrospective analysis of de-identified patient scans and prospective testing in collaboration with clinical preceptors. Successful implementation will provide Radiologist Assistants with AI-driven decision support tools to improve initial diagnostic observations, reduce workflow bottlenecks, and minimize inter-observer variability. The open-source tools and synthetic datasets generated will also serve as innovative educational resources, aligning with the program’s focus on competency in imaging procedures and radiation biology. By integrating HPC-powered analytics into radiologic practice, this work aims to advance both patient care and RA training paradigms while establishing a scalable infrastructure for collaborative medical imaging research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of a physician, to perform patient assessment, patient management, selected imaging procedures and to make initial observations of diagnostic images. Includes instruction in radiologic procedures and techniques, cross sectional anatomy, pharmacology, pathophysiology, patient assessment, patient care and management, and radiation biology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance large-scale computational analysis of historical and contemporary theatrical texts, practices, and networks. The research problem centers on the fragmented and labor-intensive nature of analyzing theatre’s sociocultural evolution, particularly the interplay between dramatic literature, production methodologies, and audience reception across diverse temporal and geographic contexts. Traditional humanities approaches struggle to synthesize the vast, heterogeneous datasets required to map these dynamics—including digitized play scripts, archival records of performances, reviews, and paratextual materials—which span multiple languages, eras, and theatrical traditions. To address this, the project will employ computational text analysis, network modeling, and machine learning techniques. Natural language processing (NLP) will be applied to identify stylistic and thematic patterns in dramatic corpora, while graph-based network analysis will model relationships between playwrights, productions, and institutions. Additionally, transformer-based models will be fine-tuned to analyze historical shifts in critical reception using multilingual review archives. These methods demand HPC resources due to the scale of data (terabytes of text, images, and metadata), the complexity of training domain-specific language models, and the need for iterative simulations to test hypotheses about cultural transmission. Expected outcomes include the creation of open-access digital tools for theatre scholars, dynamic visualizations of transnational influence networks, and data-driven insights into understudied theatrical movements. By integrating computational rigor with humanistic inquiry, this work aims to redefine how theatre history is analyzed, emphasizing systemic connections over isolated case studies. The project will also establish a methodological framework for applying HPC to performance studies, bridging gaps between computational and traditional theatre scholarship. Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, a public dataset repository, and workshops to train theatre researchers in computational methods.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the history, literature, theory, and analysis of written plays, theatrical productions, and theatre methods and organization. Includes instruction in historical method; critical theory; literary analysis; the study of themes and archetypes in dramatic literature; the history of acting, directing, and technical theatre; and the study of specific historical and cultural styles and traditions.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the spatial and temporal dynamics of aging populations in urban and rural regions, with implications for public health infrastructure planning. As demographic shifts accelerate globally, traditional analytical tools struggle to model complex interactions between population aging, migration patterns, and resource accessibility at fine-grained geographic scales. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to process multi-terabyte datasets from national censuses, health surveys, and satellite-derived geographic information systems (GIS) to construct probabilistic models of population change. Computational methods include Bayesian hierarchical spatial-temporal modeling to account for uncertainty in demographic projections, agent-based simulations to test intervention scenarios, and machine learning techniques to identify clusters of regions with similar vulnerability profiles. Key challenges requiring HPC resources involve parallel processing of 100m-resolution demographic rasters, Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling across thousands of geographic units, and real-time visualization of multidimensional simulation outputs. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for predicting healthcare demand under multiple migration and fertility scenarios, validated against longitudinal mortality and service utilization data. Results will directly inform state-level policies on clinic placement and geriatric workforce allocation while advancing methodological integration of demographic microsimulation with geospatial analytics. The requested computing allocation will enable processing timelines 12-15x faster than current university cluster capabilities, critical for meeting collaboration deadlines with public health agencies. This work contributes novel computational approaches to applied demography by addressing scale-dependent heterogeneity in population processes—a limitation in existing cohort-component models—while maintaining policy-relevant spatial granularity.
detailed_field: Sociology, demography, and population studies nec
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the practical application of demographic methods and materials for decision-making in business, education, health, and government. Includes instruction in statistics, research methods, geographic information systems, and demographic methods and techniques.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance quantitative risk management methodologies for complex business systems. The core challenge lies in modeling interdependent risks—such as financial market volatility, supply chain disruptions, and cybersecurity threats—where traditional analytical frameworks struggle to account for nonlinear interactions, dynamic feedback loops, and large-scale data integration. Current approaches often oversimplify risk dependencies or face computational bottlenecks when scaling to enterprise-level scenarios. To address this, the project will develop a hybrid computational architecture combining agent-based modeling, Bayesian network inference, and deep reinforcement learning. Agent-based simulations will capture granular interactions among stakeholders and environmental factors, while Bayesian networks will quantify probabilistic dependencies across risk domains. Reinforcement learning algorithms will then optimize risk mitigation strategies under uncertainty, iterating through millions of simulated scenarios to identify robust policies. HPC resources are essential for parallelizing stochastic simulations, training neural networks on heterogeneous datasets (market indices, operational logs, and cybersecurity incident reports), and solving high-dimensional optimization problems in near-real time. Expected outcomes include a scalable risk assessment platform capable of processing terabyte-scale datasets, dynamically updating risk exposure estimates, and prescribing adaptive mitigation measures. This work will directly contribute to the risk management field by enabling organizations to model systemic risks with unprecedented granularity, reduce computational latency in crisis response planning, and improve capital allocation decisions for risk financing. The resulting frameworks will be validated against historical crisis data and operationalized through partnerships with financial institutions and insurance providers, bridging academic research and industry risk management practices.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles of business risk measurement, mitigation, and management. Includes instruction in business analytics, foundations of insurance and risk management, investments, life and health insurance, loss prevention, property and liability insurance risk assessment, risk control, risk financing, and security.

abstract: Emerging evidence suggests that the dynamic interplay between entomopathogenic nematodes (EPNs) and their insect hosts is shaped by complex, co-evolved biochemical signaling networks and microbiome-mediated interactions. However, current models lack resolution to predict how environmental stressors—such as soil acidification and temperature fluctuations—modulate these interactions at scale, limiting our ability to harness EPNs for sustainable pest management. This project seeks to integrate multi-omics datasets with spatially explicit, agent-based models to simulate EPN-host-microbiome tripartite dynamics under shifting abiotic conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the following: (1) genome-scale metabolic network reconstructions of nematode-associated microbiomes, informed by metatranscriptomic and metabolomic profiles from experimental microcosms; (2) stochastic simulations of pheromone diffusion and receptor binding kinetics across heterogeneous soil matrices; and (3) evolutionary algorithms optimizing trait-based models of EPN foraging behavior under resource competition. The computational pipeline will leverage machine learning to identify critical thresholds in soil pH and moisture that disrupt nematode chemotaxis or alter microbial symbiont functionality. By coupling these outputs with geospatial climate projections, we aim to generate predictive maps of EPN efficacy as biocontrol agents in agroecosystems under future climate scenarios. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of strain-specific EPN-microbiome metabolic interactions and an open-source framework for simulating tri-trophic feedbacks in soil ecosystems. This work bridges entomology, nematology, and environmental systems modeling, offering novel insights into the resilience of symbiotic biological control systems while addressing urgent gaps in climate-adaptive agricultural planning. The requested HPC allocation will enable parameter sweeps across 10^6+ combinatorial scenarios, necessitating parallelized processing of 500+ TB of genomic and environmental data, which exceeds the capacity of local institutional clusters.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of nematode (roundworm) and insect species/populations in respect of their life cycles, morphology, genetics, physiology, ecology, taxonomy, population dynamics, and environmental and economic impacts. Includes instruction in applicable biological and physical sciences as well as insect toxicology and the biochemical control of insect populations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and validate computational models for optimizing personalized learning experiences in digital educational environments, addressing the challenge of scalability in adaptive instructional design. Current adaptive learning systems often struggle to dynamically adjust content, pacing, and multimodal feedback for diverse learners due to limitations in processing complex, real-time interaction data. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach to simulate learner behavior, model cognitive engagement patterns, and test adaptive media design strategies at scale. The research will employ machine learning techniques, including transformer-based neural networks and reinforcement learning, to analyze large datasets of learner interactions (e.g., keystroke dynamics, eye-tracking patterns, and multimodal feedback responses) from existing educational platforms. These models will be trained to predict optimal instructional pathways and generate design recommendations for educational media that balance pedagogical effectiveness with accessibility. Computational experiments will simulate diverse learner populations to stress-test adaptive algorithms under variable conditions, including different demographic profiles, learning disabilities, and technological access constraints. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of multiple design scenarios, reducing simulation time from weeks to hours while handling datasets exceeding 50TB in size. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source framework for prototyping adaptive educational media, (2) evidence-based guidelines for designing computationally efficient personalization algorithms, and (3) novel metrics for evaluating the equity impacts of adaptive learning systems. This work directly advances the program's focus on technology-enhanced curriculum design by providing scalable computational methods to address heterogeneity in learning needs, particularly for STEM education contexts. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale data storage, and distributed computing for real-time simulation of educational media interventions.
detailed_field: Educational/ instructional technology and media design
cip_definition: A program that focuses on designing technology for educational curricula. Includes instruction in foundations of educational technology, design, computer applications, human-computer interaction, web-based instruction, distance education, and designing and producing educational software and materials.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the dynamics of digital community formation and spiritual engagement among adolescents within youth ministry contexts. While youth ministries increasingly integrate digital platforms for outreach, mentorship, and worship, there is limited empirical understanding of how online interactions correlate with long-term spiritual development or psychosocial well-being. The research problem centers on identifying patterns in digital communication—such as social media engagement, virtual small group interactions, and multimedia content consumption—that predict meaningful spiritual growth or disengagement among youth. Using anonymized datasets from partner organizations (including text, video analytics, and longitudinal survey responses), the project will apply natural language processing (NLP) to classify emotional and theological themes in youth-generated content, network analysis to map relational dynamics within digital communities, and agent-based modeling to simulate the long-term impacts of varying ministry strategies. Computational challenges include processing large volumes of unstructured text and video data, training custom NLP models sensitive to religious vernacular, and simulating nonlinear behavioral outcomes across diverse demographic cohorts. Outcomes will provide youth ministry practitioners with evidence-based frameworks for optimizing digital outreach, mitigating risks of alienation in hybrid (online/in-person) environments, and fostering inclusive communities that align with developmental needs. By integrating computational social science methods with theological anthropology, this interdisciplinary work advances Humanities scholarship at the intersection of technology, spirituality, and adolescent development—a niche underexplored by traditional disciplines. The requested HPC resources are critical for scaling analyses beyond pilot datasets and ensuring robust, generalizable insights for faith-based organizations serving youth globally.
cip_definition: A program that prepares the ordained clergy and other religious professionals to provide spiritual, counseling, and leadership services to children, adolescents, and young adults. Includes instruction in child and adolescent psychology, human growth and development, family studies, communication skills, religious education, youth counseling, small group leadership, planning and organizing youth activities, volunteer supervision, and youth evangelism and worship.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational legal research focused on modeling the evolution of judicial reasoning in common law systems. The research problem centers on the challenge of systematically analyzing how legal principles adapt over time through appellate court decisions, particularly in areas where statutory frameworks are sparse or ambiguous. Traditional legal scholarship often relies on manual case analysis, which limits scalability and obscures macro-level patterns in judicial decision-making. This project proposes a computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP), graph theory, and temporal network analysis to map doctrinal shifts across large corpora of judicial opinions from U.S. federal appellate courts. The methodology involves training transformer-based models to identify latent legal concepts and their relational dynamics within case texts, followed by the construction of time-evolving knowledge graphs to trace precedent influence and conceptual divergence. HPC resources are critical for processing terabytes of unstructured legal text, optimizing neural architectures for domain-specific language, and simulating longitudinal network behavior. Expected outcomes include 1) a scalable framework for quantifying doctrinal stability and innovation in case law, 2) identification of understudied inflection points in judicial reasoning across civil rights and intellectual property domains, and 3) open-source tools to assist legal researchers in visualizing citation networks and predicting conceptual trajectories. By integrating computational social science methods with legal theory, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for empirical jurisprudence, offering insights into the sociotechnical forces shaping legal evolution. The results could inform judicial education, legislative drafting, and the development of AI-assisted legal research platforms, bridging gaps between traditional doctrinal analysis and data-driven policy design.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of law, for taking state and national bar examinations, and for advanced research in jurisprudence. Includes instruction in the theory and practice of the legal system, including the statutory, administrative, and judicial components of civil and criminal law.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational legal research at the intersection of jurisprudence, statutory evolution, and large-scale textual analysis. The core problem addressed is the lack of scalable frameworks for analyzing the dynamic interplay between judicial decision-making and legislative intent across jurisdictions, particularly as legal systems grapple with emerging technologies and transnational regulatory challenges. Traditional legal research methods struggle to process the growing volume of case law, legislative histories, and administrative rulings—a challenge exacerbated by the semantic complexity of legal texts and the need for temporal analysis spanning decades. This project proposes developing a novel computational architecture combining natural language processing (NLP), temporal graph analytics, and agent-based modeling to map doctrinal shifts, predict systemic responses to hypothetical legal scenarios, and identify latent biases in judicial reasoning patterns. The HPC infrastructure will enable processing of petabyte-scale legal corpora spanning common law and civil law traditions, while transformer-based language models fine-tuned on legal discourse will parse context-dependent meanings of critical statutory terms. Graph neural networks will model precedent networks and legislative influence pathways, with multi-agent systems simulating interactions between judicial actors under varying constitutional constraints. Expected outcomes include 1) an open-source toolkit for computational legal analysis, 2) empirical insights into the relationship between judicial diversity and doctrinal innovation, and 3) predictive models assessing how hypothetical AI governance frameworks might propagate through international legal systems. By bridging computational methods with jurisprudential theory, this work aims to establish new paradigms for data-driven legal scholarship while providing policymakers with evidence-based tools to evaluate regulatory interventions in complex, technology-driven societies. The resource-intensive nature of training domain-specific legal language models and conducting multi-jurisdictional simulations necessitates HPC capabilities beyond typical institutional infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of law, for taking state and national bar examinations, and for advanced research in jurisprudence. Includes instruction in the theory and practice of the legal system, including the statutory, administrative, and judicial components of civil and criminal law.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the analysis and modeling of complex jazz improvisation patterns and ensemble interactions, a critical challenge in jazz studies. While traditional analytical methods in musicology rely on manual transcription and subjective interpretation, the nonlinear, real-time dynamics of jazz performance—particularly in collective improvisation—resist reduction to static scores or isolated parameters. This research addresses this gap by developing computational tools to process and analyze large-scale audio datasets of historic and contemporary jazz recordings, capturing temporal, harmonic, and timbral features at scale. Machine learning models, including recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and transformer architectures, will be trained to identify stylistic signatures of improvisational vocabularies across eras (e.g., swing, bebop, avant-garde) and simulate interaction dynamics within ensembles. Additionally, agent-based models will be employed to study emergent behaviors in improvisational decision-making, incorporating harmonic rulesets derived from jazz theory and real performer data. The computational workload demands parallelized processing of high-resolution audio (10,000+ hours), GPU-accelerated model training, and large-memory nodes for real-time simulation of multi-agent musical interactions. Outcomes will include an open-source toolkit for computational jazz analysis, new insights into the evolution of improvisational practices, and predictive models to inform pedagogical frameworks for ensemble communication. By bridging data-driven methods and musicological expertise, this work aims to deepen scholarly understanding of jazz as a dynamic, collaborative art form while preserving its intangible cultural practices through quantitatively grounded research.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to study and master the performance and composition of Jazz. Includes instruction in the history of Jazz and related musical styles such as the Blues, Jazz composition and theory, improvisation, Jazz instrument and ensemble performance, and related topics.

abstract: This project seeks to address the urgent challenge of preserving culturally significant organic artifacts—such as historical textiles, manuscripts, and biological specimens—degrading due to fluctuating environmental conditions exacerbated by climate change. While conservation science traditionally relies on experimental methods, the complex interplay of microbial activity, material fatigue, and microenvironmental variables demands a predictive, systems-level approach. We propose an interdisciplinary framework integrating microbial ecology, materials science, and nonlinear dynamics to model degradation pathways under diverse climatic scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable large-scale simulations of artifact-microbiome interactions, leveraging metagenomic datasets from global heritage sites and hyper-resolution climate projections. Agent-based models will map microbial community dynamics, while finite element analysis will quantify stress responses in heterogeneous organic matrices. Machine learning pipelines will identify critical thresholds in environmental parameters (humidity, temperature, pollutant levels) that accelerate decay. By coupling these layers, the computational platform will predict risk profiles for artifacts and optimize preservation strategies tailored to regional climate trajectories. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible decision-support tool for cultural institutions, novel protocols for adaptive conservation, and fundamental insights into cross-scale interactions between biological systems and material surfaces. This work bridges gaps between heritage science, climate resilience, and microbial ecology, offering a transdisciplinary methodology applicable to biodiversity conservation and sustainable material design. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the computational complexity of multi-physics simulations and iterative machine learning workflows, which require parallel processing of petascale datasets and real-time parameter optimization. Success will advance both theoretical understanding of degradation mechanics and practical frameworks for safeguarding humanity’s material heritage against environmental instability.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in multi/interdisciplinary sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing complexity of data-driven decision-making in small-to-medium enterprises (SMEs) has exposed critical inefficiencies in conventional office automation systems, particularly in dynamic environments requiring real-time data synthesis from heterogeneous sources. This project seeks to address the gap in adaptive, scalable computational tools for automated data entry, transformation, and reporting—a challenge exacerbated by the limitations of off-the-shelf software in handling unstructured inputs, multi-modal data streams, and context-aware validation. We propose the development of a machine learning (ML)-augmented workflow engine optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments to enable near-real-time processing of transactional data, natural language documents, and sensor-generated datasets. The computational approach integrates transformer-based models for context-sensitive data parsing, graph neural networks to map interdocument dependencies, and agent-based simulations to model workflow bottlenecks under stochastic demand. HPC resources will be critical for training domain-specific LLMs on proprietary business corpora (invoices, emails, spreadsheets) and for parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations assessing system robustness across 10,000+ operational scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for intelligent document processing that reduces manual data entry errors by ≥40% in pilot tests while decreasing latency in report generation by 65% compared to current industry benchmarks. By demonstrating how HPC can democratize advanced automation capabilities for non-technical users, this research aims to establish new best practices for resource-constrained organizations adopting Industry 4.0 technologies. The work bridges operational research, human-computer interaction, and distributed systems engineering, advancing an emerging niche in computational business automation.
cip_title: Business/ Office Automation/ Technology/ Data Entry
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to support business information operations by using computer equipment to enter, process, and retrieve data for a wide variety of administrative purposes. Includes instruction in using basic business software and hardware, business computer networking, principles of desktop publishing, preparing mass mailings, compiling and editing spreadsheets, list maintenance, preparing tables and graphs, receipt control, and preparing business performance reports.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address scalability and efficiency challenges in automating real-time accounting data validation and anomaly detection for decentralized financial ecosystems. As businesses increasingly adopt blockchain-based transaction systems and interoperable accounting platforms, traditional bookkeeping tools struggle to process high-volume, heterogeneous data streams while maintaining audit-ready integrity. The research problem centers on developing computational models capable of dynamically reconciling cross-platform transactional data, identifying discrepancies across ledgers, and flagging probabilistic fraud indicators—all within latency thresholds required for operational decision-making. The computational approach integrates graph neural networks (GNNs) to map complex transactional relationships within distributed networks, coupled with agent-based simulations modeling multi-entity accounting interactions. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of synthetic datasets representing >10^8 daily transactions across hybrid blockchain/traditional systems, while quantum-inspired optimization algorithms will refine matching heuristics for diverse accounting standards. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for adaptive ledger reconciliation, benchmarked against conventional double-entry systems in simulated environments with injected anomaly patterns. The project aims to demonstrate ≥95% accuracy in real-time discrepancy detection while reducing computational costs for large-scale audits by orders of magnitude. By bridging distributed systems theory with accounting information systems design, this work intends to establish technical foundations for next-generation bookkeeping infrastructures capable of supporting Web3-enabled business environments. The requested computing resources will specifically accelerate training of GNN architectures on transaction graph topologies and enable stress-testing of proposed validation protocols under peak enterprise-scale loads.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide technical administrative support to professional accountants and other financial management personnel. Includes instruction in posting transactions to accounts, record-keeping systems, accounting software operation, and general accounting principles and practices.

abstract: Modern military operations increasingly rely on the integration of information-centric strategies to achieve tactical and strategic dominance. This project seeks to develop advanced computational models for simulating and optimizing Joint Information Operations (JIO) in contested, multi-domain environments. The research addresses the challenge of dynamically coordinating cyber, electronic, psychological, and spatial information operations under constraints such as adversarial countermeasures, resource limitations, and rapidly evolving threat landscapes. Current modeling tools lack the scalability to handle real-time data assimilation, probabilistic decision-making under uncertainty, and the interdependencies between kinetic and non-kinetic actions. To bridge this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to build a multi-agent simulation framework capable of emulating large-scale JIO scenarios. The computational approach integrates agent-based modeling, machine learning for predictive threat analysis, and game-theoretic optimization to evaluate decision pathways across network-centric command structures. Key innovations include adaptive algorithms for resource allocation in degraded communication environments, synthetic data generation to stress-test decision systems, and probabilistic causal models to quantify second- and third-order effects of information campaigns. Simulations will be validated against historical case studies and wargaming datasets, with sensitivity analyses to identify critical vulnerabilities in adversarial information ecosystems. Expected outcomes include a validated toolkit for operational planners to preemptively assess mission risks, optimize cross-domain synchronization, and mitigate emergent threats such as AI-driven disinformation or swarm-based cyber attacks. This work directly supports the advancement of decision superiority in modern warfare by providing a computational testbed for next-generation JIO strategies, aligning with Department of Defense priorities for maintaining information advantage in peer conflicts. The requested HPC resources—including GPU-accelerated nodes and high-memory architectures—are essential for achieving the required fidelity, parallelism, and real-time analytics capabilities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the strategic and operational use of information relative to the support of military and strategic policy and objectives. Includes instruction in information technology, decision theory and applications, military operations, command and control technology, network operations, network systems integration, computer network defense, space communications technology, and applications to specific military operational tasks.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamic interplay between transnational supply chain disruptions, socio-political instability, and environmental stressors under accelerating globalization, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model emergent risks in interconnected global systems. Traditional analyses in International Studies often treat economic, ecological, and geopolitical factors in isolation, limiting predictive capacity for cascading crises. Our research addresses this gap by developing an adaptive, multi-layered computational framework integrating agent-based modeling, geospatial network analysis, and machine learning to simulate cross-domain interactions at unprecedented scale. The model incorporates real-time trade flow data, climate vulnerability indices, and sociopolitical sentiment metrics from multilingual news corpora and satellite imagery, requiring parallelized processing of heterogeneous datasets exceeding 50 TB. Key computational challenges include optimizing graph-based algorithms to map 10^6-node supply chain networks, training transformer models on low-resource language texts to assess regional instability, and simulating feedback loops between resource scarcity and governance collapse under climate scenarios. The HPC infrastructure will enable ensemble simulations across 1,000+ parameter combinations to identify critical tipping points and resilience pathways. Expected outcomes include an open-access digital dashboard for policymakers to visualize risk propagation across sectors and a peer-reviewed framework quantifying second-order impacts of regional shocks on global equity. By bridging computational scalability gaps in social-environmental systems research, this project aims to advance methodological innovation in Globalization Studies while providing actionable insights for multilateral crisis response.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on global and international issues from the perspective of the social sciences, social services, and related fields.

abstract: The optimization of decision-making processes in agricultural enterprises remains a critical challenge due to the dynamic interplay of market volatility, production uncertainties, and resource constraints. Current analytical tools often lack the capacity to integrate multi-dimensional datasets or simulate complex scenarios at scale, limiting their utility for strategic planning. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a high-resolution computational framework to model agricultural business operations under stochastic conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement a hybrid methodology combining agent-based modeling, Monte Carlo simulations, and machine learning techniques to analyze interactions between market trends, input cost fluctuations, and yield variability. The computational framework will process large-scale historical datasets, including commodity prices, climate records, and operational cost data, to parameterize probabilistic models and simulate thousands of enterprise management scenarios. Key outputs will include predictive analytics for profit-risk trade-offs, dynamic pricing strategies, and resource allocation optimizations tailored to regional agricultural contexts. The anticipated outcomes of this research are twofold: first, to generate actionable insights for agricultural managers seeking to mitigate financial risks while capitalizing on market opportunities; second, to establish a scalable computational architecture adaptable to diverse agribusiness environments. By enabling real-time analysis of complex decision matrices, this project aims to advance data-driven management practices in the agricultural sector, directly contributing to enhanced economic resilience and operational efficiency for farming enterprises and allied industries.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on modern business and economic principles involved in the organization, operation, and management of agricultural enterprises.

abstract: This project investigates the spatial and temporal dynamics of traditional ecological knowledge (TEK) systems in mediating human-environment interactions under accelerating climate change. Focusing on marginalized agro-pastoral communities across altitudinal gradients in the Andean Altiplano, we employ high-performance computing (HPC) to model how TEK-driven land management practices buffer climate vulnerabilities at different scales. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding non-Western epistemologies as dynamic, place-based adaptive systems, particularly how their spatial implementation affects ecological resilience. Using a mixed-methods framework, we integrate ethnographic fieldwork documenting local soil classification systems and grazing strategies with geospatial analysis of LiDAR-derived topography, multitemporal satellite imagery (30-year LANDSAT series), and climate model projections (CMIP6). Computational workflows will apply agent-based modeling to simulate decision-making cascades in pasture rotation and water management under drought scenarios, while graph neural networks analyze connectivity between sacred natural sites and biodiversity hotspots. Memory-intensive tasks include processing 1m-resolution UAV photogrammetry of terraced landscapes to quantify microclimate moderation effects, coupled with Bayesian belief network analysis of intergenerational knowledge transmission. By parallelizing these workflows across 20,000+ CPU cores, we aim to resolve how TEK spatial patterns interact with biophysical variables at granular temporal scales (sub-seasonal to decadal). Expected outcomes include (1) a novel open-source toolkit for modeling socioecological systems through Indigenous spatial ontologies, (2) high-resolution vulnerability maps identifying TEK-mediated climate refugia, and (3) quantitative frameworks to evaluate place-based adaptation policies. The computational demands stem from iterative parameterization of cultural variables in ecological models and petabyte-scale raster processing across heterogeneous data types. Results will advance methodological integration of cultural geography with complexity science while informing climate justice initiatives for Indigenous land stewardship.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on human cultures and their adaptation to physical environments. Includes instruction in archaeology, biogeography, climatology, cultural anthropology, cultural geography, economic development, environmental geography, geomorphology, global environmental change, historical geography, mapping sciences, physical anthropology, political ecology, Quaternary studies, and urban geography.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of structural and material decay in historic buildings, a critical challenge in heritage conservation. Current preservation strategies often rely on static assessments or simplified environmental simulations, which inadequately capture the dynamic interplay of factors such as microclimate fluctuations, material heterogeneity, and long-term load stresses. To address this gap, we propose developing a multi-physics computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), machine learning, and agent-based modeling to simulate degradation processes across multiple temporal and spatial scales. The framework will process high-resolution 3D scans of historic structures, environmental sensor data, and historical maintenance records to parameterize material properties and stress factors. HPC resources are essential for managing the computational intensity of multi-scale simulations, particularly when modeling complex interactions between moisture infiltration, thermal expansion, and salt crystallization in masonry over decadal timeframes. Machine learning components will be trained on simulation outputs and real-world decay datasets to identify early warning signatures of structural compromise. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital toolkit for conservators to prioritize interventions based on probabilistic risk assessments. This work bridges computational engineering, materials science, and heritage studies, offering a novel methodology to extend the lifespan of culturally significant structures while respecting their authentic material fabric. By enabling data-driven preservation planning, the project aims to reduce unnecessary physical interventions and mitigate losses from unanticipated structural failures in historic buildings.
cip_definition: Any instructional program that focuses on architectural design and building techniques for historic and restored structures, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable packaging solutions requires advanced computational tools to optimize material performance, environmental impact, and cost efficiency. Current packaging materials often face trade-offs between functionality (e.g., barrier properties, mechanical strength) and sustainability (e.g., recyclability, biodegradability), while distribution systems must account for complex variables such as transportation stresses, shelf-life dynamics, and regulatory constraints. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a multi-scale computational framework to model and simulate packaging systems, from molecular interactions in biodegradable polymers to system-level supply chain logistics. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to conduct large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, finite element analysis (FEA) of structural integrity under dynamic loads, and machine learning (ML)-driven optimization of material formulations. MD simulations will predict the behavior of novel bio-based composites under varying humidity and temperature conditions, while FEA will assess package performance during transportation using real-world vibration and impact data. Concurrently, ML algorithms will identify optimal material blends that balance mechanical properties, carbon footprint, and manufacturing costs. The integration of these computational approaches will enable the design of packaging systems that meet stringent performance criteria while aligning with circular economy principles. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for packaging material behavior, a database of optimized sustainable material formulations, and decision-support tools for lifecycle assessment (LCA) of packaging systems. By providing scalable computational methods to bridge molecular-scale design and macro-scale logistics, this work will advance the development of environmentally responsible packaging solutions and inform industry standards. The requested HPC resources are critical to handling the computational intensity of multi-physics simulations and large datasets, enabling rapid iteration and validation of designs that would otherwise be infeasible with conventional computing infrastructure. This project aligns with the Packaging Science program’s interdisciplinary mission, integrating materials science, engineering, and sustainability to address pressing global challenges in packaging innovation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of scientific, technological, design, and business principles to the development of packages and packaging materials, including raw material production, conversion of raw materials into usable forms, design, distribution, and post-use recycling and reuse. Includes instruction in principles of packaging, materials sciences, distribution and transportation, engineering and technology, graphic design, packaging regulations, and business and marketing.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing real-time, multi-channel consumer engagement strategies in apparel and accessories marketing through advanced computational modeling of dynamic consumer behavior. Traditional inventory allocation and promotional tactics struggle to adapt to rapidly shifting preferences influenced by social media trends, sustainability concerns, and hyper-personalization expectations. The project will develop a high-resolution agent-based model simulating decision cascades across digital and physical retail ecosystems, incorporating heterogeneous consumer profiles, influencer network effects, and supply chain responsiveness. High-performance computing resources are required to process real-time social sentiment data streams, historical purchase patterns, and environmental variables (e.g., regional climate trends affecting apparel demand) through hybrid machine learning architectures.
