The computational framework will integrate graph neural networks to map trend diffusion across social platforms with reinforcement learning agents simulating adaptive marketing responses. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolset for identifying critical inflection points in product lifecycle management and a decision-support system for allocating marketing resources across emerging channels. This work advances computational social science methodologies in business contexts by formalizing the interaction between cultural trend dynamics and operational decision-making in fashion retail. Successful implementation could reduce overstock waste by 18-22% in test cases while improving customer retention metrics through micro-segmented engagement strategies. The models will be validated against proprietary sales data from three mid-market apparel brands and anonymized consumer interaction logs from augmented reality shopping platforms. By bridging computational scalability gaps in marketing operations research, this project establishes a template for HPC-enabled adaptive systems in consumer goods sectors facing similar velocity and variability challenges.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform operations connected with the distribution and sale of apparel and accessories. Includes instruction in wholesaling and retailing, apparel technologies, distribution, customer sales and service skills, and principles of consumer research and sales forecasting.

abstract: The increasing complexity of industrial machinery and the demand for predictive maintenance solutions require advanced computational tools to optimize operational reliability and cost-efficiency. This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity simulation framework for predictive maintenance of industrial systems, including pumps, conveyor systems, and steam propulsion equipment, by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Current predictive models often lack sufficient resolution to account for multi-physics interactions (e.g., thermal, mechanical, and fluid dynamic stresses) or real-time sensor data integration, leading to suboptimal maintenance schedules and unplanned downtime. To address this, the proposed research will employ computational fluid dynamics (CFD), finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML) algorithms to model equipment degradation under operational conditions. Large-scale simulations will integrate heterogeneous data streams—including vibration, thermal imaging, and pressure sensor outputs—to train ML models for fault detection and remaining useful life (RUL) prediction. HPC resources are critical to handle the computational intensity of multi-scale simulations, parallel processing of sensor datasets, and iterative optimization of neural networks. Expected outcomes include a validated digital twin platform capable of simulating failure modes with 85-90% accuracy, reducing maintenance costs by 15-20% in pilot industrial use cases. Additionally, the project will produce open-source tools for real-time anomaly detection, enabling broader adoption in small-to-medium enterprises. The work aligns with workforce development goals by incorporating HPC-driven methodologies into the Industrial Mechanics and Maintenance Technology curriculum, preparing technicians to utilize advanced computational tools in industrial settings. This research bridges a critical gap between theoretical predictive models and practical maintenance workflows, offering scalable solutions to enhance the resilience of industrial infrastructure.
cip_title: Industrial Mechanics and Maintenance Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair and maintain industrial machinery and equipment such as cranes, pumps, engines and motors, pneumatic tools, conveyor systems, production machinery, marine deck machinery, and steam propulsion, refinery, and pipeline-distribution systems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of Urdu, a linguistically rich yet under-resourced language with complex morphological and syntactic structures. While Urdu boasts a vast literary corpus and dynamic regional dialects, large-scale computational studies remain limited due to the lack of optimized tools and scalable infrastructure. The research problem centers on developing and applying advanced computational methods to analyze diachronic language shifts in modern Urdu literature, map dialectal variations across South Asia, and model morphological patterns in historical texts. Key challenges include processing large, unstructured datasets (e.g., digitized manuscripts, oral narratives, and social media text) and training language-specific models for tasks like tokenization, part-of-speech tagging, and syntactic parsing, which are complicated by Urdu’s right-to-left script, context-sensitive letter forms, and code-mixing practices. The computational approach integrates corpus linguistics, machine learning, and geospatial analysis. Planned workflows include building a unified Urdu text corpus (preprocessing ~10 TB of data), fine-tuning transformer-based models for semantic and stylistic analysis, and implementing parallelized algorithms to cluster dialect features across 15 regional varieties. HPC resources are essential for managing memory-intensive tasks, including graph-based representations of lexical evolution and GPU-accelerated training of deep learning models. Expected outcomes include (1) open-access computational tools for Urdu NLP, (2) quantitative insights into sociolinguistic changes post-Partition (1947–present), and (3) interactive dialect maps to inform language preservation efforts. By enabling scalable analysis of Urdu’s linguistic diversity, this project will advance scholarship in South Asian studies, support pedagogy for heritage speakers, and strengthen infrastructure for cross-lingual AI applications in multilingual regions.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Urdu language and related dialects. Includes instruction in philology; Modern Urdu; dialects; and applications in business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance physical education pedagogy and sports coaching efficacy by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex biomechanical and physiological interactions in student-athletes. Current approaches to designing training programs often rely on generalized guidelines, which inadequately address individual variability in movement patterns, metabolic responses, and injury risks. To address this gap, we propose a computational framework integrating motion capture data, physiological monitoring, and machine learning to simulate and optimize personalized training regimens. The research will utilize biomechanical datasets collected from student-athletes across diverse sports, including kinematic and kinetic measurements during skill execution, coupled with real-time physiological metrics such as heart rate variability and lactate thresholds. These datasets will be processed using parallelized computational models to analyze movement efficiency, predict injury likelihood via finite element simulations of musculoskeletal stress, and identify optimal training loads through reinforcement learning algorithms. The scale and complexity of these multi-modal datasets—spanning terabytes of high-frequency sensor data and requiring iterative model training—necessitate HPC resources for feasible processing times. Expected outcomes include the development of an open-access tool for educators and coaches to generate evidence-based, individualized training plans that balance skill development with injury mitigation. By translating computational insights into practical teaching strategies, this work aims to advance pedagogical practices in physical education, fostering safer and more effective athletic development in K–12 and collegiate settings. The project underscores the transformative potential of HPC in bridging theoretical kinesiology with applied teaching methodologies, directly supporting the program’s mission to equip educators with innovative, data-driven coaching tools.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach physical education programs and/or to coach sports at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance an interdisciplinary investigation into the dynamics of cultural and environmental resilience in historically marginalized communities. The research integrates methodologies from digital humanities, environmental anthropology, and spatial statistics to analyze how sociocultural practices mediate community responses to ecological stressors. A central challenge lies in synthesizing heterogeneous datasets—including ethnographic records, oral histories, satellite imagery, and climate models—into a unified analytical framework. To address this, we propose a computational pipeline combining natural language processing (NLP) for qualitative text analysis, agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate human-environment interactions, and Bayesian hierarchical models to quantify uncertainty across spatial and temporal scales. The ABM component will simulate decision-making processes under varying climate scenarios, requiring iterative parameter calibration and sensitivity analyses that demand substantial parallel processing capabilities. NLP tasks involve training transformer-based models on unstructured ethnographic texts to identify patterns in adaptive knowledge transmission, necessitating GPU-accelerated workloads. By correlating these outputs with geospatial and climatic data, the project aims to identify critical thresholds in resilience strategies and predict vulnerabilities under future environmental conditions. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for interdisciplinary resilience research, policy-relevant insights into culturally sustainable adaptation practices, and novel methodological contributions to integrating qualitative and quantitative data in HPC environments. This work bridges epistemic divides between social and environmental sciences, offering a scalable framework for studying complex socioecological systems. The requested computing resources are essential to manage the project’s data volume, computational intensity, and need for rapid iteration across modeling paradigms.
cip_definition: A program that derives from two or more distinct programs and that is integrated around a unifying theme or topic that cannot be subsumed under a single discipline or occupational field.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cross-border information ecosystems and their impact on strategic stability in contested regions, focusing on how emerging communication technologies reshape state and non-state actor interactions in asymmetric security environments. Traditional frameworks in international relations often overlook the computational complexity of real-time, multi-actor information flows, which increasingly influence crisis decision-making and escalation pathways. To address this gap, the research employs a mixed-methods approach integrating large-scale network analysis, agent-based modeling (ABM), and natural language processing (NLP) to simulate and analyze decentralized information dissemination patterns across social media, state-aligned media, and encrypted platforms. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process multilingual text corpora (spanning 10+ languages) from open-source intelligence (OSINT) datasets, model multi-agent interactions at scale, and run Monte Carlo simulations to assess probabilistic escalation scenarios under varying technological and geopolitical constraints. Key computational challenges include real-time sentiment analysis of adversarial narratives, dynamic network clustering to identify emergent influence clusters, and ABM calibration using historical case studies (e.g., hybrid conflicts in the South China Sea and Eastern Europe). Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible framework for quantifying information ecosystem volatility, predictive models of technology-driven escalation triggers, and policy-relevant insights into platform governance and crisis communication protocols. By bridging computational social science with security studies, this project aims to establish new methodologies for analyzing nonlinear, technology-mediated conflicts while advancing infrastructure for interdisciplinary research at the intersection of data science and strategic studies.
detailed_field: International relations and national security studies
cip_title: International Relations and National Security Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in international relations and national security studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address the growing need for advanced computational frameworks to analyze and optimize human movement patterns in sports performance and injury prevention. While traditional biomechanical studies rely on lab-based motion capture and simplified models, real-world athletic movements involve complex, dynamic interactions between neuromuscular control, environmental factors, and equipment design—a multidimensional challenge requiring high-resolution simulations. This project will develop a scalable computational platform to model athlete-specific kinematics and kinetics under variable training conditions, integrating heterogeneous datasets from wearable sensors, force plate telemetry, and 3D motion tracking. The core computational challenge lies in resolving the nonlinear relationships between muscle activation strategies, joint loading, and movement efficiency at millisecond timescales across diverse athlete physiologies. High-performance computing resources will enable the deployment of coupled machine learning and physics-based simulations, including finite element analysis of tissue stress distributions and reinforcement learning algorithms to predict optimal movement adaptations. By leveraging GPU-accelerated parallel processing, the framework will iteratively refine personalized biomechanical profiles using probabilistic optimization techniques, accounting for stochastic variables such as fatigue states and equipment interactions. Anticipated outcomes include a novel predictive tool for identifying injury-prone movement signatures in contact sports and a generative model for designing individualized training protocols. This work bridges gaps between computational biomechanics, sports engineering, and data science, offering a paradigm shift from reactive injury management to proactive risk mitigation. The resource allocation will directly support the creation of open-access simulation templates, fostering collaboration across academic and sports medicine communities while advancing computational methodologies for human-centric performance analytics.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_title: Sports, Kinesiology, and Physical Education/ Fitness, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in sports, kinesiology, and physical education/fitness, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address critical challenges in optimizing electrical system safety and efficiency across residential, commercial, and industrial environments through advanced computational modeling. Modern electrical installations face increasing complexity due to variable load demands, integration of renewable energy sources, and evolving safety standards. Traditional manual calculations and static simulations often fail to capture dynamic interactions within these systems, leading to suboptimal designs, energy losses, or compliance risks. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes the development of high-fidelity, multi-physics simulations to model electrical networks under real-world operating conditions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the project will implement parallelized finite element analysis (FEA) to simulate electromagnetic fields, thermal dynamics, and power distribution across heterogeneous circuits. Machine learning algorithms will be integrated to predict fault conditions, such as arc flashes or overload scenarios, by training on synthetic data generated from these simulations. Additionally, Monte Carlo methods will assess code compliance probabilities under diverse building configurations and NEC standards. The computational framework will incorporate real-world datasets from smart meters and IoT-enabled electrical panels to validate models. Expected outcomes include predictive tools for optimizing circuit layouts, risk matrices for maintenance prioritization, and open-source modules for estimating energy losses in aging infrastructure. By enabling granular analysis of transient phenomena and system-wide interdependencies, this work aims to advance evidence-based practices in electrical installations, reduce fire hazards, and inform updates to training curricula for electricians. The scale of these simulations—requiring thousands of parallelized iterations to account for stochastic load patterns and material degradation—necessitates HPC capabilities to achieve practical runtime and resolution. Results will be disseminated through interactive training platforms for vocational instructors and compliance dashboards for electrical inspectors.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to install, operate, maintain, and repair electric apparatus and systems such as residential, commercial, and industrial electric-power wiring; and DC and AC motors, controls, and electrical distribution panels. Includes instruction in the principles of electronics and electrical systems, wiring, power transmission, safety, industrial and household appliances, job estimation, electrical testing and inspection, and applicable codes and standards.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in human-AI collaboration, focusing on the design and evaluation of adaptive interfaces that dynamically respond to user cognitive states and contextual factors. A critical challenge in Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) is developing systems that balance real-time responsiveness with ethical and societal considerations, particularly as AI-driven technologies become embedded in high-stakes domains like healthcare, education, and decision support. Current limitations in simulating complex human behavior at scale, coupled with the computational demands of training multimodal AI models (e.g., integrating eye-tracking, physiological signals, and natural language), hinder progress in creating equitable and transparent interactive systems. To address this, the project employs a hybrid computational approach combining agent-based modeling (ABM) of diverse user populations, federated learning for privacy-preserving personalization, and reinforcement learning to optimize interface adaptations. The ABM framework will simulate 10,000+ heterogeneous agents with varying cognitive profiles, cultural backgrounds, and interaction histories, requiring parallelized computation to model longitudinal interactions. Federated learning pipelines will train adaptive models across distributed datasets while preserving user anonymity, necessitating GPU-accelerated workflows. The research will also implement real-time inference engines for multimodal data fusion, demanding low-latency HPC infrastructure. Outcomes include open-source tools for ethical interface design, benchmarks for evaluating AI-mediated interactions, and novel methodologies for embedding sociotechnical fairness constraints into adaptive systems. By enabling large-scale simulation of human-AI interaction dynamics, this work aims to advance HCI’s capacity to anticipate societal impacts during the design phase, ultimately contributing to more accountable and human-centered intelligent technologies.
cip_definition: An interdisciplinary program that focuses on the study of the interaction between people and technology and how that technology impacts society, and combines disciplines within the fields of computing and information science (information systems, software engineering, artificial intelligence and design), engineering, and the behavior sciences (cognitive science, cognitive psychology, sociology, organizational psychology, and social psychology). Includes instruction in information technology, cognitive and behavioral sciences, and systems design.

abstract: Cultural heritage preservation faces escalating challenges due to climate change, urbanization, and resource constraints, necessitating advanced tools to balance conservation priorities with socio-economic and policy realities. Current approaches often struggle to integrate large-scale spatial, environmental, and socio-cultural datasets, limiting predictive accuracy and policy responsiveness. This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing preservation strategies by modeling dynamic interactions between environmental stressors, stakeholder decision-making, and policy outcomes. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will deploy agent-based models to simulate stakeholder behaviors and land-use impacts across multi-decadal timescales, coupled with machine learning algorithms to predict site vulnerability using geospatial, climatic, and archaeological data. Parallelized geostatistical analysis will process high-resolution LiDAR and multispectral imagery to identify at-risk cultural landscapes, while Monte Carlo methods will quantify uncertainties in preservation cost-benefit scenarios. The computational intensity of these tasks—particularly the iterative simulation of complex adaptive systems and processing of terabyte-scale remote sensing datasets—requires scalable memory and GPU acceleration unavailable in local computing environments. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision-support toolkit for heritage managers, enabling real-time prioritization of intervention sites based on ecological fragility, community values, and policy constraints. The project will advance interdisciplinary methodologies in cultural resource management by formalizing data integration protocols across archaeology, environmental science, and policy analysis domains. Results will inform adaptive management frameworks for three UNESCO World Heritage sites under study, while computational workflows will be generalized for broader application in resource-constrained contexts. By bridging gaps between predictive analytics and participatory policymaking, this work aims to establish new standards for evidence-based cultural heritage stewardship in rapidly changing environments.
cip_title: Cultural Resource Management and Policy Analysis
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of cultural studies, public policy analysis, and management skills to planning, promoting, and implementing programs to preserve and protect cultural heritage sites and artifacts. Includes instruction in historical preservation and conservation, business management, policy analysis, applied economics, public relations, applied history, historical archaeology, and environmental impact studies.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to enhance pedagogical strategies for training business, innovation, and entrepreneurship educators. Current methods for teaching these educators often rely on static case studies or theoretical models, which inadequately prepare them to address dynamic challenges in entrepreneurial ecosystems, market volatility, and student-driven idea generation. To address this gap, the research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate complex, interactive business scenarios and model the efficacy of pedagogical interventions. Agent-based modeling will be used to simulate classroom environments where trainee instructors engage with virtual student cohorts, iteratively testing lesson plans and adaptive teaching strategies under variable economic conditions. Concurrently, large-scale natural language processing (NLP) will analyze historical and emerging business curricula, entrepreneurial pitch datasets, and innovation case studies to identify pedagogical patterns and gaps. These analyses will inform the design of a machine learning-driven recommendation system that proposes optimized teaching content and assessment tools tailored to diverse learner needs. The HPC infrastructure is critical for handling the parallelized execution of thousands of simulated classroom interactions, real-time NLP tasks across multilingual educational corpora, and generative AI models that create context-specific entrepreneurship challenges. Expected outcomes include a scalable platform for training educators in evidence-based, adaptive teaching practices, validated frameworks for simulating business education scenarios, and open-access datasets linking pedagogical strategies to student entrepreneurial competencies. By integrating computational modeling with teacher education, this work aims to equip instructors with data-driven tools to foster critical thinking, opportunity recognition, and business resilience in their students, ultimately strengthening vocational education outcomes.
cip_title: Business and Innovation/ Entrepreneurship Teacher Education
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach vocational business, innovation, and entrepreneurship programs at various educational levels. Includes instruction in business administration, business development, finance, idea generation, investing, logistics, management, and marketing.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance predictive modeling of groundwater contamination risks in regions impacted by unconventional shale gas development. The research addresses a critical gap in environmental geoscience: the lack of high-resolution, system-scale models capable of integrating heterogeneous geological datasets to forecast contaminant transport mechanisms (e.g., methane leakage, heavy metal mobilization) across fractured shale formations and overlying aquifers. Current models often oversimplify subsurface heterogeneity and fracture dynamics, limiting their utility for proactive resource management. To resolve this, we propose a coupled computational workflow combining 3D hydrogeological simulations (via MODFLOW 6 and PFLOTRAN) with machine learning-driven uncertainty quantification. The HPC framework will process terabyte-scale inputs, including spatially variable hydraulic conductivity data from field sites, geochemical profiles, and induced fracture networks mapped via remote sensing and borehole logs. Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will assess probabilistic contamination scenarios under varying extraction practices and climatic stressors. A novel convolutional neural network architecture, trained on simulation outputs, will identify high-risk zones and optimize mitigation strategies. This approach directly supports regulatory decision-making by quantifying the environmental trade-offs of energy development, while advancing computational methods for dynamic subsurface systems. Outcomes will include open-source tools for contamination risk assessment, a publicly accessible dataset of modeled scenarios, and policy-relevant guidelines for sustainable groundwater management in shale-rich basins. The requested computing resources are essential to achieve the spatial-temporal resolution required for actionable predictions, as preliminary tests on local clusters indicate that 10,000+ core-hours are needed per stochastic realization. By bridging geological process modeling, data science, and environmental policy, this work aligns with the Environmental Geosciences program’s emphasis on hazard mitigation, GIS-integrated resource management, and interdisciplinary sustainability solutions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the environmental implications of geological processes and human activities on Earth. Includes instruction in environmental/natural resource management, geographic information systems (GIS), geology, hydrology, regulatory agency compliance, hazard identification and mitigation, environmental law, environmental policy, and sustainability studies.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of doctrinal evolution and schism formation within religious traditions through large-scale computational analysis of historical and contemporary textual corpora. While prior scholarship has relied on manual textual criticism and qualitative case studies, the complexity of religious systems—shaped by interactions between scriptural interpretation, socio-political contexts, and communal identity—demands a quantitative, systems-oriented approach. The research will employ natural language processing (NLP) and network analysis to model semantic shifts in core theological concepts across time and geography, using digitized scriptures, commentaries, and polemical texts from three major Abrahamic traditions. A high-performance computing (HPC) environment is essential to process multilingual texts spanning two millennia, train transformer-based models for cross-temporal semantic alignment, and simulate branching patterns in doctrinal networks under varying sociocultural parameters. Key computational challenges include resolving ambiguities in metaphor-rich religious language, reconstructing influence networks from fragmentary historical records, and scaling agent-based simulations to test hypotheses about schism triggers. Expected outcomes include (1) a reproducible framework for mapping doctrinal divergence in religious systems, (2) identification of linguistic and structural markers predictive of communal fragmentation, and (3) public datasets annotating theological disputation patterns across 200+ historical crises. These results will advance theoretical debates about religious change while demonstrating scalable digital humanities methodologies for comparative religion. The requested resources—particularly GPU nodes for deep learning and high-memory nodes for large network analyses—will enable processing of terabyte-scale text collections and complex simulations impractical on standard academic computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the nature of religious belief and specific religious and quasi-religious systems. Includes instruction in phenomenology; the sociology, psychology, philosophy, anthropology, literature and art of religion; mythology; scriptural and textual studies; religious history and politics; and specific studies of particular faith communities and their behavior.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in optimizing digital communication interfaces for technical and scientific audiences. A critical challenge in technical communication lies in designing platforms that balance usability, accessibility, and information density, particularly when conveying complex STEM concepts to diverse stakeholders. Traditional user testing methods struggle to scale for analyzing large, heterogeneous datasets—such as eye-tracking metrics, interaction logs, and semantic content—generated by modern documentation systems. To address this, we propose a computational approach combining machine learning (ML) and natural language processing (NLP) to model user engagement patterns and content efficacy across multimodal technical documents. Using HPC resources, we will train deep learning models on anonymized datasets from technical documentation platforms (e.g., API manuals, scientific instructional videos) to identify latent patterns in user behavior, such as friction points in navigation or comprehension gaps in explanatory text. Concurrently, agent-based simulations will be deployed to test adaptive interface designs under scalable, variable user scenarios. The project integrates Python-based ML frameworks (TensorFlow, PyTorch) with NLP libraries (spaCy, Gensim) for semantic analysis, requiring parallelized computing to handle high-dimensional data. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework for optimizing technical content delivery, actionable guidelines for adaptive interface design, and open-source tools for automated usability assessment. This research directly supports the program’s mission to bridge technical expertise with user-centered communication strategies, offering scalable solutions for industries reliant on precise scientific knowledge transfer. By utilizing HPC, the project advances methodological innovation in communication studies, enabling data-driven refinements to digital documentation systems that are infeasible with conventional computational resources.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the communication of technical and scientific knowledge to a variety of audiences through print, video, and digital media; and that prepares individuals to function as technical writers and editors, documentation developers, web designers, and usability specialists. Includes instruction in scientific and technical writing and editing, graphic and information design, web design, audience analysis, document usability and field testing, publications management, and applications to specific technical fields.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of optimizing material performance and structural integrity in upholstered products through advanced computational modeling. Traditional upholstery design relies heavily on empirical testing, which is resource-intensive and limited in its ability to predict long-term material behavior under dynamic mechanical, thermal, and environmental stresses. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate multiscale interactions between upholstery materials—such as foams, textiles, and springs—and their operational environments. The research will focus on two primary objectives: (1) developing finite element analysis (FEA) models to predict stress distribution, fatigue, and deformation in complex upholstered assemblies (e.g., furniture, automotive seats), and (2) employing machine learning algorithms to correlate material composition with performance metrics like durability, comfort, and thermal regulation. Large-scale molecular dynamics simulations will further investigate degradation mechanisms in synthetic fibers and cushioning materials under repeated loading cycles. By integrating these approaches, the project aims to establish predictive models that reduce reliance on physical prototyping, accelerate design iterations, and enhance sustainability through data-driven material optimization. The computational workflows will be validated against experimental datasets collected from industry partners, ensuring practical relevance. Anticipated outcomes include open-access simulation tools tailored for upholstery applications, a materials database linking microstructural properties to macroscopic performance, and design guidelines for improving product lifespans. This work represents a transformative step in modernizing upholstery practices by bridging craft-based expertise with computational engineering, with potential impacts on manufacturing efficiency, waste reduction, and ergonomic innovation. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the high-resolution simulations and parameter space exploration required to capture nonlinear material behaviors at scale.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to install springs, filling, padding, covering and finishing on items such as furniture, automobile seats, caskets, mattresses, and bedsprings.

abstract: This project investigates the interplay between urban environmental stimuli and dynamic cognitive load modulation, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model how multisensory input patterns influence decision-making efficiency in pedestrian navigation contexts. While prior psychology research has examined environmental stressors or cognitive load in isolation, this work integrates real-world spatial-auditory-visual datasets with individualized cognitive resource allocation models to predict adaptive behavior in complex, noisy environments—a novel intersection of environmental psychology, cognitive neuroscience, and computational urban science. The core challenge lies in simulating high-dimensional interactions between fluctuating environmental parameters (e.g., crowd density metrics, acoustic signatures, architectural affordances) and neural resource competition processes at millisecond timescales. We propose developing hybrid neural networks that combine biologically constrained cortical column models with transformer architectures to process geospatial-temporal data streams from 12 global cities. These models will be trained on both experimental data (360-degree VR navigation tasks with EEG/fNIRS monitoring) and synthetic environments generated through procedural urban space algorithms. The HPC infrastructure is critical for three components: 1) Parallel processing of petascale urban sensor datasets, 2) Evolutionary optimization of cognitive architecture hyperparameters across 50,000+ simulated agents, and 3) Real-time ray tracing for psychoacoustic and visual clutter simulations in Unity-based experimental paradigms. Anticipated outcomes include the first predictive framework mapping nonlinear relationships between environmental complexity gradients and cognitive performance thresholds, with applications for adaptive urban design and spatial cognition-aware navigation systems. This work establishes a computational psychology paradigm for studying embodied cognition in built environments while advancing methods for coupling neural dynamical systems with large-scale environmental simulations.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific study of individual and collective behavior, the physical and environmental bases of behavior, and the analysis and treatment of behavior problems and disorders. Includes instruction in the principles of the various subfields of psychology, research methods, and psychological assessment and testing methods.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of Ancient and Byzantine Greek textual corpora, addressing critical gaps in understanding linguistic evolution and intertextual networks across millennia. Despite the centrality of philological methods in Classical studies, manual analysis of syntactic patterns, morphological shifts, and dialectal variations remains time-intensive and limited in scope. The research problem centers on reconstructing the diachronic development of Greek—from Archaic to Byzantine phases—through quantitative modeling of grammatical, lexical, and stylistic features across diverse genres (e.g., epic poetry, historiography, theological texts). A key challenge lies in processing fragmented or partially preserved manuscripts, where computational methods can mitigate ambiguities in attestation. The project will employ machine learning models (e.g., transformer-based architectures) trained on annotated corpora to automate the identification of dialectal features, syntactic structures, and formulaic expressions. Phylogenetic algorithms will map linguistic divergence across periods, while graph-based network analysis will trace intertextual dependencies in Byzantine commentaries on Classical works. HPC resources are essential for scaling these analyses to encompass the TLG Canon, DBBE, and unpublished papyrological datasets (totaling ~150 million tokens), requiring parallelized processing for feature extraction, tokenization, and semantic clustering. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible database of annotated texts with searchable linguistic metadata, (2) probabilistic models of dialect transition between Attic, Koine, and Medieval Greek, and (3) visualization tools for mapping textual reuse in late-antique scholarship. By integrating computational linguistics with traditional philology, this work aims to resolve longstanding debates about periodization thresholds and regional linguistic contact, while establishing scalable methodologies for fragmentary text analysis. The requested resources will directly support 3-4 peer-reviewed publications and a workshop on computational approaches to premodern languages.
cip_title: Ancient/ Classical Greek Language and Literature
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Greek language and literature from its origins through the fall of the Byzantine (Eastern Roman) Empire, as a secular and/or theological subject. Includes instruction in philology, Attic and Hellenistic dialects, Koine (Biblical) Greek, and Medieval or Byzantine Greek.

abstract: Agricultural business operations face growing challenges in optimizing resource allocation, supply chain efficiency, and market responsiveness due to the increasing complexity of environmental, economic, and logistical datasets. Current decision-support tools often lack the computational capacity to integrate real-time data streams from precision agriculture sensors, regional climate models, and commodity market trends, limiting their utility for dynamic farm management. This project proposes the development of a scalable computational framework to model multi-objective agricultural business decisions under uncertainty, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will combine agent-based modeling of farm-level operational choices with machine learning-driven market trend analysis, integrating heterogeneous datasets including soil health metrics, equipment telemetry, and global trade patterns. Key computational challenges include parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations for risk assessment, optimizing mixed-integer programming models for logistics planning, and training deep learning architectures on spatiotemporal crop yield data. Access to HPC infrastructure will enable iterative scenario testing across diverse agricultural systems, varying parameters such as input costs, policy constraints, and climate volatility. Expected outcomes include an open-source decision-support toolkit that quantifies trade-offs between profitability, sustainability, and resilience for agribusiness stakeholders. The project will directly address scalability barriers in existing agricultural technology platforms, providing actionable insights for enterprises managing 10,000+ acre operations. By advancing computational methods tailored to agricultural business analytics, this work aims to bridge the gap between precision agriculture data generation and operational decision-making, ultimately strengthening the competitiveness of farm enterprises in volatile markets. Results will be validated against historical performance data from partnering cooperatives, with model outputs informing adaptive management protocols for grain storage, labor allocation, and input procurement cycles.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform specialized support functions related to agricultural business offices and operations and to operate agricultural office equipment, software, and information systems. Includes instruction in basic agricultural business principles, office management, equipment operation, standard software, and database management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational models to optimize the design and fabrication of custom wood components in cabinetmaking and millwork, addressing inefficiencies in material usage, structural integrity, and production time inherent to traditional workflows. The anisotropic nature of wood, combined with complex joinery and milling operations, creates challenges in predicting material behavior during machining. Current empirical methods often result in trial-and-error waste or over-engineering. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), machine learning, and parametric design tools. Computational models will simulate stress distribution, moisture-related deformation, and toolpath efficiency across diverse wood species and geometries. Machine learning algorithms trained on historical fabrication data will predict optimal machining parameters, while multi-objective optimization workflows will balance material conservation, structural performance, and aesthetic requirements. The project requires HPC resources to manage large-scale simulations of heterogeneous wood microstructures, parallel processing of combinatorial design scenarios, and training of neural networks on 3D CAD/CAM datasets. Expected outcomes include an open-access digital toolkit for predicting wood machining outcomes, generative design templates for common millwork components, and data-driven guidelines for sustainable material selection. By bridging computational engineering with craft traditions, this research aims to reduce material waste by an estimated 15–30% in custom fabrication workflows while maintaining artisanal quality standards. Results will be validated through physical prototyping in partnership with local cabinetmaking workshops, ensuring practical relevance to both educational programs and industry practitioners. The computational infrastructure developed will serve as a template for integrating advanced simulation capabilities into vocational technical training curricula.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to set up, operate and repair industrial woodworking machinery, and to use such machinery to design and fabricate wooden components and complete articles.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution of cultural narratives and identity formation in contemporary Latin American digital media through computational analysis of large-scale, multilingual textual and visual datasets. Focusing on 21st-century social movements and diasporic communities, the research addresses a critical gap in understanding how digital platforms reshape collective memory and cultural belonging across Latin America, particularly among marginalized groups. The study employs natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision techniques to analyze over 10 million publicly available social media posts, digital archives of community-led cultural initiatives, and grassroots multimedia content from Mexico, Colombia, and Argentina. Advanced transformer-based models will be fine-tuned for regional linguistic variations and code-switching patterns, while multimodal neural networks will decode interactions between text, images, and audiovisual elements in cultural storytelling. High-performance computing resources are essential for training these models on heterogeneous data at scale, conducting temporal network analyses of narrative diffusion, and simulating cultural transmission patterns across virtual communities. Expected outcomes include a novel framework for analyzing digital cultural production in transnational contexts, open-source tools for multilingual Latin American text analysis, and new insights into how digital spaces mediate tensions between traditional cultural practices and globalized identities. The computational infrastructure will enable processing of Indigenous and Creole languages often excluded from mainstream NLP resources, directly supporting underrepresented voices in cultural studies scholarship. Results will inform cultural preservation strategies and educational initiatives addressing digital divides in the region.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the Hispanic peoples of the North and South American Continents outside Canada and the United States, including the study of the Pre-Columbian period and the flow of immigrants from other societies.

abstract: Insects are critical yet understudied agents of ecosystem dynamics, with flight dispersal mechanisms that remain poorly quantified in heterogeneous environmental conditions. This project seeks to develop a high-resolution computational framework to model micro-scale atmospheric interactions governing insect flight trajectories, leveraging entomological data to predict population-scale dispersal under climate variability. Current models oversimplify fluid-insect biomechanics, neglecting turbulence effects on species-specific morphology, such as wingbeat kinematics and body mass distributions. We propose a multi-scale simulation approach integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD) with agent-based modeling (ABM) to resolve how localized wind patterns, thermal gradients, and precipitation interact with insect physiology to shape dispersal outcomes. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable parallelized simulations of 10⁶–10⁷ agent insects across dynamic 3D atmospheric fields derived from remote-sensing datasets. Machine learning surrogates will be trained on CFD-ABM outputs to accelerate parameter space exploration, targeting species of agricultural and epidemiological concern (e.g., migratory pests, disease vectors). Validation will utilize entomological radar datasets and mark-release-recapture field trials for select Lepidoptera and Diptera species. Expected outcomes include the first open-source platform for probabilistic insect dispersal forecasting at meter-scale resolution, directly addressing gaps in precision agriculture and vector-borne disease management. By quantifying how extreme weather events and habitat fragmentation modulate dispersal efficiency, this work will inform resilience strategies for pollination networks and invasive species containment. The computational framework will prioritize scalability for global change scenarios, with generated datasets bridging entomology, atmospheric science, and environmental policy. Resource allocation will support GPU-accelerated simulations, large-scale parameter optimization, and public dissemination of models via an interactive portal for stakeholder-driven scenario testing.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of insect species and populations in respect of their life cycles, morphology, genetics, physiology, ecology, taxonomy, population dynamics, and environmental and economic impacts. Includes instruction in applicable biological and physical sciences as well as insect toxicology and the biochemical control of insect populations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of Modern Greek linguistic and literary evolution from the late 15th century to the present. The research addresses the challenge of systematically analyzing large-scale textual corpora spanning diverse genres, dialects, and historical periods, which remain underexplored due to computational limitations. Current studies of Modern Greek often rely on manual or small-scale methods, limiting insights into language change, dialectal variation, and literary trends. This project proposes a computational linguistics framework to process and analyze digitized texts—including literature, newspapers, and technical documents—using natural language processing (NLP) techniques optimized for Greek’s morphological complexity. Key methods include tokenization tailored to Greek inflectional patterns, syntactic parsing for dialect comparison, and machine learning models to trace semantic shifts in scientific or business terminology. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of terabytes of text, training of transformer-based models for stylometric analysis of literature, and dynamic visualization of linguistic changes across time and geography. Expected outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible corpus of annotated Modern Greek texts, (2) quantitative maps of dialectal divergence and convergence, and (3) identification of understudied literary movements linked to sociotechnical changes. By integrating computational rigor with philological expertise, this work will provide novel methodologies for digital humanities in less-resourced languages, support preservation initiatives for regional Greek dialects, and inform language policy in technical domains. The scale of data and complexity of models—particularly neural networks for historical text normalization—necessitate dedicated HPC resources to achieve statistically robust results within feasible timeframes.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development and use of the Greek language in the period dating from the late 15th century to the present. Includes instruction in modern Greek literature, current Greek dialects, and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: Cybersecurity defense strategies require robust frameworks to address evolving threats in complex, interconnected systems. However, scaling policy evaluations to real-world network sizes and dynamic threat landscapes remains a critical challenge. This project seeks to develop a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation platform to model cyberattack scenarios, assess defense policies, and quantify systemic vulnerabilities in large-scale networks. The research problem centers on the lack of computational tools capable of analyzing multi-layered cyber-physical systems under adversarial conditions while incorporating human decision-making, institutional policies, and emerging technologies like AI-driven attacks. The proposed approach combines agent-based modeling, network graph analytics, and Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate defensive strategies such as incident response protocols, zero-trust architectures, and resilience-focused recovery policies. High-performance computing resources will enable parallelized simulations of nation-state-level network topologies, probabilistic threat propagation models, and real-time policy adaptation algorithms. Key computational tasks include graph-theoretic vulnerability scoring, attack surface minimization under resource constraints, and stochastic optimization of defense-in-depth configurations. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for comparing policy efficacy across infrastructure sectors, metrics for cyber deterrence under asymmetric threats, and risk-aware resource allocation models. This work will directly inform national cybersecurity standards by identifying cost-effective strategies for threat reduction and providing empirical evidence for infrastructure hardening priorities. The HPC component is essential to achieve the required scale, with simulations spanning millions of nodes and terabyte-scale threat intelligence datasets. By integrating policy constraints with technical realities, this project bridges the gap between strategic cybersecurity planning and operational implementation challenges.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of strategy, policy, and standards regarding the security of and operations in cyberspace. Includes instruction in incident response, information assurance, recovery policies, vulnerability reduction, deterrence, threat reduction, and resiliency.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of adaptive, data-driven tools for educators working with young children (ages 0–5) with disabilities in early childhood special education (ECSE) settings. A critical challenge in ECSE is designing individualized instructional strategies that account for the heterogeneous developmental trajectories, sensory processing profiles, and communication needs of children with disabilities. Traditional approaches rely on manual observation and static assessment tools, which struggle to capture dynamic learning patterns or provide real-time feedback for educators. To address this gap, we propose creating computational models that simulate child-teacher interactions under varied instructional scenarios, integrating multimodal data from wearable sensors, video recordings, and structured assessments. These simulations will train machine learning algorithms to predict optimal intervention timing, modality (e.g., visual vs. tactile cues), and complexity based on individual learner profiles. The HPC environment is essential for processing high-dimensional datasets (e.g., motion-tracking data from classroom activities) and running iterative, agent-based models of learning behaviors. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for generating personalized ECSE lesson plans, validated against empirical data from partner preschool programs. This work will provide educators with evidence-based, scalable tools to improve responsiveness to neurodiverse learners while reducing planning burdens. By aligning computational modeling with early childhood pedagogy, the project aims to establish a new paradigm for special education research that bridges developmental theory, classroom practice, and emergent technologies.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals in Early Childhood Special Education Programs
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and provision of teaching and other educational services to infant and pre-school age children with special learning needs or disabilities, and that prepares individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in diagnosing learning disabilities, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising special education students, special education counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational models to optimize traditional wooden boatbuilding techniques through advanced simulations of structural integrity, hydrodynamic performance, and material behavior. While empirical methods remain foundational in the craft, modern boatbuilders face challenges in balancing historical authenticity with performance efficiency, especially as demand grows for vessels that meet contemporary safety and sustainability standards. Current manual design iterations are time-intensive and limited in evaluating complex variables such as dynamic load distributions, moisture-induced wood degradation, or hydrodynamic drag patterns. To address this, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach to simulate multi-physics interactions in wooden boat systems. Finite element analysis (FEA) will model stress distribution in hull joinery and planking under varying maritime conditions, while computational fluid dynamics (CFD) will assess hydrodynamic efficiency across hull geometries. Machine learning models, trained on historical and experimental datasets, will predict optimal wood species, joinery techniques, and spar configurations under environmental and operational constraints. These simulations will integrate parametric design principles to iteratively refine lofting and fairing processes, reducing material waste and labor costs. The HPC environment is critical for managing large-scale simulations of multi-variable scenarios, including probabilistic models of wood aging and composite material interactions. Outcomes will include a computational framework to guide boatbuilders in selecting empirically validated, high-performance designs and a publicly accessible database of material performance metrics. By bridging traditional craftsmanship with computational engineering, this work aims to enhance the durability and efficiency of wooden vessels while preserving artisanal techniques. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated nodes for FEA/CFD workloads and high-memory nodes for dataset training, enabling scalable, high-fidelity simulations that are otherwise computationally prohibitive.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to construct and repair traditional and modern wooden boats. Includes instruction in budgeting, drafting, fairing, lofting, joinery, planking, spars and rigging, and woodworking.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the dynamic interactions between urban real estate markets, climate risk, and infrastructure resilience—a nexus underexplored in traditional real estate research. The research problem centers on quantifying how granular, spatially heterogeneous climate hazards (e.g., flooding, heat stress) influence property valuation, investment decisions, and long-term urban development patterns. Current models lack the resolution to integrate real-time environmental data, agent-based decision-making, and macroeconomic feedback loops at city-scale, limiting predictive accuracy for stakeholders. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM), geospatial machine learning, and Monte Carlo simulations. The ABM module will simulate developer, investor, and policymaker behaviors under stochastic climate scenarios, while convolutional neural networks (CNNs) process high-resolution satellite imagery and LiDAR data to assess localized physical risks. Monte Carlo methods will propagate uncertainty across interconnected financial and environmental variables. HPC resources are critical to parallelize simulations across thousands of climate-realistic futures, manage petabyte-scale geospatial datasets, and optimize hyperparameters for the CNN ensemble. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible decision-support tool for quantifying climate-driven value-at-risk in real estate portfolios, novel metrics for resilience-linked property appraisal, and policy insights on zoning adaptations. By bridging computational urban science with real estate economics, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for proactive risk management in an era of climate volatility, with direct applications for institutional investors, municipal planners, and reinsurance markets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to develop, buy, sell, appraise, and manage real estate. Includes instruction in land use development policy, real estate law, real estate marketing procedures, agency management, brokerage, property inspection and appraisal, real estate investing, leased and rental properties, commercial real estate, and property management.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to investigate the mechanistic pathways and dynamic behavior of solvent-mediated chemical reactions using advanced computational modeling. Many industrially and biologically relevant reactions occur in solution-phase environments, where solvent interactions critically influence reaction rates, selectivity, and intermediate stabilization. However, traditional quantum chemistry methods often neglect explicit solvent effects due to computational cost, leading to gaps in predicting solvent-driven phenomena. This project aims to address these limitations by integrating ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) with enhanced sampling techniques to model solvated reaction systems at an atomistic level. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to perform large-scale simulations of reactive trajectories, employing hybrid density functional theory (DFT) and coupled-cluster methods for accurate electronic structure calculations. The computational workflow will leverage distributed-memory parallelism and GPU acceleration to manage the combinatorial complexity of solvent-solute interactions across multiple timescales. Key objectives include elucidating solvent reorganization dynamics during proton-transfer reactions, quantifying entropic contributions to activation barriers in aqueous media, and identifying transient intermediates undetectable via experimental methods alone. The outcomes will provide foundational insights into solvent effects on reaction mechanisms, enabling the rational design of solvent systems for catalytic applications or green chemistry processes. By correlating simulation data with experimental kinetics, this work will also advance predictive models for reaction optimization in synthetic chemistry. The requested HPC allocation will support 50,000+ core-hours for trajectory sampling, post-processing via machine learning-assisted analysis, and validation against spectroscopic datasets. This project bridges theoretical and experimental chemistry, offering a computational framework to decode solvent-mediated reactivity with atomic precision, while training students in cutting-edge computational methodologies.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the scientific study of the composition and behavior of matter, including its micro- and macro-structure, the processes of chemical change, and the theoretical description and laboratory simulation of these phenomena.

abstract: The increasing complexity of Computer Numerically Controlled (CNC) machining processes demands advanced computational tools to optimize efficiency, precision, and sustainability in manufacturing. Current challenges include minimizing material waste, reducing energy consumption, and mitigating tool wear during high-precision operations. Traditional trial-and-error methods for toolpath optimization and process parameter selection are time-intensive and often suboptimal, while predictive models for tool longevity and thermal deformation lack the resolution needed for modern CNC applications. This project proposes leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-scale simulations integrating finite element analysis (FEA), machine learning (ML), and generative design algorithms. Computational models will simulate machining dynamics—such as stress distribution, heat generation, and tool deflection—under diverse material and operational conditions. ML frameworks will analyze historical machining data to predict tool wear patterns and optimize feed rates, spindle speeds, and cutting depths. Concurrently, generative design algorithms will explore toolpath geometries that minimize energy use and material waste while adhering to tolerances specified in CAD/CAM workflows. The HPC environment is critical for handling the high-dimensional parameter space, large datasets from sensor-equipped CNC systems, and real-time adaptive simulations. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for tool life extension, energy-efficient machining protocols, and open-source toolpath optimization libraries tailored for industrial CNC systems. These results will advance sustainable manufacturing practices by reducing scrap rates and energy costs while improving machining accuracy. The project will also generate educational modules integrating HPC-driven simulations into CNC Machinist training programs, bridging advanced computational methods with hands-on technical education. By addressing computational bottlenecks, this work aims to democratize access to high-fidelity machining simulations for small-to-medium enterprises and academic institutions, fostering innovation in precision manufacturing.
cip_title: Computer Numerically Controlled (CNC) Machinist Technology/ CNC Machinist
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to operate computer numerically controlled (CNC) machine tools, such as lathes, mills, precision measuring tools, and related attachments and accessories, to perform machining functions, such as cutting, drilling, shaping, and finishing products and component parts. Includes instruction in CNC terminology, setup, programming, operations, and troubleshooting; blueprint reading; machining; lathe and mill operations; technical mathematics; computer literacy; CAD/CAM systems; shop and safety practices; equipment capabilities; and regulations and laws.

abstract: The increasing complexity of educational assessments, driven by digital learning environments and adaptive testing platforms, demands advanced computational methods to analyze high-dimensional response data, optimize test designs, and ensure valid interpretations. Traditional psychometric approaches often struggle to scale with modern datasets containing millions of interactions, fine-grained process data (e.g., clickstreams, response latencies), and complex item types. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate machine learning-enhanced psychometric models for large-scale educational assessments. The research will focus on two interrelated challenges: (1) improving the detection of aberrant response patterns in computer-based diagnostic assessments using deep learning architectures, and (2) optimizing automated essay scoring systems through ensemble models that integrate natural language processing with cognitive writing features. Computational workflows will leverage parallelized parameter estimation for mixed-effects item response theory (IRT) models, Monte Carlo simulations for testing differential item functioning across diverse populations, and hyperparameter tuning for neural networks trained on multimodal assessment data. The HPC environment is critical for managing memory-intensive operations involving tens of millions of student-item interactions from state longitudinal databases and international assessments (e.g., PISA, NAEP). Expected outcomes include open-source software packages for scalable psychometric analysis, evidence-based guidelines for deploying computationally intensive measurement models in operational testing contexts, and novel validity indices for AI-driven assessment systems. This work directly addresses the need for robust computational infrastructure in educational measurement research, enabling innovations that balance statistical rigor with practical constraints in real-world testing environments. Findings will inform the development of fairer, more adaptive assessments while establishing methodological frameworks for handling emergent data types in digital learning ecosystems.
detailed_field: Educational assessment, evaluation, and research methods
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and procedures for designing, developing, implementing and evaluating tests and other mechanisms used to measure learning, evaluate student progress, and assess the performance of specific teaching tools, strategies and curricula. Includes instruction in psychometric measurement, instrument design, test implementation techniques, research evaluation, data reporting requirements, and data analysis and interpretation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize human-centric spatial configurations within dynamic urban environments, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address gaps in traditional environmental design methodologies. While conventional approaches prioritize static metrics such as traffic flow or energy efficiency, this research focuses on the interplay between socio-cultural behaviors, ephemeral environmental conditions (e.g., microclimates, seasonal light shifts), and adaptive design interventions. The core problem lies in simulating real-time, multi-agent interactions within hyper-localized contexts—such as transient pop-up community spaces or disaster-resilient urban layouts—where existing tools lack the resolution to capture nonlinear human-environment feedback loops. Using agent-based modeling (ABM) paired with generative adversarial networks (GANs), the project will simulate scenarios integrating pedestrian movement patterns, sensory perception data (crowd-sourced via anonymized geotagged audio/visual inputs), and dynamic material responses (e.g., phase-changing materials in temporary shelters). HPC resources are critical to parallelize Monte Carlo simulations testing thousands of design permutations under stochastic environmental stressors (e.g., heatwaves, flash floods) while maintaining sub-meter spatial granularity. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adaptive environmental design, validated against case studies in three climate-vulnerable regions, and a novel metric system quantifying "socio-spatial resilience." By bridging computational social science, sensory ethnography, and parametric design, this work aims to advance evidence-based strategies for environments that are both ecologically responsive and culturally inclusive, addressing a critical gap in non-engineering design research. The scalability of the framework will enable policymakers and designers to prototype context-sensitive solutions without relying on resource-intensive physical mock-ups, thereby democratizing access to high-fidelity environmental modeling tools.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in environmental design, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the dynamics of executive coaching interventions in driving organizational change, with a focus on modeling nonlinear relationships between coaching strategies, leader behavior, and team outcomes. While executive coaching is widely utilized to enhance leadership effectiveness, the mechanisms through which specific coaching approaches translate to measurable organizational impact remain poorly quantified. Traditional qualitative methods dominate the field, limiting scalability and predictive precision. This study proposes a computational social science framework combining agent-based modeling, natural language processing (NLP), and network analysis to simulate how coaching-driven behavioral changes propagate through organizational hierarchies. High-fidelity simulations will integrate real-world data from anonymized coaching sessions (text and audio), psychometric assessments, and organizational performance metrics to train multi-agent models reflecting diverse leadership archetypes and team structures. The HPC environment will enable parallelized testing of coaching strategy variants across thousands of simulated organizational scenarios, capturing emergent phenomena in decision-making cascades and group dynamics. Key computational challenges include optimizing NLP pipelines for extracting coaching intent signals from unstructured dialogue and calibrating network diffusion parameters using federated learning approaches to maintain data confidentiality. Expected outcomes include a validated simulation toolkit for predicting the ROI of coaching interventions under different organizational conditions, with specific deliverables quantifying how micro-level coaching interactions amplify into macro-level cultural shifts. This work aims to establish a new evidence-based paradigm for designing coaching programs in complex enterprises while advancing computational methods for behavioral modeling in business contexts.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on assisting individuals achieve career goals or assisting business leaders achieve organizational change. Includes instruction in executive coaching, group dynamics, leadership, management, organizational behavior, organizational communication, and team building.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to predict adverse neonatal outcomes in high-risk pregnancies by integrating multi-modal clinical, imaging, and genomic data. Despite advances in neonatal-perinatal medicine, early identification of infants at risk for complications such as hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy, sepsis, or metabolic disorders remains limited by the heterogeneity of physiological responses and fragmented data streams. Current risk stratification tools lack the granularity to model dynamic interactions between maternal-fetal physiology, genetic susceptibility, and postnatal adaptation. To address this gap, we propose a machine learning pipeline leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs), placental histopathology images, and umbilical cord blood metabolomic profiles from a retrospective cohort of 12,000 neonates. Computational workflows will include 3D convolutional neural networks for placental image segmentation, Bayesian hierarchical models to infer temporal risk trajectories from EHR time-series data, and graph-based algorithms to map metabolite-pathway interactions. The integration of these disparate data types requires distributed memory parallelism for large-scale matrix operations and GPU-accelerated training of ensemble models. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive algorithm for neonatal morbidity in preterm and growth-restricted infants, (2) mechanistic insights into metabolomic signatures of perinatal stress, and (3) open-source tools for real-time risk visualization in clinical settings. By harnessing HPC capabilities, this work will enable unprecedented resolution in modeling transitional physiology during the critical perinatal period. The resulting computational infrastructure will directly inform targeted intervention trials and provide a template for data-driven consultation in maternal-fetal medicine. Resource allocation is essential to manage the project's ∼450 TB multimodal dataset and computationally intensive integration steps, which exceed the capacity of local clinical servers.
cip_definition: Research focused on the physiology of the normal neonate, the pathophysiology of the sick infant, and the diagnosis and management of problems of the newborn infant, including consulting with obstetricians to plan for the care of women with high-risk pregnancies.

abstract: Endocrine-driven cancers, such as those of the breast, prostate, and thyroid, are characterized by dysregulated hormonal signaling that promotes tumor progression and therapy resistance. Despite advances in endocrine therapies, a critical gap remains in understanding how spatial and temporal variations in hormone-receptor dynamics influence cellular decision-making in tumor microenvironments. This project seeks to address this gap by developing multiscale computational models to simulate hormone-receptor interactions, intracellular signaling cascades, and population-level tumor responses. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate experimental data from 3D organoid cultures and patient-derived xenografts into stochastic partial differential equation frameworks. These models will capture the emergent behavior of endocrine signaling networks under varying ligand concentrations, receptor mutations, and stromal co-signaling. Key computational challenges include resolving time-dependent feedback loops in hormone synthesis, receptor trafficking, and cross-talk with oncogenic pathways (e.g., MAPK/ERK), which require parallelized simulations across multiple spatial scales.
