abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for modeling the biomechanical and biochemical interactions of cosmetic formulations with heterogeneous skin types, with the goal of optimizing personalized skincare protocols. Despite advances in aesthetic science, estheticians lack predictive tools to account for individual variations in skin elasticity, microbiome composition, and environmental stressors when designing treatments. Current methodologies rely heavily on generalized product trials and qualitative assessments, which limit precision in addressing conditions like hyperpigmentation, acne, or age-related texture changes. The proposed research will integrate multiphysics simulations, machine learning, and high-resolution imaging datasets to model skin response dynamics at a microstructural level. Computational models will incorporate variables such as transepidermal water loss, sebum production rates, and localized inflammation markers derived from anonymized client data. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to simulate outcomes of combinatorial treatments (e.g., enzyme exfoliants paired with LED therapy) across diverse demographic and phenotypic profiles. A key innovation lies in coupling finite element analysis of mechanical stress during facial massage techniques with agent-based modeling of topical product absorption, creating a hybrid system to predict short- and long-term efficacy. Expected outcomes include an open-access decision-support toolkit for estheticians, offering probabilistic guidance on treatment customization, and a dataset correlating computational predictions with clinical observations from partner spas. By bridging gaps between empirical practice and predictive analytics, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for evidence-based skincare that enhances treatment safety, reduces trial-and-error inefficiencies, and addresses underserved populations with atypical skin profiles. The computational infrastructure developed here could later extend to virtual training environments for esthetician education, further democratizing access to advanced aesthetic methodologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to cleanse, depilate, massage, and beautify the human body and to function as licensed estheticians and skin care specialists.  Includes instruction in skin anatomy, physiology, and health; principles of nutrition; decontamination and infection control; health and safety; facial and body massage; body wrapping and spa treatments; temporary hair removal including waxing and tweezing; color and skin analysis; client consultation and care; applicable laws and regulations; business practices; and sometimes related alternative healing regimens.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of Francophone cultural narratives across postcolonial literary and visual media. The research problem centers on understanding how cultural hybridity and identity formation are represented in works produced by Francophone communities in former French colonies (e.g., Algeria, Senegal, Vietnam) and diasporic populations. Existing scholarship often relies on qualitative close readings, which limit the scale at which patterns of cultural exchange, adaptation, and resistance can be systematically traced. To address this gap, the project employs computational methods to process and analyze a multilingual corpus of novels, poetry, films, and digital media (1900–present), totaling approximately 250,000 texts and 10,000 hours of audiovisual material. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be developed to identify recurring themes, semantic shifts in key terms (e.g., “métissage,” “diaspora”), and intertextual references across genres and regions. Computer vision techniques will supplement this by decoding visual motifs in films and artworks. Graph-based network analysis will map transnational influences among creators and communities. These tasks require HPC resources due to the volume of unstructured data, the complexity of training multilingual transformer models (e.g., CamemBERT, PhoBERT), and the iterative nature of hyperparameter tuning for cross-modal analysis. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible database of annotated cultural artifacts, quantitative frameworks for tracking narrative evolution, and visualizations of transnational Francophone cultural networks. The project aims to advance interdisciplinary methodologies in Francophone studies while illuminating understudied dynamics of cultural preservation and innovation in postcolonial contexts. By integrating computational rigor with humanistic inquiry, it will provide new tools for analyzing how global Francophone communities negotiate identity in response to historical and contemporary pressures.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of France, other Francophone countries inside and outside Europe, and the French colonial experience and the associated French minorities around the world.

abstract: Microbial communities play critical roles in human health and disease, yet the mechanisms governing their ecological stability, pathogenicity, and interactions with host immune systems remain poorly understood. This project seeks to address this gap by investigating how dynamic microbial population behaviors, such as quorum sensing, horizontal gene transfer, and metabolic cross-feeding, influence community resilience and pathogen-host outcomes in mucosal environments. We propose a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) and hybrid dynamical systems to simulate microbial population dynamics under varying host immune conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve multi-scale interactions, from single-cell microbial responses to system-level community shifts, across biologically relevant spatial and temporal scales. Simulations will parameterize experimentally validated microbial traits (e.g., virulence factor expression, antibiotic resistance gene transfer rates) and incorporate stochastic immune cell recruitment dynamics derived from in vitro epithelial co-culture models. Key objectives include identifying tipping points in dysbiosis leading to pathogenic dominance, quantifying the impact of immunomodulatory metabolites on microbial competition, and predicting how targeted interventions might steer communities toward homeostatic states. Expected outcomes include a scalable computational platform for hypothesis-driven exploration of host-microbe-immune feedback loops, with direct applications to therapeutic strategies for microbiome-associated diseases. This work will advance fundamental knowledge in microbial ecology and immunology while providing actionable insights into precision microbiota manipulation. The requested HPC resources will enable the parallel execution of thousands of simulated microbial ecosystems, statistical validation of emergent patterns against multi-omics datasets, and sensitivity analyses to prioritize future experimental targets. By bridging computational and experimental microbiology, this project aims to establish predictive frameworks for managing microbial community behaviors in health and disease contexts.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of unicellular organisms and colonies, and subcellular genetic matter and their ecological interactions with human beings and other life. Includes instruction in microbial genetics, cell biology, cell physiology, virology, pathogenic microbiology, environmental microbiology, immunology, biostatistics, bioinformatics, and laboratory methods including microscopy.

abstract: Hematological disorders, including leukemia, myelodysplastic syndromes, and coagulation abnormalities, present complex molecular mechanisms that challenge conventional diagnostic and therapeutic approaches. Current limitations in integrating multi-omics data (genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic) with dynamic models of hematopoiesis and coagulation hinder the identification of predictive biomarkers and personalized treatment strategies. This project proposes a computational framework to model disease mechanisms, optimize laboratory workflows, and predict clinical outcomes in hematologic pathologies. The primary research challenge lies in processing high-dimensional datasets and simulating multi-scale biological systems, which require substantial computational resources beyond the capacity of standard laboratory infrastructure. To address this, we will employ high-performance computing (HPC) to execute large-scale machine learning pipelines for integrating heterogeneous clinical and omics data, molecular dynamics simulations of coagulation factor interactions, and agent-based models of hematopoietic stem cell differentiation. Key computational tasks include GPU-accelerated training of deep neural networks to classify leukemia subtypes from single-cell RNA-seq data, parallelized Monte Carlo simulations of thrombotic risk under varying coagulation parameters, and ensemble modeling of clonal evolution in myeloid malignancies. These analyses demand terabytes of memory, thousands of CPU core-hours per simulation, and specialized GPU nodes for matrix operations. Expected outcomes include predictive models linking genetic variants to coagulation lab test anomalies, optimized algorithms for flow cytometry data interpretation, and digital twins of bone marrow niches to test therapeutic interventions *in silico*. The resource-intensive nature of these workflows necessitates access to HPC clusters with high-throughput storage, scalable node architectures, and GPU acceleration capabilities. Successful implementation will advance precision diagnostics, reduce turnaround times for complex hematopathology testing, and provide a computational foundation for virtual clinical trials in rare hematologic disorders. This work bridges critical gaps between experimental hematology and clinical translation, with direct implications for laboratory management and evidence-based guideline development.
cip_definition: Research focused on the laboratory and analytical procedures for studying all facets of hematologic and coagulation disorders. May included related research in the management of hematology laboratories.

abstract: The integration of traditional Ayurvedic medicine with modern computational approaches presents a unique opportunity to elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying its holistic therapeutic strategies. A critical challenge lies in systematically analyzing the polypharmacological effects of Ayurvedic herbal formulations, which often involve complex multi-herb synergies poorly captured by reductionist models. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the network-level interactions between phytochemicals from classical Ayurvedic formulations and human proteomic targets, focusing on their potential to modulate inflammatory pathways implicated in chronic metabolic disorders. Using a combination of molecular docking, dynamic simulations, and machine learning, we will construct probabilistic interaction networks for 20 prioritized formulations documented in classical Sanskrit texts, incorporating data from phytochemical databases, structural proteomics, and transcriptomic repositories. The computational workflow will involve (1) virtual screening of >5,000 phytochemicals against 320 inflammation-related proteins, (2) all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to assess binding stability under physiological conditions, and (3) Bayesian network modeling to identify synergistic herb combinations. This approach addresses the technical bottleneck of evaluating combinatorial phytochemical interactions at scale—a task requiring petabytes of memory and parallelized GPU computing for feasible execution. Expected outcomes include the identification of conserved interaction patterns across formulations, validation of Ayurvedic synergy principles (such as *yukti* and *samyoga*), and predictive models for optimizing herb ratios in context-specific therapies. By establishing a computational framework to decode Ayurveda's systems-oriented pharmacodynamics, this research aims to bridge traditional knowledge with mechanistic biology, offering new paradigms for personalized, multi-target therapeutic development. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the combinatorial complexity of these analyses, which far exceeds the capacity of local institutional infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of Ayurveda, a holistic health care system based on the use of dietary, lifestyle, spiritual, pharmacological and physical therapies to remove imbalances and restore health as defined in Vedic and other classical Sanskrit authorities in the Indian tradition. Includes instruction in Sanskrit; history, philosophy, and principles of Ayurveda; Ayurvedic pharmacology; anatomy and physiology; internal medicine; herbology; diagnostic techniques; patient examination and communication; therapeutic modalities; detoxification theory and practice; mind and body behavior modification; Yoga; clinical pediatrics and gynecology; diet therapies; treatment of specific diseases; and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to characterize how intratumoral metabolic stress in solid malignancies drives cellular adaptation and therapeutic resistance, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model dynamic tumor microenvironment interactions. A critical barrier in oncology lies in understanding how spatially heterogeneous nutrient gradients, hypoxia, and acidosis in tumors reprogram cancer cell physiology to promote survival despite chemotherapy, radiation, or targeted therapies. Current experimental models struggle to resolve the multiscale feedback between tissue-scale resource distribution and single-cell metabolic decision-making. To address this, we propose a spatially explicit computational framework integrating physiological data on tumor metabolism, ion transport, and stress-response pathways. Agent-based models (ABMs) will simulate 3D tumor regions with varying glucose, oxygen, and proton concentrations, tracking individual cell states (proliferation, quiescence, apoptosis) influenced by local conditions and intercellular signaling. Differential equations will couple microenvironmental dynamics (e.g., lactate diffusion, pH buffering) to intracellular processes such as autophagy, mitochondrial plasticity, and proton pump activity. The HPC environment is essential for scaling simulations to biologically relevant tumor volumes (>10^6 cells) while resolving subcellular mechanisms. Models will be parameterized using in vitro data from nutrient-deprived cancer cell cultures and validated against murine xenograft histology. Expected outcomes include identifying metabolic dependencies that emerge under sustained stress, predicting microenvironmental niches most likely to harbor resistant cells, and testing computational interventions such as spatially fractionated radiation or pH-modulating drugs. This work will advance physiological oncology by mapping adaptive thresholds in cancer cell behavior, directly informing translational studies on microenvironment-targeted therapy combinations. The requested resources—parallelized simulations across 200+ cores and high-memory nodes for large-scale parameter optimization—are critical to achieving these aims.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of carcinogens; the onset of malignancy in cells, tissues, blood, and organs; the genetics of cancer; the anatomy and physiology of cancer cells; and the study of cancer behaviors and treatments. Includes instruction in gene expression; oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes; viral genes and cancer proliferation; regulation of signal transduction; cancer proteins; hormonal and growth factors in cancer cells; tumor promotion, progression, and metastasis; carcinogen receptors and metabolism; carcinogen ecology; immunological targeting; and studies of genetic, chemical, radiologic and other treatment therapies.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in computational linguistic research on American Sign Language (ASL) by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the spatial, kinematic, and grammatical complexity of ASL at scale. ASL’s visual-gestural modality presents unique challenges for large-scale linguistic analysis, as its phonology, morphology, and syntax are expressed through simultaneous combinations of handshapes, movements, facial expressions, and body postures. Existing tools for automated ASL processing remain limited in accuracy and scalability, particularly for modeling dynamic, multi-channel linguistic features in naturalistic signing. To bridge this gap, this project will employ GPU-accelerated deep learning architectures and 3D pose estimation algorithms to process high-resolution video corpora of ASL discourse, including historical and regional signing varieties. Computational workflows will be designed to extract and annotate kinematic trajectories, classify morphological constructions, and map syntactic dependencies across large datasets. Parallelized pipelines will enable the training of transformer-based models for sign recognition and generation, with attention mechanisms tailored to ASL’s simultaneity. The outcomes will include open-source tools for ASL transcription, a semantically tagged corpus of ASL narratives, and novel metrics for quantifying sociolinguistic variation in signing communities. By enabling fine-grained analysis of ASL’s motor-linguistic structures, this research will advance theoretical understanding of visual language typology while supporting practical applications in ASL education, digital archiving, and human-computer interaction technologies tailored to Deaf users. The scale of video data processing and model training required for robust ASL analysis necessitates HPC resources to manage memory-intensive computations, reduce runtime for iterative experiments, and facilitate reproducibility across diverse signing datasets.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on American Sign Language as a visual and motor medium of communication and discourse for deaf individuals and deaf culture. Includes instruction in the development of ASL, ASL morphology and syntax, signing technique, English translation of ASL, formal and colloquial ASL, and ASL transcription.

abstract: The dynamical evolution of planetary systems is governed by complex gravitational interactions that shape orbital architectures over billion-year timescales. However, current models struggle to reconcile observed exoplanet systems—many exhibiting tightly packed configurations, resonant chains, or high eccentricities—with formation theories. This project seeks to address this gap by performing high-resolution N-body simulations of planetary system evolution, incorporating both internal gravitational perturbations and external perturbations from stellar clusters. The research will utilize the REBOUND code with the IAS15 adaptive integrator to model systems with up to 20 interacting bodies across 1–100 Myr timescales. Key challenges include resolving close encounters, maintaining numerical stability during chaotic interactions, and statistically sampling parameter space for initial conditions consistent with protoplanetary disk models. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential due to the O(n²) scaling of gravitational calculations and the need for ensemble simulations across 10^4 parameter combinations. Each simulation requires ~500 GB of memory for phase-space tracking and ~8 hours on 256 cores for a 10 Myr integration. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of stability criteria for compact multi-planet systems, (2) quantification of stellar cluster tidal effects on planetary eccentricity distribution, and (3) publicly released simulation datasets for comparative exoplanet studies. Results will directly inform interpretation of JWST transit spectra and ESA’s PLATO mission data by linking present-day observations to formation histories. This work advances fundamental understanding of how gravitational physics shapes planetary systems, with applications to habitability studies and population synthesis models.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of planets, small objects, and related gravitational systems. Includes instruction in the structure and composition of planetary surfaces and interiors, planetary atmospheres, satellites, orbital mechanics, asteroids and comets, solar system evolution and dynamics, planetary evolution, gravitational physics, and radiation physics.

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in institutional foodservice operations by developing a computational framework to optimize dynamic decision-making in large-scale, multi-site foodservice systems. Current management practices rely on static models that inadequately account for real-time variables such as fluctuating nutritional demand, perishable inventory decay, staff scheduling constraints, and equipment utilization patterns. The proposed study will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to create a multi-agent simulation environment integrating discrete-event simulation, machine learning-based demand forecasting, and combinatorial optimization algorithms. The computational model will process heterogeneous datasets including historical meal consumption patterns, supply chain lead times, nutritional guidelines, and labor cost structures to generate adaptive management strategies. Key challenges involve parallelizing resource allocation algorithms across distributed kitchen nodes while maintaining synchronization with centralized procurement systems, as well as balancing competing objectives of waste reduction, cost containment, and nutritional compliance. The HPC infrastructure will enable scenario testing at institutional scales—simulating up to 500 concurrent service nodes with stochastic demand variations—while preserving the granularity required for menu-level optimization. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support tool capable of reducing food waste by 15-25% and labor costs by 10-18% in testbed hospital and university foodservice systems, as demonstrated through comparative analysis against traditional management approaches. The computational framework will also produce novel metrics for evaluating sustainability-performance tradeoffs in institutional food systems, contributing methodological advances to operational research in non-commercial foodservice management. By establishing scalable models for resource coordination in this understudied domain, the project aims to bridge critical gaps between operations research methodologies and applied foodservice administration challenges.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and practices relating to the administration of food service systems in institutional settings, and that prepares individuals to manage such operations in public and private facilities. Includes instruction in human nutrition, food safety, the design and organization of food service systems, purchasing, personnel management, and related business practices.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable numerical algorithms for solving high-dimensional partial differential equations (PDEs) arising in multiphysics systems, such as coupled fluid-structure interaction problems. Traditional discretization methods suffer from prohibitive computational costs and memory requirements when applied to such systems, particularly in three dimensions or with dynamic boundary conditions. The research problem centers on overcoming these limitations by designing hybrid tensor decomposition and adaptive sparse grid techniques optimized for modern high-performance computing (HPC) architectures. The proposed computational approach integrates low-rank tensor approximations with parallelizable multilevel iterative solvers to reduce the dimensionality of parameter spaces while preserving solution accuracy. Key innovations include the development of a distributed-memory framework for hierarchical tensor operations and the implementation of dynamic load-balancing strategies to address irregular computational workloads inherent to adaptive sparsity patterns. The project will validate these methods using benchmark problems from biomechanics and aerospace engineering, comparing results against conventional finite element solutions. Expected outcomes include a 40-60% reduction in memory usage and a 3-5x speedup for targeted problem classes, enabling simulations at scales previously impractical on existing systems. Successful implementation will provide an open-source software toolkit for the computational mathematics community, with direct applications in optimizing medical device design and turbulent flow analysis. The requested HPC resources—including GPU-accelerated nodes and high-bandwidth interconnects—are critical for testing weak and strong scaling properties of the algorithms up to 10^6 core-hours, as well as for managing the communication overhead of distributed tensor computations. This work bridges algorithmic innovation with practical engineering challenges, advancing the state of computational mathematics in data-sparse representations for complex physical systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of mathematics to the theory, architecture, and design of computers, computational techniques, and algorithms. Includes instruction in computer theory, cybernetics, numerical analysis, algorithm development, binary structures, combinatorics, advanced statistics, and related topics.

abstract: This project seeks to understand how rapid environmental change influences the stability of ecological networks and species coexistence mechanisms in biodiverse ecosystems. As anthropogenic disturbances and climate variability alter resource availability and species interactions, predicting community-level responses remains a critical challenge in environmental biology. We propose an integrative computational framework combining agent-based models (ABMs) of multi-trophic interactions with spatially explicit dynamic vegetation models (DVMs) to simulate ecosystem responses under projected climate scenarios. The ABMs will parameterize species-specific traits, including dispersal capacity, phenological shifts, and niche breadth, derived from empirical datasets spanning tropical and temperate forest inventories. DVMs will integrate regional climate projections (CMIP6) and soil hydrology data to simulate abiotic drivers at mesoscale resolutions (1–10 km²). High-performance computing resources are essential to resolve the stochastic, high-dimensional interactions inherent to these simulations, particularly for scaling individual-level processes to landscape-level patterns over decadal timeframes. The computational workflow will leverage parallelized Monte Carlo methods to assess variance in community resilience metrics across >10,000 parameter combinations, while machine learning algorithms (random forests, gradient-boosted regression trees) will identify key predictors of ecosystem collapse thresholds. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of biodiversity hotspots at elevated risk under IPCC warming scenarios, validated against long-term ecological monitoring data from established forest dynamics plots. By quantifying nonlinear feedbacks between species traits and environmental filters, this work will advance mechanistic understanding of extinction cascades while informing habitat corridor designs for climate-vulnerable taxa. The generated models and code will be optimized for open-source distribution, providing a transferable toolkit for conservation planning in understudied biodiverse regions.
detailed_field: Ecology, evolutionary biology, and epidemiology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the origins, functions, relationships, interactions, and natural history of living populations, communities, species, and ecosystems in relation to dynamic environmental processes. Includes instruction in biodiversity, molecular genetic and genomic evolution, mesoscale ecology, computational biology and modeling, conservation biology, local and global environmental change, and restoration ecology.

abstract: Clinical genetics faces a critical challenge in efficiently interpreting the growing volume of genomic data to diagnose rare genetic disorders accurately. While next-generation sequencing has enabled rapid identification of genetic variants, distinguishing pathogenic mutations from benign variants remains computationally intensive and time-consuming, particularly for underrepresented populations with limited reference datasets. This project seeks to address this bottleneck by developing a scalable, machine learning-driven framework to improve variant prioritization and clinical interpretation. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate multi-omics data—including whole-genome sequencing, transcriptomic profiles, and epigenomic annotations—from 50,000 patients with suspected genetic disorders, alongside publicly available datasets. Deep neural networks will be trained to predict variant pathogenicity using context-aware features such as tissue-specific gene expression, 3D chromatin structure, and evolutionary conservation patterns. Concurrently, population genetics simulations will model allele frequencies and linkage disequilibrium across diverse ancestries to reduce interpretation bias. The computational pipeline will utilize parallelized workflows for data preprocessing, distributed training of ensemble models, and large-scale hypothesis testing. Expected outcomes include a validated clinical decision-support tool that reduces diagnostic turnaround time by ≥40% in retrospective validation cohorts, novel insights into noncoding variants affecting regulatory elements in developmental disorders, and publicly shared benchmarking datasets to improve equity in genomic resources. This work will directly enhance the clinical utility of genomic testing, enabling personalized management strategies for patients with Mendelian diseases and complex structural variants. The requested HPC resources are essential to handle the petabyte-scale data storage, GPU-accelerated model training, and millions of simultaneous simulations required to achieve these aims.
cip_definition: Research on how to provide comprehensive diagnostic, management, and counseling services for individuals and families at risk for clinical disorders with a genetic basis.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and evaluate adaptive, AI-driven instructional media frameworks that dynamically personalize learning experiences for diverse student populations. A critical challenge in educational technology design lies in efficiently scaling personalized content delivery while maintaining real-time responsiveness to learner behaviors, cognitive states, and environmental contexts. Current approaches often rely on static, rule-based systems that struggle to accommodate the multidimensional variability inherent in educational settings. To address this, we propose a computational study leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train and deploy deep reinforcement learning models that optimize media delivery strategies across heterogeneous learner profiles. The research will utilize large-scale datasets of student interactions (e.g., eye-tracking, response times, and multimodal engagement signals) to simulate complex learning environments through parallelized agent-based modeling. Key computational tasks include 1) training transformer-based architectures to predict optimal media adaptations under constrained cognitive load thresholds, 2) running Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate design robustness across demographic and pedagogical variables, and 3) implementing real-time inference pipelines for prototype testing in virtual reality-based instructional scenarios. The HPC infrastructure is essential for managing the combinatorial explosion of design parameters (e.g., multimedia element sequencing, scaffolding timing, and feedback modalities) while maintaining millisecond-level latency requirements for immersive learning systems. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for computationally efficient media personalization, open-source tools for simulating educational design trade-offs, and evidence-based thresholds for adaptive system performance across devices. This work aims to advance the science of educational media design by establishing quantitative relationships between computational resource allocation, learner cognitive architectures, and pedagogical effectiveness in technology-enhanced environments.
detailed_field: Educational/ instructional technology and media design
cip_definition: A program that focuses on designing technology for educational curricula. Includes instruction in foundations of educational technology, design, computer applications, human-computer interaction, web-based instruction, distance education, and designing and producing educational software and materials.

abstract: Educating individuals with developmental delays requires tailored approaches that address heterogeneous learning needs. However, designing effective, individualized teaching strategies remains challenging due to the complex interplay of cognitive, social, and emotional factors influencing development. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multimodal educational data—including student performance metrics, behavioral observations, and physiological responses—to identify patterns predictive of optimal learning pathways. Machine learning models, including deep neural networks and ensemble methods, will be trained on longitudinal datasets encompassing diverse developmental profiles. These models will simulate the efficacy of various instructional interventions under different developmental scenarios, enabling the identification of strategies that maximize adaptive skill acquisition. Additionally, agent-based modeling will explore how dynamic classroom interactions influence outcomes for students with delays. The computational intensity of processing high-dimensional data and running parallel simulations necessitates HPC infrastructure to achieve timely results. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for personalizing education plans, decision-support tools for educators, and scalable training modules that integrate computational insights into teacher preparation programs. By bridging data-driven discovery with pedagogical practice, this research aims to advance evidence-based teaching methodologies, ultimately improving educational equity for developmentally delayed learners.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals Who are Developmentally Delayed
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults who exhibit slow social, physical, cognitive, or emotional growth patterns related to age, or a combination of such factors that affect learning, and that prepares individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identification of developmental delay patterns, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising developmentally delayed students, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: Medical education faces the challenge of efficiently training learners with diverse competencies while adapting curricula to evolving clinical guidelines, technological advancements, and heterogeneous educational outcomes. Traditional approaches to curriculum design and evaluation often rely on manual analysis of limited datasets, which may fail to capture complex interactions between pedagogical strategies, learner performance, and long-term clinical competency. This project proposes the development of a computational framework to model, simulate, and optimize medical education curricula using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The research will integrate multimodal datasets—including longitudinal student performance metrics, simulation-based assessments, faculty feedback, and clinical competency records—to identify patterns and predictors of educational success. Machine learning models, such as recurrent neural networks and ensemble methods, will be trained to forecast individual learner trajectories and evaluate the impact of curricular modifications. Agent-based simulations will model hypothetical educational interventions, enabling the exploration of emergent outcomes across diverse learner cohorts. Additionally, natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will analyze qualitative feedback from faculty and learners to refine curricular content dynamically. The computational demands of processing terabyte-scale educational datasets, parallelizing simulations across thousands of scenarios, and training deep learning models necessitate access to HPC infrastructure for memory-intensive tasks and GPU-accelerated computing. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to personalize learning pathways, evidence-based frameworks for iterative curriculum design, and scalable methods for evaluating educational interventions. By quantifying previously intangible aspects of medical pedagogy, this research aims to establish a paradigm for data-driven medical education that enhances clinical preparedness, reduces training disparities, and adapts dynamically to healthcare system needs. The resulting models and pipelines will be disseminated as open-source tools to support reproducibility and collaboration in health sciences education research.
cip_definition: Research on how to teach deliver, design, and evaluate courses and curricula for medical students, residents, and faculty.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing equitable access to digital learning resources in K-12 school libraries through data-driven collection development and personalized literacy support. School librarians face increasing demands to curate inclusive, curriculum-aligned digital collections while addressing diverse student needs, yet lack scalable tools to analyze usage patterns, identify resource gaps, or predict emerging demands. This research proposes developing a machine learning framework to process multi-modal data—including digital resource metadata, anonymized student interaction logs, and curricular standards—to model resource efficacy and recommend adaptive collection strategies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training neural networks on large-scale datasets spanning heterogeneous formats (e.g., eBook engagement metrics, database query trends, and multimedia usage analytics) while preserving privacy through federated learning techniques. Computational experiments will compare transformer-based architectures for cross-correlating resource usage with localized literacy outcomes, enabling dynamic prioritization of materials that support underrepresented learner populations. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for school librarians to simulate collection impacts, automate bias audits in digital catalogs, and generate evidence-based acquisition proposals. By integrating HPC-driven analytics into library workflows, this work aims to enhance the capacity of school library media specialists to align resources with pedagogical goals, reduce informational inequities, and demonstrate the strategic role of libraries in modern educational ecosystems. The project will further contribute novel methodologies for applying computational modeling to library science contexts, bridging gaps between information technology practices and practitioner needs in pre-service librarian education.
cip_title: School Librarian/ School Library Media Specialist
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to serve as librarians and media specialists in elementary and secondary schools as well as special instructional centers.

abstract: Higher education institutions face growing challenges in optimizing resource allocation amidst evolving enrollment patterns, financial constraints, and competing institutional priorities. Traditional decision-making frameworks often lack the capacity to model complex, dynamic interactions between academic, operational, and financial variables at scale. This project seeks to develop a computational modeling platform to simulate and evaluate resource allocation strategies across multi-campus university systems. Leveraging agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML), the research will analyze how decentralized budget decisions, faculty hiring policies, and infrastructure investments interact with student demand and institutional performance metrics. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to support large-scale simulations incorporating heterogeneous datasets—including historical enrollment records, budget archives, and facilities utilization metrics—across a network of anonymized partner institutions. The ABM framework will parameterize institutional actors (e.g., departments, administrative units) as autonomous agents operating under policy constraints, while ML techniques will identify latent patterns in cross-institutional outcomes. Expected outputs include predictive models to assess trade-offs between competing priorities (e.g., faculty workload equity vs. program expansion) and sensitivity analyses of funding allocation scenarios under demographic or economic shifts. By enabling real-time simulation of system-wide impacts from localized decisions, this work aims to advance data-driven leadership practices in higher education administration. The computational tools developed will provide actionable insights for administrators balancing strategic planning with operational sustainability, while contributing methodological innovations to the emerging field of computational organizational studies in academia. Successful validation against historical data from three public university systems will establish proof-of-concept for scaling the platform to broader institutional contexts.
detailed_field: Higher education and community college administration
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and practice of administration in four-year colleges, universities and higher education systems, the study of higher education as an object of applied research, and which may prepare individuals to function as administrators in such settings. Includes instruction in higher education economics and finance; policy and planning studies; curriculum; faculty and labor relations; higher education law; college student services; research on higher education; institutional research; marketing and promotion; and issues of evaluation, accountability and philosophy.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the interplay between social connectivity patterns and cognitive resilience in aging populations through an interdisciplinary lens integrating gerontology, computational social science, and network neuroscience. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how dynamic social behaviors—shaped by life course transitions, technological adoption, and sensory decline—modulate neurodegenerative risk profiles in older adults. While prior work has focused on static social metrics (e.g., marital status), we propose a novel computational framework to model time-varying, multilevel social interactions (in-person, digital, and community-based) and their bidirectional relationships with domain-specific cognitive trajectories. High-performance computing resources are essential to process multimodal longitudinal datasets—including geolocated activity traces, dyadic communication logs, and neuropsychological assessments from 5,000 participants in the AgingConnect Cohort—while accounting for individual differences in mobility, socioeconomic context, and sensory health. Agent-based models will simulate how age-related changes in social prioritization and communication capacity propagate through personal networks, with neural network architectures identifying nonlinear associations between interaction patterns and MRI-derived brain integrity markers. The computational pipeline requires parallelized processing of petabyte-scale temporal graph data and Monte Carlo simulations of intervention scenarios. Expected outcomes include: (1) a validated predictive model of social-cognitive interdependencies across the aging spectrum, (2) generative algorithms to optimize community-level support systems for neuroprotective social engagement, and (3) open-source tools for analyzing lifespan social dynamics at unprecedented spatiotemporal resolution. By bridging micro-scale behavioral data with macro-scale population aging trends, this work will establish computational gerontology as a distinct interdisciplinary domain, advancing both methodological innovation and translational strategies for dementia risk mitigation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the human aging process and aged human populations, using the knowledge and methodologies of the biological and health sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to develop computational frameworks to enhance the precision, sustainability, and artistic fidelity of taxidermy practices through advanced simulation, material modeling, and anatomical reconstruction. Traditional taxidermy relies heavily on manual techniques for specimen preparation, form construction, and finishing, which are time-intensive and subject to material degradation or anatomical inaccuracies. To address these challenges, this research proposes a hybrid computational-experimental approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model biological decomposition dynamics, simulate material interactions during preservation, and optimize three-dimensional form-building processes. Multi-physics simulations will quantify the effects of environmental variables (e.g., humidity, temperature) on tissue preservation, while finite element analysis will evaluate stress distribution in armature designs to improve structural longevity. Machine learning algorithms trained on 3D scans of vertebrate specimens will predict optimal sculptural parameters for species-specific mannequins, reducing trial-and-error in form construction. Additionally, molecular dynamics simulations will assess synthetic material compatibility with organic tissues to develop eco-friendly preservation alternatives. By integrating these computational workflows, the project aims to establish predictive tools for minimizing specimen waste, accelerating production timelines, and enhancing anatomical realism in taxidermy art. Outcomes will include open-access datasets of biomechanical models, a digital repository of optimized form templates, and protocols for computational-aided preservation—resources designed to support taxidermists in adapting to ecological, regulatory, and artistic demands. This interdisciplinary effort bridges computational science with artisanal craftsmanship, offering a novel paradigm for sustaining traditional practices through technological innovation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to reproduce life-like three-dimensional representations of living animals for permanent display using elements of the deceased specimen(s) as well as artificial materials, and to manage taxidermy services and businesses. Includes instruction in specimen grading and selection, caping and fleshing, preservation procedures, tanning, drying, measurements, form and armature construction, carpentry and woodworking, molding and casting, drawing, sculptural techniques, painting and finishing techniques, basic business operations, customer communications, and applicable laws and regulations.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the systemic risks posed by decentralized finance (DeFi) protocols to traditional cross-border financial systems, with a focus on liquidity dynamics and contagion pathways in multi-currency environments. The rapid growth of blockchain-based lending, staking, and automated market-making platforms has created complex interdependencies between decentralized and centralized financial systems, yet their collective impact on global monetary stability remains poorly quantified. Using high-frequency transactional data from both public blockchain ledgers and traditional forex markets, we propose to develop a multi-agent simulation framework that models liquidity flows, collateralization cascades, and arbitrage behaviors across these hybrid systems. The computational approach combines network theory, stochastic process modeling, and reinforcement learning algorithms to capture adaptive strategies of institutional and algorithmic actors under stress scenarios. High-performance computing resources are critical for maintaining temporal granularity in simulating minute-scale market interactions across 50+ fiat and cryptocurrency pairs while accounting for jurisdictional variations in settlement protocols and regulatory constraints. Expected outcomes include a risk topology mapping critical convergence points between DeFi and legacy systems, predictive metrics for liquidity shortfall propagation, and stress-testing frameworks adaptable to evolving digital asset regulations. By quantifying how decentralized protocols amplify or dampen systemic risks in international cash flow operations, this research aims to inform coordinated policy approaches for monitoring emerging financial technologies while maintaining global monetary stability. The resulting models will be validated against historical crisis analogs, including the 2022-2023 cryptocurrency market collapses, and shared via an open computational platform for central bank stress-testing collaborations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage international financial operations and related currency transactions. Includes instruction in international banking, international monetary and financial policy, money and capital markets, foreign exchange, risk analysis, and international cash flow operations.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the multiscale fluid-structure interactions governing pollen dispersal in heterogeneous environments, integrating principles from botany, aerodynamics, and environmental physics. Pollen grains, with their diverse morphologies and adaptive biomechanical properties, exhibit complex dispersal behaviors that influence ecosystem resilience, agricultural productivity, and airborne allergen distribution. However, predictive models remain limited by oversimplified representations of turbulence-pollen interactions across scales and an incomplete understanding of how microenvironmental variability (e.g., localized wind shear, humidity gradients) modulates dispersal efficiency. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC) framework coupling computational fluid dynamics (CFD) with discrete element modeling (DEM) to resolve pollen trajectories at unprecedented spatiotemporal resolution. The simulations will parameterize pollen geometries derived from micro-CT scans of 50 species, incorporating hygroscopic deformation dynamics and stochastic wind fields calibrated to LiDAR-measured canopy architectures. Multi-GPU parallelization will enable ensemble runs across parameter spaces encompassing realistic atmospheric boundary layers and climate perturbation scenarios. Validation will leverage field data from particle image velocimetry and pollen-trap networks across forest-grassland ecotones. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into morphology-mediated dispersal optimization, probabilistic maps of cross-pollination ranges under shifting precipitation regimes, and open-source tools for eco-evolutionary forecasting. By bridging microscale biophysics to landscape-scale ecological processes, this work will advance fundamental knowledge of plant adaptation while providing actionable data for biodiversity conservation and precision agriculture. The computational demands—iterative 3D Navier-Stokes solutions across billion-cell domains coupled to 10^6-particle DEM systems—necessitate allocation of 250,000 node-hours on a tier-1 HPC system, enabling transformative leaps in scale integration for environmental fluid dynamics.
cip_definition: A program with a combined or undifferentiated focus on one or more of the physical and biological sciences.

abstract: Allergic, asthmatic, and immunologic diseases exhibit complex molecular and cellular heterogeneity, complicating the development of personalized treatment strategies. Current clinical biomarkers often fail to predict disease progression or therapeutic response accurately, particularly in severe asthma and refractory atopic dermatitis. This project seeks to address this gap by integrating multi-omic patient data (genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and clinical datasets) to identify predictive signatures of treatment response and disease endotypes. The computational demands of this work require high-performance computing (HPC) resources to manage large-scale data processing, advanced machine learning workflows, and dynamic simulations of immune signaling networks. We propose a three-phase approach: (1) processing raw sequencing data from single-cell RNA-seq and TCR repertoire profiling of patient-derived samples to map immune cell states; (2) training ensemble machine learning models on integrated multi-omic datasets to predict corticosteroid and biologic therapy responses; and (3) simulating intercellular communication networks using agent-based modeling to identify critical regulatory nodes in type 2 inflammation. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid alignment of terabyte-scale sequencing files, parallelized hyperparameter optimization for predictive models, and stochastic simulations of immune cell interactions across biologically relevant timescales. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel composite biomarkers for therapy selection, mechanistic insights into resistance pathways in interleukin-targeted treatments, and a publicly accessible computational framework for simulating patient-specific immune responses. This work directly addresses the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases priority of advancing precision medicine in allergic diseases by bridging clinical observations with systems immunology. The requested resources will accelerate analyses that are currently prohibitive on local clusters, reducing project timelines from months to weeks while improving model robustness through large-scale validation. Findings will inform ongoing clinical trials and guide the development of adaptive treatment algorithms for heterogeneous patient populations.
cip_definition: Research focused on the delivery of skilled medical care to patients suffering from allergic, asthmatic, and immunologic diseases. Requires completion of a prior residency program in internal medicine or pediatrics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity simulation framework for optimizing the control and dynamic behavior of autonomous robotic systems operating in unstructured environments. A critical challenge in mechatronics and automation lies in designing robots that can adaptively respond to real-world uncertainties—such as variable terrain, dynamic obstacles, and sensor noise—while maintaining energy efficiency and operational safety. Traditional control strategies and physics-based models often fail to capture the nonlinear interactions between electromechanical components, environmental forces, and embedded decision-making algorithms, limiting system reliability. To address this, we propose a multi-physics computational approach integrating rigid-body dynamics, soft-body deformation modeling, and data-driven reinforcement learning (RL) to co-optimize mechanical design parameters and control policies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the computational complexity of simulating distributed sensor-actuator networks, training deep RL agents in parallelized virtual environments, and solving coupled mechanical-electrical-thermal systems at millisecond timescales. The proposed workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated finite element analysis for structural integrity prediction, MPI-based distributed computing for multi-agent collaboration scenarios, and containerized workflows to streamline heterogeneous simulations. Expected outcomes include a scalable digital twin platform for rapid prototyping of adaptive robotic systems, validated against experimental data from a quadrupedal inspection robot case study. This work will advance the integration of computational mechanics and machine learning in mechatronics, enabling next-generation robots with enhanced autonomy in industrial maintenance and disaster response applications. The requested resources will directly support large-scale parameter sweeps, sensitivity analyses, and validation of probabilistic control frameworks, which are infeasible on local computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of computer controlled electro-mechanical systems and products with embedded electronics, sensors, and actuators; and which includes, but is not limited to, automata, robots and automation systems. Includes instruction in mechanical engineering, electronic and electrical engineering, computer and software engineering, and control engineering.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern statistical datasets, characterized by high dimensionality, heterogeneous structures, and intricate dependencies, demands advanced computational methods to enable robust inference. This project seeks to develop and implement scalable Bayesian hierarchical models for spatial-temporal data with non-Gaussian response variables, a class of problems where traditional estimation techniques become computationally prohibitive due to high parameter dimensionality and non-conjugate likelihoods. The core challenge lies in efficiently sampling from high-dimensional posterior distributions while maintaining theoretical guarantees on mixing rates and convergence. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework combining adaptive Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) with structured variational approximations, leveraging parallel tempering strategies to escape local posterior modes. The implementation will utilize GPU-accelerated gradient computations for HMC and distributed memory parallelism via MPI to scale Markov chain transitions across nodes. A key innovation involves dynamically partitioning spatial-temporal random effects using graph-based clustering algorithms to optimize load balancing during distributed inference. The computational workflow will be validated on synthetic datasets with known ground truth and applied to a multi-terabyte epidemiological dataset tracking disease incidence across 10,000+ geographic units over a 20-year period, incorporating covariates from disparate sources (satellite imagery, electronic health records). Successful implementation will yield (1) open-source software for large-scale hierarchical modeling, (2) quantitative benchmarks comparing computational-accuracy tradeoffs across architectures, and (3) novel epidemiological insights into spatiotemporal risk factors for disease transmission. The requested high-performance computing resources are critical for testing algorithmic scalability beyond 1,000 nodes and processing raw input data through GPU-optimized preprocessing pipelines. This work directly advances statistical methodology for complex modern datasets while providing a computational blueprint for integrating Bayesian nonparametrics with exascale computing architectures.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in statistics, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development and validation of computational models for predicting treatment outcomes in patients with complex psychological disorders, particularly treatment-resistant depression (TRD) and schizophrenia-spectrum conditions. A critical challenge in clinical psychology is the heterogeneity of symptom presentation and variability in treatment response, which limits the efficacy of standardized therapeutic protocols. To address this, we propose integrating multimodal datasets—including neuroimaging (fMRI, structural MRI), electronic health records, genetic markers, and longitudinal behavioral data—into machine learning frameworks to identify patient-specific biopsychosocial predictors of intervention success. The computational pipeline will involve preprocessing large-scale neuroimaging data using containerized workflows (e.g., FSL, FreeSurfer), followed by feature extraction and dimensionality reduction techniques optimized for high-dimensional clinical data. Deep learning models (e.g., graph neural networks, transformer-based architectures) will be trained to map dynamic interactions between neural circuitry, cognitive profiles, and symptom trajectories across time. HPC resources are essential due to the computational demands of processing terabytes of neuroimaging data, parallelizing model training across thousands of hyperparameter combinations, and conducting permutation-based significance testing to ensure robustness. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive models of optimal therapeutic interventions (e.g., cognitive-behavioral therapy vs. pharmacotherapy) for individual patients, (2) mechanistic insights into neuroplasticity biomarkers associated with symptom remission, and (3) open-source tools for reproducible clinical decision support. By bridging computational psychiatry and clinical practice, this work aims to establish a framework for personalized intervention strategies, directly addressing the NIH’s emphasis on precision mental health. The requested resources will enable scaling to multi-site cohorts (N > 5,000) while maintaining compliance with HIPAA-safe computational environments for sensitive patient data.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of clinical psychology, involving the analysis, diagnosis, and clinical treatment of psychological disorders and behavioral pathologies. Includes instruction in clinical assessment and diagnosis, personality appraisal, psychopathology, clinical psychopharmacology, behavior modification, therapeutic intervention skills, patient interviewing, personalized and group therapy, child and adolescent therapy, cognitive and behavioral therapy, supervised clinical practice, ethical standards, and applicable regulations.

abstract: The molecular machinery underlying energy transduction in biological systems relies on precise, dynamic interactions among macromolecules and supramolecular assemblies. Despite advances in structural biology, the mechanistic principles governing transient conformational states, allosteric communication, and energy transfer pathways in large biomolecular complexes remain poorly resolved. This project seeks to address this gap by integrating multiscale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical (QM/MM) methods to characterize energy transduction mechanisms in two model systems: (1) the rotary dynamics of ATP synthase under varying proton motive force conditions and (2) exciton transfer pathways in light-harvesting complexes under physiological membrane environments. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to perform millisecond-scale classical MD simulations of these megadalton systems, enhanced sampling via metadynamics to map free energy landscapes, and hybrid QM/MM calculations to model electronic transitions. The proposed computational framework will employ GPU-accelerated molecular dynamics (using AMBER and GROMACS) combined with density functional tight-binding (DFTB) methods optimized for biomolecular systems. Key deliverables include atomistic models of mechanochemical coupling in ATP synthase, predictive maps of protonation-dependent conformational shifts, and dynamic profiles of exciton delocalization in disordered antenna proteins. These results will advance fundamental understanding of biological energy conversion efficiency and provide testable hypotheses for experimental validation. By resolving transient interaction networks and energy transfer bottlenecks, the work has broader implications for engineering bioinspired energy materials and targeting allosteric sites in metabolic disease. The requested HPC allocation will enable statistically robust sampling of ultrastructural dynamics at biologically relevant timescales, overcoming current limitations in system size and simulation duration that hinder conventional computing infrastructures.
cip_definition: A scientific program that focuses on the dynamics and interactions of macromolecules and other three-dimensional ultrastructures, the architecture of supramolecular structures, and energy transfer in biomolecular systems. Includes instruction in energy transduction, structural dynamics, mechanisms of electron and proton transfer in biological systems, bioinformatics, automated analysis, and specialized research techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the dynamics of real-time sports communication across digital media platforms, addressing the challenge of processing and interpreting large-scale, unstructured data generated during live sporting events. The proliferation of social media, streaming platforms, and audience interaction tools has created vast datasets encompassing text, audio, video, and engagement metrics, which traditional computational methods struggle to process efficiently. This research aims to develop a computational framework for modeling audience sentiment, content virality, and media strategy effectiveness during live events. Using natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision techniques, the project will analyze multilingual social media posts, live commentary transcripts, and broadcast video feeds to identify patterns in audience engagement, bias in sports reporting, and the impact of real-time content delivery on public perception. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of terabytes of data, training machine learning models to detect emergent themes, emotional tone, and demographic-specific reactions. Additionally, agent-based simulations will model how information spreads through fan networks, testing hypotheses about the role of influencer endorsements, crisis communication tactics, and algorithmic content prioritization. Outcomes will include open-source tools for sports journalists and communication professionals to optimize real-time reporting, audience interaction, and brand management. The project will also produce novel datasets annotating the relationship between media framing (e.g., race, gender, or nationality in athlete coverage) and audience response patterns. By bridging computational methods with communication theory, this work advances scholarly understanding of digital sports media ecosystems while providing practical resources for ethical, data-driven decision-making in sports journalism and public relations.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the methods and techniques for communicating about sports in a variety of formats, media, and contexts; and that prepares individuals to be sports reporters and writers, photojournalists, radio and television announcers, producers and directors, recreational sports promoters, and public relations specialists. Includes instruction in sports writing, photography, broadcast journalism, sports production, game rules, media and public relations, and sports promotion.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development and application of multiscale quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical (QM/MM) methods for modeling complex chemical reactions in biological and condensed-phase systems. A critical challenge in theoretical chemistry lies in accurately simulating reactive pathways in large, heterogeneous environments—such as enzyme active sites or solvated interfaces—where traditional quantum chemical methods are computationally prohibitive, and classical force fields lack the precision to capture bond-breaking/forming processes. To address this, we propose a hybrid computational framework integrating highly parallelized ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations with machine learning-accelerated free-energy sampling. The QM region will employ density functional theory (DFT) with advanced exchange-correlation functionals to model electronic rearrangements during catalysis, while the MM environment will utilize polarizable force fields parameterized via neural network potentials trained on high-level coupled-cluster data. Key targets include elucidating proton-coupled electron transfer mechanisms in metalloenzymes and predicting solvent reorganization effects on reaction barriers in aqueous organic systems. These simulations demand significant HPC resources due to the need for extensive configurational sampling, large-scale parallelization of electronic structure calculations, and iterative training of machine learning models on terabytes of trajectory data. Expected outcomes include validated protocols for balancing accuracy and efficiency in multiscale simulations, atomistic insights into experimentally observed kinetic isotope effects in biocatalysis, and open-source software tools for automating QM/MM workflow management on distributed-memory architectures. The results will directly inform experimental efforts in enzyme engineering and sustainable catalyst design, bridging gaps between theoretical predictions and empirical observations in reactive chemistry.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of mathematical and computational methods and fundamental laws of physics to describe chemical phenomena and to develop empirical models of molecules and their interactions. Includes instruction in properties of small, isolated molecules; dynamics of elementary chemical processes; reaction pathways of organic molecules; hydrogen bonding patterns in liquids; reaction rates of biological pathways; and advanced computational techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to advance Spanish language teacher education by developing computational models to analyze and predict second language (L2) learner errors in real-world classroom contexts. Spanish instructors face challenges in efficiently diagnosing learner difficulties across diverse cohorts, particularly in morphosyntactic and lexical domains, due to the dynamic and variable nature of interlanguage development. Current error analysis methods remain labor-intensive and lack scalability, limiting opportunities for personalized feedback. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) models on a multi-institutional corpus of Spanish learner writing and speech transcripts (∼5 TB), annotated for error types, proficiency levels, and corrective feedback outcomes. The computational approach will involve 1) pre-training multilingual language models on pedagogical Spanish corpora, 2) fine-tuning models for error detection and classification using curriculum-aligned learner data, and 3) implementing temporal modeling to track error patterns across instructional units. GPU-accelerated workflows will enable rapid iteration of ensemble architectures combining attention mechanisms with task-specific embeddings. Expected outcomes include an open-source diagnostic toolkit that assists teachers in identifying persistent error clusters, predicting developmental bottlenecks, and generating adaptive practice materials. By quantifying patterns in error distributions across proficiency levels and instructional contexts, this work aims to bridge computational linguistics with evidence-based pedagogy. The requested HPC resources are critical for processing heterogeneous linguistic data at scale, enabling low-latency inference for classroom applications, and advancing research on AI-assisted language teacher training frameworks. Results will be disseminated through teacher education workshops and a public repository of annotated learner datasets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach Spanish language programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a predictive analytics framework for optimizing wholesale promotional campaigns in fashion merchandising. The core challenge lies in the dynamic interplay between rapidly shifting consumer trends, fragmented retailer preferences, and supply chain constraints, which traditional campaign planning tools struggle to model in real time. Current approaches often rely on static historical data or siloed metrics, leading to inefficient resource allocation and missed opportunities in securing wholesale contracts. This project addresses this gap by integrating real-time social media sentiment analysis, geospatial demand forecasting, and multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) to simulate retailer decision-making processes under variable market conditions. The computational workflow will process terabyte-scale datasets encompassing historical purchase orders, influencer engagement metrics, and macroeconomic indicators, while MARL agents will emulate negotiation behaviors across diverse retail buyer personas. Key technical hurdles include scaling graph neural networks to model trend diffusion across regional markets and optimizing hyperparameter tuning for heterogeneous data streams. Expected outcomes include a decision-support system capable of recommending adaptive promotional strategies with quantified risk-reward profiles, potentially reducing overstock costs by 12–18% in simulated scenarios. The research will also contribute methodological advances in translating subjective fashion aesthetics into computable feature vectors for trend prediction algorithms. By aligning computational scalability with the temporal pressures of fashion cycles, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven wholesale merchandising, bridging gaps between computational social science, supply chain informatics, and aesthetic analytics. Successful implementation requires HPC capabilities for parallelized Monte Carlo simulations of seasonal campaigns and GPU-accelerated training of ensemble prediction models across 6–8 concurrent market scenarios.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to promote product lines/brands, and organize promotional campaigns, at the wholesale level to attract retailer interest, wholesale purchasing, and supply contracts. Includes instruction in wholesaling, wholesale advertising, selling, and customer relations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model the neurophysiological and biomechanical effects of yoga-based interventions, with the goal of optimizing therapeutic protocols for chronic pain and stress-related disorders. Despite growing evidence of yoga’s clinical benefits, the lack of mechanistic, individualized models limits its integration into precision health paradigms. Current approaches rely on generalized cohort studies, overlooking inter-subject variability in anatomy, neural plasticity, and stress response dynamics. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate multi-scale interactions between yoga practices (e.g., asana sequences, pranayama techniques) and physiological systems. The research integrates three computational strands: (1) biophysical modeling of musculoskeletal stress distribution during posture transitions using finite element analysis; (2) dynamic network modeling of autonomic nervous system modulation via heart rate variability and EEG data from wearable sensors; and (3) machine learning-driven optimization of personalized yoga therapy sequences based on individual biomarkers and comorbidities. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps across anatomically diverse digital twins and real-time analysis of high-density physiological datasets. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive framework for mapping yoga interventions to patient-specific neurobiomechanical profiles, with applications in chronic low back pain, anxiety disorders, and post-stroke rehabilitation. The project bridges gaps between traditional yogic knowledge systems and computational health sciences, offering a novel paradigm for non-pharmacological therapy design. Results will be disseminated through open-source tools for clinicians and yoga therapists, alongside computational datasets correlating yogic parameters (e.g., breath-to-movement ratios, postural alignment thresholds) with quantifiable health outcomes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to function as professional instructors in the spiritual and physical therapy of Yoga in private, institutional, and clinical settings. Includes instruction in the principles of Ayurveda, philosophy of Yoga, warm-up and progressive exercises, breathing exercises, meditation, Yamas and Niyamas, instructional techniques, posture adjustment, student/client counseling and assessment, advanced Yoga disciplines and styles, business practices, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamic evolution of family systems under sociocultural stressors, using a novel computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) and network theory. Family systems, as adaptive social units, are increasingly strained by global challenges such as migration, economic instability, and shifting caregiving norms. However, existing research lacks scalable tools to simulate longitudinal family interactions or quantify systemic resilience across diverse cultural contexts. The proposed work addresses this gap by developing a modular ABM platform that simulates multigenerational family decision-making processes, relational hierarchies, and resource-sharing behaviors under variable stressor scenarios. The model incorporates empirical data from ethnographic studies, demographic surveys, and psychological assessments to parameterize agents with culturally informed values, roles, and adaptive strategies.
