Computational challenges include resolving real-time feedback loops between individual agency and collective family norms, managing stochastic event chains (e.g., health crises, employment shifts), and analyzing emergent stability thresholds in high-dimensional parameter spaces. HPC resources are critical for conducting parallelized sensitivity analyses across 10,000+ simulated family-years, optimizing model fidelity through genetic algorithms, and processing temporally layered network data via graph neural networks. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated open-source toolkit for simulating culturally contextualized family systems, (2) quantitative metrics for predicting systemic vulnerability to specific stressors, and (3) evidence-based insights into intervention timing and kinship network mobilization strategies. By bridging computational social science with family systems theory, this work aims to provide policymakers and clinical practitioners with predictive models to support proactive, culturally attuned approaches to family welfare in rapidly changing societies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the family as a social unit in its developmental, dynamic, comparative, and structural aspects, and the significance of the family as a system that impacts individuals and society. Includes instruction in related principles of sociology, psychology, behavioral sciences, and the humanities.

abstract: The increasing demand for real-time, high-accuracy transcription and captioning services in dynamic media environments presents critical challenges for voice writing technologies, particularly in handling overlapping speech, diverse accents, and background noise. Current systems often struggle with latency and precision under these conditions, limiting their utility in live journalism, broadcasting, and inclusive communication contexts. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing advanced machine learning (ML) models optimized for real-time speech-to-text conversion and context-aware captioning. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we propose to train and fine-tune transformer-based architectures on large-scale multilingual speech datasets, including simulated environments with variable acoustic interference. Computational workflows will integrate parallelized training of neural networks for acoustic modeling, coupled with natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to enhance contextual disambiguation and domain-specific terminology handling (e.g., legal, medical, or technical jargon common in media transcription). Additionally, HPC-enabled simulations will model real-time captioning scenarios to optimize latency-performance tradeoffs. The expected outcomes include a robust open-source framework for adaptive voice writing systems capable of sub-second processing times with >95% accuracy in noisy settings, as validated against industry-standard benchmarks. This work will directly benefit communication professionals by improving accessibility in live events and media production while advancing computational linguistics methodologies for non-science domains. The requested resources are essential for processing terabytes of audio data and iterating complex models impractical on local infrastructure, ensuring scalability and practical deployment readiness.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to use voice writing computer software and speak a verbal shorthand language to create transcripts and screen captioning of live or recorded events intended for the public or a specific audience in a variety of media (e.g., digital, film, print, television) as well as for conferences, conversations, interviews, and meetings. Includes instruction in screen captioning, speed building, spoken shorthand, transcription, and voice input writing.

abstract: Current educational systems face challenges in ensuring equitable access to linguistically appropriate learning materials, particularly in multilingual and underserved regions. This project seeks to address the gap in understanding how linguistic complexity within curricular texts influences student comprehension and educational outcomes. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques to analyze a corpus of over 10 million pages of educational materials across 50 languages, assessing syntactic structures, lexical diversity, and readability metrics. Concurrently, we will integrate longitudinal student performance data from international assessments to model relationships between text complexity and learning efficacy. Computational challenges include parallel processing of large-scale text datasets, training multilingual transformer models for complexity classification, and running mixed-effects regression analyses to account for socio-contextual variables. The expected outcomes include a scalable framework for evaluating linguistic accessibility, evidence-based guidelines for curriculum design, and policy recommendations to mitigate disparities in material availability. By bridging computational linguistics and educational equity, this research aims to provide actionable insights for global educational stakeholders, fostering inclusive pedagogical practices and informing resource allocation strategies in diverse linguistic landscapes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general theory, practice, organization of, and public policies in education. Includes instruction in learning and teaching, the basic principles of educational psychology, the art of teaching, the planning and administration of educational activities, school safety and health issues, and the social foundations of education.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the growing need for sustainable and scalable practices in traditional printmaking by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model and optimize material interactions, ink dynamics, and substrate behavior. While printmaking techniques such as lithography, intaglio, and relief printing offer rich artistic possibilities, their reliance on physical trial-and-error processes often results in significant material waste, inconsistent outputs, and environmental concerns. Current computational tools lack the resolution to simulate the complex, nonlinear interactions between inks, solvents, and porous matrices at the scales required for practical artistic application. This project proposes a computational framework integrating fluid dynamics simulations, machine learning (ML)-driven predictive modeling, and multi-scale substrate analysis to digitally prototype printmaking processes. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to model ink viscosity, absorption rates, and drying dynamics across diverse materials (e.g., handmade paper, metal plates, fabric) under variable environmental conditions. Concurrently, generative adversarial networks (GANs) will be trained on high-resolution scans of historical and experimental prints to predict aesthetic outcomes—such as tonal gradients or texture fidelity—based on simulated parameters. The computational pipeline will be validated through iterative collaboration with printmakers, comparing physical prints against model predictions to refine accuracy. Anticipated outcomes include a reduction in material waste by 40–60% during the experimental phase of print development, the identification of novel solvent-substrate combinations for eco-friendly practices, and a publicly accessible database correlating simulation data with visual results. By bridging computational innovation and tactile artistry, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for resource-efficient printmaking while preserving the technical nuance and expressive potential central to the discipline.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions by rendering art concepts onto surfaces and transferring images, via ink or dyes, onto paper or fabric. Includes instruction in monochrome and color printing; tonality; chemistry; equipment set-up and maintenance; techniques such as serigraphy, lithography, intaglio, woodcut, block, stencil, relief, etching, and composite; and personal style development.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize resource allocation and environmental conditions in commercial plant nurseries, addressing the challenge of balancing productivity, cost efficiency, and plant health in dynamic operational settings. Nursery operations face complex interdependencies between irrigation schedules, nutrient delivery, light exposure, and climate control, which are typically managed via generalized protocols rather than data-driven strategies. Current trial-and-error approaches lead to suboptimal resource use, inconsistent plant quality, and elevated operational costs. To address this, we propose integrating high-performance computing (HPC) with multi-scale models simulating plant physiological responses, substrate dynamics, and microenvironmental variability. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on heterogeneous datasets, including hyperspectral imaging of plant stress, real-time sensor networks monitoring soil and air conditions, and historical growth performance records from partner nurseries. Parallelized simulations will evaluate millions of parameter combinations to identify optimal irrigation-fertilization-light regimens for diverse species and developmental stages. Sensitivity analyses will quantify the impact of genetic variability, seasonal weather shifts, and labor constraints on nursery output. The computational pipeline will leverage GPU acceleration for image-based phenotyping and containerized workflows to ensure scalability across nursery sizes. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool recommending real-time adjustments to nursery operations, reducing water and fertilizer waste by an estimated 20–35% while improving seedling uniformity. The models will also advance fundamental understanding of plant-environment interactions under controlled nursery conditions, with potential applications in crop breeding and precision agriculture. By transitioning nursery management from heuristic practices to predictive analytics, this work aims to strengthen the economic and environmental sustainability of horticultural industries.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to operate and manage outdoor plant farms, tree and shrub nurseries, and related facilities that develop domesticated plant products for propagation, harvesting, and transplantation. Includes instruction in applicable principles of plant science, farm and business management, nursery operations, equipment operation and maintenance, safety procedures, and personnel supervision.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing demand for advanced computational tools in optimizing real-time broadcast production workflows, particularly for live events requiring high-resolution video, multi-channel audio processing, and adaptive streaming across heterogeneous networks. As 4K/8K broadcasting and immersive audio formats become industry standards, traditional production systems face challenges in synchronizing resource-intensive tasks—such as dynamic color grading, AI-driven noise reduction, and latency-sensitive encoder optimization—without compromising output quality. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model parallel processing workflows for live production environments, simulating camera arrays, audio mixing consoles, and IP-based transmission systems under variable load conditions. Using containerized microservices architecture, we will test GPU-accelerated rendering pipelines for real-time visual effects and machine learning models trained on broadcast-specific datasets to predict bandwidth allocation needs during peak traffic. A key innovation involves developing hybrid CPU/GPU task scheduling algorithms tailored to broadcast engineering constraints, including failover redundancy and frame-accurate synchronization. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for benchmarking production system performance under simulated network stressors and actionable data to optimize hardware-software configurations for emerging formats like HDR-10+ and MPEG-H 3D Audio. This work will directly benefit educational programs training future broadcast engineers by providing case studies on computational resource allocation in modern studio environments while offering industry partners scalable models for transitioning to software-defined production infrastructures. The requested computing resources will enable large-scale simulations of multi-camera live events, which are otherwise infeasible to test in academic lab settings due to hardware costs and operational complexity.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the production of radio and television programs, and related operations, under the supervision of broadcast and studio managers, directors, editors, and producers. Includes instruction in sound, lighting, and camera operation and maintenance; power and feed control; studio operations; production preparation; broadcast engineering; related computer applications; and specialized applications such as news, entertainment, live talk, sports, commercials, and taping.

abstract: This research project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing real-time decision-making architectures for businesses operating in hyper-volatile markets, where traditional management information systems (MIS) struggle to balance computational efficiency, predictive accuracy, and interpretability. The core problem lies in the inability of conventional rule-based or single-model machine learning (ML) systems to adaptively process streaming multi-modal data—including text, sensor inputs, and transactional records—while maintaining audit trails required for regulatory compliance. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a heterogeneous ensemble learning framework that dynamically allocates computational resources to specialized submodels based on real-time feature importance and uncertainty quantification. The computational approach combines graph neural networks for cross-modal relationship extraction, lightweight online learning algorithms for rapid adaptation, and Monte Carlo dropout techniques for confidence estimation. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for both training base models on historical datasets (spanning terabyte-scale financial, logistics, and social media data) and simulating market shock scenarios through agent-based modeling. Expected outcomes include: 1) A resource-aware scheduling algorithm that optimizes model ensemble composition under strict latency constraints, 2) Quantitative benchmarks comparing energy efficiency and prediction quality across CPU/GPU hybrid architectures, and 3) Open-source tools for deploying adaptive ML pipelines within existing MIS infrastructures. This work advances the integration of edge computing paradigms with enterprise information systems, particularly for applications in algorithmic trading, emergency supply chain management, and dynamic pricing—domains where subsecond decision cycles intersect with complex business logic. The computational artifacts will enable organizations to validate the cost-benefit tradeoffs of AI-enhanced MIS architectures before large-scale implementation.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to provide and manage data systems and related facilities for processing and retrieving internal business information; select systems and train personnel; and respond to external data requests. Includes instruction in cost and accounting information systems, management control systems, personnel information systems, data storage and security, business systems networking, report preparation, computer facilities and equipment operation and maintenance, operator supervision and training, and management information systems policy and planning.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an interactive, computationally intensive multimedia installation that explores the dynamic interplay between generative algorithms, real-time audience input, and high-fidelity visual synthesis. The research addresses the challenge of creating immersive, adaptive artworks that respond fluidly to participant interactions while maintaining complex aesthetic coherence across multiple sensory channels. Current tools for real-time generative art struggle to balance computational efficiency with nuanced artistic control, particularly when scaling to high-resolution outputs or integrating heterogeneous data streams from motion capture, biometric sensors, and environmental inputs. We propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement parallelized rendering pipelines and machine learning models that enable unprecedented scale and responsiveness in interactive media systems. The computational approach combines CUDA-accelerated particle simulations, neural style transfer networks trained on custom art-historical datasets, and distributed processing architectures for low-latency sensor data integration. This infrastructure will support experimental frameworks where audience movements and physiological signals directly influence evolving 3D environments through non-linear mapping systems. Expected outcomes include both technical innovations in GPU-optimized creative coding workflows and new theoretical insights into human-computer co-creativity within immersive art contexts. The project will produce a publicly exhibited installation demonstrating these capabilities, alongside open-source tools for parameterized hybrid rendering techniques. By pushing the boundaries of real-time multimedia computation, this work aims to establish novel methodologies for complex system design in computational art while contributing reusable HPC strategies for the interdisciplinary media research community. Resource requirements focus on multi-GPU nodes for training domain-adapted generative models and high-memory instances for managing large-scale asset databases containing procedurally generated 3D meshes and texture arrays.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals creatively and technically to express emotions, ideas, or inner visions in either two or three dimensions, through simultaneous use of a variety of materials and media.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of modeling and mitigating the impacts of climate change and urban development on historic structures and landscapes through advanced computational methods. Historic preservation planning requires balancing complex variables—such as environmental stressors, material degradation, land-use policies, and economic feasibility—yet existing tools often lack the capacity to integrate multidisciplinary data at scales necessary for regional or city-wide conservation strategies. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-resolution simulation framework that combines geospatial analysis, machine learning, and agent-based modeling (ABM) to predict preservation outcomes under diverse scenarios. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable the processing of large-scale datasets, including 3D LiDAR scans of historic districts, climate projections, and socioeconomic indicators, to train predictive models assessing material decay rates and adaptive reuse viability. Concurrently, ABM will simulate stakeholder decision-making processes (e.g., developers, municipalities, conservationists) to evaluate how policy interventions and economic incentives influence preservation efforts. By coupling these approaches, the framework will identify optimal conservation pathways that minimize cultural loss while accommodating growth. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolset for preservationists to visualize trade-offs between restoration costs, regulatory constraints, and climate resilience. This work will advance interdisciplinary methodologies in cultural resource management, offering scalable solutions to a critical gap in heritage conservation planning. The computational demands of parallelized environmental simulations, real-time stakeholder interaction modeling, and high-dimensional data integration necessitate access to HPC infrastructure to achieve project goals within feasible timeframes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and implementation of plans to restore and maintain historic buildings, districts, and landscapes in a way that balances conservation and preservation with commercial and development interests. Includes instruction in architectural history, building conservation, cultural resource management, economics, historical documentation and preservation, land-use and zoning codes, public policy, public relations, real estate law, and taxation.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance German language pedagogy through the development of a data-driven, computational framework to analyze and predict language acquisition patterns among learners. A critical challenge in German language teacher education is the lack of scalable, evidence-based tools to model learner errors, track proficiency progression, and customize instructional strategies for diverse classrooms. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train machine learning models on multimodal datasets, including written and spoken learner corpora, annotated error analyses, and longitudinal performance metrics from intermediate German courses. The computational workflow will integrate natural language processing (NLP) techniques to parse syntactic and morphological errors in student-generated texts, coupled with recurrent neural networks to identify temporal patterns in language development. Additionally, agent-based simulations will model classroom interactions under varying pedagogical conditions to optimize feedback mechanisms. The scale of data—encompassing over 10,000 student responses and 500 hours of speech samples—necessitates parallelized processing and GPU-accelerated model training, which are only feasible through HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source diagnostic toolkit for teachers to predict learner difficulties and adapt lesson plans dynamically, (2) empirically validated benchmarks for proficiency milestones in German grammar and vocabulary acquisition, and (3) a repository of simulated classroom scenarios to train educators in data-informed instructional decision-making. By bridging computational linguistics with language pedagogy, this research aims to equip German language teachers with scalable, adaptive resources grounded in cognitive and sociolinguistic principles, ultimately fostering more effective, individualized instruction in multilingual learning environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach German language programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of urban crime propagation through an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework, integrating high-resolution geospatial, socioeconomic, and behavioral data to simulate how micro-level interactions between individuals and environmental factors generate macro-level crime patterns. Traditional criminological models often struggle to capture the nonlinear, adaptive behaviors underlying crime diffusion due to reliance on static correlations or simplified assumptions. The research addresses this gap by developing a computationally intensive simulation environment that models heterogeneous agents (residents, offenders, law enforcement) operating within dynamically evolving urban landscapes. The ABM will incorporate real-time anonymized crime incident reports, census tract data, and public infrastructure records from three major metropolitan areas, processed through graph neural networks to identify latent spatial-temporal dependencies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for executing parallelized parameter sweeps across 10^4+ agent configurations, optimizing model calibration through evolutionary algorithms, and validating emergent patterns against historical crime wave trajectories. Expected outcomes include identifying threshold conditions for crime hotspot formation, quantifying the efficacy of patrol allocation strategies under resource constraints, and characterizing feedback loops between community trust and policing effectiveness. The simulations will enable virtual testing of intervention scenarios—such as targeted streetlight installation or community policing adaptations—to predict their systemic impacts before real-world implementation. By bridging complexity science with criminological theory, this work aims to establish a scalable computational platform for proactive crime prevention policymaking, directly addressing the National Institute of Justice’s priority of reducing algorithmic bias in predictive policing tools through transparent, mechanistic models. The requested resources will support 18 months of large-scale ensemble simulations, requiring 256-core parallel processing capabilities and 50 TB of distributed storage for parameter space exploration and sensitivity analyses.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of crime as a sociopathological phenomenon, the behavior of criminals, and the social institutions evolved to respond to crime. Includes instruction in the theory of crime, psychological and social bases of criminal behavior, social value systems and the theory of punishment, criminal law and criminal justice systems, penology, rehabilitation and recidivism, studies of specific types of crime, social attitudes and policy, and applications to specific issues in law enforcement administration and policy.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamic interplay between tumor heterogeneity and microenvironmental stressors in driving cancer progression and therapeutic resistance. Despite advances in understanding cancer biology, the physiological mechanisms by which spatially variable oxygen gradients, metabolic competition, and stromal cell interactions shape clonal evolution remain poorly resolved. Traditional in vitro or animal models struggle to capture the multiscale, nonlinear feedback between cellular behaviors and tissue-scale pathophysiology. To address this, we propose developing a spatially explicit, multiscale computational model integrating empirical data from patient-derived xenografts and clinical imaging. The model will simulate tumor growth under physiologically realistic constraints, coupling agent-based representations of cancer cell decision-making (proliferation, migration, apoptosis) with continuum-based nutrient transport equations. Stochastic parameter sampling will explore how variations in hypoxia response pathways, substrate utilization efficiency, and fibroblast-mediated extracellular matrix remodeling influence regional clonal dominance and metastatic potential. HPC resources are essential to manage the combinatorial parameter space (>10^6 simulations), resolve high-resolution 3D tissue geometries, and perform ensemble-based sensitivity analyses. Expected outcomes include identifying microenvironmental tipping points that accelerate aggressive phenotypic transitions, mapping spatial predictors of drug resistance, and validating model predictions against longitudinal histopathology datasets. This work will advance mechanistic understanding of tumor adaptability under pathophysiological stress while providing a computational framework to prioritize combination therapies targeting both cell-autonomous and microenvironmental vulnerabilities. The requested allocation will support GPU-accelerated simulations using OpenCL-based solvers, with data parallelism managed via Slurm workload manager on clustered nodes. Results will be disseminated through open-source model repositories and integrated into graduate pathophysiology curricula.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the mechanisms underlying human disease. Includes instruction in the causes and nature of disease processes in animals and humans at the molecular, cellular, tissue, organ and organ systems level, tissue structure and function, cellular mechanisms of disease and organ systems response to disease.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of optimizing metadata generation and semantic enrichment for large-scale, heterogeneous digital collections in libraries and archives. As institutions increasingly digitize cultural heritage materials, existing metadata creation workflows—often reliant on manual or semi-automated processes—struggle to scale while maintaining accuracy and contextual depth. The research proposes the development of a computational framework leveraging transformer-based language models and graph neural networks to automate the extraction of hierarchical relationships, temporal linkages, and domain-specific ontologies from unstructured text and multimedia assets. The methodology involves training multi-modal machine learning models on curated corpora spanning digitized manuscripts, oral history transcripts, and image collections, with iterative validation by domain experts in archival science. High-performance computing resources are critical for processing terabytes of unstructured data, fine-tuning large language models on specialized vocabularies, and simulating knowledge graph embeddings that preserve contextual nuances across diverse cultural contexts. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for adaptive metadata augmentation, capable of dynamically updating semantic networks as collections expand. The project aims to significantly reduce latency in resource description workflows while enhancing discoverability through AI-generated contextual annotations. By bridging computational linguistics, digital preservation, and knowledge organization systems, this work advances the capacity of memory institutions to manage exponentially growing digital assets and supports interdisciplinary research requiring complex, cross-collection queries. The computational infrastructure will enable reproducibility studies across multiple institutions, fostering collaborative benchmarking of AI-assisted curation methodologies in library science.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the knowledge and skills required to develop, organize, store, retrieve, administer, and facilitate the use of local, remote, and networked collections of information in print, audiovisual, and electronic formats and that prepares individuals for professional service as librarians and information consultants.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance geoarchaeological investigations into the interplay between Holocene-era human settlement patterns and dynamic coastal environments in the Eastern Mediterranean. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how ancient communities adapted to rapid environmental shifts, such as sea-level fluctuations and sedimentological changes, which are poorly resolved in existing regional models due to computational limitations. By integrating high-resolution geospatial datasets, geochemical sediment analyses, and agent-based paleoenvironmental simulations, the project aims to reconstruct multi-scalar interactions between anthropogenic activity and landscape evolution. Key computational challenges include processing terabytes of LiDAR-derived topographic data, isotopic records from sediment cores, and artifact distributions across temporal scales, necessitating parallelized workflows for spatial statistics, Bayesian chronological modeling, and hydrodynamic simulations. The HPC environment will enable iterative coupling of sedimentary transport models with archaeological site formation algorithms, addressing taphonomic biases that have historically obscured interpretations of coastal settlement. Expected outcomes include the first quantitative framework for evaluating resource accessibility and mobility corridors in submerged nearshore zones, as well as probabilistic maps of paleoshoreline configurations at decadal resolution. This work will provide novel insights into human resilience to environmental stressors while establishing scalable computational methods for interdisciplinary geoarchaeology. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated simulations of sediment dynamics, machine learning-assisted artifact pattern recognition, and large-scale geodata fusion—tasks that exceed the capacity of local institutional clusters. By bridging earth science paradigms with archaeological inquiry through advanced computing, the project advances methodological innovation in both fields and offers transferable tools for studying climate-society interactions in vulnerable coastal regions worldwide.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of analytical techniques, concepts, and field methods from the earth sciences to solve archaeological questions related to human settlement, artifacts, site taphonomy, and paleoenvironments. Includes instruction in anthropology, ancient civilizations, archeology, geology, paleoclimatic reconstruction, sedimentology, and site taphonomic research.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in the computational analysis of sign languages’ structural diversity and evolution by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. While sign languages such as ASL, LSF, and Auslan exhibit complex morphological and syntactic features, large-scale comparative studies are hindered by the multidimensional nature of visual-spatial data and the lack of tools capable of processing heterogeneous datasets. The research problem centers on identifying linguistic universals and variations across sign languages, particularly in syntax and morphology, while accounting for sociolinguistic factors such as regional dialects and community-driven language change. To achieve this, the project will integrate computational linguistics, computer vision, and machine learning to analyze annotated video corpora, motion-capture datasets, and historical records of sign language use. Key methods include developing neural networks tailored for sequential sign language data, implementing 3D spatial modeling to track articulatory trajectories, and applying phylogenetic algorithms to reconstruct historical relationships between sign languages. HPC resources are essential for training deep learning models on high-resolution video data, conducting parallelized simulations of language evolution, and storing/processing terabytes of multimodal linguistic data. Expected outcomes include a scalable computational framework for cross-linguistic sign language analysis, novel insights into the typological classification of sign languages, and open-access tools for automated annotation and syntactic parsing. The project’s significance lies in advancing empirical methodologies for sign language linguistics, enabling rigorous comparisons with spoken language theories, and supporting technologies such as sign language recognition systems. By bridging computational and linguistic research, this work will contribute to preserving endangered sign languages and fostering equitable access to linguistic resources for deaf communities globally.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_title: Linguistics of ASL and Other Sign Languages
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific and scholarly study of the development, structure, and use of American Sign Language (ASL) and other visual signed languages, both as vehicles for communication within the deaf community and in relation to spoken and written languages. Includes instruction in cognitive linguistics; ASL and sign language phonology, syntax, and morphology; sociolinguistics of the deaf community; comparative linguistics; and studies of specific sign languages, including, but not limited to, ASL, Auslan (Australian Sign Language), LSF (French Sign Language), Shuwa jiten (Japanese Sign Language), HamNoSys (German Sign Language), and Gestuno.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dysregulation of intracellular signaling networks in cancer cell populations, with a focus on how microenvironmental stressors drive adaptive metabolic and ion channel responses that promote tumor survival. A central challenge in cell physiology and oncology is understanding how dynamic, multi-scale interactions between metabolic fluxes, ion gradients, and signaling proteins enable cancer cells to resist therapy. Current experimental methods struggle to resolve the spatiotemporal complexity of these processes, particularly under physiologically relevant conditions of nutrient deprivation or hypoxia. To address this, we propose an integrative computational framework combining agent-based modeling of cellular decision-making with spatially resolved reaction-diffusion simulations of ion transport and signaling kinetics. The models will incorporate empirical data from live-cell imaging and electrophysiology studies of pancreatic adenocarcinoma lines to parameterize key variables, including ATP-dependent potassium channel activity, calcium oscillation patterns, and crosstalk between AMPK and mTOR pathways. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter sweeps to identify critical thresholds in metabolic resource allocation that trigger phenotypic switching between proliferative and quiescent states. Parallelized simulations will also explore how subcellular heterogeneity in organelle positioning influences local signaling microdomains. Expected outcomes include mechanistic insights into how cancer cells optimize energy sensing and ion homeostasis under stress, with potential applications for disrupting adaptive pathways in treatment-resistant tumors. The computational pipelines developed will provide a generalizable platform for studying non-linear interactions in cell physiological systems, bridging molecular-scale events to population-level behaviors in solid tumors. This work directly aligns with the program’s focus on intracellular communication in pathophysiological contexts while avoiding overlap with excluded fields through its emphasis on integrative physiology rather than molecular biophysics or genomic-scale analyses.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of physiological processes operating within and among cells, and intracellular communication and behavior, in the context of larger systems and whole organisms. Includes instruction in cell and molecular biology, molecular physiology, cell cycle control, signal transduction, protein structure, membrane biochemistry and structure, ion channel physics, cell respiration and digestion, secretory functions, cell adhesion and communication, information encoding and decoding, and the relation of cell physiology to tissue, organ, and organismic functioning.

abstract: This research project investigates the interplay between language variation in digital communication platforms and the emergence of decentralized cultural identities, with a focus on underdocumented multilingual online communities. While prior sociolinguistic studies have analyzed language use in virtual spaces, the rapid evolution of hybridized, algorithmically mediated communication—particularly in marginalized or diaspora groups—remains understudied due to the scale and complexity of multimodal data involved. The central research problem addresses how computational linguistic patterns in user-generated content (e.g., code-mixing, emoji semantics, translingual hashtags) both reflect and actively reshape community-specific cultural practices in ways that challenge traditional frameworks of language socialization. The project employs a mixed-methods computational approach, combining transformer-based NLP models fine-tuned for low-resource languages, dynamic network analysis of interaction metadata, and ethnographic validation through collaborative annotation with community participants. High-performance computing resources are critical for processing terabytes of timestamped text, audio, and visual data from federated platforms (Mastodon, Discord servers) while maintaining ethical data sovereignty protocols through partitioned containerization. Expected outcomes include 1) an open-source toolkit for detecting emergent semiotic conventions in algorithmically opaque environments, 2) quantitative models correlating linguistic innovation rates with community resilience metrics, and 3) a theoretical framework redefining digital multilingualism as a distributed cultural process rather than static identity marker. By bridging computational linguistics with community-centered anthropology, this work aims to inform inclusive language preservation strategies and platform governance policies that recognize fluid digital-cultural ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of the anthropological, historical, and sociological context of language with a particular emphasis on language use and its role in shaping cultural and social diversity. Includes instruction in applied linguistics, data management, field methods, language heritage, socialization, structure, linguistic analysis, linguistic theory, and multilingualism.

abstract: This research project seeks to address inefficiencies in parts warehousing and inventory management operations through the development of a dynamic, real-time optimization framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC). Traditional inventory control systems struggle to adapt to stochastic demand patterns, supply chain volatility, and spatial constraints in warehouse layouts, particularly in industries with high-mix, low-volume part flows (e.g., aerospace, specialized manufacturing). The computational challenge lies in modeling multi-objective trade-offs between inventory carrying costs, order fulfillment latency, and warehouse operational capacity under uncertainty, while accounting for interdependencies between part classification, storage policies, and workforce allocation. We propose a hybrid simulation-optimization approach combining agent-based modeling, discrete-event simulation, and multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) to create a digital twin of warehouse operations. The HPC environment will enable parallelized scenario testing across heterogeneous parameter spaces, including demand shocks, equipment downtime events, and seasonal variability. Key innovations include a graph-based representation of part affinity networks to optimize storage proximity and a federated learning architecture to preserve data privacy across supply chain partners. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision support tool capable of recommending adaptive replenishment policies, dynamic pick-path optimizations, and workforce reallocation strategies. The computational intensity arises from real-time processing of IoT sensor data streams, high-dimensional state-action spaces in MARL training, and Monte Carlo simulations for risk-aware inventory planning. Results will be validated against operational benchmarks from three industrial partners, with projected reductions in excess inventory (15–22%) and order processing times (25–30%). This work bridges gaps in granular, computation-driven warehouse optimization, offering a template for integrating operations research, industrial engineering, and machine learning in niche business logistics domains.
cip_title: Parts, Warehousing, and Inventory Management Operations
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide administrative, technical, and managerial support in the operation of warehouses, control of inventory, parts identification, and the performance of counter services for customers. Includes instruction in record-keeping, equipment operation, database entry, supply logistics, shop operations and math, and customer and supplier relations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to optimize the performance and energy efficiency of heating, ventilation, air conditioning, and refrigeration (HVACR) systems under dynamic operating conditions. Current HVACR maintenance practices rely heavily on empirical guidelines and static performance data, which often fail to account for real-time environmental variables, component degradation, or complex interactions between subsystems. This gap limits the ability to predict system failures or adaptively improve efficiency, particularly in heterogeneous climates or high-demand settings. To address this, we propose a multi-scale simulation framework integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD), thermodynamic cycle analysis, and machine learning (ML) to model HVACR systems at component and system levels. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable parallelized simulations of airflow, heat transfer, and refrigerant phase changes across diverse operating scenarios, including extreme temperatures and partial-load conditions. Sensor data from field deployments will train ML models to correlate simulated behaviors with real-world performance metrics, enabling predictive maintenance algorithms. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated solvers for transient CFD analyses and distributed computing for parameter sweeps evaluating system responses to component faults or control adjustments. Expected outcomes include a digital twin platform for HVACR performance optimization, predictive fault detection models with quantified uncertainty bounds, and actionable insights for retrofitting existing systems. This work will directly inform technician training programs by identifying critical failure modes and efficiency-limiting factors, bridging the gap between theoretical diagnostics and practical maintenance strategies. By leveraging HPC capabilities, the project aims to reduce energy consumption in HVACR systems by 15–20% in modeled scenarios, contributing to sustainability goals while enhancing system reliability in residential, commercial, and industrial contexts.
cip_title: Heating, Air Conditioning, Ventilation and Refrigeration Maintenance Technology/ Technician
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, install, service and maintain the operating condition of heating, air conditioning, and refrigeration systems. Includes instruction in diagnostic techniques, the use of testing equipment and the principles of mechanics, electricity, and electronics as they relate to the repair of heating, air conditioning and refrigeration systems.

abstract: This project seeks to address inefficiencies in automated data entry workflows by developing adaptive, context-aware parsing algorithms optimized for heterogeneous document formats. While modern data entry systems rely on rigid template-based approaches, real-world documents—such as invoices, medical forms, or supply chain manifests—often exhibit structural variations that degrade accuracy and require manual correction. Our research focuses on creating a computational framework that dynamically interprets semi-structured documents through multimodal feature fusion, combining optical character recognition (OCR) outputs, spatial layout analysis, and domain-specific semantic patterns. The proposed methods leverage transformer-based architectures with attention mechanisms to model hierarchical relationships between text elements, while graph neural networks capture topological dependencies in document layouts. A key innovation involves training models to probabilistically infer missing or ambiguous data fields through cross-document contextual reasoning, reducing error propagation in downstream workflows. High-performance computing resources are critical for three aspects: 1) Processing large-scale synthetic document datasets generated via procedural augmentation to cover rare format variations, 2) Training multi-modal architectures with up to 100 million parameters across distributed GPU nodes, and 3) Running evolutionary optimization cycles to automatically adapt parsing rules for specialized domains (e.g., legal contracts vs. laboratory reports). Expected outcomes include an open-source framework that reduces manual data validation labor by 40-60% in pilot deployments with healthcare billing partners, along with novel benchmarks for evaluating context-sensitive document understanding systems. This work bridges gaps between traditional data entry paradigms and emerging requirements for intelligent document processing in data-intensive industries, advancing computational methods at the intersection of human-computer interaction, pattern recognition, and applied information systems.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to perform basic data and text entry using standard and customized software products. Includes instruction in keyboarding skills, personal computer and work station operation, reading draft texts and raw data forms, audio and tape dictation, and various interactive software programs used for tasks such as word processing, spreadsheets, databases, and others.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and predict the structural and material degradation of historic buildings under varying environmental and anthropogenic stressors, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address gaps in traditional architectural conservation practices. Architectural conservation faces challenges in quantitatively forecasting long-term material behavior, particularly for complex, multi-layered structures subjected to climate change, urban development, and tourism pressures. Current methods rely heavily on physical sampling and static simulations, which lack the resolution to capture dynamic interactions between environmental variables, material properties, and structural integrity over extended timescales. To address this, the project proposes a multi-scale computational approach integrating finite element analysis (FEA), machine learning (ML), and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate decay processes in historic masonry, timber, and mortars. High-resolution 3D scans of case-study buildings will inform geometric models, while material datasets from spectral analysis and mechanical testing will parameterize degradation algorithms. HPC resources will enable parallelized simulations of century-scale weathering cycles, thermal fluctuations, and visitor footfall impacts, iteratively refined via ML models trained on real-world conservation outcomes. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolset to prioritize intervention strategies, optimize maintenance schedules, and assess risk scenarios for heritage sites. By bridging computational engineering and conservation theory, this work aims to establish a replicable methodology for data-driven preservation planning, reducing reliance on reactive, trial-and-error approaches. The project’s computational demands—particularly the need for large-scale fluid-structure interaction simulations and ML training on heterogeneous material datasets—necessitate access to HPC infrastructure to achieve the required spatial-temporal resolution. Results will be disseminated through open-source tools and case studies on UNESCO World Heritage sites, offering scalable solutions for global conservation practice.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the architectural design principles and building techniques used in historic structures and environments, and the process of saving and restoring old buildings and districts for contemporary use and enjoyment. Includes instruction in architectural history, building conservation techniques, and material conservation.

abstract: This project seeks to elucidate the dynamic interplay between structural flexibility and functional specificity in multi-domain enzymes, a fundamental question in molecular enzymology with broad implications for understanding biochemical regulation. While static structures of such enzymes are increasingly available, the mechanistic coupling of large-scale conformational changes to catalytic activity remains poorly resolved. We propose to address this gap using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to model the free-energy landscapes governing domain movements in a prototypical ATP-dependent ligase. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to achieve the microsecond-to-millisecond timescales required to sample rare transitions between functional states. All-atom simulations will be performed using the AMBER force field on systems exceeding 250,000 atoms, incorporating explicit solvent and physiological ion concentrations. Enhanced sampling techniques, including parallel tempering and metadynamics, will be applied to map energy barriers associated with domain reorientation events. Concurrently, hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) calculations will characterize electronic rearrangements during the ligase’s chemical step, enabling direct correlation of conformational states with catalytic efficiency. This dual-scale approach—integrating nanosecond-resolution dynamics with femtosecond-scale electronic structure analysis—will uniquely resolve how allosteric communication emerges from collective atomic motions. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of conserved hinge residues that gate interdomain flexibility, (2) quantification of entropy-enthalpy compensation during substrate-induced folding, and (3) predictive rules for engineering domain interfaces to modulate activity. By bridging gaps between structural biophysics and mechanistic biochemistry, this work will provide a computational framework for analyzing multi-domain enzymes inaccessible to current experimental techniques. The requested HPC allocation will support 1.2 million core-hours across GPU and CPU nodes, enabling statistically robust sampling of rare events while maintaining atomic-level precision. Results will be disseminated through open-access trajectory archives and machine learning-derived surrogate models to aid the broader molecular biology community.
detailed_field: Biochemistry, biophysics, and molecular biology nec
cip_title: Biochemistry, Biophysics and Molecular Biology, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in biochemistry, biophysics and molecular biology, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of designing adaptive, evidence-based instructional strategies for diverse secondary classrooms through large-scale computational modeling of student learning dynamics. Secondary educators face increasing demands to personalize instruction for heterogeneous student populations, yet traditional teacher preparation frameworks lack tools to systematically analyze how varying pedagogical approaches interact with factors such as prior knowledge gaps, engagement patterns, and cognitive development trajectories. We propose developing an agent-based modeling platform that simulates classroom learning processes under different instructional conditions, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to parameterize individual student agents using empirical datasets from standardized assessments, classroom observations, and demographic records. The computational model will incorporate cognitive science principles and sociocultural learning theories to simulate multi-scale interactions between teaching strategies, curricular content sequencing, and student outcomes across thousands of virtual classroom iterations. Machine learning techniques will then identify optimal intervention points and strategy combinations that maximize learning gains for diverse student profiles. By enabling parallelized simulation of complex educational ecosystems, HPC resources are critical for processing high-dimensional parameter spaces and temporal dependencies inherent in classroom interactions. Expected outcomes include: (1) a validated computational framework for testing pedagogical hypotheses beyond observational study limitations, (2) empirically-derived guidelines for context-sensitive instructional adaptations targeting common secondary education challenge areas (e.g., STEM skill transfer, literacy development in multilingual classrooms), and (3) open-source simulation tools to enhance teacher education programs through data-driven scenario-based training modules. This work directly advances secondary teaching preparation by providing novel methodologies to analyze and optimize teaching practices at scales and resolutions unachievable through conventional educational research paradigms.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students in the secondary grades, which may include grades seven through twelve, depending on the school system or state regulations. May include preparation to teach a comprehensive curriculum or specific subject matter.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of social stratification and mobility in urban populations using large-scale demographic microdata and advanced computational methods. The research problem centers on understanding how macro-level social inequalities emerge from micro-level interactions, particularly in contexts of rapid demographic change and institutional policy shifts. Traditional analytical methods struggle to capture the nonlinear, multiscale interdependencies between individual behaviors (e.g., migration, education, employment) and structural factors (e.g., housing policies, labor market segmentation). To address this gap, we propose developing agent-based computational models (ABMs) that simulate population-scale decision-making processes under varying social and economic constraints. These models will integrate longitudinal census data, geospatial information systems (GIS) layers, and social survey datasets to parameterize heterogeneous agent behaviors across diverse socioeconomic groups. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to run thousands of parallelized simulations exploring alternative policy scenarios and demographic trajectories, enabling robust sensitivity analyses and the identification of critical leverage points in social systems. The computational workflow will employ distributed memory architectures for scaling agent populations to metropolitan-region levels (10^6–10^7 agents) while maintaining fine-grained interaction rules. Expected outcomes include (1) new insights into how institutional discrimination and network homophily jointly reproduce inequality across generations, (2) empirically grounded projections of social mobility trends under policy interventions, and (3) open-source tools for scalable ABM development in sociological research. By bridging computational social science with classical stratification theory, this work aims to advance evidence-based strategies for reducing systemic inequities while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in population-focused sociological inquiry.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of human social institutions and social relationships. Includes instruction in social theory, sociological research methods, social organization and structure, social stratification and hierarchies, dynamics of social change, family structures, social deviance and control, and applications to the study of specific social groups, social institutions, and social problems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale, multimodal writing datasets and model the evolving rhetorical strategies employed in digital writing environments. As digital platforms increasingly shape writing practices, traditional methods of rhetorical analysis—often limited to small, manually curated corpora—struggle to capture the scale, dynamism, and complexity of contemporary digital discourse. This research addresses this gap by developing computational models to identify patterns in rhetorical adaptation across genres such as social media, collaborative wikis, and AI-mediated writing tools. Using natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based architectures and graph-based discourse analysis, the project will process terabytes of timestamped text and metadata from publicly available digital writing repositories. These methods will enable the identification of rhetorical moves, genre hybridity, and audience engagement strategies at scale. HPC resources are critical for training custom NLP models on heterogeneous text-video-audio data, running high-dimensional network analyses of cross-platform discourse communities, and simulating rhetorical cascades in agent-based models of collaborative writing. Anticipated outcomes include a computational framework for mapping rhetorical innovation in digital environments, open-source tools for corpus-based writing studies, and empirical insights into how emerging technologies (e.g., generative AI) reshape compositional processes. Results will advance disciplinary understanding of digital rhetoric while informing pedagogical approaches that prepare students to navigate rapidly changing writing ecosystems. By bridging computational methods with humanistic inquiry, this work demonstrates how HPC can expand the methodological horizons of writing studies, enabling researchers to ask new questions about the sociotechnical dimensions of literacy in the 21st century.
cip_title: Rhetoric and Composition/ Writing Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in rhetoric and composition/writing studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in public relations (PR) and image management by analyzing large-scale digital communication data to model stakeholder perceptions and crisis response dynamics. Traditional PR research relies on manual content analysis or small-sample surveys, limiting the ability to capture real-time, multidimensional public sentiment across diverse platforms. The proposed study addresses this gap by employing computational methods to analyze unstructured data from social media, news archives, and organizational communications, with a focus on identifying patterns in reputation risk, crisis propagation, and message effectiveness. Using natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning models, the project will classify sentiment, detect emerging narratives, and simulate crisis scenarios based on historical data. Agent-based modeling will further explore how stakeholder networks amplify or mitigate reputational threats. These methods require HPC resources to process terabytes of text and multimedia data, train deep learning architectures, and run complex simulations iteratively. Expected outcomes include predictive frameworks for optimizing crisis communication strategies, tools for real-time reputation monitoring, and evidence-based insights into the interplay between message framing and audience segmentation. By integrating computational scalability with PR theory, this research aims to enhance the field’s capacity to manage digital-era image challenges while providing students and practitioners with data-driven decision-making models. The requested computing infrastructure will enable rapid experimentation with algorithmic approaches, reducing time-to-insight for time-sensitive applications such as misinformation response and brand recovery. This project bridges a critical methodological divide in communication studies, positioning computational PR as a transformative domain for both academic inquiry and industry practice.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the theories and methods for managing the media image of a business, organization, or individual and the communication process with stakeholders, constituencies, audiences, and the general public; and that prepares individuals to function as public relations assistants, technicians, and managers. Includes instruction in public relations theory; related principles of advertising, marketing, and journalism; message/image design; image management; special event management; media relations; community relations; public affairs; and internal communications.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of health misinformation propagation and corrective messaging efficacy across social media platforms, with a focus on vaccine-related communication. The research problem centers on identifying how structural features of online networks (e.g., echo chambers, influencer hierarchies) and linguistic attributes of messages (e.g., framing, emotional valence) interact to amplify or mitigate the spread of inaccurate health claims. Traditional methods for analyzing health communication patterns struggle to process the scale and complexity of multimodal social media data, which includes text, images, user interaction metrics, and temporal network dynamics. To address this gap, we propose a computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze terabyte-scale datasets from Twitter, Reddit, and Instagram spanning 2019–2023. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will be developed to classify message types and sentiment trajectories, while graph neural networks will model information diffusion pathways. Agent-based simulations will test counter-messaging strategies under varying network conditions. The computational workflow requires parallelized processing of 200+ million posts, dynamic network visualization, and real-time parameter optimization for machine learning models—tasks demanding GPU-accelerated nodes and large-memory infrastructure. Expected outcomes include 1) a framework for predicting high-risk misinformation superspreader events, 2) evidence-based guidelines for timing and targeting corrective health messages, and 3) open-source tools for monitoring emergent health narratives. Findings will advance theoretical understanding of trust formation in digital health environments while providing practical resources for public health organizations to improve crisis communication. The project’s scale necessitates HPC capabilities unavailable through standard institutional computing clusters, particularly for training transformer-based NLP models on heterogeneous multimedia data and running iterative network simulations with 10^6+ synthetic agents.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on how people, individually and collectively, understand and accommodate to health and illness and the role of communication and media in shaping professional health care messages and public acceptance of these messages. Includes instruction in the development and use of health-related and care-related messages and media; the goals and strategies of health care promotion; relationships, roles, situations, and social structures in the context of health maintenance and promotion; and applications to disease prevention, health advocacy, and communications concerning treatments.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational research in Czech linguistic and literary studies, addressing critical gaps in large-scale textual analysis. The research problem centers on the computational complexity of analyzing morphologically rich Czech texts across historical and contemporary corpora, which traditional methods struggle to process efficiently. Current limitations hinder comprehensive studies of linguistic evolution, dialect variation, and stylistic trends in Czech literature, particularly when scaling to the vast digital archives now available. To address this, the project proposes a multi-phase computational approach. First, we will compile and preprocess a diverse corpus of Czech texts spanning the 19th century to the present, including literary works, periodicals, and technical documents. Next, we will implement parallelized natural language processing (NLP) pipelines for tokenization, morphological disambiguation, and syntactic parsing using tools optimized for Czech’s complex inflectional system. Transformer-based models will then be fine-tuned to detect stylistic patterns, semantic shifts, and dialectal features, while clustering algorithms will map literary genre evolution. Computational demands include training neural models on large textual datasets, running high-dimensional analyses, and managing memory-intensive corpus queries. HPC resources are essential to execute these tasks within feasible timeframes, enabling batch processing of terabyte-scale data and GPU-accelerated model training. Expected outcomes include the first diachronic computational analysis of Czech morphological productivity, a publicly accessible annotated corpus for Slavic NLP research, and quantitative insights into 20th-century literary modernism’s linguistic innovations. The project will also produce open-source code for Czech-specific text processing, benefiting low-resource language NLP. By integrating computational methods with philological expertise, this work aims to redefine analytical paradigms in Czech studies while contributing scalable methodologies for under-resourced Slavic languages.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Czech language. Includes instruction in philology; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of maintaining interoperability and performance integrity in vendor-certified software ecosystems, particularly in environments requiring high reliability, such as industrial control systems or healthcare informatics. Current certification processes rely heavily on static test suites and manual validation, which struggle to adapt to dynamic, real-world computational demands or heterogeneous hardware configurations. To bridge this gap, we propose the development of an adaptive, simulation-driven framework for automated certification compliance testing, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model large-scale deployment scenarios and stress-test vendor-specific software under variable operational conditions. The research will focus on creating a modular testing architecture that integrates vendor-defined certification parameters with machine learning–driven anomaly detection, enabling real-time performance benchmarking and fault prediction. Computational workloads will involve parallelized simulations of networked software deployments across diverse hardware topologies, coupled with Monte Carlo methods to stochastically model edge cases and failure modes. Key outcomes include a scalable, vendor-agnostic validation toolkit capable of reducing certification cycle times by 40–60% while improving detection of latent compliance risks. The project will also generate novel datasets correlating certification metrics with runtime performance anomalies, offering insights into resilience patterns for vendor-supported products. By shifting certification workflows from manual checklists to computationally intensive, scenario-based testing, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for maintaining software reliability in certified ecosystems, with direct applications in safety-critical industries. The requested HPC resources are essential for handling the memory-intensive simulations and iterative model training required to achieve statistically robust validation across thousands of concurrent virtualized environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to fulfill the requirements set by vendors for professional qualification as certified installation, customization, and maintenance engineers for specific software products and/or processes. Includes training in specific vendor-supported software products and their installation and maintenance.

abstract: This project seeks to develop predictive models to optimize nurse staffing allocation in acute care settings, addressing critical gaps in balancing patient safety, workforce well-being, and operational costs. Current staffing practices often rely on static nurse-to-patient ratios, which fail to account for dynamic factors such as fluctuating patient acuity, interdisciplinary care demands, and real-time workload variability. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) and machine learning (ML) to simulate staffing scenarios under diverse clinical conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large-scale electronic health record (EHR) datasets—including patient outcomes, nurse workflow patterns, and institutional cost structures—while running parallelized simulations to identify optimal staffing configurations. The ABM will model interactions between nurses, patients, and care environments, incorporating stochastic elements such as emergent patient deteriorations and shift-to-shift workflow disruptions. ML algorithms, including recurrent neural networks and ensemble methods, will analyze historical EHR data to predict acuity trends and quantify workload impacts on clinical outcomes. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated simulation platform for testing staffing policies, (2) dynamic staffing recommendations calibrated to real-time patient and operational variables, and (3) predictive metrics linking staffing flexibility to reduced burnout rates and preventable adverse events. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this work will provide nurse administrators with evidence-based tools to align staffing decisions with evolving care demands, improving both resource efficiency and care quality. The computational pipeline developed here will be scalable to other healthcare settings, offering a template for data-driven nursing management in complex clinical environments.
cip_definition: A program that prepares registered nurses to manage nursing personnel and services in hospitals and other health care delivery agencies. Includes instruction in principles of health care administration, resource and financial management, health care law and policy, medical personnel management, and managed care operations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving cultural narratives and identity formation within Asian-American communities through large-scale digital humanities approaches. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how diasporic experiences are represented and negotiated across multimedia archives, including digitized oral histories, community newspapers, literary works, and visual art produced by Asian-American creators from the late 19th century to the present. Current scholarship often relies on qualitative close readings of limited datasets, which risks overlooking longitudinal patterns, intertextual connections, and underrepresented voices within heterogeneous Asian-American subgroups. To address this, we propose computational text and image analysis of curated corpora spanning 150,000+ documents and 40,000+ visual artifacts from public and institutional archives. Natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models fine-tuned for historical texts, will identify thematic shifts in discourses of belonging, resistance, and cultural hybridity. Computer vision methods will examine visual motifs in self-published zines, protest art, and photography to trace how material practices reflect intersectional identities. Graph neural networks will map transnational intellectual influences across authors and artists. These computationally intensive tasks require HPC capabilities for parallel processing of multilingual OCR outputs, training custom embedding models, and analyzing high-resolution images. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible interactive atlas of Asian-American cultural production, methodological frameworks for ethically computing with marginalized community archives, and new insights into how generational trauma, assimilation pressures, and solidarity movements have shaped creative expression. By centering computational approaches within cultural studies, this work aims to redefine the scale and scope of humanistic inquiry into Asian-American experiences while preserving the complexity of lived narratives.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of Asian population groups who have immigrated to the United States and Canada, or sought refugee asylum, from the colonial period to the present, and including Chinese-Americans, Japanese-Americans, Korean-Americans, Vietnamese-Americans, Cambodian-Americans, and others.

abstract: This project seeks to advance the understanding of fiber network formation and chemical interactions during pulp and paper manufacturing using high-performance computing (HPC) to overcome limitations of experimental methods in capturing multiscale phenomena. The research focuses on two interconnected challenges: (1) predicting the mechanical and optical properties of paper products based on fiber morphology, colloidal interactions, and drying dynamics, and (2) optimizing energy-intensive processes such as pulping, bleaching, and coating through molecular-scale modeling of lignin-cellulose systems. Computational methods will combine molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of fiber-fiber and fiber-additive interfaces, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models of pulp suspension flows, and machine learning (ML) techniques to bridge scales from nanoscale fiber surface chemistry to macroscopic paper sheet formation. The HPC resources will enable large-scale MD simulations (>1 million particles) to characterize lignin degradation pathways during kraft pulping, coupled with GPU-accelerated CFD to model coating uniformity in high-speed paper machines. Expected outcomes include a validated multiscale framework for predicting paper strength and porosity as functions of refining intensity, furnish composition, and drying rates, which currently require costly trial-and-error approaches in industrial settings. The project will also generate open-access datasets of simulated fiber networks and reaction kinetics for key pulping chemicals.
