By elucidating fundamental relationships between process parameters, fiber morphology, and product performance, this work aims to reduce energy consumption in paper manufacturing by 15-20% in modeled scenarios while enabling tailored paper grades for emerging applications. The computational tools developed will provide the Paper Science and Engineering community with new capabilities to design sustainable fiber-based materials and optimize circular economy strategies for wastepaper recycling.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development, and manufacturing of pulp and paper products. Includes instruction in pulp and paper science, pulping and bleaching processes, paper structure and processes, pulp and paper manufacturing, coating technology, surface and colloid science, and fibers.

abstract: This project seeks to address the critical challenge of modeling systemic financial instability arising from climate-driven economic transitions, a domain straddling computational finance, climate risk analytics, and complex systems theory. Traditional financial risk frameworks inadequately capture the nonlinear interdependencies between climate physical risks (e.g., extreme weather events) and transition risks (e.g., abrupt policy shifts or technological disruptions), particularly across multi-asset portfolios and heterogeneous institutional stakeholders. The research will develop a high-resolution agent-based model (ABM) simulating cascading market failures under dynamically evolving climate scenarios, integrating geospatial climate projections, macroeconomic indicators, and granular financial network data. The computational approach leverages parallelized Monte Carlo methods to explore stochastic climate policy pathways while employing graph neural networks to model contagion effects across interconnected financial entities. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the combinatorial complexity of 10^6+ agent interactions, multi-terabyte climate datasets (downscaled CMIP6 projections), and real-time sensitivity analyses across regulatory regimes. Expected outcomes include a scalable open-source toolkit for stress-testing financial instruments against climate tipping points, with applications to sovereign risk assessment, green bond valuation, and resilience planning for multilateral development banks. The project aims to advance methodological synergies between computational sustainability and financial engineering while providing empirically grounded insights for policymakers navigating the financial system’s capacity to absorb climate-driven shocks. By mapping emergent vulnerabilities in transition scenarios, this work addresses a critical gap in next-generation environmental, social, and governance (ESG) analytics, directly supporting the operationalization of climate-aligned financial supervision frameworks.
cip_title: Finance and Financial Management Services, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in financial management and services, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on the efficacy and scalability of arts-based interventions in healthcare settings. While arts-integrated programs—spanning music, dance, theater, and visual arts—are increasingly used to address mental health, chronic pain, and community wellness, the mechanisms underlying their therapeutic effects remain poorly quantified. Current studies face limitations in analyzing large, heterogeneous datasets (e.g., biometric sensor data, qualitative participant feedback, and longitudinal health records) that capture multidimensional outcomes. This project aims to develop computational models to identify patterns linking specific artistic modalities to physiological, psychological, and social health metrics. Using machine learning techniques, including natural language processing for qualitative narratives and deep learning for time-series biometric analysis, we will integrate multimodal datasets from clinical trials and community-based arts programs. HPC resources are critical for training models on complex, high-dimensional data (e.g., audio-visual recordings of therapy sessions, motion-capture dance data, and electronic health records) and simulating intervention outcomes across diverse populations. Key objectives include optimizing algorithms to predict patient responsiveness to arts therapies, modeling dose-response relationships, and generating digital twins of community health ecosystems to test intervention scalability. Outcomes will provide evidence-based frameworks for personalizing arts interventions, improving resource allocation in public health programs, and informing policy on arts-in-medicine integration. By quantifying the biopsychosocial impacts of arts engagement, this work addresses a critical gap in health professions research, offering scalable computational tools to advance equitable, data-driven approaches in holistic care. The requested HPC infrastructure will enable processing of terabyte-scale datasets, parallelized model training, and real-time analytics—capabilities essential for translating artistic practices into measurable health solutions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, implementation, and management of programs that use the visual and performing arts in support of health and wellness among diverse individuals and communities. Includes instruction in dance, literary arts, music, theatre, healthcare systems, program administration, and public health.

abstract: This project seeks to address critical gaps in the secure and efficient utilization of large-scale clinical datasets for predictive analytics, focusing on the development of a novel computational framework for dynamic anonymization of heterogeneous health records. While current de-identification methods prioritize static privacy preservation, they often compromise data utility for machine learning applications, particularly when handling multimodal data (e.g., imaging, genomic markers, and longitudinal EHR entries) in distributed health systems. Our research problem centers on creating adaptive anonymization protocols that maintain analytical fidelity while meeting evolving regulatory requirements across jurisdictions. The computational approach combines graph neural networks with differential privacy mechanisms, optimized for processing petabyte-scale datasets across distributed storage architectures. High-performance computing resources will enable parallelized training of privacy-preserving models on GPU clusters, coupled with simulations to quantify re-identification risks under realistic attack scenarios. Key innovations include a federated learning component for cross-institutional data sharing and entropy-based metrics to dynamically adjust anonymization granularity based on dataset complexity. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit validated against HIPAA, GDPR, and emerging AI-specific health data regulations, benchmarked on diverse clinical datasets from 15 partner hospitals. This work will directly enhance the feasibility of sharing sensitive medical records for multicenter research while maintaining compliance, potentially accelerating discoveries in precision medicine. By bridging computational scalability with regulatory-aware design, the project advances health information technology infrastructure capable of supporting next-generation AI applications without compromising patient privacy.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of health information administrators and other professionals, to construct medical records and clinical databases, perform manipulations on retrieved data, control the security and quality of records, and supervise data entry and technical maintenance personnel. Includes instruction in clinical and biomedical science data and information requirements, database management, data coding and validation, information security, quality control, health information content and structure, medical business procedures, and legal requirements.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution of cultural narratives and identity formation within understudied North American subregions, with a focus on Acadian communities in Atlantic Canada and Southwestern U.S. borderlands, using advanced computational text and geospatial analysis. Despite rich archival and contemporary sources—including multilingual oral histories, regional literature, and community media—these regions lack systematic studies that integrate large-scale qualitative data with spatial and temporal dynamics. The research problem centers on identifying patterns of cultural resilience, hybridity, and transformation across time, particularly in response to socio-environmental pressures. To address this, we propose a mixed-methods framework combining natural language processing (NLP) and geographic information systems (GIS), applied to digitized primary sources and born-digital community records. Transformer-based models will be fine-tuned to analyze multilingual texts (English, French, Spanish) for thematic and sentiment trends, while spatial networks of cultural landmarks will be reconstructed using historical maps and satellite imagery. High-performance computing resources are critical for processing terabytes of heterogeneous data, training domain-specific language models, and running iterative simulations of cultural diffusion patterns. Expected outcomes include an open-access corpus of annotated regional narratives, a computational toolkit for interdisciplinary regional studies, and visualizations tracing cultural continuity amid globalization. By revealing how subregions negotiate identity in transnational contexts, this work aims to inform cultural preservation initiatives and deepen methodological synergies between area studies and computational social science. The project’s scale—encompassing centuries of data across dispersed geographies—necessitates parallelized workflows and GPU-accelerated analytics only feasible through HPC infrastructure.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the defined geographic subregions and subcultures within modern and historical countries and societies. Includes such topics as Acadian Studies, French Canadian and Quebec Studies, Southern (U.S.) Studies, New England Studies, Southwestern Studies, Northern Studies, and others.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution of LGBTQ+ cultural narratives and community formation through computational analysis of large-scale multimedia archives. Current research in Gay/Lesbian Studies often relies on qualitative methods, limiting the scope to isolated case studies. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze digitized collections spanning literature, visual art, film, and activist publications from the 20th and 21st centuries. Computational methods will include natural language processing (NLP) for thematic modeling of texts, computer vision techniques to identify visual motifs in art and film, and network analysis to trace collaborative relationships among creators and organizations. These approaches require HPC capabilities due to the volume of data (over 10 million text pages and 500,000 visual artifacts) and the computational intensity of transformer-based models for cross-modal pattern detection. Expected outcomes include mapping shifts in LGBTQ+ representation across media, identifying understudied contributors to cultural movements, and uncovering intersections between artistic production and legal/policy milestones. The findings will advance scholarly understanding of how marginalized communities negotiate visibility in hostile environments while informing contemporary efforts to preserve LGBTQ+ heritage. By integrating computational rigor with humanistic inquiry, this project aims to establish new methodologies for studying identity-based cultural phenomena at scale.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on homosexuality in history, society, politics, and cultural life; usually with an emphasis on the modern emergence of gays and lesbians as a sociocultural minority movement, the identification of social, literary, and artistic themes and the definition of, and public policy and legal issues surrounding, the gay and lesbian community.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing dynamic resource allocation in decentralized economic systems, integrating advances in algorithmic game theory, econometrics, and high-performance computing. The research addresses the challenge of modeling large-scale, adaptive markets where heterogeneous agents with bounded rationality interact under evolving constraints, such as energy markets with real-time renewable generation shifts or decentralized finance (DeFi) platforms. Existing equilibrium-based models often fail to capture the temporal and spatial complexity of such systems, particularly when accounting for strategic behavior, network effects, and incomplete information. To bridge this gap, we propose a hybrid agent-based modeling approach combining evolutionary optimization, reinforcement learning for adaptive agent strategies, and econometric validation against historical market data. The computational architecture will leverage parallelized Monte Carlo simulations across multiple market scenarios, implemented using MPI for distributed memory systems, with graph neural networks to model inter-agent influence patterns. Key innovations include a novel mechanism for endogenous preference formation using attention-based architectures and a scalable auction protocol optimizer tested through evolutionary algorithms. The project requires high-performance computing resources to manage the combinatorial complexity of simulating thousands of interacting agents across extended time horizons, with anticipated workloads exceeding 50,000 core-hours for parameter space exploration. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly available toolkit for simulating decentralized resource allocation systems, 2) empirical insights into the computational tractability of incentive-compatible mechanisms in large networks, and 3) policy-relevant findings on market design under high volatility. Results will advance both economic theory by quantifying previously intractable forms of strategic interdependence and computer science through developments in scalable mechanism design, with applications to sustainable infrastructure planning and digital market regulation.
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on the theoretical and practical connections between computer science and economics. Includes instruction in data analysis, database design, data mining, computer algorithms, economics, econometrics, computer programing, mathematics, and statistics.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of misinformation propagation and rhetorical adaptation in digital media ecosystems through large-scale computational analysis. The proliferation of multimodal content—text, video, and algorithmically curated media—presents unprecedented challenges in tracking how narratives evolve across platforms, audiences, and socio-political contexts. Traditional methods lack the capacity to process terabytes of unstructured data or model complex interactions between users, content, and platform architectures. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to deploy transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) models for cross-linguistic sentiment analysis, topic detection, and rhetorical feature extraction across datasets from Twitter, YouTube, and emerging decentralized platforms. Concurrently, network analysis tools will map temporal shifts in information cascades and influencer hierarchies, while GPU-accelerated simulations will test counterfactual scenarios of narrative spread under varying moderation policies. The computational pipeline integrates qualitative coding frameworks with machine learning classifiers to preserve theoretical rigor in communication studies while scaling analytical depth. Anticipated outcomes include identifying latent patterns in adversarial narrative adaptation, quantifying platform-specific amplification biases, and generating predictive models of crisis communication efficacy. Results will advance methodological innovation in media effects research, offering empirically grounded insights for policymakers and journalists combating misinformation. The project’s open-source tools and datasets will enable replication studies across communication subfields, from political rhetoric to health communication. Access to HPC infrastructure is critical to process petabytes of data, reduce model training times for iterative deep learning experiments, and execute parallelized simulations of global communication networks—tasks infeasible with standard institutional resources. This work bridges computational scalability with humanistic inquiry, reinforcing the role of communication research in addressing societal challenges posed by rapidly evolving media environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on research and research methods in communication, and that spans the study of mass communication/media studies, old and new media technologies, social and political applications, and speech communication and rhetoric. Includes instruction in quantitative and qualitative methods of inquiry; interpersonal, group, organizational, and intercultural communication; theories of communication; critical thinking, argumentation, and persuasion; written communication; printed, electronic, and digital media; rhetorical tradition and criticism; media, society, and culture; consequences and effects of mass media; and media social science and criticism.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for modeling consumer decision-making processes in multi-sensory digital marketing environments. Traditional marketing models often oversimplify consumer behavior by isolating visual, auditory, or textual stimuli, neglecting the dynamic integration of these factors in immersive digital platforms such as augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), and interactive social media. The research problem centers on understanding how heterogeneous sensory inputs interact nonlinearly to influence purchasing decisions, particularly in contexts where real-time personalization and adaptive interfaces are critical. To address this, the project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) combined with deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to simulate large-scale consumer populations interacting with multi-modal marketing content. The ABM component will capture individual variability in sensory preferences and cognitive processing, while DRL will optimize stimulus combinations in real time based on evolving behavioral feedback. Computational challenges include processing high-dimensional data streams (e.g., eye-tracking, biometric responses, and clickstream patterns) and scaling simulations to reflect diverse demographic cohorts. HPC resources are essential for parallelizing these simulations, reducing latency in reinforcement learning feedback loops, and enabling sensitivity analyses across parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive model for sensory-driven consumer behavior, actionable insights into optimal stimulus integration strategies, and an open-source toolkit for adaptive digital marketing design. This work bridges gaps between cognitive science, human-computer interaction, and marketing analytics, offering a novel methodological foundation for personalized, sensory-aware marketing strategies in rapidly evolving digital ecosystems. The results will directly inform the design of next-generation marketing platforms, enhancing both consumer engagement and ethical targeting practices by reducing reliance on invasive data collection.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in general marketing and marketing research, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance comparative analyses of cultural and identity-based group dynamics through large-scale textual and visual media datasets. The research problem centers on identifying patterns of representation, intersectionality, and discursive evolution across racial, gender, sexual, and ethnic groups in transnational contexts. Traditional qualitative and small-scale quantitative methods often struggle to capture longitudinal or cross-regional trends in vast digital archives, limiting holistic insights into how group identities are constructed, contested, and transformed in public discourse. To address this gap, the project will employ computational text analysis, multimodal machine learning, and network modeling to analyze over 10 million documents (e.g., literary works, social media, historical records) and 500,000 visual artifacts (photographs, films, digital art) spanning 1900–2020. Key methodologies include transformer-based NLP models fine-tuned for multilingual sentiment and semantic role labeling to trace shifts in narratives about marginalized groups, coupled with convolutional neural networks to detect visual tropes and their sociocultural correlations. Graph-based approaches will map the diffusion of ideological frameworks across geographic and temporal boundaries. The computational workflow requires distributed processing for dataset alignment, GPU-accelerated model training, and memory-intensive simulations of cultural influence networks. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible knowledge graph linking representations to sociopolitical events, quantitative frameworks for measuring intersectional identity dynamics, and novel visualizations of cultural hegemony in transnational contexts. By enabling scalable, replicable analysis of underrepresented group histories, this work aims to advance interdisciplinary methodologies in critical cultural studies while providing infrastructure for future comparative research on identity formation. The requested HPC resources are critical to handling the project’s data volume, model complexity, and need for rapid iteration across diverse linguistic and visual domains.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the comparative study of the history, literature, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of different groups such as racial, gender, sexual, class, ethnic, geographical, and national. Includes instruction in comparative studies, comparative literature, critical race theory, cultural anthropology, cultural studies, religious studies, science studies, social and cultural theory, urban studies, and visual culture.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address the challenge of optimizing consumer-driven sustainability metrics in apparel marketing through advanced computational modeling of dynamic purchasing behaviors. As global demand for eco-conscious textile products grows, brands face operational complexity in aligning real-time marketing strategies with heterogeneous consumer preferences, supply chain constraints, and environmental impact data. Current decision-support tools lack the capacity to process multimodal datasets—including social media sentiment analysis, historical purchase patterns, and lifecycle assessment (LCA) parameters—at the scale required for agile campaign development. This project will leverage high-performance computing resources to implement a hybrid simulation framework combining agent-based modeling (ABM) of consumer decision networks with deep learning-driven trend forecasting. The ABM module will simulate 10^6+ synthetic agents interacting with evolving product attributes (price, material sustainability, style relevance) under varying market conditions, while temporal graph neural networks will analyze cross-platform consumer engagement data to predict regional preference shifts. By parallelizing Monte Carlo simulations across GPU clusters, we aim to quantify probabilistic outcomes for marketing spend allocation across digital and physical channels under multiple sustainability scenarios. The computational workflow will integrate NLP preprocessing of unstructured brand perception data, automated hyperparameter optimization for behavioral models, and visualization of multidimensional trade-off frontiers between profitability and environmental metrics. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for adaptive marketing resource allocation in circular textile economies, validated against partner datasets from mid-sized ethical fashion brands. This work bridges gaps in computational consumer science, environmental impact analytics, and textile industry practices, offering a replicable model for data-driven marketing decisions in sustainability-critical domains.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on marketing research and management as applied to the products and services of the apparel and textile industries. Includes instruction in applicable principles of textile and apparel design and manufacturing, sales and distribution systems, domestic and international market research, profitability, consumer research, and the design and implementation of marketing campaigns.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance conflict analysis and resolution through the development of a computational framework for simulating emergent conflict dynamics in digitally mediated environments. The research problem centers on the lack of scalable, data-driven models to analyze how decentralized communication platforms (e.g., social media, encrypted messaging) influence the evolution of intergroup disputes, particularly in contexts where traditional mediation frameworks are ineffective. Current approaches often rely on static network analyses or qualitative case studies, which struggle to capture the nonlinear feedback loops, adaptive agent behaviors, and real-time information cascades that characterize modern conflicts. To address this gap, the project will implement a multi-agent simulation environment integrating three computational methods: (1) agent-based modeling of polarized communities using behavioral parameters derived from empirical conflict datasets, (2) dynamic network analysis to track the spread of adversarial narratives under varying moderation policies, and (3) natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to analyze semantic shifts in conflict-related discourse across multilingual corpora. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale parameter sweeps across synthetic societies (10⁴–10⁵ agents) while maintaining the low-latency processing required for real-time sentiment and topology updates. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source toolkit for predicting conflict escalation thresholds in digital spaces and a comparative analysis of intervention strategies (e.g., algorithmic de-escalation prompts, network rewiring protocols). By bridging computational social science with conflict resolution theory, this work aims to establish quantitative foundations for evaluating platform governance policies and third-party mediation tactics in digitally exacerbated disputes. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated NLP training, distributed agent simulations via MPI frameworks, and storage for petabyte-scale interaction logs from publicly available conflict datasets.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the origins, resolution and prevention of national, intergroup and interpersonal conflicts. Includes instruction in theories of conflict, mediation and negotiation, understanding of the ethical, cultural and power dynamics that can be applied to resolve disputes in a variety of settings, including business, legal, domestic, and labor relations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze linguistic and literary evolution in Modern Greek, with a focus on identifying patterns of syntactic, morphological, and lexical change from the early modern period (late 15th century) to the present. The research problem centers on the scarcity of large-scale computational studies addressing how sociohistorical factors—such as urbanization, technological innovation, and language standardization—have shaped Modern Greek in diverse contexts, including its use in literature, media, and technical domains. Existing analyses rely on manual or small-scale methods, limiting the ability to detect subtle, systemic shifts across time, dialects, and genres. To address this, we propose a computational workflow integrating natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning (ML) techniques. A curated corpus of digitized texts—spanning literary works, newspapers, technical manuals, and oral transcripts—will be processed using transformer-based models (e.g., BERT) adapted for historical and dialectal Greek. HPC resources will enable the parallel training of these models across multiple epochs and regional varieties, as well as large-scale syntactic parsing and semantic role labeling. Key tasks include dialect classification, tracking lexical borrowing and neologisms in scientific registers, and quantifying stylistic changes in literature post-1950. Expected outcomes include (1) a diachronic map of grammatical and lexical trends correlated with sociocultural events, (2) an open-access annotated corpus for computational Hellenic studies, and (3) methodological frameworks for adapting NLP tools to under-resourced historical languages. The project will enhance scholarly understanding of Modern Greek as a dynamic, pluricentric language while demonstrating how HPC-driven approaches can address gaps in philological and linguistic research. Results will directly support pedagogical tools, language preservation initiatives, and applications in AI-driven translation systems for technical and literary Greek.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development and use of the Greek language in the period dating from the late 15th century to the present. Includes instruction in modern Greek literature, current Greek dialects, and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This project seeks to develop scalable optimization frameworks for dynamic resource allocation in large-scale, human-in-the-loop operational systems, such as logistics networks, healthcare delivery systems, and emergency response operations. A critical challenge in these domains is balancing real-time decision-making under uncertainty with long-term system efficiency, particularly when human interventions introduce nonlinear constraints and adaptive behaviors. Current methods often rely on oversimplified models that fail to capture the interdependencies between stochastic demand patterns, resource mobility, and human decision biases. To address this gap, we propose a hybrid computational approach integrating stochastic optimization, agent-based simulation, and reinforcement learning. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to handle the combinatorial complexity of these models, which involve millions of decision variables, time-dependent constraints, and multi-objective trade-offs. The computational workflow will parallelize Monte Carlo simulations for uncertainty propagation, deploy distributed solvers for mixed-integer programming subproblems, and train neural network surrogates to approximate human decision policies. Expected outcomes include novel algorithms for real-time resource reallocation under partial observability, validated against case studies from hospital bed management and disaster relief logistics. The HPC implementation will enable sensitivity analyses across parameter spaces infeasible on local clusters, directly quantifying how human intervention thresholds impact system resilience. Results will advance both methodological knowledge—providing open-source optimization libraries for human-integrated systems—and practical guidelines for adaptive resource management in high-stakes environments. This work aligns with national priorities for robust critical infrastructure and has been developed in collaboration with regional healthcare providers and urban planning agencies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development and application of complex mathematical or simulation models to solve problems involving operational systems, where the system concerned is subject to human intervention. Includes instruction in advanced multivariate analysis, application of judgment and statistical tests, optimization theory and techniques, resource allocation theory, mathematical modeling, control theory, statistical analysis, and applications to specific research problems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance osteopathic medicine research by elucidating the biomechanical and molecular mechanisms underlying osteopathic manipulative treatment (OMT). Despite the widespread clinical use of OMT to address musculoskeletal dysfunction and systemic health, the precise biophysical interactions between manual interventions, tissue response, and physiological outcomes remain poorly characterized. This gap limits evidence-based optimization of OMT protocols and hinders the integration of osteopathic principles into broader precision medicine frameworks. To address this, we propose a multiscale computational modeling approach combining finite element analysis (FEA) of musculoskeletal dynamics with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of mechanotransduction pathways activated by OMT. FEA will simulate tissue deformation, strain distribution, and fluid flow in anatomically accurate 3D models derived from patient-specific MRI/CT data. Concurrently, MD simulations will explore how mechanical forces alter ion channel conformations, extracellular matrix protein interactions, and downstream signaling cascades linked to anti-inflammatory or regenerative responses. Machine learning models will integrate these datasets to predict patient-specific OMT outcomes based on biomechanical, genomic, and clinical variables. HPC resources are essential to handle the computational intensity of multiscale simulations, large-scale medical image processing, and iterative training of predictive algorithms. Expected outcomes include a validated computational framework for mechanistically linking OMT techniques to physiological effects, identification of biomarkers for treatment responsiveness, and open-access tools for simulating osteopathic interventions in diverse patient populations. This work will strengthen the evidence base for osteopathic medicine, enable data-driven refinement of manipulative therapies, and foster interdisciplinary collaborations bridging clinical practice, systems biology, and computational biomechanics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of osteopathic medicine, involving a combination of medical principles and procedures and osteopathic principles of holistic medicine and the relationship of the musculoskeletal system to general health. Includes instruction in the basic medical sciences, preventive medicine, family and community medicine, medical informatics, disease systems, organ and physiologic systems, osteopathic principles and practice, osteopathic manipulative treatment, musculoskeletal and skin systems, clinical specialty rotations, medical ethics, and professional standards and practice management.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-fidelity computational framework to optimize diagnostic and repair strategies for modern automotive systems, with a focus on hybrid and electric vehicle (HEV/EV) platforms. The increasing complexity of automotive technologies, including integrated electrical systems, advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), and battery thermal management systems, poses challenges for traditional trial-and-error diagnostic approaches. The research problem centers on creating predictive models to simulate fault propagation, component degradation, and system-wide interactions under diverse operating conditions. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will be employed to run parallelized simulations combining finite element analysis (FEA) for mechanical stress modeling, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for thermal management systems, and machine learning algorithms trained on real-world diagnostic datasets. Key objectives include (1) developing digital twins of hybrid powertrains to predict failure modes, (2) automating fault detection in CAN bus networks using graph neural networks, and (3) optimizing battery cooling system designs through multi-physics simulations. The computational workflow will integrate open-source automotive simulation tools with custom Python-based analytics pipelines, requiring GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning tasks and high-memory nodes for large-scale parametric studies. Expected outcomes include predictive maintenance algorithms deployable in shop environments, validated thermal management strategies for extended battery life, and a publicly accessible dataset of simulated fault scenarios. This work will advance technician training methodologies by providing data-driven insights into emergent automotive technologies while reducing diagnostic time and resource waste in repair workflows. The requested HPC resources are critical to handling the ∼10^6 parameter combinations in system behavior modeling and achieving the project’s goal of bridging computational engineering with practical automotive service applications.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain all types of automobiles. Includes instruction in brake systems, electrical systems, engine performance, engine repair, suspension and steering, automatic and manual transmissions and drive trains, and heating and air condition systems.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and validate advanced statistical models to analyze complex, high-dimensional social science datasets, with a focus on understanding dynamic socioeconomic disparities and their drivers in urban populations. The research addresses key computational challenges in modeling non-linear relationships, temporal dependencies, and spatial heterogeneity within social systems using observational data prone to selection bias and missingness. We propose a hybrid computational framework combining Bayesian hierarchical modeling, stochastic agent-based simulations, and non-parametric regression techniques to account for multi-level social interactions and confounding factors. The methodology will implement Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms with adaptive sampling to estimate posterior distributions for key parameters governing inequality dynamics, while employing distributed computing strategies to handle longitudinal datasets spanning millions of records from census microdata, social surveys, and digital trace sources. High-performance computing resources are essential for three critical components: 1) Parallelized model fitting across hundreds of demographic strata using variational inference methods 2) Large-scale simulation studies to evaluate model robustness under different missing data mechanisms 3) Bootstrapped uncertainty quantification for policy impact projections through resampling techniques requiring 10^5+ iterations. Expected outcomes include new statistical approaches for causal inference in observational social data, validated computational tools for counterfactual analysis of intervention scenarios, and evidence-based insights into the temporal evolution of opportunity gaps across population subgroups. The developed methods will advance statistical computing practices in social sciences by creating scalable implementations of complex models that respect the hierarchical structure and measurement limitations inherent in real-world social data. Results will be disseminated through open-source software packages optimized for HPC architectures and policy briefs quantifying the potential impacts of different equity-oriented interventions.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the social scientific applications of relationships between groups of measurements, and similarities and differences, using probability theory and techniques derived from it. Includes instruction in quantitative social science methodologies, the principles in probability theory, binomial distribution, regression analysis, standard deviation, stochastic processes, non-parametric statistics, sampling theory, and statistical techniques.

abstract: In the domain of film and photographic preservation, the degradation of archival materials poses a significant challenge to cultural heritage conservation. Traditional restoration techniques, while effective, are labor-intensive and struggle to scale with the vast quantities of high-resolution media held in archives. This project seeks to address this bottleneck by developing computational workflows that leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to automate and enhance the restoration of degraded film and photographic collections. The research focuses on training deep neural networks—including generative adversarial networks (GANs) and vision transformers—to perform tasks such as noise reduction, scratch removal, and color stabilization across large datasets of 4K-resolution scans. These models require processing terabytes of image sequences with frame-specific temporal coherence, necessitating parallelized GPU-accelerated workflows and distributed storage systems accessible only through HPC infrastructure. Additionally, the project will explore the use of physics-based simulations to model historical film degradation processes, enabling synthetic data generation to improve model generalizability. The outcomes aim to produce open-source tools for archivists, significantly reducing the time and cost associated with large-scale preservation efforts while advancing computational methodologies in media conservation. By integrating artistic sensibilities with machine learning pipelines, this work bridges technical innovation with the ethical and aesthetic considerations inherent in visual heritage stewardship, offering a template for interdisciplinary collaboration in digital humanities and computational arts.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
cip_title: Film/ Video and Photographic Arts, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in film/video and photographic arts, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamic interplay between tumor heterogeneity and microenvironmental stressors in driving cancer progression and therapeutic resistance. Despite advances in experimental oncology, the mechanisms by which spatially varying oxygen gradients, nutrient competition, and mechanical forces shape clonal evolution and metastatic phenotypes remain poorly understood. To address this, we propose a multiscale computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) of cancer cell populations with partial differential equation (PDE)-based simulations of biophysical microenvironmental factors. The ABM will capture stochastic cell behaviors—including proliferation, migration, and adaptation to stress—guided by experimental data from 3D tumor organoids. Concurrently, PDE solvers will model diffusive transport of metabolites and extracellular matrix remodeling. This coupled approach requires HPC resources to resolve high-resolution, time-dependent interactions across scales, particularly for simulating large cell populations (≥10^6 agents) within evolving heterogeneous microenvironments. Machine learning pipelines will further optimize parameter space exploration and identify critical thresholds in stress-response pathways that predict metastatic potential. Expected outcomes include predictive maps of tumor subpopulation dynamics under hypoxia, acidosis, and therapy-induced selection pressures. These results will elucidate how microenvironmental constraints drive phenotypic plasticity and spatial competition, offering mechanistic insights into treatment failure in late-stage cancers. The computational workflows developed will also serve as a foundation for future studies exploring stroma-targeted therapies. By bridging physiological-scale modeling with cancer biology, this work aims to advance translational strategies for disrupting resilience mechanisms in aggressive malignancies.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_title: Physiology, Pathology, and Related Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in physiology, pathology, and related sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to advance evidence-based public policy design by developing a computational framework to simulate the multi-dimensional impacts of policy interventions in complex, adaptive social systems. Traditional policy analysis methods often struggle to account for dynamic feedback loops, heterogeneous stakeholder behaviors, and cascading effects across interconnected sectors such as healthcare, education, and infrastructure. To address this gap, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) approach coupled with machine learning (ML) techniques to analyze how policy choices propagate through large-scale socio-technical systems. The research will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to execute parallelized simulations capturing 100,000+ autonomous agents with diverse decision rules, interacting across spatially explicit environments. Key computational challenges include optimizing ML-assisted calibration of agent behaviors using real-world demographic datasets, managing memory-intensive simulations of multi-year policy timelines, and conducting Monte Carlo sensitivity analyses across parameter spaces. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable policy simulation toolkit capable of evaluating trade-offs between equity, cost-effectiveness, and implementation feasibility; (2) identification of leverage points for improving policy resilience in scenarios characterized by demographic shifts or resource constraints; and (3) validation of model predictions against historical policy outcomes in three case studies (urban housing initiatives, disaster response protocols, and digital inclusion programs). By enabling granular analysis of emergent system behaviors under alternative policy regimes, this work aims to provide policymakers with decision-support tools that better anticipate unintended consequences and long-term societal impacts. The requested computing resources are critical for achieving the necessary scale, speed, and statistical power to derive actionable insights from computationally intensive scenario testing.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in public policy analysis, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Agricultural business systems face increasing complexity due to climate variability, market volatility, and evolving sustainability requirements. Current decision-support tools for farm managers often rely on static models that inadequately capture dynamic interactions between crop performance, resource allocation, and economic outcomes under these multidimensional pressures. This project proposes to develop an adaptive computational framework integrating agent-based modeling, machine learning, and discrete-event simulation to optimize agricultural business decisions at operational and strategic scales. The research will focus on simulating crop selection, input allocation, and supply chain logistics under probabilistic climate scenarios while incorporating real-world constraints such as labor availability, equipment costs, and regulatory policies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to process multi-terabyte datasets spanning historical yield records, hyperlocal weather patterns, and global commodity price fluctuations. Parallelized Monte Carlo simulations will quantify risk profiles for different management strategies, while neural networks trained on heterogeneous data streams (soil sensors, satellite imagery, financial records) will generate predictive models of input efficiency. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support system that identifies Pareto-optimal solutions balancing profitability, resource conservation, and operational resilience. The computational framework will be validated against longitudinal case studies from diversified row crop operations in climate-vulnerable regions. By enabling near-real-time analysis of complex agricultural systems at unprecedented spatial and temporal resolutions, this work aims to advance precision agriculture business practices while maintaining alignment with evolving sustainability benchmarks. The resulting open-source tools will provide farm managers with actionable insights for capital allocation, risk mitigation, and adaptive planning in volatile agroeconomic environments.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: Any instructional program in agricultural business and management, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address systemic inefficiencies in juvenile correctional rehabilitation programs by developing a computational framework to model intervention outcomes and optimize resource allocation. Despite advances in juvenile justice research, rehabilitation strategies often rely on generalized, population-level approaches that fail to account for the dynamic interplay of individual psychosocial factors, facility-specific constraints, and community reintegration pathways. This gap results in suboptimal resource deployment and inconsistent long-term outcomes for justice-involved youth. To bridge this divide, we propose a multi-scale simulation platform leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze heterogeneous datasets—including behavioral histories, educational progress metrics, and facility interaction logs—while preserving participant anonymity through synthetic data generation techniques. Agent-based modeling will simulate individual trajectories under varying intervention scenarios, incorporating psychological development thresholds, staff-to-youth ratios, and program sequencing constraints. Concurrently, graph neural networks will map relational dynamics within correctional environments to identify critical intervention points. The computational pipeline will integrate federated learning architectures to enable secure collaboration across jurisdictions without raw data sharing. Expected outcomes include a decision-support toolkit capable of predicting rehabilitation success probabilities under customized resource configurations, optimizing staff training allocations, and identifying cost-effective program adaptations for diverse facility types. By translating complex psychosocial interactions into quantifiable operational parameters, this work aims to provide juvenile corrections agencies with empirically grounded strategies to improve individualized care while maintaining fiscal and logistical feasibility. The project’s computational demands—particularly in training ethically aligned AI models and running parallelized simulations across thousands of synthetic cohorts—necessitate dedicated HPC resources to achieve scalability and real-world applicability.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to specialize in the provision of correction services to underage minor populations. Includes instruction in corrections, juvenile delinquency, juvenile development and psychology, juvenile law and justice administration, social services, record-keeping procedures, and communication skills.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced simulation frameworks for optimizing hybrid electromechanical systems used in industrial automation and renewable energy applications. The research addresses a critical challenge in electromechanical technologies: the integration of precision mechanical components with adaptive control systems under dynamic operational conditions. Current design methodologies often rely on decoupled analyses, leading to suboptimal performance in real-world scenarios where thermal, vibrational, and electromagnetic factors interact nonlinearly. To overcome this limitation, we propose a multi-physics computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The project will implement coupled finite element analysis (FEA) for mechanical stress and deformation, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for thermal management, and circuit-level electromagnetic simulations in a unified workflow. Machine learning techniques will be employed to accelerate parameter space exploration for system optimization, particularly for applications requiring real-time control adjustments, such as smart manufacturing actuators and grid-scale energy storage interfaces. The HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale parallelization of transient simulations across multiple operational regimes while maintaining the temporal resolution required to capture microsecond-scale electrical-mechanical interactions. Expected outcomes include predictive models for failure mode analysis in high-cycle fatigue environments, validated against experimental data from collaborative industry partners, and open-source tools for modular system co-simulation. This work aims to establish computational best practices for next-generation electromechanical system design, with potential impacts on manufacturing efficiency, renewable energy infrastructure reliability, and the development of adaptive maintenance protocols. The requested computing resources are essential given the project's scope, which requires simultaneous execution of multi-terabyte datasets across coupled physics domains and iterative optimization runs exceeding the capacity of local institutional clusters.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in electromechanical technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the formation and evolution of cultural narratives within intersectional marginalized communities through computational analysis of large-scale digital archives, including social media, oral history transcripts, and community-generated multimedia. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how dynamic, overlapping identities—shaped by ethnicity, gender, and cultural marginalization—are negotiated and represented in decentralized digital spaces. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to capture the scale and complexity of these interactions, necessitating advanced computational approaches. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques, including transformer-based models for multilingual sentiment analysis and topic modeling, to trace patterns of identity articulation and resistance across diverse datasets. Network analysis will map the diffusion of narratives and coalition-building among communities, while image and video analysis tools will examine non-textual cultural production. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process terabytes of heterogeneous data, train custom machine learning models on low-resource languages prevalent in minority communities, and run iterative simulations of narrative spread. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible framework for analyzing intersectional cultural discourse at scale, novel insights into how digital platforms reshape collective identity preservation, and methodological advancements in applying computational tools to ethically engage with marginalized narratives. The research will directly benefit community organizations by providing scalable tools to document and amplify underrepresented voices, while advancing interdisciplinary scholarship on identity in the digital age. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project bridges computational social science and cultural studies, offering a model for resource-intensive humanities research that prioritizes ethical data practices and community-centered inquiry.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_title: Ethnic, Cultural Minority, Gender, and Group Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in ethnic, cultural minority, gender, and group studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for analyzing dynamic human-environment interactions through high-resolution spatiotemporal data, with applications to informal settlement monitoring and resilience planning. Rapid urbanization and climate change have intensified vulnerabilities in informal settlements, where traditional cartographic methods struggle to capture fluid land use patterns and micro-scale environmental risks. Current geographic information systems (GIS) lack the capacity to process multi-modal data streams—including satellite imagery, crowd-sourced mobility traces, and sensor-derived climate metrics—at the temporal granularity required for proactive policy interventions. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to implement a hybrid convolutional neural network (CNN) and agent-based modeling architecture optimized for spatial-temporal forecasting. Computational workflows will integrate petabytes of Sentinel-2 imagery, anonymized mobile device location pings, and hyperlocal precipitation/temperature data across six case study regions in Southeast Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa. Key technical challenges include developing parallelized raster algebra operations for daily land cover classification, implementing graph neural networks to model pedestrian movement through informal transit corridors, and creating uncertainty-aware visualization interfaces for municipal planners. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated containers on a clustered computing environment to manage memory-intensive geospatial joins and enable near-real-time simulation of flood propagation scenarios under varying urban growth forecasts. Expected outcomes include an open-source spatial analytics pipeline capable of identifying emerging settlement zones 8-12 months faster than existing methods, along with probabilistic risk maps quantifying exposure to extreme heat and flooding at 10-meter resolution. By advancing computational cartography's capacity to represent informal urban dynamics, this work aims to establish new standards for equitable climate adaptation planning while expanding the methodological repertoire of spatial social science.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of map-making and the application of mathematical, computer, and other techniques to the analysis of large amounts of geographic data and the science of mapping geographic information. Includes instruction in cartographic theory and map projections, computer-assisted cartography, geographic information systems, map design and layout, photogrammetry, air photo interpretation, remote sensing, spatial analysis, geodesy, cartographic editing, and applications to specific industrial, commercial, research, and governmental mapping problems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop an advanced simulation framework for optimizing child care service allocation in dynamic urban environments. The research addresses a critical gap in evidence-based decision-making tools for child care management, where traditional planning methods struggle to account for fluctuating demand, demographic variability, and regulatory constraints. By integrating computational social science with operations research, the project aims to model complex interactions between family needs, provider capacities, and policy landscapes at unprecedented granularity. The computational approach combines agent-based modeling (ABM) with multi-objective optimization algorithms to simulate parent decision-making processes, provider operational challenges, and systemic inequities in access. High-fidelity datasets—including census microdata, transportation networks, and real-time enrollment patterns—will be processed using parallelized workflows to parameterize simulations across diverse socioeconomic scenarios. The HPC infrastructure will enable sensitivity analyses at scale, testing interventions such as subsidy redistribution, facility siting strategies, and workforce training programs under varying population growth and policy conditions. Expected outcomes include a validated decision-support system capable of forecasting child care demand hotspots, quantifying trade-offs between equity and efficiency metrics, and identifying resilient allocation strategies for municipal planners. This work bridges computational techniques with social policy innovation, offering a template for data-driven management of care ecosystems while adhering to ethical constraints around privacy and bias mitigation. The scalability of the framework will be demonstrated through case studies across three distinct urban regions, with results disseminated to public agencies and advocacy organizations to inform equitable resource distribution. By situating computational social science within child care management, this project advances both methodological rigor in non-STEM HPC applications and practical tools for strengthening early childhood support systems.
cip_title: Child Care and Support Services Management
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the provision and management of child care services and that prepares individuals to plan, design, and manage child care facilities and programs that meet children's developmental needs and interests and that provide safe and healthy environments. Includes instruction in child development and psychology; home- and institution-based child care; identification of diseases, injuries, and psychological trauma and applicable referrals; parent relations; personnel and business management principles; and related laws and policies.

abstract: This project seeks to optimize radiation dose efficiency and diagnostic image quality in radiologic imaging through advanced computational modeling, addressing a critical challenge in radiologic technology. While modern imaging systems prioritize patient safety, balancing minimal radiation exposure with clinically usable image quality remains complex, particularly for pediatric, geriatric, and high-body-mass-index patients. Current protocols rely on generalized exposure parameters, which may lead to unnecessary radiation or suboptimal diagnostic outcomes. To address this, we propose developing patient-specific imaging protocols using high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate radiation-tissue interactions and image formation processes. Monte Carlo simulations will model X-ray photon transport across anatomically variable digital phantoms, incorporating tissue density, thickness, and metabolic variations derived from clinical CT datasets. Concurrently, deep learning architectures (3D convolutional neural networks and generative adversarial networks) will be trained on paired low-dose and diagnostic-quality images to predict noise reduction and artifact correction strategies. The HPC environment is essential for managing the computational intensity of Monte Carlo methods, which require ~10^8 particle histories per simulation, and for processing multi-terabyte imaging datasets during neural network training. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework to customize tube voltage, current, and filtration settings based on patient anatomy and clinical indication, potentially reducing average radiation doses by 20-40% while maintaining diagnostic accuracy. Validated models will be deployed as open-source tools for protocol optimization in clinical radiography systems. This work bridges computational physics and clinical practice, offering data-driven strategies to enhance radiation safety and imaging efficacy—key priorities for radiologic technologists and healthcare systems. Resource allocation will directly support GPU-accelerated simulations, large-scale image analysis, and the development of educational modules for training radiographers in protocol personalization techniques.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of physicians, to provide medical imaging services to patients and attending health care professionals. Includes instruction in applied anatomy and physiology, patient positioning, radiographic technique, radiation biology, safety and emergency procedures, equipment operation and maintenance, quality assurance, patient education, and medical imaging/radiologic services management.

abstract: Occupational therapy (OT) interventions aim to enhance patients’ functional independence, yet variability in individual responses to therapy remains poorly understood due to the complex interplay of biomechanical, neurological, and environmental factors. This project seeks to address this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop predictive computational models that optimize personalized OT intervention strategies. The proposed research will analyze multimodal datasets, including motion-capture recordings of patients with upper-limb mobility impairments, neuroimaging data, and longitudinal clinical outcomes from stroke and traumatic brain injury cohorts. Using scalable machine learning frameworks, we will train neural networks to identify patterns in motor recovery trajectories and simulate the biomechanical efficacy of different therapeutic exercises under varying physiological constraints. HPC resources are critical for handling the high dimensionality of these datasets, running parallelized simulations of musculoskeletal models, and performing real-time optimization of treatment parameters. Expected outcomes include a computational toolkit that predicts patient-specific responses to OT interventions, identifies optimal exercise regimens, and quantifies the biomechanical load thresholds to prevent injury during therapy. This work will advance the evidence base for precision OT by enabling data-driven clinical decision-making, potentially reducing trial-and-error approaches that delay patient progress. Additionally, the project will generate open-access datasets and models to support broader research in rehabilitation sciences. By integrating computational modeling with clinical practice, this research aligns with the Pre-Occupational Therapy Studies program’s mission to prepare future practitioners for technology-driven healthcare environments, fostering innovation in therapeutic strategies and improving functional outcomes for diverse patient populations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in occupational therapy.

abstract: The construction industry faces persistent challenges in optimizing resource allocation, material efficiency, and project timelines due to the complex interplay of dynamic variables such as material behavior, environmental conditions, and workforce productivity. Traditional manual or low-fidelity computational approaches often fail to capture these multi-scale, nonlinear interactions, leading to cost overruns, safety risks, and environmental impacts. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to model and simulate construction processes with unprecedented granularity, integrating physics-based simulations, machine learning, and real-time data assimilation. The research will focus on three computational thrusts: (1) multi-physics simulations of structural assemblies under varying loads and environmental stressors, (2) reinforcement learning models to optimize construction sequencing under uncertainty, and (3) agent-based modeling of workforce dynamics and safety scenarios. By coupling finite element analysis of material systems with discrete-event simulations of construction workflows, the framework will enable predictive analytics for decision support. The HPC environment is essential for scaling these computationally intensive models across parameter spaces encompassing diverse materials (e.g., composite concretes, engineered lumber), equipment interactions, and climate scenarios. Anticipated outcomes include validated predictive models for material waste reduction, evidence-based safety protocols, and adaptive scheduling algorithms that respond to real-time jobsite data. This work will advance computational methodologies in construction trades by establishing a paradigm for digital twin integration in small-to-medium scale projects, directly contributing to sustainable building practices and workforce training through AI-driven scenario libraries. The requested computing resources will support GPU-accelerated model training, large-scale parameter sweeps, and visualization of complex 4D construction sequences, addressing critical gaps in current industry capabilities.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the building, inspecting, and maintaining of structures and related properties. May include instruction in masonry, carpentry, electrical and power transmission installation, building/construction finishing, management, inspection and other construction-related applications.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize quality control protocols and safety assessments for complex industrial systems using high-performance computing (HPC). Current quality assurance methodologies in non-destructive testing (NDT) and process safety management often rely on generalized statistical models or empirical thresholds, which may inadequately account for dynamic operational conditions, material heterogeneities, or multi-scale failure mechanisms. To address these limitations, we propose a hybrid approach combining physics-based simulations with machine learning to predict defect propagation, system vulnerabilities, and failure probabilities in real-world manufacturing and infrastructure environments. The computational workflow will integrate finite element analysis (FEA) for micromechanical stress modeling, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for automated defect classification in sensor data, and Monte Carlo simulations to quantify probabilistic safety margins under variable operating parameters. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational intensity of these multi-physics simulations, particularly when scaling to system-level analyses of large industrial components or distributed sensor networks. Expected outcomes include predictive models for early failure detection, adaptive quality control thresholds based on real-time process data, and risk-mitigation strategies tailored to heterogeneous material systems. The developed tools will be validated against experimental datasets from collaborative industry partners, focusing on applications in additive manufacturing quality assurance and aging infrastructure monitoring. By leveraging parallel computing architectures, this work aims to establish a scalable platform for safety-critical decision support, reducing reliance on conservative safety factors that impede operational efficiency. The resulting methodologies will advance computational quality control paradigms in engineering technologies, with potential impacts on regulatory standards and predictive maintenance frameworks across multiple industrial sectors.
cip_title: Quality Control and Safety Technologies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in quality control and safety technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze evolving narrative structures, thematic patterns, and linguistic features in Anglophone children’s and adolescent literature from the 19th century to the present. While qualitative scholarship in this field is robust, large-scale computational analysis remains underutilized, particularly for tracing longitudinal shifts in representations of identity, agency, and social norms. The study will employ natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning techniques to process a curated corpus of approximately 50,000 primary texts, including novels, picture books, and early readers, alongside supplementary data from awards lists, bestseller rankings, and publisher archives. Key computational tasks include semantic role labeling to map character agency dynamics, transformer-based sentiment analysis to evaluate emotional arcs in coming-of-age narratives, and graph-based network analysis to identify intertextual influences among authors and illustrators. These methods require parallelized processing of heterogeneous text and image data (e.g., scanned illustrations with OCR-derived captions), necessitating GPU-accelerated workflows for transformer model fine-tuning and large-scale dimensionality reduction. Expected outcomes include 1) a temporally stratified taxonomy of narrative tropes correlated with historical sociocultural trends, 2) quantitative frameworks for assessing representational equity in protagonists’ demographic attributes, and 3) open-access tools to help educators and librarians critically evaluate collection gaps. By bridging computational literary studies with childhood studies theory, this project aims to establish reproducible methods for analyzing youth literature as both aesthetic artifact and cultural discourse, while providing infrastructure for future collaborative research on decolonization, disability representation, and genre evolution in the field.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scholarly study of children's and adolescent literature and that may enhance the professional work of teachers, librarians, publishers, booksellers, and creative writers. Includes instruction in period and genre studies, author studies, literary criticism, studies of various types of literary text, book artists, and children's films.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of a virtual training and predictive analytics platform tailored to cosmetology education and practice. While cosmetology is traditionally taught through hands-on apprenticeships, emerging challenges—such as the need for scalable training tools, personalized client consultations, and data-driven insights into aesthetic trends—require innovative computational solutions. Current methods lack the capacity to simulate complex, dynamic interactions between grooming techniques, material properties (e.g., hair elasticity, skin porosity), and cultural or individual aesthetic preferences at scale. The proposed research addresses this gap by integrating physics-based simulations, machine learning (ML), and large-scale cultural dataset analysis to model and predict outcomes in hairstyling, skincare, and makeup application. Computational workflows will include finite element analysis for simulating hair and skin biomechanics, generative adversarial networks (GANs) to synthesize diverse aesthetic outcomes, and natural language processing (NLP) to analyze social media and historical records for trend forecasting. These methods demand HPC resources due to the high dimensionality of data (e.g., 3D scalp models, hyperspectral imaging of skin tones) and the iterative nature of training ML models on heterogeneous datasets. Expected outcomes include an open-access virtual training environment for cosmetology students, predictive tools for personalized client recommendations, and a curated database mapping regional aesthetic trends to material science parameters. By bridging computational modeling and cosmetology practice, this work aims to elevate pedagogical standards, reduce trial-and-error in service delivery, and foster interdisciplinary dialogue between technical and creative domains.
cip_title: Cosmetology and Related Personal Grooming Arts, Other.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in cosmetology and related personal grooming services not listed above.

abstract: The optimization of food processing techniques to enhance nutritional quality, safety, and shelf-life remains a critical challenge due to the complex, multi-scale interactions between biochemical, thermal, and mechanical factors. Traditional experimental approaches often struggle to capture these dynamic processes across molecular, cellular, and industrial scales. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-scale computational models that bridge molecular-level phenomena with macroscopic food processing dynamics. Key focus areas include simulating protein denaturation and starch gelatinization during thermal treatments using molecular dynamics, analyzing heat and mass transfer in industrial-scale equipment via computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and predicting microbial inactivation kinetics under varying processing parameters. Additionally, machine learning algorithms will be employed to correlate processing conditions with physicochemical stability during storage, enabling predictive optimization of shelf-life. The integration of these computational approaches will generate actionable insights into time-temperature thresholds for pathogen reduction, energy-efficient processing protocols, and packaging configurations that minimize quality degradation. By elucidating the fundamental mechanisms governing food matrix behavior, this research aims to establish a computational framework for accelerating the design of novel processing technologies. The requested HPC resources are essential to handle the large-scale simulations, iterative parameter optimization, and high-dimensional data analysis inherent to this work. Outcomes will advance food science by providing quantitative tools to reduce waste, improve safety, and tailor functional properties of processed foods, with direct benefits to both industry practices and public health initiatives.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of biological, chemical, and physical principles to the study of converting raw agricultural products into processed forms suitable for direct human consumption, and the storage of such products.
