This project will employ all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations enhanced by free energy calculations to model the structural transitions of voltage-gated sodium (Nav) channels under physiological membrane potentials. The computational workflow will integrate explicit-solvent MD using the CHARMM36 forcefield with advanced sampling techniques, including umbrella sampling and metadynamics, to map free energy landscapes associated with key gating motions. Simulations will target the voltage-sensing domain (VSD) and pore region of NavAb, a bacterial homolog with conserved eukaryotic features, embedded in a mixed lipid bilayer mimicking neuronal membrane composition. Given the system size (~150,000 atoms) and microsecond-scale sampling required to capture slow gating transitions, high-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to achieve sufficient statistical rigor. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of intermediate states during VSD activation, (2) quantification of coupling energies between voltage-sensor movement and pore opening, and (3) characterization of lipid-protein interactions modulating gating kinetics. These results will address long-standing controversies regarding the physical basis of electromechanical transduction in ion channels and provide a framework for interpreting experimental mutagenesis data. The project’s findings will advance fundamental understanding of bioelectrical phenomena while informing therapeutic strategies for channelopathies linked to epilepsy and cardiac arrhythmias. By bridging molecular-scale dynamics with physiological function, this work exemplifies the integrative role of computational biophysics in deciphering complex biological assemblies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of physics principles to the scientific study of the mechanisms of biological processes and assemblies at all levels of complexity. Includes instruction in research methods and equipment operation and applications to subjects such as bioenergetics, biophysical theory and modeling, electrophysics, membrane biology, channels, receptors and transporters, contractility and muscle function, protein shaping and folding, molecular and supramolecular structures and assemblies, and computational science.

abstract: Dental restorative materials are critical for maintaining oral function and aesthetics, yet their long-term biomechanical performance remains unpredictable due to complex interactions between material properties, occlusal forces, and biological environments. Current experimental methods to evaluate fatigue behavior are time-intensive and fail to capture the multifactorial dynamics of real-world clinical scenarios. This project proposes a computational approach to model the degradation of novel bioactive dental composites under cyclic loading, integrating biomechanical simulations with machine learning (ML) to predict material failure. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to resolve the multi-scale, nonlinear interactions between microscale material defects, stress distribution patterns, and time-dependent viscoelastic responses. Finite element analysis (FEA) will simulate stress accumulation in 3D tooth-restoration models derived from clinical cone-beam CT scans, incorporating variable occlusal contact geometries and masticatory forces. Concurrently, molecular dynamics simulations will model polymer-ceramic interfacial bonding in bioactive composites under hydrolytic aging. A ML framework will correlate simulation outputs with experimental fatigue data to identify predictive biomarkers of failure. The resulting hybrid model aims to optimize composite formulations and clinical design parameters, reducing restoration failure rates. By leveraging HPC capabilities, this project addresses a critical gap in translational dental materials research, offering a paradigm shift from trial-and-error testing to data-driven predictive modeling. Expected outcomes include open-access computational tools for simulating restoration durability and evidence-based guidelines for material selection in complex occlusal environments. This work bridges computational engineering and clinical dentistry, advancing personalized restorative strategies while minimizing costly clinical revisions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the advanced study of dental clinical techniques and dental practice issues. Includes instruction in subjects such as the history of dentistry, advanced dental practice management, dental ethics and jurisprudence, social and behavioral science studies of dentistry, advanced restorative dentistry, oral medicine, oral radiology, advanced clinical procedures and technology, and others.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and validate computational models to enhance the pedagogical training of future physics educators by analyzing student conceptual development in physics. A critical challenge in physics education is identifying persistent misconceptions and optimizing instructional strategies to address them. While existing studies rely on classroom observations or small-scale assessments, this research leverages high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate large-scale, dynamic learning environments and model the efficacy of targeted interventions. The computational framework integrates agent-based modeling to represent diverse student cohorts, coupled with machine learning algorithms trained on longitudinal datasets of student performance, conceptual surveys, and behavioral metrics. Simulations will test hypotheses about how specific instructional methods—such as inquiry-based problem-solving or peer-led discussions—affect conceptual mastery across demographic and cognitive variability. HPC resources are essential to handle the combinatorial complexity of variables, including individualized learning trajectories, real-time feedback mechanisms, and multi-scale interactions between pedagogical content knowledge and student reasoning. Expected outcomes include predictive models that identify high-impact teaching practices, optimized lesson plans adaptable to heterogeneous classrooms, and a publicly accessible database of simulated learning scenarios for educator training. By bridging computational science and physics education research, this work aims to provide empirically grounded tools for teacher preparation programs, ultimately improving the capacity of educators to address systemic challenges in STEM learning outcomes. The scalability of the approach will also enable future extensions to other domains of science and mathematics education.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach physics programs at various educational levels.

abstract: Clinical biochemical genetics faces significant challenges in interpreting complex metabolic data to diagnose and manage rare genetic disorders. Current diagnostic workflows often rely on static reference intervals and manual variant prioritization, which struggle to account for dynamic biochemical interactions, epigenetic modifiers, and multilocus pathogenic effects. This project proposes to develop a computational framework integrating longitudinal patient metabolomic profiles, enzyme kinetic simulations, and multi-omics data to improve diagnostic accuracy and therapeutic monitoring. The research will utilize high-performance computing resources to construct predictive models of metabolic network perturbations using constraint-based modeling (CBM) and stochastic differential equations. Molecular dynamics simulations will characterize the structural consequences of novel enzyme variants identified through clinical exome sequencing, while machine learning pipelines will correlate temporal metabolite patterns with disease progression. The computational infrastructure will support three key phases: (1) large-scale integration of clinical biochemical data from 10,000+ patients with inborn errors of metabolism, (2) real-time simulation of personalized metabolic flux under therapeutic interventions, and (3) development of decision-support algorithms for variant interpretation using ensemble classifier models. Expected outcomes include an open-source platform for dynamic biomarker analysis, validated against gold-standard clinical outcomes from 500 retrospective cases. This resource will enable probabilistic risk stratification for complex biochemical phenotypes and mechanistic modeling of treatment responses, directly addressing critical gaps in managing disorders with overlapping metabolic signatures. By leveraging parallelized computing architectures, the project aims to establish new paradigms for interpreting multifactorial biochemical data in clinical genetics, ultimately reducing diagnostic odysseys and optimizing therapeutic strategies for patients with rare inherited metabolic diseases.
cip_definition: Research on how to perform and interpret biochemical analyses relevant to the diagnosis and management of human genetic diseases, and to serve as a consultant regarding laboratory diagnosis of a broad range of inherited disorders.

abstract: Child care environments play a critical role in early development, yet optimizing these settings remains challenging due to the dynamic interplay of spatial, social, and pedagogical factors. Traditional approaches rely on observational studies, which lack scalability and real-time predictive capacity. This project seeks to address this gap by developing a computational framework to simulate child interactions within varied childcare environments, enabling data-driven optimization of space utilization and activity planning. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will implement agent-based models that integrate behavioral data, developmental psychology principles, and environmental variables to dynamically replicate group interactions and individual responses. The simulations will incorporate real-world data from motion sensors, video recordings, and caregiver reports, processed through machine learning algorithms to parameterize agent behaviors. By running large-scale parameter sweeps across virtual environments, the project aims to identify configurations that maximize engagement, minimize stress indicators, and promote equitable access to learning resources. The computational intensity of modeling hundreds of children simultaneously across thousands of scenarios necessitates HPC capabilities for parallel processing and large memory allocation. Expected outcomes include actionable insights for room layout design, staff deployment strategies, and activity sequencing tailored to developmental stages. This interdisciplinary approach bridges early childhood education with computational modeling, offering a novel methodology to enhance care quality through predictive analytics. The resulting open-source tools will empower providers to make evidence-based decisions, potentially transforming standards in childcare practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to be primary providers of home, family, residential, or institutional-based child care services. Includes instruction in child growth and development, nutrition, recreation, planning and supervision of play and learning activities, child abuse and neglect prevention, parent-child relationships, and applicable legal and administrative requirements.

abstract: Occupational therapy (OT) interventions for individuals with neurological impairments often rely on generalized frameworks for motor rehabilitation, which may not account for the variability in neuroplasticity or patient-specific biomechanical constraints. This project proposes to address this gap by developing a computational framework to model and predict patient-specific motor learning trajectories during task-oriented therapy, with the goal of optimizing personalized intervention strategies. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will integrate multimodal datasets—including motion capture kinematics, electromyography (EMG), and neuroimaging-derived connectivity maps—to construct dynamic, patient-specific neuromusculoskeletal models. These models will simulate motor adaptation processes under varying therapeutic conditions, such as task complexity, feedback modalities, and fatigue thresholds. Machine learning algorithms will be trained on simulated and clinical datasets to identify predictive biomarkers of motor recovery and recommend adaptive therapy parameters. The computational pipeline will require parallel processing for large-scale parameter optimization and stochastic simulations of neural network plasticity, necessitating access to GPU clusters and scalable memory architectures. Expected outcomes include a validated predictive tool for clinical decision-making in OT, which could reduce the trial-and-error approach in therapy design and improve functional outcomes for patients with stroke or traumatic brain injury. This work bridges computational neuroscience, biomechanics, and rehabilitation science, offering a novel methodology to advance precision in occupational therapy. By aligning with pre-OT educational objectives, the project also aims to generate open-source simulation tools for training future practitioners in data-driven intervention strategies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional program in occupational therapy.

abstract: This project seeks to address the computational challenges inherent in solving high-dimensional partial differential equations (PDEs) arising in quantum dynamical systems, where traditional numerical methods fail due to exponential scaling with dimensionality. Current approaches, such as finite element or spectral methods, become intractable beyond moderate dimensions, limiting progress in understanding complex quantum phenomena. To overcome this, we propose a novel hybrid algorithm combining stochastic gradient descent with adaptive sparse grid collocation, designed to exploit low-rank structures in solution manifolds while mitigating the curse of dimensionality. The method integrates deterministic solvers for localized features and probabilistic sampling for global behavior, enabling scalable approximations in phase space. Implementing this framework requires high-performance computing (HPC) resources due to the iterative nature of the algorithm, the need for parallelized linear algebra operations on distributed sparse matrices, and large-scale parameter optimization. Key computational steps include GPU-accelerated tensor decomposition, dynamic load balancing for irregular grid refinements, and ensemble simulations to quantify numerical uncertainty. The project will leverage MPI for inter-node communication and CUDA for fine-grained parallelism, with validation against exact solutions in lower dimensions and benchmark quantum systems. Successful implementation will yield a publicly available software toolkit for high-dimensional PDEs, advancing mathematical tools for quantum mechanics and nonlinear wave propagation. Outcomes will demonstrate the feasibility of resolving 8-10 dimensional quantum systems with sub-exponential computational costs, providing a pathway to study entanglement dynamics and decoherence in scalable settings. This work bridges theoretical numerical analysis and practical HPC innovations, offering broadly applicable strategies for dimensionality reduction in computational mathematics.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of theoretical and applied mathematics to the solution of functional problems. Includes instruction in numerical analysis, numerical statistics, optimization, operational research, signal analysis, wavelets, image processing, fuzzy sets, spline, stochastic analysis, integral equations, differential equations, and partial differential equations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address complex, interconnected challenges in urban sustainability and community resilience through a multidisciplinary lens. Urban systems are inherently dynamic, involving feedback loops between socioeconomic factors, environmental stressors, and infrastructure demands. Traditional analytical tools often fail to capture these nonlinear interactions at scale, particularly when integrating heterogeneous datasets spanning demographics, climate projections, and real-time sensor networks. The research problem centers on developing a scalable computational framework to model urban systems as adaptive networks, enabling policymakers to test intervention strategies under diverse scenarios. The proposed approach combines agent-based modeling (ABM) with machine learning-driven optimization to simulate decision-making processes across individual, institutional, and infrastructural actors. HPC resources are critical for parallelizing thousands of scenario iterations that account for variable climate patterns, population growth trajectories, and resource allocation policies. Key computational challenges include managing sparse matrix operations for large-scale network analysis and training graph neural networks on temporally evolving urban datasets. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation platform capable of identifying leverage points for sustainable urban transitions, with specific applications to energy equity and flood resilience planning. The project’s significance lies in its integration of computational social science, environmental informatics, and complex systems theory—a convergence unique to interdisciplinary general studies. By creating transferable methodologies for coupling qualitative social dynamics with quantitative environmental data, this work will provide actionable insights for cities facing compound crises. The requested computing resources will enable parameter space exploration at unprecedented resolution, directly supporting graduate student training in transdisciplinary computational research while fostering collaborations between urban planners, data scientists, and community stakeholders. Results will be disseminated through interactive data visualizations and policy briefs alongside traditional academic publications.
cip_definition: An undifferentiated program that includes instruction in the general arts, general science, or unstructured studies.

abstract: The increasing complexity of global supply chain networks, compounded by demand volatility, logistical disruptions, and sustainability requirements, poses significant challenges for managerial decision-making. Traditional analytical models often fail to account for dynamic interdependencies among stakeholders, stochastic disruptions, and multi-objective trade-offs between cost efficiency and environmental impact. This project proposes a computational framework to optimize resilient and sustainable supply chain strategies using high-performance computing (HPC). We will develop agent-based simulations to model interactions among suppliers, manufacturers, and distributors under uncertainty, integrating real-world data on demand fluctuations, geopolitical risks, and carbon emissions. Machine learning techniques will be applied to forecast disruption probabilities and adaptive responses, while parallelized mixed-integer programming will optimize network reconfiguration and inventory policies across scenarios. The scale of these computations—encompassing millions of variables, non-linear constraints, and real-time sensitivity analyses—exceeds the capacity of standard computing infrastructure, necessitating HPC resources for distributed memory processing and GPU-accelerated optimization. Anticipated outcomes include a decision-support tool that quantifies trade-offs between operational resilience, cost, and sustainability metrics, enabling firms to dynamically adjust procurement, production, and distribution strategies. This research will advance management theory by formalizing computational frameworks for complexity-driven decision-making, while providing empirical insights into scalable strategies for mitigating systemic risks in global supply chains. The project also highlights the transformative role of HPC in bridging theoretical operations research with practical business applications, offering a replicable methodology for data-intensive management challenges. Results will be disseminated through open-source toolkits and case studies demonstrating computational efficiency gains over conventional optimization approaches.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to plan, organize, direct, and control the functions and processes of a firm or organization. Includes instruction in management theory, human resources management and behavior, accounting and other quantitative methods, purchasing and logistics, organization and production, marketing, and business decision-making.

abstract: Veterinary practice faces growing challenges in managing complex, multimodal data—including medical records, diagnostic imaging, and longitudinal treatment outcomes—to optimize clinical decision-making and operational workflows. Current analytical methods often lack the scalability and precision required to synthesize these heterogeneous datasets, limiting the ability to predict patient outcomes, tailor care protocols, or allocate clinic resources efficiently. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational models that integrate clinical, imaging, and operational data from veterinary practices. The research will focus on three interconnected aims: (1) creating machine learning frameworks to predict treatment responses and disease progression in companion animals using electronic health records and diagnostic imaging data, (2) simulating clinic workflow dynamics to identify operational bottlenecks and test resource allocation strategies, and (3) optimizing image analysis pipelines for rapid, automated interpretation of radiographs, ultrasounds, and MRIs. Computational methods will include deep learning architectures (e.g., convolutional neural networks for image segmentation), agent-based modeling for clinic operations, and ensemble techniques for multi-modal data fusion. By utilizing HPC infrastructure, these resource-intensive tasks—such as training models on terabyte-scale imaging datasets or running high-fidelity simulations of clinic networks—can be executed with the necessary speed and parallelism. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for predictive analytics in veterinary care, evidence-based guidelines for practice management, and improved diagnostic accuracy through AI-assisted imaging analysis. This work will directly enhance the capacity of veterinary practices to deliver personalized, data-driven care while maintaining operational sustainability, ultimately benefiting animal patients, their owners, and clinical teams. The project underscores the critical role of scalable computing in modernizing veterinary medicine and bridging translational gaps between clinical research and day-to-day practice.
cip_definition: Research focused on the provision of regular and long-term care to animals, health services to owners, and the management of independent veterinary practices. May included related research in comprehensive care and specialist referral, basic surgery, emergency medical procedures, and diagnostic imaging.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational study of cross-cultural religious textual traditions, addressing gaps in scalability and analytical depth within current digital humanities methodologies. The research problem centers on the challenge of systematically analyzing patterns in religious thought, symbolism, and narrative structures across vast, multilingual corpora, including Buddhist sutras, Abrahamic scriptures, and Indigenous oral tradition transcriptions. Traditional close-reading approaches struggle to identify latent thematic connections or quantify doctrinal evolution at scale, particularly when examining understudied textual interactions between major and minor religious traditions. To address this, we propose a multi-modal computational framework combining natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and machine learning classification. The workflow will process digitized primary texts in original languages (Sanskrit, Pali, Classical Arabic, etc.) and translations using transformer-based models fine-tuned for historical religious language, enabling semantic similarity mapping and motif tracking across traditions. Network models will then visualize the diffusion of cosmological concepts and ritual practices, while clustering algorithms will identify statistically significant variations in ethical frameworks. HPC resources are critical for training domain-specific language models, managing terabyte-scale textual datasets, and running iterative simulations of hypothetical transmission pathways. Expected outcomes include 1) a publicly accessible knowledge graph mapping interreligious conceptual exchanges in South Asian and Mediterranean contexts between 200 BCE–500 CE, 2) quantitative models challenging assumptions about doctrinal boundaries in syncretic traditions, and 3) open-source tools for automated comparative analysis of ritual narratives. By enabling systematic large-scale comparison, this work aims to redefine scholarly understanding of how religious ideas hybridize across cultural contexts while establishing computational methods as central to future phenomenological studies in religion. The requested resources directly support the development of reproducible, data-driven frameworks for analyzing religious pluralism—a pressing need in interdisciplinary humanities research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the nature of religious belief and specific religious and quasi-religious systems. Includes instruction in phenomenology; the sociology, psychology, philosophy, anthropology, literature and art of religion; mythology; scriptural and textual studies; religious history and politics; and specific studies of particular faith communities and their behavior.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an integrated modeling framework to evaluate the effectiveness of conservation policies under climate-driven uncertainties in transboundary watersheds. Managing shared water and forest resources across political boundaries presents complex challenges, as conflicting stakeholder priorities, asymmetric climate impacts, and fragmented governance often lead to unsustainable outcomes. Current decision-support tools lack the capacity to simulate multi-scale interactions between ecological dynamics, policy interventions, and climate scenarios at sufficient spatial-temporal resolution. To address this gap, we propose coupling a hydrodynamic model with an agent-based policy simulation platform, leveraging high-resolution satellite data on land use, hydrological regimes, and ecosystem services. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to execute ensemble simulations capturing 1) climate projections from CMIP6 under multiple emission scenarios, 2) adaptive policy interventions across jurisdictional boundaries, and 3) cascading impacts on biodiversity corridors and water availability. The computational workflow will parallelize parameter space exploration across 50+ policy-climate combinations at 100m spatial resolution for three case study watersheds in climate-vulnerable regions. Machine learning techniques will then reduce output dimensionality to identify policy configurations that maximize ecological resilience while minimizing cross-border trade-offs. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source tool for participatory scenario testing and policy prioritization, along with comparative analyses of institutional design principles that enhance adaptation capacity. By quantifying how distributed decision-making interacts with non-linear environmental changes, this work will provide critical insights for multilateral agreements on sustainable resource governance. The requested HPC allocation will enable computationally intensive simulations that traditional workstation clusters cannot support, particularly for fine-grained spatial optimization and uncertainty propagation across decade-scale horizons.
detailed_field: Environmental/ natural resources management and policy
cip_title: Environmental/ Natural Resources Management and Policy, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in environmental or natural resources management and policy, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of decentralized communication networks in large organizations using high-performance computing (HPC) to model emergent patterns of information flow, conflict resolution, and team cohesion. As organizations increasingly adopt distributed work structures, understanding how communication practices adapt—particularly in contexts mediated by digital platforms—is critical. Existing research lacks scalable models to analyze how real-time, multi-channel interactions (e.g., chat, video, collaborative documents) shape collective decision-making or reinforce power asymmetries in teams exceeding 500 members. To address this gap, we propose simulating organizational communication networks via agent-based modeling (ABM) and natural language processing (NLP) techniques. The ABM framework will parameterize agents with communication behaviors derived from anonymized organizational datasets (e.g., email metadata, meeting transcripts), while NLP pipelines will analyze semantic patterns in internal documentation to infer cultural norms. HPC resources are essential to handle the combinatorial complexity of modeling thousands of agents interacting across multiple virtual platforms, with simulations iterating over variables such as message latency, hierarchy transparency, and conflict escalation thresholds. Expected outcomes include identifying conditions under which decentralized communication structures improve problem-solving efficiency or inadvertently exacerbate systemic inequities. Results will contribute actionable insights for designing communication protocols in hybrid workplaces and advance computational methods for organizational research. By coupling large-scale simulations with empirical validation, this project bridges theoretical frameworks in organizational communication with data-driven computational social science, offering a replicable model for studying emergent phenomena in complex human systems.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on general communication processes and dynamics within organizations. Includes instruction in the development and maintenance of interpersonal group relations within organizations; decision-making and conflict management; the use of symbols to create and maintain organizational images, missions, and values; power and politics within organizations; human interaction with computer technology; and how communications socializes and supports employees and team members.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving legal and regulatory frameworks governing autonomous vehicle (AV) deployment across multimodal transportation networks. While existing scholarship in transportation law focuses on doctrinal or policy-based critiques, this research addresses a computational gap: modeling how heterogeneous legal regimes—spanning municipal, state, federal, and international jurisdictions—interact dynamically with rapidly advancing AV technologies. The complexity arises from (1) the scale of interconnected regulations (e.g., liability statutes, data privacy mandates, infrastructure standards) and (2) the need to simulate how emergent case law and regulatory amendments propagate uncertainty across transportation systems. Using a mixed-methods approach, the project will develop a graph-based computational model to map regulatory dependencies and conflicts, paired with agent-based simulations to evaluate how hypothetical legal scenarios influence AV adoption rates and operational risk profiles. Natural language processing (NLP) pipelines will process over 10,000 legal documents (statutes, court opinions, administrative rulings) to extract relational features, while Monte Carlo methods will quantify uncertainties in liability attribution under varying regulatory conditions. The HPC environment is critical for scaling graph traversals across multi-jurisdictional legal networks and running high-fidelity simulations incorporating real-world transportation data. Anticipated outcomes include a publicly accessible digital toolkit for policymakers to stress-test proposed regulations and a taxonomy of "legal friction points" that impede cross-jurisdictional AV interoperability. By integrating computational social science with transportation law, this work aims to establish a replicable framework for analyzing complex legal systems as dynamic, data-driven networks, offering novel insights into the governance of emerging technologies in non-science/engineering domains.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting land, sea, air, and space transportation.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of intersectional identity formation within diasporic digital communities, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze large-scale, multilingual textual and multimedia data. While existing scholarship has explored offline identity negotiation, the rapid growth of online spaces—particularly those created by and for ethnic, cultural, and gender minorities—presents novel challenges in understanding how marginalized groups construct collective narratives across decentralized platforms. Current methodological approaches struggle to process the scale and linguistic diversity of user-generated content, which often incorporates code-switching, non-standard dialects, and visual symbolism. Our research addresses this gap by developing a computational framework combining transformer-based natural language processing, multimodal network analysis, and community-detection algorithms optimized for low-resource languages. The proposed workflow will process terabytes of data from moderated forums, social media archives, and collaborative storytelling platforms, with a focus on Southeast Asian queer diaspora communities and Black feminist digital collectives. HPC resources are critical for training custom multilingual embedding models, conducting hyperparameter optimization for cultural context-aware classification, and running iterative simulations of cross-platform narrative diffusion. Expected outcomes include (1) a novel dataset annotating intersectional identity markers in non-institutional digital spaces, (2) open-source tools for ethical computational analysis of minority-led online communities, and (3) theoretical insights into how algorithmic platform architectures both constrain and enable resistant identity work. By centering computational methods within cultural and group studies paradigms, this work aims to advance interdisciplinary methodologies for studying digital marginalization while maintaining rigorous ethical safeguards for vulnerable populations. The requested GPU cluster allocations and parallel storage systems will enable processing at scales previously inaccessible to qualitative-dominant fields, bridging critical theory with computational social science.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_title: Ethnic, Cultural Minority, Gender, and Group Studies, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in ethnic, cultural minority, gender, and group studies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of digital content distribution and audience engagement in the publishing industry by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model and optimize multi-platform publishing workflows. As the volume of digital content escalates and reader preferences fragment across formats (e.g., e-books, audiobooks, interactive media), publishers face challenges in efficiently allocating editorial, technical, and marketing resources while maintaining ethical and copyright compliance. Traditional methods for workflow analysis and market prediction lack the scalability to process real-time, multimodal data from global distribution channels, social media, and consumer analytics platforms. This research proposes a computational approach combining natural language processing (NLP), agent-based modeling, and machine learning to simulate publishing ecosystems. NLP will analyze textual content trends and reader feedback at scale, while agent-based models will replicate decision-making processes across editorial, production, and marketing teams under dynamic market conditions. Machine learning algorithms will identify patterns in historical sales and engagement data to predict optimal resource allocation strategies for emerging formats and demographics. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, including cross-platform user interaction logs and copyright metadata, to evaluate scenarios such as the impact of AI-driven editorial tools or shifts in digital rights management frameworks. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for ethical resource allocation in hybrid (print/digital) publishing environments, predictive models to reduce operational bottlenecks, and actionable insights into sustainable audience expansion strategies. By integrating computational rigor with publishing industry expertise, this project aims to advance evidence-based practices for content lifecycle management, directly supporting publishers in balancing innovation with profitability and accessibility.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the process of managing the creation, publication, and distribution of print and electronic books and other text products and prepares individuals to manage the editorial, technical, and business aspects of publishing operations. Includes instruction in product planning and design, editing, author relations, business and copyright law, publishing industry operations, contracting and purchasing, product marketing, electronic publishing and commerce, history of publishing, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the understanding of equine biomechanics and rider-horse interaction dynamics, a critical yet understudied area in equestrian science. Despite the global economic and cultural significance of equine industries, quantitative models capable of predicting stress patterns in horses during training or competition remain limited. Traditional methods rely on observational data and simplified physical assessments, which lack the resolution to map complex musculoskeletal loads or optimize welfare-focused training protocols. To address this gap, we propose developing a multiscale computational framework integrating motion-capture data, finite element analysis (FEA), and machine learning (ML) to simulate and analyze equine movement under varying riding conditions. High-fidelity 3D models of horse-rider pairs, derived from MRI and LiDAR scans, will be subjected to dynamic load simulations across gaits (walk, trot, canter) and jumping sequences. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of terabyte-scale datasets, including muscle activation patterns, ground reaction forces, and saddle pressure distributions, while ML algorithms will identify predictive biomarkers for injury risk and performance efficiency. The project will validate models against empirical data from inertial measurement units (IMUs) and force plates collected from collegiate equestrian teams. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible computational toolkit for trainers and veterinarians to customize training regimens, reduce musculoskeletal injuries, and improve equine longevity. By bridging computational biomechanics with equestrian practice, this work aims to establish a paradigm for data-driven decision-making in a field traditionally reliant on subjective expertise, while demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in non-STEM disciplines aligned with animal welfare and human-equine partnerships.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the horse, horsemanship, and related subjects and prepares individuals to care for horses and horse equipment; ride and drive horses for leisure, sport, show, and professional purposes; and manage the training of horses and riders. Includes instruction in horse breeding, nutrition, health, and safety; history of the horse and horsemanship; horse development and training; riding and equestrian technique; stable, paddock, and track management; and equipment maintenance and repair.

abstract: Otolaryngologic disorders, such as head and neck cancers, chronic sinusitis, and hearing loss, involve complex interactions between genetic, molecular, and structural factors. Traditional analytical methods often struggle to integrate multimodal data—including high-resolution imaging, genomic sequencing, and patient-specific clinical records—at scales necessary to uncover actionable insights. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop advanced computational models that elucidate disease mechanisms and optimize therapeutic strategies. Using machine learning algorithms, we will analyze multi-omics datasets from tumor biopsies to identify biomarkers predictive of treatment response and metastasis in squamous cell carcinoma. Concurrently, computational fluid dynamics simulations will model sinonasal airflow in chronic rhinosinusitis patients, enabling personalized surgical planning to restore physiologic function. HPC infrastructure is critical to process terabytes of imaging data, perform real-time probabilistic network analyses on genomic interactions, and execute large-scale parameter sweeps in patient-specific anatomies. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for oncology decision support, optimized surgical approaches for airway disorders, and open-source tools for integrating heterogeneous clinical data. By harnessing HPC capabilities, this research aims to accelerate translational discoveries in otolaryngology, bridging gaps between molecular insights and patient-centered care.
cip_definition: Research focused on that prepares physicians to diagnose and provide medical and/or surgical therapy or prevention of diseases, allergies, neoplasms, deformities, disorders, and injuries of the ears, nose, sinuses, throat, respiratory and upper alimentary systems, face, jaws, and the other head and neck systems.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a computational framework for automating and optimizing the analysis of complex legal document networks, a critical but labor-intensive task in paralegal workflows. The research addresses the challenge of efficiently identifying patterns, contradictions, and jurisdictional variances within large corpora of legal texts—including court opinions, statutory codes, and contractual agreements—which currently require manual review or limited keyword-based tools. By integrating natural language processing (NLP) with graph theory, the proposed system will map semantic relationships and citation networks across multi-jurisdictional legal databases, enabling predictive modeling of case outcomes and precedent influence. Computational methods will include transformer-based language models fine-tuned on legal terminology, coupled with community detection algorithms to isolate coherent legal argument clusters. The scale of data—encompassing millions of publicly available court records and legislative texts—necessitates HPC capabilities for distributed training of deep learning architectures and real-time graph traversal operations. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for paralegal professionals to rapidly assess case law relevance, predict litigation risks, and generate draft memoranda with citation support. This interdisciplinary approach bridges legal informatics and computational linguistics, offering a novel methodology for legal assistance that prioritizes both accuracy and ethical AI deployment. By reducing time spent on document review by an estimated 40–60%, the project aims to democratize access to advanced legal analytics for under-resourced practices, while establishing benchmarks for responsible AI use in non-science domains. Results will be validated against manual analyses conducted by collaborating legal professionals, ensuring practical utility within paralegal education and workflows.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform research, drafting, investigatory, record-keeping and related administrative functions under the supervision of an attorney or court. Includes instruction in legal research, drafting legal documents, appraising, pleading, courthouse procedures, and legal specializations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address critical gaps in the study of African state formation and transnational cultural exchange from the 15th to 19th centuries. Research in African history faces unique challenges due to the scale, diversity, and fragmentation of sources—including oral traditions, archaeological datasets, colonial administrative records, and multilingual manuscripts—which hinder systematic analysis of long-term sociopolitical dynamics. This project proposes a computational approach integrating natural language processing (NLP), geospatial network modeling, and agent-based simulations to analyze these heterogeneous datasets at unprecedented scale. Key objectives include reconstructing trade and migration networks across precolonial West Africa using geocoded archaeological data, quantifying linguistic shifts in colonial-era correspondence through multilingual NLP pipelines, and simulating the impact of environmental stressors on state resilience via probabilistic climate-event models. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing terabyte-scale digitized archives, training transformer models on low-resource African languages, and running iterative simulations of complex social systems. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible geotemporal database of African political entities, new methods for cross-referencing oral and written historical sources, and quantitative frameworks for evaluating competing theories of state collapse and cultural diffusion. By enabling large-scale pattern recognition across dispersed and understudied sources, this work aims to reshape historiographical debates about African agency, connectivity, and adaptation while establishing computational humanities workflows tailored to the continent’s diverse evidentiary landscape. The requested resources will directly support the first systematic computational analysis of state formation processes in precolonial Africa, with implications for global historical scholarship and heritage preservation initiatives.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of the societies, cultures, and institutions of one or more peoples of the African Continent, usually with an emphasis on Africa south of the Sahara (and including the African diasporas overseas) from their origins to the present. Includes instruction in the historiography of specific cultures and periods; sources and materials; historical research methods; and applications to the study of specific themes, issues, periods, and institutions.

abstract: The increasing complexity of multi-omics data in comparative disease models presents a critical challenge in identifying molecular mechanisms shared between laboratory animals and humans. Current analytical workflows often lack the computational power to integrate heterogeneous datasets—such as genomics, proteomics, and metabolomics—across species, limiting insights into conserved disease pathways. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a scalable computational framework for cross-species analysis of experimental animal models, with a focus on immune-mediated disorders. Using machine learning algorithms, we will train species-agnostic models on existing multi-omics repositories to predict conserved biomarkers of chronic inflammation. Molecular dynamics simulations will further elucidate protein interaction networks perturbed in these conditions, leveraging comparative gene mapping data from murine, porcine, and non-human primate models. The HPC environment is essential for managing large-scale genomic alignments, parallelized simulations, and iterative model training, which exceed the capacity of local computing infrastructure. Expected outcomes include predictive models of disease susceptibility, prioritized therapeutic targets, and optimized protocols for translational studies. By enhancing the resolution of cross-species analyses, this work will advance the ethical refinement of animal models through reduced experimental variability and improved preclinical trial design. The resulting tools will be disseminated as open-source packages to support reproducible research in laboratory animal medicine, aligning with institutional goals to integrate computational biology into veterinary training programs. This project directly addresses the program’s emphasis on bioethics, computational modeling, and interdisciplinary approaches to experimental animal science, with implications for both human medicine and laboratory animal welfare.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of animal models of human disease and related experimental procedures, and prepares veterinarians and animal health specialists to manage the laboratory use and care of experimental animals. Includes instruction in laboratory animal husbandry, laboratory animal disease, biohazard control, gnotobiology, breeding, comparative anatomy and physiology, comparative gene mapping, protein function, physical and mathematical modeling, computer modeling, stem cell technology, colony and genetic stock management, cryopreservation, applicable regulations, and bioethics.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze and model the socio-spiritual dynamics of urban communities, focusing on the optimization of ministry interventions in rapidly changing metropolitan environments. Urban ministry practitioners face complex challenges, including transient populations, systemic inequality, and fragmented community networks, which hinder the efficacy of traditional outreach and support strategies. Current approaches often rely on qualitative assessments or small-scale surveys, limiting the ability to predict emergent needs or evaluate systemic impacts of interventions. This project addresses this gap by developing computational frameworks to integrate heterogeneous datasets—such as demographic records, public health metrics, geospatial activity patterns, and anonymized community engagement logs—into predictive models of urban spiritual and social needs. Agent-based modeling will simulate interactions between individuals, ministry organizations, and urban infrastructures to test hypothetical interventions, while natural language processing (NLP) will analyze historical sermon texts, community feedback, and social media discourse to identify patterns in spiritual concerns across demographic groups. Graph-based network analysis will map relational ties within urban populations to optimize resource allocation and collaborative partnerships. By deploying these methods on HPC infrastructure, the project aims to process large-scale datasets (spanning multiple cities and decades) and run iterative, high-resolution simulations that account for variables like migration flows, economic shifts, and crisis events. Anticipated outcomes include a scalable digital toolkit for urban ministry leaders, offering evidence-based strategies for adaptive community engagement, crisis response, and long-term resilience-building. This interdisciplinary work bridges computational social science, theology, and urban studies, advancing methodological innovation in humanities research while addressing pressing practical challenges in under-resourced urban contexts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares the ordained clergy and other religious professionals to provide spiritual, counseling, and leadership services to individuals and groups in urban communities. Includes instruction in bible study and theology, pastoral leadership and care, urban structure and context, inner city ministry, counseling ministries, family studies, homiletics, social ethics, and community organizing.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research in business and economic journalism by addressing the challenges of analyzing large-scale, dynamic datasets in real time. Business journalists increasingly confront complex financial markets, global supply chain disruptions, and rapidly evolving economic indicators, yet traditional analytical tools often lack the capacity to process heterogeneous data streams—including structured financial records, unstructured corporate disclosures, and social media sentiment—at the speed and scale required for timely reporting. The research problem centers on developing computational workflows that integrate machine learning, natural language processing (NLP), and network analysis to identify trends, anomalies, and narratives within these datasets. Proposed methods include training transformer-based models to extract semantic patterns from earnings calls and regulatory filings, applying graph algorithms to map interdependencies in global trade networks, and deploying ensemble forecasting techniques to predict market reactions to geopolitical events. These workflows will be optimized for parallel processing and GPU acceleration to handle terabyte-scale datasets. Expected outcomes include a suite of open-source tools tailored for journalistic investigations, enabling faster identification of underreported economic stories (e.g., supply chain vulnerabilities, regulatory arbitrage) and democratizing access to advanced analytics for newsrooms with limited technical infrastructure. The project also aims to produce methodological frameworks for ethically integrating automated insights into reporting processes, addressing concerns around algorithmic bias and transparency. By enhancing the computational rigor of business journalism, this work will strengthen public understanding of economic systems while maintaining the discipline’s emphasis on accuracy, context, and accountability. Resource requests include GPU nodes for model training, high-memory nodes for large-scale NLP tasks, and scalable storage for curating annotated datasets spanning financial, corporate, and media sources.
cip_definition: A program of study that prepares students to gather, analyze, and synthesize verbal and visual information to communicate stories related to business and economics across multiple media platforms. Includes instruction in accounting, business, business and economic reporting, business law, economics, finance, financial accounting and reporting, ethics, journalistic research methods and resources, and journalism skills and techniques.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research at the intersection of patent law, algorithmic decision-making, and large-scale textual analysis. The core problem addressed is the growing complexity of patent examination processes, particularly the challenge of evaluating prior art and patentability criteria across rapidly evolving technological domains. Traditional legal research methods struggle to systematically analyze the vast corpus of global patent documents, legal precedents, and technical literature required to assess patent quality or predict litigation outcomes. To address this, the project will develop computational models using natural language processing (NLP) and graph-based network analysis to map citation patterns, semantic relationships in patent claims, and historical trends in patent office decisions. HPC resources will enable processing of multi-terabyte datasets spanning USPTO, EPO, and WIPO records alongside federal court rulings and scientific publications. Key computational challenges include training domain-specific language models for legal-technical texts, implementing distributed algorithms for temporal network analysis of patent citations, and simulating policy scenarios under alternative patentability standards. Anticipated outcomes include 1) a framework for quantifying semantic similarity in patent claims to identify potential conflicts, 2) predictive models of patent validity challenges based on historical examination patterns, and 3) visual analytics tools for tracing technological evolution through patent landscapes. This work bridges computational social science and legal informatics, offering novel methodologies for patent scholars while providing practical tools to enhance transparency in patent systems. The resource-intensive nature of processing legally sensitive documents at scale necessitates specialized HPC infrastructure with secure data handling capabilities, parallel processing for ensemble machine learning models, and high-memory nodes for graph computations spanning millions of patent documents. Results will inform ongoing debates about algorithmic assistance in legal decision-making and contribute to evidence-based patent policy reform.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting patents.

abstract: The proposed research investigates the molecular mechanisms underlying plant circadian rhythm plasticity in response to non-canonical environmental stressors, specifically nanoparticulate pollutants and polarized light regimes. While plant circadian systems are well-studied under typical abiotic stresses, emerging anthropogenic factors create unique spatiotemporal signaling challenges that existing models cannot resolve. This project employs a novel computational framework integrating live-cell imaging data of organelle dynamics with hyperspectral fluorescence correlation spectroscopy (FCS) datasets to map real-time protein-cofactor interactions in Arabidopsis thaliana under controlled stress matrices. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process terabytes of light sheet microscopy videos (captured at 30 fps over 72-hour cycles) using convolutional neural networks trained to detect phase-shift patterns in chloroplast-nucleus signaling. Molecular dynamics simulations will parameterize newly discovered cryptochrome-phytochrome heterodimers observed in preliminary studies, requiring GPU-accelerated sampling of 10+ microsecond trajectories to characterize allosteric regulation under quantum mechanical/molecular mechanical (QM/MM) constraints. Expected outcomes include 1) a predictive model of circadian entrainment thresholds for engineered nanoparticle exposure, 2) identification of plasticity-mediating phosphorylation motifs in clock-associated proteins through comparative kinome network analysis, and 3) open-source tools for correlative 4D organelle tracking across heterogeneous cell populations. This work bridges plant molecular biology with environmental nanotoxicology and quantum biology, addressing critical gaps in understanding how non-linear stressors disrupt temporal coordination of photosynthesis and stress adaptation. The computational infrastructure will enable unprecedented resolution of plant circadian systems at multiple scales, directly informing biotechnological strategies to enhance crop resilience in rapidly changing light pollution and nanomaterial-impacted ecosystems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of molecular biology, biochemistry, and biophysics to the study of biomolecular structures, functions, and processes specific to plants and plant substances. Includes instruction in the biochemistry of plant cells, nuclear-cytoplasmic interactions, molecular cytostructures, photosynthesis, plant molecular genetics, and the molecular biology of plant diseases.

abstract: Montessori pedagogy emphasizes individualized, self-directed learning within mixed-age classrooms, yet the dynamic interplay between student autonomy, teacher guidance, and environmental design remains understudied at scale. This project seeks to model the efficacy of Montessori instructional strategies using agent-based simulations to optimize teacher training frameworks. The research problem centers on identifying how computational modeling can predict the outcomes of Montessori practices—such as material selection, lesson sequencing, and classroom spatial organization—on student engagement and skill acquisition. Current studies rely on small observational datasets or qualitative assessments, limiting generalizability. To address this gap, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulation platform that replicates multi-agent classroom environments. The computational approach integrates behavioral data from Montessori classrooms (e.g., student-teacher interactions, material usage patterns, and movement logs) into adaptive algorithms that simulate learning trajectories under varying pedagogical conditions. Each agent will employ reinforcement learning to mimic child decision-making aligned with Montessori principles of intrinsic motivation. Parallelized Monte Carlo methods will assess thousands of parameter combinations to identify optimal teacher interventions. The HPC infrastructure is critical for managing the stochasticity and combinatorial complexity inherent in modeling heterogeneous student cohorts over extended time horizons. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive tool to evaluate the impact of specific Montessori training modules on classroom outcomes, (2) data-driven recommendations for personalizing teacher guidance strategies, and (3) an open-source framework for simulating developmental pedagogies. This work will directly inform the design of competency-based assessments in Montessori teacher education programs, enhancing the scalability of training while preserving pedagogical fidelity. By bridging computational analytics with Montessori theory, the project advances a novel paradigm for evidence-driven teacher preparation in specialized educational methodologies.
detailed_field: Teacher education, specific levels and methods
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach students at various grade levels according to the pedagogical principles and methods developed by Maria Montessori and her followers.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to analyze and optimize the integration of live musical theatre performance elements—vocal delivery, choreography, and technical staging—using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. While musical theatre relies on the real-time synchronization of diverse artistic and technical components, existing methods for evaluating performance cohesion remain largely subjective or constrained by small-scale empirical studies. This research addresses the challenge of modeling complex interactions between performers, audience perception, and technical systems (e.g., acoustics, lighting) in dynamic, large-venue environments. The computational approach combines biomechanical motion capture data, real-time vocal acoustics analysis, and audience sightline simulations to quantify performance coherence. Machine learning models will be trained on multimodal datasets—including historical performance recordings, sensor data from wearable devices on actors, and environmental variables from stage machinery—to identify patterns in successful artistic integration. HPC resources are essential for processing terabytes of audiovisual data, running parallelized simulations of audience experience across seating configurations, and optimizing reinforcement learning algorithms for adaptive technical cueing systems. Expected outcomes include predictive models to guide rehearsal prioritization, a digital twin framework for pre-visualizing staging choices, and evidence-based recommendations for balancing artistic expression with technical feasibility. By establishing quantitative metrics for traditionally qualitative aspects of musical theatre, this work aims to advance pedagogical tools for training performers and technicians while enhancing the scalability of productions across diverse venues. The computational pipeline developed here will be shared as an open-source toolkit, fostering collaboration between performing arts practitioners and computational researchers.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles and techniques for integrating theatre, music, and dance into a unified production. Includes instruction in acting, dance, voice, technical theater, musical genres, piano, and history of musical theater.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a high-resolution simulation framework to optimize dynamic pricing, inventory management, and workforce scheduling in omnichannel retail environments. Retail businesses face escalating complexity in balancing real-time demand fluctuations across physical and digital channels while maintaining profitability and customer satisfaction. Traditional analytical models struggle to account for interdependent variables such as localized consumer behavior, supply chain disruptions, seasonal trends, and labor constraints at scale. We propose an interdisciplinary computational approach integrating agent-based modeling, machine learning, and discrete-event simulation to create a decision-support system for retail managers. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to train deep reinforcement learning models on historical transaction data (POS systems, e-commerce logs, inventory records) and simulate millions of scenario permutations across heterogeneous retail configurations. The agent-based component will model customer purchasing patterns and employee-customer interactions using behavioral data from loyalty programs and workforce management platforms. Parallelized Monte Carlo methods will assess risk profiles for inventory strategies under stochastic demand conditions. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to minimize stockouts and markdown losses while improving service levels, with sensitivity analyses quantifying trade-offs between staffing costs and sales conversion rates. This work will advance retail management research by enabling granular, system-wide optimization previously constrained by computational limitations. Results will be validated against real-world case studies from partner retailers, with open-source release of core simulation modules to support academic and industry collaboration. The project directly addresses critical gaps in retail operational agility, particularly for small-to-midsize businesses adapting to rapid market shifts.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage the operations of a wide variety of retail businesses, including department stores; independent and chain stores; fashion, food and beverage, and pharmaceutical establishments; and online retail businesses. Includes instruction in retail management, merchandise management, customer service management, marketing, organizational behavior, accounting, finance, business law, and personnel management.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance the fidelity and scalability of flight simulation environments to address critical challenges in pilot training and operational safety within dynamic airspace conditions. Current simulation tools often lack the computational capacity to model complex, real-time interactions between aircraft systems, environmental variables, and human decision-making with sufficient granularity. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for simulating multifactorial flight scenarios, including extreme weather, system failures, and high-density air traffic. The computational approach integrates computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models for aircraft performance, machine learning algorithms to simulate adaptive pilot responses, and large-scale Monte Carlo methods to statistically evaluate risk across thousands of parallelized scenarios. By leveraging GPU-accelerated computing and distributed memory architectures, the framework will resolve high-resolution aerodynamic interactions, real-time weather data assimilation, and multi-crew communication dynamics at scale. Expected outcomes include the identification of previously undetected risk patterns in emergency procedures, optimization of cockpit resource management protocols, and the generation of synthetic training datasets to improve pilot preparedness for rare but high-consequence events. The results will directly inform updates to FAA-approved training curricula and provide a validated platform for testing next-generation aviation technologies, such as AI-assisted navigation systems. This work addresses a critical gap in aviation safety research, where traditional methods struggle to account for the nonlinear interdependencies between human, technical, and environmental factors in modern flight operations. Access to HPC resources is essential to achieve the required computational throughput for these massively parallel simulations while maintaining the low-latency performance necessary for real-time training applications.
cip_title: Airline/ Commercial/ Professional Pilot and Flight Crew
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to the flying and/or navigation of commercial passenger and cargo, agricultural, public service, corporate and rescue fixed wing aircraft. Includes instruction in principles of aircraft design and performance, aircraft flight systems and controls, flight crew operations and procedures, radio communications, navigation procedures and systems, airways safety and traffic regulations, and governmental rules and regulations pertaining to piloting aircraft. Programs may qualify individuals to sit for the FAA commercial and airline aircrew examinations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance understanding of the biopsychosocial mechanisms underlying psychosocial stress and its impact on cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk—a critical issue in health/medical psychology. Current models often oversimplify the dynamic interactions between psychological stressors, behavioral coping strategies, and physiological biomarkers, limiting their utility in designing effective, personalized interventions. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating multilevel longitudinal data—including psychometric surveys, wearable device outputs (e.g., heart rate variability), and clinical biomarkers—from a diverse cohort of 5,000 participants. Agent-based modeling will simulate how individual differences in stress appraisal and coping behaviors interact with social determinants (e.g., socioeconomic status) to influence cardiovascular outcomes over time. Concurrently, machine learning pipelines will identify nonlinear patterns and predictive signatures of CVD risk progression. These analyses demand HPC capabilities due to the scale of heterogeneous data, the computational intensity of Bayesian hierarchical models (to handle missing data and temporal dependencies), and the need for high-dimensional parameter space exploration in simulations. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational model clarifying how psychosocial factors modulate physiological stress pathways, (2) actionable risk stratification tools to guide preventive behavioral interventions, and (3) open-source software for scalable analysis of biopsychosocial datasets. By elucidating mechanisms linking psychological processes to health outcomes, this work will directly inform counseling strategies and community-based prevention programs, aligning with the health/medical psychology focus on integrative, non-clinical interventions. The requested resources are essential to overcome current computational bottlenecks in modeling complex, real-world biopsychosocial interactions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the psychological study of health and illness, and recovery, from the perspective that these phenomena arise from a combination of physical, behavioral, and social conditions. Includes instruction in abnormal and social psychology, psychophysiology, psychopharmacology, learning processes, clinical and behavioral therapies, biopsychosocial modeling, clinical procedures and assessment, preventive education, psychotherapy, rehabilitation processes, and research methods.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the multi-dimensional drivers of economic development disparities across low- and middle-income countries, with a focus on infrastructure investment, industrialization pathways, and policy coordination. A persistent challenge in development economics is modeling the dynamic, non-linear interactions between public-sector decisions, private-sector responses, and exogenous shocks (e.g., climate stressors, commodity price volatility) at subnational and transnational scales. Existing partial equilibrium frameworks often fail to capture feedback loops between fiscal policy, labor mobility, and productivity growth, particularly in contexts with fragmented data. To address this, we propose a computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) with Bayesian hierarchical econometrics. The ABM component will simulate firm-household-government interactions under varying infrastructure investment scenarios, while spatial econometric models will estimate region-specific elasticities of development outcomes (e.g., GDP per capita, employment rates) to policy variables using 20+ years of World Bank, IMF, and georeferenced satellite data. Key computational challenges include calibrating heterogeneous agent behaviors across 150+ regions, solving high-dimensional parameter spaces for counterfactual policy simulations, and processing multi-terabyte remote sensing datasets to proxy infrastructure quality. HPC resources will enable parallelized Monte Carlo sampling for uncertainty quantification, distributed training of machine learning classifiers to identify latent development clusters, and GPU-accelerated matrix operations for large-scale spatial autoregressive models. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable toolkit for evaluating trade-offs between centralized vs. decentralized development policies, (2) empirically grounded projections of how targeted industrial corridors could alter regional inequality in South Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa, and (3) open-source code for replicating computational experiments. Results will inform ongoing debates about optimal investment prioritization in multilateral development finance, particularly regarding transportation networks and energy infrastructure. By quantifying the combinatorial effects of policy levers, this work aims to advance methodological integration in development economics while providing actionable insights for sustainable growth strategies.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the systematic study of the economic development process and its application to the problems of specific countries and regions. Includes instruction in economic development theory, industrialization, land reform, infrastructural development, investment policy, the role of governments and business in development, international development organizations, and the study of social, health, and environmental influences on economic development.

abstract: This project seeks to advance understanding of ocean-atmosphere coupling processes that drive tropical climate variability and extreme weather events under anthropogenic warming. A critical knowledge gap persists in modeling mesoscale ocean eddies and their cascading impacts on atmospheric convection, cloud feedbacks, and heat redistribution—processes poorly resolved in current-generation Earth system models (ESMs). To address this, we propose high-resolution coupled simulations using the Community Earth System Model (CESM) at an unprecedented 0.1° ocean/0.25° atmosphere resolution, explicitly resolving eddy-driven heat transport and air-sea interactions at storm-resolving scales. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated components of the Model for Prediction Across Scales (MPAS) framework optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) architectures. Key innovations include a multi-scale nesting approach to isolate eddy feedback mechanisms and machine learning-based parameterization of subgrid-scale cloud microphysics trained against ARM observational data. Simulations will span 50 model years under CMIP6 SSP2-4.5 forcing, requiring 8 million core-hours on a tier-2 HPC cluster to generate 3 PB of output data. Expected outcomes include (1) quantification of eddy-mediated ocean heat uptake efficiency, (2) improved representation of Madden-Julian Oscillation dynamics in warming scenarios, and (3) uncertainty reduction in projected tropical cyclone intensification rates. Results will directly inform the 7th IPCC Assessment Report by constraining climate sensitivity tied to ocean mixing processes. The resource request supports development of an open-source diagnostics package for eddy-resolving climate model intercomparison, fostering community-wide advances in high-resolution climate prediction. This work bridges critical gaps between oceanographic small-scale physics and global climate response, with implications for coastal resilience planning and mitigation strategy evaluation.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the climate system of the earth with emphasis on the physical, dynamical, and chemical interactions of the atmosphere, ocean, land, ice, and the terrestrial and marine biospheres. Includes instruction in biology, chemistry, climate analysis, climate change adaptation/mitigation, climate policy, ecology, energy development, environmental impacts, marine chemistry, meteorology, and oceanography.

abstract: This research project seeks to address critical gaps in computational resources for Lao language studies by developing scalable natural language processing (NLP) tools and analyzing historical and contemporary Lao texts. Despite Lao’s status as a linguistically and culturally significant language in Southeast Asia, it remains under-resourced in computational linguistics, with limited annotated corpora, dialectal dictionaries, or NLP models.
