This hinders scholarly analysis of Lao literature, philological research, and practical applications in technology. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) to train transformer-based language models on a newly compiled corpus of Lao texts spanning classical literature, modern media, and regional dialects. Computational methods will include semi-supervised learning to overcome data sparsity, neural machine translation for cross-dialectal mapping, and graph-based algorithms for syntactic analysis of classical Lao poetry. Additionally, HPC resources will enable large-scale phonetic alignment to trace diachronic shifts in tonal systems and dialect variation. Outcomes will include the first open-source NLP toolkit for Lao, optimized for tasks such as tokenization, part-of-speech tagging, and named entity recognition, as well as a dialect classification framework to inform sociolinguistic studies. The resource demands are substantial: preliminary experiments indicate that training a Lao-specific BERT model requires processing over 10 million tokens across diverse genres, with iterative hyperparameter tuning necessitating GPU-accelerated workflows. By enabling these analyses, the project aims to advance Lao literary scholarship, support language preservation efforts, and create infrastructure for applied uses in Lao-speaking communities, such as educational technology and low-resource machine translation. Results will be disseminated through open-access platforms and collaborations with Lao academic institutions to ensure sustainable impact.
detailed_field: Foreign languages, literatures, and linguistics nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the Lao language. Includes instruction in philology; dialects; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing dynamic, multi-stakeholder supply chain networks under conditions of asymmetric information and behavioral uncertainty. Traditional supply chain models often assume rational decision-making and perfect information sharing, but real-world scenarios involve strategic misreporting, cognitive biases, and evolving trust relationships among suppliers, distributors, and buyers. The project aims to bridge this gap by integrating agent-based modeling, game-theoretic principles, and reinforcement learning to simulate complex interactions across decentralized networks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to execute large-scale parallel simulations that capture heterogeneous agent behaviors, probabilistic disruption events, and adaptive negotiation processes. The computational approach will employ evolutionary algorithms to identify Pareto-optimal resource allocation strategies while incorporating real-time data assimilation from synthetic market environments. Key challenges include scaling memory-intensive simulations across nodes to handle 10^4–10^5 autonomous agents with distinct decision policies and maintaining low-latency communication between optimization modules. Expected outcomes include a novel protocol for quantifying resilience trade-offs in trust-deficient supply networks and an open-source toolkit for scenario-based stress testing. This work will contribute to management science by advancing computational methods to address strategic opacity in operational systems, with direct applications to ethical sourcing networks, blockchain-enabled logistics, and public-private infrastructure partnerships. Results will be validated against historical supply chain disruption datasets and operational benchmarks from collaborative industry partners.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the application of statistical modeling, data warehousing, data mining, programming, forecasting and operations research techniques to the analysis of problems of business organization and performance. Includes instruction in optimization theory and mathematical techniques, data mining, data warehousing, stochastic and dynamic modeling, operations analysis, and the design and testing of prototype systems and evaluation models.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate the interplay between spatial configurations in residential built environments and their socio-environmental impacts, with a focus on optimizing housing designs for both human well-being and energy efficiency. While housing design traditionally prioritizes functional or aesthetic considerations, emerging evidence suggests that spatial layouts—such as room adjacency patterns, circulation pathways, and shared space distribution—profoundly influence social dynamics among occupants and aggregate energy use. However, modeling these complex relationships requires analyzing high-dimensional datasets spanning architectural schematics, occupant behavior patterns, and thermal performance metrics. The project proposes a novel computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate occupant movement and social interactions, coupled with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations to assess heating/cooling load distributions. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify design features that minimize energy consumption while maximizing opportunities for social cohesion, using training data derived from parametric variations of multifamily housing prototypes. High-performance computing resources are essential to manage the iterative simulation workflows, which involve parallelized execution of thousands of design permutations across variable occupancy scenarios and climate profiles. The research will utilize existing datasets from smart home sensors, anonymized social network analyses, and architectural blueprints, supplemented by synthetic data generation for underrepresented housing typologies. Expected outcomes include a predictive model quantifying trade-offs between spatial connectivity metrics and energy performance indicators, as well as generative design guidelines for adaptable housing layouts. These results aim to advance evidence-based architectural practices that simultaneously address climate resilience and societal needs for community-oriented living environments, offering policymakers a data-driven foundation to revise building codes and sustainability incentives.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the behavioral, social, economic, functional, and aesthetic aspects of housing, interiors, and other built environments. Includes instruction in analyzing, planning, designing, furnishing, and equipping residential, work, and leisure spaces to meet user needs and the study of related public policies.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern diesel engines, coupled with stringent emissions regulations and demand for fuel efficiency, necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize engine design and maintenance strategies. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multi-physics simulation frameworks for analyzing combustion dynamics, thermal stress distribution, and component wear in heavy-duty diesel engines. Current experimental methods are limited by cost, time, and the inability to isolate variables in real-world operating conditions. Computational modeling offers a scalable alternative but requires significant computational power to resolve high-fidelity, transient phenomena across coupled domains (fluid dynamics, thermodynamics, structural mechanics). The research will employ finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) using ANSYS Fluent and OpenFOAM to simulate combustion efficiency under varying fuel injection timings, exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) rates, and turbocharger configurations. Machine learning models (TensorFlow/PyTorch) will be trained on simulation outputs to predict component fatigue life and optimize maintenance intervals. Validation will leverage experimental data from engine test benches and field sensors. The project aims to identify design modifications that reduce NOx and particulate emissions by 15–20% without compromising power output, while extending service intervals for high-stress components like piston rings and cylinder liners. Outcomes will directly inform curriculum updates in Diesel Mechanics Technology programs, providing students with access to cutting-edge predictive maintenance tools and simulation-based learning modules. By integrating HPC-driven insights into technician training, this work bridges the gap between theoretical engine diagnostics and data-driven decision-making in industrial settings, addressing workforce needs in an era of increasingly digitized diesel systems.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to repair, service, and maintain diesel engines in vehicles such as automobiles, buses, ships, trucks, railroad locomotives, and construction equipment; as well as stationary diesel engines in electrical generators and related equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the impact of quantum computing-driven market microstructure dynamics on financial decision-making under uncertainty, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model emergent trading behaviors in decentralized finance (DeFi) ecosystems. Traditional financial models struggle to account for the nonlinear interactions between algorithmic trading agents, liquidity fragmentation across blockchain-based platforms, and real-time risk propagation in markets dominated by quantum-inspired optimization strategies. The research addresses this gap by developing an agent-based simulation framework that integrates quantum annealing techniques with game-theoretic liquidity provision models, calibrated to multi-chain DeFi transaction data. Using HPC clusters, we will simulate order book evolution across synthetic markets under varying quantum computing adoption scenarios, analyzing cascading effects on price discovery, arbitrage opportunities, and systemic stability. Computational experiments will employ hybrid quantum-classical optimization algorithms to resolve high-dimensional portfolio allocation problems in environments with nanosecond latency constraints. Expected outcomes include 1) quantitative benchmarks for quantum advantage in dark pool routing efficiency, 2) topology-aware risk metrics for cross-protocol liquidity shocks, and 3) adaptive hedging strategies resilient to quantum-accelerated front-running attacks. By mapping the computational complexity frontier where classical HPC infrastructure intersects with emerging quantum financial technologies, this work aims to establish foundational frameworks for next-generation market surveillance systems while informing regulatory approaches to quantum-ready financial infrastructure. The requested resources will enable large-scale parallelism of market scenario simulations, storage of petabyte-scale limit order book reconstructions, and real-time analysis of quantum circuit optimization patterns across heterogeneous compute architectures.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to plan, manage, and analyze the financial and monetary aspects and performance of business enterprises, banking institutions, or other organizations. Includes instruction in principles of accounting, financial instruments, capital planning, funds acquisition, asset and debt management, budgeting, financial analysis, and investments and portfolio management.

abstract: The proposed research aims to investigate the dynamic interplay between tumor microenvironmental stressors and cellular metabolic adaptations in driving cancer progression and therapeutic resistance. Despite advances in understanding cancer pathophysiology, the mechanisms by which heterogeneous tumor populations coordinately respond to hypoxia, nutrient deprivation, and oxidative stress remain poorly resolved. This project will employ a multiscale computational framework to model metabolic network plasticity and intercellular signaling in physiologically structured tumor microenvironments. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate spatially resolved, three-dimensional tumor systems incorporating single-cell metabolic flux analysis, stochastic nutrient gradient dynamics, and agent-based cell fate decision algorithms. The computational pipeline will integrate bulk and single-cell RNA-seq datasets from patient-derived xenograft models of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) to parameterize metabolic heterogeneity. Parallelized simulations will quantify emergent properties of tumor-stroma metabolic symbiosis under varying oxygenation and pH conditions, with iterative validation against in vitro microfluidic culture experiments. Expected outcomes include identification of microenvironmental thresholds that trigger collective metabolic reprogramming events, predictive biomarkers of adaptive resistance to metabolic inhibitors, and spatially mapped vulnerabilities for combination therapy targeting. This work will establish a novel computational platform for simulating physiologically constrained tumor evolution, directly addressing the National Cancer Institute’s priority to bridge systems biology with translational oncology. The requested HPC allocation will enable large-parameter-space explorations (10⁵+ core-hours) required for statistically robust analysis of stochastic microenvironmental interactions, which are computationally intractable on local clusters. By elucidating principles of stress-adaptive metabolic coordination in tumors, this research aims to advance precision oncology strategies while contributing open-source simulation tools to the cancer physiology community.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_title: Physiology, Pathology, and Related Sciences, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in physiology, pathology, and related sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The proposed research project seeks to advance the design and optimization of next-generation electromechanical systems through high-fidelity computational modeling and simulation. Electromechanical technologies increasingly integrate complex interactions between electrical, mechanical, and control subsystems, particularly in applications such as precision robotics, renewable energy converters, and industrial automation. However, existing design methodologies struggle to resolve multi-domain dynamics at scale, leading to inefficiencies in energy use, material performance, and operational reliability. This work addresses these challenges by developing a coupled multiphysics framework to simulate electro-thermal-mechanical phenomena across multiple spatial and temporal scales. The computational approach combines finite element analysis for structural and thermal behavior with circuit-level electromagnetic simulations, augmented by machine learning techniques to accelerate parameter optimization. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the computational intensity of these simulations, which involve iterative solving of nonlinear partial differential equations across millions of mesh elements, real-time co-simulation of control algorithms, and large-scale design space exploration. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated computing for parallelized solver tasks and distributed memory architectures for parametric studies. Expected outcomes include validated models for predicting fatigue life in high-frequency actuators, optimized topologies for energy-efficient hybrid drives, and open-source tools for modular co-simulation workflows. These results will provide critical insights into failure modes and efficiency bottlenecks while establishing scalable computational workflows adaptable to diverse electromechanical applications. By enabling high-resolution virtual prototyping, this work aims to reduce development cycles and material waste in electromechanical system manufacturing, with potential impacts across aerospace, clean energy, and advanced robotics sectors. The requested computing resources will support both baseline simulations and sensitivity analyses across 50+ design variables, requiring sustained access to teraflop-scale processing capacity and petabyte-tier storage for transient simulation datasets.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in electromechanical technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale historical datasets, enabling novel insights into the socio-cultural dynamics of 19th-century urban migration in Europe. Traditional historiographical methods struggle to efficiently process the vast quantities of digitized census records, municipal archives, and periodical collections now available, limiting scholars’ ability to identify patterns in migration flows, occupational shifts, and community formation across time and space. The research addresses this gap by applying computational text analysis, spatial modeling, and network analysis to these heterogeneous datasets, which collectively exceed 20 terabytes. Key tasks include training machine learning models to classify occupations from unstructured census entries, reconstructing migration networks using probabilistic record linkage, and simulating urbanization patterns via agent-based models. These methods require significant parallel processing capabilities to handle iterative model training, geospatial computations, and large-scale graph analytics. The project will utilize GPU-accelerated nodes for neural network training and high-memory nodes for processing graph-based representations of population movements. Expected outcomes include (1) a scalable pipeline for integrating fragmented historical records, (2) visualizations of migration corridors and their correlation with industrial development, and (3) statistical evidence challenging existing narratives about urbanization timelines in secondary cities. By demonstrating how computational methods can interrogate understudied archival materials at scale, this work aims to advance digital historiography, offering a template for analyzing complex societal transitions while preserving granularity in historical interpretation. Results will be disseminated through open-access tools and a public database of annotated migration records, fostering interdisciplinary collaboration in computational humanities.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general study and interpretation of the past, including the gathering, recording, synthesizing and criticizing of evidence and theories about past events. Includes instruction in historiography; historical research methods; studies of specific periods, issues and cultures; and applications to areas such as historic preservation, public policy, and records administration.

abstract: Dental prostheses require precise biomechanical compatibility to ensure long-term functionality and patient comfort, yet current design methodologies rely heavily on empirical techniques with limited predictive capability for material fatigue, interfacial stress distribution, and microbial adhesion. This project proposes a computational framework to optimize the design and fabrication of dental prostheses by integrating multiscale biomechanical modeling, machine learning-driven material optimization, and patient-specific oral microenvironment simulations. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to address the computational complexity of modeling heterogeneous materials (e.g., zirconia, polymers, alloys) at micron-scale resolutions, simulating dynamic occlusal forces over multiyear timelines, and analyzing microbial biofilm formation under variable salivary conditions. The research will employ finite element analysis (FEA) to map stress gradients in prostheses, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to evaluate material degradation pathways, and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) trained on clinical imaging data to predict anatomical fit. A novel aspect involves coupling these models with real-world sensor data from intraoral scanning devices to validate simulations against biomechanical wear patterns observed in prostheses retrieved from patients. Expected outcomes include predictive algorithms to guide the selection of material compositions and geometric configurations that minimize interfacial failure risks, reduce iterative prototyping, and extend prosthesis lifespan. By establishing a computational pipeline tailored to dental laboratory workflows, this work aims to bridge the gap between traditional craft-based fabrication and data-driven precision manufacturing, ultimately enhancing clinical outcomes for patients requiring complex restorative interventions. The scale of parameter space exploration (e.g., material hybrids, occlusal load scenarios) necessitates HPC capabilities to achieve statistically robust results within feasible timeframes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of dentists, to design and construct dental prostheses such as caps, crowns, bridges, dentures, splints, and orthodontic appliances. Includes instruction in dental anatomy, dental materials, ceramics technology, impressions, complete dentures, partial dentures, orthodontics, crowns and bridges, sculpture, bonding and assembly techniques, and equipment operation.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to model the efficacy of adaptive instructional strategies in general science teacher education, with a focus on improving pre-service teachers’ ability to integrate cross-disciplinary science concepts into pedagogically sound lesson plans. A key challenge in science education research is understanding how novice teachers assimilate complex, interconnected scientific domains (e.g., bridging biology and physics) while simultaneously mastering evidence-based teaching practices. Traditional qualitative methods struggle to capture the dynamic, multi-variable interactions between content knowledge, pedagogical reasoning, and classroom implementation. To address this, we propose an agent-based modeling (ABM) approach using high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate diverse learning trajectories of pre-service teachers under varying instructional conditions. The ABM will integrate empirical data from teacher education programs—including cognitive assessments, classroom observation metrics, and longitudinal performance data—to parameterize agents representing teachers, students, and curricular elements. Computational experiments will test hypotheses about how resource allocation (e.g., simulation-based training, mentorship networks) influences the development of pedagogical content knowledge. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify critical thresholds in instructional design that predict successful classroom outcomes. The scale of analysis—encompassing thousands of simulated classrooms with varying demographic and institutional constraints—necessitates parallelized computing for parameter space exploration and sensitivity analyses. Outcomes will provide actionable insights for optimizing science teacher training programs, particularly in under-resourced educational contexts. By quantifying relationships between instructional inputs and teaching competence, this work aims to establish a predictive framework for scaling effective interventions, directly supporting national efforts to strengthen STEM education pipelines. The requested HPC resources are essential to manage the computational intensity of multi-agent simulations and large-scale data integration, enabling granular analysis of emergent behaviors in teacher development systems.
cip_title: Science Teacher Education/ General Science Teacher Education
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach general science programs, or a combination of the biological and physical science subject matter areas, at various educational levels.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance the pedagogical frameworks within Family and Consumer Sciences (FCS) education by integrating computational modeling and data-driven insights into teacher training curricula. A critical challenge in FCS instruction lies in equipping educators to address multifaceted, real-world issues—such as sustainable resource management, nutritional epidemiology, and household economic decision-making—with methodologies that reflect systemic complexity. Traditional approaches often rely on static case studies or simplified theoretical models, limiting teachers’ ability to contextualize dynamic interactions between socioeconomic, environmental, and health-related variables. To address this gap, the proposed research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and analyze large-scale simulations of household systems, consumer behavior patterns, and community health dynamics. Agent-based models will simulate decision-making processes in diverse family structures, while machine learning algorithms will identify trends in public datasets related to nutrition, budgeting, and sustainable practices. These computational tools will generate actionable insights into how interrelated factors influence outcomes in domains central to FCS education. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing high-dimensional datasets, running parallelized simulations, and training predictive models that capture nonlinear relationships. Outcomes will include modular teaching resources—such as interactive simulation dashboards and data-driven case studies—that enable FCS teacher candidates to explore complex systems in classroom settings. By grounding pedagogical strategies in computationally derived evidence, this project aims to improve the preparedness of future educators to teach critical thinking and problem-solving skills aligned with real-world challenges. The work will also establish a framework for integrating computational literacy into FCS teacher education, fostering interdisciplinary connections between home economics and emerging data science methodologies.
cip_title: Family and Consumer Sciences/ Home Economics Teacher Education
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach vocational home economics programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop an adaptive optimization framework for large-scale, dynamic event logistics using high-performance computing (HPC) resources. The growing complexity of hybrid and in-person events—driven by real-time attendee behavior data, multi-vendor coordination, and sustainability constraints—has outpaced traditional planning tools, which struggle with dynamic variables such as last-minute attendee preferences, resource bottlenecks, and environmental impact targets. The core research problem lies in creating computational models that integrate real-time data streams (e.g., mobile app interactions, IoT sensor feeds) with multi-objective optimization to balance cost efficiency, attendee satisfaction, and carbon footprint reduction. Leveraging HPC resources, the project will employ agent-based modeling to simulate attendee movement and vendor interactions across virtual and physical event spaces, paired with Monte Carlo methods to assess risk scenarios in supplier contracts and spatial layouts. Machine learning techniques will be applied to historical event datasets to predict emergent crowd behaviors and resource utilization patterns. The computational workflow requires parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets representing attendee profiles, vendor capabilities, and venue specifications, with iterative optimization cycles to update floor plans, scheduling, and vendor assignments in near-real time. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support tool that reduces logistical planning time by 40–60% for events exceeding 10,000 participants while maintaining compliance with hospitality law and accessibility standards. The project bridges computational science and event management by formalizing a novel methodology for dynamic resource allocation in transient, high-stakes business environments. Results will be validated against industry benchmarks from three international conference case studies, with open-source release of non-proprietary algorithm components to advance research in computational event analytics.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, budget, and implement conferences, meetings, and other special events in the public or private sectors. Includes instruction in principles of meeting and event planning; special event management; budgets and finance; site selection; contracts, vendors, and negotiations; marketing and promotions; food and beverage management; audio-visual basics and meeting technology; and hospitality law.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of intercultural communication in global digital networks, with a focus on identifying patterns of miscommunication and bias in multilingual, cross-platform media environments. As international communication increasingly relies on digital platforms—from social media to diplomatic channels—the volume and complexity of data require advanced computational methods to analyze cultural nuances, sentiment shifts, and information diffusion at scale. The research problem centers on the lack of tools capable of processing large-scale, multilingual datasets while accounting for contextual cultural variables, which hinders the development of evidence-based strategies for effective global communication. To address this, the project will employ natural language processing (NLP) models, network analysis, and machine learning techniques to examine intercultural interactions across three domains: multinational corporate communications, transnational journalism, and public diplomacy campaigns. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential for training transformer-based models on diverse linguistic corpora, simulating communication network dynamics under varying cultural parameters, and processing real-time data streams from platforms like X (Twitter), news aggregators, and international forums. Expected outcomes include (1) a computational framework for quantifying cultural context in communication practices, (2) identification of high-risk scenarios for miscommunication in crisis diplomacy and global marketing contexts, and (3) actionable insights for optimizing cross-cultural message design. The results will directly benefit practitioners in international journalism, intercultural training, and foreign service by providing data-driven tools to navigate complex communication landscapes. By leveraging HPC capabilities to handle terabyte-scale datasets and computationally intensive sentiment-culture linkage analyses, this project advances scholarly understanding of how cultural dimensions intersect with digital communication technologies in an increasingly interconnected world.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the specialized knowledge and skills needed for effective communication in the international community and among people of different cultures; and that prepares individuals to function at the national and international levels as journalists, public relations specialists, travel industry representatives, intercultural trainers, and/or foreign service officers. Includes instruction in journalism, communications, intercultural and international relations, marketing and public relations, and global communications policy.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision in non-invasive diagnostics for early-stage neurodegenerative disorders, focusing on the integration of retinal imaging biomarkers with multimodal neurophysiological data. While neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s are traditionally diagnosed via clinical evaluation and neuroimaging, these methods often lack sensitivity in early stages. Emerging evidence suggests that retinal microvascular and structural changes detectable via optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) correlate with central nervous system pathology. However, existing analytical pipelines for OCTA lack the resolution to disentangle subtle, spatially heterogeneous biomarkers, and integration with electrophysiological signals (e.g., EEG) remains computationally underexplored. The research problem centers on developing a scalable computational framework to identify high-dimensional retinal-electrophysiological signatures predictive of preclinical neurodegeneration. Using federated datasets from neurology-ophthalmology cohorts (n ≈ 15,000 scans), we will train graph convolutional networks (GCNs) to model retinal microvascular networks as spatially dynamic graphs, incorporating topological metrics and localized血流动力学 features. Concurrently, recurrent neural networks (RNNs) will process time-series EEG data to capture transient oscillatory patterns. A transformer-based multimodal fusion architecture will then correlate cross-modal features, optimized via contrastive learning to handle sparse annotation. Computational workflows will require GPU-accelerated processing of 3D OCTA volumes (~8 TB) and real-time EEG synchronization, necessitating HPC resources for distributed training and hyperparameter optimization. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated predictive model for preclinical neurodegeneration risk stratification, (2) open-source tools for multimodal biomarker integration, and (3) novel insights into retina-brain axis dynamics. This work bridges ophthalmology, neurology, and computational modeling, directly supporting the pre-PA focus on diagnostic innovation and interdisciplinary patient care. By enabling earlier intervention, the project aligns with healthcare’s shift toward preventive medicine while providing a scalable framework for future studies integrating imaging and physiological data streams.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission to a professional physician assistant program.

abstract: The increasing complexity of dynamic, decentralized networks in extreme environments—such as deep-sea sensor arrays or distributed lunar communication relays—demands novel approaches to resource allocation and latency mitigation. Traditional networking paradigms, optimized for terrestrial infrastructure, fail to address the unique constraints of these systems, including intermittent connectivity, asymmetric data flows, and severe energy limitations. This project proposes a bio-inspired computational framework to model and optimize such networks by integrating fluid dynamics principles with adaptive swarm intelligence algorithms. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will simulate multi-agent network topologies under stochastic environmental conditions, using GPU-accelerated discrete event simulations to model signal propagation delays, node failure cascades, and energy-aware routing protocols. The computational model will incorporate real-world datasets from underwater acoustic networks and space-ground link experiments to calibrate boundary conditions. Key innovations include a hybrid continuum-discrete method to approximate network behavior as a compressible fluid flow, enabling scalable prediction of congestion patterns, and a evolutionary optimization layer to dynamically reconfigure priority queues and bandwidth allocation. Expected outcomes include a publicly available toolkit for simulating extreme-environment networks, validated against physical testbeds, and novel protocols demonstrating ≥40% improvements in energy efficiency and packet delivery ratios under simulated Martian regolith interference scenarios. This work bridges gaps between telecommunications engineering, computational physics, and astrobiology, offering foundational insights for next-generation interplanetary internet architectures and ecological monitoring systems operating beyond conventional infrastructure limits.
cip_title: Computer Systems Networking and Telecommunications, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in computer systems networking and telecommunications, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Advances in oncology pharmacy require precise integration of pharmacogenomic, clinical, and molecular data to optimize therapeutic strategies for cancer patients. A critical barrier in this field is the computational complexity of modeling multi-omics datasets to predict patient-specific drug responses, particularly in heterogeneous malignancies. This project proposes the development of a scalable machine learning framework to analyze high-dimensional genomic, transcriptomic, and pharmacokinetic data, coupled with real-world clinical outcomes, to identify predictive biomarkers and personalize treatment regimens. The research will employ ensemble learning algorithms, neural networks, and Bayesian inference models to integrate sparse, multi-modal datasets while accounting for tumor evolution and drug resistance mechanisms. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to manage the iterative training of models on terabyte-scale datasets, perform parallelized molecular dynamics simulations of drug-target interactions, and conduct sensitivity analyses across diverse patient cohorts. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive models for chemotherapy and targeted therapy response in solid tumors, (2) identification of novel combinatorial drug targets to overcome resistance pathways, and (3) an open-source computational pipeline for adaptive therapy optimization. The HPC infrastructure will enable rapid processing of whole-exome sequencing data from 2,000+ patients (retrospective cohort) and real-time analysis of prospective data from ongoing clinical trials. By leveraging distributed computing for large-scale parameter optimization and cross-validation, this work aims to reduce computational bottlenecks that currently limit clinical translation. The results will directly inform precision dosing protocols, enhance therapeutic efficacy, and minimize adverse drug events in oncology practice. This project bridges computational innovation with clinical pharmacy by providing a template for resource-efficient, data-driven decision support in cancer care.
cip_definition: Research focused on oncology pharmacy.

abstract: Critical care management in adult and gerontology populations faces significant challenges due to the heterogeneity of conditions such as sepsis, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and multi-organ failure, which require rapid, personalized interventions. Current predictive models for outcomes and treatment responses in critically ill patients often lack the granularity to account for complex interactions between aging-related physiological decline, comorbidities, and dynamic clinical variables. This project proposes to develop an advanced computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to integrate multi-omics data, real-time physiological monitoring, and electronic health records (EHRs) for precision risk stratification and therapeutic optimization. The research will employ machine learning algorithms, including ensemble methods and deep neural networks, to analyze high-dimensional datasets from 5,000+ ICU patients across 15 institutions. Key computational tasks include federated learning to preserve data privacy, time-series analysis of vital sign trends, and genome-wide association studies (GWAS) to identify aging-specific biomarkers of critical illness progression. HPC resources are essential for training models on large-scale datasets, simulating virtual patient cohorts to test intervention scenarios, and optimizing hyperparameters in computationally intensive workflows. Expected outcomes include predictive models for 72-hour mortality, renal injury, and ventilator liberation success, validated against prospective ICU data. The project will also generate open-source tools for real-time clinical decision support, enabling dynamic recalibration of treatment protocols based on evolving patient states. By elucidating mechanisms linking gerontological factors to critical care outcomes, this work aims to reduce ICU length of stay, minimize adverse events in vulnerable populations, and establish a scalable infrastructure for data-driven critical care research.
cip_definition: Research focused on medical and clinical issues in Adult/Gerontology Critical Care

abstract: The increasing digitization of cultural heritage materials has generated vast collections of digital artifacts, yet libraries and archives face significant challenges in preserving and providing access to these resources as formats degrade and obsolescence accelerates. This project seeks to address the critical gap in scalable computational methods for analyzing and preserving heterogeneous digital collections, particularly those with complex dependencies between file formats, metadata schemas, and software ecosystems. Current approaches often rely on manual curation or limited automation, which cannot scale to the petabytes of data held in modern repositories. We propose developing a machine learning framework optimized for high-performance computing (HPC) environments to automate the detection of at-risk digital objects, predict degradation pathways, and recommend preservation interventions. The computational workflow will integrate graph neural networks to model format dependencies, transformer-based architectures for metadata enrichment, and agent-based simulations to evaluate preservation strategy outcomes under varying resource constraints. By leveraging GPU-accelerated training and distributed storage systems, the framework will process multi-modal data (text, images, binary files) across millions of objects while maintaining chain-of-custody documentation required for archival integrity. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for large-scale digital preservation analytics, empirical models of format obsolescence patterns, and benchmark datasets for evaluating computational preservation methods. This work will provide libraries with evidence-based strategies to prioritize at-risk materials, reduce curation costs, and extend the lifespan of digital collections. The HPC infrastructure is essential given the need for parallel processing of terabyte-scale corpora, real-time simulation of decade-spanning preservation scenarios, and comparative analysis across diverse institutional collections. Results will advance both library science practice and computational preservation as an emerging interdisciplinary field.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in library science, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a comparative study of cultural adaptation and identity negotiation within transnational diaspora communities through computational analysis of multilingual literary texts. Traditional scholarship in Comparative Group Studies has been constrained by manual, small-scale textual analysis, limiting systematic comparisons across linguistic, temporal, and geographic boundaries. To address this, we propose a computational framework that integrates natural language processing (NLP), multilingual transformer models, and network analysis to examine patterns of cultural retention, hybridity, and transformation in a corpus of over 50,000 literary works produced by diaspora authors across 15 languages from the 20th and 21st centuries. The research will deploy custom-trained language models to identify thematic motifs, stylistic features, and intertextual references, while graph-based methods will map transnational literary influences and evolving narrative structures. HPC resources are critical for processing computationally intensive tasks, including cross-lingual embedding alignment, large-scale topic modeling, and training domain-specific models for underrepresented languages. Expected outcomes include a publicly accessible digital archive of annotated texts, quantitative frameworks for analyzing cultural hybridity, and methodological innovations at the intersection of computational linguistics and critical identity studies. By uncovering systemic patterns in how diasporic groups navigate belonging and cultural change, this project aims to deepen theoretical understandings of transnational identity while providing scalable tools for interdisciplinary humanities research. The findings will directly inform curriculum development in global cultural studies and offer evidence-based insights for policymakers addressing multicultural cohesion in pluralistic societies.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
detailed_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the comparative study of the history, literature, sociology, politics, culture, and economics of different groups such as racial, gender, sexual, class, ethnic, geographical, and national. Includes instruction in comparative studies, comparative literature, critical race theory, cultural anthropology, cultural studies, religious studies, science studies, social and cultural theory, urban studies, and visual culture.

abstract: The increasing volume of digitized and born-digital archival materials presents significant challenges in metadata generation, sensitivity assessment, and long-term preservation. Traditional archival workflows, reliant on manual appraisal and description, struggle to scale with heterogeneous, large-scale collections, risking information inaccessibility or inadvertent exposure of private data. This project seeks to address these challenges through the development of computational tools that leverage machine learning (ML) and natural language processing (NLP) to automate metadata extraction, classify sensitive content, and model preservation risks in archival datasets. The research will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train and deploy deep learning models on corpus-scale datasets, including digitized text, images, and complex digital objects (e.g., emails, spreadsheets). Key computational tasks include fine-tuning transformer-based architectures for context-aware metadata tagging, optimizing computer vision pipelines for handwritten document analysis, and simulating decay patterns in digital file formats under varying preservation conditions. By parallelizing workflows across GPU nodes, the project aims to process multi-terabyte collections efficiently, enabling rapid identification of personally identifiable information (PII) for redaction and generating probabilistic models to prioritize archival interventions for at-risk formats. Anticipated outcomes include open-source software tools for archivists, validated frameworks for integrating computational methods into existing archival standards, and a public benchmark dataset for evaluating archival ML applications. This work bridges archival science, data ethics, and computational linguistics, offering scalable solutions to enhance accessibility while addressing ethical and legal responsibilities in digital stewardship. The requested HPC resources are critical to handling the computational complexity of multimodal data analysis and ensuring reproducible, institution-agnostic methodologies for the archival community.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to identify, manage, preserve, and make available records with long-term value for documentation, legal, research, and other purposes. Includes instruction in appraisal and collection development, information and records management, archival preservation, access systems, management of electronic records, archival outreach, and legal and ethical issues.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to investigate the interplay between urban environmental stressors, epigenetic modifications, and population-level health disparities through an integrative computational framework. Rapid urbanization has created complex exposures to pollutants, noise, and socio-economic inequities, yet their combined biological impacts remain poorly understood. This project will develop multiscale models linking geospatial environmental data, epigenetic clocks derived from blood methylation profiles, and public health records across diverse demographic groups. High-performance computing resources are essential to process terabyte-scale datasets spanning atmospheric chemistry measurements, traffic patterns, epigenetic arrays (Illumina EPIC), and electronic health records from municipal databases. Machine learning pipelines will identify exposure signatures correlated with accelerated biological aging, while agent-based models will simulate how policy interventions (e.g., green space allocation, emissions regulations) might mitigate epigenetic aging disparities across neighborhoods. The computational architecture will integrate graph neural networks to model spatial-temporal dependencies in environmental variables and transformer-based models to decode non-linear interactions between epigenetic markers and disease risk. Expected outcomes include a novel open-source toolkit for cities to prioritize health equity interventions, predictive biomarkers of environmental stress susceptibility, and mechanistic insights into how chronic urban exposures become biologically embedded. This interdisciplinary approach bridges environmental science, computational epigenetics, and urban policy design, offering a scalable methodology to address emerging challenges at the human-environment interface. The requested resources will enable processing of heterogeneous data streams at unprecedented resolution, supporting both basic science discovery and translational applications in public health planning.
cip_definition: An interdisciplinary program that focuses on understanding the human being from the biological, social science, and humanities perspectives and that addresses contemporary issues related to biology and society, such as global health and disease, environmental policy, bioethics, and biotechnology.

abstract: The development of efficient catalytic processes is critical for sustainable chemical manufacturing, yet the molecular-level understanding of reaction mechanisms in heterogeneous systems remains a significant challenge. This project proposes to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the dynamic behavior of transition metal catalysts under industrial biofuel production conditions. Current experimental methods struggle to resolve atomic-scale interactions and transient intermediates, limiting the rational design of catalysts optimized for low-temperature operation. The research will employ multiscale computational models, integrating density functional theory (DFT) for electronic structure analysis, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to track reaction pathways, and machine learning (ML) algorithms to predict structure-activity relationships. HPC resources are essential to manage the computational complexity of these tasks, including large-scale parallel calculations for high-throughput screening of bimetallic catalyst compositions and long-timescale MD simulations to capture rare catalytic events. Data from collaborative experimental studies on catalyst performance will validate the computational models. Expected outcomes include identifying catalyst formulations with improved activity and selectivity at reduced energy inputs, directly addressing industrial needs for decarbonized processes. The project will also generate an open-access database of catalytic properties, enabling broader innovation in chemical technology. By bridging molecular insights with industrial applicability, this work aims to advance sustainable manufacturing practices while training students in cutting-edge computational methodologies. The requested HPC allocation will support intensive simulations that are infeasible on local clusters, ensuring robust sampling of chemical space and statistically significant results. This research aligns with global priorities in energy efficiency and underscores the transformative role of computational science in chemical technology.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific principles and technical skills in support of chemical and biochemical research and industrial operations. Includes instruction in principles of chemistry and biochemistry, technical mathematics, computer applications, radiochemistry, industrial biochemistry, chemical instrumentation, physical chemistry, laboratory research methods, industrial processing methods and equipment, and test equipment operation and maintenance.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize individualized learning pathways for gifted and talented (G/T) students by analyzing multidimensional educational datasets. Current methods for designing personalized curricula rely on static assessments and manual analysis, which struggle to account for the dynamic interplay of cognitive, socioemotional, and environmental factors influencing gifted learners. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train machine learning models on large-scale, longitudinal datasets spanning academic performance, psychometric evaluations, behavioral observations, and demographic variables from diverse G/T populations. These datasets, aggregated from partner K-12 districts and national repositories, will be processed using parallelized pipelines to identify latent patterns in talent development trajectories. Neural architecture search (NAS) methods will be employed to iteratively design ensemble models capable of predicting optimal pedagogical interventions for specific learner profiles. Additionally, agent-based simulations will model classroom-scale interactions under varying instructional strategies to evaluate scalability. The computational workload necessitates HPC resources due to the high dimensionality of input features (e.g., fine-grained skill mastery metrics, creativity indices), the combinatorial complexity of intervention scenarios, and the need for real-time adaptation in planned teacher-facing tools. Expected outcomes include an open-source predictive framework to assist educators in dynamically tailoring instruction, evidence-based criteria for recognizing atypical giftedness manifestations, and scalable protocols for aligning curricular rigor with asynchronous developmental rates. By enabling rapid analysis of heterogeneous data streams, this work aims to transform how educators design responsive learning environments that nurture both academic talent and socioemotional well-being in G/T students.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of the Gifted and Talented
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults exhibiting exceptional intellectual, psychomotor or artistic talent or potential, or who exhibit exceptional maturity or social leadership talents, and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying gifted and talented students, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising gifted and talented students, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: Soil health is a critical determinant of agricultural productivity, yet predicting soil behavior under dynamic environmental conditions remains a major challenge due to the complex interplay of physical, chemical, and biological factors. This project seeks to develop a multiscale computational framework to model soil-microbe-plant interactions under varying nutrient and moisture regimes, with a focus on optimizing sustainable soil management practices. Current limitations in experimental methods restrict the ability to resolve spatially heterogeneous microbial communities and their metabolic processes at relevant scales, necessitating high-fidelity simulations. We propose a hybrid approach combining agent-based modeling (ABM) of microbial dynamics with finite element analysis (FEA) of soil hydrology and nutrient transport. The ABM component will simulate microbial population interactions, extracellular enzyme production, and organic matter decomposition across micrometer-to-meter scales, while FEA will model pore-scale water flow and solute diffusion. Machine learning techniques will be employed to parameterize models using empirical data from soil metagenomics, hyperspectral imaging, and sensor networks. High-performance computing resources are essential to handle the computational intensity of coupling these frameworks, particularly for 3D simulations across >10^6 grid cells and stochastic microbial interactions involving >10^8 agents. Expected outcomes include (1) predictive models identifying soil management strategies that enhance carbon sequestration and nutrient retention under drought scenarios, (2) mechanistic insights into microbial community resilience to chemical inputs, and (3) open-source simulation tools for the soil science community. By bridging microbial ecology and soil physics through scalable computation, this work will advance precision agriculture strategies while reducing reliance on resource-intensive field trials. The requested allocation of 500,000 CPU-hours and 50 TB of storage will support model calibration, sensitivity analyses, and large-scale scenario testing over 12 months.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
cip_definition: Any instructional program in the soil sciences, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive analytics framework to optimize treatment personalization and resource allocation in mental health care settings, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. Mental health disorders exhibit high heterogeneity in symptom presentation, treatment response, and long-term outcomes, complicating clinical decision-making. Current approaches to treatment planning often rely on static protocols or clinician experience, which may not adequately account for dynamic interactions between patient-specific factors (e.g., genetic predispositions, psychosocial stressors, medication metabolism) and system-level constraints (e.g., staffing ratios, facility capacities). To address this gap, we propose a computational pipeline integrating machine learning (ML) and agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate patient trajectories and service utilization patterns under varying intervention scenarios. The research will utilize de-identified electronic health records (EHRs) from 50,000+ psychiatric patients, including demographic, pharmacological, and longitudinal outcome data, alongside synthetic datasets modeling care delivery workflows. Deep learning architectures (transformers, graph neural networks) will be trained to predict individual treatment responses, while ABMs will simulate population-level impacts of different staffing models and referral pathways. Computational challenges include handling high-dimensional multimodal data, addressing temporal dependencies in treatment histories, and managing stochasticity in behavioral simulations. HPC resources are critical for parallelized hyperparameter optimization, large-scale Monte Carlo simulations, and sensitivity analyses across diverse demographic subgroups. Expected outcomes include (1) validated predictive models for personalized psychotropic medication selection, (2) evidence-based recommendations for balancing clinician workloads with patient acuity levels, and (3) open-source tools for dynamic risk stratification in community mental health systems. By bridging clinical psychiatry with computational modeling, this work aims to enhance the precision and equity of mental health services while providing training opportunities for psychiatric technicians in data-driven care coordination.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of psychiatrists, psychologists, nurses, and other mental health care professionals, to provide direct patient care services, assist in developing and implementing treatment plans, administer medications, and perform related administrative functions. Includes instruction in mental health theory, applied psychopathology, patient communication and management, crisis intervention, psychotropic medication, mental health treatment procedures, substance abuse, record-keeping, clinical administrative skills, and applicable standards and regulations.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of personalized, data-driven training frameworks for optimizing athletic performance and injury resilience in competitive sports. While advances in wearable sensors and motion-capture systems have generated vast datasets on biomechanics, physiological responses, and training loads, existing analytical tools lack the capacity to integrate multimodal data streams in real time or model complex interactions between biomechanical factors, training regimens, and individual athlete physiology. The project addresses this gap by implementing a computational pipeline combining graph neural networks (GNNs) to model athlete-specific biomechanical synergies, reinforcement learning (RL) agents to simulate adaptive training responses, and probabilistic causal inference to identify injury risk thresholds under dynamic workloads. HPC resources are critical for scaling these methods to process high-frequency sensor data (e.g., 3D joint kinematics, muscle activation patterns) from athlete cohorts while maintaining low-latency feedback for real-world training applications. The proposed framework will be validated using datasets from collegiate track-and-field athletes, with performance metrics compared against traditional periodization models. Anticipated outcomes include open-source tools for coaches to design individualized programs that balance performance gains with injury mitigation, as well as novel computational benchmarks for movement efficiency analysis. By bridging sports science, machine learning, and high-performance computing, this work aims to establish a replicable paradigm for data-intensive athlete development while addressing scalability challenges unique to sports analytics.
detailed_field: Parks, recreation, leisure, fitness, and sport studies and management
cip_title: Sports, Kinesiology, and Physical Education/ Fitness, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on activities and principles that promote physical fitness, achieve and maintain athletic prowess, and accomplish related research and service goals. Includes instruction in human movement studies, motivation studies, rules and practice of specific sports, exercise and fitness principles and techniques, basic athletic injury prevention and treatment, and organizing and leading fitness and sports programs.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance research on optimizing agricultural resource allocation under climate uncertainty in the U.S. Midwest. Agricultural economics faces critical challenges in modeling complex, dynamic systems where climate variability intersects with economic decision-making, market fluctuations, and heterogeneous farm-level practices. Existing models often oversimplify spatial and temporal interactions, limiting their utility for policy design. Our work addresses this gap by developing a multi-scale computational framework integrating agent-based modeling (ABM), high-resolution climate projections, and econometric analysis. The ABM component will simulate farmer decision-making processes—incorporating risk preferences, adaptive behaviors, and market feedbacks—while coupling with biophysical crop yield models driven by 1km-resolution climate data. Concurrently, Bayesian hierarchical econometric methods will analyze 20 years of farm-level survey data to parameterize agent behaviors and validate model outputs. The computational intensity arises from fine spatial granularity (100,000+ agent entities), hourly climate data processing, and Monte Carlo simulations across diverse climate scenarios. HPC resources are essential to achieve parameter estimation via Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling at scale and to run ensemble simulations quantifying economic resilience under varying policy interventions. Expected outcomes include (1) identification of regionally differentiated adaptation strategies that balance productivity and sustainability, (2) quantification of trade-offs between market-driven resource allocation and climate risk mitigation, and (3) open-source tools for dynamic policy impact assessment. Results will inform USDA extension programs and international agricultural trade analyses, contributing to evidence-based frameworks for climate-smart agriculture. The project requires 250,000 core-hours annually for three years, prioritizing parallelized model calibration and scenario testing on GPU-accelerated nodes.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of economics to the analysis of resource allocation, productivity, investment, and trends in the agricultural sector, both domestically and internationally. Includes instruction in economics and related subfields as well as applicable agricultural fields.

abstract: The increasing complexity of global financial markets, driven by the proliferation of algorithmic trading, decentralized finance (DeFi) protocols, and cross-border regulatory fragmentation, has amplified systemic risks that traditional risk management frameworks struggle to quantify. This project seeks to develop a dynamic, multi-layered network model to simulate contagion effects across interconnected financial ecosystems, with a focus on non-bank financial intermediaries (NBFIs) and crypto-asset markets. The research addresses the critical gap in understanding how liquidity shocks propagate between decentralized platforms and traditional financial institutions, particularly under stress scenarios involving simultaneous market dislocations and smart contract failures. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) combined with graph neural networks (GNNs) to capture heterogeneous agent behaviors, cross-market dependencies, and time-varying network topologies at scale. Computational experiments will simulate crisis scenarios using real-world data streams, including blockchain transaction histories, derivatives market exposures, and regulatory filings. The parallelized architecture will enable Monte Carlo simulations across millions of agent interactions while maintaining microsecond-level resolution for high-frequency trading dynamics. Expected outcomes include (1) a risk propagation heatmap identifying critical junctures where DeFi protocols could amplify traditional market stresses, (2) quantitative metrics for "network fragility" under varying regulatory assumptions, and (3) an open-source framework for stress testing hybrid financial systems. By integrating techniques from complex systems theory, cryptographic verification processes, and market microstructure analysis, this work aims to provide policymakers and institutional risk managers with actionable tools to mitigate systemic vulnerabilities emerging at the intersection of conventional and decentralized finance.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the strategies used to define and manage acceptable financial risk for companies. Includes instruction in banking and bank regulations, derivative securities, interest rate and credit markets, financial engineering of systematic risk, and equity, bond, futures, and options markets.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the development of dynamic, large-scale Bayesian hierarchical models for analyzing spatial-temporal business data in the context of climate-driven market volatility. Traditional business forecasting tools often struggle to integrate high-dimensional environmental datasets—such as satellite-derived climate metrics, regional regulatory shifts, and supply chain geolocation data—with real-time market performance indicators. The computational complexity of modeling nonlinear interactions across these variables, particularly under uncertainty, exceeds the capacity of standard statistical software and workstations. This project proposes a novel computational framework combining Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods with distributed tensor factorization to estimate latent relationships between climate stressors and sector-specific financial outcomes. The HPC environment will enable parallelized sampling for multi-level models spanning terabytes of heterogeneous data from public (NOAA, IPCC) and proprietary (global logistics sensors, equity trading APIs) sources. Key challenges include optimizing memory allocation for irregularly sampled time series and validating model stability across GPU-CPU hybrid architectures. Expected outcomes include: (1) an open-source library for scalable Bayesian inference on business-environment interdependencies, (2) predictive insights into climate-adaptive investment strategies for Fortune 500 partners, and (3) methodological advancements in uncertainty quantification for decision-making under cascading ecological and economic shocks. By bridging computational statistics, environmental science, and business analytics, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven resilience planning in industries facing escalating climate-related financial disclosures. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated parameter estimation, hyperparameter tuning via evolutionary algorithms, and sensitivity analyses across 50+ sector-specific model variants.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the application of mathematical statistics to the description, analysis, and forecasting of business data. Includes instruction in statistical theory and methods, computer applications, data analysis and display, long- and short-term forecasting methods, and market performance analysis.

abstract: This project seeks to develop an integrated computational framework for optimizing industrial automation systems in dynamic manufacturing environments, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address scalability and real-time decision-making challenges. Current methodologies for managing complex production systems—particularly those integrating robotic automation, sensor networks, and adaptive process control—struggle to balance computational efficiency with the high-fidelity modeling required for precision manufacturing. Traditional simulations often oversimplify multi-variable interactions, leading to suboptimal resource allocation, energy inefficiencies, and delayed responses to process anomalies. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hybrid approach combining discrete-event simulation, multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), and parallelized finite element analysis (FEA) to model system-wide interactions at scale. HPC resources will enable the simultaneous execution of high-resolution simulations capturing material flow, thermal dynamics, and equipment wear, while MARL algorithms train adaptive control policies across distributed compute nodes. The computational workflow will integrate Python-based optimization libraries with GPU-accelerated FEA solvers, utilizing MPI for inter-node communication to synchronize real-time data from digital twin representations of production lines. Expected outcomes include a validated framework for predictive maintenance scheduling, energy consumption minimization, and throughput optimization under variable demand constraints. By quantifying the trade-offs between computational granularity and decision latency, this work aims to establish scalable benchmarks for HPC-driven industrial process optimization. The results will directly support the deployment of agile, data-driven manufacturing systems, reducing downtime by an estimated 15–20% in pilot-scale implementations while providing open-source tools for broader adoption in small-to-medium enterprises. This project aligns with national priorities for smart manufacturing resilience and workforce training in advanced computational modeling techniques.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of engineers engaged in the management and design of systems, execution of new product designs, improvement of manufacturing processes, and the management and direction of the physical or technical functions of an organization. Includes instruction in basic engineering principles, project management, industrial processes, production and operations management, systems integration and control, quality control, and statistics.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance understanding of family system dynamics and improve therapeutic interventions through large-scale computational modeling. Family systems are inherently complex, with interactions influenced by individual behaviors, relational patterns, and systemic stressors such as financial instability or cultural conflicts. Traditional analytical methods often struggle to capture the nonlinear, interdependent nature of these dynamics, limiting the ability to predict outcomes or design targeted interventions. To address this, we propose developing agent-based models (ABMs) that simulate family interactions across diverse scenarios, incorporating variables such as communication styles, conflict resolution strategies, cultural norms, and stressors. These models will integrate empirical data from anonymized clinical records, longitudinal family studies, and validated psychometric assessments to parameterize agents and validate outcomes. Machine learning techniques will be applied to identify patterns in interaction data and refine model accuracy. The scale of these simulations—encompassing thousands of virtual families with varying structures and contextual factors—requires HPC resources to manage parallel processing, optimize parameter space exploration, and reduce computational latency. Expected outcomes include identifying resilience factors that buffer against systemic dysfunction, uncovering critical thresholds for intervention efficacy, and mapping how cultural or socioeconomic variables moderate therapeutic outcomes. This work will directly inform the development of adaptive, personalized family therapy frameworks and training tools for clinicians. By bridging computational social science with family psychology, the project aims to establish a novel methodology for studying relational systems, with implications for improving evidence-based practices in counseling and applied psychology. Access to HPC infrastructure is essential to achieve the necessary computational depth and scalability, enabling transformative insights into family dynamics that traditional methods cannot attain.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide therapeutic, evaluative, and research services to families and individuals in the family unit context. Includes instruction in natural and family systems theory, family and group rituals, family evaluation and assessment, marital and couples therapy, sex therapy, parenting, interviewing techniques, genogram construction, family sculpting, diversity issues, family violence, family law, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The increasing complexity of pediatric diagnostic imaging, particularly in the context of rare diseases and developmental anomalies, necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize image analysis, reduce radiation exposure, and improve diagnostic accuracy. Current clinical workflows often rely on manual or semi-automated methods, which are time-consuming and prone to variability, especially when interpreting subtle anatomical and functional changes in growing patients. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven framework for automated, multimodal analysis of pediatric radiology data, integrating magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), computed tomography (CT), and ultrasound. The primary research problem lies in creating scalable algorithms capable of processing large, heterogeneous imaging datasets while accounting for age-specific anatomical variations and minimizing radiation dose in iterative imaging protocols. The computational approach will leverage deep learning architectures, including 3D convolutional neural networks and transformer models, to perform tasks such as anomaly detection, organ segmentation, and dose-optimized image reconstruction. These models will be trained on a curated dataset of over 50,000 de-identified pediatric imaging studies, augmented with synthetic data to address class imbalances in rare pathologies. HPC resources will enable distributed training across multiple GPU nodes, hyperparameter optimization at scale, and validation through computational phantoms simulating pediatric anatomies. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated pipeline for automated detection of 15+ congenital and acquired pediatric conditions, (2) dose-reduction algorithms achieving diagnostic-quality CT images with ≤30% of standard radiation exposure, and (3) open-source tools for age-adjusted z-score mapping of organ development. By providing radiologists with quantitative, population-normalized metrics and AI-assisted decision support, this work aims to establish new standards for precision imaging in pediatric care while generating computational models that explicitly address the unique requirements of developing anatomical systems.
cip_definition: Research focused on all forms of diagnostic imaging as it pertains to the diagnosis and treatment of diseases in the newborn, infant, child, and adolescent.

abstract: Clinical pathology laboratories generate vast, heterogeneous datasets from multi-omic analyses, diagnostic imaging, and high-throughput biomarker assays, yet integrating these data to improve disease diagnosis and mechanistic understanding remains a critical challenge. Current computational workflows struggle to harmonize disparate data types—such as genomic sequences, proteomic profiles, and clinical chemistry parameters—while maintaining the resolution required for actionable insights. This project proposes to develop a scalable, high-performance computing (HPC) framework to enable real-time integration of multimodal clinical pathology data, with an emphasis on identifying predictive signatures for autoimmune disorders and hematologic malignancies. Leveraging GPU-accelerated machine learning pipelines, we will train ensemble models on curated datasets from clinical chemistry, flow cytometry, and targeted DNA sequencing to detect subtle diagnostic patterns. Computational methods will include dimensionality reduction for cross-platform data fusion, graph-based neural networks to model biomarker interactions, and Bayesian inference to quantify diagnostic uncertainty.
