The HPC infrastructure will also support large-scale simulations of host-pathogen interactions in virology and toxicology studies, using molecular dynamics to map antigen-antibody binding affinities. Anticipated outcomes include validated predictive models for early-stage lupus nephritis and myelodysplastic syndromes, alongside optimized pipelines for clinical variant interpretation in molecular diagnostics. This work will directly enhance translational capabilities in academic medical centers by reducing turnaround times for complex cases and enabling data-driven refinements to laboratory test panels. The requested computing resources are essential to process petabytes of raw mass spectrometry, digital pathology, and next-generation sequencing data while adhering to HIPAA-compliant federated learning protocols across partner institutions. By bridging clinical laboratory data silos through advanced computation, this project aims to establish a new paradigm for precision diagnostics in pathology.
cip_definition: Research focused on the clinical laboratory analysis and diagnosis of disease. Includes instruction in performing clinical chemistry, cytogenetics, immunology, laboratory management, microbiology, molecular biology, quality control, serology, toxicology, and virology.

abstract: Neonatal morbidity and mortality remain significant global health challenges, particularly among preterm infants and those with complex perinatal conditions. This project seeks to address critical gaps in understanding the molecular and physiological mechanisms underlying neonatal sepsis and respiratory failure, two leading causes of adverse outcomes in this population. Current limitations in integrating multi-omics data (genomic, proteomic, metabolomic) with high-resolution clinical datasets hinder the development of predictive models for early diagnosis and personalized interventions. We propose a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze longitudinal multi-omics profiles from 500 neonates in combination with real-time physiological monitoring data (heart rate variability, oxygen saturation patterns) and maternal-fetal health records. Machine learning approaches, including recurrent neural networks and graph-based models, will be employed to identify dynamic biomarker signatures predictive of sepsis onset and respiratory deterioration. Parallelized computational fluid dynamics simulations will model pulmonary mechanics in preterm infants with bronchopulmonary dysplasia, incorporating patient-specific CT-derived airway geometries and ventilator parameters. The scale of data integration (≥10 TB heterogeneous datasets) and complexity of multi-scale modeling necessitate HPC resources for distributed memory processing, GPU-accelerated deep learning, and large-scale parameter optimization. Expected outcomes include: (1) identification of novel predictive biomarkers for neonatal sepsis 24-48 hours prior to clinical manifestation, (2) development of individualized ventilation strategy simulations to reduce ventilator-induced lung injury, and (3) creation of open-source computational tools for real-time analysis of neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) datasets. This research directly addresses the program's focus on pathophysiology and clinical management of sick newborns, with potential to transform risk stratification protocols and inform NICUs’ integration of precision medicine approaches. The requested computing resources will enable processing timelines impossible with institutional cluster capacities, particularly for time-sensitive analyses correlating acute clinical events with multi-omics cascades.
cip_definition: Research focused on the physiology of the normal neonate, the pathophysiology of the sick infant, and the diagnosis and management of problems of the newborn infant, including consulting with obstetricians to plan for the care of women with high-risk pregnancies.

abstract: Aging is a complex biopsychosocial process influenced by dynamic interactions between individual health trajectories, social networks, and environmental contexts. While existing gerontological research often examines these factors in isolation, there is a critical need for integrative computational models to simulate how multi-level systems—from cellular aging to community-level support structures—co-evolve over time and influence disparities in healthspan. This project seeks to develop an agent-based modeling (ABM) framework to simulate longitudinal aging processes in diverse populations, incorporating high-dimensional datasets spanning biomarkers, social determinants of health, and geospatial environmental exposures. The computational challenge lies in scaling ABM architectures to handle heterogeneous data from longitudinal aging studies (e.g., biomarker time series, social network dynamics) while maintaining interpretable linkages between micro-level mechanisms (e.g., chronic inflammation) and macro-level outcomes (e.g., cognitive decline). High-performance computing resources will enable parallelized parameter space exploration, Bayesian calibration of model priors using population-level aging datasets, and sensitivity analyses across synthetic cohorts representing global diversity in aging experiences. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source ABM toolkit optimized for gerontological research, (2) novel insights into resilience mechanisms that buffer against social-environmental stressors, and (3) predictive models identifying critical intervention windows for delaying age-related functional decline. By bridging computational social science with systems biology approaches, this work addresses a methodological gap in gerontology while advancing equitable precision health strategies for aging populations. The proposed simulations will require sustained access to GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning integration and ≥100TB of distributed storage for multimodal data harmonization, exceeding the capabilities of standard institutional computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the human aging process and aged human populations, using the knowledge and methodologies of the social sciences, psychology and the biological and health sciences.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate how organizational leadership practices in higher education institutions influence workforce development outcomes during periods of rapid technological change. As institutions face growing demands to align training programs with evolving industry needs, leaders must navigate complex decision-making processes involving stakeholder priorities, resource constraints, and workforce skill gaps. Current qualitative approaches provide limited capacity to model dynamic interactions between these variables at scale. We propose leveraging agent-based modeling (ABM) and natural language processing (NLP) to simulate decision pathways in institutional leadership teams and predict their downstream effects on workforce readiness. High-performance computing resources are essential for processing longitudinal workforce data from public repositories (e.g., IPEDS, O*NET) and running thousands of parameterized simulations capturing diverse leadership scenarios. The ABM framework will model agents representing administrators, faculty, and industry partners, incorporating behavioral patterns derived from interview transcripts and policy documents analyzed through transformer-based NLP models. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of leadership strategies that optimize alignment between institutional training investments and regional labor market needs, and 2) predictive metrics for evaluating how decision timelines affect workforce retention in critical technology sectors. Results will provide actionable insights for designing leadership development programs that enhance adaptive capacity in educational organizations, particularly regarding AI integration and digital transformation challenges. By combining computational social science methods with human resource development theory, this work advances empirical foundations for data-driven leadership in education while demonstrating novel applications of HPC resources to administrative decision science.
cip_title: Education and Human Resource Studies/ Development
cip_definition: A program that focuses on learning in individual, group, and organizational contexts through lifelong learning, career development, training and development, and organizational development.

abstract: Aromatherapy leverages the complex chemical composition of essential oils to elicit therapeutic effects, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying their efficacy remain poorly characterized. This gap hinders the development of evidence-based protocols for optimizing blends, ensuring safety, and personalizing treatments. Traditional experimental methods struggle to address the combinatorial complexity of essential oil mixtures, which often contain hundreds of bioactive compounds interacting synergistically or antagonistically with physiological targets. This project proposes a computational framework to model these interactions at scale, requiring high-performance computing (HPC) resources to overcome current limitations in processing power and data handling. The research will integrate molecular dynamics simulations, machine learning, and cheminformatics to investigate three key areas: (1) the binding affinities of essential oil constituents (e.g., terpenes, phenolics) to human receptors involved in pain, inflammation, and neurotransmission; (2) the physicochemical dynamics of dermal and olfactory absorption pathways; and (3) the stability and interaction profiles of blended oils under varying carrier formulations. Large datasets from public repositories (e.g., PubChem, ChEMBL) and phytochemical databases will be cross-referenced with ethnobotanical records to prioritize understudied botanicals. Simulations will employ GPU-accelerated docking (AutoDock-GPU) and all-atom molecular dynamics (GROMACS) to model multi-component systems, while neural networks will predict synergistic relationships and toxicity risks. Outcomes will include predictive models for optimizing therapeutic blends, a curated database of aroma-chemical interactions, and quantitative safety thresholds for common application methods. By elucidating structure-activity relationships in aromachemistry, this work aims to advance clinical aromatherapy from anecdotal practice to a precision modality grounded in molecular evidence, directly informing curriculum updates in safety protocols and blend design for academic training programs. The requested HPC resources are critical to managing the terabytes of simulation data and enabling real-time analysis of multi-scale biochemical networks.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to provide therapeutic care through the preparation and application of extracted essential oils from plants, including flowers (botanicals), roots, berries, and bark. Includes instruction in aromatherapy history and theory, basic physiology of absorption, aromachemistry, organic chemistry, botanical taxonomy, carrier oils, essential oils, extraction methods, blending techniques, application methods, safety, client consultation and treatment planning, business management, professional standards and ethics, and applicable regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to optimize additive manufacturing processes for next-generation composite materials, addressing critical gaps in process reliability and material performance prediction. Additive manufacturing enables complex geometries and multi-material structures, but defects such as porosity, residual stress, and interfacial delamination remain persistent challenges. Current simulation tools lack the resolution to model multi-physics interactions—including thermal gradients, phase transitions, and dynamic material interfaces—at the spatiotemporal scales required for industrial applications. To overcome these limitations, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-driven approach combining finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to resolve process-structure-property relationships. High-fidelity FEA-CFD coupled simulations will model heat transfer, melt pool dynamics, and stress evolution during layer-by-layer deposition, while graph neural networks (GNNs) will predict defect formation probabilities across parameter spaces. The computational workflow will leverage distributed-memory parallelism and GPU acceleration to handle meshes exceeding 100 million elements, with adaptive mesh refinement targeting regions of high thermal or mechanical gradient. Validation will utilize synchrotron X-ray imaging datasets of in-situ process monitoring. Expected outcomes include (1) a validated multi-scale model for defect prediction in metal-ceramic composites, (2) an open-source simulation toolkit optimized for exascale architectures, and (3) process parameter recommendations to minimize defects in industrial laser powder bed fusion systems. By integrating HPC-enabled simulations with experimental data, this work aims to reduce trial-and-error iterations in additive manufacturing by 40-60%, directly supporting advancements in aerospace, energy, and biomedical device applications. The requested computing resources are essential to achieve the necessary spatial resolution (<5 μm) and temporal resolution (<1 ms) across full-scale part simulations, which exceed the memory and runtime capabilities of local cluster systems.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in engineering technologies and engineering-related fields, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Healthcare aides and attendants face significant challenges in optimizing care delivery across dynamic patient populations, particularly in resource-constrained environments. This project seeks to address critical inefficiencies in task prioritization and intervention timing through advanced computational modeling. We propose developing a machine learning framework that integrates real-time patient biometric data, electronic health records (EHRs), and environmental sensor inputs to predict care needs and recommend optimal aide workflows. The research will utilize high-performance computing (HPC) resources to train deep neural networks on multi-modal datasets encompassing over 500,000 historical patient interactions, requiring parallel processing capabilities to handle high-dimensional temporal data from wearable devices and institutional databases. Computational methods will include time-series analysis for early deterioration detection, natural language processing of clinical documentation, and reinforcement learning to simulate task allocation strategies across varying staffing ratios. Agent-based models will further test proposed interventions in simulated care environments with probabilistic patient trajectories. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive algorithm capable of identifying 85% of imminent care needs (e.g., fall risks, medication windows) with 60-minute advance warning, and (2) optimized workflow templates demonstrating ≥25% improvement in aide response times across simulated scenarios. By establishing computational evidence for data-driven care prioritization, this work aims to reduce preventable adverse events while enhancing training protocols for patient care technicians. The requested HPC infrastructure will enable large-scale validation of models across diverse demographic profiles and facility types, directly supporting the program's mission to advance evidence-based practices in routine patient care education.
cip_definition: Any other instructional program that prepares individuals to provide routine patient care and assistance.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the biomechanical and optical interactions governing corneal deformation under varying intraocular pressure (IOP) and mechanical stress, a critical factor in conditions such as keratoconus and post-refractive surgery ectasia. Current clinical models lack the resolution to predict individual susceptibility to vision-threatening deformations due to the cornea’s complex, anisotropic microstructure and dynamic response to physiological forces. To address this gap, we propose a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled multiscale modeling framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA) with ray-tracing simulations. The FEA component will simulate stress-strain distributions across corneal lamellae using patient-specific data from corneal topography, optical coherence tomography, and tonometry. Concurrently, GPU-accelerated ray-tracing will model light propagation through the deformed corneal geometry to quantify aberrations and visual quality degradation. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing high-resolution 3D corneal meshes (∼10^6 elements per simulation), solving nonlinear viscoelastic constitutive equations, and iteratively coupling biomechanical and optical outputs across thousands of parameter combinations. Expected outcomes include a predictive platform correlating microstructural anomalies with macroscopic optical deficits, enabling early diagnosis of subclinical keratoconus and personalized refractive surgery planning. By elucidating how regional variations in collagen fibril orientation modulate both mechanical stability and optical performance, this work will advance therapeutic strategies for preserving visual function in progressive corneal disorders. The computational pipeline will be disseminated as an open-source tool for translational vision research, addressing a critical need for integrative models in physiological optics.
detailed_field: Physiology, oncology, and cancer biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of vision, visual processes, and related phenomena and clinical research and treatment modalities. Includes instruction in ocular anatomy and physiology, microbiology of the eye, electrophysiology, neurophysiology, corneal physiology, photochemistry, psychophysics, visual biophysics and motor systems, sensory mechanisms and photoreception, eye circulation and metabolism, geometric and physical optics, ocular development across the life span, visual stimuli and perception, color vision, eye motility, biometrics and measurement techniques, visual pathology, and environmental issues.

abstract: Agricultural power machinery operation faces critical challenges in balancing operational efficiency, energy consumption, and environmental impact. Current equipment configurations and usage protocols often rely on generalized guidelines, leading to suboptimal performance under variable field conditions, soil types, and crop requirements. This project proposes a computational framework to model and simulate the dynamic interactions between agricultural machinery, environmental variables, and operational tasks. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are requested to develop multi-scale simulations integrating computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for sprayer nozzle efficiency, finite element analysis (FEA) for stress distribution in tillage implements, and machine learning models to optimize real-time equipment adjustments. The study will parameterize equipment such as terrestrial crop-sprayers, precision planters, and harvesters using sensor-derived field data from collaborating farms, including soil moisture, crop density, and terrain topology. Parallelized simulations will evaluate millions of operational scenarios to identify energy-efficient configurations, minimize soil compaction risks, and predict wear patterns in mechanical components. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for adaptive equipment calibration, decision-support tools for fuel and input optimization, and a publicly accessible database of machinery performance metrics under diverse agronomic conditions. By linking computational insights to practical operational workflows, this research aims to advance precision agriculture practices, reduce greenhouse gas emissions per unit yield, and extend machinery service life. The HPC-driven approach addresses a critical gap in agricultural engineering, where traditional trial-and-error field testing cannot adequately capture the complex, nonlinear relationships between machinery operation and agroecosystem responses.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to operate specialized farm, ranch, and agribusiness power equipment of a stationary, mobile, or hand-operated nature. Includes instruction in operating specialized equipment such as terrestrial and airborne crop-spraying equipment; tractors and hauling equipment; planting and harvesting equipment; cutting equipment; power sources and systems for silos, irrigation, pumping, and applications such as dairy, feeding and shearing operations; processing equipment; and applicable electrical, mechanical, and safety principles.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the study of immersive theatrical environments through large-scale simulation and real-time rendering. The research problem centers on the challenge of modeling dynamic, multi-sensory performance spaces that integrate complex variables such as acoustics, lighting, audience movement, and interactive set elements. Traditional stagecraft tools lack the computational capacity to simulate these interdependent systems at scale, limiting the design and testing of innovative productions. To address this, the project will employ agent-based modeling to simulate audience-performer interactions, finite element analysis for acoustic propagation in non-static set designs, and GPU-accelerated ray tracing to optimize dynamic lighting configurations. Additionally, machine learning techniques will be applied to historical performance datasets to identify patterns in audience engagement, informing adaptive staging strategies. The computational workflows will be validated against empirical data from live theatrical experiments, with iterative refinements to improve accuracy. Expected outcomes include a scalable framework for prototyping immersive environments, reducing reliance on physical mock-ups, and enabling the exploration of previously impractical staging concepts. This work holds significance for the performing arts by expanding the creative possibilities of theatrical design while addressing logistical and safety constraints inherent to live productions. The resulting tools will be disseminated as open-source resources to support collaborative innovation across academic and professional theatre communities. By integrating computational rigor with artistic practice, this project aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven stagecraft, fostering interdisciplinary advancements at the intersection of performing arts and HPC.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_title: Dramatic/ Theatre Arts and Stagecraft, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in dramatic/theatre arts and stagecraft, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable biomanufacturing processes necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize biocatalytic systems and bioreactor designs. Current challenges in modeling enzyme-substrate interactions, multiphase fluid dynamics in bioreactors, and metabolic network dynamics in microbial systems limit the efficiency of scaling laboratory-scale processes to industrial production. This project seeks to address these gaps by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop multiscale models integrating molecular-level enzyme kinetics with reactor-scale transport phenomena. The research will employ hybrid computational methods, including molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to resolve atomic-scale interactions of engineered enzymes with non-conventional substrates, coupled with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to model nutrient transport and shear stress distributions in large-scale bioreactors. Machine learning algorithms will be implemented to accelerate parameter optimization for complex kinetic models derived from experimental datasets. The HPC infrastructure will enable parallelized simulations of alternative bioreactor configurations and microbial strain designs, reducing computational time for predictive analysis from weeks to days. Expected outcomes include validated models for (1) predicting enzyme stability in solvent-rich industrial environments, (2) optimizing gas-liquid mass transfer in aerobic fermentation systems, and (3) identifying metabolic bottlenecks in lignocellulosic biofuel production pathways. These computational tools will directly inform experimental prototyping efforts, significantly reducing resource-intensive trial-and-error approaches. The project’s significance lies in its potential to advance scalable bioprocess design for pharmaceutical intermediates, bio-based plastics, and renewable biofuels, aligning with global sustainability goals. By establishing an open-access repository of validated simulation workflows, this work will also enhance collaborative opportunities across the biochemical engineering community, fostering innovation in computational bioprocess engineering.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the study of biochemical processes in living organisms, properties of biological materials, and processes using biochemical agents such as cells, enzymes, and antibodies. Includes instruction in biology, chemistry, physics, biochemistry, thermodynamics, fluid dynamics, bioprocesses, and chemical engineering.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance computational modeling and optimization of metal fabrication processes, addressing critical challenges in precision, efficiency, and material performance. Metal fabrication workflows—including welding, thermal cutting, and structural assembly—are constrained by empirical trial-and-error approaches, which lead to material waste, energy inefficiency, and unpredictable mechanical outcomes under complex thermal and mechanical stresses. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes a multiphysics computational framework integrating finite element analysis (FEA), computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and machine learning (ML) to simulate and optimize fabrication parameters in silico. High-fidelity simulations will model heat transfer, phase transformations, and residual stresses during welding and cutting processes, while ML algorithms will iteratively refine process variables (e.g., torch speed, temperature gradients, filler material composition) to minimize defects and maximize structural integrity. The scale of these simulations—requiring meshes with >10^8 elements to resolve micron-scale material behavior and multiphase interactions—necessitates HPC resources for parallelized computation and large-scale data processing. Additionally, generative adversarial networks (GANs) will be trained on simulation outputs and experimental datasets to predict optimal fabrication pathways for novel alloys or complex geometries. Anticipated outcomes include a validated digital twin framework for real-time process optimization, reduced material waste by ≥15% in targeted workflows, and predictive models for defect avoidance in high-stress applications. This work will directly support curriculum development in computational metallurgy and digital fabrication within the Metal Fabricator program, providing students and industry partners with open-source tools to bridge theoretical training with advanced manufacturing practices. By integrating HPC-driven insights into vocational education, the project aims to elevate technical proficiency in next-generation metal fabrication technologies.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills to further process ferrous and/or non-ferrous metal plates or shapes, and to manufacture and/or install products as interpreted through technical drawings. Includes instruction in trade tools, shop equipment, reading and interpreting blueprints, material handling, welding, thermal cutting, metallurgy, template pattern development, plate and structural fabrication, destructive and non-destructive testing, inspection, shipment preparation and fabrication installation.

abstract: Military information systems face escalating demands for real-time adaptability in contested cyber environments, where traditional static resource allocation frameworks struggle to balance computational efficiency with dynamic threat response. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled decision support system to optimize resource distribution across heterogeneous military networks under adversarial conditions. The research addresses the critical gap in scalable, predictive models capable of simulating multi-domain cyber-physical attacks while maintaining mission-critical latency thresholds. Leveraging parallelized agent-based simulations, the project will model network nodes as autonomous agents with embedded reinforcement learning policies, iteratively trained on HPC clusters to maximize resilience against emergent attack vectors. Computational workflows will integrate graph-theoretic representations of network topology with stochastic game theory to anticipate adversarial behavior, dynamically reallocating bandwidth, storage, and processing resources through distributed optimization algorithms. Key challenges include developing hybrid architectures that synchronize GPU-accelerated machine learning inference with CPU-bound cryptographic verification processes across distributed military clouds. The proposed work will validate models using anonymized operational data from field exercises, scaled through HPC-enabled synthetic data generation to preserve security constraints. Expected outcomes include an open-source simulation framework for testing resource allocation strategies under cyber warfare conditions, quantitative metrics for infrastructure hardening prioritization, and novel protocols for edge computing coordination in bandwidth-constrained tactical environments. This research directly supports next-generation command-and-control systems by providing computational tools to maintain information superiority through adaptive resource management, with potential applications in allied interoperability frameworks and automated cyber defense systems.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, design and application of computer and networking technology to the military environment. Includes instruction in planning; program development; graphical user interfaces; rapid prototyping; program construction; data types, operations; control flow; arrays; records; file I/O; database access; event-driven OOP structures; and enabling global-networked communications, including databases, systems analysis and design, decision support systems, and network security.

abstract: Radiological imaging data are growing in complexity and volume, driven by advancements in multi-parametric and multi-modal acquisition techniques. However, conventional computational methods struggle to efficiently process and analyze these large-scale datasets, limiting the development of robust tools for disease diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment monitoring. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to accelerate the analysis of heterogeneous radiological data, including dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI, diffusion-weighted imaging, and radiomic features extracted from CT and PET scans. The core challenge lies in integrating multi-dimensional imaging data with clinical variables while addressing computational bottlenecks in feature extraction, model training, and validation. We will employ distributed computing strategies to parallelize image preprocessing pipelines, optimize memory-intensive radiomic feature calculations, and train deep learning architectures for tumor phenotyping and outcome prediction. The HPC environment will enable rapid iteration of ensemble models combining convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for image analysis and graph-based methods for capturing spatial relationships within lesions. Validation will involve multi-institutional datasets from oncology cohorts, requiring scalable workflows to handle >50,000 imaging studies and associated metadata. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-source computational platform for large-scale radiological data integration, (2) validated predictive models for glioblastoma progression and lung cancer treatment response, and (3) benchmarks comparing HPC-optimized algorithms against conventional methods in processing speed and predictive accuracy. This work will directly address current limitations in translating quantitative imaging biomarkers into clinical practice by providing the computational infrastructure needed to analyze complex radiological data at scale. Successful implementation could reduce time-to-insight for imaging research by orders of magnitude while enabling discovery of novel biomarkers through analysis of previously intractable datasets. The requested resources will support GPU-accelerated computations, distributed storage for intermediate outputs, and high-throughput job scheduling essential for reproducible radiomics research.
cip_definition: Research focused on Radiology

abstract: The increasing complexity of genomic data presents a critical challenge in clinical genetics, where integrating cytogenetic and molecular findings is essential for accurate diagnosis of genetic disorders. Current analytical pipelines struggle to harmonize heterogeneous data types—such as chromosomal microarray, next-generation sequencing, and epigenetic profiles—while scaling to population-level datasets. This project seeks to address these limitations by developing an integrative computational framework powered by high-performance computing (HPC) to resolve ambiguities in variant interpretation and uncover novel genotype-phenotype relationships. We will process multi-modal genomic data from 10,000 retrospectively collected clinical cases, including unresolved diagnoses of developmental disorders and hereditary cancers, using graph-based genome representations to unify structural variants, single-nucleotide variations, and copy-number alterations. Deep learning models trained on HPC clusters will predict variant pathogenicity by incorporating 3D chromatin architecture data and functional genomic annotations, enabling context-aware prioritization of candidate variants. Additionally, we will implement distributed algorithms to detect cryptic chromosomal rearrangements from low-coverage whole-genome sequencing, reducing reliance on resource-intensive traditional cytogenetics. The HPC environment is indispensable for managing petabyte-scale data storage, parallelizing genome-wide association analyses across millions of loci, and optimizing hyperparameters for ensemble models through iterative GPU-accelerated workflows. Expected outcomes include a validated open-source platform for unified cytogenomic analysis, a curated repository of reclassified variants of uncertain significance, and improved diagnostic yield for complex cases. By bridging computational scalability gaps in multi-omics integration, this work will advance precision diagnostics and inform guidelines for clinical reporting of intertwined cytogenetic and molecular findings, directly enhancing management strategies for patients with rare genetic diseases.
cip_definition: Research on how to direct and interpret both clinical cytogenetic and molecular genetic analyses relevant to the diagnosis and management of human genetic diseases.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to address critical gaps in understanding gene-environment interactions that drive differential susceptibility to chemical toxicants, with a focus on mechanisms underlying xenobiotic metabolism and toxicokinetic variability in human populations. Traditional in vitro and animal models often fail to recapitulate the complexity of human genetic diversity and its impact on molecular responses to environmental toxins. This project will employ computational toxicology approaches to model population-scale variations in detoxification pathways, leveraging existing toxicogenomics datasets from human cohort studies. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to conduct large-scale simulations of cytochrome P450 enzyme polymorphisms and their functional consequences on toxin bioactivation across diverse virtual patient populations. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations will characterize structural perturbations caused by genetic variants in key metabolizing enzymes, while physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling will integrate these data to predict interindividual differences in toxin clearance rates. A novel machine learning framework will be developed to identify gene-gene-environment interactions that modulate pulmonary toxicity outcomes for common air pollutants. Expected outcomes include the identification of high-risk genetic signatures for chemical susceptibility and predictive models of toxicant-pathway interactions that account for real-world genetic diversity. These computational tools will enable precision risk assessment strategies and inform targeted countermeasures against environmental toxicants. The scale of genomic data integration, complexity of multi-compartment PBPK models, and need for high-throughput virtual screening of toxin-enzyme interactions necessitate dedicated HPC infrastructure to achieve biologically relevant simulation timescales and population-level statistical power. This work directly advances molecular toxicology's capacity to bridge mechanistic insights with population health protection goals.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the genetic determinants of susceptibility to external pollutants and poisons; the interaction of toxic agents with biological systems at the molecular and cellular levels; and the development of countermeasures and treatments. Includes instruction in pharmacogenetics, biomolecular structure, gene expression and regulation, transgenic modeling, toxic events signaling, transcriptional activation, mutagenesis and carcinogenesis, pulmonary toxicology, xenobiotic metabolism, oxidative stress, risk assessment, molecular dosimetry, and studies of specific toxins and treatment therapies.

abstract: This research seeks to model the impact of decentralized climate compliance mechanisms on global supply chain resilience, focusing on how heterogeneous carbon pricing regimes and sustainability-linked trade agreements influence multinational enterprise (MNE) decision-making. While climate policy is increasingly shaping international commerce, existing frameworks fail to capture the nonlinear interactions between evolving regulatory landscapes, geopolitical trade barriers, and adaptive supply network reconfiguration. The project will develop an agent-based computational model simulating MNE responses to multi-jurisdictional carbon constraints, incorporating real-world data on 1) regional carbon tax trajectories, 2) cross-border green certification reciprocity, and 3) logistics network vulnerabilities exposed by recent climate disruptions. High-performance computing resources are required to process petabyte-scale trade flow datasets from UN Comtrade and the OECD, train deep reinforcement learning agents representing corporate sustainability strategists, and run Monte Carlo simulations across 10^4 potential policy combination scenarios. The computational architecture will integrate graph neural networks to model supply web dependencies with transformer-based prediction of regulatory cascade effects. Anticipated outcomes include a decision support system capable of identifying critical policy leverage points for maintaining trade continuity during climate-driven market transitions, as well as risk matrices quantifying the trade competitiveness impacts of asymmetric decarbonization timelines. This work addresses an urgent gap in computational international business research by providing quantitative frameworks to align cross-border commerce with planetary boundaries while mitigating protectionist trade distortions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage international businesses and/or business operations. Includes instruction in the principles and processes of export sales, trade controls, foreign operations and related problems, monetary issues, international business policy, and applications to doing business in specific countries and markets.

abstract: This project seeks to develop and validate computational models to optimize individualized educational strategies for students with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Current approaches to designing personalized learning plans rely heavily on qualitative observations and trial-and-error adjustments, which can delay effective interventions. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze large-scale, multimodal datasets from classroom settings, including behavioral recordings, sensory response metrics, and longitudinal academic performance data. Machine learning models will be trained to identify patterns linking specific instructional methods, environmental adjustments, and communication supports to measurable improvements in engagement, skill acquisition, and emotional regulation. A key innovation involves agent-based simulations of student-teacher interactions, which will test hypothetical teaching strategies under diverse virtual scenarios before real-world implementation. These simulations will incorporate dynamic variables such as sensory sensitivities, communication preferences, and task complexity. The computational workflow requires parallel processing of high-resolution video data (for nonverbal behavior analysis) and real-time optimization of adaptive learning algorithms. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive framework to guide educators in selecting evidence-based strategies during individualized education program (IEP) development, (2) quantified thresholds for environmental adaptations (e.g., lighting, noise levels) that maximize student focus, and (3) open-source tools for simulating ASD learning profiles to enhance teacher training programs. By bridging computational analytics with special education pedagogy, this research aims to empower teachers with data-driven decision-making tools while preserving the human-centric values of autism education. The HPC resources are critical for handling the project’s multimodal data integration, large-scale parameter space exploration, and rapid iteration of simulation models.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Autism
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with autism, and that prepares individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with autism, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising autistic students, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.

abstract: Agricultural communication plays a critical role in bridging scientific advancements with practical applications, yet the dynamic, data-rich nature of modern agricultural systems presents challenges in synthesizing and disseminating actionable insights. This project seeks to address the growing disconnect between agricultural research outputs and their effective translation to stakeholders—farmers, policymakers, and industry professionals—by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to analyze large-scale datasets and model communication efficacy. The core research problem involves understanding how multi-modal agricultural information (e.g., technical reports, social media, sensor data) propagates through heterogeneous audiences, and how computational tools can optimize content delivery for clarity, engagement, and behavioral impact. Using natural language processing (NLP) and network analysis, we will process terabytes of textual, visual, and temporal data from agricultural extension services, digital news platforms, and participatory sensing networks. Machine learning models will identify patterns in audience receptivity, misinformation risks, and content diffusion pathways across regional and demographic scales. Agent-based simulations will test communication strategies under varying scenarios, such as drought advisories or pest management guidelines, to predict outcomes on stakeholder decision-making. HPC resources are essential for training transformer-based NLP architectures, running parallelized simulations, and managing spatially explicit datasets spanning crop yield records, climate projections, and economic indicators. Expected outcomes include a framework for data-driven agricultural communication design, predictive tools to prioritize high-impact messaging, and actionable insights into mitigating misinformation in rapidly evolving contexts like precision agriculture adoption or climate adaptation. By integrating computational social science with agricultural systems analysis, this work aims to enhance the scalability and precision of science communication, directly supporting food security and sustainable agricultural practices.
major_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences
detailed_field: Agricultural, animal, plant, and veterinary sciences nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply journalistic, communication, and broadcasting principles to the development, production, and transmittal of agricultural information. Includes instruction in basic journalism, broadcasting, film/video, and communication techniques; the production of technically specialized information products for agricultural audiences; and the principles of agricultural sciences and business operations needed to develop and communicate agricultural subject matter in effective ways.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the spatial and temporal dynamics of cross-cultural exchange networks in early modern Eurasia (1500–1800 CE) using large-scale computational analysis of multilingual trade records, travelogues, and diplomatic correspondence. The central research problem revolves around identifying patterns of knowledge transfer, commodity circulation, and intercultural interaction that traditional close-reading methods struggle to reconstruct from fragmentary, multi-archive sources. Our team will employ high-performance computing resources to process and analyze a corpus of digitized historical documents spanning 12 languages from the Ottoman, Safavid, Mughal, and Qing empires, alongside European colonial archives. Computational methods will include natural language processing pipelines adapted for historical orthographies, network analysis of named entities (e.g., merchants, institutions, commodities), and geospatial modeling of trade routes using probabilistic record linkage across disparate datasets. The analysis will leverage GPU-accelerated transformer models to handle non-Latin scripts and OCR-corrected texts, while distributed computing frameworks will enable systematic comparison of exchange patterns across political and linguistic boundaries. Expected outcomes include 1) a geotemporal database mapping the evolution of trans-Eurasian connections, 2) quantitative models testing hypotheses about the relationship between state formation and commercial networks, and 3) visualization tools for analyzing multi-decadal shifts in intercultural contact zones. This computationally intensive approach will provide new empirical foundations for debates about early modern globalization, challenging Eurocentric narratives through systematic analysis of Asian-language sources. The project will demonstrate how HPC resources can advance historical methodology by enabling systematic analysis of previously intractable multilingual corpora at continental scales.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in history, not elsewhere classified

abstract: The rise of antibiotic-resistant bacterial pathogens poses a critical threat to global public health, necessitating advanced approaches to elucidate resistance mechanisms and evolutionary trajectories. Current gaps in understanding how pathogenic bacteria adapt to antimicrobial pressures and evade host immune responses hinder the development of targeted interventions. This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the genetic, structural, and population-level factors driving pathogenicity and resistance in clinically relevant bacterial species, including multidrug-resistant *Staphylococcus aureus* and *Pseudomonas aeruginosa*. We will integrate large-scale genomic datasets from clinical isolates with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to address two interconnected aims: (1) characterize the genetic diversity and evolutionary dynamics of resistance genes across bacterial populations using comparative genomics and Bayesian phylogenetic modeling, and (2) simulate interactions between bacterial virulence factors—such as adhesins, secretion systems, and antibiotic-modifying enzymes—and their molecular targets to identify mechanistic vulnerabilities. HPC resources will enable the assembly and analysis of terabyte-scale sequencing data from global surveillance cohorts, as well as microsecond-scale MD simulations of bacterial membrane proteins interacting with host immune molecules (e.g., phagocyte receptors) and antimicrobial compounds. By coupling population genomics with atomistic resolution modeling, this work aims to uncover conserved structural motifs in resistance determinants, map transmission pathways of high-risk clades, and predict mutational hotspots that facilitate immune evasion. Expected outcomes include the identification of novel resistance biomarkers, actionable targets for anti-virulence therapies, and frameworks for real-time genomic surveillance of emerging pathogens. This research will directly inform clinical strategies to mitigate resistance spread and enhance the design of next-generation antimicrobials, aligning with public health priorities to combat drug-resistant infections.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of pathogenic bacteria that are significant factors in causing or facilitating human disease. Includes instruction in the pathogenesis of bacterial diseases, bacterial genetics and physiology, bacterial anatomy and structure, antigens, bacterial reproduction, bacterial adhesion, phagocytes, and the identification of new or mutated bacteria and bacterial agents.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop a novel framework for optimizing dynamic portfolio strategies in decentralized finance (DeFi) markets, a rapidly evolving subset of blockchain-based investment ecosystems. Traditional quantitative models in securities analysis struggle to address the unique computational challenges of DeFi, including hyper-volatility, non-linear dependencies among tokenized assets, and real-time liquidity shifts across automated market makers (AMMs). The project aims to resolve these limitations by integrating agent-based simulations of AMM protocols with reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms to identify adaptive trading policies under stochastic market conditions. Computational workflows will involve large-scale Monte Carlo simulations to model liquidity pool dynamics, coupled with distributed training of RL agents across thousands of parallelized market scenarios. Key challenges include scaling graph-based representations of cross-protocol arbitrage opportunities and optimizing memory-intensive backtesting across multi-chain transaction histories. The proposed HPC infrastructure will enable processing of on-chain data spanning 10+ DeFi platforms (e.g., Uniswap, Curve, Balancer) and synthetic datasets reflecting stress events like flash crashes or protocol exploits. Anticipated outcomes include (1) a publicly accessible benchmark for DeFi portfolio performance under regime-switching conditions, (2) open-source tools for simulating composable yield strategies, and (3) quantitative insights into systemic risks arising from leverage recursion in lending protocols. By bridging computational finance with blockchain analytics, this work will provide institutional investors and regulatory bodies with empirically grounded frameworks for evaluating DeFi instruments—a critical need as tokenized securities gain traction in global markets. The resource request targets 200,000 GPU-hours annually to support continuous training cycles and live market inference pipelines.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to manage assets placed in capital markets, and related technical operations. Includes instruction in security analysis, debt and equity analysis, investment strategies, securities markets, computer-assisted research, portfolio management, portfolio performance analysis, and applications to specific investment problems and business situations.

abstract: The increasing complexity of music industry ecosystems, driven by digital platforms, dynamic consumer behavior, and globalized markets, necessitates advanced computational tools to optimize decision-making for music organizations. Traditional analytical methods often fail to capture the scale and interdependencies of data from streaming services, social media, ticket sales, and artist contracts, limiting the ability to forecast trends, allocate resources efficiently, or mitigate financial risks. This project proposes the development of a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework to model and simulate music industry dynamics, with a focus on improving strategic planning for artist promotion, event logistics, and revenue optimization. The research will employ machine learning algorithms, including graph neural networks and clustering techniques, to analyze large-scale datasets spanning music consumption patterns, regional market disparities, and cross-platform engagement metrics. Agent-based modeling will simulate stakeholder interactions (e.g., artists, venues, distributors) under varying economic and regulatory scenarios, while Monte Carlo methods will assess financial risks in tour planning and merchandising investments. The computational workload requires parallel processing capabilities to handle real-time data integration from APIs (e.g., Spotify, Ticketmaster) and probabilistic simulations of multi-year industry trends. Expected outcomes include predictive tools to identify underserved markets, optimize tour routing based on energy/cost constraints, and evaluate the impact of licensing policies on revenue streams. By leveraging HPC resources, this project aims to provide music managers and organizations with scalable, data-driven strategies to enhance operational resilience, maximize artist visibility, and adapt to rapidly shifting industry landscapes. The resulting models and datasets will be disseminated through an open-access platform tailored for academic and industry stakeholders in music management, fostering collaboration between computational researchers and arts administrators.
major_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design
detailed_field: Visual arts, media studies, and design nec
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to organize and manage music organizations, operations, facilities, and personnel. Includes instruction in business and financial management; marketing and fundraising; personnel management and labor relations; event promotion and management; music products merchandising; artist agency and promotion; music law; and applications to specific activities such as managing theaters, recording studios and companies, bands and other ensembles, individual artists, and music organizations.

abstract: Maritime law enforcement faces unique challenges in detecting and responding to illicit activities across vast, dynamic ocean environments. Traditional methods for monitoring piracy, smuggling, and illegal fishing often rely on fragmented data streams, manual analysis, and reactive strategies, leading to inefficiencies in resource deployment and delayed interventions. This project proposes the development of an integrated computational framework to optimize maritime surveillance and enforcement operations through advanced predictive analytics, real-time sensor fusion, and multi-agent simulation. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process heterogeneous datasets—including satellite imagery, automatic identification system (AIS) trajectories, historical incident reports, and environmental sensor networks—using machine learning models to identify anomalous vessel behavior and forecast high-risk zones. Agent-based modeling will simulate interdiction scenarios, incorporating variables such as patrol vessel dynamics, weather conditions, and adversarial tactics to evaluate response protocols and resource allocation strategies. A key innovation lies in coupling hydrodynamic simulations with reinforcement learning algorithms to model vessel pursuit dynamics under varying sea states, enabling the design of adaptive interception pathways. The computational demands of training deep neural networks on terabyte-scale geospatial datasets and running parallelized, stochastic simulations necessitate access to GPU-accelerated nodes and distributed memory architectures. Expected outcomes include a decision-support tool for real-time threat prioritization, a risk-based patrol optimization engine, and a scenario-testing platform for training personnel in emergent threat environments. By bridging computational science and maritime operational requirements, this work aims to establish a scalable framework for enhancing situational awareness, reducing response times, and improving the cost-effectiveness of maritime law enforcement agencies globally.
cip_definition: A program focusing on the application of law enforcement and security principles and procedures to the marine environment. Includes instruction in criminal and nautical law, nautical terminology, seamanship and vessel operation, vessel maintenance, navigation and navigation systems, meteorology, vessel and passenger safety, radar and remote sensing systems, communications systems, vessel pursuit and stop, boarding and arrest techniques, investigative and evidence techniques, weaponry and applications to specific situations such as piracy, drug trafficking and smuggling.

abstract: Cybersecurity policy frameworks must rapidly adapt to evolving adversarial tactics, yet existing approaches to strategy development often lack rigorous, data-driven validation of resilience under complex, large-scale attack scenarios. This project seeks to address this gap by developing computational models to simulate multi-stage cyber conflicts across heterogeneous infrastructure networks while evaluating the cascading impacts of policy decisions on systemic security outcomes. Leveraging high-performance computing resources, we propose an agent-based modeling environment that integrates geopolitical decision-making algorithms with technical vulnerability landscapes, simulating nation-state and criminal threat actors targeting cross-sector digital ecosystems under varying defense postures. The computational framework will process real-world datasets on critical infrastructure interdependencies, historical incident patterns, and emerging attack vectors to parameterize scenarios ranging from regional ransomware campaigns to coordinated infrastructure disruption. Machine learning techniques will be applied to analyze simulation outputs, identifying policy configurations that optimize tradeoffs between proactive defense investments, incident response agility, and economic constraints. By modeling recursive feedback loops between attacker adaptation and defender policy adjustments at petabyte scale, this research aims to produce quantifiable metrics for policy resilience—a novel contribution to cybersecurity strategy literature. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for stress-testing defense policies under synthetic crisis conditions and evidence-based recommendations for dynamic resource allocation frameworks. This work directly supports policymakers in transitioning from reactive compliance-based paradigms to anticipatory, scenario-hardened strategies while establishing computational social science methodologies for cybersecurity governance research.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the study of strategy, policy, and standards regarding the security of and operations in cyberspace. Includes instruction in incident response, information assurance, recovery policies, vulnerability reduction, deterrence, threat reduction, and resiliency.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing complexity of analyzing multimedia news content in real time, a critical challenge in modern broadcast journalism. As media consumption shifts toward digital, on-demand platforms, journalists must rapidly process vast quantities of video, audio, and social media data to identify emerging stories, verify sources, and assess public sentiment. Existing tools for content analysis often lack the scalability to handle high-resolution video streams or multi-modal datasets, limiting their utility in dynamic news environments. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a computational framework leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to enable large-scale, real-time analysis of broadcast media. The project will utilize machine learning models—including natural language processing for transcription and sentiment analysis, computer vision for detecting visual biases or manipulated footage, and graph-based algorithms to map the propagation of narratives across platforms. These models will be trained on diverse datasets spanning historical news archives, live broadcasts, and social media interactions, requiring parallelized processing across GPU clusters to manage computational demands. Key outcomes include an open-source toolkit for automated content tagging, anomaly detection in news streams, and visualizations of narrative networks, all optimized for integration into broadcast journalism workflows. By accelerating the identification of misinformation patterns and ethical risks in news production, this research aims to strengthen accountability in media reporting while equipping journalists with scalable tools to meet the demands of 24/7 news cycles. The requested HPC resources are essential to process terabytes of multimedia data, train multi-modal AI systems, and simulate real-world scenarios where latency and accuracy are critical to maintaining public trust in journalism.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the methods and techniques for reporting, producing, and delivering news and news programs via radio, television, and video/film media; and that prepares individuals to be professional broadcast journalists, editors, producers, directors, and managers. Includes instruction in the principles of broadcast technology; broadcast reporting; on- and off-camera and microphone procedures and techniques; program, sound, and video/film editing; program design and production; media law and policy; and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a predictive maintenance framework for commercial and industrial vehicles using high-performance computing (HPC) to address inefficiencies in traditional maintenance practices. Current vehicle maintenance protocols often rely on reactive or scheduled interventions, leading to unnecessary downtime, premature part replacements, or unexpected failures. To overcome these challenges, we propose a computational approach integrating telemetry data from onboard sensors, historical maintenance records, and physics-based simulations of vehicle component degradation. The research problem centers on modeling complex interactions between mechanical wear, environmental conditions, and operational stressors across diverse vehicle platforms. HPC resources will enable large-scale parameter optimization for machine learning models predicting failure probabilities, coupled with finite element analysis simulations of critical components (e.g., engine blocks, transmission systems) under varied load scenarios. The computational workflow will employ parallelized algorithms to process real-time sensor streams while iteratively training neural networks on historical fault patterns. Expected outcomes include an adaptive maintenance recommendation system capable of optimizing service intervals at fleet-wide scales, reducing operational costs by 15-30% in preliminary trials. Additionally, the project will generate open-access datasets of simulated component stress profiles to support educational tool development for technician training programs. The requested computing resources are essential for handling the multi-terabyte datasets involved, executing millions of finite element simulations across parameter spaces, and maintaining low-latency processing for real-time diagnostic applications. Successful implementation will advance data-driven decision-making in vehicle maintenance while bridging emerging computational methods with hands-on repair technologies.
cip_title: Vehicle Maintenance and Repair Technology/ Technician, General
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to apply technical knowledge and skills in the adjustment, maintenance, part replacement, and repair of vehicles and mobile equipment.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable, data-driven framework to optimize pedagogical strategies for teaching complex engineering concepts using high-performance computing (HPC) to model learner interactions with simulation-based training environments. Engineering education faces a critical challenge in balancing conceptual rigor with accessible, personalized instruction, particularly as virtual labs and digital twins become central to modern curricula. Traditional pedagogical models struggle to adapt to heterogeneous learner profiles, leading to inefficiencies in skill acquisition. To address this, we propose an HPC-enabled analysis of multimodal educational datasets—including interaction logs, eye-tracking metrics, and assessment outcomes from virtual engineering simulations—to identify patterns in concept mastery, cognitive load, and problem-solving behaviors. Machine learning models (e.g., graph neural networks and transformer-based architectures) will be trained on these datasets to predict optimal instructional pathways, dynamically adjusting content delivery based on real-time performance metrics. The computational workflow involves parallelized processing of terabyte-scale datasets, coupled with agent-based simulations of classroom-scale learning trajectories under varying pedagogical conditions. By leveraging GPU-accelerated clusters, this approach will enable rapid iteration of teaching strategies across diverse demographic and disciplinary contexts. Anticipated outcomes include a validated framework for adaptive engineering education, open-source tools for simulation analytics, and evidence-based guidelines for deploying AI-augmented instruction in virtual labs. This work bridges gaps between educational theory, computational modeling, and engineering practice, offering a template for data-informed curriculum design in emerging technical domains. The requested HPC resources are essential to handle the combinatorial complexity of multivariate learning data and to simulate large-scale educational environments with low-latency feedback—a capability unattainable with conventional computing infrastructure.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach engineering and/or engineering subject matter areas, at various educational levels. Includes instruction in general engineering principals or at least one specific engineering discipline and in educational curriculum, instruction, pedagogy.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing large-scale, multi-domain industrial systems under uncertainty, with applications in logistics, manufacturing, and energy distribution networks. A central challenge in systems engineering lies in balancing competing objectives—such as cost efficiency, resilience, and sustainability—while accounting for stochastic demand, resource variability, and dynamic interdependencies among subsystems. Current methods often rely on simplified models or heuristic decomposition strategies that fail to capture system-wide interactions at scale. We propose a hybrid approach combining mixed-integer programming, agent-based simulation, and distributed reinforcement learning to model complex systems holistically. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical for three components: (1) parallelizable scenario analysis to evaluate thousands of stochastic futures via Monte Carlo methods, (2) GPU-accelerated training of deep reinforcement learning policies for real-time adaptive control, and (3) distributed optimization of system architectures using decomposition-coordination algorithms across multiple compute nodes. The computational workload requires sustained access to clustered GPU nodes and large-memory CPUs due to the combinatorial nature of design space exploration and the need to maintain terabyte-scale datasets for scenario libraries. Anticipated outcomes include novel algorithms for scalable systems optimization, validated through case studies on pharmaceutical supply chain redesign and renewable-integrated microgrid planning. This work will advance systems engineering methodologies by enabling end-to-end analysis of systems with >10^6 decision variables and nonlinear constraints, while providing open-source computational tools for the research community. Successful implementation will directly inform resilient infrastructure design principles and contribute to the development of next-generation decision support systems for industry practitioners.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply mathematical and scientific principles to the design, development and operational evaluation of total systems solutions to a wide variety of engineering problems, including the integration of human, physical, energy, communications, management, and information requirements as needed, and the application of requisite analytical methods to specific situations.

abstract: This research project seeks to investigate how cross-national disparities in educational access and learning outcomes are shaped by intersecting policy, socioeconomic, and cultural factors, with a focus on low- and middle-income countries. Current comparative studies often rely on simplified models that inadequately capture complex interactions between macro-level institutional conditions, household dynamics, and student trajectories. To address this gap, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze multi-decadal, multi-source datasets spanning 120+ countries, including harmonized assessments (PISA, TIMSS), UNESCO demographic records, policy document archives, and longitudinal migration surveys. Computational workflows will integrate multilevel Bayesian modeling, natural language processing of educational policy texts, and agent-based simulations of educational decision-making under resource constraints. These methods require iterative parameter estimation across billions of data points and thousands of parallel simulations to account for contextual variability. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of policy configurations that most effectively mitigate achievement gaps in differing national contexts, 2) network analysis of educational migration patterns correlated with transnational skill demands, and 3) open-source tools for comparative analysis of equity-oriented education reforms. The scale of geospatial-temporal modeling and text corpus analysis (20+ million policy documents across 50 languages) necessitates HPC capabilities for distributed memory processing and GPU-accelerated transformer models. Results will advance methodological approaches in international education research while providing evidence for targeted interventions addressing Sustainable Development Goal 4 (Quality Education). Resource allocation will support critical computations that cannot feasibly run on local infrastructure, particularly cross-national counterfactual policy simulations requiring weeks of continuous processing across 500+ cores.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the educational phenomena, practices, and institutions within different societies and states in a comparative perspective, and the study of international educational issues. Includes instruction in comparative research methods, country- or area-specific studies, cross-national studies of learning and teaching styles, international educational policy and development, and analyses of educational migration patterns and experiences.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the transmission and transformation of cultural narratives across Western Europe from the late medieval period to the early modern era using computational text analysis. The research addresses a critical gap in understanding how regional identities and collective memory were shaped through textual production, particularly in understudied vernacular sources such as municipal records, regional chronicles, and popular literary works. Current scholarship often relies on manual analysis of curated canonical texts, limiting the scale at which patterns of cultural exchange can be identified. The project will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process and analyze a corpus of digitized manuscripts and early printed materials (1200–1700 CE) across six Western European languages, comprising approximately 15 million pages of text from 30 archival collections. Computational methods will include multilingual topic modeling to trace thematic evolution, named entity recognition for mapping geographic and institutional networks, and semantic similarity analysis to detect intertextual influences. Custom transformer-based models will be trained to account for orthographic variations in historical languages, while graph algorithms will reconstruct dissemination pathways of narratives across regions. The scale of data and complexity of multilingual, temporally layered analysis necessitate parallelized processing and GPU-accelerated model training, which are only feasible through HPC infrastructure. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of previously unrecognized nodal points in cultural transmission, particularly in peripheral regions such as Occitania and Frisia; 2) quantitative evidence challenging center-periphery models of cultural exchange; and 3) an open-access digital atlas visualizing narrative networks. This work will provide scholars with new methodological frameworks for interrogating cultural hybridity in Western Europe while preserving computational reproducibility. By centering non-elite textual production, the project aims to reshape discussions about cultural agency in premodern Europe and inform contemporary debates about regional identity formation.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of historical Western Europe, defined as including Britain, Ireland, France, the Low Countries, the Iberian Peninsula, Italy, the Western Mediterranean, and related island groups and borderlands.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance precision and efficacy in electrolysis-based hair removal, a specialized domain within electrology that intersects applied biophysics, dermatological health, and clinical cosmetology. Despite its established clinical use, electrolysis treatment protocols remain largely empirical, with limited quantitative frameworks to predict optimal current parameters (direct current, alternating current, or blended modalities) for diverse skin types, hair morphologies, or anatomical regions. This gap results in variable clinical outcomes, including suboptimal hair removal efficacy, prolonged treatment durations, and elevated risks of tissue trauma. The research problem centers on developing a computational model to simulate electrochemical and thermolytic interactions between probe currents and heterogeneous biological tissues, enabling data-driven optimization of treatment parameters. The proposed approach integrates finite element analysis (FEA) for multi-physics modeling of electric field distributions, joule heating dynamics, and follicular disruption mechanisms across layered skin substrates. High-resolution 3D meshes, informed by clinical imaging and histopathological data, will simulate diverse physiological scenarios (e.g., variations in skin conductivity, follicle density, and hydration levels). Parallelized computational workflows will iteratively evaluate thousands of parameter combinations (current intensity, frequency, pulse duration) to identify protocols that maximize follicle destruction while minimizing collateral thermal damage. Machine learning techniques will further refine predictive correlations between input parameters and clinical outcomes. Expected outcomes include a validated simulation toolkit for personalized treatment planning, reducing trial-and-error in clinical practice. By bridging computational biophysics and clinical electrology, this project aims to establish a foundational framework for evidence-based practice in a field traditionally reliant on heuristic expertise. The computational outputs will be disseminated via open-source platforms to support practitioner training and regulatory guideline development, enhancing both safety standards and client outcomes in electrolysis care.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to permanently remove hair from the human scalp, face, and body using specialized charged solid needle probes, and to function as licensed electrologists and electrolysis technicians.  Includes instruction in direct current electrolysis, alternating current/high frequency thermolysis, blend/dual modality treatments, equipment theory and operation, safety and sanitation, client evaluation and care, laws and regulations, and business practices.

abstract: The proposed research aims to address the challenge of optimizing drug delivery systems for poorly soluble therapeutics, a critical barrier in pharmaceutical development. Many promising drug candidates exhibit low bioavailability due to solubility limitations, necessitating advanced formulation strategies.
