The expected outcomes include a suite of open-source tools for real-time security decision support, validated through partnerships with private security firms. These tools aim to reduce operational costs by 15–20% while improving incident response times and client satisfaction metrics. By bridging gaps between operations research, data science, and security management, this project addresses a critical niche in modern security services administration, offering scalable solutions for an industry increasingly reliant on predictive analytics and adaptive resource planning. The work underscores the transformative potential of computational methods in non-traditional STEM domains, advancing both academic knowledge and practical applications in security services innovation.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, manage, and supervise services providing private security protection for people and property and related investigative and consulting functions. Includes instruction in security and loss prevention services, private security and investigation techniques, security technologies, personnel management, business operations, marketing, applicable law and regulations, and client relations.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of optimizing instrumental performance pedagogy through computational analysis of biomechanical and acoustic data. While traditional music training emphasizes subjective feedback, emerging computational methods offer opportunities to quantitatively assess performance techniques, yet such approaches remain underexplored in wind and string instrument pedagogy. The research will employ high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multimodal datasets—including motion capture, electromyography (EMG), and high-fidelity audio recordings—captured during live performances by advanced student musicians. Computational workflows will integrate kinematic modeling of embouchure (for wind instruments) and bow-arm dynamics (for strings) with spectral analysis of timbral output, correlating physiological patterns with acoustic outcomes. Machine learning models trained on these datasets will identify biomechanical inefficiencies linked to suboptimal sound production or injury risks, enabling the development of adaptive feedback tools for performers. A parallel strand will simulate large-scale ensemble coordination dynamics by modeling real-time acoustic interactions between instrumentalists in virtual performance spaces, requiring distributed-memory parallelization to resolve latency-sensitive auditory feedback loops. Expected outcomes include open-source frameworks for performance analysis, evidence-based pedagogical guidelines to reduce repetitive strain injuries, and novel metrics for ensemble synchronization. By bridging computational rigor with artistic practice, this work aims to advance data-driven methodologies in music performance research while demonstrating the transformative role of HPC in domains beyond traditional STEM fields. Resource requests focus on GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning tasks and high-memory systems for handling terabyte-scale multimodal datasets.
cip_definition: A program that generally prepares individuals to master musical instruments and performing art as solo and/or ensemble performers. Includes instruction on one or more specific instruments from various instrumental groupings.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing demand for high-fidelity modeling of next-generation electrical and electronic systems operating in high-frequency regimes, such as advanced IoT sensor networks and reconfigurable smart grid components. A critical challenge lies in accurately simulating electromagnetic interference, thermal dissipation, and signal integrity in densely integrated circuits and hybrid analog-digital systems, where traditional lumped-element models fail to capture nonlinear interactions at scale. To overcome these limitations, we propose a computational framework leveraging multi-physics finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations coupled with finite element analysis (FEA) for multiphase material systems. The research will employ parallelized solvers to model 3D electromagnetic wave propagation, Joule heating effects, and transient responses in heterogeneous substrates under realistic operational conditions. Key innovations include adaptive mesh refinement for multi-scale geometries and machine learning-accelerated parameter optimization to reduce computational costs. The requested high-performance computing resources will enable large-scale parametric studies of novel metamaterial-based shielding configurations and gallium nitride (GaN) power electronics designs across terahertz to megahertz frequency bands. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for minimizing cross-talk in ultra-compact RF modules, thermal management strategies for high-power density converters, and open-source simulation workflows tailored for industry-relevant electronic systems. By bridging the gap between device-level physics and system-level performance constraints, this work will directly support the development of energy-efficient communication infrastructure and resilient power electronics—critical needs in renewable energy integration and 5G/6G deployment. The computational methodologies developed will also provide a template for resource-efficient co-design of emerging electronic technologies beyond conventional Moore’s Law scaling paradigms.
cip_definition: Any instructional program in electrical and electronic engineering-related technologies, not elsewhere classified

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying light-driven structural dynamics in photoreceptor proteins, with a focus on plant photomorphogenesis and microbial rhodopsins. A critical gap in photobiology lies in understanding how ultrafast photochemical events, such as photon absorption and energy transfer, translate into large-scale conformational changes that regulate biological function. Traditional experimental methods struggle to resolve these processes at atomistic spatiotemporal scales, necessitating advanced computational approaches. We propose multiscale molecular dynamics (MD) simulations combined with quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) frameworks to model light-induced isomerization, proton transfer, and signal propagation in phytochromes and bacteriorhodopsin. These systems require simulations spanning microsecond timescales with explicit solvent models, exceeding the capacity of local computing infrastructure. The HPC allocation will enable GPU-accelerated simulations using Amber and GROMACS, coupled with time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) to model excited-state dynamics. Parallel tempering methods will be employed to sample rare conformational transitions, while Markov state models will identify kinetic pathways linking photoactivation to functional outcomes. Expected outcomes include resolving residue-level determinants of signal transduction efficiency, predicting mutation effects on photocycle kinetics, and elucidating environmental factors (e.g., pH, redox state) that modulate light sensitivity. This work will directly inform efforts to engineer optogenetic tools with tailored spectral responses and improve photosynthetic efficiency in synthetic biology applications. By bridging femtosecond photophysics to millisecond biological responses, the project advances fundamental knowledge of photobiological signaling while providing a computational framework for optimizing light-driven bioenergy and photomedicine technologies.
detailed_field: Biochemistry, biophysics, and molecular biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the effects of light energy on living organisms, the manufacture and processing of luminescence by organisms, and the uses of light in biological research. Includes instruction in bioluminescence, chronobiology, photomedicine, environmental photobiology, organic photochemistry, photomorphogenesis, photoreceptors and photosensitization, molecular mechanics of photosynthesis, phototechnology, vision, ultraviolet radiation, radiation physics, and spectral research methods.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to address operational inefficiencies in small-to-medium brewery and brewpub supply chains, focusing on dynamic inventory optimization under variable demand and sustainability constraints. The craft brewing industry faces unique challenges due to fluctuating raw material availability (e.g., region-specific hops, seasonal adjuncts), complex regulatory environments, and consumer preference volatility, compounded by the need to maintain product consistency while reducing waste. Traditional inventory management systems often fail to account for these multidimensional variables, particularly at smaller scales where margins are tight and computational resources for predictive modeling are limited. This study proposes developing a machine learning framework integrated with discrete-event simulation to model real-time decision-making scenarios, incorporating geospatial agricultural data, weather patterns, supplier reliability metrics, and social media sentiment analysis for demand forecasting. The computational approach will employ parallelized Monte Carlo methods to simulate thousands of supply chain configurations, optimizing for cost, carbon footprint, and product freshness simultaneously. Key innovations include the development of a novel freshness decay model specific to unpasteurized craft beers and a multi-objective optimization algorithm balancing ethical sourcing commitments with financial viability. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for brewers to simulate operational scenarios, predictive insights for grain contracting strategies under climate uncertainty, and a quantitative framework for evaluating the trade-offs between localized sourcing and distribution network efficiency. By bridging brewing science, operations research, and environmental sustainability, this project aims to create computational tools that enhance both economic resilience and ecological stewardship in craft beverage manufacturing. The HPC resources will enable processing of large-scale IoT datasets from fermentation monitoring systems and high-resolution climate models, which are computationally prohibitive on standard enterprise hardware.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, manage, and market breweries and brewpubs. Includes instruction in brewing science, food services management, logistics and distribution, business networking, personnel management, business planning and capitalization, brewing industry operations, marketing, alcohol and liquor law and regulations, finance, and ethics.

abstract: This project seeks to address the growing challenge of optimizing resource allocation in heterogeneous computing architectures, which integrate diverse components such as CPUs, GPUs, and FPGAs to meet escalating computational demands in real-world applications. As systems grow more complex, traditional static allocation strategies struggle to balance performance, energy efficiency, and hardware utilization, particularly in dynamic workloads common to cloud computing, edge environments, and AI-driven applications. To overcome these limitations, this research proposes the development of adaptive resource management frameworks that leverage machine learning (ML) and real-time system telemetry. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are critical to train ML models on large-scale, multi-node simulations of heterogeneous systems under varying workloads, while also enabling the evaluation of dynamic allocation algorithms across diverse hardware configurations. The computational approach includes creating modular simulation environments using containerized workloads, profiling tools for hardware-software interaction analysis, and reinforcement learning models to predict optimal resource distribution. Expected outcomes include novel allocation strategies that reduce latency by 15–20% in mixed CPU-GPU workflows, improve energy efficiency by 10–15% through predictive power management, and provide generalized guidelines for architecture-aware resource partitioning. The resulting frameworks will be validated against industry-standard benchmarks and open-source compute orchestration tools, with findings disseminated as reusable optimization modules for system administrators and developers. By advancing adaptive resource management techniques, this work aims to lower barriers to efficient heterogeneous system deployment in sectors reliant on scalable computing infrastructure, including autonomous systems, distributed AI training, and real-time data processing pipelines. The requested HPC resources will directly support large-scale parallelism in simulations, iterative model training, and comparative analysis across thousands of hardware-software permutations.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of professionals who use computer systems. Includes instruction in basic computer design and architecture, programming, problems of specific computer applications, component and system maintenance and inspection procedures, hardware and software problem diagnosis and repair, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the dynamics of cross-platform misinformation dissemination in digital media ecosystems, with a focus on understanding how false narratives emerge, evolve, and gain traction across social networks, news outlets, and participatory media. The research addresses a critical gap in communication and journalism studies: the lack of scalable computational tools to analyze hyperconnected, multimodal content (text, video, memes) in near-real time, particularly during crisis events where misinformation spreads rapidly. Current methods struggle to process the volume, velocity, and linguistic diversity of global digital discourse, limiting researchers’ ability to map influence networks or identify early amplification patterns. To overcome these barriers, we propose deploying transformer-based natural language processing models fine-tuned for multilingual irony and context-aware claim detection, coupled with temporal graph neural networks to model narrative propagation across 10+ platforms (Twitter/X, Telegram, TikTok, etc.). The computational workflow requires processing 500+ TB of timestamped posts, images, and metadata, necessitating high-performance computing resources for distributed training of deep learning architectures, large-scale graph traversals, and ensemble clustering of visual-textual motifs. Expected outcomes include (1) a novel framework for tracing misinformation mutation rates across media formats, (2) identification of understudied “bridge” communities that facilitate cross-platform viral spread, and (3) open-source tools for journalists to visualize risk hotspots in emerging narratives. By leveraging GPU-accelerated pipelines for multimodal fusion and temporal network analysis, this work will advance computational communication research methodologies while providing actionable insights for media professionals combating information disorders. The requested allocation of 200,000 node-hours on a cluster with >= 4 NVIDIA A100 GPUs and high-memory nodes will enable processing at scales previously inaccessible to non-STEM communication researchers.
cip_title: Communication, Journalism, and Related Programs, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in communication, journalism, and related fields, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Environmental toxicants contribute significantly to human disease, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying genetic susceptibility to these agents remain poorly understood. This project seeks to characterize gene-environment interactions that dictate differential toxicological responses to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), a class of pollutants linked to organ damage and epigenetic dysregulation. Current limitations in predicting individual susceptibility arise from the complexity of PAH metabolism, which involves cytochrome P450-mediated bioactivation, DNA adduct formation, and variable repair capacities influenced by genetic polymorphisms. To address this, we propose a multi-scale computational framework integrating physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling with machine learning-driven analyses of population-level genomic data. High-performance computing (HPC) resources will enable 1) large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of PAH interactions with polymorphic P450 isoforms (CYP1A1, CYP1B1), 2) probabilistic modeling of adduct accumulation across simulated tissue compartments, and 3) genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of epigenetic aging markers in existing toxicogenomics datasets. The computational workflow will leverage GPU-accelerated docking simulations (AMBER, GROMACS) and distributed deep learning architectures (TensorFlow, PyTorch) to identify critical susceptibility loci and metabolic bottlenecks. Expected outcomes include predictive models of individual PAH toxicity thresholds and mechanistic insights into genetic variants that modulate detoxification pathways. This work will directly inform targeted prevention strategies for high-risk populations and advance precision toxicology frameworks for environmental risk assessment. The requested HPC allocation is essential for managing the project's terabyte-scale simulation outputs and computationally intensive genome-phenome association analyses, which exceed the capacity of local institutional clusters.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the genetic determinants of susceptibility to external pollutants and poisons; the interaction of toxic agents with biological systems at the molecular and cellular levels; and the development of countermeasures and treatments. Includes instruction in pharmacogenetics, biomolecular structure, gene expression and regulation, transgenic modeling, toxic events signaling, transcriptional activation, mutagenesis and carcinogenesis, pulmonary toxicology, xenobiotic metabolism, oxidative stress, risk assessment, molecular dosimetry, and studies of specific toxins and treatment therapies.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to model the complex interplay between dietary patterns, gut microbiome dynamics, and personalized health outcomes, with the goal of advancing precision nutrition frameworks. Current approaches to dietary recommendations often rely on population-level data, which fail to account for individual variability in metabolic responses, microbiome composition, and genetic predispositions. To address this gap, we propose a computational pipeline integrating multi-omics data (metagenomic, metabolomic, and transcriptomic profiles) with longitudinal dietary intake records and health metrics. The project will employ machine learning algorithms to identify nonlinear relationships between specific food components, microbial metabolic pathways, and biomarkers of wellness (e.g., inflammation, glycemic control). Agent-based modeling will simulate how individualized microbiome communities respond to dietary perturbations over time, while high-dimensional optimization techniques will explore tailored dietary interventions. The scale of data integration—encompassing terabyte-level genomic datasets, heterogeneous health records, and dynamic food composition databases—necessitates HPC capabilities for parallelized processing, large-memory node utilization, and GPU-accelerated deep learning workflows. Expected outcomes include the development of predictive models that map personalized food-microbiome-health triads, enabling nutritionists to design targeted dietary strategies that account for an individual’s unique biological context. This work will contribute novel computational tools to the emerging field of precision nutrition, with potential applications in mitigating diet-related chronic diseases and optimizing wellness across diverse populations. By bridging gaps between computational systems biology and applied nutrition science, the project aligns with the program’s focus on advancing food-related health interventions while operating in a specialized niche that transcends traditional disciplinary boundaries.
cip_title: Foods, Nutrition, and Wellness Studies, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the role of foods and nutrition in human health and wellness. Includes instruction in nutritional care and education, the planning and provision of food services, the development of consumable food products, life-span nutrition and wellness, the principles of nutritional assessment, and food safety and food composition.

abstract: This project seeks to advance our understanding of quantum chromodynamics (QCD) in non-perturbative regimes by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to simulate quark-gluon interactions in extreme conditions, such as those present in the early universe or high-energy heavy-ion collisions. Despite progress in lattice QCD, simulating systems with dynamical fermions at near-physical quark masses and high baryon densities remains computationally prohibitive due to the sign problem and the need for fine lattice spacings. This limits predictions for phase transitions, hadron structure, and transport coefficients critical to interpreting experimental results from collider facilities. To address this, we propose large-scale lattice QCD simulations using improved staggered fermion discretizations and hybrid Monte Carlo algorithms optimized for GPU-accelerated architectures. The simulations will employ multi-grid solvers and hierarchical integration schemes to reduce critical slowing-down, enabling access to larger spatial volumes and smaller pion masses. A key focus is the development of machine learning-driven analysis pipelines to extract spectral functions and equation-of-state parameters from correlator data, mitigating systematic uncertainties in continuum extrapolations. Additionally, we will explore finite-density systems via reweighting techniques and complex Langevin dynamics, benchmarking against perturbative results where applicable. Successful execution will yield high-precision determinations of quarkonium dissociation temperatures, strangeness content in neutron stars, and shear viscosity-to-entropy ratios, directly impacting the interpretation of heavy-ion collision data and astrophysical observations. The generated datasets will be shared via a public repository to support collaborative theory-experiment comparisons. By utilizing 500,000 node-hours on a Tier-2 HPC cluster, this project will provide foundational insights into QCD thermodynamics while advancing computational methods for the particle physics community. The outcomes will inform future experimental campaigns at the Electron-Ion Collider and Facility for Antiproton and Ion Research, bridging gaps between ab initio calculations and observable phenomena.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the basic constituents of sub-atomic matter and energy, and the forces governing fundamental processes. Includes instruction in quantum theory, field theory, single-particle systems, perturbation and scattering theory, matter-radiation interaction, symmetry, quarks, capture, Schroedinger mechanics, methods for detecting particle emission and absorption, and research equipment operation and maintenance.

abstract: Counseling psychology faces growing demands to optimize therapeutic interventions through data-driven insights, yet computational approaches remain underutilized in analyzing complex client-counselor dynamics. This project seeks to address this gap by developing machine learning (ML) models to identify patterns in therapeutic interactions that predict intervention success, using anonymized session transcripts and longitudinal outcome data from diverse counseling populations. The research will focus on two objectives: (1) creating natural language processing (NLP) pipelines to quantify linguistic markers of therapeutic alliance and client progress across modalities (individual, group, and family therapy), and (2) training multimodal neural networks to integrate language data with standardized assessment metrics (e.g., symptom inventories, session feedback) for outcome prediction. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential due to the computational intensity of transformer-based NLP models and the need to process over 50,000 hours of session data while maintaining strict privacy-preserving protocols through federated learning architectures. The proposed workflow includes distributed training of bidirectional encoder representations across multiple client subgroups, coupled with explainable AI techniques to interpret model decisions for clinical relevance. Anticipated outcomes include a validated framework for identifying micro-interventions associated with positive outcomes in specific cultural and demographic contexts, as well as open-source tools for real-time session analysis to support counselor training. This work aligns with counseling psychology’s emphasis on evidence-based practice while addressing scalability challenges in personalized intervention design. By leveraging HPC capabilities to handle high-dimensional, nested datasets characteristic of therapeutic processes, the project aims to advance computational methods in applied psychological research without replicating clinical psychology’s diagnostic-focused paradigms. Results will be disseminated through counseling-focused journals and integrated into graduate training modules on data-informed practice.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for the independent professional practice of psychological counseling, involving the rendering of therapeutic services to individuals and groups experiencing psychological problems and exhibiting distress symptoms. Includes instruction in counseling theory, therapeutic intervention strategies, patient/counselor relationships, testing and assessment methods and procedures, group therapy, marital and family therapy, child and adolescent therapy, supervised counseling practice, ethical standards, and applicable regulations.

abstract: The increasing complexity of modern communication systems and electronic devices necessitates advanced computational tools to address challenges in design optimization, electromagnetic interference mitigation, and signal integrity analysis. This project seeks high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and validate multi-physics simulation frameworks for next-generation wireless communication systems and high-frequency electronic circuits. The research focuses on two interconnected objectives: (1) modeling wave propagation and scattering in dense urban environments for 5G/6G millimeter-wave networks, and (2) analyzing crosstalk effects in high-speed printed circuit boards (PCBs) with sub-6 GHz and millimeter-wave coexistence. Leveraging finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) methods and machine learning-assisted optimization algorithms, the simulations will account for multi-scale electromagnetic phenomena, material nonlinearities, and thermal effects across three-dimensional geometries. The computational workflow will integrate GPU-accelerated Maxwell solvers with neural network surrogates to reduce simulation costs while maintaining physical fidelity. Expected outcomes include optimized antenna array configurations for base stations, interference mitigation strategies for IoT device clusters, and predictive models for signal degradation in multi-layer PCBs. By enabling large-scale parametric studies across 100+ design variables, the HPC resources will directly support the development of energy-efficient communication hardware prototypes and contribute to standardization efforts for spectrum sharing in smart city applications. The resulting open-source simulation tools and datasets will provide the research community with validated benchmarks for emerging challenges in electromagnetic compatibility and heterogeneous network design. This work aligns with national priorities in advanced communication infrastructure while addressing critical gaps in practical engineering methodologies for industry applications.
cip_title: Electrical, Electronic, and Communications Engineering Technology
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply basic engineering principles and technical skills in support of electrical, electronics and communication engineers. Includes instruction in electrical circuitry, prototype development and testing, systems analysis and testing, systems maintenance, instrument calibration, and report preparation.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolutionary and neurophysiological underpinnings of cross-species social learning strategies using computational modeling and large-scale behavioral data analysis. Social learning—critical for survival in many species—varies in complexity across taxa, but the mechanisms driving these differences remain poorly resolved. Traditional experimental methods face limitations in scaling species comparisons, integrating neural data with behavioral outcomes, and simulating evolutionary trajectories under dynamic ecological pressures. To address this, we propose a multi-phase computational approach leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources. First, agent-based models will simulate social learning dynamics across virtual populations of primates, corvids, and cetaceans, incorporating neurophysiological constraints (e.g., memory capacity, neural connectivity) derived from empirical datasets. Second, machine learning pipelines will analyze over 50TB of existing species-specific behavioral video archives and electrophysiology recordings to identify conserved and divergent neural-behavioral correlates. Third, phylogenetic comparative models will integrate these results with evolutionary trees to test hypotheses about the emergence of complex social learning strategies. HPC resources are essential for optimizing deep reinforcement learning architectures, running parallelized evolutionary simulations across parameter spaces, and processing high-dimensional neural data. Expected outcomes include a predictive framework linking neuroanatomical adaptations to social learning diversity, validated against empirical data from collaborating primate cognition labs. This work will advance comparative psychology by bridging micro-scale neural mechanisms and macro-scale evolutionary patterns, with broader implications for understanding cognitive evolution and designing biologically inspired AI systems. The requested computing allocation will enable iterative model refinement and large-scale synthetic experiments impractical on local clusters.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the behavior of members of particular species or groups and the relationship of the behaviors of the species or group to their evolutionary origins. Includes instruction in differential psychology, experimental and physiological psychology, psychopharmacology, psychology of individual differences, reinforcement theory, and neurophysiology.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance interdisciplinary research in collaborative theatre and dance performance design, with a focus on optimizing real-time, data-driven decision-making in live productions. A central challenge in integrating dance and theatre lies in synchronizing dynamic artistic elements—such as movement, lighting, sound, and spatial design—into cohesive performances, particularly when accounting for variable audience perspectives and environmental constraints. Traditional rehearsal and design workflows often rely on iterative, manual adjustments, which are time-intensive and limited in scalability. To address this, we propose developing a computational framework that simulates and analyzes multi-modal performance data, including motion-captured choreography, acoustic profiles, and stage lighting interactions. Using agent-based modeling and physics-based rendering, the framework will simulate audience sightlines, dancer-actor trajectories, and equipment load dynamics across diverse venue configurations. Machine learning models will be trained on historical performance datasets to predict aesthetic outcomes (e.g., emotional impact of lighting transitions) and logistical risks (e.g., spatial collisions). HPC resources are critical for processing high-resolution motion data (60+ dancers/actors), rendering complex 3D environments in real time, and iterating design permutations at scale. Expected outcomes include a suite of open-source tools for predictive performance planning, reducing technical rehearsal time by 30–50% in pilot case studies, and generating novel metrics for evaluating spatial-auditory cohesion in hybrid theatre-dance works. This work will establish a foundation for computationally enhanced creative practices in the performing arts, enabling artists to test experimental concepts virtually while preserving the embodied integrity of live performance. By bridging computational modeling with artistic intuition, the project aims to redefine collaborative workflows in theatre and dance education and professional production.
detailed_field: Dance, drama, theatre arts, and stagecraft
cip_definition: A program of study that focuses on integrating the studies of dance and theatre arts to provide perspectives in all facets of production, performance, and critical engagement. Includes instruction in acting, aesthetics, choreography, costume design, criticism, dance, improvisation, music analysis, playwriting, theatre performance history, scene design, stage lighting, and technical theatre.

abstract: The increasing complexity of genomic data in clinical diagnostics presents a critical challenge in the accurate interpretation of genetic variants underlying human diseases. While next-generation sequencing and high-resolution cytogenetic techniques generate vast multimodal datasets—including structural variants, copy number variations, and single-nucleotide variants—existing analytical frameworks often analyze these data types in isolation, limiting diagnostic yield. This project seeks to address this gap by developing an integrated computational platform that unifies clinical cytogenetic and molecular genetic analyses through advanced machine learning and network-based algorithms. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to process multi-terabyte genomic datasets from patients with undiagnosed developmental disorders, congenital anomalies, and hereditary cancers. Key computational tasks include graph-based representation of chromosomal rearrangements, probabilistic modeling of variant pathogenicity across heterogeneous data sources, and deep learning-driven prioritization of candidate genes within spatially resolved 3D genomic interaction networks. By simulating population-scale linkage disequilibrium patterns and epigenetic constraints, the framework will improve the identification of clinically actionable variants while reducing false-positive interpretations. The proposed work will also establish automated pipelines for reconciling discordant results between cytogenetic and molecular assays, a persistent challenge in clinical reporting. Successful implementation is expected to enhance diagnostic accuracy by 15-20% in complex cases and reveal novel genotype-phenotype correlations through large-scale integration of publicly available biomedical databases. This project directly aligns with the Laboratory Genetics and Genomics mission by advancing computational methods essential for translating multidimensional genomic data into clinically interpretable insights. The requested HPC resources are indispensable for managing memory-intensive genome graphs, training neural networks on whole-genome alignment data, and performing real-time comparative analyses across thousands of clinical samples. Outcomes will be disseminated through open-source tools and validation studies in collaboration with CAP/CLIA-certified diagnostic laboratories.
cip_definition: Research on how to direct and interpret both clinical cytogenetic and molecular genetic analyses relevant to the diagnosis and management of human genetic diseases.

abstract: The practice of wilderness medicine requires adapting clinical decision-making to austere environments where environmental stressors—such as hypothermia, altitude illness, or traumatic injury in remote settings—intersect with severe resource constraints. Current clinical guidelines often lack robust, dynamic models to predict patient outcomes under variable environmental and logistical conditions, limiting the ability to optimize care when resources are scarce. This project seeks to address this gap by developing high-fidelity computational models to simulate patient physiology, environmental interactions, and resource utilization strategies in wilderness contexts. Using high-performance computing (HPC), we will create multi-scale simulations integrating real-world environmental data (e.g., temperature, altitude, humidity), physiologic parameters, and equipment/resource availability. Machine learning approaches will train predictive models on heterogeneous datasets, including retrospective field case reports, controlled hypobaric/hyperthermic chamber experiments, and sensor data from portable monitoring devices. Agent-based modeling will evaluate triage protocols under simulated resource shortages, while finite element analysis will assess heat retention or insulation properties of improvised medical equipment. By iteratively validating models against field data from wilderness medicine expeditions, this work aims to generate adaptive, evidence-based algorithms for clinical decision support in resource-limited settings. The outcomes will provide a framework for dynamically adjusting treatment priorities, evacuation timing, and resource allocation based on real-time environmental and physiologic inputs. This research has direct implications for improving patient survival in disaster response, military medicine, and global health contexts, while advancing computational methods for environmental physiology modeling. Access to HPC resources is critical to manage the computational complexity of multi-parametric simulations and enable rapid, scalable analysis of scenarios with high-dimensional variables.
cip_definition: Research on how to practice medicine with limited resources in austere environments or to provide healthcare anywhere in which environmental conditions have physiologic insult to a patient.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenge of developing culturally responsive educational tools for Indigenous students in Tribal/First Nation schools by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model adaptive, personalized learning systems rooted in Native knowledge frameworks. Despite growing recognition of the need for pedagogies aligned with Indigenous ways of knowing, scalable computational tools that integrate cultural contexts, multilingual needs (including heritage languages and English language learners), and diverse learning styles remain underdeveloped. This research will employ machine learning (ML) techniques to analyze qualitative and quantitative datasets—including oral histories, student engagement metrics, and community-defined educational priorities—to design dynamic curriculum modules. Agent-based modeling will simulate classroom interactions under varying conditions (e.g., rural vs. urban Tribal schools, hybrid learning environments) to optimize instructional strategies. HPC resources are critical for training large language models on low-resource Indigenous languages, processing multimodal educational data (text, audio, visual), and iteratively testing culturally grounded pedagogical scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-access computational framework for generating adaptive lesson plans that center Tribal sovereignty in content delivery, tools to support educators in addressing language preservation and revitalization, and evidence-based insights into how culturally contextualized AI-driven systems can improve academic engagement for Native students. By prioritizing collaboration with Tribal education partners, this work aims to advance equitable resource allocation in Indigenous education while avoiding extractive research practices. The project directly supports the preparation of educators in Tribal schools by bridging computational innovation with Indigenous pedagogical traditions.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design and implementation of instructional and advising services for American Indian, Alaska Native, and Hawaiian Native students at various learning levels and that prepares individuals to perform teaching and administrative functions in Tribal/First Nation schools. Includes instruction in the cultural traditions and social patterns, history and politics, learning styles and issues, curriculum design, LEP and minority education strategies, counseling techniques and social issues, rural education services, distance education, adult education techniques, school administration, applicable laws and regulations, and research issues.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a large-scale computational analysis of stylistic and thematic evolution in Anglophone literary texts from the 18th century to the present. While traditional literary scholarship relies on close reading of select works, this study addresses the challenge of systematically tracing patterns across vast, heterogeneous corpora—a task impractical without computational scaling. The research problem centers on identifying and quantifying shifts in narrative voice, metaphor usage, and semantic networks within genres such as the novel, essay, and poetry, using digitized collections from Project Gutenberg, the HathiTrust, and bespoke archives. By applying natural language processing (NLP) techniques—including transformer-based language models for semantic role labeling, graph algorithms for intertextual network mapping, and unsupervised clustering for stylistic categorization—we aim to model how sociohistorical contexts (e.g., industrialization, postcolonialism) correlate with measurable changes in literary form. The computational workflow requires parallel processing of over 500,000 texts (20TB of unstructured data), iterative training of custom classifiers to discern genre-specific rhetorical features, and memory-intensive simulations of semantic diffusion across temporal networks. Expected outcomes include: (1) a publicly accessible interactive visualization platform mapping literary trends against historical metadata; (2) quantitative frameworks for re-evaluating periodization in literary history; and (3) open-source tools to bridge computational methods with qualitative humanities scholarship. This work will provide novel insights into the dynamics of cultural production while establishing scalable methodologies for interdisciplinary textual analysis. The scale of data ingestion, model complexity, and need for real-time interaction with multidimensional datasets necessitates HPC infrastructure, particularly GPU nodes for deep learning tasks and high-memory nodes for graph computations.
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on the English language, including its history, structure and related communications skills; and the literature and culture of English-speaking peoples.

abstract: The increasing complexity of edge computing environments, characterized by heterogeneous hardware, fluctuating resource availability, and stringent latency requirements, presents a critical challenge for adaptive runtime systems. Traditional static resource allocation strategies fail to dynamically optimize performance under these conditions, leading to suboptimal utilization and energy inefficiency. This project proposes the development of a machine learning-driven runtime framework that autonomously adjusts computational resource allocation, task scheduling, and power management in real time for edge devices operating in dynamic, resource-constrained settings. The research will leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate large-scale edge networks with varying topologies, workloads, and hardware configurations. Computational methods will include the design of lightweight reinforcement learning models trained on synthetic and real-world IoT workload traces, coupled with discrete-event simulations to evaluate system behavior under stochastic network conditions. Key innovations include a hybrid architecture that balances centralized coordination with decentralized decision-making and a novel metric for quantifying the trade-offs between latency, energy consumption, and hardware wear. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework demonstrating ≥20% improvement in energy efficiency and ≤15% reduction in task completion time variance compared to state-of-the-art schedulers across simulated manufacturing and smart city use cases. The HPC component is essential for validating scalability across 10,000+ node configurations and stress-testing fault tolerance mechanisms under simulated hardware failures. This work bridges gaps between embedded systems programming, distributed systems theory, and machine learning operations (MLOps), offering a programmable foundation for next-generation edge computing infrastructures while advancing methodologies for self-optimizing systems in transient computational environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the general writing and implementation of generic and customized programs to drive operating systems and that generally prepares individuals to apply the methods and procedures of software design and programming to software installation and maintenance. Includes instruction in software design, low- and high-level languages and program writing; program customization and linking; prototype testing; troubleshooting; and related aspects of operating systems and networks.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize dynamic resource allocation for next-generation military space systems, focusing on enhancing the resilience and operational efficiency of satellite constellations in contested environments. As adversarial counter-space capabilities—including electronic warfare, cyberattacks, and directed-energy threats—increasingly jeopardize space-based assets, traditional static scheduling models fail to address the real-time, adaptive decision-making required for mission-critical operations. The research problem centers on creating robust algorithms to autonomously reconfigure satellite tasking, communication pathways, and sensor utilization in response to emergent threats while maintaining coverage priorities for intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) missions. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, the project will implement a hybrid simulation architecture combining agent-based modeling of multi-domain threat scenarios with reinforcement learning (RL) systems trained to optimize resource trade-offs under uncertainty. Computational workflows will integrate orbital mechanics simulations, probabilistic threat impact assessments, and latency-sensitive decision trees to stress-test allocation strategies across millions of synthetic conflict scenarios. Expected outcomes include a validated machine learning model capable of reducing single-point failure risks by 40% in simulated engagements and a decision-support toolkit to inform future satellite constellation designs. By addressing the intersection of autonomous systems, operational art, and asymmetric warfare in the space domain, this work fills a critical gap in military-focused computational research, advancing capabilities distinct from conventional aerospace engineering or pure systems science. The HPC infrastructure is essential to achieve the required scale for modeling heterogeneous space architectures and emergent threat behaviors at fidelity levels impractical for traditional computing environments.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design, development, and operation of missiles, satellites and other space-based systems for military purposes. Includes instruction in the military applications of space, space technology, aerospace engineering, systems architecture, orbital mechanics, launch and retrieval systems, ground support systems, satellite communications, and space-based sensor systems.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolving legal and regulatory frameworks governing cyber insurance in an era of escalating digital risks. The rapid proliferation of cyber threats, coupled with inconsistent international regulatory standards and complex liability structures, has created systemic uncertainties in insurance markets. Traditional legal analysis methods struggle to model the cascading effects of multi-jurisdictional litigation, dynamic policy exclusions, and probabilistic risk scenarios at scale. The project will employ agent-based modeling (ABM) to simulate interactions between insurers, policyholders, regulators, and adversarial actors across heterogeneous legal environments. Computational legal analytics techniques, including natural language processing (NLP) of insurance contracts, case law, and regulatory texts, will inform parameterization of risk scenarios. Monte Carlo simulations will assess the financial stability implications of emerging liability doctrines under varying threat landscapes. By integrating actuarial data with statutory and case law databases, the models will quantify how judicial interpretations of policy language (e.g., "war exclusion" clauses in state-sponsored cyberattacks) propagate through global insurance networks. Expected outcomes include a computational framework for stress-testing regulatory proposals, identifying critical vulnerabilities in coverage standardization efforts, and predicting litigation hotspots arising from artificial intelligence-related liabilities. The HPC infrastructure is essential for processing terabyte-scale legal corpora, running parallelized scenario analyses across 50+ jurisdictional models, and maintaining probabilistic graphs of liability pathways. Results will advance methodological integration of computational social science with insurance jurisprudence while providing policymakers and industry stakeholders with evidence-based tools to address systemic risks in digital insurance markets.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of the law, policies, and regulations affecting insurance.

abstract: This project seeks to investigate the evolution of cultural narratives and identity formation across Scandinavia through computational analysis of digitized textual and visual media spanning the 19th to 21st centuries. The research addresses a critical gap in Scandinavian Studies: the lack of systematic, large-scale methods to trace how regional myths, gender norms, and transnational cultural exchanges have been constructed and contested in public discourse. The primary challenge lies in processing and interpreting multilingual sources—including literature, periodicals, political pamphlets, and folk art archives—across Denmark, Sweden, Norway, Iceland, and Sápmi (the Sámi cultural region), which require advanced computational resources due to their volume (estimated 50 TB) and linguistic complexity. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC), the team will employ natural language processing (NLP) models optimized for historical Scandinavian languages and dialects, alongside computer vision techniques to analyze visual motifs in digitized art and ephemera. Key computational tasks include cross-regional sentiment analysis, semantic network mapping of recurring narrative themes, and temporal modeling of cultural diffusion patterns. The HPC infrastructure is essential for training transformer-based models on low-resource languages like Old Norse and contemporary Sámi, as well as for parallel processing of high-resolution image datasets. Expected outcomes include an open-access database of annotated cultural artifacts, visualizations of narrative shifts tied to historical events (e.g., Nordic welfare state development, Greenlandic independence movements), and frameworks for quantifying intersectional identity representations in marginalized groups. This work will provide the first pan-Scandinavian computational study of cultural memory, offering scholars quantitative tools to complement qualitative traditions in area studies while preserving endangered linguistic heritage. The resource request supports GPU-intensive workloads for model training and sustained memory allocation for large-scale corpus analytics.
major_field: Area, ethnic, cultural, gender, and group studies
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the history, society, politics, culture, and economics of one or more of the peoples of Scandinavia, defined as Northern Europe including Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden, and related island groups (e.g., Greenland) and borderlands.

abstract: This project seeks to address the challenges of analyzing large-scale, multilingual, and culturally nuanced communication data in international contexts, with a focus on improving predictive models for intercultural miscommunication risks in digital platforms. As global interactions increasingly occur online, understanding how cultural dimensions—such as power distance, individualism, and communication styles—manifest in text, audio, and visual media requires advanced computational methods. Existing tools for sentiment analysis, topic modeling, and cross-cultural discourse analysis often fail to account for contextual subtleties or the dynamic interplay of cultural identities in real-time interactions. To bridge this gap, we propose developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework that integrates natural language processing (NLP), network analysis, and machine learning models trained on diverse intercultural datasets. These datasets include multinational social media exchanges, diplomatic correspondence archives, and global crisis communication case studies. The computational workload involves parallel processing of terabyte-scale unstructured data, multilingual embeddings aligned with cultural variables, and agent-based simulations of communication breakdown scenarios. By leveraging GPU-accelerated clustering and transformer-based models fine-tuned for low-resource languages, this approach aims to identify patterns in how cultural assumptions influence interpretation biases. Expected outcomes include (1) an open-access toolkit for predicting miscommunication risks in intercultural negotiations, (2) evidence-based guidelines for adaptive communication strategies in multinational organizations, and (3) scalable methods to evaluate the cultural alignment of AI-mediated translation systems. The requested HPC resources are critical due to the need for iterative model training across heterogeneous data types and the simulation of complex, multi-actor communication networks. This work directly supports the program’s mission to advance effective global communication by providing empirically grounded, computationally robust insights into intercultural dynamics.
detailed_field: Applied communication, advertising, and public relations
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the specialized knowledge and skills needed for effective communication in the international community and among people of different cultures; and that prepares individuals to function at the national and international levels as journalists, public relations specialists, travel industry representatives, intercultural trainers, and/or foreign service officers. Includes instruction in journalism, communications, intercultural and international relations, marketing and public relations, and global communications policy.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance the computational analysis of dialectal variation and language contact phenomena across Romance languages, with a focus on understudied regional varieties of Spanish, French, and Italian. While Romance linguistics has long prioritized written corpora and qualitative methods, the increasing availability of digitized oral histories, sociolinguistic interviews, and crowdsourced speech data presents an opportunity to model phonetic, syntactic, and lexical variation at unprecedented scales. However, processing these multimodal datasets—which include audio, transcriptions, and metadata—requires intensive computational workflows for speech alignment, feature extraction, and geospatial modeling. Current tools for dialectometry and historical linguistics struggle to handle the volume and heterogeneity of such data, particularly when analyzing cross-linguistic interference in multilingual regions (e.g., Occitan-Provençal varieties in southern France or Sardinian-Italian contact zones). Our team proposes a pipeline integrating forced alignment algorithms optimized for nonstandard phonology, transformer-based models fine-tuned on low-resource Romance varieties, and graph-based networks to trace diachronic changes in morphosyntactic structures. HPC resources will enable parallel processing of over 50,000 hours of speech data from archival and contemporary sources, as well as large-scale simulations of language shift dynamics under varying sociodemographic conditions. Expected outcomes include (1) open-access computational models for identifying and dating contact-induced changes in Romance languages, (2) interactive maps visualizing dialect continua and transitional zones, and (3) a comparative framework to evaluate theories of grammatical borrowing against empirical patterns. By bridging digital humanities methods with computational linguistics, this work will expand the methodological toolkit for analyzing language variation while preserving linguistic diversity in rapidly globalizing speech communities.
cip_title: Romance Languages, Literatures, and Linguistics, General
cip_definition: A general program that focuses on one or more of the Romance languages of Western, Central, and Southern Europe. Includes instruction in philology; linguistics; dialects and pidgins; literature; and applications to business, science/technology, and other settings.

abstract: The increasing prevalence of pediatric endocrine disorders, including growth hormone deficiencies, congenital adrenal hyperplasia, and early-onset type 2 diabetes, underscores the urgent need to advance precision diagnostics and therapeutic strategies. Current approaches to understanding these heterogeneous conditions are limited by fragmented analyses of hormonal, genetic, and metabolic data, which fail to capture the dynamic, systems-level interactions governing endocrine pathophysiology. This project proposes to address this gap by integrating multi-omics datasets—including longitudinal hormone profiles, whole-exome sequencing, and single-cell transcriptomics from pediatric cohorts—with clinical outcomes to model endocrine dysregulation computationally. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will develop scalable machine learning frameworks to identify predictive biomarkers and subtype-specific pathways, while dynamical systems modeling will simulate hormone-regulatory networks under genetic and environmental perturbations. Key computational challenges include processing high-dimensional datasets (≥10^6 features per patient), optimizing parallelized workflows for genome-wide association studies, and deploying GPU-accelerated neural networks to resolve temporal patterns in hormonal time-series data. The project will utilize existing cohorts from the National Pediatric Endocrine Registry (n=4,500 patients) and generate new single-cell data from adrenal and pancreatic tissues (n=200 samples). Expected outcomes include (1) a validated computational pipeline for stratifying patients by disease mechanism, (2) mechanistic insights into puberty-associated metabolic decompensation in monogenic diabetes, and (3) in silico screening of repurposed therapies targeting thyroid axis dysregulation. By enabling large-scale integration of clinical and molecular data, this HPC-driven approach will advance personalized management strategies for endocrine disorders, reduce diagnostic delays, and provide a template for computational endocrinology in pediatric populations. Resource allocation will directly support data storage (≥500 TB), multi-node CPU/GPU computations for model training, and open-source tool development to share models with the clinical research community.
cip_definition: Research focused on the diagnosis and management of endocrine diseases and the regulation of hormone balance in childhood and adolescence.

abstract: This project seeks to develop advanced computational models to enhance the precision and efficiency of non-destructive testing (NDT) and material analysis using industrial radiologic technologies. Current methods for interpreting radiographic data, such as x-ray diffraction analysis and real-time thickness monitoring in manufacturing, face challenges in resolving subtle material defects or dynamic variations due to limitations in processing complex, high-volume datasets. To address this, we propose leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to simulate radiation-matter interactions at unprecedented resolutions and optimize algorithmic workflows for defect detection and measurement accuracy. The computational approach integrates Monte Carlo simulations of radioisotope-based imaging systems with machine learning models trained on synthetic and experimental radiographic datasets. These simulations will account for variable material compositions, geometric complexities, and real-world noise factors, while neural networks will be deployed to automate anomaly detection in x-ray images and refine thickness prediction algorithms. By parallelizing these processes across HPC architectures, we aim to reduce computational bottlenecks in high-fidelity modeling and enable near-real-time analysis of continuous monitoring systems. Expected outcomes include validated predictive models for defect classification in metallic alloys, optimized algorithms for thickness measurement under dynamic industrial conditions, and open-source tools for simulating radiologic inspection scenarios. This work will directly benefit industries reliant on precision NDT, such as aerospace and additive manufacturing, by improving inspection reliability while reducing downtime. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated nodes for deep learning workloads and high-memory nodes for large-scale radiation transport simulations, which are critical to achieving the project’s goals.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply scientific principles and technical skills to the operation of industrial and research testing equipment using radioisotopes. Includes instruction in x-ray analysis of materials, nondestructive testing and inspection of materials, and continuous measurement of paper or metal thickness.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a scalable computational framework to enhance decision-making agility in Joint Command/Control, Communications, and Intelligence (C3/C4I) systems through advanced modeling of multi-domain operational environments. Military command structures face growing challenges in synthesizing real-time data from distributed sensors, legacy platforms, and coalition networks, particularly under contested or degraded communications. Traditional simulation tools struggle to model the dynamic interplay between human decision cycles, emergent AI-driven analytics, and adversarial cyber-physical threats at operationally relevant scales. The research addresses this gap by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to construct a hybrid agent-based and discrete-event simulation environment. This platform will integrate machine learning models trained on historical mission data with synthetically generated scenarios reflecting multi-domain operations (MDO) complexities, including electronic warfare effects, network latency variability, and cognitive workload thresholds for command staff. Key computational challenges involve optimizing parallelized simulations of 10,000+ interacting entities across air, land, maritime, space, and cyber domains while maintaining microsecond-scale temporal resolution for critical C2 message passing. The project will employ containerized workflows to evaluate mitigation strategies for spectrum congestion, AI-assisted decision support system failures, and coalition data fabric interoperability constraints. Expected outcomes include quantifiable metrics for resilience trade-offs in alternative C3 architectures and validated models of human-machine teaming under multi-stress operational conditions. By enabling large-scale virtual stress testing of next-generation command systems, this work aims to inform capability investments and doctrinal adaptations for joint all-domain command and control (JADC2) environments. The computational infrastructure will also serve as a testbed for evaluating quantum-resistant encryption protocols and edge computing paradigms in future C4I modernization roadmaps.
cip_title: Joint Command/ Task Force (C3, C4I) Systems (MILITARY)
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the principles, technology and operational use of command and control (C3, C4I) systems as applied to joint and combined military operations involving unified commands. Includes instruction in information technology, communications systems, network systems and architecture, systems engineering, C3 and C4I doctrine and policy, C3 and C4I systems management, intelligence, operational and strategic planning, interagency operations, operational security and deception.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze the evolution of cross-cultural trade networks in premodern Asia (c. 1200–1800 CE), with a focus on integrating fragmented textual, archaeological, and geospatial datasets. The research problem centers on reconstructing dynamic economic and cultural exchanges across South Asia, Southeast Asia, and East Asia, where surviving records—including merchant logs, port registries, and multilingual epigraphic materials—are dispersed, heterogeneous, and computationally demanding to process at scale. Traditional historiographic methods struggle to systematically correlate these sources or model large-scale patterns of interaction over time. The project will employ natural language processing (NLP) pipelines optimized for classical Chinese, Arabic, and Sanskrit texts to extract named entities, transaction records, and route descriptions. These outputs will feed into spatial network models built using graph databases and agent-based simulations to map shifting trade corridors, quantify commodity flows, and assess the impact of political events on regional connectivity. A parallel workflow will apply computer vision techniques to LiDAR-derived archaeological site data from maritime entrepôts, automating the identification of infrastructure patterns linked to commercial activity. By synthesizing these computational approaches on HPC infrastructure, the project aims to resolve longstanding debates about the role of monsoon seasonality, imperial policies, and transregional institutions in shaping Asia’s economic integration. Expected outcomes include an open-access geotemporal database of trade nodes and routes, scalable tools for multilingual historical text analysis, and quantitative frameworks for evaluating connectivity’s influence on cultural exchange. This work will provide a replicable model for data-driven historical inquiry while advancing scholarly understanding of Asia’s premodern globalization, with implications for contemporary discussions about regional interdependence.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the development of the societies, cultures, and institutions of the Asian Continent from their origins to the present. Includes instruction in the historiography of specific cultures and periods; sources and materials; historical research methods; and applications to the study of specific themes, issues, periods, and institutions.

abstract: The increasing complexity of human-technology interaction demands interfaces that adapt to individual cognitive and perceptual differences, yet current design frameworks lack robust computational models to account for neurodiverse user populations. This project addresses the challenge of simulating dynamic, personalized user interactions by developing a high-fidelity neurocognitive modeling platform. The research integrates multimodal datasets—including eye-tracking, electroencephalography (EEG), and behavioral logs—to train agent-based models that simulate attention, memory, and decision-making processes across diverse cognitive profiles. Leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources, we will deploy large-scale parameter sweeps to explore how neural variability influences interface usability, particularly for users with attention-deficit or sensory-processing differences. Computational workflows will combine dynamical systems theory for simulating neural oscillations, reinforcement learning for adaptive interface behavior, and graph-based analytics to map user-task mismatches. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for predicting interaction bottlenecks and generating evidence-based design guidelines for cognitively inclusive interfaces. By scaling neurocognitive simulations to thousands of parallelized user scenarios, this work aims to advance human-centered design paradigms beyond static accessibility standards, enabling real-time interface personalization rooted in computational neuroscience. The resource request supports GPU-accelerated model training, storage for petabyte-scale interaction datasets, and runtime for ensemble simulations that capture the nonlinear dynamics of human-technology synergy. This interdisciplinary effort bridges gaps between affective computing, neuroergonomics, and interaction design, offering a novel pathway to democratize technology access through biologically grounded computational tools.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on incorporating a human perspective into designing, researching, and creating technological interfaces. Includes instruction in design, human-computer interaction, learning, neuroscience, perception, product design, user-centered design, and usability.

abstract: This project seeks to develop a computational framework to model and optimize the spatial and temporal allocation of law enforcement resources in urban environments, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to address operational inefficiencies in dynamic policing contexts. Traditional resource allocation strategies often rely on static crime hotspot maps or historical incident data, which fail to account for real-time variables such as shifting population densities, transient events, or emergent crime patterns influenced by socio-economic disruptions. The research problem centers on the lack of adaptive, predictive tools that integrate multi-source data streams—including 911 call logs, traffic sensors, social media activity, and environmental sensors—to simulate urban crime dynamics and propose optimized patrol deployment strategies. Using agent-based modeling (ABM) and graph neural networks (GNNs), the project will simulate interactions between law enforcement units, civilian populations, and environmental factors at city-scale resolution. HPC resources are critical to process high-dimensional datasets (spanning terabytes of geospatial-temporal data) and to run thousands of parallelized simulations testing allocation strategies under diverse scenarios, including routine patrols, large-scale public events, and crisis responses. Expected outcomes include a scalable decision-support system that identifies resource allocation policies balancing crime deterrence, response times, and community trust metrics. The computational framework will be validated against real-world datasets from municipal police departments, with iterative feedback from law enforcement stakeholders. By bridging computational social science, urban analytics, and operational research, this project aims to advance evidence-based policing practices while addressing ethical considerations in predictive policing algorithms. The resulting tools will provide a foundation for agencies to dynamically allocate resources in complex, evolving environments, potentially reducing operational costs and improving public safety outcomes.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to perform the duties of police and public security officers, including patrol and investigative activities, traffic control, crowd control and public relations, witness interviewing, evidence collection and management, basic crime prevention methods, weapon and equipment operation and maintenance, report preparation and other routine law enforcement responsibilities.

abstract: This project seeks to enhance driver and safety education pedagogy by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex, dynamic driving scenarios and evaluate the efficacy of instructional strategies. Current driver education curricula often rely on static simulations or limited real-world practice, which fail to account for the unpredictable, high-risk environments novice drivers may encounter. To address this gap, we propose developing a computational framework to simulate diverse driving conditions—including adverse weather, traffic variability, and pedestrian interactions—and analyze how different teaching methods influence learner decision-making and safety outcomes. Using agent-based modeling and machine learning, we will simulate interactions between virtual instructors, student drivers, and environmental factors across millions of scenarios, varying instructional techniques (e.g., feedback timing, scenario sequencing, and risk exposure gradients). These simulations will be informed by real-world driving data from existing studies, processed via GPU-accelerated pipelines to train adaptive models of student behavior. The HPC infrastructure is critical for scaling these simulations to statistically significant levels, enabling granular analysis of how pedagogical variables correlate with long-term retention of safe driving practices. Expected outcomes include identifying optimal instructional patterns for mitigating high-risk behaviors, such as distracted driving or improper hazard response, and generating evidence-based guidelines for tailoring teacher training programs to diverse learner needs. By translating computational insights into practical pedagogical tools, this work aims to equip driver education instructors with data-driven strategies to improve student preparedness, ultimately contributing to reduced traffic incidents among newly licensed drivers.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to teach driver and safety education programs at various educational levels.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop an agent-based modeling framework for optimizing team composition and dynamics in decentralized, gig-based work environments. As organizations increasingly adopt hybrid and project-driven structures, traditional human resource strategies struggle to address the volatility of skill demand, worker autonomy, and team cohesion in distributed teams. The research problem centers on the absence of computational tools capable of simulating large-scale, adaptive workforce ecosystems that balance operational efficiency with employee well-being. Using HPC capabilities, the project will construct a dynamic simulation environment integrating psychological principles of motivation, skill decay models from adult learning theory, and real-time labor market data. The computational approach combines reinforcement learning to model worker decision-making with network analysis to map emergent collaboration patterns across evolving projects. Key objectives include identifying critical thresholds for workload flexibility that minimize burnout while maintaining productivity, and quantifying the long-term organizational impact of personalized career development pathways in transient teams. The simulation will be validated against longitudinal datasets from platform-based workforces in technology and creative industries. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for predicting workforce stability under varying incentive structures and a taxonomy of intervention strategies to enhance retention in decentralized environments. By bridging computational social science with strategic human resource planning, this work aims to establish a new paradigm for data-driven organizational design in post-industrial labor markets, directly contributing to the development of adaptive human resource systems for volatile economic conditions.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to apply integrated training, organizational development, and career planning and counseling skills to the design, management, and evaluation of programs to improve individual productivity, employability, and job satisfaction and organizational effectiveness. Includes instruction in psychology; organizational behavior; principles of adult education; occupational counseling; skill testing and evaluation; program design; consulting practice; organizational development; and applications to issues such as training, management development, customer service, and total quality management.

abstract: The integration of high-performance computing (HPC) into fiber and textile arts presents an innovative pathway to address the computational challenges inherent in simulating complex material behaviors, optimizing sustainable fabrication processes, and generating intricate, data-driven designs. Traditional approaches in textile creation often rely on manual experimentation, limiting scalability and precision when working with advanced materials or multi-layered structures. This project seeks to leverage HPC resources to model the mechanical and aesthetic properties of novel fibrous composites, such as bio-based polymers and recycled textiles, using finite element analysis (FEA) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD). These simulations will predict stress distribution, draping behavior, and dye diffusion kinetics under varying environmental conditions, enabling the design of durable, adaptable textiles with reduced material waste.
