High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to parameterize models using multi-terabyte datasets from remote sensing, acoustic telemetry, and regional fishery observatories, while running ensemble simulations that incorporate climate projections, habitat connectivity matrices, and stochastic fishing effort distributions. Parallelized model architectures will enable sensitivity analyses across key parameters—including temperature-dependent metabolic rates, prey availability thresholds, and gear-specific catch efficiency—to identify tipping points in stock resilience. Outputs will quantify trade-offs between fishery yields, bycatch reduction, and conservation targets under proposed marine protected area configurations and adaptive quota systems. By leveraging GPU-accelerated machine learning for real-time parameter optimization and scenario interpolation, this work aims to reduce computational bottlenecks in spatial fishery forecasting. Outcomes will provide resource managers with decision-support tools to balance ecological and socioeconomic priorities in data-limited fisheries, particularly for transboundary stocks affected by range shifts. The requested HPC allocation will directly support advancements in scalable, interoperable modeling infrastructure for aquatic resource management, addressing critical gaps in predictive capacity for fisheries facing 21st-century global change pressures.
cip_title: Fishing and Fisheries Sciences and Management
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the husbandry and production of non-domesticated fish and shellfish populations for recreational and commercial purposes and the management of fishing and marine/aquatic product processing to ensure adequate conservation and efficient utilization. Includes instruction in the principles of marine/aquatic biology, freshwater and saltwater ecosystems, water resources, fishing production operations and management, fishing policy and regulation, and the management of recreational and commercial fishing activities.

abstract: The increasing complexity of precision mechanical systems in industries such as aerospace, advanced manufacturing, and medical devices demands advanced maintenance strategies to ensure reliability and minimize operational disruptions. Current diagnostic and predictive methods are constrained by computational limitations in processing high-dimensional, real-time sensor data and simulating multi-physics degradation processes, often resulting in reactive maintenance practices and costly downtime. This project seeks to address these challenges by developing a high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled framework for precision systems maintenance. The research integrates large-scale sensor data analytics with high-fidelity simulations to model wear, fatigue, and failure mechanisms in critical components. Computational methods include parallelized finite element analysis for simulating stress distributions under dynamic operational conditions and machine learning algorithms, such as graph neural networks, to identify anomaly patterns in multi-sensor networks. The project will leverage GPU-accelerated clusters to process terabyte-scale datasets in real time, enabling adaptive maintenance protocols that dynamically adjust to system performance metrics. Validation will focus on case studies involving precision robotic actuators and high-resolution medical imaging systems, where micro-scale material degradation significantly impacts functionality. Anticipated outcomes include an open-source computational toolkit for predictive maintenance, optimized repair scheduling algorithms, and quantifiable reductions in unplanned downtime for industrial partners. By bridging computational scalability with precision repair methodologies, this work aims to establish new benchmarks for proactive maintenance in technology-driven sectors. The requested HPC resources are essential to support the concurrent execution of multi-physics simulations and machine learning workflows, which exceed the memory and processing capabilities of existing local infrastructure.
cip_title: Precision Systems Maintenance and Repair Technologies/ Technicians, Other
cip_definition: Any instructional program in precision systems maintenance and repair, not elsewhere classified

abstract: Pediatric diseases often involve complex interactions between genetic, environmental, and developmental factors that are challenging to disentangle using traditional clinical research methods. This project aims to advance precision medicine for pediatric populations by developing computational models to predict disease progression and treatment responses in children with rare or heterogeneous conditions, with an initial focus on pediatric autoimmune disorders. The research problem centers on the lack of robust, scalable frameworks to integrate high-dimensional multi-omics data (genomic, epigenomic, proteomic) with longitudinal clinical records while accounting for developmental trajectories. To address this, we propose a machine learning pipeline leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to analyze terabyte-scale datasets from multicenter cohorts, including the NIH’s Childhood Arthritis and Rheumatology Research Alliance registry. Computational methods will include deep learning architectures (e.g., transformer-based models for temporal data) to identify dynamic biomarkers, Bayesian network models to infer causal pathways in disease flares, and population-scale genomic simulations to assess genotype-phenotype associations. These analyses require parallelized processing of whole-genome sequences, GPU-accelerated model training across thousands of patient trajectories, and large-scale permutation testing to address multiple hypothesis challenges inherent in pediatric datasets with small sample sizes. Expected outcomes include (1) a predictive framework for stratifying autoimmune disease risk in genetically susceptible children, (2) validated computational biomarkers of treatment response, and (3) open-source tools for pediatric-specific multi-omics integration. The HPC resources are critical for achieving the necessary scale and speed, as preliminary benchmarks show a 200-fold acceleration in model convergence using distributed computing compared to local clusters. This work will provide clinically actionable insights to reduce diagnostic delays and optimize immunosuppressive therapy regimens, directly addressing unmet needs in pediatric rheumatology. All models and anonymized data will be shared via a FAIR-compliant portal to accelerate collaborative research in pediatric precision medicine.
cip_definition: Research focused on Pediatric Medicine

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a predictive analytics framework to optimize decision-making in multi-stakeholder information technology (IT) project environments, with a focus on dynamic risk interdependencies and resource allocation under uncertainty. Traditional project management tools struggle to model cascading risks in large-scale IT initiatives—such as enterprise cloud migrations or cybersecurity overhauls—where technical dependencies, evolving security threats, and human factors create nonlinear, high-dimensional optimization challenges. The proposed computational approach integrates agent-based modeling, graph neural networks, and discrete-event simulation to capture how technical system behaviors, team interactions, and external pressures co-evolve during project execution. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are required to train models on heterogeneous datasets (project timelines, communication logs, vulnerability scans) and simulate thousands of scenario permutations across variable team structures and threat landscapes. Key innovations include a temporal hypergraph architecture to represent shifting dependencies between technical tasks and stakeholder priorities, coupled with reinforcement learning to identify adaptive resource allocation policies. Expected outcomes include a publicly available benchmarking dataset of simulated IT project scenarios, metrics for quantifying "resilience entropy" in team-process architectures, and prescriptive guidelines for mitigating cascading failures in complex IT implementations. This work bridges computational social science with IT operations research, offering novel methodologies to address growing concerns about systemic risk in digitally transformed organizations. By leveraging parallelized simulations and deep learning at scale, the project aims to advance predictive capabilities beyond current Monte Carlo-based project risk tools, directly supporting the National Strategic Computing Initiative’s priorities in decision-centric modeling.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to design, develop, and manage information technology projects in a variety of companies and organizations. Includes instruction in principles of project management, risk management, procurement and contract management, information security management, software management, organizational principles and behavior, communications, quality assurance, financial analysis, leadership, and team effectiveness.

abstract: This research project seeks to develop a computational framework to optimize real-time adaptive sales tactics in dynamic customer interactions, leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) to model complex, multi-agent decision-making processes. While traditional sales training emphasizes static scripts and generalized strategies, emerging challenges—such as hyper-personalization demands, rapidly shifting consumer preferences, and the integration of AI-assisted tools in sales operations—require a data-driven understanding of how adaptive tactics influence customer outcomes. The core research problem centers on quantifying the nonlinear relationships between sales representative behaviors (e.g., linguistic patterns, emotional tone adjustments, and real-time objection handling) and customer purchasing decisions across diverse demographic and psychographic segments. Using an agent-based modeling approach, we will simulate millions of buyer-seller interaction scenarios parameterized by empirical data from CRM systems, voice analytics, and biometric feedback sensors. HPC resources will enable parallelized Monte Carlo simulations to explore the phase space of possible tactics, while graph neural networks will identify latent decision pathways in customer responses. The computational framework will integrate reinforcement learning to train adaptive sales agent models, optimizing for ethical persuasion metrics and long-term customer lifetime value. Expected outcomes include a predictive toolkit for generating context-aware sales recommendations and a sensitivity analysis platform to stress-test strategies under market uncertainties. This work bridges behavioral economics, computational linguistics, and operations research, offering novel insights into scalable, ethically grounded sales process optimization. By quantifying previously intangible "soft skills," the project aims to advance both academic research in human-computer collaborative selling and practical tools for sales force training in rapidly evolving digital markets.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to possess the skills associated with direct promotion of products and services to potential customers and to function as independent sales representatives and managers. Includes instruction in consumer psychology, image projection, public speaking and interpersonal communications, sales organization and operations, customer relations, professional standards and ethics, and applicable technical skills.

abstract: Effective administration of special education programs requires dynamic resource allocation strategies that balance complex legal, ethical, and pedagogical demands while addressing diverse student needs. However, current approaches to program evaluation and decision-making often rely on static datasets or manual processes, limiting administrators’ ability to model the cascading effects of policy changes, funding shifts, or student population fluctuations. This project proposes the development of an agent-based computational model to simulate resource allocation scenarios in special education administration at the district level. The model will integrate multi-year datasets on student Individualized Education Program (IEP) requirements, staffing patterns, budget constraints, and compliance outcomes from state education records. High-performance computing resources are essential to process these heterogeneous datasets at scale, run thousands of parallel simulations with varying parameters, and apply machine learning techniques to identify optimal resource distribution patterns under evolving conditions. The computational framework will explicitly model interactions between student needs (categorized by disability type and required services), staff qualifications, legal mandates from the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA), and fiscal limitations. Expected outcomes include predictive metrics for service delivery gaps, evidence-based staffing ratio recommendations, and scenario analysis tools to support administrators in proactive resource planning. By enabling real-time simulation of complex tradeoffs between inclusion mandates, specialized service requirements, and budgetary realities, this research aims to advance data-driven decision-making in special education leadership while maintaining rigorous compliance with federal and state regulations. The resulting computational toolkit will be validated against historical program outcomes from three partner school districts and disseminated as an open-source framework for adaptive special education administration.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals to plan, supervise, and manage programs for exceptional students and their parents. Includes instruction in special education theory and practice, special education program development, evaluation and assessment in special education, state and federal law and regulations, managing individual education plans, problems of low- and high- disability students, mainstreaming, special education curricula, staff management, parent education, communications and community relations, budgeting, and professional standards and ethics.

abstract: The development of scalable control frameworks for quantum dynamical systems represents a critical engineering challenge at the intersection of quantum physics, computational mathematics, and control theory. Current approaches to optimizing control protocols for quantum devices—such as qubits in quantum computers or sensors—struggle with the exponential scaling of computational complexity as system size increases. This project seeks to overcome these limitations by leveraging high-performance computing (HPC) resources to design and validate efficient, adaptive control algorithms for multi-qubit systems. The research will employ tensor network simulations to model quantum dynamics, combined with gradient-based optimization and machine learning techniques to iteratively refine control sequences under realistic noise conditions. By parallelizing these simulations across GPU clusters, the project aims to achieve system sizes of 20+ qubits, a regime where classical computational methods typically fail. The anticipated outcomes include open-source software tools for quantum control optimization, experimentally validated protocols for error suppression in near-term quantum devices, and fundamental insights into the trade-offs between control fidelity and computational resource demands. This work will directly address bottlenecks in the engineering of reliable quantum technologies, with potential applications in quantum computing, precision sensing, and materials simulation. The computational demands of simulating quantum systems in a parameter-optimized framework necessitate access to HPC resources, including GPU nodes for accelerated linear algebra operations and high-memory nodes for managing large state-vector representations. Successful implementation will provide a template for integrating physics-informed machine learning with HPC infrastructure to tackle emerging engineering problems in quantum device design.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals for admission or transfer to a baccalaureate-level program in any of the fields of engineering.

abstract: This research project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to advance a computational comparative law framework analyzing the evolution and interaction of legal principles across civil and common law systems. The core research problem lies in the inability of traditional legal scholarship to systematically evaluate how doctrinal concepts—such as proportionality, fiduciary duty, or good faith—emerge, diverge, or converge within large-scale, multilingual corpora of judicial decisions, statutes, and scholarly commentaries. While qualitative comparative analysis dominates the field, the scale and linguistic complexity of global legal texts (spanning 50+ jurisdictions and six languages) necessitate computational methods to detect latent patterns, semantic shifts, and cross-jurisdictional influences. The project will develop a pipeline combining transformer-based natural language processing (NLP) for semantic similarity analysis, dynamic network models to trace doctrinal migration, and phylogenetic algorithms to reconstruct legal concept evolution. HPC resources are critical for training multilingual legal language models, processing terabyte-scale text datasets, and running parallelized simulations of normative diffusion across jurisdictions. Expected outcomes include 1) identification of understudied convergence points between civil and common law systems in emerging areas like digital rights and climate liability, 2) a quantitative framework for predicting legal harmonization pressures, and 3) open-access tools for mapping citation networks and conceptual analogies across legal traditions. By integrating computational social science methodologies with doctrinal legal analysis, this work aims to establish a replicable paradigm for data-driven comparative law research while addressing infrastructure gaps in non-STEM disciplines. The results will provide actionable insights for international judicial training programs and transnational policy design, demonstrating the transformative potential of HPC in advancing rigorous, empirically grounded legal scholarship.
cip_definition: An advanced, professional study of legal systems and philosophies in comparative perspective.

abstract: This project seeks to advance our understanding of light-driven molecular mechanisms in photosynthetic systems through high-performance computing (HPC)-enabled simulations of energy transfer and charge separation dynamics. Photosynthetic organisms rely on precise protein-pigment interactions to convert light energy into chemical energy, but the atomic-scale dynamics governing these processes—particularly under fluctuating environmental light conditions—remain poorly resolved. Traditional experimental methods struggle to capture ultrafast photophysical events or disentangle the roles of specific amino acid residues in modulating excited-state behavior. To address this gap, we propose multiscale molecular dynamics (MD) and quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) simulations to model light-harvesting complexes (LHCs) and reaction centers in cyanobacteria. The simulations will integrate time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) to track exciton migration and charge transfer pathways across femtosecond to microsecond timescales. HPC resources will enable the analysis of conformational landscapes under variable light intensities and spectral compositions, directly testing hypotheses about photoprotective quenching mechanisms and photodamage repair. Additionally, we will develop machine learning-accelerated workflows to predict mutagenesis targets for optimizing energy transfer efficiency in synthetic photobiology applications. The computational pipeline will be validated against experimental spectroscopic data and cryo-EM structures. By elucidating how light quality and quantity dynamically reshape photosynthetic machinery, this work will provide foundational insights into environmental photobiology and photomorphogenesis. Outcomes will inform bioengineering strategies for improved solar energy conversion systems and advance predictive models of organismal responses to climate-driven light regime shifts. The requested resources—50,000 node-hours on GPU-accelerated clusters and 50 TB of storage for trajectory datasets—are critical for achieving the sampling depth required to resolve rare conformational states and statistically robust mechanistic conclusions.
detailed_field: Biochemistry, biophysics, and molecular biology nec
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the scientific study of the effects of light energy on living organisms, the manufacture and processing of luminescence by organisms, and the uses of light in biological research. Includes instruction in bioluminescence, chronobiology, photomedicine, environmental photobiology, organic photochemistry, photomorphogenesis, photoreceptors and photosensitization, molecular mechanics of photosynthesis, phototechnology, vision, ultraviolet radiation, radiation physics, and spectral research methods.

abstract: The proposed research seeks to investigate the emergent dynamics of large-scale neural circuits underlying cognitive flexibility and their dysregulation in neuropsychiatric disorders such as schizophrenia. While clinical studies have identified altered functional connectivity patterns in these conditions, the biophysical mechanisms linking cellular-level properties to system-level network dysfunction remain poorly understood. This project will employ biologically detailed spiking neural network models to simulate cortical-subcortical interactions during cognitive task-switching paradigms, integrating empirical data from electrophysiological recordings and diffusion tensor imaging to constrain model architecture. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to simulate networks containing >100,000 multicompartment neurons with realistic synaptic plasticity rules, capturing the timescale interactions between fast spiking activity (milliseconds) and slow neuromodulatory effects (seconds to minutes). Parallelized simulations will systematically vary parameters related to dopamine receptor density, interneuron connectivity gradients, and axonal conduction delays—factors hypothesized to govern metastable network states. Machine learning approaches will then identify critical parameter combinations that recapitulate clinical biomarkers of cognitive inflexibility. The computational workflow requires sustained access to GPU-accelerated nodes for model training and CPU clusters for parameter space exploration. Expected outcomes include 1) a mechanistic framework explaining how molecular and microcircuit anomalies propagate to macroscale network dysfunction, 2) predictive models of personalized neuromodulation targets based on virtual patient-derived network configurations, and 3) open-source simulation tools optimized for HPC environments to study multiscale neural dynamics. By bridging scales from synaptic physiology to cognitive behavior, this work aims to advance translational strategies for circuit-based interventions while establishing computational neuroscience infrastructure for the broader neurobiology community.
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the interdisciplinary scientific study of the molecular, structural, physiologic, cognitive, and behavioral aspects of the brain and nervous system. Includes instruction in molecular and cellular neuroscience, brain science, anatomy and physiology of the central nervous system, molecular and biochemical bases of information processing, behavioral neuroscience, biology of neuropsychiatric disorders, and applications to the clinical sciences and biomedical engineering.

abstract: The increasing complexity of client interactions, patient scheduling, and regulatory compliance in veterinary practices has exposed critical inefficiencies in traditional reception workflows. This project seeks to develop a computational framework for optimizing veterinary reception operations through the integration of natural language processing (NLP), discrete-event simulation, and predictive analytics. The research addresses a gap in non-science computational applications by focusing on service-oriented workflows in animal care—a domain not adequately served by existing models in healthcare administration or business logistics. High-performance computing (HPC) resources are essential to process large datasets of anonymized client communication logs (e.g., phone transcripts, email chains), electronic health records, and staff activity metrics from 14 partner veterinary clinics. The computational approach involves three phases: 1) Training NLP models to classify client intent and emotional tone in unstructured text/voice data, 2) Building parallelized simulations of clinic flow under varying demand scenarios, and 3) Developing reinforcement learning agents to recommend real-time scheduling adjustments. Key challenges include managing temporal dependencies in appointment data and maintaining compliance with veterinary privacy regulations during model training. Expected outcomes include an open-source toolkit for clinic workflow optimization that reduces client wait times by 15-20% in simulation trials while maintaining compliance with AVMA ethical guidelines. This work establishes a novel computational paradigm for service quality improvement in veterinary care, demonstrating how HPC resources can drive innovation in traditionally non-technical vocational domains. The project further contributes methodological advances in applying simulation architectures to small-scale service environments with constrained resources.
cip_definition: A program that prepares individuals, under the supervision of office managers, veterinary technicians, or veterinarians, to provide customer service, visitor reception, and patient intake and discharge services. Includes instruction in veterinary office and animal care facility procedures, veterinary terminology, interpersonal skills, record-keeping, customer service, telephone skills, data entry, interpersonal communications skills, and applicable policies and regulations.

abstract: This project seeks to leverage high-performance computing (HPC) resources to develop and optimize computational models that advance the design of personalized educational interventions for students with hearing impairments, including deafness. Current tools for tailoring instruction to this population often rely on static, generalized frameworks that inadequately address the diverse linguistic, cognitive, and sensory profiles of learners. The research problem centers on bridging this gap by creating dynamic, data-driven models capable of simulating individualized learning pathways and predicting the efficacy of multimodal teaching strategies (e.g., visual, tactile, or sign language-based interventions) in real time. The project will employ machine learning techniques to analyze heterogeneous datasets, including eye-tracking patterns during sign language acquisition, tactile response metrics, and longitudinal academic performance data from deaf and hard-of-hearing students. These datasets will train neural networks to identify optimal instructional sequences and adaptive feedback mechanisms tailored to individual needs. Additionally, agent-based modeling will simulate classroom environments under varying conditions—such as differing instructor-to-student ratios or assistive technology configurations—to evaluate scalable teaching approaches. HPC resources are critical due to the computational intensity of processing high-dimensional sensory data and running parallelized simulations across thousands of scenarios. Expected outcomes include an open-source framework for generating individualized education plans (IEPs) with embedded predictive analytics, as well as evidence-based guidelines for integrating computational tools into teacher training programs. By quantifying the impact of specific interventions on learning outcomes, this work aims to empower educators with empirically validated strategies, reduce trial-and-error in classroom practice, and improve equitable access to quality instruction for deaf and hard-of-hearing learners.
cip_title: Education/ Teaching of Individuals with Hearing Impairments Including Deafness
cip_definition: A program that focuses on the design of educational services for children or adults with hearing impairments including deafness which adversely affect their educational performance, and that may prepare individuals to teach such students. Includes instruction in identifying students with hearing impairments, including deafness, developing individual education plans, teaching and supervising hearing-impaired students, counseling, and applicable laws and policies.
